commits.title: chore(ralph): update working_set.md for loop #35 (CREATE OPERATOR CLASS pg_opclass slice 409)

New parseCreateOpFamilyTail (parser) captures [schema.]name USING method;

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): regproc/regprocedure OID→name resolution at query output
commits.description:
Neither dispatch.go's/dispatch_extended.go's shared appendTypedCellText nor
expr.go's ::regproc cast resolved a non-zero pg_proc OID to a function name
(regprocout), so pg_type.typinput/typoutput, pg_operator.oprcode/oprrest/
oprjoin, and pg_am.amproc all rendered raw OIDs on a direct SELECT, and
`<oid>::regproc` was a silent no-op cast. New leaf-package reverse index
internal/catalog.RegprocName, backed by generated
pg_proc_names_generated.go (cmd/gen-pg-proc-data -names), lets both
internal/executor and internal/server resolve OIDs without the import
cycle that blocks internal/executor from reaching internal/initdb's
existing table directly.

commits.title: chore(ralph): update working_set.md for loop #62 (dispatch type-format parity)
feat(M0119-0004): unify extended vs simple-query type-formatting (dispatch)
commits.description:
dispatch_extended.go's per-cell wire-formatting switch only special-cased
float4/float8 and fell back to the generic AppendValueText for
date/time/timetz/bytea/regclass, diverging from dispatch.go's fuller
switch (a discovery from loop #61's pg_aggregate work). Extracted the
switch into a shared (*Server).appendTypedCellText used by both result
loops, closing the divergence at its root instead of patching cases
one at a time. New TestExtendedQueryTypedColumnsMatchSimpleQuery pins
it via the raw wire protocol (confirmed failing pre-fix).

indexes the already machine-generated pgProcAllEntries() (3397-row PG18

aggFuncNameOrDash convention used for user-defined aggregates).

Closes DU-002 slice 405 resume point (b). Deferred (ledger row appended):

query-output time (pg_type/pg_operator/pg_am columns still render raw

commits.description:
Closes the DU-002 slice 405 deferral's resume point (c): CREATE AGGREGATE
was not WAL-logged, so a user-defined aggregate vanished on restart. Adds

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CREATE AGGREGATE pg_dump round-trip (DU-002 slice 405)
commits.description:
Ports the upstream 'CREATE AGGREGATE dump_test.newavg' pg_dump TAP fixture
(public-schema-adapted), a new object family for M0119-0004.

Two previously-hidden, aggregate-agnostic gaps blocked this and are fixed
generally, not as aggregate-specific workarounds:

- pg_aggregate was never SQL-queryable at all, even for the 161 built-in
  aggregates goopg has shipped since M0106-0010 (the heap file was only ever
  wired for PG18-standby fidelity, never registered as a queryable
  catalog.Table). New registerPgAggregateView (internal/initdb/pg_aggregate_view.go)
  mirrors pg_index's existing heap-write-plus-Virtual-read split.
- regproc/oid cross-type comparison was unimplemented in the analyzer, so
  pg_dump's own dumpAgg query (`a.aggfnoid = p.oid`) raised 42804. New
  isOIDFamily helper in isComparable covers the whole "reg*" OID-alias
  family, which real PostgreSQL treats as binary-coercible with oid.

Also: parser.CreateAggregateStmt.FinalFuncModify (previously discarded);
catalog.UserAggregate.OID + ListUserAggregates(); pg_proc now emits a
prokind='a' row per aggregate; executor.routineOrAggregateArgs so
pg_get_function_arguments resolves a non-Routine aggregate OID; two curated
builtins (int4_avg_accum/int8_avg, the functions PG's own avg(int4) uses);
a live pg_aggregate heap-row write for PG18-standby fidelity.

Verified against a real running server + real pg_dump 18.3 (byte-identical),
and that the aggregate actually executes at runtime (SELECT newavg(a) FROM t).

Deferred (ledger row appended): schema-qualified aggregates land in public
regardless of qualifier; built-in aggregates' transfn/finalfn still render
raw OIDs on direct query; CREATE AGGREGATE is not yet WAL-logged (same
round-trip-first/persistence-later split as TRANSFORM/CAST/CONVERSION/COLLATION).

commits.title: test(M0119-0004): verify COMMENT ON CAST resolves type-name synonyms
commits.description:
Closes the last open item from the loop #51 DROP CAST synonym-key fix:
CommentOnStmt's CAST handler (execCompatNoop case "cast") calls the same
catalog.CastByTypes choke point that RegisterCast/DropCast were fixed to
key through TypeNameToOID, but that inheritance was never independently
re-verified. New TestCommentOnCastResolvesTypeNameSynonym confirms
COMMENT ON CAST (real AS text) resolves a cast registered as
(float4, text) with no further production change needed.

commits.title: fix(M0119-0004): DROP CAST fails to resolve PG type-name synonyms
commits.description:
RegisterCast/DropCast/CastByTypes keyed the cast registry on the raw
lowercased parsed type spelling, so DROP CAST (real AS text) failed to
find a cast created via CREATE CAST (float4 AS text) — PG's built-in
type-name synonyms (real/float4, integer/int4, double precision/float8)
never cross-resolved. Fix keys through TypeNameToOID instead, matching
how pg_cast's virtual view already renders castsource/casttarget.

Also fixes a latent bug in the same path: TypeNameToOID falls back to
OIDText for unrecognized names (domains/enums/composites), which would
have collapsed distinct user-defined-type casts into one bucket if keyed
naively — castKeyTypeName detects the fallback and preserves per-type
distinctness.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CREATE/DROP COLLATION restart persistence + fix missing DROP COLLATION
commits.description:
Fourth and last object of the slice-389 restart-persistence backlog
(Transform/Cast/Conversion already closed). Discovered mid-loop that DROP
COLLATION had no implementation at all: no catalog.DropCollation method
existed and execDropCompat had no "collation" case, so DROP COLLATION on
an existing user collation always errored "does not exist" and IF EXISTS
silently no-op'd without touching the registry. Implemented DROP
COLLATION itself, then added WAL restart persistence (RecordKind 42/43)
following the Transform/Cast/Conversion template, wired into open.go
after schema/conversion replay since a collation is schema-scoped.

commits.title: chore(ralph): update working_set.md for loop #49 (CREATE CONVERSION restart persistence)
feat(M0119-0004): CREATE/DROP CONVERSION restart persistence + fix WAL-scan checkpoint collision
commits.description:
Third of the slice-389 "in-memory only" backlog to close (TRANSFORM/CAST
closed prior loops): CREATE/DROP CONVERSION now survives a restart via
new RecordKindCreateConversion(40)/DropConversion(41) WAL records +
CreateConversionDuringRecovery/DropConversionDuringRecovery catalog hooks
+ internal/initdb/conversion_ddl_recovery.go, wired after schema replay
since conversions are schema-scoped.

Also fixes a real cross-cutting bug found while landing this: all four
DDL-recovery scanners (schema/transform/cast/conversion) blindly switched
on rec.Payload[0] without checking whether rec was a PG-native/canonical
XLogRecord (e.g. an XLOG_CHECKPOINT_SHUTDOWN) whose MainData carries no
goopg kind tag at all. A checkpoint's raw redo-LSN low byte coincidentally
matched RecordKindCreateConversion(40), causing a false-positive decode on
a bare Init+Open with zero conversions ever appended - the same collision
class wal.ApplyRecord already guards against for physical replay, just
never guarded in the catalog-only scanners. Fixed via new exported
wal.IsGoopgNativeRecord, wired into all four replay*DDLRecords loops.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CREATE/DROP CAST restart persistence via WAL replay
commits.description:
Second of the slice-389 "in-memory only" restart-persistence backlog to
close (TRANSFORM closed loop #47). New RecordKindCreateCast(38)/
RecordKindDropCast(39) WAL kinds + Encode/Decode functions mirror the
TRANSFORM template; RegisterCastDuringRecovery/DropCastDuringRecovery
catalog hooks; new internal/initdb/cast_ddl_recovery.go replay driver
wired into open.go; executor emits the WAL record at CREATE/DROP CAST.

TestEncodeDecodeCreateCastRoundTrip caught a real 1-byte buffer
under-allocation in the first EncodeCreateCast cut before it landed.

Verified live: 3x restart cycle on an isolated port confirms CREATE CAST
(WITHOUT FUNCTION / WITH INOUT / WITH FUNCTION forms) and DROP CAST both
survive a restart with correct OIDs/context/method/funcOID.

commits.title: chore(ralph): update working_set.md for loop #47 (CREATE TRANSFORM restart persistence)
feat(M0119-0004): CREATE/DROP TRANSFORM restart persistence via WAL replay

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): expose builtin pg_proc rows for CREATE TRANSFORM (DU-002 slice 404 follow-up)
commits.description:
Closes the slice-404 resume point: catalog.LookupBuiltinProc/BuiltinProcs
hand-curates int4recv/prsd_lextype (the two builtins the CREATE TRANSFORM

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CREATE/DROP TRANSFORM round-trip skeleton (DU-002 slice 404)
commits.description:
New object family: parser captures FOR type LANGUAGE lang (FROM/TO SQL WITH
FUNCTION ...), catalog.Transform registers it with a stable OID, and
pg_transform.VirtualRows renders it for pg_dump's getTransforms/dumpTransform.
resolveTransformFunc ports PostgreSQL's CreateTransform + check_transform_function
validation (return-type role check, volatility/prokind/SETOF/arg-count/arg-type),
reusing CREATE CAST's WITH-FUNCTION resolution style.

Not yet wired into the DU-002 connsetup fixture: the canonical PG test case
references builtin functions (int4recv, prsd_lextype), and goopg's server-side
pg_proc catalog does not expose builtins at all (empirically verified: 0 rows

also already silently affects CAST's WITH FUNCTION and CONVERSION's
FROM-function on any builtin reference. Recorded in the deferral ledger with
a concrete resume point.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CONVERSION conproc FuncOID cross-reference (DU-002 slice 403)
commits.description:
Close the slice-402 deferral: pg_conversion.conproc is a real regproc/OID
reference in PostgreSQL, not captured text. UserConversion now carries

Catch up fix_plan.md + the 0110-0001 design doc with slices 398-403 (accrued
undocumented across several loops); deferral ledger row for slice 403.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CONVERSION FROM-function validation (DU-002 slice 402)
commits.description:
CreateConversionCommand requires the FROM function to resolve to a real
catalog function with the fixed signature
(int4,int4,cstring,internal,int4,bool)->int4. resolveConversionFunc mirrors
LookupFuncName/get_func_rettype: no matching overload -> 42883, wrong
return type -> 42P17. execCompatNoop's "conversion" case now validates this
after the encoding-name checks (slice 401) before registering. Closes the
slice-399/400/401 deferral (b)-remainder; conproc OID cross-referencing
(like castfunc) stays deferred.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CREATE CONVERSION encoding-name validation (DU-002 slice 401)
commits.description:
Mirror the static encoding-name checks in PG's CreateConversionCommand
(conversioncmds.c): a CREATE [DEFAULT] CONVERSION whose FOR/TO encoding name
does not resolve via pg_char_to_encoding is now rejected with
ERRCODE_UNDEFINED_OBJECT (42704), and a conversion to/from SQL_ASCII
(pg_enc ID 0) is rejected with ERRCODE_INVALID_OBJECT_DEFINITION (42P17),
matching upstream. Previously goopg stored an unknown encoding as ID -1
(dumping FOR '') and silently accepted SQL_ASCII.

New executor helper validateCreateConversionEncodings returns the resolved
pg_enc IDs and a ready *ExecError; execCompatNoop case "conversion" calls it
and reuses forEnc/toEnc (no double EncodingNameToID). Valid conversions are
unaffected and still round-trip byte-identical through pg_dump.

Closes the encoding-name half of slice-399 deferral (b). The FROM-function
existence/return-type/runtime-probe checks (LookupFuncName + get_func_rettype
+ OidFunctionCall6) stay deferred (no in-catalog conversion functions / no
encoding-conversion engine) — recorded in the deferral ledger.

Tests: TestValidateCreateConversionEncodings (executor unit, 7 cases incl.
unknown-beats-SQL_ASCII ordering) + slice-401 server-level 42704/42P17
negative assertions in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup.

commits.title: docs(ralph): add missing status column to four 2026-06-30 ledger rows

vs pg_dump 18.3, instead of FOR '' from a -1 ID.

- .ralph/deferral_ledger.md: slice-400 row (399(b) pg_proc validation + (c)

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): CREATE CAST argument/return-type validation (DU-002 slice 398)
commits.description:
Port PG's CreateCast argument/return-type rules (functioncmds.c) so a malformed
CREATE CAST is rejected with SQLSTATE 42P17 instead of silently registered.
Closes the slice-397 deferral (c).

- internal/executor/operators_ddl.go: new validateCreateCast(s, routine) +

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): array-metachar OPTIONS value quoting (DU-002 slice 384)
commits.description:
Closes the array-metacharacter quoting deferral carried since slices 378–380.
PostgreSQL renders foreign srvoptions/fdwoptions/umoptions text[] via array_out,
which double-quotes any `name=value` element containing a comma/brace/whitespace/
double-quote/backslash (and ""/NULL case-insensitively), backslash-escaping
embedded "/\. goopg previously comma-joined the literal bare (`{host=a,b}`), so
an option value carrying a metacharacter (`host 'a,b'`) split on its embedded
comma when pg_dump re-parsed it via pg_options_to_table, corrupting the list.

- NEW arrayTextLiteral wraps elements as {…}, quoting each.
- optionsArrayLiteral delegates to it (metachar-free elements stay byte-identical
  bare; `host 'a,b'` → `{"host=a,b"}`).
- The 3 pg_class.reloptions renderers (table/toast/index) route through
  arrayTextLiteral for one authoritative quoter (values are numeric/bool/enum so
  output is unchanged but the path is now metachar-safe).

Round-trip works because existing parseTextArray already unquotes `"host=a,b"`
→ `host=a,b`, which pg_options_to_table splits on the first `=` to recover `a,b`.

Tests: new TestQuoteArrayElement + TestOptionsArrayLiteralMetachar (catalog) +
end-to-end goopg_srv_mc (`OPTIONS (host 'a,b')`) fixture/assertion in

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): trigger EXECUTE FUNCTION non-string args pg_dump round-trip (DU-002 slice 369)
commits.description:
PG's gram.y TriggerFuncArg stores every argument form as a string in

EXECUTE FUNCTION trig_fn(0042, 3.14, foo) dumps as
EXECUTE FUNCTION trig_fn('42', '3.14', 'foo').

goopg's parseCreateTriggerTail previously captured only TokenStringLit args and
p.advance()-skipped every other token, dropping numeric/identifier trigger args
entirely. It now also captures TokenIntLit (canonicalised via new
canonicalTriggerIntArg helper, mirroring psprintf("%d")), TokenNumericLit, and
TokenIdent token text into FuncArgs. buildTriggerDefString already re-quotes
every stored arg, so no deparse change was needed. Resolves the slice-368
deferral.

in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup + extended TestParseCreateTriggerFuncArgs case.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): negative numeric literal '-N'::type pg_dump round-trip (DU-002 slice 364)
commits.description:
A unary minus applied DIRECTLY to a numeric literal now dumps as PG's folded
'-N'::type Const form in every context the two pg_dump deparse twins feed —
CHECK predicates (table + domain), column DEFAULTs, expression-index keys,
partition-key expressions, and function-argument defaults. Resolves the
long-recurring negative-literal deferral behind slices 302/360(a)/362(b)/363.

The prior deferral assumed matching '-N'::type required threading the
column/argument type into the type-blind deparser. The empirical unblock: PG's
get_const_expr/make_const derive the cast type from the LITERAL's own (negated)
magnitude, NOT the column type — a bigint column's `<> -100` dumps
'-100'::integer, `DEFAULT -9000000000` dumps '-9000000000'::bigint, and
`DEFAULT -2147483648` (INT_MIN) dumps '-2147483648'::integer (boundary
magnitude <= 1<<31). New shared helper parser.NegatedLiteralSQL renders
'-N'::{integer,bigint,numeric} for a bare IntegerConst/NumericConst operand;
both twins (executor.defaultExprToSQL, catalog.formatExprForAttrdef) call it in
their OpUnaryNeg arm and fall back to the compound `(- (operand))` form for a
non-folded negation (slice-302 negdef cases unchanged). Byte-identical vs real
pg_dump 18.3 across all contexts.

Tests: TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup slice-364 dchkneg/neglit/neglit_ix +
unit TestDefaultExprToSQLBinaryParen / TestFormatExprForAttrdefExpr (both
updated -1 -> '-1'::integer).

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): compound/function-call DOMAIN CHECK pg_dump round-trip (DU-002 slice 363)
commits.description:
A generic (non-IN) domain CHECK now dumps with PostgreSQL's per-node
parenthesization instead of the legacy token-text wrap CHECK ((<raw>)):
  CHECK (VALUE > 0 AND VALUE < 100) -> CHECK (((VALUE > 0) AND (VALUE < 100)))
  CHECK (length(VALUE) > 0)         -> CHECK ((length(VALUE) > 0))

This is the domain twin of slice 362 and resolves slice-362 deferred-(a).
New renderDomainCheckPredicate (internal/executor/operators_ddl.go) re-parses
the stored raw text and deparses via the fully-parenthesizing defaultExprToSQL
(the same renderer the table-CHECK path uses), with the same re-parse
round-trip fallback guard. upcaseDomainValuePlaceholder rewrites every bare
`value` ColumnRef back to the uppercase VALUE keyword, since the lexer
case-folds it on re-parse but PG deparses the CoerceToDomainValue placeholder
uppercase. The dump site routes only generic CHECKs through the new renderer;
a CHECK (VALUE IN (...)) form keeps the legacy raw wrap because it is stored as
a pre-synthesized byte-exact ScalarArrayOp deparse defaultExprToSQL cannot
reproduce. Single-comparison slice-96 domains are byte-unchanged.

Byte-verified against a throwaway PG 18.3 cluster.

Deferred (ledger): a negative literal in a domain CHECK (VALUE < -5 ->
'-5'::integer) still byte-diverges (type-blind defaultExprToSQL), same gap as
slice-360(a)/362(b).

TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup.

commits.description:

table-level CHECK constraint now dumps with PostgreSQL's per-node
parenthesization (`CHECK (((a > 0) AND (b > 0)))`, `CHECK ((length(name) > 0))`)
instead of goopg's legacy token-text wrap `CHECK ((<raw>))`.

goopg stores a CHECK body as token-reconstructed raw text
(parser.parseCheckExpr); new renderCheckPredicate (operators_ddl.go) re-parses
it and deparses via the fully-parenthesizing defaultExprToSQL — the same
renderer the index-predicate/expression-index/partition-key paths use —
wrapping once as `CHECK (%s)`. A re-parse round-trip guards the change: if the
raw text fails to parse or the deparse is not re-parseable, the legacy raw wrap
is kept so the dump never emits non-SQL garbage. Single-comparison slices
127-129 are byte-unchanged. Byte-verified vs real pg_dump 18.3.

- dispatch (server/query.go): isHeapACLObject also fires for a '(' before

- read: pg_attribute seqscan attacl decode hook (sibling of the typacl hook)

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004-ACLHEAP): pg_attribute.attacl column-ACL store + AttrACLText renderer
commits.description:
Column analogue of loop #84's TypeACLText — the catalog step-2 building block
for the attacl (column-level GRANT) follow-up. Low blast radius: nothing on the
GRANT path calls it yet, so live behaviour is unchanged.

Key design divergence from typacl/proacl: a column's acldefault('c', owner) is
EMPTY (the owner and PUBLIC hold no implicit column privilege), so attacl is
NULL until the first column GRANT, carries NO leading owner aclitem and no
implicit PUBLIC entry, and returns to NULL once the last column privilege is
revoked (a table empties to {}, a column to NULL). The attacl renderer therefore
cannot reuse relaclTextLockedFor (which always prepends the owner entry), and the
relACLEmptied/relACLOwnerRevoked machinery does not apply.

internal/catalog/catalog.go:
- attrACLKey{relOID uint32; attNum int16} — a struct key, NOT a packed
  relOID<<16|attnum uint32 (overflows for real table OIDs >2^16).
- New composite-keyed stores attrACLs (grantee->priv->grant-option) +
  attrACLOrder (grant order), initialized in NewInMemory.
- attrACLPrivOrder = {INSERT/a, SELECT/r, UPDATE/w, REFERENCES/x} — the
  column-grantable subset in canonical aclitemout bit order.
- GrantColumnPrivilege / GrantColumnPrivilegeWithGrantOption /
  RevokeColumnPrivilege + AttrACLText(relOID, attNum) renderer; all four added
  to the Catalog interface.

(mixed-case all-alnum stays UNQUOTED per PG putid; only unsafe chars quoted).

commits.description:

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004-ACLHEAP): PG-native aclitem[] binary codec building block
commits.description:
Wiring loop #85's GRANT…ON TYPE parser capture toward the heap-backed pg_type
catalog revealed a previously-unknown blocker: the heap codec cannot encode a
non-empty aclitem[]. codec.go's `case "aclitem[]"` only handles a KindBytes
passthrough or emptyArrayTypeBytes(1033), so a NewStringDatum("{=U/postgres,…}")
silently drops the ACL; the generic encodeArrayValuePG has no aclitem element
entry and would mis-type it as a text array (elemtype 25, varlena elements) that
a PG18 standby / pg_dump getTypes cannot parse (it expects elemtype 1033 +
16-byte fixed AclItem structs). Because pg_type is heap-backed precisely for
PG18-standby basebackup parity, the typacl blob must be byte-faithful.

Land the dedicated, PG-native _aclitem codec as a self-contained,
behaviour-neutral building block (no caller yet -> nil blast radius), matching
the loop #84 (renderer) / #85 (parser) cadence:

  - internal/executor/codec_aclitem.go: encodeAclItemArrayText(aclText,
    resolveOID) parses canonical aclitemout text {grantee=privs/grantor,…} into
    the on-disk ArrayType varlena (same 24-byte 1-D no-NULL header as
    codec_array.go, elemtype 1033, one 16-byte AclItem per entry: ai_grantee Oid
    + ai_grantor Oid + ai_privs AclMode uint64, low 32 bits = privilege bits /
    high 32 bits = grant-option bits per acl.h ACL_GRANT_OPTION_FOR(privs)=
    privs<<32; empty grantee = ACL_ID_PUBLIC 0). Pure: role name<->OID resolution
    is injected by the caller, so no catalog dependency. decodeAclItemArrayText
    inverts it. Privilege letters follow ACL_ALL_RIGHTS_STR "arwdDxtXUCTcsAm"
    (letter at index i -> bit 1<<i); role-name quoting mirrors PG putid.
  - codec_aclitem_test.go: priv-letter<->AclMode (incl. grant option), a
    byte-exact golden for {=U/postgres} (40-byte blob), round-trip
    (PUBLIC/owner/owner+PUBLIC+grantee/grant-option/relacl-style multi-priv/
    non-owner grantor), empty (owner-revoke-all -> valid empty _aclitem), and a
    quoted-role-with-comma top-level-split case.

This is the encode/decode primitive every later heap-ACL re-sync (typacl now,
attacl next) builds on. Design 0119-0004 updated with the loop #86 progress
note; milestone box stays unchecked (the high-blast-radius reroute + heap-write
+ full gate set remain a dedicated loop).

via pre-commit hook.

slot: a full REVOKE deletes its aclitem and a later GRANT to that same grantee

GRANT SELECT TO rg_b; REVOKE SELECT FROM rg_a; GRANT INSERT TO rg_a ->
relacl {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,rg_b=r/postgres,rg_a=a/postgres} (b before a);
pg_dump emits the rg_b SELECT line before the rg_a INSERT line.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): ACL grantee grant-order preservation in relacl/proacl/nspacl (DU-002 slice 354)
commits.description:
Fixes a real divergence masked by every prior multi-grantee slice: goopg
rendered relacl grantees via sort.Strings (alphabetical), but PostgreSQL's
aclupdate (src/backend/utils/adt/acl.c) appends a brand-new grantee's aclitem
to the end of the array, so relacl preserves GRANT ORDER. The two coincide only
when grants are issued alphabetically -- which slices 352/353 happened to do. A
reverse-order grant (GRANT SELECT TO og_role_z then og_role_a) exposed it: real
PG 18.3 stores {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,og_role_z=r/postgres,og_role_a=r/
postgres} (z before a), while goopg emitted og_role_a first -> pg_dump GRANT
lines in the wrong order.

Engine change (internal/catalog): new tableACLOrder map[uint32][]string records
per-relation first-grant order of non-owner grantees; grant appends on first
appearance, revoke drops on full revoke (dropTableACLOrderRole), all
delete(tableACLs,oid) teardown sites mirror into tableACLOrder, and
relaclTextLockedFor iterates that list (skip owner + stale entries, sorted-append
backstop so a grant is never silently dropped) instead of sorting. Because
table/sequence/schema/function ACLs all funnel through the one tableACLs store
and relaclTextLockedFor core, the fix covers relacl/proacl/nspacl uniformly.
Owner-first rendering (vs PG's PUBLIC-before-owner function default) is unchanged
and pg_dump-invisible.

Blast radius nil for alphabetical grant sequences (grant order == sorted order
=> byte-unchanged); the only behavioral change is non-alphabetical sequences now
matching real PostgreSQL.

Tests: four internal/catalog/relacl_test.go units corrected -- they had encoded
the old alphabetical order, which real-PG verification proved wrong
(grantee_role-before-another_role, PUBLIC-before-named_role, grantee_fn-last).
New DU-002 slice 354 in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (reverse-order grant ->
z-before-a GRANT lines asserted via strings.Index, byte-identical vs real
pg_dump 18.3); slices 352/353 comments de-staled. Design

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): owner-side function REVOKE (pg_proc.proacl) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 347)
commits.description:
The owner-side counterpart of slice 346's PUBLIC-side function REVOKE. A
function's acldefault('f', owner) grants EXECUTE to BOTH the owner and PUBLIC, so
the two single-role revokes diverge: REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC -> proacl
{postgres=X/postgres} (slice 346); REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM postgres ->
{=X/postgres} (PUBLIC's implicit EXECUTE SURVIVES); both -> {} (verified vs real
PG 18.3). Unlike a table/sequence -- whose default grants only the owner so
REVOKE ALL FROM owner empties to {} (slices 341/343) -- the function owner revoke
leaves a surviving non-owner aclitem.

goopg got this wrong two ways: (1) recordFunctionRevoke (slice 346) seeded only
the owner's implicit EXECUTE, so revoking the owner emptied the array and pg_dump
wrongly also emitted a `... FROM PUBLIC;` line, stripping PUBLIC's surviving
default on restore; (2) relaclTextLockedFor re-added the absent owner as
postgres=<default>/postgres whenever the owner key was missing from a non-empty
array and relACLEmptied was unset, so {=X/postgres} rendered as
{postgres=X/postgres,=X/postgres} (owner resurrected -> pg_dump dropped the owner
REVOKE). The pre-existing relACLEmptied flag is too narrow: it fires only when
the owner revoke also empties the whole array.

Fix (catalog + server): new OID-keyed flag relACLOwnerRevoked (the broader
"owner's implicit default was explicitly revoked, regardless of surviving
grantees"; relACLEmptied is its whole-array-empty special case). RevokeTablePrivilege
sets it whenever the owner entry is fully removed; relaclTextLockedFor suppresses
the leading owner entry when relACLEmptied||relACLOwnerRevoked and the empty-byRole
early-return renders {} for either (covers revoking every grantee in one statement,
where the last-removed entry is a non-owner so relACLEmptied stays unset);
MaterializeOwnerACL never resurrects a revoked owner; an owner-side GrantTablePrivilege
clears both flags; DropTableACL clears both. recordFunctionRevoke now seeds BOTH
owner + PUBLIC implicit EXECUTE, but only while proacl is still NULL (via the
newly interface-exposed Catalog.ProcACLText(oid)=="") -- re-seeding on a second
REVOKE would resurrect an already-revoked grantee, so `... FROM PUBLIC` then
`... FROM postgres` must reach {} not {=X/postgres} (PG expands acldefault exactly
once). Slice 346 stays byte-identical. The OID-keyed flag also fixes a latent
table bug (REVOKE ALL ON TABLE FROM owner while a grantee survives now correctly
suppresses the owner). Dump-fidelity only; near-zero blast radius.

Tests: TestProcACLRevokeFromOwner (catalog: owner-only -> {=X/postgres};
owner+PUBLIC -> {}; owner re-GRANT -> {postgres=X/postgres,=X/postgres}) +
slice-347 fixture/assert in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (asserts
`REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.ownrevfn(integer) FROM postgres;` appears and no
spurious `... FROM PUBLIC;`; byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3). catalog+server+
initdb+testport-connsetup suites PASS; build clean; pgbench smoke (pre-commit).

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): function-level REVOKE (pg_proc.proacl) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 346)
commits.description:
The routine REVOKE analogue of the table REVOKE slices (338+); the follow-up
slice 345 deferred. `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.revokefn(integer) FROM
PUBLIC` is the most common real-world function ACL mutation, and goopg silently
dropped it (the REVOKE recorder bailed on the `function` object class),
re-granting PUBLIC's default EXECUTE on restore.

A function's acldefault('f', 10) = {=X/postgres,postgres=X/postgres} grants
EXECUTE to BOTH owner and PUBLIC; PostgreSQL leaves proacl NULL until the first
GRANT/REVOKE. REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC on a never-granted routine
materializes proacl = {postgres=X/postgres}; pg_dump's getFuncs diffs it against
acldefault('f', proowner) and emits REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION
public.revokefn(integer) FROM PUBLIC; (byte-identical to pg_dump 18.3).

Fix (server-only; catalog primitives from slices 340/345 reused):
tryRecordTableRevoke gains function/procedure/routine branches dispatching to
new recordFunctionRevoke, which resolves the OID via the shared
lookupFunctionOID/splitFunctionList, materializes the owner's implicit default
EXECUTE first via MaterializeOwnerACL, then RevokeTablePrivilege per role (PUBLIC
lower-cases to the reserved pseudo-role; a never-granted PUBLIC is an
absent-entry no-op, leaving the owner-only array). ProcACLText renders
{postgres=X/postgres}.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): function-level GRANT (pg_proc.proacl) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 345)
commits.description:
The routine analogue of the table/schema/sequence GRANT slices (331-344).
goopg projected pg_proc.proacl=NULL for every routine, silently dropping
function GRANTs from the dump. A function's acldefault('f',10) =
{=X/postgres,postgres=X/postgres} grants EXECUTE to BOTH owner and PUBLIC, so
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.grantfn(integer) TO func_grantee materializes
proacl = {=X/postgres,postgres=X/postgres,func_grantee=X/postgres}; pg_dump's
getFuncs diffs it against acldefault('f',proowner) and emits
GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION public.grantfn(integer) TO func_grantee; (EXECUTE is the
sole function privilege -> renders ALL).

pg_proc is a VIRTUAL table (unlike heap-backed pg_attribute), so this is a pure
projection - no heap re-sync. Three pieces:
- catalog: functionACLPrivOrder (EXECUTE->X) + ownerFunctionACLString="X" +
  ProcACLText(procOID) reusing the object-type-agnostic relaclTextLockedFor core
  (routines share the OID-keyed tableACLs store; routine OIDs from a disjoint
  FirstRoutineOID=1<<17 range).
- server: recordFunctionGrant (tryRecordTableGrant function/procedure/routine
  branches) resolving the OID via Routines().Lookup with a unique-by-name
  fallback, a paren-aware splitFunctionList, seeding the implicit PUBLIC EXECUTE.
- pg_proc_view.go: project cat.ProcACLText(r.OID) for user routines (built-ins
  stay NULL).

Scope: GRANT only - function REVOKE and WITH GRANT OPTION not modelled.

Verified vs real PostgreSQL 18.3 (postgres/local_install). Tests: new
TestProcACLText (internal/catalog/relacl_test.go) + slice-345 fixture/assert in
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup. Gates: catalog+server+initdb suites +
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup PASS; build clean.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): owner-zero coexisting with a grantee ({grantee=…/postgres}) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 344)
commits.description:
After a full owner-side `REVOKE ALL … FROM postgres` empties relacl to {}, a
subsequent `GRANT SELECT … TO bob` re-materializes the array but PostgreSQL keeps
the owner at zero (absent): relacl = {bob=r/postgres}, not
{postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,bob=r/postgres}. pg_dump diffs that against
acldefault('r', 10) and emits BOTH the owner REVOKE ALL and the grantee GRANT.

goopg previously cleared the relACLEmptied flag on any GRANT and re-inserted the
owner's full default whenever the owner key was absent from a non-empty array, so
it rendered the owner holding its default and pg_dump dropped the REVOKE ALL —
silently restoring the owner's default privileges on restore.

Fix (catalog-only): relACLEmptied is re-interpreted from "the array is {}" to
"the owner explicitly holds zero privileges (absent)", subsuming the {} case.
GrantTablePrivilegeWithGrantOption clears the flag only for an owner-side GRANT;
relaclTextLockedFor suppresses the leading owner entry when the flag is set,
rendering only grantee items. Object-type-agnostic (OID-keyed).

Tests: new TestRevokeAllFromOwnerThenGrantGrantee + slice-344 fixture/assert in
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (both REVOKE ALL and GRANT lines asserted, no
re-grant to the zeroed owner; byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3). Design doc

No new production code: recordTableRevoke (internal/server/grant_ddl.go) already
passes allSequencePrivileges to Catalog.MaterializeOwnerACL for an owner-side ON
SEQUENCE revoke, and the empty-array (relACLEmptied) state plus its
relaclTextLockedSeq rendering are object-type-agnostic. This slice pins the

commits.description:
The schema analogue of slice 341. REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA ownrevall_sch FROM
postgres strips the owner's implicit default schema privileges (USAGE, CREATE)
and leaves pg_namespace.nspacl as a non-NULL empty aclitem array {} (distinct
from the NULL of a never-granted schema). pg_dump's buildACLCommands diffs {}
against acldefault('n', 10) = {postgres=UC/postgres} and emits a bare
`REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA ownrevall_sch FROM postgres;` with NO re-GRANT.

Before this slice recordSchemaRevoke (slice 339) modelled only grantees, so an
owner-side schema revoke found no entry to clear and left nspacl NULL ->
pg_dump emitted nothing, silently restoring the owner's default schema
privileges on restore.

Fix is server-only (the catalog primitives are already object-type-agnostic):
recordSchemaRevoke now mirrors the table path in tryRecordTableRevoke, calling
Catalog.MaterializeOwnerACL(oid, "postgres", allSchemaPrivileges) before the
per-privilege RevokeTablePrivilege when the revoked role is the owner. REVOKE
ALL expands to every schema privilege, empties the materialized owner entry,
and the catalog records nspacl = {} via the shared relACLEmptied empty-array
path (slice 341), rendered for schemas through NamespaceACLText.

RevokeAllFromOwnerEmptyArray/MaterializeOwnerACL + slice-342
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3) PASS;
go build ./... clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): full owner-side REVOKE ALL -> empty relacl array {} round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 341)
commits.description:
PostgreSQL treats a full owner REVOKE distinctly from a partial one (slice 340).
`REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.ownrevall_t FROM postgres` strips every implicit
default privilege and leaves pg_class.relacl as a non-NULL but empty aclitem
array {} (array_length=0, relacl IS NOT NULL) -- distinct from the NULL of a
never-granted table. pg_dump's buildACLCommands diffs {} against acldefault('r',
10) and emits a bare `REVOKE ALL ... FROM postgres;` with no re-GRANT.

Before this slice goopg's RevokeTablePrivilege dropped the owner's now-empty
entry and then the whole relation entry, reverting relacl to NULL -> pg_dump
diffed NULL against acldefault and emitted nothing, silently restoring the
owner's full default privileges on restore.

Fix is catalog-only; server recording is unchanged (the slice-340 owner-revoke
path already calls MaterializeOwnerACL then RevokeTablePrivilege per privilege,
and REVOKE ALL simply expands to every table privilege):
- new field relACLEmptied map[uint32]bool records relations whose ACL array was
  explicitly emptied by an owner REVOKE ALL.
- RevokeTablePrivilege sets the flag when the last remaining aclitem is the
  owner's own entry and it is removed; a trailing grantee revoke keeps the
  slice-338 NULL behaviour.
- relaclTextLockedFor returns "{}" (not "") for an empty byRole when the flag is
  set.
- GrantTablePrivilege / DropTableACL clear the flag; MaterializeOwnerACL
  early-returns when set so a second owner-side REVOKE on an already-empty array
  does not resurrect privileges.

Scope: empty array only. A GRANT to a non-owner role after an owner REVOKE ALL
is {bob=r/postgres} in PG (owner stays absent/zero, pg_dump emits both the
REVOKE ALL and the grantee GRANT); goopg's owner-default fallback renders
{postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,bob=r/postgres} -- modelling a persistent
owner-explicitly-zero entry coexisting with grantees is a follow-up.
schema/sequence owner REVOKE ALL not wired; column-level (attacl) / database
(datacl) projection still open.

Gates: TestRevokeAllFromOwnerEmptyArray (new) + reused Relacl/Revoke/
MaterializeOwnerACL/NamespaceACLText PASS; TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup
DU-002 slice 341 (exact `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.ownrevall_t FROM postgres;`,
no owner re-GRANT; byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3) PASS; go build ./...
clean; pgbench TPC-B smoke = pre-commit hook.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): owner-side REVOKE-of-default (relacl) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 340)
commits.description:
PostgreSQL leaves pg_class.relacl NULL while a relation's owner holds its
implicit default privileges; the first owner-side REVOKE materializes relacl
as the owner default minus the revoked bits. `REVOKE TRIGGER ON TABLE
public.ownrev_t FROM postgres` yields {postgres=arwdDxm/postgres}, and
pg_dump's buildACLCommands diffs that against acldefault('r', relowner) and
re-emits `REVOKE ALL ... FROM postgres;` + `GRANT <surviving> ... TO postgres;`.

goopg's REVOKE recorder modelled only non-owner grantees (the owner is implicit
in the ACL store), so a REVOKE from the owner found no entry and left relacl
NULL -> pg_dump emitted nothing, silently dropping the change on restore.

Fix (server recording + small catalog primitive; pg_dump formats from the
projected relacl text):
- catalog: new MaterializeOwnerACL(relOID, owner, ownerPrivs) records an
  explicit owner aclitem = full default, once (never clobbering a prior revoke);
  renderer relaclTextLockedFor special-cases the owner key via the extracted
  renderACLLetters helper (owner still emitted first).
- server: tryRecordTableRevoke calls MaterializeOwnerACL before
  RevokeTablePrivilege when the grantee is the owner.

Scope: single-privilege owner revoke only (REVOKE ALL from owner -> NULL in
goopg vs PG's empty {} array, a follow-up); schema/sequence owner-revoke unwired
(the primitive is object-type-agnostic).

Gates: TestMaterializeOwnerACL (new) + reused Relacl/Revoke/NamespaceACLText +
slice-340 TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (both REVOKE/GRANT lines exact, no
TRIGGER re-grant; byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3) PASS; build clean.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): GRANT then partial REVOKE (relacl) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 338)
commits.description:
REVOKE was a documented pure no-op, so after GRANT SELECT, INSERT ... TO r
then REVOKE INSERT ... FROM r, the GRANT recorder's r=ar/postgres survived and

- catalog.go: InMemory.RevokeTablePrivilege(relOID, role, priv) clears the bit,

- server/query.go: intercepts single-statement autocommit REVOKE.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): GRANT to a mixed-case quoted role name (relacl case preservation) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 337)
commits.description:
PG role names are case-significant when double-quoted; aclitemout renders the
role's true name in pg_class.relacl (MixedCase=r/postgres, bare because
all-alnum), and pg_dump re-quotes a mixed-case identifier via fmtId -> TO
"MixedCase". goopg's ACL store keys privileges by the lower-cased role name
(case-insensitive HasTablePrivilege/truncate-conflict lookups), so
relaclTextLockedFor rendered `mixedcase` and pg_dump emitted TO mixedcase (a
different, nonexistent role) -- the slice-336 deferred limitation.

Fix (rendering-only, internal/catalog/catalog.go): new field
roleACLDisplay map[lowerRole]originalSpelling, populated in
GrantTablePrivilegeWithGrantOption only when the spelling differs from its
lower-case; relaclTextLockedFor resolves the lower-cased key through it after
the PUBLIC->"" mapping and before aclQuoteName, so mixed-case + special-char
composes ("Weird-Role"=r/postgres). No grant_ddl.go change (handleQuery passes
the raw original-case matchable; splitGrantList trims quotes -> store gets
MixedCase). Zero blast radius: display map consulted only in rendering; lookups
read the lower-cased key (all case variants resolve).

PG's aclitemout/putid double-quotes a grantee whose name has any char outside

via fmtId. Slices 331-335 rendered grantees raw, so a hyphenated role emitted

client-side by pg_dump's fmtId -> already round-trips.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): WHEN-condition trigger round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 329)
commits.description:
A trigger with a WHEN (condition) qualification was silently dropped on dump:
parseCreateTriggerTail recognised WHEN but discarded the body via a paren-balance
token loop. pg_get_triggerdef_worker (ruleutils.c) reads pg_trigger.tgqual and
emits `WHEN (<cond>) ` between FOR EACH and EXECUTE FUNCTION, building old/new
range-table entries + get_rule_expr(varprefix=true) so column refs render with
lowercased old./new. qualifiers; prettyFlags=0 fully parenthesizes the boolean
OpExpr, so `NEW.b <> OLD.b` round-trips as `WHEN ((new.b <> old.b))`.

Dump-fidelity only (the condition is not yet evaluated at trigger-firing time):
- parser ast.go/ddl.go: CreateTriggerStmt.WhenExpr; parseCreateTriggerTail now
  parses `WHEN '(' a_expr ')'` via the standard expression parser. The lexer
  already lowercases the unquoted NEW/OLD qualifier onto each *ColumnRef.
- catalog.go: Trigger.WhenExpr (tgqual projection stays empty — pg_dump drives
  off pg_get_triggerdef, never reads tgqual directly).
- operators_ddl.go: execCreateTrigger copies WhenExpr.
- expr.go: buildTriggerDefString emits the WHEN clause via the executor twin
  defaultExprToSQL (preserves the ColumnRef qualifier + fully parenthesizes binary
  OpExprs, slice 298); the catalog twin formatExprForAttrdef drops the qualifier
  so it was unusable here.

Completes the pg_get_triggerdef getter battery (timing, OR-ed events, UPDATE OF,
CONSTRAINT TRIGGER, REFERENCING, WHEN).

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): per-column operator class round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 312)
commits.description:
A B-tree index column may declare a non-default operator class
(CREATE INDEX ... (a text_pattern_ops)), which selects the comparison
semantics: text_pattern_ops orders by raw byte value (driving LIKE 'pfx%' /
prefix-range scans) vs the default text_ops collation order. PG carries it
through pg_index.indclass and re-emits it in pg_get_indexdef_worker via
get_opclass_name -- after the column/expression (and any COLLATE) and before
ASC/DESC, suppressing the type's default opclass. pg_dump emits
pg_get_indexdef(oid) verbatim so the opclass rides along.

goopg's parseIndexColumnList already CONSUMED the bare opclass ident (to reach
the trailing ASC/DESC/NULLS modifiers) but DISCARDED the name; catalog.Index had
no per-column opclass field and BuildIndexDef emitted none, so
CREATE INDEX ... (a text_pattern_ops) dumped as a plain (a) -- silently widening
the index back to the default opclass on restore (the restored index can no
longer back the prefix-range scans the original supported).

Threaded the opclass parallel to the existing ASC/DESC ordering:
- parser ast.go: new IndexColOrder.OpClass (empty = default opclass).
- parser ddl.go parseIndexColumnList: capture the previously-discarded name into
  order.OpClass.
- catalog.go: Index.ColOpClasses []string (mirrors pg_index.indclass);
  BuildIndexDef emits ' <opclass>' after the column and before ASC/DESC, gated
  on a non-empty entry.
- executor operators_ddl.go: new indexHasOpClass guard ORs into the
  store-non-default-metadata condition; copies ColOrders[i].OpClass.

goopg records only an explicitly-written opclass and emits it unconditionally,
so a non-empty entry is by construction non-default (a plain column stores '' and
emits nothing). The explicit-default edge (user writes text_ops, PG drops it) is
the same one the partition-key opclass path (slice 300) already accepts. Dump-
fidelity only: goopg builds every index with default B-tree comparison regardless
of the declared opclass. Blast radius nil for plain indexes.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): deferred EXCLUDE constraint checking (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED)
commits.description:
The last of the four deferrable constraint kinds. An EXCLUDE constraint declared
DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED (or deferred via SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED) now
tolerates a transient conflict mid-transaction and enforces the constraint at
COMMIT (23P01 exclusion_violation), mirroring deferred-unique one-for-one.

- session.go: deferredExclChecks queue + DeferredExclusionCheck + Add/Take/
  TakeMatching; ExclusionConstraintDeferred wraps the shared constraintDeferredByName.
- deferred_exclusion.go (new): excludeCheckDeferred gates the enqueue at the single
  INSERT chokepoint checkExclusionConstraintsForInsert (queue+continue);
  queueDeferredExclusionCheck captures the WITH = btree key or WITH && box text;
  RunDeferredExclusionChecks drains at COMMIT under FreshSnapshot() with the
  ≥2-live rule (recheckDeferredExclusionEq btree count; recheckDeferredExclusionOverlap
  box-overlap count).
- Wired at all three deferral boundaries after FK+UNIQUE: execCommit, simple-query
  dispatch (shared rollback block, ExecError.Code 23P01 drives wire SQLSTATE),
  SET CONSTRAINTS … IMMEDIATE.
- Gated on idx.IsExclusion && idx.Deferrable -> zero blast radius; no parser/catalog
  change (deferrable flags already populated for exclusion indexes).

Oracle-grounded vs PG 18.3: transient resolved -> COMMIT OK; surviving conflict ->
23P01 "Key (c)=(5) conflicts with existing key (c)=(5)." + rollback; NOT DEFERRABLE
still immediate; SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE. Tests
TestPort_InitiallyDeferredExclusionCommit + TestPort_SetConstraintsExclusionDeferral;
full executor + -race + prior deferred FK/UNIQUE/NND e2e + fk-snapshot PASS.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): deferred UNIQUE with NULLS NOT DISTINCT (NULL-keyed rows)
commits.description:
Composes the deferred-unique queue (loop #20) with NND enforcement
(loops #14-17), which previously did not interoperate. In
checkUniqueIndexes{ForInsert,ForUpdate} the key==nil arm (a NULL key
column on an NND index, found by heap scan not the btree) ran the
immediate checkNullsNotDistinctViaHeapScan raise unconditionally,
never consulting uniqueCheckDeferred — so UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT
DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED wrongly raised 23505 immediately on a
transient NULL duplicate and never queued a COMMIT recheck.

Fix: the NND arm now defers when uniqueCheckDeferred, queuing a
DeferredUniqueCheck carrying the candidate per-key-column NULL pattern
(NNDKeyCols []DeferredNNDKeyCol{ColName,Null,Key}; dedup widened via
sameNNDKeyCols). The immediate scanner's nndKeyCol is lifted to package
scope and its loop extracted to scanNNDLiveMatches(.., stopAt): immediate
stopAt=1 (candidate not yet inserted), recheckDeferredNNDUniqueKey
stopAt=2 (candidate is itself one live match at COMMIT, >=2 = 23505),
both under FreshSnapshot() + isLiveForUniqueCheck.
runAllDeferredUniqueChecks branches on c.NNDKeyCols != nil; SET
CONSTRAINTS .. IMMEDIATE rides the same branch.

Gated on idx.NullsNotDistinct && rowHasNullKeyColumn && uniqueCheckDeferred
=> zero blast radius. Oracle-grounded vs PG 18.3.

Tests: TestPort_InitiallyDeferredNNDUniqueCommit + DeferredNNDMultiColumn
+ SetConstraintsNNDDeferral; full executor + -race + prior deferred
unique/FK e2e PASS. Design 0119-0004-deferred-unique-nnd.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): deferred UNIQUE/PK constraint checking (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED)
commits.description:
A UNIQUE / PRIMARY KEY declared DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED (or deferred via
SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED) now queues its uniqueness check to COMMIT instead of
raising immediately, so a transient duplicate (e.g. UPDATE t SET id = id+1 over a
contiguous range) is tolerated mid-transaction and only the final state is
enforced. Mirrors the deferred-FK machinery one-for-one.

- New internal/executor/deferred_unique.go: uniqueCheckDeferred (analogue of
  fkCheckDeferred, short-circuits on !idx.Deferrable), RunDeferredUniqueChecks
  drains at COMMIT under mvcc.Manager.FreshSnapshot(), recheckDeferredUniqueKey
  RangeScans the backing btree counting distinct live visible heap tuples
  (>=2 = 23505; the candidate row is itself one).
- session.go: deferredUniqChecks queue + Add/Take/TakeMatching (dedup on
  IndexName+Key); per-name/ALL/declared-default resolver extracted to
  constraintDeferredByName, shared by FKConstraintDeferred + UniqueConstraintDeferred.
- Enqueue at checkUniqueIndexes{ForInsert,ForUpdate}. Commit chokepoints:
  execCommit after the FK block; simple-query dispatch.go TxCommit shares one
  rollback block with FK (ExecError Code drives 23503 vs 23505). SET CONSTRAINTS
  … IMMEDIATE drains the matching unique subset.
- Catalog already carried Index.Deferrable/InitiallyDeferred — no parser/catalog
  change. Gated entirely on idx.Deferrable -> zero blast radius (pgbench/TPC-H PK
  not deferrable).

Tests: TestPort_InitiallyDeferredUniqueCommit + TestPort_SetConstraintsUniqueDeferral;
full executor + -race executor/mvcc unique/upsert/conflict + FK-deferral e2e +
TestPort_IsolationFk* regression PASS. Design 0119-0004-deferred-unique.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): deferred-RI fresh-snapshot — drop ConstraintsOverrideActive gate
commits.description:
Plain DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED foreign keys are now enforced at COMMIT on
the simple-query path (psql/lib/pq/isolation runner), which bypasses
transactionOp.execCommit — not only under a SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED override.

The loop-#18 gate existed because running the deferred check unconditionally
raised a spurious 23503 on the fk-snapshot spec: the parent-existence scan used
the transaction's pinned snapshot, which a REPEATABLE READ session cannot use to
see a concurrently-committed (partitioned) parent row. Mirror PG's deferred-RI
machinery (RI_FKey_check/ri_PerformCheck push GetLatestSnapshot):

- new exported mvcc.Manager.FreshSnapshot() wraps captureSnapshot() (latest
  committed state; CLOG + partition-detach epoch already attached);
- runAllDeferredFKChecks saves ctx.Snap, installs the fresh snapshot for the
  queued checks, restores via defer — one chokepoint covering BOTH the execCommit
  and simple-query dispatch paths, so fullTableFKCheck's child-row scan and
  assertParentExists's parent probe both see post-snapshot commits;
- dispatch.go TxCommit drops the `&& sess.ConstraintsOverrideActive()` gate.

Own uncommitted child rows stay visible (TupleVisibleSubxact self-check on
ctx.Tx.XID); own deletes stay hidden (effXmax==selfXID). Zero blast radius on an
empty deferred queue (early return → no snapshot taken; TPC-H/pgbench/IMMEDIATE
constraints untouched).

Tests: TestPort_IsolationFkSnapshot (7 perms) + full FK isolation group PASS; new
TestPort_InitiallyDeferredFKCommit (plain INITIALLY DEFERRED, no override —
ordered commit + raise-at-COMMIT + orphan rollback); TestPort_SetConstraintsDeferral
PASS; -race mvcc(snapshot/commit/visibility)+executor(FK/upsert/conflict) PASS;
internal/server FK/commit units PASS. Design 0119-0004-deferred-ri-fresh-snapshot.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): SET CONSTRAINTS runtime FK-deferral control
commits.description:
Adds SET CONSTRAINTS { ALL | name [, ...] } { DEFERRED | IMMEDIATE }, the
runtime control over FK-deferral timing that was previously swallowed as a wire
no-op. New parser.SetConstraintsStmt -> planner.Utility -> executor
setConstraintsOp; BasicSession deferral state (constraintsAllMode + per-name
map, reset per txn) drives FKConstraintDeferred(name, initiallyDeferred) with PG
precedence (per-name > ALL > declared default). A single fkCheckDeferred(ctx,fk)
helper replaces the four open-coded Deferrable&&InitiallyDeferred&&inTx sites in
operators_fk.go (byte-identical with no override). ... IMMEDIATE runs the
now-immediate queued checks at the SET statement.

The simple-query COMMIT path (which bypasses transactionOp.execCommit) now runs
executor.RunDeferredFKChecks before TxnMgr.Commit, gated on
ConstraintsOverrideActive() so a plain DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint
keeps its prior behaviour (activating the check unconditionally regressed the
pass-required fk-snapshot spec, whose deferred-RI check needs a fresh snapshot to
see a concurrently-committed partitioned parent - a separate pre-existing gap,
ledgered). query.go routes SET CONSTRAINTS to the executor; extended path is a
correctly-tagged no-op; utilityTag returns SET CONSTRAINTS.

set_constraints_test (precedence + TakeDeferredFKChecksMatching), end-to-end
TestPort_SetConstraintsDeferral (control immediate-fail / deferred ordered /
raise-at-COMMIT / raise-at-IMMEDIATE via a pinned *sql.Conn). fk-snapshot + full

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): NULLS NOT DISTINCT ON CONFLICT arbiter on reordered partition leaf
commits.description:
Closes the final NND enforcement sub-feature (c); sub-features (a)-(c) are now
all complete. An INSERT … ON CONFLICT (nndcol) DO UPDATE/NOTHING routing to a
partition leaf whose column order differs from the parent (partLeaf != nil)
skipped the NND heap-scan fallback entirely (`if !conflicted && partLeaf ==
nil`), wrongly INSERTING a duplicate NULL row where PG routes to the conflict
action.

Root cause is a row/column-order mismatch, not missing logic: probeArbiterNND →
checkNullsNotDistinctViaHeapScan / rowHasNullKeyColumn resolve each index key
column by NAME against the passed cols and read the candidate at the matching
ordinal, so cols and the row must share column order. On the partitioned path
cols/writeTbl are already the leaf's, but the loop passed the parent-ordered
`inserted`. Fix: pass `insertedForLeaf` (already remapped to leaf order on the
reordered path; the same slice as `inserted` on every non-reordered path) and
drop the guard. conflictRow is still decoded in leaf order, so the downstream
partLeaf leaf→parent remap is unchanged. Zero blast radius outside NND.

Test TestNullsNotDistinctOnConflictReorderedPartitionLeaf (parent (a,b,c) / leaf
(c,b,a) / NND (a,b); DO NOTHING skip + DO UPDATE target) — confirmed RED before
the fix (duplicate NULL / 2 rows), GREEN after. Design 0119-0004 §10.

Gates: internal/executor NND suite + -race on Upsert/Conflict/NullsNotDistinct/
Partition/Arbiter PASS; TestPort_IsolationInsertConflict*/Merge* PASS; build clean.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): NULLS NOT DISTINCT CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX build over NULL-keyed data
commits.description:
Closes sub-feature (b) of design 0119-0004 (§9). Both index-build paths
(collectBTreeEntries / backfillBTree via encodeCompositeBTreeKey) raised
42804 "column is null and cannot be indexed" on ANY NULL key column,
rejecting CREATE INDEX over any NULL-containing column — a divergence from
PostgreSQL, which admits NULLs in indexes (distinct by default) and only
collides them under NULLS NOT DISTINCT.

encodeCompositeBTreeKey now returns hasNullKey instead of erroring. Default
and non-unique builds SKIP NULL-keyed rows (mirroring the runtime maintain
path — goopg's byte-key btree has no null bitmap), and a
unique && nullsNotDistinct build dedups null-bearing rows among themselves
via a build-local seenNull / nndNullKeyDedupKey map (presence byte 0x00/0x01
+ btree column encoding), raising 23505 on a duplicate NULL pattern. The
dedup key is never stored in the btree, so the design's "no sentinel keys in
stored/scanned keys" constraint is unaffected.

The NullsNotDistinct flag is set on the catalog index after createBTreeIndex
builds it, so it is now threaded as a new nullsNotDistinct parameter through
createBTreeIndex -> bulkBuildBTree[WithPredicate] -> collectBTreeEntries /
backfillBTree. All 16 createBTreeIndex call sites pass it: the five
NND-capable constraint/index forms forward the real flag, PK and non-unique
forms pass false; the matview-rebuild bulkBuildBTree forwards
idx.NullsNotDistinct.

Zero blast radius for default indexes: nullsNotDistinct == false changes the
build only in that a NULL-keyed row is skipped instead of erroring (a strict
improvement); no non-NULL row's key bytes or storage change, seenNull is nil.

Tests: 4 new build-path tests in nulls_not_distinct_test.go. Full
internal/executor suite + -race on Unique/Index/NullsNotDistinct/Upsert/
Conflict/DDL/Partition PASS.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): NULLS NOT DISTINCT ON CONFLICT/upsert arbiter enforcement
commits.description:
A NULL-keyed INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (nndcol) DO UPDATE/NOTHING against a
NULLS NOT DISTINCT arbiter index was inserting a duplicate instead of
routing to the conflict action: encodeArbiterKey returns a nil key on a
NULL conflict-key column (NULLs distinct by default), so the btree probe
saw conflicted=false.

- New probeArbiterNND (operators_upsert.go) reuses the plain-path matcher
  checkNullsNotDistinctViaHeapScan and decodes the conflicting tuple; the
  upsert Next loop falls back to it after probeArbiterWaiting on the
  non-reordered path (partLeaf == nil), so DO NOTHING skips and DO UPDATE
  targets the existing NULL row.
- indexKeyColumnsChanged made NND-aware (new nndKeyColumnsEqual,
  operators_storage.go): a NULL->NULL no-key-change DO UPDATE now skips the
  uniqueness probe so it doesn't self-conflict with the not-yet-stamped old
  tuple (the upsert checks before applyUpdate, unlike plain UPDATE).

Gated entirely behind idx.NullsNotDistinct -> zero blast radius for every
non-NND index. Closes sub-feature (a) of the loop-#14 ledger row; design
0119-0004 section 8.

Tests: 3 new in nulls_not_distinct_test.go (DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE / NULLS
DISTINCT control); full internal/executor suite + -race PASS;
TestPort_IsolationInsertConflict*/Merge* PASS.

commits.title: feat(M0119-0004): NULLS NOT DISTINCT uniqueness enforcement at INSERT/UPDATE
commits.description:
Closes the long-deferred enforcement half of NULLS NOT DISTINCT (the
dump-fidelity/catalog layer landed in M0110-0001 slices 134-138; the flag
was dumped but never honoured at runtime). Two NULLs on an NND-unique
index must collide (23505); goopg's encodeIndexKeyFromCols returns a nil
btree key on any NULL key column, so NULL rows were neither indexed nor
checked.

Fix (design 0119-0004, agent-reviewed before impl): checkUniqueIndexes
ForInsert/ForUpdate fall back to checkNullsNotDistinctViaHeapScan when the
nil-key reason is a genuine NULL key column on an idx.NullsNotDistinct
index. The heap scan (mirroring checkGistOverlapExclusion) reports a
conflict when a live tuple matches the candidate's NULL pattern AND
non-NULL values (non-NULL columns compared byte-equal under
encodeBTreeKeyForColumn). btree, all scan-probe builders, and the codec
are left untouched: probe paths never build a NULL key, so equality/range
SELECTs on an NND index are byte-identical. UPDATE self-conflict is
prevented by the existing stamp-old-xmax-before-check ordering. New
nndDetail renders a NULL key column as `null` (PG: `Key (a)=(null)`).

Blast radius nil outside NND: catalog.Index.NullsNotDistinct defaults
false; the branch is dead code for every existing index and for any
non-NULL reason a key is nil.

Deferred (ledger 2026-06-29): ON CONFLICT/upsert arbiter (encodeArbiterKey
ignores the flag -> a NULL-keyed upsert mis-inserts a duplicate; the
helper already returns the conflicting ItemPointer for the follow-up),
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX build over NULL-keyed data (pre-existing 42804), and
COPY/apply-worker (intentionally skip the check).

Tests: internal/executor/nulls_not_distinct_test.go (single/multi-col
enforcement, NULLS-DISTINCT control admits duplicate NULLs, NULL->NULL
no-key-change UPDATE no self-conflict). Full executor suite + -race on the
unique/upsert family PASS; go build clean.

commits.title: feat(M0117-0006): wire transaction_buffers GUC into live CLOG SLRU pool sizing
commits.description:
Part B follow-up. SetCLOGBuffers existed but was never called from production,
so the transaction_buffers GUC was dead-ended and the live CLOG SLRU pool
always auto-tuned to the 16-page bank floor regardless of postgresql.conf.

Thread the value through: new OpenOptions.TransactionBuffers field; Open()
calls clog.SetCLOGBuffers(opts.TransactionBuffers) immediately before
EnablePGSLRUMirror (a no-op once the pool exists); cmd/goopg start reads the
GUC via intGUC and passes it in. Boot default 0 keeps the auto-16 floor, so
behaviour is byte-identical for every default deployment; a non-zero override
now actually sizes the live pool instead of being silently dropped.

Regression: TestTransactionBuffersFromGUC (+ nil-registry) pins the GUC read;
TestSetCLOGBuffersSizesPool pins SetCLOGBuffers -> pool.nslots =
EffectiveCLOGBuffers(n,0) (auto floor / explicit 128 / below-floor clamp 16).

commits.title: feat(M0117-0006): Part B — SLRU buffer pool is the live CLOG store
commits.description:
Wire clogBufferPool (Part A) in as the live in-memory commit-log store,
replacing the fully-resident per-XID banks on every production path. The
pool faults bounded BLCKSZ pages from pg_xact/ on demand (16x denser, memory
bounded by transaction_buffers) instead of holding one byte per XID.

- CLog.pool atomic.Pointer, promoted by EnablePGSLRUMirror AFTER the
  flat-file->SLRU backfill so it faults from a complete pg_xact/ directory.
- GetStatus->pool.getStatus; setStatus->pool.setStatus (PG clear-then-set;
  bootstrap XIDs <FirstNormal kept zero for basebackup byte-equality);
  applyGroupBatchLocked->pool.flushDirty replaces flushDirtyPagesLocked +
  mirrorGroupToSLRULocked (one fsync per touched segment).
- Bulk callers re-pointed (all run after EnablePGSLRUMirror in initdb.Open):
  InitializeAsCommitted/MarkUnknownAsAborted sweep via pool + one flushDirty
  (M0117-0004 Unknown->Aborted guard preserved); HighestKnownXID via new
  highestSLRUXID() SLRU tail scan; TruncateCLOG via new pool.invalidateBelow.
- Legacy never-fsynced global/pg_xact flat file retired: SLRU is the single
  durable store (basebackup already excluded it; PG has no such file).
  OpenCLog tolerates its absence; loadFromSLRU repopulates from the SLRU.
- Single-store design resolves the M0117-0004 dual-store hazard (no second
  store to disagree, so clear-then-set is correct). flushWAL barrier left nil
  (synchronous commit; async = M0117-0007 Part B). Pool auto-sized (16 pages).

The "gates SKIP in the autonomous WSL2 loop" deferral reason on record across
loops #7-#10 was empirically disproven: standby-attach + checksum-streaming
E2E, -race mvcc/wal (incl xlog_replay), and the TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=33 spot-check
all RUN and PASS here. Part C (remove the resident banks) remains deferred.

TestE2E_ChecksumStreamingGoopgToPG; TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=33 spot-check PASS;

commits.title: fix(M0117/0117-0010): TPC-H spot-check data-target fallback (gate now runs, not SKIPs)
commits.description:
The mandated executor/planner pre-commit gate scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh
silently SKIPped on a fully-loaded 2.2GB data dir even after 0117-0009
cleared the startup fsync storm. Root cause: the gate probed the
user=tpch/db=tpch HammerDB load identity, but goopg registers CREATE
ROLE/USER + CREATE DATABASE in-memory only (internal/server/role_ddl.go),
so the tpch role/db do not survive the gate's fresh restart. The loaded
tables persist in the postgres database (lineitem = 5,999,786). The
`role "tpch" does not exist` probe matched the table-missing SKIP
heuristic, masking the loaded data dir.

Fix (script-only, nil engine blast radius): probe the configured tpch
target first, and on a (role|database) does-not-exist error fall back to
superuser@postgres and re-probe; run Q12/Q13 against the resolved target.

Verified end-to-end: fresh start -> postgres@postgres -> Q12=2, Q13=33,
RESULT=PASS (matches spotcheck_expected.env; confirms HEAD has no
row-count regression). With 0117-0009 + 0117-0010 the populated-data
Q12/Q13 gate is now demonstrably runnable.

Design 0117-0010 + README index; fix_plan M0117 enabler note (corrects
0117-0009's "reload role" note -- data was never lost, only mis-probed).

commits.title: fix(M0117/0117-0009): batched CLOG→SLRU startup backfill (clears spot-check infra-hang)
commits.description:
EnablePGSLRUMirror's startup backfill projected the resident commit-status
banks into the pg_xact/ SLRU by calling mirrorToSLRUUnlocked once per
committed/aborted XID — each an open+ReadAt+WriteAt+f.Sync()+Close cycle, i.e.
~NextXID fsyncs. On the 6M-row bench data dir (~1.5M XIDs) on WSL2's slow fsync
this took >6 min (stuck on segment 0000), so the server never reached
scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh's 60s readiness window and the mandated
executor/planner gate infra-FAILED. That was the sole reason loops #7/#8
reported BLOCKED and deferred the entire M0117 CLOG live-path tail.

The per-XID f.Sync() is the live per-commit durability barrier; the backfill
does not need it (a one-shot re-projection of in-memory state re-derived from
the flat file on every start — a crash mid-backfill just re-runs it). Route the
backfill through the existing batched mirrorTerminalRangeBatchedUnlocked (added
by M0110-0004 for the byte-identical pg_resetwal sweep): it builds each
segment's page buffer in memory (read-first + strict-OR per XID via GetStatus,
identical lane arithmetic) and fsyncs once per segment — ~1.5M fsyncs collapse

formed write-side). ALTER INDEX ... SET (fastupdate=...) now parses (new

commits.title: fix(M0118-0008): BEGIN; LOCK in one simple-query message is txn-scoped (design 0118-0134)
commits.description:
Restores two pass-required isolation specs, vacuum-concurrent-drop and
vacuum-skip-locked, which had been silently RED since commit d1f40e28
(async-notify, design 0118-0090). Found by git-bisecting
TestPort_IsolationVacuumConcurrentDrop.

Both specs define their lock step as one two-statement step
{ BEGIN; LOCK part1 IN SHARE MODE; }. The async-notify loop changed the
isolation runner to send a multi-statement step as ONE simple-query message
(execMultiStatement, needed for NOTIFY de-dup / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT discard).
That exposed a latent server bug: dispatchSimpleQueryViaExecutor seeds
ectx.TxnLockBackendID ONCE before the per-statement loop from the message-entry
transaction state -- autocommit for "BEGIN; LOCK ..." -- so when LOCK runs later
in the same loop it sees TxnLockBackendID==0 and acquireRelLockTxn degrades to a
display-only no-op. No real ShareLock is taken, so the concurrent ANALYZE/VACUUM
never <waiting>-blocks and the post-wait drop re-check + "relation no longer
exists" WARNING never fire.

Fix: refresh ectx.TxnLockBackendID at the top of the statement loop from the
live connTx.InExplicit() state, so a transaction-scoped lock that follows a
BEGIN in the same PQexec message is held to commit -- matching upstream
exec_simple_query (one PQexec = one transaction command list). Blast radius
confined to multi-statement messages that change transaction state mid-message.

Gates: strict TestPort_IsolationVacuumConcurrentDrop + VacuumSkipLocked PASS
(were red at HEAD); full TestPort_Isolation* suite PASS (657s, no regression);
gofmt/vet clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): stats PROMOTED — isolation-runner connection reuse (design 0118-0133)
commits.description:

pass-required. Not a pgstat change — every pgstat subsystem the spec exercises
landed in 0118-0123..0132. The last blocker (L3732) was in the isolation
runner itself.

Upstream isolationtester.c opens one connection per session ONCE (in main) and
reuses it for every permutation, so a session GUC set by a step (here SET
track_functions='all') persists forward. stats.spec's final permutations read
pg_stat_get_function_calls after s2_func_call WITHOUT re-setting
track_functions, relying on that persistence. goopg's runPermutation opened
fresh per-session connections each permutation -> boot default
track_functions='none' -> the call was untracked -> NULL not 1.

Fix hoists per-session connection creation from permutation scope to spec scope:
- new sessionConns + (*IsolationRunner).openSessionConns build the per-session
  notice/notify queues, *sql.DB handles, *sql.Conn, pid->session map ONCE per
  spec in RunSpec (SET application_name + backend-PID record done once, stable).
- runPermutation no longer opens/closes connections; it still runs each
  session's setup SQL every permutation (re-applies SET
  stats_fetch_consistency='none') but never resets the connection, so step-set
  GUCs persist exactly as upstream.
- sc.drainQueues() clears transient message queues per permutation (monotonic
  notice total kept — notices <n> blockers are delta-vs-baseline).
- post-permutation sc.healthy() rebuilds the set if a timed-out step left a
  connection busy; close() is 3s-bounded against a stuck lib/pq read.

TestPort_IsolationStats flipped to runIsoSpecStrict (PASS byte-for-byte all
permutations). CSV D-002 rationale updated + md regenerated. Full
TestPort_Isolation* strict suite re-run (4 parallel batches): zero regressions
from connection reuse — vacuum-skip-locked/vacuum-concurrent-drop fail
identically at HEAD (pre-existing SKIP_LOCKED WARNING gap),
tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock is a load-induced flake (passes solo).

commits.description:

transactional, mirroring PgStat_TableXactStatus / AtEOXact_PgStat_Relations.
A new staging tier sits in front of the per-session pending counters: DML

no-op; attempted tuples_* always count). TRUNCATE rides a truncDropped flag
through pending into shared at flush, forgetting prior live/dead counts. 2PC
moves staging into a per-gid record at the detached PREPARE and folds it into
the finalising backend's pending at COMMIT/ROLLBACK PREPARED. Scan counters
stay non-transactional.

abort/ROLLBACK PREPARED, TRUNCATE-in-2PC, and cross-backend COMMIT/ROLLBACK
PREPARED table-stats permutation matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte. Spec stays
defer (SLRU stats is the final rung).

commits.title: fix(M0118-0130): btree recycled-page zero-initialization race
commits.description:
Fixes intermittent 'btree: item length mismatch keyLen=9 total=37'
error under concurrent pgbench TPC-B load.

Root cause: pinNewOrRecycled zeroed recycled page bytes WITHOUT
holding the page content lock. A concurrent reader could observe a
partially-zeroed posting-list item where the BTPostingFlag (0x8000)
high bit was cleared while the 37-byte payload remained intact,
causing isPostingRaw→false→parseItem rejection.

Fix: wrap the zeroing loop with slot.Lock()/slot.Unlock() so the
page is atomically visible only after full zero-initialization.

commits.title: fix(M0118-0129): HOT update corruption fix — infomask flags + orphan cleanup
commits.description:
Fixes three root-cause bugs identified via PG18 source comparison:

**Bug A — Missing HEAP_HASVARWIDTH (0x0002):** tryApplyHOTUpdate and
writeHeapRowReturning never stamped the bit; PG's heap_fill_tuple sets it
automatically for varlena columns (heaptuple.c:326). Without it, PG18
standby nocachegetattr crashes. The pgRowHasVarWidth helper existed but
was only wired in the PG-canonical writeHeapRowReturningPG.

**Bug B — Missing HEAP_HASEXTERNAL (0x0004):** The constant did not exist
in goopg. PG's heap_fill_tuple stamps it for TOAST-external columns
(heaptuple.c:343). Added HeapHasExternal + pgRowHasExternal helper.
Wired across all three write paths.

**Bug C — Orphan HEAP_ONLY_TUPLE on stamp failure:** When PageAddHeapTuple
succeeded but PageStampHotOldTuple failed (e.g. PagePruneOpt invalidated
the old slot), the new tuple persisted as a live orphan with no CTID link
or index entry. Added PageRemoveHeapTuple for best-effort cleanup.

Design doc: docs/design/0118-0129-hot-update-corruption-fix.md

./internal/server/... PASS; full pre-commit unit suite PASS.

commits.title: fix: make index-scan decode errors non-fatal (skip tuple)
commits.description:
The index-scan and update-via-index decode paths propagated transient
tuple-decode errors as hard query errors, aborting the transaction.
All other scan paths (scanMatching, seqScanOp, EPQ, FK recheck,
lockrows) already silently skip undecodable tuples.

Under concurrent pgbench TPC-B load, a HOT update chain can produce a
tuple whose filler column appears truncated ('DecodePhysicalPGRow:
filler: truncated 4-byte varlena header'), causing the transaction to
abort and subsequent commands to fail with 25P02 ('current transaction
is aborted').

Fix: return continue/skip-tuple in updateViaIndex and indexScanOp.Next
decode-error paths, consistent with scanMatching.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): intra-grant-inplace enabler — perm 9 (plpgsql REVOKE + rowmark awaits ACL xmax, design 0118-0116)
commits.description:

(first divergence L206 -> L235, now perm 10). Enabler, NOT a promotion —

Two gaps closed for perm 9 (b1 grant1 b3 sfu3 revoke4 c1 r3):

1. plpgsql body parser rejected a bare REVOKE inside revoke4's DO $$ ... $$
   block. GRANT/REVOKE are not reserved keywords (the SQL lexer keeps them as
   plain identifiers), so a leading REVOKE fell through to parseAssign and
   failed with "expected ':=' or '=' after revoke" BEFORE the EXCEPTION WHEN
   others handler could run, so goopg emitted an ERROR PG never raises. Added a
   leading grant/revoke-ident case to bodyParser.parseStmt routing to
   parseSQLStmt like the other embedded SQL statements (general fix: GRANT/REVOKE
   work in any plpgsql function/DO body now). Unit TestParseGrantRevokeEmbeddedSQL.

2. sfu3's pg_class rowmark (SELECT relhasindex FROM pg_class ... FOR UPDATE)
   completed immediately instead of <waiting ...> behind grant1's uncommitted
   ACL change. Refactored ddlOp.waitForTableACLChange into the free function
   waitTableACLChange(ctx, tableOID); lockRowsOp.maybeRecordPgClassRowMark now
   records the rowmark FIRST (so a peer GRANT/REVOKE blocks behind it via
   waitForPgClassRowMarks) THEN awaits the table's ACL xmax, mirroring PG's
   acquire-LockTuple-then-await-tuple-xmax order. Method returns *ExecError
   propagated by drainAndStamp.

is pg_class with an oid=<const> filter; ordinary SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on user
tables is byte-unchanged, and with no pending ACL change the wait is an

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): intra-grant-inplace enabler — deadlock victim releases its XID in place (perm 8 ordering, design 0118-0115)
commits.description:
Enabler, NOT a promotion. Closes the last perm-8 divergence left by 0118-0114
(a completion-order swap). PG's AbortTransaction releases the deadlock victim's
XID the instant the deadlock is reported, so the winner (grant1, blocked on the
victim's sfnku2 rowmark xmax) unblocks at the abort, before the victim's explicit
c2 COMMIT; goopg kept the victim's XID active until that COMMIT.

Fix releases the victim's XID in place via mvcc.Manager.ReleaseXIDWaiters: the
shared liveness predicate xidActiveWithSubxact returns false for a released XID
(and its top parent) WITHOUT clearing the proc-array slot, so snapshot visibility
still reads the still-open slot/CLOG (correct — the victim is write-less). The
explicit c2 then finalises the empty txn through the canonical commit path. Wired
via Context.DeadlockVictim (set only in waitPgClassInplaceXID on cycle detection)
to a dispatch failure-path AbortInPlaceOnFail call gated on DeadlockVictim +
SavepointDepth()==0, confining the change to the pg_class in-place deadlock path.

Result: perms 1-8 byte-identical; first divergence advanced L184 to L206. Spec
stays defer (perm 9 = DO-body REVOKE the plpgsql parser rejects; perm 10 =
DELETE FROM pg_class virtual-catalog tuple delete).

NO KEY UPDATE|SHARE|UPDATE}` takes a tuple lock that ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): prepared-transactions PROMOTED — SSI dangerous-structure check at PREPARE TRANSACTION (design 0118-0112)
commits.description:
prepared-transactions.spec drives an s1 --rw--> s2 --rw--> s3 dangerous
structure under two-phase commit across all 1500 permutations; exactly one
of the three SERIALIZABLE xacts must abort with 40001 in each. Building on
the same-backend 2PC enabler (0118-0110), goopg now runs the SSI
dangerous-structure check at PREPARE TRANSACTION time and treats a
PREPARED-but-not-committed peer like an already-committed one.

SSI substrate (internal/mvcc):
- SerializableXact.Prepared / PrepareSeqNo mirror SXACT_FLAG_PREPARED /
  prepareSeqNo; set only on the PREPARE path (a normal COMMIT is gated out
  by FinishedAt), so the 100+ non-2PC specs are byte-unchanged.
- Manager.PrepareCheckForSerializationFailure runs the pre-commit scan and
  on success stamps Prepared/PrepareSeqNo.
- preCommitCheckForSerializationFailureLocked: when the pivot is Prepared it
  cannot be doomed (durable, may yet COMMIT PREPARED), so the
  preparer/committer commits suicide (40001).
- onConflictCheckLocked: additive prepared branches in Cases 2/3 (compared
  against PrepareSeqNo); the reader is doomed when the writer is committed
  OR prepared. All new branches guarded by Prepared.

Server (internal/server):
- execPrepareTransaction runs the SSI check for a SERIALIZABLE txn and on
  failure aborts via the canonical rollback path + reports 40001 (later
  COMMIT PREPARED then reports "does not exist").
- PREPARE on an aborted block silently rolls back (no 25P02), matching
  PrepareTransactionBlock on TBLOCK_ABORT; dispatch failed-txn guard lets
  isTwoPhaseStmt through.

Blast radius nil for non-2PC: with no prepared xact the SSI code reduces to
the prior committed-only logic.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): intra-grant-inplace enabler — ADD PRIMARY KEY waits on concurrent GRANT (design 0118-0109)
commits.description:
Permutation 1 of intra-grant-inplace.spec now byte-identical (first divergence
L17->L62). ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY does an in-place relhasindex=true update on
the pg_class tuple; PG takes no heavyweight lock for a concurrent uncommitted
GRANT SELECT ON <table> -- its lock IS the catalog tuple xmax -- so ADD PRIMARY
KEY must <waiting ...> behind the GRANT and resume on COMMIT. goopg served the
GRANT as a CompatNoopStmt and ran ADD PRIMARY KEY immediately.

Replays the xmax wait (pg_class sibling of 0118-0098's pg_database case):
- parser resolves a table-target GRANT/REVOKE into CompatNoopStmt.TableACL
  (grantObjectName / grantNonTableClass; default object class is TABLE)
- execCompatNoop records the writer XID keyed by table OID
  (InMemory.SetTableACLChangeXID, mutex-guarded map[oid]xid)
- execAlterTableAddPrimaryKey calls waitForTableACLChange -> mvcc.WaitForXID
  before building the PK index

NOT a promotion -- perms 3,4,7-11 still need real pg_class rowmark locking
(FOR NO KEY UPDATE/FOR UPDATE/FOR KEY SHARE + DELETE FROM pg_class on a virtual
catalog row + LockTuple deadlock detection), the Effort-L runtime shared-catalog
MVCC-tuple-lock core. Spec stays defer.
