commits.title: feat(M0118-0002): VACUUM (TRUNCATE ...) option parse — index-only-bitmapscan enabler (design 0118-0108)
commits.description:
VACUUM (TRUNCATE false) <tbl> (documented PG syntax) was rejected with
'unrecognised VACUUM option (got truncate)'. The parenthesised VACUUM
option loop had a truncate case but matched only via acceptIdentKeyword,
while TRUNCATE lexes as the unreserved keyword KwTruncate (it also leads
TRUNCATE TABLE), so the case never fired and parsing hit the default
error. Accept the keyword token too. TRUNCATE is the only VACUUM option
word that is also a SQL keyword, so no other option is affected.

NoTruncate is recorded for parity; vacuumCore never physically truncates
trailing empty pages, so TRUNCATE false/true are behavioral no-ops today.

Enabler, NOT a promotion: clears the index-only-bitmapscan.spec s2_vacuum
divergence; the spec stays deferred behind EXPLAIN-over-DECLARE-CURSOR and
the BitmapOr plan (both Effort-L).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): timeouts.spec PROMOTED — statement/lock timeout parity (design 0118-0107)

statement_timeout/lock_timeout against table-level (LOCK TABLE) and row-level
(DELETE behind a concurrent UPDATE) lock waits; whichever timeout is shorter
fires first, canceling with 57014 (statement timeout) or 55P03 (lock timeout).
Blocked steps are (*)-marked upstream because the 10ms timeout may fire before
the isolation tester observes "waiting"; goopg's runner already honours (*).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0007): eval-plan-qual.spec PROMOTED — EPQ recheck over a join (design 0118-0106)
commits.description:
Closes the M0118-0007 planner/output-format group: eval-plan-qual now
strict-passes all 50 permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3.

The last divergence was selectresultforupdate — SELECT ... FOR UPDATE OF jt
over a join whose locked jt is the inner index scan. goopg folds the index
key condition into the per-row EvalPlanQual recheck, but the key `jt.id = y`
references another join input's column whose ColumnRef.Index lives in the
join coordinate space; epqRecheckFilter decodes only the locked table's own
columns, so y(idx 1) was misread as jointest.data -> jt.id=jt.data -> false
-> the post-update row was wrongly dropped (0 rows). Fix: fold the index key
into the recheck ONLY when ix.Key is row-local/constant (new

commits.title: feat(M0118-0005): fk-deadlock.spec PROMOTED — FK existence scan made FOR KEY SHARE-aware (design 0118-0094)
commits.description:
A child INSERT's FK check is the equivalent of SELECT … FOR KEY SHARE on the
referenced parent row. FOR KEY SHARE conflicts ONLY with a key-changing
modification (key UPDATE / DELETE) and is COMPATIBLE with a concurrent no-key
UPDATE. scanRelForFKMatch treated ANY in-flight non-self non-lock-only xmax as a
conflict and made the caller WaitForXID, so a child INSERT blocked behind a peer's
still-in-flight no-key parent UPDATE where PG proceeds — a sibling-paths gap vs
lockRowsOp, which already keys its wait on keysUpdated.

Fix makes the FK scan key-aware via two helpers:
  - fkXmaxIsKeyChanging (single-xid): HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED set OR a
    structurally-detected DELETE (self-pointing/invalid t_ctid — the chainMembers
    test, since goopg omits HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED on DELETE).
  - multixactUpdaterIsKeyChanging: updater member StatusUpdate vs StatusNoKeyUpdate.
A no-key updater is now a clean FK match (no wait); a key UPDATE/DELETE still
records pending and waits + re-scans (23503 / moved-partition paths unchanged).
Only blocking left is the two parent no-key UPDATEs serialising via the existing
UPDATE-conflict path. Bounded: the change only NARROWS the FK wait.

permutations byte-identical to PG 18.3). Gates: FK siblings + row-lock/deadlock/
multixact isolation batch PASS no regression; -race executor + executor/multixact/
mvcc unit suites PASS; go build ./... clean; D-002 CSV + status md regenerated.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): REINDEX CONCURRENTLY pg_toast.<name> routing (TOAST-exposure slice 5, design 0118-0088)
commits.description:
Promotes reindex-concurrently-toast to strict — the LAST unpromoted spec of the
M0118-0008 isolation group; the full 25-spec group now passes strict.

REINDEX {TABLE,INDEX} CONCURRENTLY on a pg_toast.<name> relation/index waits for
lockers of the TOAST relation (not the parent table): a transaction locks the
toast rel only when it toasts a value (DML write) or drops the table, never on a
bare parent LOCK TABLE — so lrex1+ins1 waits while lrex1-alone does not.

- catalog: ToastRelFileNode(parentRel) (synthetic toast lock node) +
  ToastParentTable(toastOID).
- acquireWriteLockTxn also RowExclusive-locks the toast rel after the parent;
  dropTableByRef AccessExclusive-locks it. Confined to toast-bearing user tables;
  observed only by the toast REINDEX wait (RowExclusiveLock is self-compatible).
- reindexOp resolves a pg_toast target via LookupToastRel, waits on the toast
  relation's lockers for both object types, then re-checks existence so a
  DROP-committed parent yields relation "pg_toast.<name>" does not exist (42P01).

byte-identical); sibling concurrency/DDL specs strict, no regression; toast slice
tests PASS; go build + gofmt clean; -race lockmgr; D-002 CSV + status md regen;

2. The ALTER INDEX parser had no RENAME arm and fell into its no-op branch with an

commits.description:

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): alter-table-4 PROMOTED — post-lock inherited-column type re-validation (design 0118-0082)
commits.description:
Closes the alter-table-4 isolation spec — all 4 permutations byte-for-byte vs
PG 18.3 via strict TestPort_IsolationAlterTable4, on top of enablers 0118-0080
(perms 1&2) and 0118-0081 (perm 3).

Perm 4 (s1b s1delc1 s1modc1a s2sel s1c s2sel) runs ALTER TABLE c1 ALTER COLUMN a
TYPE float on the inheritance child while a concurrent SELECT SUM(a) FROM p waits
on c1's lock; once s1 commits, PostgreSQL's make_inh_translation_list
(optimizer/util/appendinfo.c) re-matches each parent attribute to the child by
name and raises "attribute \"a\" of relation \"c1\" does not match parent's type"
(ERRCODE_INVALID_COLUMN_DEFINITION, 42611) because a is now float on c1 but
integer on p.

goopg mutates c1's type in the shared catalog immediately (execAlterColumnType),
and the post-lock child scan from 0118-0081 only skipped a *vanished* child — it
never re-checked column types — so s2sel scanned the detached c1 and returned
sum 1 instead of erroring (first divergence at spec L65).

Fix: new planner.SeqScan.InheritParentOID (set beside SkipIfVanished on every
inheritance-child scan in the allDesc expansion loop) drives a post-lock check in
seqScanOp.Open — validateInheritedColumnTypes mirrors make_inh_translation_list:
match each non-dropped parent column to the child by name and compare canonical
type class via new canonicalTypeClass (collapses integer/int4 and double
precision/float8/float, resolves domains, folds in IsArray, deliberately ignores
typmod args so only a genuine base-type change trips it → zero false positives on
legitimate inheritance scans), returning the 42611 error with the parent attr
name + child rel name on mismatch. Runs only for inheritance-child scans (the
skipIfVanished marker) with a non-zero parent OID, AFTER the lock (so the error
appears post-<... completed>, not reordering <waiting ...>); partition leaves
(LockParentOID) and direct scans untouched.

Gates: TestPort_IsolationAlterTable4 strict PASS (4 perms); no regression across
AlterTable1/AlterTable3/InheritTemp strict + full go test
./internal/{executor,planner,catalog}/; go build ./... + gofmt clean; pgbench
smoke = pre-commit hook.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): DROP TABLE defers catalog removal to COMMIT + inheritance-child skip-if-vanished — alter-table-4 perm 3 enabler (design 0118-0081)
feat(M0118-0008): ALTER TABLE {NO} INHERIT defers catalog mutation to COMMIT + child lock — alter-table-4 perms 1&2 enabler (design 0118-0080)
feat(M0118-0008): partition-concurrent-attach PROMOTED — INSERT routing-path locks + fresh-snapshot ATTACH re-scan (design 0118-0079)
commits.description:
All 3 permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3 via runIsoSpecStrict, closing the
spec on top of enablers 0118-0075..0078. Two final gaps:

Gap 1 (INSERT routing-path lock, perms 1 & 3): PG ExecInsert opens every
partition a tuple is routed into in RowExclusiveLock; goopg locked only the
named INSERT target (tpart) and nothing along the routing path, so an
INSERT INTO tpart routing through the intermediate DEFAULT tpart_default never
contended with a concurrent ATTACH's AccessExclusiveLock (0118-0076) on that
default. New lockRoutingPathPartitions walks the parent chain from the routed
leaf up to (excluding) the named target and RowExclusive-locks each
intermediate partition via acquireWriteLockTxn, wired into insertOp.Next right
after routing resolves the leaf — perm 1's INSERT waits behind the ATTACH then
re-routes onto the now-visible tpart_2 (23514); perm 3's INSERT holds the lock
to commit so the ATTACH acquire waits. RowExclusive is self-compatible/DML-grade
so concurrent partitioned INSERTs never block each other; single-level
partitioned and non-partitioned INSERTs are a no-op.

Gap 2 (fresh snapshot for the ATTACH re-scan, perm 3): checkDefaultPartitionDataConflict
now refreshes synthCtx.Snap = TxnMgr.SnapshotFor(ctx.Tx) before scanning
(mirrors detach-4 0118-0064) because the attaching statement's snapshot predates
the lock wait and could not see the concurrent INSERT's just-committed rows —
perm 3's ATTACH now finds them and raises 23P01 naming the leaf default
tpart_default_default.

Gates: strict PASS (3 perms); 14 partition/DDL strict siblings PASS single run
(DetachPartitionConcurrently1/2/3/4 + AlterTable1/2/3 + CreateTrigger +
InheritTemp + TruncateConflict + ClusterConflict{,Partition} + VacuumConflict);
go test ./internal/executor/ + -race partition/insert paths; go build ./...
clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): INSERT enforces DEFAULT partition constraint — partition-concurrent-attach enabler (design 0118-0078)
commits.description:
Reconstruct PG's implicit default-partition constraint at INSERT time: a row
routed to (or directly inserted into) a DEFAULT partition is rejected with 23514
when its parent partition-key value is owned by a non-default sibling. New
checkDefaultPartitionInsertConstraint walks the target's PartitionParentOID
ancestry and re-routes the parent key one level per default ancestor; wired at
both heap-write sites in insertOp.Next. Reads the live catalog after the INSERT's
RowExclusiveLock is granted (the 0118-0076/0077 wait), so it sees a just-committed
concurrent ATTACH — PG's route-pre-commit/check-post-commit. partition-concurrent-
attach permutation 2 now matches PG byte-for-byte; spec stays defer (perms 1/3
need INSERT routing-path locks).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): ATTACH PARTITION defers catalog registration to COMMIT — partition-concurrent-attach enabler (design 0118-0077)
commits.description:
Mirrors the 0118-0074 DROP INDEX deferral (opposite direction: keep the new
partition INVISIBLE until commit). A non-default ALTER TABLE … ATTACH PARTITION
issued inside an explicit transaction now records a BasicSession pending entry
instead of registering the child synchronously; ApplyPendingPartitionAttaches
does the real RegisterPartitionChild + PartitionBounds at COMMIT, invoked before
TxnMgr.Commit on both commit paths (executor execCommit + server dispatch
TxCommit). So an uncommitted attach is invisible to other sessions and a
concurrent INSERT routes to the DEFAULT partition, blocking on the open attach's
AccessExclusiveLock (piece b, 0118-0076). Probe: partition-concurrent-attach
permutation 2 now shows <waiting ...>/<... completed>. Spec stays defer (still
needs perm-1 routing-path locks + post-wait constraint re-validation).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): ATTACH PARTITION locks the DEFAULT partition — partition-concurrent-attach enabler (design 0118-0076)
feat(M0118-0008): ALTER TABLE ATTACH PARTITION enforces default-partition conflict check — partition-concurrent-attach enabler (design 0118-0075)
commits.description:
Wire checkDefaultPartitionDataConflict into the AlterTableAttachPartition
executor case (was only on the CREATE TABLE PARTITION OF path), so attaching a
non-default partition over rows already in the parent's visible DEFAULT raises
23P01, mirroring PG ATExecAttachPartition -> check_default_partition_contents.
Also resolve the LEAF default partition for the error message (nested
sub-partitioned default), matching PG's tpart_default_default naming.

Standalone, plain-SQL-testable core of partition-concurrent-attach; spec stays
defer (remaining blockers = deferred-until-commit attach visibility + default
AccessExclusiveLock + post-wait constraint re-validation, the per-session MVCC
catalog milestone shared with alter-table-4).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): DROP INDEX defers catalog removal to COMMIT — partition-drop-index-locking PROMOTED (design 0118-0074)
commits.description:
A non-CONCURRENTLY DROP INDEX issued inside an explicit transaction now
defers its catalog/relfile/WAL/pg_class-xmax removal until COMMIT, so the
dropped index's pg_class row + the dropper's AccessExclusiveLock stay
visible to other sessions until the dropping transaction commits — the
transactional-DDL cross-session catalog-visibility piece that was the last
blocker (4 of 4) for the partition-drop-index-locking isolation spec.

- session.go: PendingIndexDrop record + BasicSession.pendingIndexDrops +
  Add/Take/CancelPendingIndexDropsToDepth; EndExplicitTransaction drains
  the slice (safety net for every ROLLBACK path).
- operators_ddl.go: execDropIndex records the drop and continues instead
  of removing (when !Concurrent && InExplicitTransaction); new
  ApplyPendingIndexDrops mirrors the immediate path, run before commit.
- operators_tx.go: execCommit applies; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT cancels by depth.
- dispatch.go: server simple-query TxCommit path applies before TxnMgr.Commit
  (the path the isolation runner uses). Sibling commit paths kept in sync.
- Autocommit keeps the immediate, non-blocking removal (historical behaviour).

Known limitation: the deferral keeps the index visible to the dropping
session too (shared catalog, not yet per-session MVCC-filtered); this spec
never re-queries it from the dropper, so output is byte-identical. Full
same-session invisibility remains the MVCC-catalog milestone (alter-table-4,
partition-concurrent-attach).

TestPort_IsolationPartitionDropIndexLocking strict PASS (both permutations);
no regression DropIndexConcurrently1/ReindexConcurrently/ReindexSchema/
MultipleCic; go test ./internal/executor/ + -race (DROP INDEX/txn/savepoint/
commit); in-txn DROP INDEX regress cases (stats.sql rollback, matview.sql
autocommit) unaffected; go build ./... clean.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): pg_stat_activity retains last query on idle — partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0073)
commits.description:
Closes "blocker 3" of 4 for the partition-drop-index-locking isolation spec;
NOT a promotion. The spec's s3getlocks joins pg_locks to pg_stat_activity and
selects s.query, which PG shows as each backend's verbatim last query (with the
trailing ';'). Two surgical halves:

1. Engine (activity/registry.go UpdateState): removed the idle-clear branch so
   the active query text persists through the return to idle, matching PG's
   "query shows the last query that was executed" in all non-active states.
   A never-run backend still reports NULL; QueryStart is untouched on idle.

2. Runner fidelity (testport/framework isolation_runner.go execStep): for a
   single-statement step, send the trimmed verbatim body (preserving the
   trailing ';') instead of the ';'-stripped splitSQLStatements result, so the
   query goopg stores matches what PG's isolationtester sends. splitSQLStatements
   and its unit tests are unchanged; multi-statement steps keep the split form.

Probe: the entire first s3getlocks snapshot now matches PG byte-for-byte. Spec
stays defer — only blocker 4 (transactional-DDL cross-session catalog
visibility, milestone-sized) remains.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): SELECT locks the scanned relation's indexes — partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0072)
commits.description:
Closes "blocker 2" of partition-drop-index-locking. PostgreSQL AccessShare-locks
every index of a scanned relation (get_relation_info -> index_open), not just the
index a plan probes, held to end-of-transaction. New helper
(*Context).acquireScanIndexReadLocksTxn enumerates Catalog.IndexesOnTable and
AccessShare-locks each via the existing acquireScanReadLockTxn hook (held-to-commit
in an explicit txn, transient in autocommit, system catalogs skipped). Wired into
all three scan-open paths that already take the table AccessShare lock: seq scan,
index scan, index-only scan. A bare SELECT on a leaf partition now appears in
pg_locks holding AccessShare on its indexes, blocking a concurrent DROP INDEX.

NOT a promotion: spec stays defer on (3) idle-query retention and (4) txnl-DDL
cross-session catalog visibility (milestone-sized).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): DROP INDEX locks the index relation tree — partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0071)
commits.description:
execDropIndex (!s.Concurrent) now acquires, in PG RangeVarCallbackForDropRelation
order: the target index relation itself, the heap partition tree (blocks on a
leaf a reader holds in ACCESS SHARE), then the descendant child indexes. Closes
blocker 1 of partition-drop-index-locking; spec stays defer (blockers 2/3/4).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): live tableLockMgr -> pg_locks bridge -- partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0070)
commits.description:
Wire LockManager.AllLocks() (0118-0069) into the live pg_locks view so
partition-drop-index-locking's s3getlocks (pg_locks JOIN pg_class JOIN
pg_stat_activity) sees real transaction-scoped relation locks. Adds a
LockBackendID->wire-PID registry (per-connection in server.go),
tableLockMgrPgLockRows() enumerating relation-level holders/waiters, and
dedups globalRelLockMgr so an explicit-txn LOCK TABLE is surfaced once
with a real PID. Probe: spec's 1st s3getlocks 0 -> 4/7 rows, PID-joined.
Enabler only; spec stays deferred (index-relation + SELECT-index locks,
idle-query retention, txnl-DDL catalog visibility remain).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): LockManager.AllLocks() enumerates pg_locks holders/waiters — partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0069)
feat(M0118-0008): CREATE INDEX recurses partition tree — partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0068)
commits.description:
CREATE INDEX on a partitioned table now fans out into every existing
partition descendant, building a matching child index on each and
attaching it (PartitionParentOID + RegisterIndexPartitionChild, so
pg_inherits keeps children out of standalone pg_dump) to its immediate
parent index — mirroring PG DefineIndex. Children auto-named
<partition>_<col>_idx, deduped _idx1 on collision, which is why the
spec's s3getlocks references both ..._subpart_child_id_idx and
..._subpart_child_id_idx1. Enabler only; full promotion still needs the
pg_locks->real-tableLockMgr bridge + DROP INDEX child cascade (ledger).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): DROP INDEX locks partition tree — partition-drop-index-locking enabler (design 0118-0067)
commits.description:
Non-CONCURRENTLY DROP INDEX now takes a txn-scoped AccessExclusiveLock on the
index's table and recursively on every partition descendant (top-down) before
dropping, mirroring PG RangeVarCallbackForDropRelation. Lifts the spec's first
divergence: s2drop/s2dropsub now <waiting ...> behind s1's ACCESS SHARE on the
leaf partition and complete on s1commit (byte-match PG). No-op in autocommit
(TxnLockBackendID==0) so the hot path is unchanged; CONCURRENTLY excluded.

Remaining divergence (deferred): s3getlocks needs a pg_locks->real-tableLockMgr
bridge + partitioned-index child-index creation.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): PL/pgSQL single-column SELECT INTO record keeps field access — reindex-concurrently-toast enabler (design 0118-0066)
commits.description:
bindSelectIntoRow scalar-shortcut a single-column SELECT … INTO straight
onto the target even when the target is a `record` variable, so the
_<var>_<col> sub-field + compositeVarFields entry the qualified-name
expression path reads were never registered; r.field then hit the
catch-all "qualified names are not supported in PL/pgSQL expressions
(0A000)". Guard the scalar shortcut with !frame.isRecordVar(name) so a
record/composite target routes to bindRecordRowComposite (the multi-column
SELECT * INTO r path, 0118-0054). Plain scalar targets unaffected.

Advances reindex-concurrently-toast's setup DO block past the r.table_name
error (new wall: routine_column_usage 42P01); spec still fundamentally
needs real TOAST relations (reltoastrelid=0), stays defer. Enabler, not a
promotion.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): register allow_system_table_mods GUC — reindex-concurrently-toast enabler (design 0118-0065)
commits.description:
reindex-concurrently-toast.spec's global setup runs SET allow_system_table_mods
TO true to deterministically rename a table's TOAST relation/index before
REINDEX ... CONCURRENTLY. goopg did not register the GUC, so the first setup
statement failed 'unrecognized configuration parameter' (22023), aborting
permutation 0. Register it mirroring PG guc_tables.c (PGC_SUSET, bool, boot off,
DEVELOPER_OPTIONS), following the allow_in_place_tablespaces precedent: a
recognised developer no-op (goopg gates no catalog-structure modification on it).
Also add the mandatory commented sample-file entry (TestSampleConfigCoversRegistry
requires every file-settable GUC there).

NOT a promotion: the spec remains multi-loop (next divergence is a PL/pgSQL
qualified-name-in-EXECUTE error, and beneath that it needs real TOAST relations
as catalog objects — goopg stores text/bytea inline so reltoastrelid is 0).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): detach-partition-concurrently-4 PROMOTED — UPDATE fires RI parent-check + detach re-validates after wait (design 0118-0064)
commits.description:
Closes the last 3 (WHERE CURRENT OF) permutations; all 21 byte-for-byte via strict
TestPort_IsolationDetachPartitionConcurrently4. Two FK behaviours (not positioned-DML):

1. UPDATE now fires the RI_FKey_check parent-existence assertion just like INSERT.
   goopg only ran checkFKInsert from insertOp; updateOp did no parent lookup, so

   FK-key UPDATEs on FK tables) + recheckChildFKs() (delegates to new

   updateWithFrom) after BEFORE triggers, before the heap write.

   referencing row a waited-on session committed during the wait; the detacher now re-runs

   violation is recognised (d4_fk_a_fkey_1).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): detach-partition-concurrently-4 cursor-pinned snapshot at DECLARE + abort-releases-snapshot (design 0118-0063)

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): detach-partition-concurrently-4 FK existence checks observe CURRENT detach epoch (design 0118-0062)
commits.description:
detach-4 asserts that inserting a value living only in a concurrently-
detaching partition fails its FK check EVEN UNDER REPEATABLE READ: PG's
RI_FKey_check runs under the latest snapshot, so a detach-pending partition
is invisible to the FK check the instant it is marked, while a plain
SELECT/cursor in the same RR txn still sees the row.

design 0118-0060) — correct for READ COMMITTED (fresh per-statement
snapshot == current epoch) but wrong for REPEATABLE READ (txn snapshot
predates the detach ⇒ snapEpoch < DetachPendingEpoch ⇒ partition not
filtered ⇒ FK scan wrongly found the value ⇒ insert wrongly succeeded).

Fix: snapDetachEpoch (operators_fk.go) now returns the global
mvcc.CurrentPartitionDetachEpoch() instead of the snapshot epoch. Scoped
to the two FK existence scans (scanTableForMatch / scanTableForMatchFKWait
via allDescendants); ordinary query/cursor partition expansion still uses
the snapshot epoch (SearchPathCatalog.CurrentPartitionDetachEpoch),
preserving the RR-visible-row asymmetry.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): detach-partition-concurrently-2 PROMOTED — FK-safe concurrent detach + hybrid wait (design 0118-0060)
commits.description:
DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY is now safe for a foreign key referencing the
partitioned table. Three pieces:

- allDescendants (FK existence scan) prunes detach-pending leaves invisible to
  the snapshot, so a concurrent INSERT of a value living only in the detaching
  partition fails 23503 while a value in a still-attached partition succeeds.
- detachPartitionFKRefCheck (RI_PartitionRemove_Check analog) runs before
  MarkPartitionDetachPending and fails the detach synchronously with
  'removing partition X violates foreign key constraint <fkname>_<N>' when a
  committed referencing row routes to the detaching partition.
- Hybrid detach wait: waitForRelationLockers(parent+leaves) for RC table-users
  + WaitForPinnedSnapshotsToCommit (new atomic procSlot.pinnedSnap) for RR/SSI
  pinned snapshots; a RC BEGIN-only session blocks neither. Replaces 0118-0059
  snapshot-only wait; detach-1 still passes.

Byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 5 permutations via
TestPort_IsolationDetachPartitionConcurrently2 (runIsoSpecStrict).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): detach-partition-concurrently-1 PROMOTED — snapshot-relative partition visibility wiring (design 0118-0059)
commits.description:
Wires the 0118-0058 snapshot-visibility foundation primitives into six live
sites so ALTER TABLE … DETACH PARTITION … CONCURRENTLY makes the partition
invisible at the correct, snapshot-relative time. detach-partition-concurrently-1
now passes byte-for-byte via TestPort_IsolationDetachPartitionConcurrently1
(runIsoSpecStrict, all 13 permutations).

Detach executor (operators_ddl.go AlterTableDetachPartition, DetachConcurrently
branch) is now two-phase keyed on a global mvcc partition-detach epoch:
- phase 1: mvcc.NextPartitionDetachEpoch() + im.MarkPartitionDetachPending KEEPS
  the child registered (relpartbound stays set, so s3i reads relpartbound IS NULL
  = f) while every snapshot taken afterwards captures the higher epoch and omits
  it — READ COMMITTED sees it gone immediately, a REPEATABLE READ reader whose
  snapshot predates the detach still sees it until commit;
- wait: TxnMgr.WaitForOlderSlotsToCommit (snapshot-based, not lock-based — a RR
  session that has only PREPAREd a statement holds no lock yet is still waited
  for; a lock-only wait would finish too early for those perms);
- interrupt (timeout/cancel): ClearPartitionDetachPending reverts phase 1
  (FINALIZE-resume of an interrupted detach is detach-3/4 work, deferred);
- phase 2: UnregisterPartitionChild + clear bounds + ClearPartitionDetachPending
  (relpartbound now NULL ⇒ s3i flips f→t).
Plain DETACH / DETACH FINALIZE stay synchronous (else branch).

Snapshot threading: ctxPlanCatalog stamps SnapshotPartitionDetachEpoch =
ctx.Snap.PartitionDetachEpoch onto SearchPathCatalog (the snapshot is established
before planner.Plan — confirmed empirically: the RC/RR row-count split only
resolves with the per-statement epoch).

Sibling paths: SELECT expansion (planner.go collectAllPartitionLeaves via the new
currentPartitionDetachEpoch wrapper-chain walk) and INSERT routing
(operators_storage.go routeToPartitionDepth) BOTH filter the visible partition
set through catalog.VisiblePartitionChildren by the snapshot epoch — a row the
SELECT omits is the row the INSERT refuses to route.

Plan-cache bypass: new partitionDetachPending gate added to BOTH dispatch.go
(simple) and dispatch_extended.go (extended) so each statement re-plans against
its own snapshot epoch while a detach is pending (mirrors
sessionTempInheritanceActive).

pg_node_tree NULL framing: TypedVirtualCell returns NullConst for an empty
decompiled-expression cell (relpartbound, adbin, conbin, indexprs, …) so
relpartbound IS NULL reads true after finalize instead of matching a non-NULL
empty string.

detach-2 likely falls out of the same machinery (probe next loop); detach-3/4
additionally need persisted inhdetachpending / pg_partition_tree / FINALIZE /
cancel-then-resume (deferred).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): partition-detach snapshot-visibility foundation (design 0118-0058)
commits.description:
Lay the zero-blast-radius primitives a snapshot-relative partition descriptor
needs to promote detach-partition-concurrently-1. The spec couples a READ
COMMITTED "partition disappears now" view with a REPEATABLE READ "partition
stays until commit" view; goopg's synchronous UnregisterPartitionChild on a
non-MVCC shared catalog + a stale cross-session plan cache yields 2 rows in all
isolation levels (perm 1 diverges 2 vs 1). The two cases are coupled, so a
plan-cache bypass alone would regress the RR perms — the real fix is a
snapshot-relative partition descriptor. Mirrors the inherit-temp precedent
(0118-0036 primitives -> 0118-0037 wiring).

Nothing is wired into a live planner/executor/detach path, so behaviour is
byte-identical and there is no row-count regression risk on the hot path:
- mvcc: global monotonic partitionDetachEpoch (Next/CurrentPartitionDetachEpoch)
  + Snapshot.PartitionDetachEpoch captured in captureSnapshot/Clone (RR freezes
  the epoch at BEGIN, RC advances it per statement).
- catalog: Table.DetachPendingEpoch (a detach-pending child stays registered so
  an older snapshot still scans it); InMemory.MarkPartitionDetachPending /
  ClearPartitionDetachPending (O(1) pendingPartitionDetachCount) /
  HasPendingPartitionDetach (future plan-cache-bypass gate); and the chokepoint
  filter VisiblePartitionChildren(children, snapshotEpoch).

The design doc enumerates the atomic multi-site wiring for the next loop.

+ TestPartitionDetachEpochMonotonic/TestCaptureSnapshotRecordsPartitionDetachEpoch

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY waits for concurrent table users (design 0118-0057)
commits.description:
ALTER TABLE ... DETACH PARTITION ... CONCURRENTLY completed synchronously in
goopg's executor (ignored the DetachConcurrently flag from 0118-0048), so the
isolation runner never rendered the <waiting ...> marker the four
detach-partition-concurrently-{1,2,3,4} specs require -- the first divergence
after the parser/pg_backend_pid/pg_cancel_backend enablers.

When act.DetachConcurrently is set, after UnregisterPartitionChild the executor
now blocks on the existing (*Context).waitForRelationLockers (WaitForLockers
analog, 0118-0029) for both the parent and the detached child: a partitioned-
parent SELECT locks the children (acquireScanReadLockTxn), so a concurrent
reader holds the detached child's AccessShare until commit and the detacher
parks behind it. No lock of its own (CONCURRENTLY contract); inherits 57014
cancellation (statement_timeout / lock_timeout / peer pg_cancel_backend -- the
detach-3/4 s1cancel path). Gated on DetachConcurrently -> plain DETACH/FINALIZE
unchanged; blast radius nil.

Enabler, NOT a promotion: detach-1's <waiting>/<... completed> markers now
byte-match PG (probe); first divergence advances to perm 1's repeated-SELECT
row content (cross-session plan-cache reuse + RR snapshot-stable partition
visibility remain, ledgered).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): pg_cancel_backend(pid) scalar built-in (design 0118-0056)
commits.description:
pg_cancel_backend(pid int4)->bool was seeded in pg_proc (OID 2171) but had
no executor handler, so a SQL call fell through evalFuncCall to
evalStoredRoutineFuncCall and hard-failed "function pg_cancel_backend does
not exist" -- the next divergence (after 0118-0055 pg_backend_pid) of
detach-partition-concurrently-3/-4 (step s1cancel).

goopg multiplexes connections in one OS process, so a cancel calls into the
process-wide cancel registry that already backs the wire CancelRequest path.
The wire path checks a per-connection secret (it arrives unauthenticated off
a fresh socket); the SQL function runs inside an authenticated backend, so
new cancelEntry.cancelNoSecret() + backendCancelRegistry.cancelByPID(pid)bool
fire the target's active query cancel func with no secret check -- true if
the pid is a live backend (even idle, as PG), false if unknown.

New strict evalFuncCall case (NULL pid -> NULL) delegates to
ctx.CancelBackend, which the server wires in BOTH dispatch paths (simple +
extended) -- sibling-path discipline; depends only on the registry, not on
per-session Activity. Enabler, not a promotion: detach-3/4's next divergence
advances to DETACH ... CONCURRENTLY two-phase <waiting>.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote plpgsql-toast — FOR-loop snapshot + record-field SELECT INTO (design 0118-0054)
commits.description:

- assign6: ForSelectStmt materializes all rows up front (deep-copied; op

- fetch-after-commit: SELECT ... INTO now calls substitutePlpgsqlFrameVarsInSQL

  token when r isRecordVar (literal from the _<var>_<field> binding), guarded
  so a plain table.column qualifier is untouched. Was: 42P01 missing
  FROM-clause entry for table "r".

goopg stores text inline (no external TOAST chunk to orphan), so the
missing-chunk detoast correctness the spec guards holds structurally; the
advisory-lock/VACUUM <waiting ...> markers ride the runner's 300ms timing.

All 7 permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3; promoted to pass-required via

commits.description:
A `record` var bound by `SELECT * INTO r` is now a first-class composite,

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): PL/pgSQL scalar subquery x := (SELECT …) (design 0118-0051)
commits.description:
A top-level (SELECT …) in a PL/pgSQL expression (assignment RHS or RETURN
operand) is now planned+executed against the live catalog → first column of
the first row (NULL when no row; SQLSTATE 21000 when >1 row), instead of the

before lowering (a subquery can't lower to a planner.Expr) via new

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): PL/pgSQL SELECT INTO statement form (design 0118-0050)
commits.description:
Enabler for plpgsql-toast (not a promotion). A top-level INTO clause in a
PL/pgSQL-body SELECT is now reinterpreted as variable assignment instead of
being mis-parsed as SQL CREATE-TABLE-AS (SELECT ... INTO <table>).

parseSQLStmt special-cases a leading SELECT: detects a depth==0 INTO keyword,
peels off optional STRICT + the comma-separated target list, reconstructs the
query with the INTO clause excised, and returns a new SelectIntoStmt AST node.
Runtime bindSelectIntoRow binds scalar (single target), record sub-fields
(single target, multi-column), or positional scalars (multi-target); no row
yields NULL; STRICT raises P0002/P0003. Probe confirms plpgsql-toast assign1
now runs (length(x)=6000); divergence advances to assign2 subquery assignment.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): PL/pgSQL transaction control in DO blocks (design 0118-0049)
commits.description:
Implement COMMIT;/ROLLBACK; inside a non-atomic PL/pgSQL routine (top-level DO
or procedure outside an explicit transaction): the statement commits/rolls back
the current transaction and continues in a fresh one; an atomic context (DO
inside BEGIN...COMMIT) raises SQLSTATE 2D000 (invalid transaction termination),
matching PostgreSQL.

The transaction lifecycle is server-owned (connTxState/dispatch), so a new
optional Context.PLpgSQLCommitChain callback bridges the layers: the parser
emits a TxControlStmt node, the runtime invokes the callback (nil => 2D000),
and the dispatch installs it ONLY in auto-commit mode (the closure commits/rolls
back the current tx, releases only xact-scoped advisory locks, begins a fresh RC
tx+snapshot, and reassigns the outer tx/snap + ctx.Tx/ctx.Snap so the trailing
auto-commit and per-statement RC refresh follow the chained tx). Blast radius
nil: only the new TxControlStmt case ever calls the callback.

Enabler (NOT a promotion): lifts plpgsql-toast's first blocker; its divergence
now advances to PL/pgSQL SELECT...INTO var / record handling (deferred).

...RollbackChain / ...CommitInExplicitBlockRejected; TestPort_IsolationSubxidOverflow
+ FreezeTheDead strict PASS (no dispatch regression); executor+server units; go
vet clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook.

Parser-only — the executor performs a synchronous detach in both cases,
unchanged. Enabler, NOT a spec promotion: full detach-concurrently parity needs
the Effort-L two-phase concurrent-detach + transactional-DDL cross-session
catalog visibility (ledger 2026-06-23).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): alter-table-1 VALIDATE CONSTRAINT lock semantics (design 0118-0047)
commits.description:
Promote the alter-table-1 isolation spec to pass-required (runIsoSpecStrict in
TestPort_IsolationAlterTable1) — all 170 permutations byte-identical to PG 18.3.

The only new piece on top of alter-table-2's ADD FK NOT VALID is
ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT name:
  - Parser: new AlterTableValidateConstraint action kind; parseAlterTableAction
    matches VALIDATE CONSTRAINT name (VALIDATE is an identifier-keyword).
  - Executor: the new AlterTable dispatch case takes a transaction-scoped
    ShareUpdateExclusiveLock via acquireDDLLockTxn (AlterTableGetLockLevel ->
    AT_ValidateConstraint, the minimum lock) and flips the named FK's
    convalidated from 'f' to 't' (ForeignKey.NotValid=false); unknown name -> 42704.

ShareUpdateExclusive does not conflict with AccessShare reads, RowShare FOR
UPDATE, or RowExclusive INSERT, so VALIDATE never blocks the reader session; the
only wait in the spec is the INSERT behind the still-uncommitted ADD CONSTRAINT's
ShareRowExclusiveLock, exactly as in alter-table-2. No-op in autocommit / for
system catalogs keeps the dump/load + pgbench path lock-free.

strict PASS; parser+executor units PASS; go vet clean.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): alter-table-2 ADD FK NOT VALID lock semantics (design 0118-0046)
commits.description:
Promote alter-table-2 to pass-required (strict), byte-identical to PG 18.3
across all 48 permutations. The spec mixes ALTER TABLE b ADD CONSTRAINT bfk
FOREIGN KEY (a_id) REFERENCES a (i) NOT VALID with concurrent reads /
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / INSERT on both tables.

Two changes:
1. Parser: the ADD FOREIGN KEY arm now accepts the NOT VALID trailer in any
   order with [NOT] DEFERRABLE [INITIALLY ...] (new AST AlterTableAction.NotValid;
   new catalog.ForeignKey.NotValid -> pg_constraint.convalidated='f').
2. Executor: AlterTableAddForeignKey takes a transaction-scoped
   ShareRowExclusiveLock on the altered table via acquireDDLLockTxn
   (AlterTableGetLockLevel -> AT_AddConstraint). The standard lock matrix then
   drives every permutation: a concurrent INSERT (RowExclusiveLock) conflicts so
   one of s1b/s2d waits until the other commits, while SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
   (RowShareLock) and plain reads proceed. No-op in autocommit / for system
   catalogs, so pg_dump-restore / HammerDB-load and pgbench TPC-B are untouched.

AlterTable3/CreateTrigger/SequenceDdl strict PASS; parser/catalog/executor units;
go vet clean; pgbench smoke (pre-commit hook).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): vacuum-no-cleanup-lock pg_class relstats from VACUUM (design 0118-0045)
commits.description:

reltuples now reflect what a non-aggressive VACUUM observes even while a cursor
pins the only heap page (no cleanup lock).

commits.title: test(M0118-0008): dollar-quote-aware isolation step splitter (design 0118-0044)
commits.description:
The isolation harness's splitSQLStatements handled single-quotes and --
comments but not dollar-quoted strings, so a `do $$ ... commit; ... $$;`
STEP body (plpgsql-toast) was split at the first body-internal `;` and goopg
received the truncated `do $$\n declare x text`, replying with a false
"unterminated dollar-quoted string" lex error (a harness artifact; goopg
lexes $$...$$ correctly).

New dollarOpener helper recognises a $tag$ opener (empty/identifier tag, no
`$` inside per PG manual 4.1.2.4, rejects $1 positional params); the splitter
tracks an active dollarCloser and copies bytes verbatim until the exact
closer. Setup blocks bypass the splitter, so dollar-quoted CREATE FUNCTION
bodies are unaffected. With correct splitting, plpgsql-toast's first
divergence moves to the real blocker (unsupported PL/pgSQL statement: COMMIT
in a DO block); the spec stays deferred.

Test-harness only; no engine change; cannot regress any spec. Unit
TestSplitSQLStatementsDollarQuote; framework pkg PASS;
TestPort_IsolationMergeUpdate strict PASS (no regression); go vet clean.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote cluster-conflict-partition (design 0118-0041)
commits.description:
Twelfth M0118-0008 promotion; partitioned-table sibling of cluster-conflict.
cluster-conflict-partition (4 perms) now matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte with NO
engine change.

Key insight: ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO does NOT recurse to partition children
(tablecmds.c AT_ChangeOwner never recurses), so after setup only the parent is
owned by the test role. Upstream cluster() takes an AccessExclusiveLock on the
named PARENT (so it waits behind a concurrent LOCK ... IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE
MODE on the parent then completes on commit — perms 1/2), then
get_tables_to_cluster_partitioned enumerates leaves WITHOUT locking them and
skips every leaf the role does not own (cluster_is_permitted_for_relation false;
WARNING suppressed by client_min_messages=ERROR), so a leaf held in SHARE UPDATE
EXCLUSIVE is never touched and CLUSTER returns immediately (perms 3/4).

goopg's clusterOp.Next (no-op index-order rewrite, design 0118-0040) locks only
the named parent and never processes leaves, so the captured output is
byte-identical to PG by both routes: parent-locked perms wait on goopg's parent
AccessExclusiveLock; leaf-locked perms never touch the leaf and return at once.
The runner's 300ms timing threshold renders the immediate-completion perms
without a <waiting ...> marker.

Promotion only: new TestPort_IsolationClusterConflictPartition (runIsoSpecStrict);
design 0118-0041 + README index; D-002 rationale (comma-free) + regen
port-status.md/target-inventory.md/upstream-isolation-coverage.md; fix_plan +
ledger + working_set.

Deferred (no port spec needs it): per-leaf CLUSTER processing + a faithful
non-owner CLUSTER 'must be owner of table' error.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote vacuum-conflict + cluster-conflict via ownership-based maintenance privilege (design 0118-0040)
commits.description:
Eleventh M0118-0008 promotion; second/third members of the *-conflict family.
vacuum-conflict (16 perms) and cluster-conflict (2 perms) now match PG 18.3
byte-for-byte.

Unlike truncate-conflict's grantable table privilege, VACUUM/ANALYZE/CLUSTER key
on table OWNERSHIP (vacuum_is_permitted_to_vacuum / cluster_rel owner check).
Four changes:

1. New catalog.Table.Owner (owning role name; empty = bootstrap superuser OID 10;
   pg_class.relowner output unchanged — field is check-only).
2. ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO role now records the owner: parser captures it into
   AlterTableStmt.OwnerTo (was discarded), executor execAlterTable sets tbl.Owner
   and takes a txn-scoped AccessExclusiveLock (AlterTableGetLockLevel; no-op in
   autocommit, which is how the specs issue the grant). CURRENT_USER/SESSION_USER/
   CURRENT_ROLE -> empty owner (bootstrap superuser).
3. New maintenancePermitted(ctx,tbl) wired into the explicit-target loop of
   expandVacuumTargets/expandAnalyzeTargets BEFORE any lock (mirrors PG
   expand_vacuum_rel's no-lock pg_class ACL check): a non-superuser SET ROLE
   session that does not own the relation skips it immediately with
   'WARNING: permission denied to vacuum/analyze "X", skipping it' and NO wait;
   after ALTER ... OWNER TO the role owns the table so VACUUM/ANALYZE are
   permitted and block on a conflicting LOCK ... IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE MODE
   until commit.
4. clusterOp.Next now takes a blocking AccessExclusiveLock via
   acquireRelLockMaybeTransient so CLUSTER waits behind the same SHARE UPDATE
   EXCLUSIVE holder, then completes.

Blast radius nil for superuser usage (Owner empty => maintenancePermitted always
true; pgbench/TPC-H/every existing VACUUM/ANALYZE caller unchanged).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote truncate-conflict via TRUNCATE privilege model + role-DDL batch fix (design 0118-0039)
commits.description:
Tenth M0118-0008 promotion; first of the *-conflict family. truncate-conflict
now matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte across all 8 permutations.

Three problems:
1. Batch-swallow root cause: the setup `CREATE ROLE x; CREATE TABLE y` is one
   batch the parser can't parse (CREATE ROLE unsupported), and the parse-failure
   recovery handed the whole batch to tryHandleRoleDDL which dropped the trailing
   CREATE TABLE (truncate_tab never existed). New splitLeadingRoleDDL +
   firstTopLevelSemicolon peel the leading role statement off and recurse on the
   remainder; standalone role DDL untouched (DROP ROLE already parsed).
2. TRUNCATE privilege model: catalog ACL store (tableACLs;
   Catalog.GrantTablePrivilege/HasTablePrivilege/DropTableACL), SET/RESET ROLE now
   track connTx.NonSuperuserRole, an autocommit table-level GRANT recorder
   (server/grant_ddl.go), and a pre-lock check in execTruncate:
   NonSuperuserRole!="" && !HasTablePrivilege(oid,role,"TRUNCATE") => 42501
   "permission denied for table <name>" immediately (no wait; superuser/owner bypass).
3. Granted autocommit TRUNCATE must wait: execTruncate switched acquireDDLLockTxn
   (no-op in autocommit) -> acquireRelLockMaybeTransient so it blocks behind a
   concurrent open SELECT; preserves inherit-temp (its TRUNCATE is in an explicit txn).

commits.title: fix(M0118-0008): INSERT…SELECT fewer source columns than table — crash fix + default-fill (design 0118-0038)
commits.description:
INSERT INTO t SELECT a,b with no explicit column list, where the SELECT

range in insertOp.Next — ColumnIndex=[0,1,2] indexed a 2-col source row)
instead of default-filling the trailing target columns.

more expressions than target columns"; explicit-list under-wide → 42601
"more target columns than expressions"; implicit-list under-wide →
truncate ColumnIndex to the source width so the executor's
applyDefaultsForMissing fills the rest. Type-independent; VALUES path
unaffected.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote inherit-temp via session-scoped inheritance expansion + TRUNCATE-blocks-scan locking (design 0118-0037)
commits.description:
Inheritance expansion of a persistent parent now excludes another
session's temporary children (RELATION_IS_OTHER_TEMP) via
catalog.AccessibleInheritanceChildren, wired at every expansion site:

- planner SELECT (collectInheritanceDescendants) — session token threaded
  through SearchPathCatalog.TempOwnerToken/CurrentTempOwner and discovered
  by planner.currentTempOwner walking the catalog wrapper chain.
- executor UPDATE / DELETE / UPDATE..FROM / DELETE..USING / TRUNCATE
  expansion — owner from sessionTempOwner(ctx).

The cross-session plan cache is bypassed when
catalog.HasTempInheritanceChildren() is true, so one session's inh_parent
plan is never served to another.

TRUNCATE now takes a transaction-scoped AccessExclusiveLock and a bare
autocommit scan takes a transient AccessShareLock (acquireScanReadLockTxn
-> acquireRelLockMaybeTransient), so s2_select_p blocks behind s1's
in-progress TRUNCATE inh_parent while s2_select_c on its own temp child
proceeds.

Spec PROMOTED to pass-required: TestPort_IsolationInheritTemp (strict,
all 9 permutations byte-identical to PG 18.3).

Deferred (ledger): FK/MERGE/VACUUM inherit-temp filtering (shared
allDescendants helper needs an owner param; no port spec exercises it).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): inherit-temp foundation — per-session temp-relation ownership (design 0118-0036)
commits.description:
Lay the per-session temp ownership concept the inherit-temp isolation spec
needs, without yet wiring it into the live read/write paths (blast radius nil).

goopg keeps all relations — permanent and temporary, from every session — in
one shared in-memory catalog, so a parent's inheritance expansion wrongly
scans ANOTHER backend's temp child. PG isolates each backend's pg_temp_N via
RELATION_IS_OTHER_TEMP, so s1's `SELECT a FROM inh_parent` returns 4 rows
where goopg returns 6. A faithful fix must exclude other-session temp children
at every inheritance/partition expansion site (planner SELECT + executor
UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/FK/MERGE) in one atomic change (sibling-paths
discipline: a missed site is a silent row-count regression). This commit lands
the central, zero-blast-radius pieces so the wiring loop is a fan-out over one
shared helper:

- catalog.Table.TempOwner — owning session's stable token ("" = permanent or
  session-less temp, visible to all, preserving legacy single-session behaviour).
- catalog.AccessibleInheritanceChildren(children, sessionTempOwner) — shared
  filter dropping other-session temp children; the single chokepoint the wiring
  loop calls everywhere. Same-slice fast path; nil-in/nil-out.
- config.SessionRegistry.UniqueID() — process-unique, non-zero, lifetime-stable
  per-connection identity (atomic counter minted in NewSessionRegistry).
- executor.sessionTempOwner(ctx) — derives "s<id>" from AdvisorySessionIdentity
  (UniqueID interface); stamped at both CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE sites.

Nothing reads TempOwner in live paths yet. Wiring fan-out + planner-token
plumbing + the last-two-permutation TRUNCATE-on-parent blocking semantics are
deferred (ledger + design 0118-0036 enumerate the resume point).

Units: TestAccessibleInheritanceChildren, TestSessionRegistryUniqueID,
TestSessionTempOwner. catalog/config/executor packages green; gofmt clean.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote vacuum-concurrent-drop via blocking maintenance lock + post-lock existence re-check (design 0118-0035)
commits.description:
VACUUM/ANALYZE without SKIP_LOCKED now take a blocking per-relation
ShareUpdateExclusiveLock (or AccessExclusiveLock for VACUUM FULL) via
acquireRelLockMaybeTransient, mirroring vacuum.c vacuum_open_relation ->
LockRelationOid. Previously a heavyweight relation lock was taken only on the
SKIP_LOCKED path, so VACUUM/ANALYZE never waited behind a concurrent
LOCK part1 IN SHARE MODE (no <waiting ...>). ShareUpdateExclusive conflicts
with Share, so s2 now parks until s1 commits.

After the lock is taken each target is re-checked against the live catalog via
the new relationStillExists helper (catalog.InMemory.LookupTableByOID, the
try_relation_open analog): a target DROPped by the transaction that committed
while we waited is skipped -- emitting
WARNING: skipping vacuum/analyze of "X" --- relation no longer exists only for
an explicitly named relation (vacuumTarget.explicit) while a partition child
reached by expanding a partitioned table is skipped silently. The existing
severity-aware isolation runner renders the WARNING line.

vacuum-concurrent-drop promoted to pass-required: TestPort_IsolationVacuumConcurrentDrop
strict PASS (6 permutations, byte-identical to PG 18.3). Eighth M0118-0008
promotion.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): fix SELECT-list SRF nested in scalar expr (design 0118-0034)
commits.description:
A set-returning function nested inside a larger SELECT-list scalar
expression (e.g. generate_series(1,n) % 4) previously collapsed to a
single row holding the SRF's start value instead of expanding to one row
per series element with the enclosing expression applied to each. This
silently dropped rows: INSERT INTO t SELECT generate_series(1,1000) % 4
inserted exactly one row instead of 1000.

Planner now pre-scans the SELECT list for SRFs nested inside scalar
expressions, wraps each into the ProjectSet operator, and the executor
evaluates the enclosing expression per generated step.

Verified on a real server (fresh data dir): gs%4, gs+100, gs(2,10,2)*10,
bare gs all expand correctly; INSERT...SELECT gs%4 -> 1000 rows; join
sanity unchanged. Unit: TestSelectListSRFInsideExpression. TPC-H spotcheck
is environmentally blocked (SLRU-backfill startup hang on the 6M-row set,
not a regression); pgbench smoke runs via pre-commit hook.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote vacuum-skip-locked via conditional maintenance lock + severity-aware isolation runner
commits.description:
VACUUM/ANALYZE (SKIP_LOCKED) now take a conditional per-relation lock
(new (*Context).tryAcquireMaintenanceLock mirroring PG ConditionalLockRelationOid:
ShareUpdateExclusiveLock, or AccessExclusiveLock for VACUUM FULL) and skip a
contended relation instead of waiting. expandVacuumTargets/expandAnalyzeTargets
tag each relation explicit (user-named -> WARNING 'skipping vacuum/analyze of X
--- lock not available') vs partition-expanded (silent skip), and collect
partitioned parents. ANALYZE of a partitioned parent then reads each leaf
partition under a blocking AccessShareLock (analyzeInheritanceWait) for
inheritance stats -- SKIP_LOCKED does not cover this scan -- so it waits under
ACCESS EXCLUSIVE but not SHARE; plain VACUUM never waits.

The isolation runner now echoes each captured server message with its real
protocol severity (pq.Error.Severity) instead of a hard-coded NOTICE:, so
WARNING: lines render. Strictly more faithful; NOTICE-emitting specs unchanged.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote alter-table-3 via ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER lock + abort-time lock release
commits.description:
ALTER TABLE ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER now takes a transaction-scoped
ShareRowExclusiveLock (acquireDDLLockTxn, mirrors PG AlterTableGetLockLevel):
it conflicts with a concurrent INSERT's RowExclusiveLock (waits) but not with
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE's RowShareLock (proceeds). The parser arm (formerly a
pure no-op) flags AlterTableStmt.EnableDisableTrigger for a TRIGGER target.

connTxState.Fail() now releases the failed transaction's tableLockMgr locks
immediately (ReleaseTableLocks), gated on SavepointDepth()==0, mirroring PG's
AbortTransaction dropping heavyweight locks at abort rather than at the explicit
ROLLBACK (verified on real PG 18.3: zero pg_locks rows while idle in transaction
aborted). Subtransaction abort retains locks per PG; idempotent with End().

promotion (design 0118-0032).

commits.description:

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote reindex-schema isolation spec via REINDEX SCHEMA per-relation locking
commits.description:
REINDEX SCHEMA now locks every non-virtual user table in the schema in OID
(creation) order: a plain reindex takes a ShareLock per relation (conflicts with
a concurrent SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE holder so it waits) while REINDEX SCHEMA
CONCURRENTLY waits for lockers without taking a conflicting lock (reuses the
0118-0029 waitForRelationLockers primitive). The OID-ordered stall lands on the
earliest-created locked table first, so a concurrent DROP of a later not-yet-
reached table proceeds while the reindex waits -- byte-identical to PG 18.3.

The autocommit lock uses a new (*Context).acquireRelLockMaybeTransient,
generalised out of acquireSequenceLockTxn (held-to-commit in an explicit txn;
transient acquire+release in autocommit so the wait still happens during
acquisition). 4th M0118-0008 promotion (design 0118-0030).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0008): promote reindex-concurrently isolation spec via REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY wait-for-lockers
commits.description:
Two fixes make reindex-concurrently match PG 18.3 byte-for-byte (6 perms):

1. Parser: parseReindex now accepts CONCURRENTLY in the modern post-type
   position (REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY name) in addition to the legacy
   pre-type spelling.

2. Wait-for-lockers: new (*Context).waitForRelationLockers, the WaitForLockers
   analog. It polls tableLockMgr.Holders and returns once no other backend
   holds a lock on the table, taking no lock of its own so concurrent reads
   (AccessShare) and writes (RowExclusive) proceed unimpeded -- the CONCURRENTLY
   contract, since REINDEX holds only ShareUpdateExclusive. reindexOp.Next calls
   it for REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY.

The isolation runner detects blocking purely by timing (300ms), so a poll loop
that simply does not return renders as <waiting ...> and completes the instant
the lockers drain. A bare BEGIN registers no table lock, so a REINDEX started
before any concurrent table access returns immediately (perm 1) while the
blocking perms complete right after the last concurrent commit. Read-only on
the lock manager, gated on Concurrently && TABLE, so zero hot-path blast radius;
the primitive is reusable by the other CONCURRENTLY specs.

Gates: TestPort_IsolationReindexConcurrently strict PASS (6 perms); lock-sibling
regression (create-trigger, sequence-ddl, drop-index-concurrently-1) PASS;
-race lockmgr+executor PASS; parser units PASS; pgbench smoke via pre-commit.

so concurrent nextval/SERIAL inserts never block at the table level.

(2) physically removed the chain root line pointer (the index points there),
orphaning the live chain tip so the updated row vanished from index scans and

pd_prune_xid fast-path gate and delegates; new PageVacuumPrune runs the kernel
unconditionally (VACUUM must prune regardless of the opportunistic hint) and
returns the surviving-LP_NORMAL count for Stats.Live. vacuumCore now emits the
RecordKindHeapPruneOpt WAL record (carries redirects+unused, replay already
exists) and collects index-vacuum TIDs only from fully-removed Unused slots
(redirected roots keep their valid index entry).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): lock_timeout + statement-timeout-aware lock waits (timeouts row-level)
commits.description:
Implements PostgreSQL's lock_timeout GUC and corrects the cancel message a
statement emits while waiting for a lock. Both the heavyweight lock manager
(LOCK TABLE) and the transaction-XID waiter (WaitForXID, used by every
UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/SELECT…FOR… that blocks on a concurrent writer) now honour
lock_timeout and abort with the exact upstream messages:
  - lock_timeout      -> "canceling statement due to lock timeout"
  - statement_timeout -> "canceling statement due to statement timeout"
  - client cancel     -> "canceling statement due to user request"

Before: all three mapped to "user request", lock_timeout armed no timer, and
row-level waits (epqWait) swallowed the cancel and spun into a spurious 40001.

- NEW leaf pkg internal/lockwait: carries the lock-wait budget down the request
  ctx as a duration (re-armed per wait, like ProcSleep enable_timeout_after) +
  ErrLockTimeout sentinel; stdlib-only so lockmgr/mvcc can depend on it.
- lockmgr.acquire: lock-timeout select case (shares unparkWaiter splice-and-
  repair with ctx.Done()).
- mvcc.WaitForXID: cond-broadcast timer + lock-deadline check after ctx.Err().
- dispatch.go: sessionLockTimeout, attaches budget when lock_timeout>0.
- executor: lockWaitTimeoutError / lockWaitCancelError; epqWait returns a
  timeout *ExecError that all write-path call sites surface (plain cancel still
  swallowed -> historical retry); lockRowsOp WaitForXID sites likewise.

Hot path untouched: lock_timeout defaults off, no timer/ctx-value when unset.

Table-level half of timeouts.spec (SELECT taking ACCESS SHARE so LOCK TABLE
conflicts) deferred (perf-sensitive); spec not yet promoted to port.

(1) lockRowsOp.stampLockInner's real-updater branch now conflict-filters its

keeps s1's lock.

(2) The HOT UPDATE producer carries the old tuple's non-conflicting lockers

compute_new_xmax_infomask) so after the updater commits s3 FOR UPDATE waits on

commits.title: feat(M0118-0009): self-savepoint lock-upgrade preserves outer lock — delete-abort-savept-2 PASS 4/4
commits.description:
A SELF row-lock upgrade inside a savepoint (s1 holds FOR KEY SHARE at the top
level, SAVEPOINT f, FOR NO KEY UPDATE under the sub-XID) overwrote the xmax with
a single sub-XID member, discarding the outer top-level KEY SHARE. After
ROLLBACK TO f aborts the sub-XID the row had no surviving lock, so a conflicting
s2 FOR UPDATE woke and completed immediately instead of waiting until s1 COMMIT.
lockRowsOp.stampLockInner combined a lock-only xmax into a MultiXact (preserving
the prior holder via stampMultiLock) only for foreign holders; the self path
fell through to the single-xmax stamp.

Fix: new predicate hasOuterSelfLockMember(hdr) (true iff the lock-only xmax holds
an active self member stamped under a level != the current writerXID — an outer
savepoint/top-level lock) widens the producer gate to
!isSelfXID(xmax) || hasOuterSelfLockMember(hdr). stampMultiLock already keeps
every member whose xid != writerXID() as a survivor, so s1d now builds
{top-level KEY SHARE, sub-XID NO KEY UPDATE}; ROLLBACK TO drops only the sub-XID
and conflictingLockHolders waits s2's FOR UPDATE on the surviving KEY SHARE.
Same-level self re-lock yields no survivor (combined=false) -> unchanged
single-xmax stamp (hot path untouched); strict no-op outside a savepoint.

multixact.MembersConflict (DoesMultiXactIdConflict port) skips self. s3's FOR
UPDATE is parked outside the tuple xmax, so s1 sees only the compatible {s1,s2}
members and the deadlock detector is never consulted.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0003): synchronous simple lock-upgrade deadlock detection — deadlock-simple promoted (slice 16)
commits.description:
PG's JoinWaitQueue (proc.c) resolves a *simple* lock-upgrade deadlock
synchronously the instant the second upgrader joins the queue — it returns
PROC_WAIT_STATUS_ERROR (requester is the victim) WITHOUT waiting for
deadlock_timeout, so the victim errors immediately with no <waiting> marker.
goopg's tableLockMgr (slice 15) routed the LOCK TABLE upgrades through lockmgr
correctly and victim selection (youngest backend) was already right, but lockmgr
only had the timeout-driven detector, so it parked both upgraders and the error
surfaced late — diverging on the <waiting> marker and timing.

Fix (lockmgr only): new lockState.hasSimpleDeadlock(b,m) mirrors the
JoinWaitQueue scan — when b already holds a lock here and would queue behind the
first conflicting waiter w whose held locks also conflict with b's request, it is
a simple deadlock and b is the victim. Acquire checks it after canGrantImmediately
(mutually exclusive at the deciding waiter) and before enqueueing, then
ReleaseAll(b) (mirroring the timeout victim path so the survivor's wake-pass
fires) and returns ErrDeadlockDetected (mapped to 40P01 by acquireRelLockTxn).

Scope: simple single-object lock-upgrade deadlock only. Multi-object cycles,
soft-deadlock queue reordering, and the row-lock xmax/WaitForXID wait graph
remain on the timeout detector / future slices.

commits.description:
LOCK TABLE now takes a real, transaction-scoped heavyweight lock so a
conflicting LOCK in another session blocks until COMMIT/ROLLBACK; previously
execLockTable only recorded the lock in the pg_locks display registry and
never waited.

The lockmgr package already had every primitive (conflict matrix, blocking
Acquire, non-blocking TryAcquire for NOWAIT, and canGrantImmediately's
JoinWaitQueue early-grant rule written explicitly for this spec) but

acquireRelLock/acquireTupleLock are no-ops and cross-statement ROW blocking

contention -> 55P03, lock cycle -> 40P01. pg_locks display registry unchanged.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0003): advisory-lock owner-identity enabler — lock-update-delete hang removed (resume #3)
commits.description:
Validate + land the prior loop's interrupted WIP (died at api_limit mid-task).
The lock-update-delete isolation spec uses a session-level advisory lock as its
synchroniser: s2 takes pg_advisory_lock(0) in auto-commit setup (before BEGIN),
then unlocks it after BEGIN while s1 blocks in pg_advisory_xact_lock(0). That
step order exposed an advisory-lock owner-identity bug that hung the spec.

advisorySessionIDFromContext preferred ctx.Session (the *BasicSession, nil before
the first BEGIN) over the per-connection AdvisorySessionIdentity (the
*config.SessionRegistry, stable for the whole connection). So an auto-commit
pg_advisory_lock() keyed on the SessionRegistry could never be matched by a
pg_advisory_unlock() issued after BEGIN (keyed on the now-non-nil BasicSession):
the lock leaked for the server-process lifetime and the next acquirer blocked
forever.

Fix — five sibling acquire/release sites now key on the per-connection sess:
- advisorySessionIDFromContext prefers AdvisorySessionIdentity (fallback
  BasicSession then BackendID only for unit-test contexts).
- dispatchSimpleQueryViaExecutor / executeExtendedQueryViaExecutor release the
  per-statement xact-scoped locks under AdvisorySessionIdentity first.
- connTxState.End releases under a new connTxState.AdvisoryID (= sess).
- pg_advisory_unlock_all already routed through advisorySessionIDFromContext.

Separately, PostgreSQL frees all advisory locks (session- and xact-scoped) at
backend exit; new executor.ReleaseAllAdvisoryLocks is deferred in
runPostStartupLoop so a session-scoped lock the client never unlocked / abandoned
cannot strand the key.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0003): land MultiXact member store (SLRU analog, engine-first)
commits.description:
Completes the keystone-half of resume point #1 of the MultiXact subsystem
(docs/design/0118-0002): the in-memory member store that resolves a MultiXactId
to its immutable member set — the analog of PostgreSQL's multixact SLRU
(pg_multixact/offsets + pg_multixact/members). Still engine-first/wire-later
(mirrors internal/amcheck): a pure, mutex-guarded data structure with NO
executor/storage hot-path wiring.

internal/multixact/store.go:
  - Store: monotone MultiXactId allocator from FirstMultiXactId (NewStore /
    NewStoreAt(next) to seed from pg_control.nextMulti; Next() to read it);
    Members(multi) resolves an id to a defensive copy of its sorted member set.
  - Create(m1,m2)            <- MultiXactIdCreate          (multixact.c:430)
  - CreateFromMembers(set)   <- MultiXactIdCreateFromMembers(:811): single-updater
    validation (ErrMultipleUpdaters) + identical-set dedup (setKey over the
    mxactMemberComparator (xid,status)-ascending sort, :1652/:1704 mXactCacheGetBySet).
  - Expand(multi,add,live)   <- MultiXactIdExpand          (:483): immutability by
    new-id, already-member no-op, obsolete->singleton, keep-still-of-interest
    (in-progress OR committed-updater; aborted updater dropped).
  - Liveness{IsInProgress,DidCommit} injects transaction state into Expand's
    filter (zero value = conservative keep-all, mirrors MembersConflict's isCurrent);
    the leaf package does not own liveness.

Two documented divergences from the SLRU (neither affects member-set semantics):
the dedup cache is global+unbounded (upstream's mXactCacheGetBySet is per-backend
LRU-capped at 256) and ids are never truncated/vacuumed (wraparound is deferred).

internal/multixact/store_test.go: 19 pure/deterministic tests, -race clean —
allocator/clamp, sorted round-trip + defensive copy, unknown-id, identical-set
dedup vs distinct-set, identical-pair/multi-updater/invalid-input rejection,
no-input-mutation, and the full Expand matrix (new-id immutability, already-member
no-op, finished-locker drop + committed-updater keep, aborted-updater drop,
obsolete singleton, nil-liveness keep-all, invalid input) + a 16x64 concurrent
create asserting the allocator advanced by exactly the unique-set count.

(HEAP_XMAX_IS_MULTI) is the sibling-path step (stamp + decode twins change
together); then resume #2/#3 and spec promotion. See deferral ledger.

commits.description:

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): insert-conflict-do-nothing-2 isolation spec passes — multi-row ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING under RR/SERIALIZABLE
commits.description:
The RR/SERIALIZABLE sibling of the already-passing insert-conflict-do-nothing.
Two sessions each run INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (one a single row, the
other a self-conflicting two-row batch) while both sit in REPEATABLE READ then
SERIALIZABLE, across all eight commit/insert interleavings.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING never raises a serialization failure even at SERIALIZABLE:
the arbiter probe finds the live committed duplicate and skips the row, recording
no write to seed an SSI conflict-in edge (unlike DO UPDATE, which can take 40001,
or a bare unique violation, which is 23505). Every conflicting insert is a no-op,
so the final SELECT shows only the first committed value and no transaction aborts.

Pure promotion — ZERO engine change. goopg's M0100-0002 eager-XID arbiter path
plus the M0104 RR/SERIALIZABLE levels already produce this outcome; the
INCLUDE-column primary key was already supported. Found by re-probing the "(plain)"
remaining failed-spec set after the M0118-0003 row-locking freebie vein was
exhausted. Isolation pass count 38 -> 39 (total oracle pass 62 -> 63).

commits.description:

commits.title: feat(M0118-0003): nowait-3 isolation spec passes — blocking FOR UPDATE waits on a row-lock holder
commits.description:
stampLockInner's lock-only-xmax branch no longer gates on
waitPolicy ∈ {NOWAIT, SKIP LOCKED}; it now enters on any genuine
tupleLockConflicts against an active holder and dispatches on the wait
policy: SKIP LOCKED drops the row, NOWAIT raises 55P03, and the default
blocking policy WaitForXID(holder) then recurses to re-evaluate the
tuple (handling the holder committing its lock, aborting, or upgrading
to a real update). Mirrors the real-updater wait path directly above.

s3's concurrent FOR UPDATE NOWAIT still fails fast because while s2 is
parked in WaitForXID it holds the statement-scoped lockmgr tuple lock,
so s3's tryAcquireTupleLock returns the same relation-qualified 55P03.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0003): skip-locked isolation spec passes — FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT
commits.description:
skip-locked.spec now passes (TestPort_IsolationSkipLocked, all 21 generated
permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3). Two sessions each repeatedly
SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1 over a 2-row queue must
claim disjoint rows (1 and 2), skipping rows the other session row-locked,
without ever blocking. Isolation pass count 34 -> 35.

Four changes:

- Planner: liftLimitAboveLockRows reshapes Project(Limit(Sort)) into
  Limit(LockRows(Project(Sort))) when a lock clause uses SKIP LOCKED and the top
  Project directly wraps a non-WITH-TIES Limit, copying the LIMIT/OFFSET exprs
  onto new LockRows.LimitCount/OffsetCount. PG plans Limit -> LockRows -> Sort so
  the lock claims rows in the LIMIT's order and stops after LIMIT
  successfully-locked rows; goopg's default Limit-below-lock would turn a skipped
  row into a missing result. Scoped to SKIP LOCKED so every existing
  FOR UPDATE/SHARE plan (incl. TPC-H) is byte-for-byte unchanged.

- Executor drain cap: lockRowsOp.Open evaluates LimitCount(+OffsetCount) like
  limitOp.Open into maxDrain; drainAndStamp already stops at
  successCount >= maxDrain, and a skipped row takes the epqSkipped continue path
  without incrementing successCount, so the lock claims exactly LIMIT rows.

- Executor skip: removed the SKIP LOCKED Open-reject (relation RowShareLock is
  still taken with the normal blocking policy). stampLock gains a SKIP LOCKED arm
  (tryAcquireTupleLock -> epqSkipped on 55P03); stampLockInner's lock-only-xmax
  branch (the same cross-statement signal NOWAIT reads) now also returns
  epqSkipped under SKIP LOCKED when the conflicting locker is still active.

- Sort TID preservation (the real blocker): a Sort between LockRows and the scan
  dropped the slot's hasCTID/ctid side-channel, so no row was ever locked (the
  spec returned row 1 everywhere). sortOp now carries a compact []sortCTID in
  lockstep with its in-memory rows (sorted together via a permutation) and
  re-attaches it on Next; projectOp already propagates it up to drainAndStamp's
  ms.hasCTID fallback. Spilled sorts disable the side-channel (the N-way merge
  can't carry it) — rare for row-locking queries and no worse than before.

Deferred siblings (recorded in the deferral ledger): skip-locked-2 (multixact),

commits.title: feat(M0118-0003): nowait isolation spec passes — FOR UPDATE NOWAIT tuple-level fail-fast
commits.description:
nowait.spec now passes (TestPort_IsolationNowait, all 6 perms byte-for-byte vs
PG 18.3). FOR UPDATE NOWAIT must immediately raise 55P03 "could not obtain lock
on row in relation" rather than block when another session holds the row lock.

Two blockers cleared:

- Parser: PG gram.y allows select_limit BEFORE or AFTER the for_locking_clause
  (`… FOR UPDATE [SKIP LOCKED|NOWAIT] LIMIT n`); goopg only handled the former.
  Factored limit/offset/fetch parsing into parser.parseSelectLimitClauses, now
  invoked at both grammar sites.

- Executor: goopg's lock manager is statement-scoped (dispatch.go assigns a
  fresh BackendID per Query message + ReleaseAll at each statement's end), so a
  tuple lock taken by s1a is released before s2a runs. Cross-statement conflict
  detection therefore rides the persisted lock-only xmax in the heap page.
  stampLockInner previously ignored lock-only xmax and silently overwrote it; it
  now detects a conflicting lock-only xmax held by a still-active xact
  (tupleLockConflicts + TxnMgr.IsXIDActive) and, for NOWAIT only, returns the
  relation-qualified 55P03. Block and SKIP LOCKED paths are untouched, so no
  currently-passing spec changes (lock-committed-update re-verified PASS).

Isolation pass count 33 -> 34. Deferred siblings (nowait-2..-5, lock-nowait, the
skip-locked family — the latter needs the Limit-above-LockRows plan shape) are
recorded in the deferral ledger.

Tests: TestPort_IsolationNowait, TestParseSelectForUpdateBeforeLimit,
TestTupleLockConflicts.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): index-only-scan isolation spec passes — multi-block global setup + float GUC parse
