commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): receipt-report isolation spec passes — de-facto READ ONLY SSI modeling
commits.description:
The daily-receipts read-only anomaly (210 permutations, only 6 genuine
serialization failures) now matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte. goopg previously
over-aborted 48-vs-6 because it modeled every SERIALIZABLE xact as read-write,
so the declared READ ONLY s3 closed dangerous structures it can only appear to
precede.

Ports upstream's de-facto READ ONLY machinery (predicate.c):
- SerializableXact.SnapshotSeqNo: the lastCommitBeforeSnapshot analogue,
  captured at the FIRST-statement snapshot in Manager.SnapshotFor (NOT BeginAt —
  all three sessions BEGIN at permutation start, so the anomaly hinges on s3's
  first SELECT). New committedBeforeSnapshot(peer,obs) predicate.
- Load-bearing skip in checkForSerializableConflictOutLocked
  (CheckForSerializableConflictOut 4123-4137): a READ ONLY reader of an
  already-committed writer records no rw-conflict unless the writer holds an
  out-conflict committed before the reader's snapshot. Must run before the edge
  is recorded, else Case 1 of onConflictCheckLocked fires regardless of order.
- OnConflict Cases 2/3 carry the !ReadOnly / committedBeforeSnapshot clauses and
  the PreCommit far-conflict scan skips a READ ONLY in-flight Tin.

All changes are gated on the declared ReadOnly flag, so only
serializable-parallel-2/3 and read-only-anomaly-3 share the paths (re-verified
PASS); the skip can only suppress an edge, never add one, so there is no
false-negative risk for read-write specs. Isolation pass count 31 -> 32.

Verified: TestPort_IsolationReceiptReport (210 perms); new TestCommittedBeforeSnapshot
+ TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_ReadOnly* mvcc unit tests; full internal/mvcc
PASS incl -race; regression set (serializable-parallel{,-2,-3}, read-only-anomaly{,-2,-3},
two-ids, total-cash, simple-write-skew, matview-write-skew, project-manager,
classroom-scheduling) re-verified PASS.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): matview-write-skew isolation spec passes — relation-wide conflict-in for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
commits.description:
The matview-write-skew spec runs a SERIALIZABLE REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
CONCURRENTLY (reads parent orders, rewrites the order_summary matview) against
a concurrent SERIALIZABLE reader/writer of the parent; every overlap is a
dangerous structure so the second committer must abort with 40001.

goopg passed the 4 refresh-before-read permutations (read-side conflict-out
sees s1's concurrent xmax) but failed the 4 read-before-refresh permutations:
execRefreshMatView rewrites the matview heap via the low-level writeHeapRow
path, which never runs the per-tuple ssiRecordTupleWrite hook, so no
reader->refresher rw-edge formed. ssiRecordTupleWrite's conflict-in walk is
upward-only (tuple->page->relation) and could not reach the matview reader's
per-tuple SIREAD anyway.

Fix mirrors upstream CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn (predicate.c), used
by TRUNCATE/DROP for the logical-mass-delete-of-the-whole-relation shape:
- mvcc: new Manager.CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn(+ReportingFailure) —
  relation-wide all-granularity conflict-in scanning the predicate-lock
  registry for any tag on (db,rel) plus the retained-committed-reader walk.
- executor: new ssiRecordTableWrite hook, invoked from execRefreshMatView
  before the truncate.
No read-side change needed (matview scans already take per-tuple SIREAD); the
wrong "matviews never participate in predicate locking" comment is corrected
(upstream PredicateLockingNeededForRelation excludes only syscat + temp).

Runner fidelity (also unblocks receipt-report's date-render half): DATE
columns render MM-DD-YYYY (DateStyle Postgres MDY) via sql.NullTime scan;
pqprintFormat replicates libpq PQprint content-based right-justification.

Isolation pass count 30 -> 31. Verified by TestPort_IsolationMatviewWriteSkew
(byte-for-byte, all 8 perms) + 8 TestCheckTableForSerializableConflictIn mvcc
unit tests; full mvcc -race + executor suites green; no regression on the
serializable spec set.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): read-only-anomaly-3 isolation spec passes — SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE safe-snapshot deferral
commits.description:
The O'Neil read-only transaction anomaly: s3 is declared SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY
DEFERRABLE. PostgreSQL avoids the anomaly without aborting anyone by deferring
s3's snapshot (GetSafeSnapshot) until a safe snapshot is available — s3r blocks
(<waiting ...>) while the concurrent read-write s2 is active, then completes once
s2 commits, observing the final committed state (X=-11 Y=20).

Two blockers fixed:

1. DEFERRABLE was never parsed: it lexes as the unreserved keyword token
   KwDeferrable, but parseBeginModes matched it with acceptIdentKeyword (TokenIdent
   only), so BEGIN ... READ ONLY DEFERRABLE failed with "syntax error ... got
   deferrable". Now matched with acceptKeyword(KwDeferrable); recorded in the new
   BeginStmt.Deferrable / Transaction.Deferrable plan field.

2. No safe-snapshot deferral existed. SerializableXact gains ReadOnly/Deferrable
   flags (set after Begin by Manager.MarkSerializableModes, wired in BOTH BEGIN
   paths — executor execBegin and server/dispatch.go auto-commit promotion).
   Manager.SnapshotFor calls Manager.waitForSafeSnapshot before capturing a
   SERIALIZABLE xact's first snapshot: a ReadOnly+Deferrable xact enrolls every
   concurrent declared-read-write SERIALIZABLE xact active at that instant and
   blocks on a sync.Cond (ssiCond, bound to ssiMu) until each has FinishedAt
   stamped (commit or abort); releaseSerializableLocked broadcasts on finish. A
   snapshot taken after all writers drain is always RO_SAFE, so the reader is
   never aborted. No-op for every non-deferrable serializable workload.

Deliberate divergence (design §17): no RO_UNSAFE early-abort/retry refinement —
the sole DEFERRABLE spec resolves to a safe snapshot; the deferral is a pure
false-positive eliminator (worst un-modelled case waits longer, never wrong).

Verified: TestPort_IsolationReadOnlyAnomaly3 byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3, plus the
deterministic TestSafeSnapshot* mvcc unit suite (waits for committing/aborting
writer, returns immediately with no writers / not deferrable / only RO peers;
-race x2). 12 SSI serializable port specs re-verified — no regression. Isolation
pass count 29 -> 30.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): serializable-parallel-2/3 isolation specs pass — ALTER TABLE SET (reloptions) table-level storage parameters
commits.description:
serializable-parallel-2 and -3 exercise PG's SXACT_FLAG_RO_SAFE
read-only-safe-snapshot optimisation in a parallel worker. Crucially neither
spec writes anything: s1/s3 are SERIALIZABLE but issue only SELECT, and s2/s4
are SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY. A workload with no writes has no rw-antidependency
and therefore no dangerous structure, so the observable outcome is anomaly-free
— every step commits and each read returns the same stable snapshot (-2:
COUNT(*) = 100; -3: the full 10-row table). goopg has neither a parallel
executor nor an explicit RO_SAFE early-release, but matches PG 18.3
byte-for-byte because the anomaly-free outcome is identical to the
serial-equivalent (same reason the base serializable-parallel member passes).

The sole blocker was the setup DDL `ALTER TABLE foo SET (parallel_workers = 2)`:
goopg's parser rejected it ("expected ADD or DROP") because table-level
SET/RESET (reloptions) was unimplemented. The parallel-cost GUCs the specs also
set already existed.

Fix (parser + executor, additive):
- parser: new isAlterReloptVerb + a SET/RESET `(` dispatch arm in
  parseAlterTableAction that reuses parseWithOptions. Guarded on the
  parenthesized form so bare SET SCHEMA / SET TABLESPACE / SET LOGGED still fall
  through to the existing dispatch. New AlterTableSetReloptions /
  AlterTableResetReloptions AST kinds + AlterTableAction.With map.
- executor: execAlterTableSetReloptions / execAlterTableResetReloptions merge
  (SET) or clear (RESET) the four modeled storage parameters (parallel_workers,
  fillfactor, autovacuum_enabled, toast_tuple_target) on the live catalog.Table
  fields; unrecognized lowercase names are accepted and ignored, matching the
  CREATE TABLE WITH path. reloptions render from the virtual pg_class builder, so
  the mutation is immediately visible to pg_dump / pg_class with no heap re-sync.

VALIDATE-THEN-APPLY atomicity: PG validates the whole option list before
applying any of it (statement atomicity), and Go map iteration order is
unspecified, so a field-by-field apply would leave a nondeterministic partial
state on a rejected multi-option SET. The executor validates every option into a
pending set first and commits the field mutations only after the entire list
passes. Bounds and SQLSTATEs are identical to the CREATE TABLE WITH sibling.

Regression:
- TestAlterTableSetReloptions{MatchesCreateWith,Merge,Bounds,Atomic} — the
  MatchesCreateWith case is the sibling-path lock pinning ALTER == CREATE WITH.
- TestPort_IsolationSerializableParallel2 / 3 pass byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3
  (genuine --- PASS, uncached). Full internal/executor + internal/parser green;
  build + gofmt clean. Isolation pass count 27 -> 29.
- Design doc 0118-0001 §16 added + README index; target-inventory CSV ×2 pass and
  derived coverage/inventory docs regenerated.

The mandated tpch-spotcheck pre-commit gate is infra-blocked on this WSL2 host:
startup's CLog->PG-SLRU mirror (EnablePGSLRUMirror/mirrorToSLRUUnlocked) does an
O(num_xids) per-XID fsync backfill over the 6M-row / ~1.5M-xact bench dataset,
far exceeding the script's 60s readiness window (>6 min stuck on segment 0000).
This change is DDL-only and cannot touch the Q12/Q13 SELECT query path — it adds
two new functions and a switch case for two new AST kinds, modifying no existing
executor path — so it is committed under the practice-card escape hatch with the
pgbench pre-commit smoke (fresh empty cluster) as the live regression guard.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): serializable-parallel isolation spec passes — debug_parallel_query no-op developer GUC
commits.description:
serializable-parallel.spec is the read-only-anomaly-2 SSI cycle verbatim
(bank_account X/Y write-skew; read-only s3's id IN ('X','Y') observation of
s1's committed write dooms s2wx with 40001), differing only in that s3's

goopg has no parallel executor, so the GUC is semantically a no-op and the
serial SSI outcome is identical; the §9 single-column full-key per-tuple SIREAD
locks already build the correct conflict graph for s3's two PK point reads. The
sole blocker was that debug_parallel_query (renamed from force_parallel_mode)
was unregistered, so its session-setup SET raised 42704 'unrecognized
configuration parameter' before any step ran.

Fix (config-only, additive): register debug_parallel_query as a no-op developer
enum (off/on/regress; boot off; PGC_USERSET) per guc_tables.c, plus the matching
commented entry in postgresql.conf.sample (required by TestSampleConfigCoversRegistry).
Nothing in the planner consults the value. Corrects §8's pessimistic claim that
the whole serializable-parallel family needed finer per-access-method locking —
the base member needed only the GUC.

Regression: TestDebugParallelQueryGUC pins registration/enum/case-insensitivity/
invalid-value rejection; TestPort_IsolationSerializableParallel passes both
permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3. Isolation pass count 26 -> 27.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): classroom-scheduling re-lands as a genuine pass — seconds-less timestamptz literal parse
commits.description:
The classroom-scheduling isolation spec was marked pass in 2c1b7c8f, but that
was a stale Go test-cache result: run with -count=1 it failed its global-setup
INSERT 100% (8/8 SKIP) with `invalid timestamp "2010-04-01 10:00" (22007)`.
`ok` from a cached run masks a `--- SKIP`, so the false pass slipped through.

Root cause: the spec books rooms on the half-hour with seconds-less literals
(`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE '2010-04-01 10:00'`), but evalTypedStringLit's
timestamp/timestamptz layout list only accepted `HH:MM:SS` forms — none match
an `HH:MM` time with no seconds. PostgreSQL's timestamptz_in accepts seconds-less
times plus an optional numeric timezone offset.

Fix (executor-only, additive — zero mvcc/SSI-engine change): the
timestamp/timestamptz case now also tries `2006-01-02 15:04` and the
tz-suffixed variants (`…15:04:05.999999-07`, `…15:04:05-07`, `…15:04-07`).
Tz-bearing layouts are listed first so an explicit offset is honoured (→UTC)
before the zone-less fallbacks treat the wall clock as UTC; a zone-less layout
rejects tz-bearing input via Go's "extra text" error, so ordering never
mis-parses. The full-second forms TPC-H/pgbench depend on stay unchanged, and
per-node CacheValid memoization keeps the extra layouts to one first-eval pass.

- TestEvalTypedStringLitTimestampForms: pins seconds-less / explicit / fractional
  / date-only / numeric-offset forms + out-of-range rejection for both types.
- TestPort_IsolationClassroomScheduling now 5/5 PASS (was 0/8 SKIP).
- 16 SSI / timestamp isolation specs re-verified green; vet + build clean.
- Design doc 0118-0001 §14 added + §12 note resolved; CSV §12 rationale corrected
  ("sole blocker" → two co-equal global-setup blockers) and derived docs regen'd.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): referential-integrity isolation spec passes — index-only-scan records the per-tuple SSI conflict-out against a deleted tuple's xmax
commits.description:
referential-integrity is a two-table SERIALIZABLE write skew (a int PK / b)
standing in for an application-enforced foreign key. 35 of 36 generated
permutations already matched PG 18.3; the lone failure was the ordering where
the pivot s1 commits first (rx2 ry2 wx2 rx1 wy1 c1 c2) and s2 must abort last.

Root cause: rx1 = SELECT i FROM a WHERE i=1 selects only the indexed PK column,
so the planner picks an index-only scan. indexOnlyScanOp's non-ALL_VISIBLE
heap-fetch fallback recorded the relation-grain SIREAD and the invisible-tuple
phantom edge, but for a VISIBLE tuple it returned the row without the per-tuple
conflict-out the heap-fetching index-scan and seq-scan paths both run. So when
s1's scan observed the a(i=1) row that in-flight s2 had DELETEd (its header
carries Xmax = s2), no reader->deleter rw-edge formed; the pre-commit 2-cycle
walk skips already-committed pivots, so it only fired when the in-flight partner
committed first.

Fix (executor-only, zero mvcc/SSI-engine change): the found (visible) branch of
indexOnlyScanOp's fallback now calls ssiRecordTupleRead on the HOT-resolved live
version (xmin AND xmax), mirroring operators_index.go. The helper short-circuits
for RC/RR and its tuple-grain SIREAD is pruned by the relation-grain lock already
held, so only the precise per-tuple conflict-out takes effect — not a coarse
lock, so no over-abort. All 36 permutations now match PG 18.3 byte-for-byte
(TestPort_IsolationReferentialIntegrity); the 14 previously-passing SERIALIZABLE
specs remain green. Isolation pass count 25 -> 26.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): classroom-scheduling isolation spec passes — timestamptz B-tree key type unblocks a zero-SSI-change double-booking write skew
commits.description:
timestamptz joins the accepted B-tree key types. PG stores timestamp and
timestamptz identically as int64 micros-since-epoch, so timestamptz reuses the
timestamp key path (EncodeTimestamp) in encodeBTreeKeyForColumn plus both
index-only-scan key decoders; isTimestamptzType added to isSupportedBTreeKeyType.

The classroom-scheduling SERIALIZABLE double-booking write skew needed zero SSI
change — the inserted/updated rows fall within the concurrent readers' overlap
predicates so SIREAD cross-cover matches PG. The sole blocker was the PK
(room_id text, start_time timestamptz) rejecting the timestamptz key at global
setup (0A000 btree v0 only supports int4 / numeric keys).

25th passing isolation spec. All permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3.

Tests: TestPort_IsolationClassroomScheduling (3/3);
TestDDLCreateTimestamptzBTreeIndexAcceptsType + TestDDLTimestamptzRangeScanParity.
Design doc 0118-0001 §12; coverage/inventory regenerated.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): temporal-range-integrity isolation spec passes — date B-tree key type unblocks a zero-SSI-change cross-table write skew
commits.description:
temporal-range-integrity.spec is a SERIALIZABLE temporal write skew across two
tables: s1 reads statute with a date-range predicate then INSERTs offense; s2
reads offense with a date-range predicate then DELETEs statute. Any overlap must
raise 40001 — but the expected output is not uniform: permutations where s1
commits before s2's read serialize cleanly, while those where s2's read misses
s1's uncommitted insert close the two-rw-edge dangerous structure and abort.

The SSI machinery needed ZERO change. The deleted statute row and the inserted
offense row both fall within the concurrent readers' predicates, so the
relation/tuple-grain SIREAD locks cross-cover exactly as PG's finer locks do —
the dangerous-structure detection validated across the prior 23 specs reproduces
the abort pattern byte-for-byte, including the empty-relation predicate reads.
TestPort_IsolationTemporalRangeIntegrity, stable 3/3 at ~2.5s.

The sole blocker was B-tree key-type support. statute's primary key is
(statute_cite text, eff_date date); text is an accepted key type but date was
not, so global setup aborted with `0A000 btree v0 only supports int4 / numeric
keys, got "date"`. A PG date is int32 days since the 2000-01-01 epoch, so date
now joins the accepted key types (isDateType -> isSupportedBTreeKeyType) and
encodeBTreeKeyForColumn encodes it order-preservingly through the existing int4
path (btree.EncodeInt4(days)) using the same days-since-epoch arithmetic the wire
codec uses — so a probe key from a DATE literal is byte-identical to the
backfilled row's key. Both index-only-scan key decoders gained the symmetric date
case (DecodeInt4 -> days -> time.Time) so a date-keyed index-only scan round-trips
instead of falling through to the float8 default — a latent sibling-path bug
closed in the same change. This unblocks date-keyed indexes generally (TPC-H date
columns), not only this spec.

Regression: TestDDLCreateDateBTreeIndexAcceptsType + TestDDLDateRangeScanParity
(mirroring the M0044 timestamp tests). CSV flipped to pass + coverage/inventory
regenerated (24 isolation specs pass). Design doc 0118-0001 section 11 added;
classroom-scheduling note updated (timestamptz remains the distinct follow-on).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): partial-index isolation spec passes — parenthesised INSERT query source unblocks a zero-SSI-change SSI promotion
commits.description:
partial-index.spec exercises SSI predicate locking through a PARTIAL index
(CREATE INDEX test_idx ON test_t(id) WHERE val2 = 1): two SERIALIZABLE xacts
each SELECT * WHERE val2 = 1, then UPDATE a row OUT of the partial index. Any
overlap must raise 40001. The SSI machinery needed ZERO change — the section-9
index-scan SIREAD granularity already records the per-tuple read locks that
cross-cover the UPDATE targets, so all generated permutations match PG 18.3
byte-for-byte (TestPort_IsolationPartialIndex, stable 3/3 ~23s).

The sole blocker was a parser gap. The spec setup seeds with
`insert into test_t (select generate_series(0,10000), 'a', 2)` — a fully
parenthesised query source. PostgreSQL's insert_rest grammar permits a
SelectStmt (incl. select_with_parens) as the source, so the leading '(' opens a
query, NOT a column list; goopg's parseInsert unconditionally consumed it as a
column-name list and failed at `select` (42601).

Fix: a nextIsParenQuerySource() peek scans the run of leading '(' and reports
whether the first non-'(' token is a reserved query keyword (SELECT/VALUES/
WITH/TABLE) — none of which can be a bare column name, making the lookahead
unambiguous. When true the source is parsed via the existing
parseParenthesisedSelectStmt (reused from set-op RHS handling, so nested
((SELECT …)) works); the check applies both for a bare source
(INSERT INTO t (SELECT …)) and after a column list (INSERT INTO t (a,b) (SELECT …),
also valid upstream). Strictly additive — only input that previously raised a
syntax error now parses, so no existing INSERT parse changes.

- internal/parser/dml.go: parseInsert restructured; isQueryStartKeyword +
  nextIsParenQuerySource helpers.
- internal/parser/dml_test.go: TestParseInsertParenthesisedSelectSource,
  TestParseInsertColumnListThenParenthesisedSelect,
  TestParseInsertPlainSelectSourceUnchanged.
- internal/testport/isolation_port_test.go: TestPort_IsolationPartialIndex.
- docs/design/0118-0001-isolation-spec-port-strategy.md: §10 + Passing list.
- docs/test-port/{target-inventory.csv,.md,upstream-isolation-coverage.md}:
  partial-index → pass (22 → 23 isolation specs passing).

Gates: build ./...; gofmt+vet clean; parser pkg tests PASS (incl 3 new);
TestPort_IsolationPartialIndex PASS (-count=3); ralph-state-guard OK.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): predicate-lock-hot-tuple isolation spec passes — zero-engine-change SSI write-skew promotion
commits.description:
Two SERIALIZABLE xacts each SELECT i IN (5,7) then UPDATE one of the two
rows; the cross-covering point reads form a write-skew dangerous structure
so the later committer s2 aborts at c2 with 40001. Already correct via the
M0118-0001 single-column full-key index-scan SIREAD granularity: each
IN-list point lookup on the PRIMARY KEY index records exact per-tuple SIREAD
locks, so w1 (update i=7) and w2 (update i=5) each install an rw-edge to the
other reader and close the 2-cycle. goopg has no HOT update so the setup
HOT-update is a plain update; the predicate-lock correctness the spec
guards still holds.

Added TestPort_IsolationPredicateLockHotTuple; PASS stable across -count=3
(~1.4s/run). CSV flipped pass + regen (.md + upstream-isolation-coverage.md).

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): WAL buffer reserves segment-crossing pad footprint — multiple-row-versions isolation spec passes
commits.description:
The buffered WAL append paths (state.tryAppend fast path + state.appendPGCompat
Path B) reserved only conservativeSize (paddedLen+64) ring bytes, but a record
whose stripe reservation straddles a WAL segment boundary occupies up to
2*conservativeSize: reserveEmittedAndPublish emits an XLOG_NOOP pad over the gap
[curr,boundary) via emitSegmentPad -> walBuffer.writeReserved AND re-lands the
record at the boundary (a second writeReserved). Near-full, the second write left
the [head,head+cap) ring window and returned errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange,
intermittently breaking the multiple-row-versions spec's 1,000,000-row bulk
INSERT setup (~50% of runs).

Fix: reserve reserveSize = 2*conservativeSize in canHold/tryReserve/
releaseReservation (tryAppend) and needsDrain/canHold/Path-B need
(appendPGCompat). The crossing predicate gives gapLen < total <= conservativeSize,
so footprint < 2*conservativeSize is a strict, curr-independent (race-free) upper
bound; a record crosses at most one boundary. Single writers never tripped it
(Path A drains+resets before a crossing); the overflow needs concurrency. SSI
behavior was already correct (single-column full-key index-scan SIREAD granularity);
this WAL ring race was the only remaining blocker.

- internal/wal/segment_cross_reservation_test.go: regression guard (8x6000
  concurrent appends, 32KiB segments, near-full ring) — fails 3/3 reverted to
  conservativeSize, green -race -count=5.
- TestPort_IsolationMultipleRowVersions PASS 3/3 @ ~67s (no skip); CSV pass + regen.
- docs/design/0107-0007aj + README index.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): single-column full-key index-scan SIREAD granularity — read-only-anomaly-2 passes, multiple-row-versions SSI-correct
commits.description:
The SERIALIZABLE index scan acquired an EAGER relation-grain SIREAD in
indexScanOp.openPrep, covering every version of a matched key. So a write to
an INTERVENING version (s2's v1 in multiple-row-versions; the phantom-covered X
in read-only-anomaly-2) spuriously matched the reader's lock and installed a
false rw-edge, over-aborting a transaction PG commits.

Fix (executor/operators_index.go): drop the eager relation lock; decide
granularity at the end of Rescan once the matched TID set is known
(ssiRecordIndexScanGapLock). A SINGLE-COLUMN FULL-KEY point lookup that matched
>=1 tuple relies on the exact per-tuple SIREAD recorded in Next (locks only the
version actually read). Empty probes (the read-write-unique phantom gap),
leading-column probes on a COMPOSITE index (read-write-unique-4 WHERE year=2016),
and range scans keep the relation-grain gap lock. The full-key/single-column
restriction is what keeps it safe: classic write-skew has the writer overwrite
the SAME version the reader read (tuple-grain catches it); only the
intervening-version case diverges.

Outcome:
- read-only-anomaly-2.spec -> pass (TestPort_IsolationReadOnlyAnomaly2), both
  permutations byte-identical vs PG 18.3.
- multiple-row-versions made SSI-correct (TestPort_IsolationMultipleRowVersions
  matches PG byte-for-byte when setup succeeds); kept as a skip-on-defer anchor,
  NOT yet pass_required — its 1,000,000-row single-transaction setup INSERT
  intermittently trips the orthogonal WAL-buffer ring race
  errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange (~50% of runs, before any step executes).
- Full passing family stays green: read-write-unique{,-2,-3,-4}, simple-write-skew,
  two-ids, total-cash, project-manager, read-only-anomaly, update-conflict-out.
  mvcc + executor unit tests pass.

SSI-gated (ssiActive) so RC/RR index scans — including TPC-H default isolation —
are unaffected; tids collection and row decode are untouched (row counts
unchanged).

Files: internal/executor/operators_index.go; internal/testport/isolation_port_test.go
(+TestPort_IsolationMultipleRowVersions); docs/design/0118-0001 §9 + Status;
target-inventory CSV (read-only-anomaly-2 pass) + regen coverage/inventory.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): read-write-unique-4 isolation spec passes — index-scan SSI completeness lets the conflict-in walk replace the blanket post-wait 40001
commits.description:
read-write-unique-4 mixes both outcomes in one spec: the both-read permutation
(r1 r2 w1 w2 c1 c2) must abort 40001, while the single-reader permutations
(r1 w1 w2 c1 c2 / r2 w1 w2 c1 c2) must raise a 23505 unique violation.
uniqueCheckWithWait previously hard-coded 40001 for every post-wait unique
conflict between two SERIALIZABLE writers, over-firing the single-reader cases.

- uniqueCheckWithWait now defers the 40001-vs-23505 decision to the SSI
  conflict-in walk against the committed conflicting tuple's location: a pivot
  to an already-committed peer yields 40001, otherwise the duplicate falls
  through to 23505 (mirrors upstream _bt_check_unique /
  CheckForSerializableConflictIn ordering). RR keeps its prior 40001.

- Closed the SERIALIZABLE index-scan / index-only-scan predicate-lock gaps the
  blanket rule was masking. Both operators now (1) take a relation-grain SIREAD
  on the heap relation at Open — phantom coverage held even when the probe
  matches no key — and (2) register the invisible-tuple conflict-out
  (ssiRecordInvisibleTupleRead) for INSERT-before-READ, the analog of
  seqScanOp.Next. The conflict-out lands read-write-unique-3's LANGUAGE SQL
  insert-if-not-exists path (each session reads the key, finds the peer's
  in-flight insert invisible, then inserts the duplicate itself).

All four read-write-unique{,-2,-3,-4} now pass via the real SSI machinery with
the blanket-40001 heuristic removed; SimpleWriteSkew/TwoIds/TotalCash/
ProjectManager and the full dedicated isolation set regress clean.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): project-manager isolation spec passes — PHANTOM predicate locking now closes the dangerous structure where one session commits before the other's conflicting write
commits.description:
Four coordinated SSI changes (all ssiActive-gated; RC/RR/pgbench/TPC-H byte-identical):

1. Relation-level SIREAD on SERIALIZABLE seq scans. seqScanOp.Open acquires a
   relation-grain predicate lock (ssiRecordRelationRead) — the analogue of
   PredicateLockRelation in upstream heap_beginscan (heapam.c:1162): "in a heap
   scan there is nothing more fine-grained to lock". Skips system catalogs /
   temp / matview per PredicateLockingNeededForRelation. Handles the
   READ-before-INSERT phantom: the later insert's conflict-in finds the reader.

2. Conflict-out on physically-present invisible tuples. seqScanOp.Next's
   invisible branch now calls ssiRecordInvisibleTupleRead(rel, xmin), the
   analogue of HeapCheckForSerializableConflictOut's !visible paths
   (heapam.c:9254) — a concurrent inserter's row is on the page but invisible to
   us, so reader->inserter is registered from its xmin. Handles INSERT-before-READ.

3. Retained committed readers' predicate locks. The permutations where one
   session COMMITs before the other's conflicting write needed the committed
   reader's SIREAD to remain discoverable. releaseSerializableLocked now, on
   commit, detaches the xact from the GLOBAL handle-keyed holder sets only
   (detachPredicateLocksFromGlobalLocked — a reused proc-slot handle could alias)
   but KEEPS sx.predicateLocks; checkForSerializableConflictInLocked gains a walk
   over ssiState.finished, forming R->W against any retained committed reader that
   overlaps the writer (reader.FinishedAt > writer.BeginAt) and owns a covering
   tag. Mirrors PG keeping a committed SERIALIZABLEXACT's predicate locks alive.

4. Write-path mid-statement abort. CheckForSerializableConflictInReportingFailure
   returns a *SerializationFailureError when the writer becomes the newly-doomed
   pivot with an out-conflict to an already-committed partner (predicate.c:4667,
   "Canceled on identification as a pivot, during write"). ssiRecordTupleWrite now
   returns that error; all seven write sites (insert x2, update-via-index,
   update-via-seqscan, delete, MERGE update/delete) propagate it so the statement
   fails in place (25P02). Deferred pivot dooms still surface at COMMIT as before.

vs PG 18.3. Regression-clean: total-cash/two-ids/simple-write-skew/read-write-unique
+ lock-committed{,keyupdate} + insert-conflict-do-update{,2,3,4}/do-nothing +

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): total-cash isolation spec passes — read-path SSI reader-kill now aborts MID-STATEMENT (40001) where PG 18.3 does, plus the index-UPDATE conflict-in sibling-path fix it surfaced
commits.description:
The read-only-anomaly variant total-cash aborts the reader DURING a SELECT
(rxy2), not at COMMIT: when an in-flight reader closes a dangerous structure to
an already-committed writer it cannot abort, PG ereports in place. goopg
previously deferred all dooms, so the read step printed its result and the error
landed on the reader's COMMIT — a timing mismatch.

mvcc: new CheckForSerializableConflictOutReportingFailure returns a
*SerializationFailureError when the reader must die now. reader.Doomed is set
ONLY by the read-path reader-kill arm of onConflictCheckLocked (the write path
dooms the WRITER; PreCommit dooms the pivot at commit), so it is an exact
predicate for mid-statement abort — covering both predicate.c's entry doom-check
(4032) and the OnConflict reader-kill (4676). No signature change to onConflict.

executor: ssiRecordTupleRead now returns an error (ssiReadAbortError → ExecError
40001); threaded through the three SERIALIZABLE read sites — seqScanOp.Next,
indexScanOp.Next, and the UPDATE/DELETE scanMatching loop — releasing any held
page RLock first. The statement aborts in place, marking the txn failed (25P02)
so the following COMMIT is a silent rollback, matching isolationtester output.

Sibling-path fix (root cause of the failing permutations): updateViaIndex (the
PRIMARY KEY / index-driven UPDATE path) never called ssiRecordTupleWrite, so a
SERIALIZABLE UPDATE found via an index installed NO write-path conflict-in edge
from concurrent SIREAD holders — unlike the seqscan path. total-cash's
wy2-before-rxy1 permutations therefore never formed the s1->s2 edge and the
reader-pivot 2-cycle was missing. updateViaIndex now records the conflict-in on
the old tuple's (rel,blk,slot) like the seqscan path; no-op for RC/RR.

Deferred pivot/write-skew dooms (the writer is the victim — two-ids /
simple-write-skew) leave reader.Doomed clear, so the hook returns nil and the
reader keeps running. All 20 total-cash permutations now byte-identical vs PG
18.3; the full UPDATE/MERGE/conflict isolation suite stays green.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): two-ids read-only-anomaly isolation spec passes — committed SERIALIZABLE xacts are RETAINED past commit so SSI raises 40001 on the multi-xact pivot where PG 18.3 does
commits.description:
The read-only anomaly in two-ids has the dangerous structure s3 →rw→ s2 →rw→ s1
where the pivot's out-conflict partner (s1) has ALREADY COMMITTED by the time the
closing s3 →rw→ s2 edge is drawn. goopg previously scrubbed a committed xact's
edges and deleted it at finish, so the s2 →rw→ s1 edge to committed s1 was gone —
a false negative (no 40001 at s2's commit).

Three coordinated mvcc changes (no executor/hot-path change), mirroring predicate.c:

- Retention: releaseSerializableLocked(handle, committed) keeps COMMITTED xacts in
  a new ssiState.finished pointer slice with rw-edges intact and the ConflictOut
  flag (SXACT_FLAG_CONFLICT_OUT) set; aborts still scrub+drop. xacts stays
  active-only (proc-slot handle reuse safe); edges address peers by pointer (no
  handle aliasing). serializableXactByXIDLocked scans finished, so a read of a
  committed writer's tuple still finds the writer.
- Overlap-scoped purge: BeginAt/FinishedAt share one dense counter;
  purgeFinishedSerializableLocked (run at register + finish) drops a retained xact
  once no active xact began before it finished — goopg's SxactGlobalXmin analogue.
- onConflictCheckLocked: port of OnConflict_CheckForSerializationFailure (cases 1-3)
  run at edge creation on both conflict hooks; deferred-doom of the transaction
  upstream would cancel (it fails at its own PreCommit). two-ids is entirely Case 2
  (doom the in-flight pivot), matching PG's all-at-COMMIT output.

Snapshot.XidIsConcurrent gate (load-bearing once retention is on): the read-path
conflict-out now skips a writer the reader already sees committed (writer committed
before the reader's pinned firstSnap) — an ordinary read, not an anti-dependency.
Mirrors predicate.c's XidIsConcurrent; without it two-ids' wx1 c1 rxwy2 … perm
raised a spurious 40001.

two-ids promoted to pass (TestPort_IsolationTwoIds, all 90 generated permutations
byte-identical vs PG 18.3). simple-write-skew + read-write-unique +
lock-committed-update regression PASS; mvcc -race PASS. total-cash (needs
mid-statement Case-3 reader-kill), project-manager/classroom-scheduling (need
phantom/empty-range predicate locking), and receipt-report (READ ONLY parser +
SSI modeling) remain deferred — see ledger + design doc 0118-0001.

commits.title: feat(M0118-0001): simple-write-skew isolation spec passes — runner auto-generates all permutations + SSI 40001 emits the bare upstream errmsg vs PG 18.3
commits.description:
Two engine fixes unblock the first M0118 SSI-anomaly slice and promote
simple-write-skew.spec to pass via TestPort_IsolationSimpleWriteSkew.

1. Auto-permutation generation (run_all_permutations parity).
   Most SSI anomaly specs declare NO explicit `permutation` lines, so upstream
   isolationtester.c run_all_permutations runs EVERY interleaving of the
   per-session step sequences (each session's steps in declaration order). The
   goopg runner previously left IsolationSpec.Permutations empty for those
   specs, ran zero permutations, and mis-reported every declared step as
   "unused step name" — an instant spurious defer. framework/isolation.go
   generateAllPermutations now mirrors run_all_permutations_recurse (pick the
   next unconsumed step from each session in declaration order, recurse, emit
   when all piles exhausted); the 6 interleavings of simple-write-skew match
   expected/simple-write-skew.out byte-for-byte.

2. SSI 40001 wire-message parity (clean errmsg + DETAIL).
   predicate.c emits a bare errmsg + a separate "Reason code:" DETAIL + a retry
   HINT, and isolationtester/psql print only the primary errmsg. goopg's
   commit-path abort built "<errmsg>: " + SerializationFailureError.Error(), and
   Error() itself appends the reason in parens — doubling and inlining the
   reason so it never matched the oracle. mvcc.SerializationFailureError now
   exposes PrimaryMessage() (bare errmsg) + Detail() ("Reason code: <reason>.");
   both wire seams (executor/ssi.go ssiPreCommitCheck, server/dispatch.go
   explicit-COMMIT path) emit the clean primary message with the reason as
   DETAIL and the retry HINT, matching operators_storage.go's during-write site.
   Error() is unchanged (its parenthesised reason stays for Go-side logging).

The 3+-transaction read-only / multi-version anomalies in the same family
(two-ids, total-cash, receipt-report, project-manager, classroom-scheduling)
still defer on an SSI dangerous-structure COMPLETENESS gap — a false-negative

dedicated TestPort_Isolation* functions are kept as t.Skip promotion anchors;

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): PRODUCTION fix — a unary-minus column/argument DEFAULT now round-trips byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3 instead of dumping a Go pointer string
commits.description:
Latent opcode bug in BOTH default-deparse twins. The parser tags a unary
minus `-x` with parser.OpUnaryNeg (select.go:2420), but
catalog.formatExprForAttrdef and executor.defaultExprToSQL each had only a
`case parser.OpSub` arm — and OpSub is BINARY subtraction `a - b`, a node the
parser never emits for a unary minus. So a real `DEFAULT -…` matched no arm
and fell through to fmt.Sprintf("%v", e), dumping a Go pointer string like
`&{0 - 0xc0001a2f00}` and corrupting every unary-minus default pg_dump
re-emits. The pre-existing unit test masked this by hand-constructing
UnaryOp{Op: OpSub} (a node the parser never produces) — a sibling-path
divergence where the unit test was green while the live deparse path was
broken (DU-002 slice 302).

Both twins now key on parser.OpUnaryNeg, mirroring PG's get_rule_expr:
- Bare numeric operand (`DEFAULT -5`): PG folds `- ICONST` into a negative
  typed Const at parse time (gram.y doNegate), deparsed by pg_get_expr as
  `'-5'::integer`. goopg is type-blind in this renderer so it emits the
  re-parseable `-5` (semantically identical; matching the `'-N'::type` cast
  needs the column/argument type — deferred to a later slice).
- Compound operand (`DEFAULT -(1 + 2)`, an OpExpr PG does NOT fold):
  get_rule_expr deparses `(- (operand))`; goopg now emits `"(- " + operand +
  ")"`, byte-identical to real pg_dump 18.3.

Guards (all green): unit twins TestFormatExprForAttrdefExpr /
TestDefaultExprToSQLBinaryParen (corrected to OpUnaryNeg; new literal +
compound cases). End-to-end TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (real pg_dump
18.3): table public.negdef pins `nb integer DEFAULT (- (1 + 2))` and
`nc integer DEFAULT ((- (1 + 2)) * 3)`; function
public.fneg(x integer DEFAULT (- (1 + 2))) pins the executor twin via
pg_get_function_arguments; plus a negative guard that the pre-fix
`DEFAULT &{` Go-pointer corruption does not appear.

feat(M0110-0001): a comma-literal function-call generation expression (concat(ka, ',', la)) inherited onto a partition leaf round-trips end-to-end vs real pg_dump 18.3 — the adversarial complement to slice 294, colliding the string literal '','' directly with the argument-separator comma to pin the TokenSymbol-gated spacing on the oracle path (DU-002 slice 295)
commits.description:
TEST-ONLY (no production change). Slice 294 proved a string literal whose body
is `-`; this slice makes the literal body BE A COMMA, so the literal `','`
collides directly with the argument-separator comma. The pre-slice-294
Value-based switch would have matched the literal token's `,` value against the
`,` separator case (noSpace) AND dropped its quotes, collapsing the three commas
into the malformed `concat(ka,,,la)`. Slice 294's TokenSymbol gating (the
symbol-only switch skips TokenStringLit) plus renderTok re-quoting render it
distinctly as `concat(ka, ',', la)`. This fixture pins that gating on the ORACLE
path: dumping a live goopg server, real pg_dump 18.3 reads goopg's stored source
verbatim, so the assertion pins goopg's own canonical rendering (no ::text cast;
out-of-scope pg_get_expr divergence). Table named pgkc (pgcc already taken).

Guards: TestGeneratedColumnExprCanonicalSpacing PASS (new case comma_literal_arg);
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup PASS (3.89s vs real pg_dump 18.3 — asserts pgkc_1
prints the inline na text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (concat(ka, ',', la)) STORED, the
malformed concat(ka,,,la) is ABSENT, attnum order, ATTACH survives).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): PRODUCTION fix — re-quote string-literal tokens in joinGeneratedExprTokens so a function-call generation expression with a string-literal argument (concat(ka, '-', la)) inherited onto a partition leaf round-trips end-to-end vs real pg_dump 18.3 (DU-002 slice 294)
commits.description:
Slices 291-293 pinned the call-paren/comma-spacing branches of
joinGeneratedExprTokens for IDENTIFIER arguments only. A string-literal
argument exposed a latent production bug: the lexer stores a literal's
UNQUOTED body ('-' -> Token.Value "-"), and the helper space-joined token
values raw, so concat(ka, '-', la) would have round-tripped as the malformed
concat(ka, -, la) (quotes dropped, literal indistinguishable from a minus
operator). Fix: a renderTok closure re-quotes TokenStringLit (doubling any
embedded single quote); the punctuation spacing rules are gated on TokenSymbol
so a literal body of )/,/(/. can't be mistaken for a punctuator. For the
operator/call/grouping-paren expressions of slices 283-293 (no string literals)
every punctuator is already a TokenSymbol, so the gating is a NO-OP there -
byte-identical output, zero regression. Because the test dumps a LIVE goopg
server, real pg_dump reads goopg's stored source verbatim, so the assertion
pins goopg's own canonical concat(ka, '-', la) (goopg does not add the ::text
cast real PG's pg_get_expr injects; out-of-scope divergence).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): wide multi-level partition tree (multiple leaves + sibling sub-partitioned middle node) round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 263)
commits.description:
Slice 171 first proved a sub-partitioned partition (psub_east: a LIST child of psub
partitioned BY RANGE, with one leaf psub_east_lo) — but the tree was a single chain:
one middle node, one leaf. This slice widens it to the two fan-out shapes a real
partition tree has, neither previously exercised end to end through pg_dump:

  (a) one middle node, MULTIPLE leaves — psub_east gains a second leaf
      psub_east_hi FOR VALUES FROM (100) TO (200) alongside psub_east_lo, so
      pg_inherits emits TWO child rows both pointing at the same psub_east parent;
      the per-parent inhseqno counter (parentSeq map in
      catalog.go::pg_inherits.VirtualRows) must increment independently per leaf,
      and pg_dump emits a separate ATTACH for each.
  (b) SIBLING sub-partitioned middle node — psub_west is a second LIST partition
      of psub, itself partitioned BY RANGE, with its own leaf psub_west_lo FOR
      VALUES FROM (0) TO (100). Crucially psub_west_lo's bound text is IDENTICAL to
      psub_east_lo's, so the leaf->parent link cannot be inferred from the bound —
      only from each child's own PartitionParentOID. The test verifies the
      immediate parent via the full single-line form
      "ALTER TABLE ONLY public.psub_west ATTACH PARTITION public.psub_west_lo
      FOR VALUES FROM (0) TO (100)", which a wrong-parent regression (attaching to
      the sibling psub_east or the grandparent psub) would break.

No production code changed — pg_inherits already keys each parent row off the
child's own PartitionParentOID (catalog.go ~4110), so width + a second middle node
fall out for free; this slice proves and guards the wide tree.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): dedicated MINVALUE/MAXVALUE keyword AST node disambiguates an unbounded RANGE-partition edge from a quoted text literal 'MINVALUE' (DU-002 slice 261)
commits.description:
Slice 169 captured the open-edge RANGE keywords by collapsing the bare
MINVALUE/MAXVALUE token into StringConst{Value:"MINVALUE"} — byte-identical to
the quoted text literal 'MINVALUE'. That collision was latent but real on two
paths: (1) at routing, compareRangeBoundStr inspected BOTH the key and the bound
string for the "MINVALUE"/"MAXVALUE" sentinel, so a row whose real text partition
key was literally "MINVALUE" was treated as -inf and mis-routed; (2) a real text
bound value 'MINVALUE' was indistinguishable from the unbounded edge. This slice
gives the unbounded edge its own node so the two are never confused.

- AST (expr.go): new PartitionRangeBoundKeyword{pos,IsMax} (false->MINVALUE/-inf,
  true->MAXVALUE/+inf) with Keyword(); distinct from StringConst.
- Parser (parsePartitionBoundValues, ddl.go): bare minvalue/maxvalue now emit the
  new node; a quoted 'MINVALUE' still flows through parseExpr to StringConst, so
  the two are finally separable.
- Catalog (catalog.go): new parallel []bool flags From/ToUnbounded[Max] on
  PartitionBound. Routing (FindRangePartitionForDatums -> rangeStrTupleGE/LT) now
  calls the rewritten compareKeyToRangeBound, which treats the KEY as a concrete
  value ALWAYS and consults the explicit flags for the bound edge.
  boundElemUnbounded/boundElemUnboundMax prefer the flags and fall back to the
  legacy bound-string sentinel for pre-slice-261 bounds (older in-memory bounds
  keep routing correctly).
- Executor (operators_ddl.go / operators_ddl_partition.go): exprToString,
  boundExprToSQLLiteral, rangeBoundExprToSQLLiteral handle the new node (replacing
  the StringConst.Value=="MINVALUE" checks); new rangeBoundUnboundedFlags derives
  the []bool flag tuples at partition-creation time; execCreatePartitionChild and
  execAlterTable populate pb.From/ToUnbounded[Max].
- No pg_dump-side change: FromValueLiterals still receives the uppercase
  MINVALUE/MAXVALUE so FormatPartitionBound emits the same FOR VALUES FROM
  (MINVALUE) TO ... as before.

Guards (3 levels): parser.TestPartitionRangeBoundKeywordDistinctFromStringConst
(bare keywords -> PartitionRangeBoundKeyword with the right IsMax, quoted
'MINVALUE' stays StringConst); catalog.TestCompareKeyToRangeBoundDisambiguation
(real text key "MINVALUE" compares as a concrete string not +/-inf, flag-driven
edges behave as +/-inf, nil flags fall back to the legacy sentinel); and the
existing prange_am fixture (FROM (MINVALUE) TO ('m')) in
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup continues to byte-match real pg_dump 18.3, proving
the keyword-node rewrite preserves the dump round-trip. parser+catalog+executor
suites PASS. Design: 0110-0001 Slice 261.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): parallel_workers storage parameter round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 195)
commits.description:
A table WITH (...) clause can carry multiple storage parameters, but goopg only
ever extracted fillfactor (slice 54): execCreateTable validated every WITH key
as lowercase, then read fillfactor alone and dropped any other recognized
reloption, so CREATE TABLE ... WITH (parallel_workers=4) succeeded but silently
lost the option (pg_class.reloptions stayed fillfactor-only/NULL; pg_dump never
re-emitted it).

Add parallel_workers as a second persisted reloption, mirroring the fillfactor
extraction (parse + bounds-check 0-1024 per PG reloptions.c heap entry) with one
key difference: 0 is a VALID explicit value (PG's reloption default is -1=unset),
so a zero-check cannot distinguish "set to 0" from "unset". catalog.Table now
carries both ParallelWorkers int and a ParallelWorkersSet bool guard; only the
flag decides whether the option surfaces. The pg_class virtual view builds an
ordered reloptions list (fillfactor first, then parallel_workers) ->
{fillfactor=70,parallel_workers=4}, which pg_dump's appendReloptionsArray renders
back as WITH (fillfactor='70', parallel_workers='4').

goopg has no parallel query, so parallel_workers is advisory catalog/dump-only
state (runtime unchanged, like slice 194's GeneratedVirtual). Base-table-only:
partitioned tables still reject WITH; the leaf-partition WITH path keeps
fillfactor only.

plain), TestParallelWorkersOutOfBoundsRejected (1025/99999 -> 22023), and the
pg_dump TAP fixture optpw asserting the combined WITH clause round-trips.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): VIRTUAL vs STORED generated-column strategy round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 194)
commits.description:
PG18 admits GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr) [STORED|VIRTUAL] (default VIRTUAL);
pg_dump keys on pg_attribute.attgenerated ('s' -> ... STORED, 'v' -> bare
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)). goopg parsed both keywords but discarded the
choice (attGeneratedFor hardcoded "s"), so a VIRTUAL column always dumped as
STORED. Record the declared strategy on catalog.Column.GeneratedVirtual
(STORED->false, VIRTUAL/bare->true per PG18 default), thread it through both
CREATE TABLE column paths (+ clear under INCLUDING GENERATED), and map it in
attGeneratedFor -> 'v'/'s'. goopg still materializes every generated column on
write; GeneratedVirtual is catalog/dump-only, runtime unchanged.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-leaf-partition USING access-method clause parses + round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 193)
commits.description:
PG's CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF grammar is OptPartitionSpec
table_access_method_clause OptWith OnCommitOption OptTableSpace, so a leaf
partition may carry a USING <method> clause between PARTITION BY and WITH. The
partition-child parser arm jumped from the optional PARTITION BY block straight
to WITH, leaving the USING token unconsumed -> syntax error (same sibling-path
gap as slices 191/192). Mirror the non-partition path: accept and discard the
method name. goopg has a single heap access method, so relam stays default and
pg_dump emits no USING clause; the child round-trips like an access-method-less
leaf.

(TestPartitionChildUsingClause, TestPartitionChildUsingBeforeWith),

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-leaf-partition TABLESPACE clause parses + round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 192)
commits.description:
PG's CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF grammar admits OptTableSpace (after
OptWith/OnCommitOption). The non-partition CREATE TABLE path already
accepts-and-discards TABLESPACE (storage manager does not honour tablespaces),
but the partition-child parser arm returned after WITH/ON COMMIT, so a trailing
`TABLESPACE name` left the token unconsumed and the whole statement failed with
a syntax error -- a divergence from both the main path and PG.

Mirror the main path in the partition-child arm: acceptKeyword(KwTablespace) +
parseIdent, discarding the name. reltablespace stays 0 (default sentinel), so
pg_dump emits no TABLESPACE clause and the child round-trips exactly like an
option-less leaf.

pg_dump fixture ptbs/ptbs_1 ... TABLESPACE pg_default with no-spurious-TABLESPACE/WITH
and ATTACH-bound assertions in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): extend attcollation/typcollation fix to array types (DU-002 slice 189)
commits.description:
Slice 188 set the heap pg_type.typcollation for the collatable scalars
(name/text/bpchar/varchar) + _text, but left _name(1003), _bpchar(1014),
_varchar(1015) at 0 — while executor.userTypeAttrsForOID already reports the
element-inherited collation for those array OIDs (_name->950, _bpchar/_varchar->100,
since a PG array inherits its element's typcollation). So a varchar[]/bpchar[]/
name[] column had attcollation=100/100/950 but heap typcollation=0, making
pg_dump's getTableAttrs (a.attcollation <> t.typcollation) fire and spuriously
emit COLLATE pg_catalog."default" on a column the user never collated — the
slice-187 regression, still latent for array columns (no prior fixture used one).

typcollation==attcollation invariant for the full collatable family. Audit
complete: no other built-in heap type is collatable.

three array OIDs; collarr fixture in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup asserts no
spurious COLLATE on default-collation array columns.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-column COLLATE round-trips + close slice-187 attcollation regression (DU-002 slice 188)
commits.description:
Two coupled fixes that make column collations round-trip through pg_dump.

(a) Capture explicit COLLATE: a column-level `COLLATE <name>` was parsed-and-
discarded. Now captured via parseCollationName onto ColumnDef.Collation, threaded
through both CREATE TABLE column paths to catalog.Column.Collation, and resolved to
its collation OID in the virtual pg_attribute row (collationNameToOID) so attcollation
reports it (collatable types only).

(b) Close the silent slice-187 regression of TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup: goopg's
virtual pg_attribute reported attcollation=100 for text/varchar/bpchar while the
bootstrapped pg_type heap hardcoded typcollation=0. Slice 187 populated pg_collation,
so findCollationByOid(100) began resolving and pg_dump spuriously emitted
`COLLATE pg_catalog."default"` on every collatable column. Fixed by setting heap
typcollation to PG-canonical values (pgTypeCollationForOID: name->950,
text/bpchar/varchar/_text->100, else 0) — matches pg_type.dat AND agrees with
executor.userTypeAttrsForOID's attcollation (sibling-path invariant). Default columns
now 100==100 (no clause); explicit COLLATE "C" -> 950<>100 -> COLLATE pg_catalog."C".

Tests: TestParseColumnDefCollation (parser capture incl. qualified/quoted forms),
TestPgTypeRowCanonicalTypcollation (heap typcollation at FormData offset 144), and the
collcol round-trip in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (PASS — was FAILING at HEAD).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): populate pg_collation virtual view with built-in collations (DU-002 slice 187)
commits.description:
The pg_collation virtual view (OID 3456) was a VirtualRows->nil stub, so
SELECT * FROM pg_collation / psql \dO / collation-OID joins saw an empty
relation (divergence from PG, which always has the BKI-pinned collations).

Populate VirtualRows with the 7 built-in collations from PG18's
pg_collation.dat: default(100), C(950), POSIX(951), ucs_basic(962),
unicode(963), pg_c_utf8(811), pg_unicode_fast(6411). collnamespace=11,
collowner=10, collisdeterministic=t, collicurules=NULL; libc rows carry
collcollate/collctype, builtin/ICU rows carry colllocale (+collversion=1
for builtin). Mirrors initdb's bootstrapPgCollationTuples seed; duplicated
in catalog.go because catalog cannot import initdb (cycle).

All OIDs < 16384 -> pg_dump skips them (no fixture output change); value is
\dO parity + prerequisite for per-column COLLATE round-trip (parser still
discards column COLLATE at internal/parser/ddl.go:2448).

New TestPgCollationVirtualRows pins row count, 12-column width, and the
full per-OID value vector against pg_collation.dat.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): close validateDefaultExpr compound-expr recursion gap (DU-002 slice 186)
commits.description:
validateDefaultExpr rejects column refs / aggregates / subqueries / SRFs in a
column DEFAULT but only recursed into FuncCall args, BinaryOp, UnaryOp, and
CastExpr. An offending leaf hidden inside a compound expression (ARRAY[…], CASE,
row constructor, IN-list, IS [NOT] NULL, IS DISTINCT FROM, COLLATE, subscript,
EXTRACT) slipped through, so goopg accepted DEFAULTs PostgreSQL rejects with
42P17 / 42803 / 0A000. The defcol fixture (slice 181) round-trips exactly these
compound shapes, which surfaced the gap.

Add recursion arms for ArrayConstructorExpr, RowExpr, CaseExpr (operand + each
WHEN/THEN + ELSE), InExpr (operand + list; populated subquery rejected),
IsNullExpr, IsBoolExpr, IsDistinctFromExpr, CollateExpr, ArraySubscriptExpr, and
ExtractExpr; fold ExistsExpr + ArraySubqueryExpr into the existing SubqueryExpr
rejection arm. Validation-only — no change to how a valid DEFAULT is stored or
evaluated.

TestDefaultExprRejectsNestedColumnRefs pins rejection across 12 compound forms;
TestDefaultExprAcceptsConstantCompounds guards against over-rejecting the
constant-only compound DEFAULTs the defcol fixture relies on.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-column SET (attoptions) round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 185)
commits.description:
ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN c SET (n_distinct=0.5, ...) now survives a
pg_dump round-trip. The fourth sibling of slices 182 (SET STORAGE) / 183
(SET COMPRESSION) / 184 (SET STATISTICS), this time for pg_attribute.attoptions.

pg_dump's dumpTableSchema renders array_to_string(a.attoptions, ', ') and emits
`ALTER TABLE ONLY <t> ALTER COLUMN <c> SET (...);` when non-empty. The parser
already had a `SET (` arm in the table ALTER-COLUMN path but consumed the
parenthesized block with a brace-depth counter and discarded the contents,
emitting a bare AlterTableAlterColumnSet the executor treated as a no-op;
buildUserPGAttributeRow hardcoded attoptions=NULL.

Fix (3 layers, mirroring 182/183/184):
- parser: parseColumnSetOptions replaces the discard loop, capturing each
  `name [=] value` normalized to PG's stored `name=value` form (leading `-` for
  negative n_distinct lexes as TokenOperator). New AlterTableAction.SetOptions.
- buildUserPGAttributeRow: emits the PG text-array literal `{opt1,opt2}` in
  attoptions when Column.Options is non-empty, else NULL. goopg's array_to_string
  (-> parseTextArray) consumes the `{...}` literal so the dump query renders
  identically to PG.
- AlterTableAlterColumnSet executor arm (was a no-op) copies act.SetOptions onto
  catalog.Column.Options AND flushes via delete-old-rows + syncTableToCatalogHeap
  (load-bearing: pg_dump scans the persisted pg_attribute heap).

RESET (...) left as the pre-existing no-op (pg_dump never emits it). Dump-fidelity
only; goopg does not act on n_distinct planner hints.

Tests: TestParseAlterTableSetColumnOptions, TestUserPGAttributeOptionsOverride,
and an optcol fixture in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (2 positive + 1 negative).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-column SET STATISTICS target round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 184)
commits.description:
Third sibling of slices 182 (SET STORAGE) / 183 (SET COMPRESSION), for
pg_attribute.attstattarget. pg_dump's dumpTableSchema emits
`ALTER TABLE ONLY <t> ALTER COLUMN <c> SET STATISTICS <n>;` whenever
attstattarget >= 0; the PG18 default NULL (decoded -1) emits nothing.

The parser had no SET STATISTICS arm in the table ALTER-COLUMN path (only the
ALTER INDEX expression-column path), so the clause fell through to the no-op
consumer; buildUserPGAttributeRow hardcoded attstattarget=NULL. Fixed in 3
layers, mirroring 182/183:

  1. Parser: new SET STATISTICS arm in the table ALTER-COLUMN path emits
     AlterTableSetStatistics{CheckExpr=value, ColumnName}. Leading `-`
     (SET STATISTICS -1 reset) accepted; `-` lexes as TokenOperator.
  2. buildUserPGAttributeRow: emits the integer in attstattarget when
     Column.StatTarget != nil && *>= 0, else NULL.
  3. AlterTableSetStatistics executor arm (table branch) parses CheckExpr,
     sets/clears Column.StatTarget (a *int: nil=unset, so SET STATISTICS 0 is
     distinguishable from never-set), and flushes via delete-old-rows +
     syncTableToCatalogHeap re-sync (load-bearing: pg_dump scans the persisted
     heap, not the live catalog object).

No CREATE TABLE threading (SET STATISTICS is ALTER-only). New field
catalog.Column.StatTarget *int. Dump-fidelity only (goopg does not sample
per-column statistics targets).

Tests: TestUserPGAttributeStatTargetOverride, TestParseAlterTableSetStatistics,
statcol fixture in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (2 positive + 1 negative).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-column COMPRESSION method round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 183)
commits.description:
The exact analogue of slice 182 (SET STORAGE) for the sibling pg_attribute
column attcompression. A per-column TOAST compression method — written inline
(`a text COMPRESSION lz4`) or via `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN c SET
COMPRESSION {pglz|lz4}` — was silently dropped from the dump. pg_dump's
dumpTableSchema reads a.attcompression and emits
`ALTER TABLE ONLY <t> ALTER COLUMN <c> SET COMPRESSION <method>;` whenever the
char is 'p' (pglz) or 'l' (lz4); the PG18 default '\0' emits nothing. goopg's
parser previously discarded the COMPRESSION keyword and buildUserPGAttributeRow
hardcoded attcompression="", so the method never reached the dump.

1. Parser: new normalizeCompressionMethod helper (pglz/lz4; default/unknown →

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): per-column SET STORAGE override round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 182)
commits.description:
pg_dump's dumpTableSchema emits `ALTER TABLE ONLY <t> ALTER COLUMN <c> SET
STORAGE <mode>;` only when a column's attstorage differs from its type's
typstorage. The parser accepted `ALTER COLUMN ... SET STORAGE` and the executor
recorded the strategy on catalog.Column.Storage, but two layers dropped it:

1. buildUserPGAttributeRow populated attstorage unconditionally from the type
   default, so attstorage always equalled typstorage and pg_dump never emitted
   the statement. New storageNameToAttCode helper maps

   when Column.Storage is set.
2. pg_attribute is a heap populated by syncTableToCatalogHeap at CREATE TABLE;
   the AlterTableSetStorage arm only mutated the in-memory catalog, leaving the
   stale heap row reporting the type default. The arm now flushes the override
   through the same delete-old-rows + syncTableToCatalogHeap re-sync path
   DROP COLUMN / SET NOT NULL use.

The per-element rangeBoundExprToSQLLiteral delegates to boundExprToSQLLiteral for

commits.description:
An UNLOGGED table now dumps as `CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE` instead of being

from tbl.Unlogged, and add indexPersistence(idx) so an index inherits its

does not change WAL/storage behaviour for unlogged tables here — only the
dumped DDL is corrected.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): RETURNS TABLE function round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 165)
commits.description:
goopg's parser desugars RETURNS TABLE(col type, ...) into trailing OUT args
(mode 'o') + RETURNS SETOF record. pg_dump renders functions from the
server-side deparsers pg_get_function_arguments + pg_get_function_result (both
used verbatim), so the table columns leaked into the arg list and the result
rendered as SETOF record:

  ret_tab(OUT id integer, OUT label text) RETURNS SETOF record

instead of upstream's:

  ret_tab() RETURNS TABLE(id integer, label text)

PG stores TABLE columns with proargmode='t'; print_function_arguments excludes
them and pg_get_function_result renders TABLE(name type, ...).

Fix (contained, zero execution-path risk): thread a ReturnsTable bool marker
parser->executor->catalog.Routine rather than introduce a new 't' argmode
(which would force every mode=="o" consumer — the planner's OUT-column
expansion, CALL exec — to learn it, risking a silent result-column regression).
Table columns stay stored as OUT args so the planner's OUT-column expansion is
unchanged; only the three deparsers in expr.go change, gated on r.ReturnsTable:
buildFunctionArguments (skip table cols, no IN/OUT prefix flip),
pg_get_function_result (new buildTableResult helper), and buildFunctionDef
(pg_get_functiondef sibling).

catalog suites PASS; new unit tests TestPgGetFunctionResultReturnsTable[NoArgs];

The other sibling -- goopg's format_type (executor/expr.go) -- already maps

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): array return type round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 162)
commits.description:

now round-trips through pg_dump. Slice 159 proved an array works as an ARGUMENT
type (VARIADIC arr integer[]), but the RETURN-type path was a separate, broken
code path — a sibling-path divergence.

Root cause: the parser stores an array type as the base name ("integer") with
IsArray set, not as "integer[]". The CREATE FUNCTION executor re-appends the

view's typeNameToOIDStr then resolved prorettype to the scalar element OID 23
instead of the array OID 1007, and pg_dump's format_type(prorettype) emitted
"RETURNS integer" — silently dropping the array.

Fix: compute the return-type name the same way as argument types (re-append
"[]" when s.ReturnType.IsArray) so prorettype=1007; format_type(1007) already
renders "integer[]" on the goopg server (slice 159 exercised the same OID).

value "-" in both row builders. TypedVirtualCell parses "-" as a non-integer and
falls back to StringConst("-"), so the wire text is exactly "-" and dumpFunc
suppresses the clause. The physical heap-backed pg_proc bootstrap catalog
already typed prosupport regproc (binary 0, correct on disk); only the virtual
view diverged.

The `$_$ SELECT $1 + 1 $_$` quoting is correct, not a bug: pg_dump escalates the
dollar-tag when the body contains a bare `$` (here the `$1` parameter).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): COMMENT ON FUNCTION round-trips through pg_dump (DU-002 slice 147)
commits.description:
Two coupled bugs blocked the round-trip:
1. parseCommentOnTail had no FUNCTION branch — the statement fell through to
   the unsupported default and the server silently swallowed it.
2. The load-bearing one: even after the comment reached pg_description under
   classoid=pg_proc (1255), pg_dump dropped it. collectComments matches a
   pg_description row to a dumpable object by {classoid, objoid}, and getFuncs
   records each function's catId.tableoid from pg_proc.tableoid. goopg's
   pg_proc is a virtual view whose Table struct never set OID, so its tableoid
   resolved to 0 (resolveTableoidForBinding returns b.table.OID); 1255 != 0 →
   no match → comment discarded. (TYPE/DOMAIN worked in slice 146 only because
   pg_type is heap-backed with OID=1247.)

Fix:
- parser: KwFunction branch reads parseObjectName + parseFunctionArgList into
  new CommentOnStmt.Args.
- executor: execCommentOn `function` case resolves the routine via
  Routines().Lookup and keys the row under pg_proc (1255).
- initdb: registerPgProcView sets OID: catalog.ProcedureRelationId (new const
  1255) so pg_proc.tableoid resolves correctly — also a latent fix for any tool
  joining/filtering pg_proc by tableoid.

Pure dump-fidelity; no catalog-schema change. Tests:
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup creates public.add_one(integer) + comment and
asserts `COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.add_one(integer) IS '…';` reappears verbatim

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): rewound sequence dumps setval(N,false) byte-identically (DU-002 slice 125)
commits.description:
setval(seq, N, false) with N != start rewinds a sequence's value to N
without marking it called. Real PG stores last_value=N / is_called=false,
so pg_dump keeps the schema CREATE SEQUENCE ... START WITH 5 and emits
SELECT pg_catalog.setval('public.rewound_seq', 30, false) in the data
section. SequenceRowData's not-called branch previously returned the bare
s.start, so goopg dumped setval(.., 5, false) — silently dropping the
rewind and corrupting restored continuity.

Fix: the not-called branch now returns current + increment. The registry
stores current = nextTarget - increment (RegisterSequence -> start-increment;
setval(N,false)/RESTART WITH N -> N-increment), so current+increment is the
exact on-disk last_value pg_dump reads (start for fresh, N after rewind).
SequenceRowData is the single shared function behind both SELECT * FROM <seq>
and the pg_get_sequence_data SRF, so both sibling paths are fixed in one place;
the pg_sequences view is unaffected (sources AllSequenceInfos, emits NULL
last_value while not-called).

Verified byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3. First production code change
in the sequence-dump slice series (115-125).

commits.description:

setval('public.bumped_seq', 42, true) the process-global seqRegistry state is
current=42/called=true, so SequenceRowData returns (42, true), the
pg_get_sequence_data SRF projects it, and pg_dump emits
SELECT pg_catalog.setval('public.bumped_seq', 42, true). The true is load-bearing
(restore continues at 43, not 1). No production code change -- SequenceRowData's
called=true branch already returns current as last_value; this is a regression
guard. Verified byte-identical vs real pg_dump 18.3. Exact (42, true) positive
assert + 3 negative guards rejecting (1,false)/(42,false)/(1,true).

Discovered (deferred to slice 125): SequenceRowData's called=false branch returns
s.start not current+increment, so setval(seq, N, false) with N != start diverges
from real pg_dump; fix touches shared pg_sequences view + SELECT * FROM <seq>.

identity sequence 'i' and the serial sequence 'a' on the same table; a
