Guarded by the enriched arr fixture (speeds real[], times time[], zoned
timestamptz[]) in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup and new rows in
TestUserPGAttributeArrayColumn.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): float8/date/timestamp array columns survive pg_dump (DU-002 slice 64)
commits.description:
Slice 63 mapped only bool/numeric/int2/int4/int8/text array element types, so a
`ratios double precision[]` / `days date[]` / `moments timestamp[]` column fell
back to its scalar element OID and dumped without the array dimension. The DDL
and heap-loader paths already route through catalog.ArrayOIDForBase/
BaseOIDForArray generically, so this slice only extends the three
element-type-keyed tables (identical proven 3-site pattern):

  1. catalog/codec.go: OIDArrayFloat8=1022, OIDArrayDate=1182,
     OIDArrayTimestamp=1115 consts + float8/date/timestamp cases in
     ArrayOIDForBase & its inverse BaseOIDForArray.
  2. executor/pg18_user_catalog_rows.go userTypeAttrsForOID: _float8/_timestamp
     rows use typalign 'd' (8-byte elements), _date uses 'i'; all typlen=-1,
     typstorage 'x'.
  3. executor/expr.go formatTypeOID: 1022->"double precision[]", 1182->"date[]",
     1115->"timestamp without time zone[]".

Element scalar OIDs (701/1082/1114) already existed; only the array mappings
were missing. Guarded by the enriched arr fixture (ratios double precision[],
days date[], moments timestamp[]) in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (passes via
the exit-0 path) and new rows in executor.TestUserPGAttributeArrayColumn.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): bool/numeric array columns survive pg_dump (DU-002 slice 63)
commits.description:
Slice 62 mapped only int2/int4/int8/text element types, so a `flags boolean[]`
or `prices numeric(10,2)[]` column fell back to its scalar element OID and dumped
as `boolean`/`numeric(10,2)`, losing the array dimension. The DDL and heap-loader
paths were already generic (ArrayOIDForBase/BaseOIDForArray), so this extends the
three element-type-keyed tables:

- catalog/codec.go: OIDArrayBool=1000, OIDArrayNumeric=1231 + bool/numeric cases
  in ArrayOIDForBase and BaseOIDForArray.
- executor/pg18_user_catalog_rows.go: _bool/_numeric rows in userTypeAttrsForOID.
- executor/expr.go: formatTypeOID renders 1000 as boolean[] and 1231 by recursing
  on the numeric element with the carried typmod, so numeric(10,2)[] round-trips
  precision/scale.

Guarded by the enriched arr fixture in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (exit-0
path, asserts genuinely run) and new bool/numeric cases in
TestUserPGAttributeArrayColumn.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): array column survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 62)
commits.description:
An array-typed column dumped as its bare element type (`tags text`, not
`tags text[]`): the parser captured the SQL `[]` suffix (ColumnType.IsArray)
but CREATE TABLE's addCol dropped it, so buildUserPGAttributeRow stored the
scalar element OID and pg_dump's format_type(atttypid,atttypmod) never rendered
the `[]` suffix.

catalog.Type now carries IsArray; addCol propagates it; buildUserPGAttributeRow
remaps the scalar OID to the array OID (text→_text 1009, int2→_int2 1005,
int4→_int4 1007, int8→_int8 1016) with attndims=1 while atttypmod still carries
the element typmod. userTypeAttrsForOID gains the four array OID cases.
loadUserTablesFromHeap reverse-maps the persisted array OID back to the element
type and re-flags IsArray so the column round-trips across restart. The runtime
evaluator is untouched (Type.Name still holds the element type).

Guarded by TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (arr fixture) and
executor.TestUserPGAttributeArrayColumn.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): RECURSIVE VIEW survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 61)
commits.description:
A CREATE RECURSIVE VIEW is dumped through the same pg_get_viewdef path as a
plain view, so a recursive view with an empty body aborts the WHOLE dump with
`definition of view "v" appears to be empty (length zero)` — the slice-57
blocker, repeated for the recursive parse path. parseCreateRecursiveViewTail
built the wrapped-CTE AST (for execution) but set NO RawDef, so pg_get_viewdef
returned NULL.

PostgreSQL stores a recursive view as a regular view over a WITH RECURSIVE CTE
and pg_dump re-emits it as a plain CREATE VIEW. goopg now mirrors that by
synthesizing the wrapped form into RawDef:
`WITH RECURSIVE name(cols) AS (<verbatim body>) SELECT cols FROM name`. The body
is captured verbatim via captureSrcSpan; the CTE header and outer projection
list the declared columns explicitly (no deparser — same documented fidelity
gap as the verbatim plain-view body). The leading WITH keyword means
applyViewColumnAliases bails (it only rewrites bodies starting with SELECT), so
the column names come solely from the synthesized projection.

Guarded end-to-end by TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (the foo_rec fixture, which
round-trips as `CREATE VIEW public.foo_rec AS WITH RECURSIVE ...`) and by
parser.TestParseCreateRecursiveViewRawDef.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): MATERIALIZED VIEW survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 60)
commits.description:
pg_dump dumps a materialized view's AS clause through the same
createViewAsClause -> pg_get_viewdef path as a plain view (pg_dump.c
dumpTableSchema RELKIND_MATVIEW branch emits `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW … AS
<body> WITH NO DATA;`) and aborts the WHOLE dump with `definition of view
appears to be empty (length zero)` when pg_get_viewdef returns NULL. goopg
already surfaces matviews in pg_class as relkind='m', but execCreateMatView
captured the body only as the SELECT AST (tbl.View, for REFRESH) and never as
raw text — tbl.ViewDef stayed "" — so any matview made the dump fail (the
slice-57 plain-VIEW bug, repeated for the matview parse path).

Fix (additive): CreateMatViewStmt gains a RawDef field, parseCreateMatViewTail
captures the verbatim body via captureSrcSpan (up to the optional WITH [NO]
DATA clause, mirroring parseCreateViewTail), and execCreateMatView stores it on
catalog.Table.ViewDef. pg_get_viewdef keys on View!=nil && ViewDef!="", so it
now echoes the matview body unchanged.

Guards: TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (foo_mv fixture, PASS first run);
parser.TestParseCreateMatViewRawDef. parser+executor+catalog suites PASS.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): GENERATED STORED column survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 59)
commits.description:
A GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr) STORED column dumped as a plain column — the
generation clause was silently dropped, a stored-vs-computed semantic loss on
restore. pg_dump (dumpTableSchema) prints the inline GENERATED clause only when
print_default is true, which requires BOTH pg_attribute.attgenerated='s' AND a
pg_attrdef row (tbinfo->attrdefs[j] != NULL); getTableAttrs forces separate=false
for generated columns so they stay inline. goopg already set attgenerated='s' but
left atthasdef=false (DefaultExpr nil) and emitted no pg_attrdef row for generated
columns.

Fix (2 sites): atthasdef now reports true when GeneratedExpr != "", and the
pg_attrdef virtual view emits a row for generated columns with adbin =
col.GeneratedExpr (a column is never both DEFAULT and GENERATED, so DefaultExpr
takes precedence). pg_get_expr passes adbin through verbatim, so the dumped clause
has single parens; PG's deparser may add normalizing parens — both restore to an
equivalent stored generated column.

Guarded end-to-end by TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup (new `gen` fixture table).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): VIEW explicit column-list survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 58)
commits.description:
A view created with an explicit column list (CREATE VIEW v (col_a, col_b) AS
SELECT id, name FROM foo) dumped as the underlying column names (id, name),
silently losing the declared names. PG's pg_get_viewdef bakes the names into
the select list as `expr AS cN`.

pg_get_viewdef now calls applyViewColumnAliases when the view has an explicit
column list (catalog.Table.ViewColumnAliases, already populated by CreateView).
It splices ` AS <name>` into the captured raw select-list text: finds the
top-level FROM boundary (paren/bracket + quote aware so EXTRACT(.. FROM ..) and
subqueries are safe), splits on top-level commas, quotes non-simple idents.
Bails to raw text (names lost) on count mismatch, `*`/`x.*`, or an item that
already carries a top-level AS alias — documented fidelity gaps.

Tests: executor.TestApplyViewColumnAliases (13 cases incl. every bail path);
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup asserts the renamed view round-trips
(CREATE VIEW public.foo_rview AS SELECT id AS col_a, name AS col_b FROM
public.foo;). Design doc 0110-0001 slice-58 entry + guard paragraph.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): VIEW survives pg_dump via pg_get_viewdef (DU-002 slice 57)
commits.description:
A single user VIEW made pg_dump abort the entire dump with
"definition of view appears to be empty (length zero)": createViewAsClause
calls pg_get_viewdef(oid), which goopg stubbed to NULL. Table DATA emitted
after the view never appeared either.

Fix captures the raw view body verbatim instead of building a full SQL
deparser: the parser now keeps the source string and a captureSrcSpan helper
slices the body span into CreateViewStmt.RawDef (trailing semicolon and
WITH CHECK OPTION excluded); execCreateView stores it on catalog.Table.ViewDef;
pg_get_viewdef resolves the arg by OID (pg_dump) or name (psql) and returns
ViewDef + ";" (pg_dump strips the trailing ';' and wraps it in CREATE VIEW
... AS <body>).

Fidelity gap (documented): raw text is not schema-qualified, so an unqualified
view would fail to restore under search_path=''; qualified views round-trip
cleanly. RECURSIVE/materialized views capture no RawDef yet (follow-up).

Tests: parser.TestParseCreateViewRawDef; TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup
fixture gains a CREATE VIEW and asserts it round-trips. parser/catalog/
executor/initdb suites green.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): secondary-index ASC/DESC + NULLS ordering survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 56)
commits.description:
A plain CREATE INDEX round-trips through pg_dump's getIndexes ->
pg_get_indexdef path, but goopg's parseIndexColumnList parsed and then
SILENTLY DISCARDED each key column's ASC/DESC + NULLS FIRST/LAST modifiers,
so `CREATE INDEX ... (col DESC)` round-tripped as an ascending index — a
silent semantic change.

Thread the ordering end-to-end, mirroring PG's pg_index.indoption:
- parser captures per-column IndexColOrder{Descending,NullsFirst} into
  CreateIndexStmt.ColOrders (NullsFirst pre-resolved to the DESC default
  unless an explicit NULLS clause overrides);
- catalog.Index gains parallel ColDescending/ColNullsFirst slices,
  populated by execCreateIndex only when non-default (a plain index keeps
  empty slices and dumps byte-identically);
- BuildIndexDef renders the ordering with ruleutils.c's default-suppression
  (DESC prints NULLS LAST only when overridden; ASC prints NULLS FIRST only
  when set).

Also fixes a latent parser bug: NULLS lexes as a bare ident, so the greedy
opclass-name detection mis-read `(col NULLS FIRST)` as opclass `nulls`.

Durability: indoption bits are not persisted to the on-disk pg_index heap,
so ordering is lost across a restart; pg_get_indexdef reads the in-memory
AllIndexes catalog, so the dump is faithful within a session (the test path).

Unit guards: parser.TestParseCreateIndexColOrders,
catalog.TestBuildIndexDefColOrder. TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup asserts a
plain, partial, and two ordered indexes all round-trip.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): COMMENT ON COLUMN survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 55)
commits.description:
pg_dump emits the canonical 3-part `COMMENT ON COLUMN schema.table.col`, but
goopg's parser handled only the bare 2-part `table.col`: parseObjectName
consumes two dotted parts and parseCommentOnTail's column case never read the
trailing `.col`, so the 3-part form raised "expected IS after object name". That
parse error was silently swallowed by the server's COMMENT no-op fallback, so
the column comment never reached pg_description and pg_dump dropped it. The TABLE
comment (2-part) already round-tripped.

Fix (parser-only): the column case now checks for a trailing `.col` after
parseObjectName — present means the parsed name is the (optionally
schema-qualified) table and the trailing identifier is the column; absent keeps
the 2-part table.col mapping. execCommentOn already resolved a schema-qualified
ObjName via LookupTable, so no executor change was needed.

Guards: internal/parser/comment_on_test.go TestParseCommentOnColumn (2- and
3-part forms); TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup now asserts both a TABLE and a
COLUMN comment round-trip through real pg_dump (exit 0).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): non-empty reloptions (fillfactor) survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 54)
commits.description:
WITH (fillfactor=N) was parsed and bounds-validated into CreateTableStmt.With
but never persisted on the catalog table, so the pg_class virtual view always
emitted "" (NULL) for reloptions and pg_dump produced a bare CREATE TABLE,
silently dropping the storage parameter. (Slice 47 had made an *empty*
reloptions read as NULL; this closes the complementary set case.)

Fix: (1) new catalog.Table.Fillfactor field; (2) the executor CREATE TABLE
path extracts s.With["fillfactor"], bounds-checks it (PG's 22023 for values
outside 10-100, mirroring the existing CREATE INDEX check), and assigns it;
(3) the pg_class virtual view's reloptions cell emits the text[] literal
{fillfactor=N} when set, "" otherwise. pg_dump's getTables reads the array,
nonemptyReloptions sees one element, and the dump renders WITH (fillfactor='70')
-- confirmed end-to-end by the real pg_dump binary in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup.

The fixture carries fillfactor on a dedicated public.opt table so the slice-47
"foo has no options" guard is unaffected (tightened to the exact empty-element
signature WITH (" so a legitimate fillfactor WITH clause does not trip it). The
slice also adds a cross-namespace regression guard: CREATE SCHEMA s + s.widget
round-trip byte-identically (already worked; now guarded).

Unit guards: executor.TestFillfactorSurfacesInPgClassReloptions,
executor.TestFillfactorOutOfBoundsRejected.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): table-level composite FOREIGN KEY survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 53)
commits.description:
A table-level `FOREIGN KEY (a, b) REFERENCES t (x, y)` in the CREATE TABLE
body was a parser no-op: the CONSTRAINT-named case skipped tokens to the next
comma/paren and there was no anonymous FOREIGN KEY branch at all, so composite
FKs never reached the catalog, pg_constraint, or pg_dump. The inline column
REFERENCES path only ever handled single-column FKs.

Fix (sibling paths kept in sync with the inline column path):
 - parser/ast.go: new TableForeignKeyDef AST node + CreateTableStmt.TableForeignKeys.
 - parser/ddl.go: new parseTableForeignKey(name) helper parsing
   FOREIGN KEY (cols) REFERENCES t [(refcols)] [ON DELETE/UPDATE action]
   [[NOT] DEFERRABLE [INITIALLY ...]], wired into both the CONSTRAINT-named
   case and a new anonymous table-level branch.
 - executor/operators_ddl.go: register each as a catalog.ForeignKey, auto-naming
   an anonymous FK <table>_<firstcol>_fkey (PG ChooseConstraintName convention).

No deparse/pg_constraint change was needed: buildForeignKeyDefString already
joins multiple columns and the conkey/confkey ordinal loops already iterate
fk.Columns/fk.RefColumns.

Guards: executor.TestCreateTableTableLevelCompositeForeignKey (anonymous+named
forms, multi-column conkey/confkey, composite deparse) and the pg_dump fixture
(bar composite PK + baz composite FK round-trip byte-identically through real
pg_dump in TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): FK referential actions survive pg_dump (DU-002 slice 52)
commits.description:
ON DELETE / ON UPDATE referential actions now survive pg_dump on both FK
declaration paths. The inline column-FK path already parsed and stored the
action (slice 51); the ALTER TABLE ADD FOREIGN KEY path dropped it at three
layers — the parser never consumed the ON DELETE/UPDATE clause (so the syntax
in fact errored before the comma/end-of-statement), the AlterTableAction AST
had no OnDelete/OnUpdate field, and the executor never set the catalog FK's
OnDelete/OnUpdate.

Fix mirrors the inline column path: (1) AlterTableAction gains OnDelete/OnUpdate
fields; (2) the ALTER parser parses the action clauses ahead of the [NOT]
DEFERRABLE trailer, reusing parseFKAction; (3) the executor copies them into the
catalog FK. With the catalog carrying the action, pg_constraint.confupdtype/
confdeltype (fkActionChar) and pg_get_constraintdef (fkActionClause, slice 51)
emit the clauses.

Fixture: inline self-FK now carries ON DELETE CASCADE; ALTER-added foo_mgr_fkey
carries ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL. Both round-trip byte-identically
(pg_get_constraintdef emits ON UPDATE before ON DELETE, mirroring ruleutils.c,
and omits the default NO ACTION).

Gates: gofmt/vet/build clean; parser+catalog+executor PASS;
TestAlterTableAddForeignKeyCapturesActions + TestForeignKeySurfacesInPgConstraint
PASS; TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup PASS (exit-0, both FK actions round-trip).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): FOREIGN KEY constraints survive pg_dump (DU-002 slice 51)
commits.description:
A column-level REFERENCES FK was silently dropped from pg_dump while a
sibling UNIQUE constraint dumped fine. pg_dump's getConstraints joins
pg_constraint ON conrelid WHERE contype='f' and renders each via
pg_get_constraintdef; goopg's catalog.ForeignKey carried no name/OID, so
pg_constraint emitted no contype='f' row and the join found nothing.

Fix (sibling paths kept in sync):
- catalog.ForeignKey gains Name+OID, auto-assigned <table>_<col>_fkey at
  DDL time in both the CREATE TABLE inline-REFERENCES path and the
  ALTER TABLE ADD FOREIGN KEY path (latter honours explicit name).
- pg_constraint.VirtualRows emits the contype='f' row: conkey/confkey
  ordinals, confrelid=referenced table OID, confupdtype/confdeltype via
  new fkActionChar helper, confmatchtype='s', conparentid=0.
- pg_get_constraintdef gains an FK branch (buildForeignKeyDefString)
  mirroring ruleutils.c: FOREIGN KEY (cols) REFERENCES public.tbl(refcols)
  fully schema-qualified (pg_dump runs with search_path=''), ON UPDATE/
  ON DELETE/DEFERRABLE appended only when non-default, MATCH SIMPLE omitted.

Fixture self-FK parent_id REFERENCES public.foo(id) now dumps as
ADD CONSTRAINT foo_parent_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES
public.foo(id). Unit guard executor.TestForeignKeySurfacesInPgConstraint;
integration guard TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): PK column implicit NOT NULL survives pg_dump (DU-002 slice 50)
commits.description:
PG18 pg_dump derives the inline NOT NULL clause from a contype='n'
pg_constraint LEFT JOIN (getTableAttrs / determineNotNullFlags), not from
attnotnull. goopg set the PK column's attnotnull=true but deliberately
excluded PK columns when registering named <table>_<col>_not_null
constraints, so the join found nothing and the column dumped as bare
`id integer` instead of `id integer NOT NULL`.

Verified against real PG18: `id integer PRIMARY KEY` materialises a
foo_id_not_null (contype='n', conkey={1}) constraint alongside foo_pkey.

Fix: drop the pkColSet exclusion on CREATE TABLE so every not-null column
(PK columns included) registers its named NOT NULL constraint, and add the
identical registration to the ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY sibling path
(which also flips attnotnull), guarding against a duplicate when the column
already carried a NOT NULL constraint.

TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup now asserts `id integer NOT NULL` survives
the dump. executor/catalog/initdb suites green; gofmt+vet clean.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): table CHECK constraints survive pg_dump (DU-002 slice 49)
commits.description:
A column-level CHECK was silently dropped from the dumped CREATE TABLE.
Two independent causes, both required:

1. pg_dump gates its per-table CHECK query on pg_class.relchecks > 0 and
   then asserts the returned row count equals relchecks (getTableAttrs).
   The user-table pg_class row hardcoded relchecks=0, so the query never
   ran. It now counts the table's visible NamedChecks (name+OID, exactly
   the set pg_constraint emits as contype='c'), so the count assertion
   holds.
2. pg_get_constraintdef(c.oid) handled only index-backed UNIQUE/PRIMARY
   KEY/EXCLUDE constraints and returned NULL for a contype='c' OID. It
   gained a CHECK branch that renders `CHECK ((expr))` (+ ` NO INHERIT`
   when set), mirroring PG's deparser's extra paren layer.

The fixture's `qty integer ... CHECK (qty >= 0)` now dumps as the
auto-named `CONSTRAINT foo_qty_check CHECK ((qty >= 0))`. The PRIMARY KEY
ADD CONSTRAINT path already worked and is now also asserted. Known
remaining divergence (next slice): implicit NOT NULL on a PRIMARY KEY
column (goopg dumps `id integer`, PG `id integer NOT NULL`).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): column type-modifier fidelity — pg_dump emits numeric(p,s)/varchar(n) (DU-002 slice 48)
commits.description:
buildUserPGAttributeRow hardcoded atttypmod=-1, so pg_dump's getTableAttrs —
which renders each column via format_type(atttypid, atttypmod) — printed every
typmod-bearing column as its bare base type (numeric(10,2)→numeric, character
varying(8)→character varying), a schema-fidelity loss.

New pgAttTypmod(typOID, args) computes the PG-canonical atttypmod from the
declared type args, mirroring the backend typmodin functions (numeric:
((p<<16)|s)+VARHDRSZ; character/character varying: n+VARHDRSZ; else -1).
formatTypeOID gained the numeric-typmod decode branch (the char/varchar decode
already existed), matching numerictypmodout. CREATE TABLE now reproduces the
declared precision/length faithfully.

Guards: executor.TestUserPGAttributeTypmod pins the atttypmod encoding and the
format_type round-trip; TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup fixture enriched with
amount numeric(10,2) + code character varying(8) asserting both survive the dump.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): array-typed virtual cell → NULL — pg_dump drops spurious WITH (DU-002 slice 47)
commits.description:
After slice 46 pg_dump exits 0 with the correct column list, but the dumped
CREATE TABLE still carried a spurious `WITH (""='')` reloptions clause. The
virtual pg_class view stores relacl/reloptions as "" (meaning NULL), but
planner.TypedVirtualCell had no case for array column types, so the empty cell
became StringConst("") — which goopg's array machinery parses as a single
empty-string element ({""}), so array_length(reloptions,1)=1. pg_dump's
getTables reads array_remove(array_remove(c.reloptions,…),…) and its
nonemptyReloptions test (strlen>2) saw {""} as non-empty, emitting WITH (""='').

Fix: TypedVirtualCell now maps an empty array-typed virtual cell (text[]/_text,
aclitem[]/_aclitem, oid[]/_oid, int2[]/int4[], char[], name[], float4[],
anyarray) to NullConst — PostgreSQL's convention for an absent reloptions /
default ACL — while a non-empty cell passes through as the array text literal.
The dumped CREATE TABLE is now byte-identical to upstream for a plain table
(no WITH clause). As the single type-conversion choke point, this also repairs
every other array-typed virtual-catalog column (proconfig, proacl, nspacl,
datacl, …) that previously decoded an absent value as {""}.

Guards: planner.TestTypedVirtualCell (empty text[]/aclitem[]/oid[]/_text → NULL;
non-empty {a,b} passes through) and the TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup no-`WITH (`
assertion. Verified end-to-end against a live goopg server: pg_dump emits a clean
`CREATE TABLE public.foo (id integer, name text);`.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): SRF-as-join-left projection offset — pg_dump emits column list (DU-002 slice 46)
commits.description:
pg_dump's getTableAttrs reads columns via
`unnest('{oid}'::oid[]) src JOIN pg_attribute a ON src.tbloid=a.attrelid`.
Slice 45 aligned the join key; the join still emitted a scrambled row and
pg_dump failed `invalid column numbering in table "foo"` (exit 1). The join
CONDITION resolved a.attrelid correctly, but the PROJECTION of right-side
columns was not shifted by the 1-column unnest (left) prefix — a.attname
returned attrelid (16403) and a.attnum returned attlen (4).

Root cause in planner buildBindingsPosMap (internal/planner/bushy.go): its
collect walker advanced the running offset `off` for *Values (and scans/
Project) but not for leaf FROM-clause set-returning / table-function nodes.
With `off` left too low, remapTopProjection shifted the right-side scan's
projection columns DOWN by the SRF's output width. Fix: FromUnnest,
GenerateSeries, GenerateSubscripts, UserSrfScan, ScalarFuncScan, and the Pg*
table functions now advance `off` by len(Output()), mirroring the *Values
case; their own columns need no remap (posMap returns the old index for
bindings absent from scanMap). Sibling-path fix: join-condition resolution
already offset via the binding table; projection went through
buildBindingsPosMap and did not.

pg_dump now reaches exit 0 AND emits the real column list (id integer,
name text).

Guards: planner.TestSRFJoinRightProjectionOffset (VALUES-left reference vs
unnest-left / generate_series-left projection-index parity); promoted
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup column-list assertion (id integer, name text).

commits.title: ci(ralph): per-run-unique data dir / log / cgroup scope in precommit gate
commits.description:
A respawned concurrent loop committing (and firing its own pre-commit gate)
while another commit runs collided on the fixed systemd scope name
("Unit ralph-precommit-goopg.scope was already loaded"), spuriously failing
the gate. Suffix the data dir, log, and scope with the PID so concurrent gate
runs stay independent — the free-port probe already handles the listen-port
half of the same hazard.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0001): typed unnest elements join catalog columns (DU-002 slice 45)
commits.description:
pg_dump's getTableAttrs reads a table's columns via
  FROM unnest('{oid}'::oid[]) AS src(tbloid)
  JOIN pg_attribute a ON src.tbloid = a.attrelid
but the join matched nothing: expandArrayDatum returns every array element as a
text KindString ("s:16403"), whose datumKey differs from the KindInt key an oid
catalog column (pg_attribute.attrelid, written via NewIntDatum) derives — so the
hash join bucketed the two sides apart and the dump emitted an empty column list.

coerceUnnestElem casts each element to its declared output-schema type
(oid/xid/int/float/numeric/bool family only; text-family stays a string; a cast
failure falls back to the raw element so a malformed synthetic array never aborts
the scan) before the row is materialised, in both the single-arg and multi-arg
unnest paths. With this the join key lines up and pg_attribute rows flow.

Guards: executor.TestCoerceUnnestElem_{JoinKeyParity,TextUnchanged,
NullPassthrough,BadValueFallsBack}. Executor pkg PASS; gofmt/build clean;
TestPort_PgDumpConnectionSetup PASS. tpch-spotcheck SKIPPED (no data dir).

Next blocker (slice 46, diagnosed): the join now matches but pg_dump fails
"invalid column numbering in table" — the projection of right-side columns is
not shifted by the 1-column unnest (left) prefix (join condition resolves

commits.title: ci(ralph): machine-enforce the pgbench CI-parity pre-commit gate
commits.description:
The Ralph loop committed once per slice after running only targeted
`go test`, and never the pgbench workload — so the pgbench TPC-B
concurrency-regression class (spurious 40001 / "current transaction is
aborted" under contention) reached CI undetected. The eventual fix was
landed by a separate manual session, not the loop's own gate, proving the
loop is structurally blind to the CI-parity workload.

Close the blind spot with an in-repo, machine-enforced gate:

- .githooks/pre-commit: runs the pgbench smoke on every commit
  (RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=smoke) and rejects the commit on failure.
- scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh: add RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE (full|smoke)
  to bound per-commit cost, plus a free-port probe so a stray server on the
  fixed port can no longer make pg_isready connect to the wrong server and
  mis-report the gate.
- Makefile: `make install-hooks` sets core.hooksPath=.githooks (idempotent).
- .ralph/AGENT.md, .ralph/PROMPT.md: document the enforced gate; mandate the
  pgbench smoke on every commit regardless of which files changed; forbid
  `git commit --no-verify`.
- analysis/ralph-pgbench-gate-enforcement-20260616.md: process-gap diagnosis.

up to planParent, mirroring the existing generate_series precedent. The
analyzer needed no change — tableFuncColumns builds the SRF output columns but
never resolves the arg expression. getForeignDataWrappers now passes

commits.title: fix(M0110-0003): LEFT JOIN inner-only pushdown shift/classify completion
commits.description:
The pg_amcheck exclude-pattern anti-join (--exclude-relation/--exclude-schema/
--exclude-table) panicked the backend: a general planner correctness bug.

Root cause is the recurring sibling-path divergence between the two LEFT JOIN
inner-only ON-conjunct pushdown helpers. classifyConjunctSide->walkColumnRefs
(pushdown.go) decides a conjunct is inner-only and pushable to a Filter on the
inner plan; shiftColumnRefsBy (planner.go) rebases its ColumnRef.Index by
-leftWidth once pushed. Both hand-enumerate Expr kinds in a switch, and several
sub-expression-bearing kinds were missing from one or both.

In pg_amcheck's `toast` exclusion CTE, the conjunct
  ('pg_toast' ~ ep.nsp_regex OR ep.nsp_regex IS NULL)
over a 5-col exclude_pat VALUES build relation: the `~` ref classified it
sideRight (pushed + shifted) but the IS NULL's inner ref was an *IsNullExpr that
shiftColumnRefsBy left at combined index 43 -> MaterializedSlot.Get(43) on a
width-5 row -> panic via joinOp.Open->drainRowsCtx->filterOp.Next.

Fix: add *IsNullExpr/*IsBoolExpr/*IsDistinctFromExpr/*CollateExpr/*RowExpr to
shiftColumnRefsBy, and the same set plus *CastExpr to walkColumnRefs. The
*CastExpr add to walkColumnRefs is the dangerous-direction twin: before it,
cast(outer.col)=inner.col hid the outer ref so a mixed conjunct could be wrongly
pushed below the LEFT JOIN. Generalizes 0097-0023.

Verified end-to-end on a live capped server: the 5-col VALUES anti-join CTE and
the real pg_amcheck --exclude-relation/--exclude-schema both exit 0 with no
panic in the server log. Test: planner/shift_colrefs_in_test.go
TestShiftColumnRefsByIsNullExpr. Design doc 0110-0011 + README index.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): AC-003 index missing-main-relation-fork detection
commits.description:
Port the index file-removal corruption tier of pg_amcheck's 003_check.pl:
a btree index whose backing file was removed on disk must be reported as
`index "<name>" lacks a main relation fork` (exit 2), mirroring upstream
bt_index_check_callback's smgrexists(MAIN_FORKNUM) guard (verify_nbtree.c:318).

Root cause fixed: goopg's smgr opens relation files with os.O_CREATE, so a
naive Pool.NBlocks on a removed fork silently RECREATED it as an empty
0-block file and the btree engine reported the index clean — a false negative
exactly where PG reports corruption.

- storage.Manager.Exists / Pool.Exists: stat-only fork-existence probe
  (pure os.Stat(relPath), never the O_CREATE relFile path). Every live rel
  always has an on-disk file, so a stat never false-negatives a live rel and
  never recreates a removed one.
- evalBtIndexCheck calls Pool.Exists before NBlocks; absent -> XX002
  (ERRCODE_INDEX_CORRUPTED) with the verbatim message. Covers both
  bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check.

filter ABOVE the lateral nested-loop, so verify_heapam was opened for every
pg_class row and raised "could not open relation" on the first non-heap
sibling (an index/sequence OID) before the filter could drop it — exit 2 on a
healthy target whenever the database held more than one relation.

conjunct (sideLeft by index range AND column name) onto the lateral join's
outer child, matching PostgreSQL's nested-loop qual placement. The outer child
occupies the join's leading columns so indices already align. collectScanOutputNames
is extracted as a shared helper and now covers the *Values node that backs
virtual catalog relations (pg_class). The pass is a no-op unless the residual
Filter's direct child is a Lateral join, so non-lateral shapes (all of TPC-H)
are untouched.

return exit 0 over a multi-table/indexed database (verified end-to-end).

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): AC-002 gap #7a — row-valued IS [NOT] NULL semantics
commits.description:
pg_amcheck's compile_database_list bootstrap query counts checkable
databases per inclusion pattern with COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d IS NOT
NULL), where `d` is a whole-row reference to a LEFT-OUTER-JOINed CTE.
The planner expands a whole-row variable into a RowExpr of its column
refs; the executor's IsNullExpr case evaluated that RowExpr to a
composite Datum and called Datum.IsNull() — but a constructed RowExpr
is never itself a NULL Datum, so `d IS NOT NULL` was wrongly true even
for an outer-join non-match (all fields null). Every inclusion pattern
therefore looked checkable and pg_amcheck never emitted the no-match
error, so `--database qqq` silently exited 0.

Apply SQL/PG row-null semantics to a RowExpr operand of IS [NOT] NULL
(evalRowNullTest): `row IS NULL` is true iff EVERY field is null,
`row IS NOT NULL` iff EVERY field is non-null — deliberately not
inverses, applied recursively to nested rows. An unmatched pattern's
include_pat.checkable now becomes 0 and pg_amcheck errors `no
connectable databases to check matching "<pat>"`.

This is a general correctness fix (row-valued IS [NOT] NULL now matches
PostgreSQL everywhere, not just in amcheck's query).

on the remaining gap #7c (per-database amcheck-installed detection).

table); 002_nonesuch patProbe end-to-end guard via real pg_amcheck.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): AC-002 gap #4 — CTE visible inside a FROM-subquery
commits.description:
A WITH-list CTE was not in scope when the planner resolved a
non-correlated derived table in the OUTER statement's FROM clause:

  WITH x(a) AS (SELECT 1) SELECT a FROM (SELECT a FROM x) s
  -> ERROR: relation "x" does not exist

The analyzer already handled this (resolveTable walks the parent
scope chain for CTEs). The bug was in the planner:
planSubqueryRangeVar's non-correlated branch (lateralCtx == nil)
re-planned the subquery via Plan(), which re-runs analyzer.Analyze
on the subquery STANDALONE — without the enclosing WITH scope — and
rejects the CTE reference as a missing relation.

Fix: route the non-correlated branch through
planSelectWithParent(rv.Subquery, cat, nil), mirroring the lateral
branch. It skips the analyzer re-pass (the outer Plan() already
analyzed the whole tree under the correct scope) and inherits the
package-level planCTEs map, so the CTE substitutes in.

two-level nesting, end-to-end).

("public".verify_heapam(...)), which goopg's parser rejects (only
unqualified FROM-clause table functions parse). 002_nonesuch now
self-skips via a new gap-#5 preflight probe; gap #5 is its own loop.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): amcheck SQL surface S5 — named-argument (:= / =>) parsing
commits.description:
pg_amcheck emits its amcheck calls with the legacy `name := value`
named-argument spelling:
  bt_index_check(index := c.oid, heapallindexed := false)
  bt_index_parent_check(index := c.oid, heapallindexed := false, rootdescend := false)
  verify_heapam(relation := c.oid, on_error_stop := false, check_toast := false,
                skip := 'none', startblock := N, endblock := N)   -- FROM-clause SRF

goopg already stripped the modern `name => value` spelling positionally
(M0097-0003), but only:
  - for `=>`, not `:=`, and

    FROM-clause SRF arg loop (parseRangeVar), the sibling path.

Both paths now accept `:=`/`=>` and strip the name, mapping positionally.
The verify_heapam executor's positional order (relation, on_error_stop,
check_toast, skip, startblock, endblock) and bt_index_check's (index first)
already match pg_amcheck's named order, so the strip binds correctly.

The argument name may be an unreserved keyword (e.g. `index`, `skip`), so the
token check accepts TokenKeyword too — unambiguous because the `:=`/`=>`
lookahead gates it (new shared helper isNamedArgNameToken).

commits.title: fix(M0110-0010): btree vacuum relinks live siblings on adjacent-leaf deletion
commits.description:
VacuumIndexPages deletes every leaf emptied by dead-tuple pruning in two
phases: PHASE 1 stamps BTDeleted|BTHalfDead and records the leaf's captured
btpo_prev/btpo_next; PHASE 2 (unlinkEmptyLeaf / unlinkEmptyLeafFPI) relinks
neighbours from those captured pointers. When an ADJACENT run of leaves is
emptied in one pass (the common case for a range DELETE + VACUUM), a captured
neighbour is itself a leaf deleted in the same pass: for L0->L1->L2->L3->L4
with L1,L2,L3 emptied, the survivors L0.next and L4.prev end up pointing at
the deleted block L2. The on-disk leaf sibling chain is left structurally
broken; amcheck's sibling-link tier correctly flags "points to deleted block".

Fix (mirrors PostgreSQL _bt_unlink_halfdead_page): a new liveSibling() walk
skips any BTDeleted/BTHalfDead page and relinks the nearest LIVE left/right
sibling. Two facts make a simple skip-walk correct and order-independent:
PHASE 1 stamps every target leaf BEFORE any unlink runs, and recycleBlock does
not wipe the page, so the chain through dead pages stays navigable. Both the
WAL-emitting path and the FPI fallback share the computation (sibling paths
stay in agreement), and it is also correct for CompleteDeferredDeletions, which
iterates by block number rather than chain order.

No WAL format change: the BtreeUnlinkPage record already carries arbitrary
LeftSibBlk/RightSibBlk/LeftSibNewNext/RightSibNewPrev and replayBtreeUnlinkPage
applies whatever blocks the record names; only the computed values change.

Discovered by the real-producer page-deletion validation (M0110-0003).
- TestVerifyBtreeEngineDetectsStaleSiblingLinkAfterAdjacentLeafDeletion flipped
  to silence: TestVerifyBtreeEngineSilentAfterAdjacentLeafDeletion (DoD).
- New storage-layer regression
  TestVacuumIndexPagesAdjacentLeafRunRelinksLiveSiblings asserts every survivor
  links only to live blocks and the chain is bidirectionally intact.

commits.title: feat(M0117-0007): CLOG async-commit LSN tracking (gap G8 Part A)
commits.description:
Effort-L async-commit durability change on CLOG (highest-blast-radius
subsystem), decomposed. Part A lands PG's per-LSN-group commit-LSN tracking
(group_lsn) + the XLogFlush-before-page-write barrier on the M0117-0006 buffer
pool as composing infrastructure, WITHOUT a live caller (the pool is not yet the
live store — M0117-0006 Part B deferred), so blast radius is nil. The live
synchronous_commit=off activation (Part B) defers WITH M0117-0006 Part B, to a
dedicated session that can run the full TPC-H/recovery gate, per the m0074
central/high-risk precedent.

- internal/mvcc/clog_bufferpool.go:
  - clogXactsPerLSNGroup=32, clogLSNsPerPage=clogXactsPerPage/32=1024,
    lsnIndexInPage (= PG GetLSNIndex minus the slotno*CLOG_LSNS_PER_PAGE base,
    since each clogPageSlot carries its own groupLSN[1024]uint64).
  - clogPageSlot.groupLSN []uint64, zeroed on every fault-in (in-memory only,
    never persisted — an on-disk page's WAL is already durable, group LSN
    invalid).

  - groupLSNFor read side (== the *lsn out-param of TransactionIdGetStatus).
  - flushWAL func(uint64) error injected hook (nil ⇒ off, default); the
    eviction path (pinPageLocked) and flushDirty call it with the page's max

commits.title: feat(M0117-0005): CLOG incremental flush + group commit (gap G7)
commits.description:
Part A — incremental flat-file flush. setStatus no longer rewrites the whole
global/pg_xact file on every single-XID commit (O(N) per commit). It records
the touched 8 kB flat page (clogFlatPageSize, always wholly inside one bank)
in a dirtyPages set; the durable write replays only those pages with WriteAt.
The flat file stays un-fsynced (the fsynced pg_xact/ SLRU is the source of
truth; MarkUnknownAsAborted repairs the cache after a crash). The bulk callers
(InitializeAsCommitted, MarkUnknownAsAborted, TruncateCLOG) keep the whole-file
rewrite, which now takes flushMu and clears dirtyPages.

Part B (clog_groupcommit.go) — a faithful Go port of
clog.c:TransactionGroupUpdateXidStatus: concurrent committers CAS-push a
{xid,status,done} node onto a Treiber stack (atomic.Pointer head ≙
ProcGlobal->clogGroupFirst); the first arrival is the leader, takes flushMu,
Swaps the whole stack to nil in one atomic op (ABA-free), applies the batch
durably (one incremental flat-page pass + one fsync per touched SLRU segment
instead of one per XID, OR lane semantics ≙ TransactionIdSetStatusBit), drops
the lock, then wakes every follower's done channel. goopg serialises all
durable writes on one flushMu, so PG's same-page grouping restriction is
dropped (the leader batches across pages/segments freely).

All new CLog fields are zero-value-ready, so &CLog{}/OpenCLog need no
constructor change. Pinned by clog_groupcommit_test.go (2000 concurrent
committers → durable flat reopen + SLRU-only reconstruction; incremental vs
whole-file flat equivalence; dirty-set drain/idempotency).

commits.title: feat(M0117-0004): SUB_COMMITTED (0x03) CLOG lane (gap G5 SUB_COMMITTED)
commits.description:
Teach goopg's PG-byte-compatible pg_xact/ SLRU mirror the fourth 2-bit lane
value, 0x03 = TRANSACTION_STATUS_SUB_COMMITTED (clog.h:30): a subtransaction
that committed while its parent top-level XID is still in progress. Before
this change TxnStatus had only Unknown/Committed/Aborted, the 0x03 lane was
never written, and loadFromSLRU decoded any 0x03 as Committed with a defensive
OR-artifact comment — conflating PG's real "resolve via parent" state with
corruption and leaving the mirror unable to round-trip a sub-committed subxact
(blocking durable subxact resolution for an attached PG standby / 2PC /
post-backend-exit readers).

- Add TxnStatusSubCommitted = 3 (raw byte equals the on-disk lane so the
  flat-file and SLRU encodings agree) + pgClogStatusSubCommitted = 0x03.
- Write seam: mirrorToSLRUUnlocked + batched mirrorTerminalRangeBatchedUnlocked
  emit 0x03; new public primitive CLog.SetSubCommitted(xid) routes through
  setStatus (flat file + SLRU), mirroring SetCommitted/SetAborted.
- Read seam: loadFromSLRU decodes 0x03 -> SubCommitted (was -> Committed).
- Resolution: CLog.DidCommit(xid, parentOf) mirrors transam.c
  TransactionIdDidCommit — Committed->true, Aborted/Unknown->false,
  SubCommitted->recurse on the parent link (the M0117-0003 SubxactMap supplies
  parentOf; nil/zero parent -> false per PG's missing-pg_subtrans-entry branch;
  bounded by a visited set against cyclic links).

OR mirror semantics are deliberately kept (not switched to PG's clear-then-set):
OR preserves a durable committed bit against a stale in-memory abort, and the
0x03 it can produce resolves identically to the old "treat as committed" intent.
Visibility (SeesCommittedXID, M0117-0002) only flips on a positive Aborted, so a
bare SubCommitted read stays conservatively "assume committed" — the change
cannot make a live tuple less visible. Non-goal: SUB_COMMITTED->COMMITTED
finalisation (PG's two-pass tree write) is deferred; no live caller wires
SetSubCommitted yet (encode/decode + resolution machinery only, like the
M0117-0002/0003 primitives).

Design: docs/design/0117-0004-clog-sub-committed-lane.md (+ README index).
Pinned by the extended clog_dual_store_consistency_test.go (all four lane
values round-trip flat-file <-> SLRU + DidCommit parent resolution) and new
TestCLogSubCommittedResolvesViaParent.

commits.title: feat(M0117-0003): pg_subtrans restore-on-restart (gap G5 read path)
commits.description:
M0117 added a write path to a PG-byte-compatible pg_subtrans SLRU mirror
(SubtransSLRU.SetParent, opted in via SubxactMap.EnablePersistence) but
nothing read it back on startup, and the Manager's runtime subxact store
(subxactParents) never touched the SLRU — so the persistence machinery was
dead in production and subxact parentage was lost across a restart.

- SubtransSLRU.ScanParents: walk every %04X segment, decode 4-byte slots,
  invert the subtransLocate page/segment arithmetic to recover each
  subxid->parent; skip zero/bootstrap slots and non-normal parents.
- SubxactMap.RestoreFromSLRU: merge the scan into the in-memory parents map
  under lock; error if persistence is disabled (loud mis-wire).
- Manager.SetSubxactMap (mirrors SetCLog): when a map is attached the Manager
  routes RegisterSubXid/MarkSubxactAborted/TopLevelXid/IsAborted/IsSubxact
  through it (registration writes through to the SLRU, PG-faithful per
  subtrans.c SubTransSetParent). Stored in an atomic.Pointer so the per-tuple
  TupleVisibleSubxact hot path stays lock-free; nil (every existing caller and
  test) is byte-identical to v0.
- initdb.Open: create the map, EnablePersistence(<datadir>/pg_subtrans),
  RestoreFromSLRU, attach — before any query runs.

Deliberately diverges from PG's StartupSUBTRANS zero-on-startup: G5 consumers
(durable standby resolution / 2PC / post-backend-exit readers) need durable
parentage. Conservative — parentage only redirects a sub-XID to its top-level
ancestor; the ancestor's own commit/abort decision is unchanged, so it never
makes a tuple more visible.

Known follow-ups: no pg_subtrans truncation yet; SUB_COMMITTED lane is
M0117-0004.

commits.title: feat(M0117-0002): runtime CLOG-consulting visibility fallback (gap G4)
commits.description:
Snapshot.SeesCommittedXID only consulted the proc-array snapshot plus the
in-memory Aborted array (M0100-0002). An in-window XID not in InProgress and
not in that array was *assumed committed*. The Aborted array is rebuilt empty
on restart — it is NOT the durable commit log — so after a restart a recovered
rolled-back row could read as committed at runtime (recovery consults the CLOG
when re-scanning the heap, but the runtime snapshot path did not). Gap G4.

Add an optional *CLog to Snapshot (Snapshot.WithCLog / Manager.SetCLog, attached
in captureSnapshot) and consult it in the [Xmin,Xmax) residual case. Conservative
contract: only a positive TxnStatusAborted flips visibility to invisible;
TxnStatusCommitted and TxnStatusUnknown fall through to the unchanged v0 "assume
committed" default. goopg's runtime commit path does not write CLOG (only
recovery/bootstrap do), so the fallback is a strict no-op for runtime-new XIDs
(status Unknown) and cannot regress the live OLTP/TPC-H path, while correctly
hiding recovered aborts the in-memory array forgot. Sub-OldestClogXid XIDs skip
the consult via the wraparound-safe storage.XIDPrecedes (M0117-0001).

Sibling audit (visibility.go <-> subxact_visibility.go): SeesCommittedXIDWith-
Subxacts resolves to the top-level ancestor then delegates to snap.SeesCommittedXID,
so it inherits the fallback with no separate edit; Clone() carries the CLOG.
nil CLOG (no SetCLog call) => byte-identical to prior behaviour.

Mirrors PG HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC's TransactionIdDidCommit/DidAbort consult.

commits.title: fix(M0110-0007): btree split relinks old right sibling's prev-link
commits.description:
On a non-rightmost split, insertIntoBlock spliced the new right page
between L and its old right sibling S but never updated S.btpo_prev,
leaving the doubly-linked sibling chain half-relinked on any non-append
insert pattern. btpo_prev is load-bearing (page deletion reads op.Prev
and WAL-logs RightSibNewPrev to relink siblings), so the stale left-link
was a real on-disk correctness gap.

Fix mirrors PostgreSQL _bt_split: relink S.btpo_prev = rightBlk under the
same atomic split WAL record, which now carries an optional third page
(btreeSplitHeaderSize 18->22 with a SibBlk field; replayBtreeSplit
WriteBlocks it on recovery). Lock order strictly left->right
(blk -> rightBlk -> oldNext), deadlock-free. On-disk page format
unchanged; only the WAL record format changed.

commits.title: fix(storage): MAXALIGN vacuum repack offsets (amcheck found PG-standby segfault)
commits.description:
The amcheck heap engine's per-page tests inject corruption by hand (the only
way to write damage), leaving a complementary risk untested: does the engine
stay silent on pages produced by goopg's real on-disk mutators? New
internal/amcheck/verify_heapam_realpage_test.go (6 tests) drives the real
producers — same-page HOT chain (PageStampHotOldTuple + heap-only successor,
mirroring tryApplyHOTUpdate), the chain after PageSetItemIDRedirect pruning, a
VacuumHeapPage-pruned page, a NewHeapTupleWithNulls nullable multi-attr tuple,
the HOT chain through the clog tier, and the whole-relation driver — asserting
zero false-positive findings.

The vacuumed-page test failed and exposed a real latent bug:
storage.VacuumHeapPageBySlots repacked surviving tuples with `upper -= len(body)`
without MAXALIGN, producing non-8-byte-aligned line-pointer offsets. Its sibling
PageAddHeapTuple deliberately MAXALIGNs because (M0106-0010) a non-aligned offset
segfaults a PG18 standby's heap_deform_tuple on the first SELECT; the engine
faithfully ports PG's "not maximally aligned" check and correctly flagged it.

Fix: `upper -= maxAlign8(len(e.body))` in the repack loop — restores
sibling-path agreement (pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree). Vacuum only removes
tuples and survivors were inserted with the same alignment, so the aligned
repack can never overflow the page.

green (wal = replay shares the repack kernel). Design doc 0110-0005 extended.

commits.title: fix(ralph): state-guard self-heals prev-loop clean-exit marker
commits.description:
The every-loop `make ralph-state-guard` failure (status=running vs
progress=completed, loops #5-#11) was misdiagnosed as concurrent-loop
corruption. ppid analysis confirms a single --live loop. Real cause: the
driver writes progress={"status":"completed"} after every clean claude exit
(ralph_loop.sh "Clear progress file") — meaning "this loop's claude finished",
not "project done". The next loop sets status=running without touching
progress, so the steady state during any loop is status=running (loop N) +
progress=completed (loop N-1 marker), which the guard flagged as corruption.
Prior loops' manual progress restore was stomped on the next exit → recurred.

Add an autoRepair rule (the complement of the existing stale-status rule):
when a completed progress is NOT newer than a live running status by > max-skew,
reconcile progress -> in_progress (the live status is authoritative). The guard
now self-heals via its -fix pass with no manual edits. Genuine project
completion is unaffected (status is completed/graceful_exit, not running).

3 new tests; design doc root-0018; MAINT-STATEGUARD-RECONCILE in fix_plan.

(status=running vs progress=completed) and the auto-repair rule did not match
because the two timestamps are ~simultaneous (status 03:49:04 UTC = 12:49:04
JST, progress 12:48:59 JST), not the >2min stale-completed pattern it guards.

Restore progress.json to in_progress (consistent with the running loop and the
incomplete fix_plan) so the guard passes again. Also gitignore the stray
root-level `validate-ralph-state` ELF (a 3.2 MB `go build ./cmd/...` output;

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): amcheck heapallindexed fingerprint+probe core (verify_nbtree)
commits.description:
Ports the heapallindexed logic of bt_check_every_level/bt_tuple_present_callback
(postgres/contrib/amcheck/verify_nbtree.c) into internal/amcheck as
heapallindexed.go (VerifyBtreeHeapAllIndexed) — the last B-tree verification
tier, consuming the loop-#60 Bloom primitive. Pure function over two
btree.LeafEntry slices: fingerprints every index leaf entry into a filter sized
to the exact count, then probes the index tuple each live heap tuple would form;
emits one BtreeReport (verbatim upstream message + heap block) per lacking entry.
Sound via the filter's no-false-negatives contract — a healthy heap tuple is
never flagged; false positives only mask a <2% fraction of real misses.

One fingerprintLeafEntry (TID.Block big-endian ++ TID.Offset ++ key bytes)
drives both the fingerprint and probe phases, so a present (key, TID) hashes
identically on both sides (sibling-path invariant). New exported
btree.PageLeafEntries is the canonical leaf reader the wire-later fingerprint
phase uses — expands posting-list items to one entry per heap TID (unlike
PageItemKeys, which collapses to one separator key), beside PageItemKeys/
PageDownlinks as single source of truth against v3->v4 layout drift.

Divergences: no bt_normalize_tuple step (goopg does not TOAST index keys, so
leaf and heap-formed key bytes are already one canonical EncodeXxxKey form), and
the Bloom seed is a parameter (caller randomizes per run, tests pin it).

Engine-first/wire-later, new files only — zero contaminated files touched. The
B-tree verification engine is now logic-complete; only the SQL surface (blocked
on a clean tree) remains. 6 amcheck tests + 1 btree TestPageLeafEntries.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): amcheck Bloom filter primitive (heapallindexed)
commits.description:

+ .h) into internal/amcheck as bloomfilter.go -- the foundational primitive
for the last remaining B-tree verification tier, heapallindexed. The filter

coupling, so it lands engine-first/wire-later in new files only (zero

importing it would entangle amcheck with the executor package, and the

halves avalanched for the double-hashing split).

spurious corruption report), realistic-regime FP rate <5%, seed-distinguishes

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): B-tree item-count ceiling tier (verify_nbtree)
commits.description:

(verify_nbtree.c:3396-3402) as the third internal/amcheck B-tree tier,
folded into VerifyBtreePage after the level checks (upstream order).

goopg's index tuple (keyLen|block|offset|key) is stored unaligned, so the
ceiling differs from PG's MaxIndexTuplesPerPage. Compute it from goopg's own
per-item footprint and export as btree.MaxItemsPerPage =
(BlockSize-SizeOfPageHeaderData)/(4+itemPrefixSize) = 680, defined beside
itemPrefixSize as the single source of truth. Message is upstream-verbatim
with the goopg constant.

Divergences handled: the bound ignores the per-page opaque area (like upstream,
extra headroom -> no false positives); the check is skipped on deleted pages
(goopg returns earlier; deleted pages hold no live items; avoids type-punned
fields), whereas upstream checks them; a non-itemIDSize pd_lower surfaces as a
damaged-page finding, never a panic.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): bt_target_page_check item-order/high-key tier (verify_nbtree)
commits.description:
Add VerifyBtreeItemOrder, the second internal/amcheck B-tree index tier,
porting bt_target_page_check's two page-local key invariants
(verify_nbtree.c:1565-1642): the item-order invariant (items strictly
ascending) and the high-key invariant (each key <= the high key on a leaf,
strictly < on an internal page). Upstream corruption messages are mirrored
verbatim ("item order invariant violated for index %s", "high key invariant
violated for index %s") so the later SQL surface and 003_check port reuse them.

Keys are decoded through a new exported btree.PageItemKeys (one separator key
per physical line pointer, collapsing a posting-list item's many TIDs to its
single shared key) and compared with btree.CompareKeys -- the same comparator
the live index uses -- keeping the inline 2-byte-length item layout (a v3->v4
drift hazard) a single source of truth, the same discipline as ParseMeta/
ParseOpaque.

goopg/PG divergences handled faithfully: the high key lives in the opaque
special area (no P_HIKEY slot to skip; rightmost gating via
Next==InvalidBlockNumber), and an internal page's leftmost negative-infinity
downlink has an empty key that satisfies both invariants without a special
case (empty < every real separator), mirroring upstream's zero-attribute
negative-infinity tuple.

Engine-first/wire-later: the SQL surface (CREATE EXTENSION amcheck +
verify_heapam SRF + bt_index_check) remains deferred until the working tree is
clean. All changes are new code or additive exports; zero contaminated files
touched.

Tests: 10 new amcheck tests (new makeItemsPage builder, each self-checked
through the real readers) + 1 new btree TestPageItemKeys (posting-collapse).
internal/amcheck and internal/access/btree suites PASS; gofmt/vet clean.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): page-structural bt_index_check (verify_nbtree) engine
commits.description:
Start the B-tree index-side companion to the verify_heapam engine, since
pg_amcheck runs bt_index_check() on every index (003_check/005_opclass_damage
exercise it), so the AC-002 promotion needs it too.

internal/amcheck/verify_nbtree.go (VerifyBtreePage) ports the page-structural
palloc_btree_page tier from postgres/contrib/amcheck/verify_nbtree.c: metapage
(block 0) magic/version validation and leaf/internal page-level consistency,
with deleted pages exempt; corruption messages are byte-for-byte upstream
(incl. the in index "%s" clause, supplied as a parameter).

To avoid re-decoding goopg's metapage/opaque format (changed v3->v4 — a
sibling-path drift hazard), add purely-additive exported accessors to the
uncontaminated internal/access/btree/btree.go: BTreeMagic, BTreeVersion,
ParseMeta, ParseOpaque, and a BTPageOpaque.IsDeleted method. The engine reads
goopg's layout solely through these.

PG-divergent checks documented as NOT ported: high-key-as-item-P_HIKEY (goopg
keeps the high key in the opaque area) and the MaxIndexTuplesPerPage ceiling
(goopg's inline index-tuple layout needs its own size accounting).

10 new unit tests (hand-built clean/corrupt pages, each self-checked through
the real decoders); btree package tests still pass; gofmt/vet clean. Design
doc 0110-0005 + README index extended. All net-new code lands in new files;
the SQL surface remains deferred on a clean tree.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): page-structural HOT-chain tier in verify_heapam engine
commits.description:
Extend internal/amcheck.VerifyHeapPage with the page-structural subset of
upstream verify_heapam.c's HOT (update) chain validation: VerifyHeapPage now
takes the page's block number and builds successor[]/predecessor[] arrays to
detect a redirect that does not point at a heap-only tuple, intersecting HOT
chains (redirect and normal cases), and HOT-updated/heap-only flag mismatches
across a chain link. All five messages are upstream-verbatim.

goopg divergences handled: t_ctid.block is a plain uint32 at off+12 (not PG's
bi_hi/bi_lo BlockIdData split); HEAP_HOT_UPDATED/HEAP_ONLY_TUPLE live in
t_infomask. A normal->normal link forms only on curr_xmax==next_xmin && !=0
(non-multi update xid); a multi xmax is skipped (goopg has no on-disk multixact).

The clog-dependent HOT-chain checks (xmin commit-status across a link and
root-of-chain-but-heap-only) stay deferred — they need per-tuple commit status.

8 new unit tests (5 corruption + 3 false-positive guards incl. cross-block
CTID); 23 total PASS. Design doc 0110-0005 extended. All changes in new files
under internal/amcheck/.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0003): infomask-only header invariants in verify_heapam engine
commits.description:
Extend internal/amcheck's VerifyHeapPage with the two check_tuple_header
invariants decidable from the tuple header bytes alone (no clog/TupleDesc/toast):

  - multixact xmax must not be hint-bit committed
    (HEAP_XMAX_COMMITTED | HEAP_XMAX_IS_MULTI)
  - a HOT-updated tuple must carry a valid xmax ("... but xmax is 0")

Messages mirror verify_heapam.c verbatim for later SRF/004_verify_heapam reuse.

goopg packs HEAP_HOT_UPDATED/HEAP_ONLY_TUPLE into t_infomask (not t_infomask2
like upstream; see storage/prune.go + heap_update), so the HOT check reads
goopg's field. HEAP_XMAX_IS_MULTI (0x1000) is defined locally since goopg has no
on-disk multixact and never sets it — fires only on injected corruption (zero
false positives). The heap-only-but-not-updated invariant is intentionally NOT
ported: goopg never sets HEAP_UPDATED (reuses 0x2000 for HeapKeysUpdated in
t_infomask2), so a verbatim port would false-positive on every healthy HOT
successor.

15 unit tests PASS (4 new, incl. two false-positive guards). Design doc
0110-0005 extended. All in new internal/amcheck/ files; SQL surface still
deferred to a clean tree.

commits.title: feat(M0110-0004): batch CLOG implicit-abort SLRU mirror; enable pg_resetwal maximal-override restart (RW-002 a)
commits.description:
The maximal SLRU-derived-override final restart in
TestPort_PgResetwal001BasicServer was deferred because it appeared to hang.

Root cause: pg_resetwal --next-transaction-id advances NextXID ~1M past the
bootstrap pg_xact segment, so on the next initdb.Open the implicit-abort sweep
(CLog.MarkUnknownAsAborted over [1, NextXID)) stamps ~1M XIDs, and the old
per-XID SLRU mirror (mirrorToSLRUUnlocked) called f.Sync() on every one →
~1M fsyncs → startup looked hung (~20s+).

Fix: remove the per-XID mirror from the sweep's hot loop. After the in-memory
stamping pass, CLog.mirrorTerminalRangeBatchedUnlocked projects the whole
swept range into the pg_xact/ SLRU segment files with ONE fsync per
~1M-XID segment, OR-merging onto existing bytes (mirrors PG
TransactionIdSetStatusBit; idempotent; byte-identical final state; skips
xid<FirstNormalTransactionID per the PG lane-zero invariant).

The maximal-override restart is now enabled and passes (2.5s, no hang).
RW-002 remainder: only the unclean-shutdown/--force branch (no goopg v0 crash
state) — stays defer.

Tests: TestCLogMarkUnknownAsAbortedBatchedSLRU (cross-segment regression);
all 3 TestPort_PgResetwal* PASS; go test -race ./internal/mvcc ./internal/initdb PASS.

commits.title: docs(M0110-0004): deferral-ledger line for RW-002 remainder
feat(M0110-0004): clean-shutdown DB_SHUTDOWNED state; port pg_resetwal server tier (RW-003)
commits.description:
Root cause: wal.Checkpointer.runCheckpoint unconditionally stamped
pg_control State=DB_IN_PRODUCTION on every checkpoint, including the final
shutdown checkpoint in Runtime.Close. After a clean `goopg stop`,
pg_controldata reported "in production" and upstream pg_resetwal refused
without --force ("database server was not shut down cleanly") — the sole
blocker for the pg_control read/write round-trip tier of RW-002.

Fix (mirrors PG CreateCheckPoint(CHECKPOINT_IS_SHUTDOWN), xlog.c):
- runCheckpoint gains a `shutdown` flag selecting DBStateShutdowned vs
  DBStateInProduction for the on-disk State byte.
- New Checkpointer.CheckpointShutdown() runs the checkpoint with shutdown=true.
- Runtime.Close calls CheckpointShutdown() for the final durable checkpoint
  (no WAL after it). The earlier OnStop checkpoint stays DB_IN_PRODUCTION so a
  crash in the OnStop->Close window remains correctly flagged unclean.

goopg startup replays WAL regardless of State (no startup path branches on it),
so clean restart, SELECT, and crash recovery are unaffected (verified).

Test port (RW-003 -> port): TestPort_PgResetwal001BasicServer drives upstream
pg_resetwal against a real goopg cluster — PGDATA 0700/0600 perms, `-n`
checkpoint dump, postmaster.pid lock refusal while running, `--pgdata` reset
WITHOUT --force after clean shutdown, SELECT 1 after reset, --next-oid 100000
override + spot-check, restart after override. RW-002 narrowed to the
unclean-shutdown/--force branch (no goopg crash state in v0) + SLRU-derived id
overrides + 002_corrupted.

Also: TestCheckpointerShutdownSetsDBShutdowned unit test; CSV/md regenerated;
design doc 0110-0004 updated.

Gates: go build ./...; go test -race ./internal/wal ./internal/control
./internal/initdb (PASS); TestPort_PgResetwal001 (both tiers PASS);
TestPort_Recovery (PASS); ralph-state-guard (PASS).

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): flip initdb --data-checksums default false→true (regress-gated)
commits.description:
goopg `init` now defaults data page checksums ON for both `-k` and
`--data-checksums`, matching upstream PG 18 (initdb commit 04bec894).
`--no-data-checksums` still overrides (useDataChecksums = *dataChecksums &&
!*noDataChecksums, unchanged).

Both validation gates already landed (gate (a) crash-recovery/FPI replay,
gate (b) cross-impl standby read). The default flip changes the on-disk format
of every new cluster, so per the M0106 "codec/format change → re-run full
suite" lesson it was gated by re-running the entire regress-port suite on a
checksummed data dir:

  go test -timeout 3000s -run TestPort_RegressSuite ./internal/testport/
  → ok ... 2618.543s (0 unexpected diffs)

A per-page CRC trailer cannot change query output — its only failure mode is a
checksum-verification error on read, which aborts a query rather than returning
a wrong row count, so the suite's clean run IS the read-path validation.

Design doc 0102-0019 + README index marked complete; M0102-0010 closed.

commits.title: test(M0102-0010): gate (b) checksummed goopg primary → real PG standby verifies pd_checksum
commits.description:
Lands the standby-read / physical-replication validation gate (the last of
two) for the --data-checksums default-ON flip. A --data-checksums goopg
primary fills ~115 heap pages, CHECKPOINTs them to disk before the clone,
then pg_basebackup -X streams the cluster to a real PostgreSQL standby. PG
inherits goopg's version-1 pg_control (SHOW data_checksums = on) and verifies
pd_checksum on every page read; a full seq-scan returning the exact 4000 rows
+ sum(length(payload)) proves goopg's FNV-1a checksum bytes are byte-identical
to upstream's. A mismatch would abort the scan with 'invalid page in block N'
— the cross-implementation proof gate (a) (goopg-verifies-goopg) cannot give.

- internal/testport/e2e_checksum_replication_test.go: new
  TestE2E_ChecksumStreamingGoopgToPG (PASS 2.45s vs real PG binaries; skipped
  under -short / GOOPG_SKIP_M0102_E2E / missing PG binaries).
- internal/testutil/cluster/cluster.go: additive Options.InitArgs threads
  extra 'init' args (--data-checksums); empty default = byte-identical.
- docs/design/0102-0019: gate (b) DONE; both flip-gates now pass; the one-line
  default-ON flip stays deferred to a dedicated regress+TPC-H-gated loop.

commits.title: test(M0102-0010): validate checksummed cluster survives crash recovery (FPI replay)
commits.description:
Adds TestCrashRecoveryReplaysChecksummedClusterCleanly — gate (a) of two
for the deferred --data-checksums default-ON flip. Runs the SIGKILL /
WAL-replay sequence on a DataChecksums=true cluster and proves every
recovered page is checksum-valid two ways: the post-recovery btree reads
go through the checksum-enabled Manager (a bad replayed page surfaces as
*ChecksumError, not a wrong answer) and an on-disk VerifyPage walk
re-checks every populated block's pd_checksum.

This is the architectural proof that the FPI restore path
(restoreDecodedXLogBlockImage -> writeBlockOrExtend -> Manager.WriteBlock
-> checksummedForWrite) recomputes the checksum per replayed block rather
than writing a stale image verbatim or bypassing the checksum write seam.

Default stays OFF; the flip remains gated on (b) standby-read / physical-
replication validation. Design doc 0102-0019 updated (gate (a) DONE,
gate (b) pending).

Gates: gofmt/vet clean; go test ./internal/initdb PASS;
go test -race ./internal/storage ./internal/wal PASS.

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): enable initdb --data-checksums via offline stamp pass
commits.description:
Land the user-facing -k/--data-checksums enablement. Rather than thread the
cluster checksum flag through the ~40 scattered direct bootstrap page-write
sites (a missed site = silent unbootable cluster), stamp checksums in one
offline pass after bootstrap completes — stampClusterChecksums, mirroring
pg_checksums --enable: walk global/+base/<db>/, and for every relfilenode file
(relFileNamePattern) run each block through the loop-#30 checksumRelationData
and rewrite in place. Non-relation metadata (PG_VERSION, pg_filenode.map,
pg_internal.init, pg_control, CLOG/WAL) is named non-numerically / lives
elsewhere so the strict numeric filter never touches it.

Init calls it (guarded by opts.DataChecksums) after writePgControl and before
the trailing fsync; the Init reject is removed. CLI registers
-k/--data-checksums/--no-data-checksums (--no-data-checksums overrides -k).
Default stays OFF (byte-identical bootstrap, structurally guaranteed by the
guard); the PG-18 default-ON flip is deferred until recovery/replication
validation.

Tests: TestInitDataChecksumsBootstrapsVerifiablePages (e2e boot — every
relation page verifies under the off/BlockSize convention + reads block 0 of
pg_type/pg_class/pg_attribute through a checksummed Manager) and
TestInitCommandDataChecksums (CLI flags drive pg_control version). Design doc
0102-0019 + README index updated.

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): add bootstrap data-checksum routing primitive
commits.description:
checksumRelationData(raw, enabled) is the single helper the ~50 direct
os.WriteFile bootstrap page-write sites will route through to make a
--data-checksums cluster bootable. Disabled (the default, and the only
reachable mode while Init rejects --data-checksums) returns the input
slice verbatim — byte-identical to a plain WriteFile. Enabled returns a
copy with pd_checksum stamped into every BlockSize block, built on the
loop-#29 storage.PageSetChecksumCopy engine.

The block number folded into each checksum is derived from the block's
byte offset within the file (off/BlockSize), matching how the runtime
smgr verifies a block on read. One helper is therefore uniform across
single-page heaps, multi-page heaps, and multi-page btree files with no
per-site block-number bookkeeping. New/all-zero pages pass through
unchanged (upstream PageIsNew). The multi-page numbering and
never-mutate-input invariants are proven in isolation by
checksum_bootstrap_test.go (5 cases incl. transposition rejection and
partial-tail-verbatim), de-risking the eventual site sweep.

The ~50-site sweep + e2e boot test + dropping the Init reject + CLI flags
+ PG-18 default-ON flip remain (deferral ledger 2026-06-13). Design doc
0102-0019 updated with the routing-primitive and remaining-sweep sections.

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): add data-page checksum engine (initdb option deferred)
commits.description:
Land the reusable data-page-checksum engine, the high-blast-radius core of
initdb --data-checksums. Defer the user-facing option: a bootable checksummed
cluster needs pd_checksum on ~38 distinct direct os.WriteFile bootstrap
page-write sites (no shared helper), so Init rejects --data-checksums until
that exhaustive wiring + an e2e boot test land.

Engine (all default-OFF → byte-identical; verified by TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=33):
- storage/checksum.go: PageSetChecksumCopy (copy-then-set, never mutates the
  shared buffer) + VerifyPage (checksum half of PageIsVerifiedExtended).
- storage/smgr.go: ManagerConfig.{ChecksumsEnabled,IgnoreChecksumFailure,
  OnChecksumFailure} wired at the relFile level — the lowest seam shared by
  the sync (readBlock/writeBlock/extend/extendBatch) and AIO (ReadAt/WriteAt)
  paths, where the block number is always known. Writes emit a checksummed
  copy; reads verify and return *ChecksumError on mismatch (non-fatal under
  IgnoreChecksumFailure). Disabled = one bool check, no copy/verify/alloc.
- control/pgcontrol.go: expose DataChecksumVersion (offset 252), preserved
  across UpdateControlFile.
- initdb/pgcontrol.go: buildPgControl/writePgControl write 1/0 at offset 252.
- initdb/open.go + wal/recovery.go: read the field to enable the Manager.

Tests: storage/checksum_io_test.go (round-trip, corruption detection,
ignore-failure, disabled=byte-identical, ExtendBatch, new-page skip);
initdb/data_checksums_test.go (version 1/0; Init reject).
Design doc: docs/design/0102-0019-initdb-data-checksums.md.

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): add initdb --locale-provider/--locale/--lc-* options
commits.description:
Adds the libc + builtin collation-provider option family to goopg init,
porting the validation logic from PostgreSQL's initdb.c (setlocales,
setup_locale_encoding, check_locale_encoding, and the main() option-
combination checks). New internal/initdb/locale.go: resolveLocaleProvider,
pgGetEncodingFromLocale (codeset-suffix port for a frontend that cannot
setlocale), checkLocaleEncoding, and resolveLocale (combo checks, builtin
canonicalization C/C.UTF-8/PG_UNICODE_FAST, ICU rejection, builtin-UTF8
requirement). Options gains LocaleProvider/Locale/LC*/BuiltinLocale/
ICULocale/ICURules with matching long-form init CLI flags. Init validates
up front before any layout; seedPostgresqlConf seeds lc_* GUCs first;
bootstrapPostgresDatabase writes datlocprovider/datcollate/datctype/
datlocale (no-option default byte-identical to the prior libc/C row, no
format change). icu provider recognized but rejected (no USE_ICU build);
locale-derived default encoding still deferred (fixed C/UTF8 locale).
Closes the always-run non-ICU locale cases of 001_initdb.pl. On-disk
PG-compat only. Ninth initdb-option gap closed under M0102-0010.

Design: docs/design/0102-0018-initdb-locale-options.md
Tests: internal/initdb/locale_test.go, cmd/goopg/main_test.go

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): add initdb -E/--encoding default-encoding option
commits.description:
Ports encnames.c name handling (clean_encoding_name, pg_char_to_encoding
with the full pg_encname_tbl alias set + NAMEDATALEN guard,
pg_valid_server_encoding, pg_encoding_to_char) and initdb.c get_encoding_id
into a new internal/initdb/encoding.go. Adds Options.Encoding + the
-E/--encoding CLI flag; Init validates the name up front (before auth/layout)
and threads the resolved pg_enc ID into bootstrapPostgresDatabase, which writes
it into pg_database.encoding for all three seeded databases instead of the
hard-coded PG_UTF8 (6). Client-only encodings (SJIS/BIG5/GBK/UHC/GB18030/JOHAB/
SHIFT_JIS_2004) and unknown names are rejected with initdb's exact wording.

Scope: name validation + ID mapping only. The locale-derived default encoding
and the check_locale_encoding/check_icu_locale_encoding mismatch checks are
deferred with the --locale family (goopg's fixed C/UTF8 locale makes them
no-ops). No server-side encoding enforcement (on-disk PG-compat, like the
0102-0016 pwfile verifier). No on-disk format change.

Design doc: docs/design/0102-0017-initdb-encoding-option.md.
Tests: internal/initdb/encoding_test.go, pg_database_encoding_test.go,
cmd/goopg/main_test.go (TestInitCommandEncoding).

commits.title: feat(M0102-0010): add initdb -A/--auth, --auth-host/--auth-local, --pwfile
commits.description:
Auth bootstrap for goopg init: choose the pg_hba.conf authentication
methods and set the bootstrap superuser password from a file.

New internal/initdb/auth_bootstrap.go:
- resolveAuthMethods ports check_authmethod_unspecified (default trust +
  warning), the ident<->peer cross-map (initdb.c:3255-3258),
  check_authmethod_valid, and check_need_password (both sides a password
  method without --pwfile -> "must specify a password"); validated up
  front before any filesystem layout.
- buildPgHBAConf(host,local) substitutes the methods into the local and
  loopback-host rules (external 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 stay reject);
  defaultPgHBAConf() now delegates to buildPgHBAConf("trust","trust")
  (byte-identical default).
- readSuperuserPasswordFile ports get_su_pwd (first line, CRLF strip,
  empty/unreadable -> error).
- encodeSuperuserPassword builds the pg_authid.rolpassword verifier
  (auth.NewSCRAMSecret(...).String() by default, auth.MD5Shadow when md5
  chosen per initdb.c:1402-1413) and returns the password_encryption GUC
  value (md5 only).

Wiring: Options.AuthMethodHost/AuthMethodLocal/PwFile; Init overwrites
pg_hba.conf after SampleFiles, threads password_encryption through
seedPostgresqlConf (new arg), and writes the verifier into the OID-10
superuser row via bootstrapPostgresRoleWithPassword (non-NULL text, so
HEAP_HASNULL stays clear). CLI: -A/--auth sets both sides;
--auth-host/--auth-local override one side; --pwfile. -W/--pwprompt is
out of scope (non-interactive). Exported auth.MD5Shadow as the single
source of truth for the md5 rolpassword form.

auth does not yet read rolpassword, so the verifier is for on-disk PG
compatibility. No on-disk format change. Seventh initdb-option gap closed

commits.description:

fsync, so the relaxed modes are flushed durably. Net on-disk result is
identical to upstream's create-at-group-mode, satisfying 001_initdb.pl's
check_mode_recursive($datadir, 0750, 0640). log_file_mode is seeded
before the -c/--set loop so an explicit override still wins. No on-disk
format change; default path unchanged. Completes the entire 001_initdb.pl

commits.title: fix(ralph-guard): parse tz-less timestamps as local, not UTC
commits.description:
parseTimestamp in cmd/validate-ralph-state parsed the tz-less progress.json
format ("2006-01-02 15:04:05") via time.Parse, which assumes UTC. The Ralph
loop driver writes progress.json wall clocks in local time, so on a non-UTC
host (JST) a local progress timestamp parsed as UTC looked ~9h ahead of the
RFC3339-UTC status.json timestamp, tripping a spurious "progress newer than
status" skew error and blocking `make ralph-state-guard` for multiple loops
(#14/#15).

Use time.ParseInLocation(..., time.Local) for the tz-less layouts; RFC3339
still resolves via time.Parse since it carries its own offset. Adds two
regression tests covering the local-zone parse and the cross-zone validate
path.
