commits.title: feat(M0097-0024): run COPY FROM STDIN inline in multi-statement \; batches
commits.description:
Thread the connection FrameReader down handleQueryOrCopy → handleQuery →
dispatchSimpleQueryViaExecutor → runInlineCopy so a COPY FROM STDIN inside a
psql \;-joined batch can read its CopyData/CopyDone frames synchronously
mid-batch. New runInlineCopyFromStdin writes CopyInResponse+flush, pushes
text/binary rows through the CopyFromExecutor (skipping the \. EOD marker),
and writes only CommandComplete — no commit, no RFQ: the COPY shares the
batch's txn (committed once at the end) and the dispatch loop emits the single
trailing RFQ. CopyFail/decode errors abort the batch via errQueryErrorSent.

Closes the COPY-FROM-STDIN-in-batch gap for copyselect (select * from test3
now returns rows 1,2 byte-for-byte vs PG). Remaining copyselect diff is the
query-form bare legacy CSV options (csv header force quote t) — 2 lines.

Tests: TestCopyFromStdinInMultiStatementBatch, TestCopyFromStdinInBatchAbortsOnFail
(replace TestCopyFromStdinInBatchDeferred).
Design: docs/design/0097-0024f-copy-from-stdin-in-multi-statement-batch.md

commits.title: feat(M0097-0024): run COPY inline in multi-statement \; batches
commits.description:
psql's \; joins commands into one simple-query message (internal ;);
the server runs them in order with one CommandComplete each + a single
trailing ReadyForQuery. goopg mishandled embedded COPY: a batch starting
with COPY hit "expected exactly one COPY statement" (whole message routed
to the single-COPY path), and a batch reaching a COPY via the
multi-statement dispatcher leaked the internal "planner.Copy has no
executor path yet" (0A000).

Fix (internal/server):
- handleQueryOrCopy routes any query with an internal ; to the
  multi-statement dispatcher even when it starts with COPY ; single COPY
  statements keep the copyInState fast path.
- dispatchSimpleQueryViaExecutor intercepts *parser.CopyStmt before the
  executor via new runInlineCopy, which streams COPY TO (and server-side
  COPY FROM file) within the batch's shared transaction, writing only
  CommandComplete; the loop emits the single trailing ReadyForQuery and
  aborts the batch on the errQueryErrorSent sentinel.

COPY FROM STDIN inside a batch is deferred with a clean 0A000 error (no
internal leak); full support needs synchronous CopyData reads mid-batch.

Verified live on 5599: copyselect cases 1-3 match PG byte-for-byte.
Tests: TestCopyToInMultiStatementBatch, TestCopyToBatchStopsOnError,
TestCopyFromStdinInBatchDeferred. Design: 0097-0024e.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0024): PG-correct syntax errors for COPY query-form FROM/col-list
commits.description:
The parenthesised-query form of COPY is TO-only and column-list-free in
PostgreSQL's grammar, so `copy (select …) from stdin` → `syntax error at
or near "from"` and `copy (select …) (t,id) to stdout` → `… near "("`.
goopg leaked a byte-0 `COPY (query) is only valid with TO` and a generic
`expected FROM or TO`. parseCopy now splits direction handling on source
form (query form accepts only TO, else errSyntaxAtCur — a new bare
"syntax error at or near TOKEN" helper). Sibling wire fix:
dispatchCopyViaExecutor's parse-error arm threads syntaxErrorMsg so psql
renders LINE/caret instead of leaking the internal "(byte N)" suffix.

Closes copyselect gap #1; only psql \;/\. STDIN handling remains.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0024): reject COPY (SELECT INTO) with PG-compatible message
commits.description:
copyselect's 'copy (select t into temp test3 ...) to stdout' must fail with
'ERROR:  COPY (SELECT INTO) is not supported'. PostgreSQL's grammar accepts
SELECT INTO inside COPY (...) then DoCopy rejects it (copyto.c,
ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED). goopg has no SELECT INTO support, so
parseSelect stops at the reserved INTO keyword and the dangling token tripped
parseCopy's ')' check into a stray 'expected )'.

Mirror PG's grammar-accepts/command-rejects split: parser flags
CopyStmt.SelectInto and skipInnerQueryRemainder skips the unparsed
'INTO <target> FROM ...' tail (paren-depth tracked) up to the matching ')';
planCopy returns 0A000 'COPY (SELECT INTO) is not supported' before catalog
work. Wire rendering via the same dispatchCopyViaExecutor path as the
view-rejection fix.

Tests: TestParseCopySelectIntoFlagged, TestPlanCopySelectIntoRejected.
Verified live on 5599. Design: docs/design/0097-0024c-copy-select-into-rejection.md.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0024): bind trailing ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET to whole set op
commits.description:
A UNION B ORDER BY 1 parked the trailing ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET on the
RHS branch (parsed via recursive parseSelect), so it applied to B alone
and — for copyselect's `… UNION select * from v_test1 ORDER BY 1` — hit
42601 "'*' is not allowed here" (positional sort resolved against an
unexpanded star on the standalone branch). The planner's
wrapSetOpSortLimit already resolves these against the combined set-op
output but reads them from the outer SelectStmt, which was empty.

Fix in parseSelect: after s.SetOp = setOp, lift the RHS branch's
trailing OrderBy/Limit/Offset up to s when s carries none of its own.
Chains lift bottom-up so the outermost SELECT owns them, exactly where
wrapSetOpSortLimit reads them. Closes the top remaining copyselect
blocker (verified end-to-end on a live server).

Tests: TestParseSetOpTrailingOrderByBindsToWhole,
TestParseSetOpChainTrailingOrderBy.
Design: docs/design/0097-0024b-setop-trailing-orderby-binding.md.

commits.title: feat(M0097-0003c): type virtual catalog-table cells (sysviews 11→9)
commits.description:
catalog.Table.VirtualRows() returns rows as [][]string; both
planner.buildVirtualValues and executor.rematerialiseVirtualRows wrapped
every cell in a StringConst regardless of declared column type, so
int8/int4/bool virtual columns compared lexicographically. sysviews
exposed it: pg_backend_memory_contexts `total_bytes >= free_bytes`
evaluated "1048576" >= "524288" → '1' < '5' → wrongly f.

Fix: new shared helper planner.TypedVirtualCell(pos, value, colType)
parses integer-family → IntegerConst and bool → BooleanConst, with a
StringConst fallback for non-parsing values (display is keyed on the
column wire type, so typed cells render identically). Both sibling
paths route through it (sibling-paths-must-agree).

sysviews 11→9 diff lines; the two residual diffs need a synthetic
"Caller tuples" Bump context row + int[] path array-subscripting
(separate mechanisms, out of scope). No regression across 13
int-heavy passing cases. Baseline CSV reconciled (sysviews 33→9,
copyselect 59→55, tid 81→47).

Test: TestTypedVirtualCell.
Design: docs/design/0097-0003c-virtual-cell-numeric-typing.md

commits.title: fix(M0097-0003): SERIAL pseudo-types type-check as their integer base
commits.description:
SERIAL/BIGSERIAL/SMALLSERIAL are not real types — PostgreSQL resolves
them to int4/int8/int2 (pg_typeof reports "integer"). goopg keeps
"serial" as the stored catalog type (the INSERT auto-increment path keys
off the name) and the codec already aliases serial→int4, so reads and
pg_typeof worked — but the analyzer/planner type system did not know the
aliases. Result: `serial_col = 1` raised 42804 "operator = has
incompatible operand types \"serial\" and \"int8\"" and `serial_col + 1`
raised "operator + requires numeric operands", blocking any
comparison/arithmetic on a serial column with an integer literal
(e.g. WHERE id = N on a serial PK; the first blocker in copyselect).

Fix (purely additive, storage/INSERT untouched): add the serial aliases
to analyzer isNumericTypeName (gates comparison via isComparable AND
arithmetic via isNumericLike) and planner isIntegerLikeType /
promoteIntType (arithmetic result-type promotion: serial→int4,
bigserial→int8, smallserial→int2). The planner's NUMERIC/DECIMAL-only
isNumericTypeName is intentionally left untouched.

Sibling-path divergence: the codec canonicalised serial→int4 but the
type-checking path had not.

Tests: TestSerialPseudotypeIntegerTypeCheck (internal/analyzer, incl.
serial-vs-text still-errors negative case), TestPromoteIntTypeSerialFamily
(internal/planner). Design:
docs/design/0097-0003b-serial-pseudotype-integer-typecheck.md.

commits.title: feat(M0097-0036): TID type input validation, normalization, and output
commits.description:
goopg's '…'::tid cast was a no-op string passthrough, so '(-1,0)'::tid
printed (-1,0) instead of PG's unsigned (4294967295,0), out-of-range
'(4294967296,1)'/'(1,65536)' were silently accepted, and pg_input_is_valid/
pg_input_error_info reported tid as always valid.

Implements faithful tidin semantics (src/backend/utils/adt/tid.c):
- cStrtoul10Full: C strtoul base-10 + full-consumption + negative wrap
- parseTidInput: block = uint32 BlockNumber via the SIZEOF_LONG>4 round-trip
  guard (-1→4294967295, 4294967296 rejected); offset = uint16 ≤ USHRT_MAX

The ::tid cast, pg_input_is_valid('…','tid'), and pg_input_error_info('…','tid')
all route through the single parseTidInput helper (sibling-paths-must-agree).

Tests: TestParseTidInput, TestEvalCastTidNormalizesAndValidates
(internal/executor/tid_cast_test.go). tid regress normalized diff 81→47 lines;
residual is TID handling (min/max(ctid), currtid2(), ctid system column),
tracked as separate features under M0097-0036.

Design: docs/design/0097-0036c-tid-input-validation.md

commits.title: feat(M0097-0024): top-level UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT [ALL] set operations
commits.description:
Planner/analyzer accepted only UNION ALL; all other set ops returned
0A000. Now one planSelect path plans every variant:
- SetOp plan node gains Op (parser.SetOpType); zero value SetOpUnion
  keeps implicit partition/inheritance UNION ALL sites unchanged.
- Equal-column-count check -> 42601.
- wrapSetOpSortLimit applies trailing ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET resolved
  against the combined output (1-based position -> ColumnRef, out of
  range 42P10; or output column name) -- the copyselect
  "... UNION ... ORDER BY 1" shape.

Executor setOp keeps UNION ALL streaming (preserves currentTID for
FOR UPDATE partition scans) and buffers the rest with multiset
semantics keyed by rowKey: UNION distinct, INTERSECT min(lc,rc)/
distinct, EXCEPT max(0,lc-rc)/distinct.

Tests: TestSetOpMultisetSemantics, TestSetOpOrderByPosition;
analyzer/planner reject-tests updated. Verified live incl.
COPY (... UNION ... ORDER BY 1) TO STDOUT. copyselect still defers on
a separate SELECT *-in-set-op-branch star-expansion bug + psql \;/\..

Design: docs/design/0097-0024-setops-union-intersect-except.md

commits.title: fix(M0097-0009): reject table-form COPY against a plain view (copyselect)
commits.description:
planCopy resolved the relation but never checked its kind, so
COPY <view> {TO|FROM} planned the view as a heap relation instead of
erroring. PostgreSQL rejects it first on relation kind with 42809.
Now errors when tbl.View!=nil && !tbl.IsMatView (matviews exempt),
direction-specific message+hint. Sibling wire fix: dispatchCopyViaExecutor
now threads planErrorHintFields(err) so the HINT reaches the client.
Closes the 2 ERROR + 2 HINT view-rejection lines in copyselect.

Test: TestPlanCopyViewRejected.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0032): count(*) FILTER aggregate dedup + pg_hba_file_rules.error NULL (sysviews 33→11)
commits.description:
aggregateCallKey omitted the FILTER predicate, so a bare count(*) and a
count(*) FILTER(...) in the same query collapsed onto one unfiltered
aggregate slot — the filtered count silently reported the unfiltered
total (engine-wide; any bare + filtered same-name/same-arg twin). Fold
the filter into the dedup key, add an IsNullExpr case to parserExprKey
so IS NULL/IS NOT NULL filters don't collide, and resolve fc.Filter in
buildAggregateCall's count(*)/zero-arg early returns. Also drop the
trailing pg_hba_file_rules.error cell so it materialises as SQL NULL.

Tests: TestAggregateFilterDistinguishedInDedupKey,
TestPgHbaFileRulesErrorIsNull.

commits.title: feat(M0097-0009): COPY (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE … RETURNING) TO STDOUT
commits.description:
COPY (query) TO accepted only SELECT bodies; PostgreSQL also streams the
RETURNING rows of a data-modifying statement. Add parser dispatch
(CopyStmt.QueryDML + parseCopyInnerQuery), planner gating (require
RETURNING, else 0A000 "COPY query must have a RETURNING clause"), and
fix a commit-ordering bug in the wire COPY path: runCopyTo emitted
CommandComplete/ReadyForQuery before the COPY-internal transaction
committed, so COPY(DML) writes were invisible to the client's next
command. Split into runCopyToStream + commit-before-complete, mirroring
the CopyFrom path.

Tests: parser/planner/server COPY-DML cases incl. a visibility
regression test. copydml regress still needs CREATE RULE + trigger
NOTICE output (no rewrite-rule system) so it does not yet pass.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0032): expand SELECT * in non-recursive CTE bodies (sysviews)
commits.description:
registerAnalyzedCTE fed each CTE-body target straight into analyzeExpr,
which rejects a bare StarExpr (42601), so any WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM t)
failed — including sysviews' with-contexts pg_backend_memory_contexts
query, which emitted a spurious trailing "'*' is not allowed here".
The sibling derived-table path (synthesizeSubqueryTable) already expanded
stars, so FROM (SELECT * ...) x worked while the CTE form did not.

New shared helper expandInnerStarColumns materialises unqualified * (all
in-scope rels) or qualified t.* (matching rel) into concrete columns;
both registerAnalyzedCTE and synthesizeSubqueryTable call it, kept in
sync per the sibling-paths rule. WITH RECURSIVE star bodies remain a
separate analyzeRecursiveCTE problem.

Tests: TestAnalyzeWithCTEStarBodyExpands, TestAnalyzeWithCTEStarBodyKnowsColumnSet

commits.title: fix(M0097-0032): COLLATE expr postfix + complete pg_wait_events types (sysviews)
commits.description:
ORDER BY ... COLLATE "C" raised a parser syntax error: goopg had no
general a_expr COLLATE any_name production. Added a high-precedence
postfix in parseExprPrec (alongside ::/[...]) that consumes+discards the
collation reference (correct for "C"/"POSIX" == byte order == Go string
comparison); helper skipCollationName handles qualified names.

pg_wait_events listed only 6 wait-event types; PG 18 emits 9. Added
BufferPin, Extension, IPC rows (canonical names from wait_event_names.txt).
The sysviews wait-event query now returns the exact 9 expected rows.

Tests: TestParseCollatePostfix, TestPgWaitEventsCoversAllTypes.
Design: docs/design/0097-0032c-collate-postfix-and-wait-event-types.md.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0003): functional-dependency GROUP BY recognises only PRIMARY KEY
commits.description:
isColumnFunctionallyDetermined accepted both primary-key and unique
indexes when deciding whether an ungrouped column may pass through a
GROUP BY, but PostgreSQL's check_functional_grouping recognises only
PRIMARY KEY constraints (unique constraints are deferrable and, when
nullable, admit multiple NULLs). So GROUP BY on a unique-but-not-PK
column wrongly succeeded — state-dependent on whether the inline-UNIQUE
index was registered, producing a spurious 'relation already exists' in
the shared-cluster functional_deps run. Fix: skip non-primary indexes.

Also: execCreateView validates the view body via planner.Plan and now
converts a non-0A000 *planner.PlanError into an *ExecError so the wire
layer renders a clean 'ERROR:  <message>' line instead of the raw
Error() string '42803: ... (byte N)' (the simple-query path already
extracts Code/Message separately — sibling-path divergence).

functional_deps stays 21 normalized diff lines; the residual is now
entirely the out-of-scope DROP CONSTRAINT ... RESTRICT view->constraint
(pg_depend) dependency-tracking feature plus prepared-plan re-validation.

Tests: TestGroupByPrimaryKeyEstablishesFunctionalDependency,
TestGroupByUniqueColumnRejected (internal/planner/functional_deps_test.go).
Design: docs/design/0097-0003-functional-dep-pk-only-grouping.md.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0032): timezone_abbreviations GUC + verbose utc_offset (sysviews 41→33)
commits.description:
Register the timezone_abbreviations GUC (TypeString/ContextUserset, BootVal
'Default') so sysviews.sql's SET timezone_abbreviations = 'Australia'/'India'
succeed silently instead of erroring with "unrecognized configuration
parameter". Added the matching postgresql.conf.sample entry.

Fix pg_timezone_names/pg_timezone_abbrevs output: new verboseIntervalOffset
helper (mirrors EncodeInterval INTSTYLE_POSTGRES_VERBOSE) renders utc_offset as
"@ 7 hours 52 mins 58 secs ago" — pg_regress forces
intervalstyle=postgres_verbose and goopg emits virtual-table strings verbatim —
and stores is_dst as "f" not "false".

sysviews regress diff 41→33 (verified end-to-end); guc unchanged at 592.
Tests: TestVerboseIntervalOffset, TestPgTimezoneAbbrevsLMTRow.
Design: docs/design/0097-0032b-timezone-abbreviations-guc-and-verbose-offset.md

commits.title: fix(M0097-0036): merge JOIN USING/NATURAL column in unqualified SELECT *
commits.description:
expandStarTarget iterated every binding's full column list with no
usingHidden check, so `SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2 USING (id)` emitted the
join column twice (id,t,id,t) vs PG's id,t,t. The right binding already
carried usingHidden (set in planFromItem to hide the right-side copy from
unqualified column lookup, M0097-0003/0006) but the star-expansion path
had drifted from the lookup path. Now skip usingHidden columns for an
unqualified `*` only; a table-qualified `t2.*` still expands fully.

Test: TestPlanSelectStarJoinUsingMergesColumn. copyselect 69->59,
join 10246->9933 normalized diff; 17 previously-passing regress cases
re-verified. Design: docs/design/0097-0036b-star-using-join-merge.md.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0032): complete + sort pg_settings enable_* GUCs (sysviews 73→41)
commits.description:
sysviews.sql queries pg_settings WHERE name LIKE 'enable%' without ORDER BY
and expects PostgreSQL 18's 24 alphabetically-sorted planner enable_* GUCs
(PG's pg_settings is backed by the sorted GUC table). goopg's pg_settings
virtual table hand-coded only 20 in registration order, one mis-named
(enable_gather_merge vs PG's enable_gathermerge).

Renamed enable_gathermerge; added the 4 missing GUCs (distinct_reordering,
group_by_reordering, self_join_elimination, tidscan); and sort.Slice the
returned rows by name so output honours PG's sorted-GUC contract for every
pg_settings consumer. sysviews diff 73->41; guc unchanged at 592 (no
regression). Test: TestPgSettingsEnableGUCsCompleteAndSorted.

commits.title: fix(M0111-0007): truncate name to NAMEDATALEN-1=63 in PG-format encode
commits.description:
encodeValuePG's name arm copied the full input string into the fixed
64-byte NameData buffer with no NAMEDATALEN-1=63 truncation, so a
64-char input filled all 64 bytes (no NUL terminator) and decoded back
as 64 chars. PostgreSQL's namein() truncates name to 63 bytes; the
sibling encodeValueStorage path already did, but the PG-native encoder
(primary heap path since M0111-0001) had drifted. The off-by-one
widened name columns by one, kept a trailing byte PG clipped, and
corrupted WHERE row counts.

Fix: clip to 63 bytes before copy, mirroring storage-encode.

Recovers the `name` regress case (failed, 77 diff lines -> pass) — the
6th and LAST of the M0106-0010 PG-format codec regressions. All six are
now recovered. No previously-passing case regressed.

Test: TestEncodePhysicalPGNameTruncation.
Design: docs/design/0111-0007-pg-format-name-encode-truncation.md.

commits.title: fix(M0097-0036): dispatch CREATE TEMP VIEW/SEQUENCE instead of mis-parsing as table
commits.description:
parseCreate consumed the TEMP/TEMPORARY prefix then unconditionally called
parseCreateTableTail, so CREATE TEMP VIEW/SEQUENCE/MATERIALIZED VIEW were
mis-parsed as tables. CREATE TEMP VIEW produced no *CreateViewStmt, so no
view landed in the catalog and a later DROP VIEW failed with
"view does not exist". Now dispatches on the object keyword after TEMP.

Also accept the reserved KwLocal keyword in the GLOBAL/LOCAL prefix
(CREATE LOCAL TEMP ... previously errored). Add CreateViewStmt.Temporary.

functional_deps regress diff 24 -> 21 lines (verified end-to-end).
Tests: TestParseCreateTempView, TestParseCreateTempSequence.

commits.title: fix(M0111-0006): decode PG-format float4/float8 as KindNumeric
commits.description:
decodePhysicalPGValueMctx lumped float4/float8/real/double into the
shared text/varchar decode case, returning a KindString Datum. Since
goopg stores floats as varlena text (M0111-0002) and this PG-native
decoder is the primary heap-read path (M0111-0001), float columns
sorted lexicographically instead of numerically — e.g. SELECT f1 FROM
TEMP_FLOAT ORDER BY f1 put -1234 ahead of -2147483647.

The legacy decodeValue/arena decoders always parsed float text back to
KindNumeric (M0097-0003 "for correct ORDER BY numeric sort"); the
PG-native path lost it. Split floats into a dedicated case that parses
the varlena-text payload to KindNumeric (NaN/Inf string fallback),
mirroring the legacy decoders. Display is unaffected: float8 output is
keyed on column type (%.15g), not Datum kind.

Recovers the numerology regress case (failed, 60 diff lines -> pass);
float4 680->676, float8 1031->1027; no previously-passing case
regressed. Pinned by TestDecodePhysicalPGFloatKind.

Design: docs/design/0111-0006-pg-format-float-decode-kind.md

commits.title: fix(M0111-0005): int2 storage-encode out-of-range message parity
commits.description:
encodeValuePG's int2/smallint arm emitted the bare "smallint out of
range" (int2pl/int2mul arithmetic wording) when a string literal
overflowed on INSERT (the int2in input-function path, e.g.
INSERT INTO INT2_TBL(f1) VALUES ('100000')). PostgreSQL reports
"value \"100000\" is out of range for type smallint" (22003) there;
the bare wording is reserved for arithmetic overflow, which goopg
already raises in the expression evaluator before the storage-encode
path. The sibling int4 arm directly below already did this -- the two
had drifted. Mirrored int4.

Recovers the int2 regress case (failed, 4 diff lines -> pass), the
5th of the 6 M0106-codec regressions to be reclaimed. Baseline +
inventory CSVs updated, coverage md regenerated (14 pass now).

Test: TestEncodeValuePGInt2OutOfRangeMessage.
Design: docs/design/0111-0005-int2-encode-out-of-range-message.md.

commits.title: fix(executor): restore int2/int4 overflow check in fast-path evaluator (M0097-0037)
commits.description:
The M0097-0019 audit (bf9c791) flagged 6 regressed regress cases and
attributed them to the M0106-0010 PG-format codec switch. For int2/int4 that
attribution was wrong. The real cause is the M0107-0003 compiled fast-path
expression evaluator: evalFastExpr's ExprBinaryOp case called evalBinary but
omitted the int2/int4 overflow range check that the interpreted evalExprSlot
applies, and the compiled node never stored ResultType. So a projected
int2*int2 / int4*int4 silently returned the out-of-range value (e.g. 65534)
instead of raising 22003. The interpreted path stayed correct, so
pg_typeof(expr) masked the bug.

Fix (internal/executor/exprnode.go):
- ExprBinaryOp nodes carry an overflow code in payload[1] (overflowCodeForType
  from BinaryOp.ResultType); evalFastExpr applies the same
  smallint/integer-out-of-range check after evalBinary.
- Float-typed BinaryOps now compile to ExprAdapter so evalExprSlot's float64
  path handles them (output parity; strictly more correct than before).
- int8/bigint keep the no-check fast path, matching evalExprSlot.

Result: regress int4 -> pass (verified: fails at HEAD c64e5c2 without this
change, passes with it; independent of the M0111-0004 codec decode fix that
recovered portals_p2/select_implicit). int2 44 -> 4 diff lines; the residual 4
are a separate pre-existing bug (INSERT '100000' reports "smallint out of
range" instead of "value 100000 is out of range for type smallint"). Coverage
md now 14 pass.

TestBuildExprFloatFallsBackToAdapter in internal/executor/phase_c_test.go.
Gates: go test ./internal/executor/ ./internal/planner/ ./internal/server/
green (except pre-existing TestAnalyzeRespectsStatsTarget, verified
independent of this change). Design: docs/design/0097-0037-fast-path-int-overflow.md.

docs(ralph): mark M0111-0001 as fixed
fix(executor): prevent column loss in UPDATE re-encode (M0111-0001)
commits.description:
Under concurrent UPDATE load, the goopg-format decoder
(decodeGoopgRowIntoMctx) could accidentally accept PG-format tuple
bytes as valid legacy data, setting the filler column to NullDatum
when the tuple body was too short.  The subsequent re-encode
(encodeRowPG) would skip the null column, producing a truncated
12-byte tuple that lacked the filler varlena entirely.  Later reads
of that tuple would fail with "DecodePhysicalPGRow: filler: truncated
varlena" because len(data[off:]) was 0.

Fix: in updateViaIndex and tryApplyHOTUpdate, after building the new
row from SET expressions, restore any non-generated column that
became null during the decode→rebuild cycle by copying the old row's
value.  This prevents column loss even when the decoder mis-parses
the on-disk format.

Verified: pgbench STANDARD c=10 60s → 682.8 TPS, zero client aborts.
Previously ~1743 transactions before DecodePhysicalPGRow errors.

commits.description:
The TOAST encode/decode round-trip was broken because goopg wrote the
raw 12-byte TOAST pointer directly into the PG-format tuple, but the
varlena decoder interpreted those bytes as a text varlena header instead
of recognising them as a TOAST reference.

- encodeRowPG: wrap the 12-byte TOAST pointer in a PG short varlena
  header (0x1B = VARATT_IS_EXTERNAL_ONDISK, 13 bytes total)
- decodePhysicalPGValueMctx: detect the 0x1B header and return a

commits.title: fix(executor): try PG-native format first in decodeRowIntoMctx
commits.description:
The index scan path (and any caller of DecodeRowInto / decodeRowIntoMctx)
was trying the goopg legacy format before the PG-native format.  Since
M0106-0010 all new tuples are written in PG-native format via EncodeRowPG,
but the legacy decoder could accidentally accept PG-format bytes as valid
legacy data (e.g. interpreting a PG varlena header byte as a legacy flag
byte), silently returning wrong values for a subset of rows.

When both decoders failed, the PG-format error was surfaced, producing
the "DecodePhysicalPGRow: filler: truncated varlena" symptom observed
in pgbench UPDATE workloads.

Now PG-native format is tried first, with legacy format as fallback for
cold-storage tuples that predate M0106.

commits.title: fix(executor,btree): TOAST sanity check + BTree stats counter regression
commits.description:
Three coupled fixes to resolve the pgbench SU crash and virtual address
space exhaustion on WSL2:

1. TOAST numChunks sanity check in decodeGoopgRowIntoMctx (codec.go)
   Root cause of OOM crash: after the char(N)/bpchar varlena fix (47f6c5b),
   updated pgbench_accounts rows are 13 bytes in PG physical format
   (4+4+4+1 varlena for empty filler). When aid=2 (or any aid ≡ 2 mod 256),
   the first LE byte is 0x02 — the goopg decoder's TOAST flag. The decoder
   then reads 12 "pointer" bytes and finds off=13==len(data), so it
   "succeeds" with a fake KindToastPointer. numChunks comes from the high
   bytes of abalance (e.g. abalance=-124 → numChunks≈4.2B) → DetoastValue
   tries make([][]byte, 4.2B) → 96 GB allocation → "runtime: out of memory".
   Fix: reject TOAST pointers with numChunks > 1<<20 (≈1M chunks × 2KB
   each = 2 GB max, well above any real TOAST column), causing the goopg
   decoder to fail and the caller to fall through to decodePhysicalPGRowIntoMctx
   which correctly decodes PG-physical rows.
   Regression pin: TestDecodeRowGoopgImplausibleToastChunksSanityCheck.

2. BTree stats counter revert from stats.Counter to atomic.Uint64
   btreeStatsCounters embedded stats.Counter fields made sizeof(BTree) = 32 KiB
   (2 × 16 KiB Counter = 256 shards × 64 bytes). Since btree.Open() is called
   per-statement, high-concurrency pgbench SU allocates 32 KiB per open at
   ~12K opens/second = 384 MB/s of heap churn. On WSL2 (limited virtual address
   space ≈ RAM+swap ≈ 95 GB), the Go runtime's 96 GB heap reservation fails.
   Reverted to atomic.Uint64 (16 bytes per counter) → sizeof(BTree) = 96 bytes.
   Regression pin: TestBTreeSizeIsSane (size < 1 KiB assertion).

3. Fix char(N) alignment and varlena detection (from 47f6c5b, separate concern)
   physicalPGTypeAlign and pgPhysicalTypeIsVarlena now distinguish char (no
   args, single byte) from char(N) (bpchar with length modifier, varlena)
   correctly. The goopg decoder TOAST sanity check handles the resulting
   13-byte PG-physical rows without crashing.

Performance results after all fixes (WSL2, scale=100, 90s):
  c=50 SU:  1,428 TPS (gate ≥ 2,000 — below gate on WSL2)
  c=100 standard: 1,582 TPS ✓ (gate ≥ 500)
  c=100 SU: 1,641 TPS ✓ (gate ≥ 500)

commits.title: fix(executor,server): char(N)/bpchar varlena encoding + extended-query procNum forwarding
commits.description:
Two coupled fixes that unblock the M0107 pgbench c50/c100 SU gate:

1. codec.go — char(N) (bpchar) varlena encoding parity
   encodeValuePG treated char without a length modifier and char(N)
   (character(84), bpchar) identically as single-byte encoding. PG physical
   format requires char(N) to use varlena (header + data), exactly like
   "character"/"bpchar". Without this, pgbench's filler character(84) column
   was written as one byte but read back expecting a 4-byte varlena prefix,
   causing "DecodePhysicalPGRow: filler: truncated 4-byte varlena header" on
   every client at high concurrency.

   Updated three sites in codec.go:
   - encodeValuePG: len(t.Args)==0 → single byte; len>0 → varlenaTextBytes
   - physicalPGTypeAlign: char(N) → alignment 4 (bpchar); char → alignment 1
   - pgPhysicalTypeIsVarlena: char(N) → true; char → false

   Regression pins: TestEncodeValuePGCharNoArgs, TestEncodeValuePGCharWithArgs,
   TestEncodeValuePGCharWithArgsIsVarlena, TestEncodeValuePGCharAlignmentMatches
   in internal/executor/codec_bpchar_varlena_test.go.

2. server.go / extended.go / copy.go / dispatch_extended.go — procNum forwarding
   Extended query protocol and COPY transactions were calling TxnMgr.Begin without
   a procNum, defaulting to 0 and potentially overwriting the connection's own
   ProcArray slot when an explicit BEGIN block was active. Thread procNum through
   from the connection's slot (offset by DefaultProcArraySize/2 for auto-commit
   transactions to avoid collisions).

commits.title: fix(executor): slotToRow handles *Slot (Phase C concrete type)
commits.description:
`slotToRow` lacked a case for `*Slot` — the concrete slot type
introduced by M0107 Phase C (`BuildFastIterator` / `projectOpNext`).
Expressions that convert the slot to a Row before delegating to
legacy `evalExpr` (InExpr, CaseExpr, SubqueryExpr, ExistsExpr,
ExtractExpr, FuncCall) fell to the `default` branch and returned
nil, causing spurious "column ref X/N on nil slot" errors when any
of those expression types appeared in a query executed via the fast
path (simple query protocol) or via ExprAdapter in the fast expr tree.

Add `case *Slot` → `v.Row()` to `slotToRow`, matching the pattern
used for `*MaterializedSlot` and `*VirtualSlot`.

Impact: fixes nil-slot errors for queries like
  SELECT (setting IN ('read committed','read uncommitted')) AS c
    FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'default_transaction_isolation'
and more generally any query whose projection or filter contains
an expression that goes through the ExprAdapter path while running
under the M0107 Phase C fast-path executor.

commits.title: perf(storage): M0107-0008 COMPLETE — per-slot semaphore replaces pool-wide pinCond
commits.description:
Replace Pool.pinCond *sync.Cond (pool-wide Broadcast thundering herd) with
per-slot runtimeshim.SemaAcquire/Release using two new parallel arrays:
  - slotSema []uint32     — runtime semaphore cell per slot
  - slotWaiters []int32  — exact waiter count written/read under pinMu

Protocol: waiter increments slotWaiters[i] under pinMu, releases pinMu,
calls SemaAcquire, decrements on wake. Loader reads exact count under pinMu
before clearing ioInflightBit, then releases sema exactly N times — no
thundering herd, no cross-slot wakeups.

Removes: slotIOCond struct, pinCond field, all pinCond.Broadcast() sites.

M0107-0008 is now feature-complete: Nanotime + PinP + SemaAcquire all
wired to production callers.

Regression: TestSlotSemaArraysInitializedCorrectly, TestSlotSemaConcurrentPinSameBlock
(8-goroutine deadlock gate), TestSlotSemaWaiterCountReturnsToZero,
TestSlotSemaNoPinCondInPool in internal/storage/bufpool_sema_test.go.

commits.title: fix(wal): M0107-0010 MemRing ResetToPos — walsender zero-read fix
commits.description:
MemRing was created in loadState with head=tail=0. After the first Path B
(async-drain stripe writer) append advanced tail past 0x105CEA0, ReadAt at a
lower segment-start LSN (0x1000000) returned true-with-zeros because the ring
was never populated at those offsets. Walsender served those zeros to PG standbys:
"invalid magic number 0000 in WAL segment 000000010000000000000001, LSN 0/1000000".

Fix: add MemRing.ResetToPos(pos) (head=tail=pos under write lock) and call
st.memRing.ResetToPos(writePos) in loadState. ReadAt then misses for positions
before writePos; walsender falls back to disk (valid initdb WAL). For fresh
clusters (writePos=0) ResetToPos is a no-op.

Gates: TestE2E_FailoverGoopgToPG/async PASS; all WAL/executor/server/storage tests
PASS -race; make ralph-state-guard PASS.

1981 ≥ 500, tests -race clean).

commits.title: fix(executor): M0107-0009 HOT update encoding parity + goopg over-read guard
commits.description:
Two coupled fixes close the heap UPDATE corruption ("truncated 4-byte
varlena header") deferred from M0107-0007 loop 5.

(A) decodeGoopgRowIntoMctx: change post-loop guard from `off < len(data)`
(trailing bytes) to `off != len(data)` (trailing bytes OR over-read).
The over-read case (off > len) occurred when the loop guard (off >= len →
NullDatum, no off advance) left off > len after the loop, causing the
prior guard to evaluate FALSE and the decoder to "succeed" with wrong
values. With the new check, PG-encoded data falling through the guard
correctly reaches decodePhysicalPGRowIntoMctx.

(B) tryApplyHOTUpdate: when LogCanonical != nil, use EncodeRowPG +
NullBitmapPG + SetNatts + HeapXmaxInvalid — matching writeHeapRowReturning's
canonical-WAL path. Previously HOT updates always used EncodeRow (goopg
format), creating mixed encoding that caused decodeGoopgRowIntoMctx to
occasionally "succeed" on PG-encoded rows with wrong column values (filler
becoming NULL, counter corrupted).

commits.title: fix(mvcc): M0107-0007 CLog.flush TOCTOU race causing slice bounds panic
commits.description:
CLog.flush scans banks for the highest used position (lastUsedBank,
lastUsedLen), allocates out[:lastUsedLen], then re-reads b.data under
a per-bank lock. Between scan and copy, another goroutine can commit
more transactions, growing b.data beyond lastUsedLen. The subsequent
copy(out[start:start+len(b.data)], b.data) then writes past out's end.

Fix: cap copyLen to len(out)-start so the copy never exceeds the
pre-allocated buffer, regardless of concurrent b.data growth.

Triggered consistently at c=100 pgbench concurrency once M0107-0007
parallel WAL writes increased throughput enough to hit the race.

commits.title: fix(wal): M0107-0007 stripe B — three ring-window correctness fixes
commits.description:
Fix three pre-existing bugs surfaced by the pgbench c=100 SU gate:

1. MemRing.AdvanceWindow: add proactive ring eviction before WriteReserved.
   After cap bytes of WAL, PublishUpTo(end) sets head=end-cap, leaving
   window [end-cap, end). The next write at pos=end has pos>=head+cap →
   errMemRingReservedOutOfRange. AdvanceWindow(pos+len) slides head to
   max(head, pos+len-cap) before each write. Called from stripeAppend,
   stripeAppendBuiltEmitted, and emitSegmentPad.

2. reserveEmittedAndPublish: skip sub-24-byte segment-boundary gaps.
   When a record leaves a gap of < 24 bytes before the boundary,
   buildSegmentPadRecord panics ("padLen below minimum 24"). Fix: skip
   to boundary directly without calling onCrossSegment, leaving the
   tiny gap as zeros. xl_prev chain preserved by keeping t.prev unchanged.

3. walBuffer.writeReserved: use head (not base) for upper-bound check.
   After partial drain, head advances but base doesn't slide until
   head-base >= cap. Using base+cap as the upper bound rejects valid
   writes at [base+cap, head+cap). Fix: check lsn+n <= head+cap.
   Ring-offset arithmetic still uses base.

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B — async drain: atomic head/base + lock-free appendPGCompat Path B
commits.description:
Closes the last Lock()-on-hot-path bottleneck in the WAL append flow.

Two coupled changes:
1. walBuffer.head and walBuffer.base upgraded to atomic.Int64 (parallel
   to the tail upgrade in 0107-0007r).  Concurrent stripe writers'
   free()/writeReserved range checks are now race-free against the
   state-loop drain goroutine's advanceHead stores.  advanceHead stores
   base-first-then-head to avoid transient out-of-range errors on the
   write path.

2. appendPGCompat Path B drops appendMu.Lock()/Unlock() — drain runs
   without any outer lock.  Safety: drain reads [head, head+need) while
   stripe writers write at lsn >= tail >= head+need (disjoint regions);
   advanceHead is single-writer (state-loop goroutine only).

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B call-site rewrite part 3 — tryAppend RWMutex parallel writers
commits.description:
Replace state.appendMu sync.Mutex with sync.RWMutex and switch tryAppend's
PG-compat Path B from Lock()/Unlock() to RLock()/RUnlock(). Multiple backend
goroutines now hold RLock simultaneously and proceed on different WAL stripes
in parallel, eliminating the dominant serialisation point on the hot path.

Supporting changes:
- tryAppend: drop s.writePos/s.writeLSN/s.prevRecPtr updates (Lock paths
  derive from core.Load()); CAS-max storeMaxLSN for writeLSNMirror
- appendPGCompat Path A: read writePos/prevRecPtr from core.Load() under
  Lock() to account for concurrent tryAppend advances; drop s.prevRecPtr
  update (tracker resetPosition is authoritative)
- appendRaw: read writePos from core.Load(); add resetPosition(end,
  trackerPrev) — fixes pre-existing latent bug where the tracker stayed at
  the pre-raw position, causing the next Append to overwrite raw bytes
- flushUpTo/close: use max(s.writeLSN, writeLSNMirror.Load()) so
  tryAppend-written LSNs are visible without holding appendMu

- AppendRaw tracker reset: no overwrite after AppendRaw

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B foundation 23 — append parity gate
commits.description:

emitWithPageHeaders + walBuf.append` sequence (state.append's

surface a real prev-RecPtr convention divergence. Legacy
state.append stores prevRecPtr = writePos + leading

store t.prev in record-CONTENT space inside

depends only on data already in scope under posMu via

parityDeferredReason constant; removing the Skips is the gate the
prev-RecPtr resolution must pass to declare slice B's call-site
rewrite ready for PG-compat traffic. The single-record case
(TestAppendXLogPayloadParityFirstRecordAlwaysAgrees) is ACTIVE

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B foundation 21 — predictXLogRecordLen
commits.description:
Add pure size-prediction helper that mirrors wrapXLogMainData +
encodeRecordXLog's byte arithmetic. Returns (realRecLen, paddedLen)
without allocating or encoding.

The slice B call-site rewrite for state.append's PG-compat path
needs to pass recordLen to core.AppendBuiltEmitted BEFORE the build
closure can encode (encoding requires the post-reservation prev
LSN). Predict-then-reserve is the only zero-cost path; encode-
then-reserve costs 2× allocation, stash-and-patch needs CRC
recompute.

Pairing:
  realRecLen, paddedLen := predictXLogRecordLen(payload)
  core.AppendBuiltEmitted(procNum, paddedLen,
      func(start, prev uint64, total, leading int) ([]byte, error) {
          record, _, err := encodeRecordXLog(payload, prev)
          if err != nil { return nil, err }
          out, _ := emitWithPageHeaders(record, realRecLen,
              int64(start), segSize, sysID, tli)
          return out, nil
      })

Branches mirror wrapXLogMainData exactly: M0106-0010 canonical
envelope (0xFE prefix + ≥7 bytes), short wrap (≤ 0xFF), long wrap
(> 0xFF).

Six regression tests including the keystone byte-for-byte
agreement matrix against encodeRecordXLog across 12 payload
shapes. Verified: go test -race ./internal/wal/ PASS (4.12 s);
go vet clean.

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B foundation 14 — stripeAppend composer
commits.description:
Adds `stripeAppend` writer-side composer in internal/wal/stripe_append.go.
Performs one stripe-locked WAL append by composing seven slice B
primitives in the exact order the slice B contract requires:

1. appendLockSet.lockByProcNum (foundation 2): pick stripe via procNum & 0x7
2. insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish (foundation 9): joint (curr, prev)
   advance + insertionTracker stripe slot publish under posMu — closes
   the pre-reserve race from foundation 6 §"Pre-reserve race"
3. walBuffer.writeReserved (foundation 5): bytes-side ring write
4. MemRing.WriteReserved (foundation 8): walsender mirror write
5. insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle) (foundation 6):
   END marker so drain-side tailPublisher stops capping safeTail
6. drop stripe lock

Steps (5) and (6) are deferred so LIFO ordering runs END-marker before
unlock — matches the lock-ordering tier documented in foundation 13's
publishVisibility design.

Symmetric counterpart of foundation 13 publishVisibility (drain-side
composer): stripeAppend writes bytes without advancing visibility;
publishVisibility advances visibility without writing bytes. Together
they cover the full slice B write/publish lifecycle so the planned
call-site rewrite installs each as a one-liner.

Cross-segment crossings handled by insertPosTracker.onCrossSegment
fired under posMu inside step (2); call-site rewrite will install
foundation 12 emitSegmentPad as that hook so a reservation that
straddles a segment boundary automatically gets an XLOG_NOOP pad
record with the xl_prev chain preserved.

Error handling and END marker: if walBuf.writeReserved or
memRing.WriteReserved returns an error, the deferred END marker still
fires so drain's tailPublisher is not frozen at the failed
reservation's start LSN. Error returned verbatim; start/prev returned
even on error for forensic logging.

Nil-safety: locks/posTracker/insertTracker are required (structured
errors before any side effect; nil insertTracker would re-open the
pre-reserve race); walBuf/memRing individually nil-safe so the
composer works under Config.WALBuffers == 0 and/or
wal_sender_memory_buffer == 0. Empty record rejected with structured
error.

PG counterpart: XLogInsertRecord in xlog.c calls WALInsertLockAcquire
+ ReserveXLogInsertLocation (with WALInsertLockUpdateInsertingAt
under the same lock) + CopyXLogRecordToWAL + WALInsertLockRelease;
goopg's stripeAppend fuses the equivalent five steps into one.

15 regression tests cover: happy path with publishVisibility round
trip; four defensive nil/empty rejections; two partial-ring paths
(walBuf nil / memRing nil); two error-with-END-marker paths (range
violation in each ring); procNum stripe selection; cross-segment with
pad record decode + xl_prev chain validation; concurrent disjoint
stripes with permutation check; same-stripe serialisation; concurrent
drain-consistency end-to-end with race detector; 5s watchdog. All

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B foundation 10 — walBuffer.publishTail
commits.description:
Bytes-side mirror of [[0107-0007o]] MemRing.PublishUpTo. Under the
slice B 8-stripe writer model a stripe lands bytes via
walBuffer.writeReserved without touching tail; the drain goroutine —
after consulting tailPublisher for the safe watermark — calls
publishTail to monotonically advance tail so the freshly-published
bytes become drainable (visible to resident / readForDrain / readAt).

Contract: nil-safe; monotonic store; returns post-update tail; does
NOT mutate head/base. Unlike MemRing.PublishUpTo, publishTail never
auto-evicts on overflow — walBuffer residents are pre-disk and
silently evicting them would lose data. Concurrency upgrade
(b.tail → atomic.Int64) is a separate follow-on foundation.

Eleven regression tests cover monotonicity, nil-safety, drain
composition, visibility edge, no-auto-eviction, and a stripe-
concurrent disjoint-writer scenario under -race with a 5s deadlock
watchdog.

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B foundation 4 — insertPosTracker (PG-compat prevRecPtr chain)
commits.description:
Adds insertPosTracker primitive in internal/wal/insert_pos.go: joint
(curr, prev) update under a single sync.Mutex, matching PG's
ReserveXLogInsertLocation insertpos_lck spinlock. reserve(size)
returns (start, prev) so the caller can stamp prev verbatim into
the next record's xl_prev. Segment crossings fire onCrossSegment
with (gapStart, boundary, gapPrev) so the gap can be padded with
buildSegmentPadRecord ([[0107-0007j]]); the reservation that
triggered the crossing then lands at boundary with prev=gapStart
so the xl_prev chain remains unbroken across the boundary.

Why a mutex instead of CAS: two atomic.Uint64s can't be CAS-updated
together, and the joint atomicity of (curr, prev) is required for
chain correctness. PG faces the same constraint and picks a spinlock;
we follow with sync.Mutex.

Writer. Foundation-first pattern matches slice C.

recovery-resume (non-zero startCurr/startPrev), single crossing,
exact-boundary fast path, invalid-size panic, zero-segSize panic,
concurrent reserves forming a complete chain, concurrent crossings
firing the hook exactly (lastSeg-firstSeg) times, and the
across-boundary prev linkage. go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/
PASS (3.13 s).

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0007 slice B foundation 3 — buildSegmentPadRecord (XLOG_NOOP)
commits.description:
Add `buildSegmentPadRecord(padLen, prev) ([]byte, error)` in new file
`internal/wal/segment_pad.go`: a pure byte-builder for the
`RmgrXLog`/`XLOG_NOOP` (0x20 per PG `pg_control.h:70`) record that the
slice-B lsnAllocator ([[0107-0007h]]) onCrossSegment hook will emit to
fill the `[start, boundary)` gap left when a cross-segment reservation
hops to the next segment.

Encoding branches per padLen p (header is always 24 B):
  - p == 24: header only, no chunk header (parser's headerLoop exits
    immediately when len(wrapped)-off (=0) <= datatotal (=0)).
  - 26 <= p <= 281: short chunk (xlrBlockIDDataShort, 1B tag + 1B len)
    + (p-26) zero data bytes.
  - p >= 282: long chunk (xlrBlockIDDataLong, 1B tag + 4B len)
    + (p-29) zero data bytes.
  - p < 24 or p == 25: explicit error. maxAlignXLog (records aligned
    to 8 B on disk) guarantees real reservations produce padLen in
    {24, 32, 40, ...} which are all encodable; the explicit error is
    defence-in-depth.

PG-compat: byte-format-identical to PG18 `RM_XLOG_ID`/`XLOG_NOOP`. A
PG18 standby replaying a goopg stream containing this record falls
through `xlog_redo`'s NOOP branch (xlog.c:8508 `/* nothing to do here
*/`) with no on-disk effect — preserving the parent milestone's §6
"WAL record format guarantee".

Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite mounts the hook;
foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] /
[[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]]
/ [[0107-0007g]]).

Eight regression tests in `internal/wal/segment_pad_test.go`: minimum
size (padLen=24, all header fields + CRC valid); round-trip table
across every encoding boundary (24, 26, 100, 281, 282, 1024, 64 KiB)
via the full structured decoder confirming MainData length and
all-zero contents; rejects-too-small (0/1/8/16/23); rejects-1-byte-body
(padLen=25); prev propagation (0, 1, 0xDEAD_BEEF, max); body-all-zero
past chunk header (byte-diff replay invariant); CRC determinism (two
identical builds produce identical bytes); CRC corruption detection
(single-bit body flip invalidates CRC).

Verified: go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestBuildSegmentPadRecord'
./internal/wal/ PASS (1.02 s); go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/
PASS (3.13 s).

docs/design/README.md).

commits.title: feat(executor): M0107-0007 slice C call-site part 2 — adaptive batched-extend tail
commits.description:
Closes parent §3 steps 5–6 in internal/executor/operators_storage.go.
New constant extendBatchSize = 8 and helper
batchExtendAndRegisterFSM(pool, fsm, rel) in heap_insert_select.go: one
Pool.ExtendRelationBatch call appends eight empty pages in one syscall
and FSM-registers blocks [firstBlk+1 .. firstBlk+7] at empty-page free
space; firstBlk is left out of the FSM so the caller's normal
markHeapInsertDirty → FSM.RecordFreeSpaceForPage path records the
post-insert remainder unchanged.

lockHeapExtend signature changes from `unlock` to `(unlock, contended
bool)`: TryLock first, fall through to blocking Lock() with
contended=true. writeHeapRowReturning and writeHeapRowReturningPG now
(a) re-consult the FSM via selectFSMCandidatePage after taking the
extend lock (cross-stripe pickup), (b) re-check the tail block, (c)
branch on contended — true → batchExtendAndRegisterFSM; false →
original Pool.PinNew fast path. The adaptive gating preserves the
single-INSERT-grows-by-one-page invariants every HOT-update / VACUUM /
LockRows / partition test was written against, and mirrors PG's
RelationExtensionLockWaiterCount-driven extraBlocks heuristic in
RelationGetBufferForTuple.

Three new tests in heap_insert_select_test.go pin the batched-extend
half; two new assertions in extend_lock_stripe_test.go pin the
contended/uncontended contract.

PASS.

commits.title: feat(executor): M0107-0007 slice C call-site part 1 — pin-aware FSM consultation
commits.description:
writeHeapRowReturning / writeHeapRowReturningPG in

helper selectFSMCandidatePage(ctx.FSM, ctx.Pool, rel, minFreeBytes)
from [[0107-0007e]] instead of the single-block
ctx.FSM.GetPageWithFreeSpace(rel, minFreeBytes). Matching
(BlockNumber, bool) signature makes the change a one-liner per call
site; the surrounding `if ctx.FSM != nil` wrapper is removed because
the helper handles nil-FSM / nil-Pool itself.

Under low concurrency the selected block is unchanged. Under high
concurrency every backend's Pool.SlotPinCount probe biases it away
from the hot tail page so backends spread across cold FSM candidates
instead of converging on one slot's content lock. Per-record WAL
emission is byte-identical — only the block-reference number embedded
in XLOG_HEAP_INSERT for a given workload changes under contention,
which PG standby replay handles per-record.

FSM registration for the extras) and slice B (8-stripe
wal.Writer.appendLocks) stay deferred for the parent milestone's WAL

Algorithm: O(blocks · log K) via insertion-sort buffer of length K=n
(K typically 4). Lock discipline mirrors GetPageWithFreeSpace (RLock
held for entire scan; returned slice is caller-owned).

Regression coverage in internal/storage/fsm_test.go: four tests cover
basic top-K ordering, edge cases (nil/n<=0/minFreeBytes=0/empty/ties),
1000-block scan with known top-4 outliers, and read-only invariant.

Verified: go test -race -count=1 ./internal/storage/ PASS (5.35 s).

commits.title: feat(executor): M0107-0007 slice A — 8-stripe heap-extend lock
commits.description:
Replace single per-relation `sync.Mutex` (heapExtendLocks sync.Map →
*sync.Mutex) with an 8-stripe `heapExtendLockSet` ([8]paddedMutex). A
backend extending a relation picks `set.locks[procNum & 0x7]`, allowing
up to 8 parallel extenders per relation. Matches PG's striping intent
on RelationExtensionLock (parent chapter §4) with goopg-specific 8-way
distribution because Go mutexes are heavier than PG LWLocks.

paddedMutex (sync.Mutex + [56]byte = 64 B) ensures adjacent stripes
occupy distinct cache lines; size pinned at compile time via
unsafe.Sizeof in TestPaddedMutexSize. Correctness: Pool.PinNew
(internal/storage/bufpool.go:638) already holds pinMu over victim claim
+ bufmap publish, and storage.Manager.Extend allocates distinct block
numbers per call — so concurrent extension from different stripes is
safe. The single mutex previously existed to reduce wasted PinNew churn
under load, not for correctness.

Two callers (writeHeapRowReturning, writeHeapRowReturningPG) already
had ctx in scope; now pass ctx.ProcNum (plumbed end-to-end by
M0107-0004 ProcArray).

Tests:
  - TestPaddedMutexSize: 64 B layout pin
  - TestLockHeapExtendStripesByProcNum: peak concurrency == 8
  - TestLockHeapExtendCollidesOnSameStripe: procNum 0 vs 8 serialise

Verified: go test -race -count=1 ./internal/executor/ ./internal/storage/
./internal/wal/ ./internal/server/ — all PASS.

Out of scope (deferred to slice B and slice C of M0107-0007):
- Slice B — 8-stripe wal.Writer.appendLocks per parent §2
- Slice C — FSM-driven pin-count-aware ranking + batched extension §3

PG-compat: none. In-memory contention structure only; no on-disk file
format, WAL record, catalog tuple, or wire-protocol byte changes.

Design: docs/design/0107-0007a-heap-extend-lock-striping.md
Indexed in: docs/design/README.md

commits.title: feat(aio): M0107-0008 loop-14 — Engine.inFlight gauge via stats.Counter
commits.description:
Migrate the AIO Engine's `inFlight` gauge from `atomic.Int64` to
`stats.Counter` — first signed-delta consumer of the per-P primitive
and the eighth concrete migration on M0107-0008. Hot path is each
Method's Submit (`Add(1)`) and `finishHandle` (`Add(-1)`); per-P
sharding scatters cross-core cache-line bouncing the shared field
previously took on every Submit/completion.

Cross-shard `Sum()` = `(#Add(+1)) − (#Add(−1))` = current gauge
value at any consistent point; `Stats.InFlight int64` field type and
`pg_aios`-summary view contract preserved. Closes the last hot-path
additive site on `Engine` and the M0107-0008 in-scope migration
shopping list; see design doc 0107-0008n for the closure conditions
on the remaining atomics.

commits.title: feat(storage): M0107-0008 loop-13 — bufpool victim counters via stats.Counter
commits.description:
Migrate Pool.dirtyVictimCount / Pool.totalVictimCount from atomic.Int64
to stats.Counter — the seventh concrete consumer of the per-P counter
primitive from 0107-0008f.

Hot path is chooseVictimSlot's valid-page eviction branch, called from
foreground Pin on every cache miss against a cold page. Multi-backend
concurrent eviction previously bounced the shared totalVictimCount line
on every cross-P miss. Per-P sharding via stats.Counter scatters writes
across 256 cache-line-padded shards.

DirtyVictimRate() reads switch from .Load() to .Sum(); ResetVictimStats()
from .Store(0) to .Reset(). Both readers are cold-path (bgwriter ~200 ms
tick + DoD test).

Existing TestBgwriterDoDDirtyVictimRate covers the counters end-to-end
through the public API and continues to PASS under -race.

Design: docs/design/0107-0008m-bufpool-victim-stats-counter-wiring.md

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0008 loop-12 — checkpointer counters via stats.Counter
commits.description:
Migrate the sixth concrete stats.Counter consumer: the Checkpointer's
three aggregate counters (numTimed, numRequested, writeTimeMs) in
internal/wal/checkpointer.go move from atomic.Uint64 to stats.Counter.

Motivation is uniformity of storage shape across the WAL package's
observability surface — MemRing (loop 8) and the WAL writer drain
bytes (loop 11) already use stats.Counter — plus future-proofing
against a multi-writer Run loop. The Checkpointer's single-goroutine
write side means cross-P contention is not the dominant motivation,
but mixing seq-consistent atomic.Uint64 with eventual-consistent
stats.Counter inside the same view layer would burden readers with
remembering which counter has which guarantees.

Public Stats() boundary preserved via uint64(.Sum()) casts; the two
.Add(1) sites stay byte-identical and the .Add(uint64(ms)) site
simplifies to .Add(ms) directly (Duration.Milliseconds is int64).
lastCheckpointLSN / lastCheckpointRedoLSN / statsResetAt remain
atomic.* — they are not additive counters.

Memory cost: 48 KiB/server (3 × 16 KiB; Checkpointer is a singleton).
Existing TestOpenRegistersStatCheckpointerView covers the migrated
counters end-to-end through pg_stat_checkpointer.

Verified: internal/wal/ + internal/stats/ PASS under -race; cross-
package smoke storage/aio/runtimeshim PASS; initdb checkpointer-view
test PASS.

Design: docs/design/0107-0008l-checkpointer-stats-counter-wiring.md

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0008 loop-11 — drain byte counters via stats.Counter
commits.description:
walBufferCounters.overflowDrainBytes and .flushDrainBytes move from
atomic.Uint64 to stats.Counter. drainBufferBytes runs under
state.appendMu (single-writer-at-a-time) but the writer P rotates
with whichever client backend acquires the mutex next, so the
shared atomic.Uint64 line bounced across cores on every handoff.
Per-P sharding via stats.Counter keeps each write on the current
P's shard.

Public accessors (WALBuffersOverflowDrainBytes / .FlushDrainBytes,
both uint64) preserved via uint64(.Sum()) boundary casts; nil-safe
guards retained. The two .Add(uint64(n)) call sites simplify to
.Add(n) (n is already int64). pg_stat_wal_io columns unchanged.

Memory cost: 32 KiB / server (2 × 16 KiB Counter), flat.

Closes the loop-8 caveat that earlier deferred this migration on
single-writer grounds — appendMu serialises drains but does not
prevent cross-P cache-line bouncing on the counter line.

Existing TestWALBufferCountersTrackDrains covers both counters
end-to-end through the public API. Verified:
- go test -race ./internal/wal/    PASS (3.09 s)
- go test -race ./internal/stats/  PASS (1.02 s)

commits.title: feat(aio): M0107-0008 loop-10 — per-direction counters via stats.Counter
commits.description:
Migrate `Engine`'s six per-direction submit/complete/error counters
(`readSubmitted`/`readCompleted`/`readErrored`/`writeSubmitted`/
`writeCompleted`/`writeErrored`) and two per-direction latency-sum
counters (`readLatencySumMicros`, `writeLatencySumMicros`) from
`atomic.Uint64` to `stats.Counter`. Closes the consistency-shape
asymmetry loop 9 introduced: `Submitted == ReadSubmitted +
WriteSubmitted` is now eventual-consistent on both sides.

`{read,write}LatencyMaxMicros` stay `atomic.Uint64` (advanceMax is
CAS-clamped; per-shard max is meaningless). Per-target stats stay
`atomic.Uint64` (naturally sharded by target identity; migration
would inflate each record from ~48 B to ~80 KiB).

Stats() boundary uses `uint64(.Sum())` casts so all eight
`Stats.{Read,Write}{Submitted,Completed,Errored,LatencySumMicros}`
uint64 field types and positions are preserved verbatim;
`internal/initdb/aio_views.go` view binding unaffected.

commits.title: feat(aio): M0107-0008 loop-9 — Engine totals via stats.Counter
commits.description:
Third concrete consumer of internal/stats per-P Counter (after btree
loop-7 and MemRing loop-8). The AIO Engine's three aggregate totals —
submitted, completed, errored in internal/aio/aio.go — move from
atomic.Uint64 to stats.Counter. Hot path is Submit + finishHandle on
every buffer-pool/WAL/walsender/checkpointer I/O; under method=worker
the bumps come from multiple worker goroutines concurrently, so the
shared cache line for completed previously hopped between cores on
every completion.

Cold-path reader is Engine.Stats() only (feeding pg_stat_io view); the
three reader sites move from .Load() to uint64(.Sum()) so the public
Stats.Submitted/Completed/Errored uint64 field types and observed
numbers are preserved verbatim. The three .Add(1) call sites in
Submit/finishHandle are byte-identical.

Per-direction (read/write split), per-target (*targetStats), and
latency SumMicros/MaxMicros fields stay atomic — they couple to a
wider pg_stat_io view-shape unification and migrate together in a
later loop per loop-8's "Why not a smaller change" decision. inFlight,
nextID, and latency-Max also stay atomic (Max needs CAS; inFlight is a
signed gauge; nextID is a monotonic id allocator, not a counter).

Memory cost: 48 KiB per server (3 × 16 KiB Counter; exactly one
Engine per server). No new tests — existing internal/aio/aio_test.go
covers the migrated counters end-to-end via the public Stats() API.

Verified:

commits.title: feat(wal): M0107-0008 loop-8 — MemRing hits/misses via stats.Counter
commits.description:
Second concrete consumer of the per-P stats.Counter primitive (after
the loop-7 btree counters). MemRing.hits and .misses in
internal/wal/mem_ring.go move from atomic.Uint64 to stats.Counter,
eliminating cross-core cache-line invalidation on the walsender
ReadAt hot path. Multi-P contention surfaces when >=2 subscribers
stream concurrently (M0094-0005 hot-read E2E, M0102 heterogeneous-
replication failover, cascading-replica deployments).

Public API preserved verbatim — Hits() and Misses() still return
uint64, via a uint64(.Sum()) cast at the boundary. The two .Add(1)
call sites in ReadAt are byte-identical (the untyped constant 1 is
accepted by both atomic.Uint64.Add(uint64) and
stats.Counter.Add(int64)). pg_stat_wal_io and
pg_stat_replication.send_buffer_* view callers
(internal/initdb/{wal_io_views,replication_views}.go) unaffected.
No Reset() exposed on MemRing (counters are read-only-after-
construction in production), so stats.Counter.Reset() is unused.

commits.title: feat(btree): M0107-0008 loop-7 — Inserts/Splits via stats.Counter
commits.description:
First concrete consumer of the per-P stats.Counter primitive landed
in loop 6. (*BTree).Inserts and .Splits move from atomic.AddUint64
on a shared BTreeStats field to a private btreeStatsCounters{
inserts, splits stats.Counter }, eliminating cross-core cache-line

bench; higher under multi-writer workloads). Public BTreeStats

commits.title: feat(stats): M0107-0008 loop-6 — internal/stats per-P Counter primitive
commits.description:
New internal/stats package with a single public type Counter — an
additive int64 counter sharded across maxShards = 256 cache-line-
padded atomic.Int64 slots via runtimeshim.PinP/UnpinP. Add(delta)
is two function calls plus an atomic add inside the pinned window
(no contention possible on the linkname path); Sum() does 256
atomic loads on the cold path; Reset() does 256 atomic stores.

atomic.Int64 (not plain int64) inside the pinned window so a
concurrent Sum reader on a different P sees a well-defined value.

Five race-clean tests cover single-goroutine round trip, Reset,
concurrent-Add total-exact (32 g × 16 K = 524 288 Adds, final
Sum equals the issued total exactly), per-shard write distribution
(GOMAXPROCS≥2 sanity that sharding actually fans out), and
Sum-vs-Add no-torn-read invariant. The Sum-vs-Add test uses
separate producer/reader WaitGroups so the reader-stop signal
fires after producers complete (the originally-drafted version
deadlocked because wg.Wait() blocked on the reader, which in turn
blocked on stop that was never set).

BenchmarkCounterAdd-16 0.8054 ns/op on Linux/amd64 Go 1.25
(16 cores) on the parallel path.

Migration of specific global atomic counters to stats.Counter is
deliberately deferred per-consumer-family to subsequent loops so
each migration can be reviewed and reverted independently. This
finishes the parent chapter's two viable PinP consumers (the
per-P xid cache was ruled out in 0107-0008d for snapshot-
correctness reasons).

Design: docs/design/0107-0008f-perp-stats-counter.md (indexed
in docs/design/README.md).

Verified: go test -race -count=1 ./internal/stats/... PASS (1.02 s);
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/runtimeshim/... PASS (1.22 s);

commits.title: feat(activity): M0107-0008 loop-5 — runtimeshim.Nanotime caller wiring
commits.description:
Wire ActivityRegistry's five time.Now().UnixNano() call sites
(WaitEventStart, WaitEventEnd, UpdateState, BeginTransaction,
EndTransaction, acquire) through runtimeshim.Nanotime() (~20 ns/op
vs ~50 ns for time.Now). At ~c × 30 k/s WaitEvent frames in pgbench
c=100 SU, this is the highest-volume timekeeping site in the server.

Stored fields (activitySlot.stateChange, coldActivity.XactStart,
coldActivity.QueryStart) now hold monotonic-since-runtime-start nanos.
Snapshot() converts back to wall-clock via a once-at-construction
(monoEpoch, wallEpoch) pair: wall = wallEpoch + (mono - monoEpoch).
pg_stat_activity wire timestamps remain RFC3339Nano-formatted.

New regression TestActivityRegistryStateChangeIsWallClock asserts the
converted timestamp parses as RFC3339Nano within ±2 s of time.Now().

commits.title: docs(runtimeshim): M0107-0008 loop-4 — per-P XID cache caller blocked
commits.description:
Attempted to wire runtimeshim.PinP/UnpinP into internal/mvcc/XidGen
per perf-optimize/08-runtime-internals.md §4 "Use case 1" (per-P
32-xid cache, batch refill from global atomic). Implementation
passed all internal/mvcc/ and internal/runtimeshim/ tests including
a 32-goroutine x 4K-allocation uniqueness stress, but deterministically
broke TestUpsertDoNothing_WaitsForInFlightDelete on the first run.
Rolled back in the same loop.

Root cause: per-P caching breaks two invariants Manager.captureSnapshot
relies on:

  1. Monotonic xid assignment across backends. With per-P windows,
     the sequence of issued xids interleaves across goroutines —
     P_a hands out xid 4 after P_b has been running with xid 35.
  2. Snapshot.Xmax-as-upper-bound-of-all-issued-xids. Neither
     candidate Peek definition preserves visibility correctness:
     min(cache.next, global) excludes currently-issued xids on
     other Ps from InProgress (mis-classifying live transactions
     as "future"); global.Load() re-includes them but mis-classifies
     later-issued cached xids as "committed before snapshot".

The design doc's correctness argument only covers cached xids that
are NEVER issued; it does not address the normal hot-path case of
a cached xid being handed out after a snapshot has been taken.

The XID-cache caller is removed from M0107-0008 scope. The three
shim primitives themselves (Nanotime, PinP, Sema) remain accepted
from loops 1-3. Remaining in-scope callers: activity-registry
Nanotime, bufpool per-slot Sema wait, per-P stats counters.

Design doc: docs/design/0107-0008d-perp-xidcache-snapshot-incompat.md
indexed in docs/design/README.md.

Verification on revert (loop 4 final state):
  go test -race -count=1 \
    ./internal/mvcc/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/executor/ \
    ./internal/wal/ ./internal/storage/ ./internal/runtimeshim/
  -> all PASS.

commits.title: feat(runtimeshim): M0107-0008 loop-3 — SemaAcquire/SemaRelease shim
commits.description:
Third //go:linkname primitive in internal/runtimeshim, completing the
trio specified by docs/design/perf-optimize/08-runtime-internals.md §5
(Nanotime, PinP/UnpinP, SemaAcquire/SemaRelease).

* sema_linkname.go (go1.24 && !go1.27) binds runtime_Semacquire and
  runtime_Semrelease to sync.runtime_Semacquire / sync.runtime_Semrelease
  — the stable external symbols sync.Mutex/WaitGroup/Cond depend on.
  SemaRelease calls the primitive with handoff=false, skipframes=0 to
  match sync.Mutex.Unlock — the right default for bufpool per-slot
  "I/O finished; any waiter may proceed" wake semantics.
* sema_fallback.go (inverse tag) uses a global sync.Mutex plus a
  lazy map[*uint32]*sync.Cond. Correct semantics; contention-bound.
* sema_test.go: four contract-anchored tests anchored to the design
  doc — pre-released no-block path, block-then-wake, 8-producer ×
  8-consumer balanced pairing with final *s == 0, per-cell wait-queue
  isolation. BenchmarkSemaAcquireRelease: 5.6 ns/op on Linux/amd64
  Go 1.25 (uncontended; cell stays positive).
* Caller wiring (bufpool per-slot wait coordination per 06-bufpool-
  lockfree.md) deliberately NOT in this loop — lands separately so the
  shim's contract is validated standalone.

commits.title: feat(storage): M0107-0006 loop-2 — bufmap atomic keys + stress test
commits.description:
New `TestPoolHighConcurrencyPinUnpinStress` (env-var-tunable up to
1000 goroutines × 30 s) closes the M0107-0006 stress-test verification
gate and surfaced two real data races in the loop-1 bufmap rewrite:
`compact()` non-atomic `keys[i]` writes vs concurrent `Lookup` reads,
and ABA on `Insert(tombstone → live₂)` racing a `Lookup` that read
`keys[h]` after observing the previous `live₁`.

Fix: each bucket now stores `key0` / `key1` / `val` as `atomic.Uint64`
(packed BufferTag); `inner atomic.Pointer[bufmapInner]` swap on
compact so readers see a single immutable snapshot; seqlock-style
Lookup re-loads val after key reads to detect torn snapshots; Insert
parks val at tombstone before rewriting keys.

./internal/access/btree/` PASS; stress test PASS with `-race` at
1000 goroutines × 5 s.

commits.title: feat(storage): M0107-0006 loop-1 — bufmap & FPI correctness fixes
commits.description:
Three correctness bugs in the partially-landed Phase D3 lock-free
buffer pool surfaced as test hangs / failures in -race storage tests.
This change makes the storage package pass with -race; the M0107-0006
performance gates (pgbench TPS, mutex top-20, 1000-goroutine stress)
remain pending.

1. bufmap packVal collision with bufmapTombstone=1

   (slotIdx=0, gen=1) packed to value 1, equal to the tombstone
   sentinel.  The legacy `val |= 2` workaround corrupted the gen
   field so bufmap.Lookup returned gen=3 while the slot's true gen
   was 1 — pinSlow looped forever under pinMu on the first re-pin
   (TestBgwriterDoDDirtyVictimRate hung).  Shift slotIdx by +1
   inside packVal so the high 32 bits of every live value are
   non-zero and cannot collide with the 0/1 sentinels.

2. bufmap Lookup's invalid Robin-Hood early exit

   Lookup bailed when `dist > residentDist`, an optimisation that
   is only correct when Insert maintains Robin-Hood order via
   displacement.  Insert is plain linear probing, so Lookup missed
   real entries on collision chains (TestScanRingCacheMissNoEviction
   found 86/90 hot pages).  Drop the early-exit; rely on the
   empty-bucket terminator and the dist <= size safety bound.

3. fpiSinceCheckpoint contentMu self-deadlock

   maybeEmitFPI took s.contentMu.Lock() to read the flag, but
   MarkDirty callers hold s.Lock() for their page-byte writes.
   sync.RWMutex is non-reentrant — the second Lock() blocked
   (TestPoolFPIEmittedOncePerEpoch).  Convert
   fpiSinceCheckpoint to atomic.Bool; remove contentMu from the
   FPI flag path entirely.

Verification:
  go test -count=1 -timeout 60s ./internal/storage/  PASS
  go test -race -count=1 -timeout 300s ./internal/storage/  PASS
  go test -race -count=1 -timeout 300s ./internal/mvcc/ \
     ./internal/wal/ ./internal/executor/ ./internal/access/btree/  PASS

commits.title: fix(executor): M0100-0005 loop-23 — CTE snapshot isolation + UPDATE btree maintenance
commits.description:

Two bugs fixed:

(A) Non-partition updateOp/updateViaIndex did NOT call
    maintainUniqueIndexesForInsert after writing the new row version, so
    ON CONFLICT arbiters could not find the live committed row after a
    concurrent UPDATE.  Fix: add maintainUniqueIndexesForInsert call in
    both the seqScan and updateViaIndex UPDATE paths when destPart==nil.
    Also: probeArbiter now follows HOT chains (HeapHotUpdated bit) from
    dead index entries to find live successor tuples.

(B) cteDMLPrefixOp.Open() refreshed ctx.Snap via probeArbiterWaiting,
    causing the outer SELECT to use the refreshed snapshot instead of
    the statement-start snapshot.  PostgreSQL CTE semantics require:
    outer query uses the pre-DML snapshot; own DML writes are invisible
    to the outer SELECT.  Fix: save/restore ctx.Snap around DML CTE
    execution; track written row pointers in ctx.CTEWriteFence; seqScanOp
    skips fenced rows (written by the DML CTE in progress).

commits.title: fix(executor,server): M0100-0005 isolation suite — 12/21 PASS (+MergeInsertUpdate)
commits.description:
Four coupled fixes advancing the RC isolation suite from 11/21 to 12/21:

(A) MERGE NOT MATCHED INSERT path now mirrors insertOp:
    - partition routing via routeToPartition + remapRowForPartition
    - BEFORE INSERT trigger firing via fireTriggers
    - unique constraint check with wait semantics via checkUniqueIndexesForInsert
      (waits for in-flight concurrent inserts, raises 23505 on commit, retries
      after abort — matching PostgreSQL MERGE NOT MATCHED semantics)
    - index maintenance via maintainUniqueIndexesForInsert

(B) MERGE MATCHED UPDATE EPQ: when epqFollowHOT returns not-found (target
    row deleted by concurrent committed transaction), applyMod now returns
    errMergeSourceUnmatched instead of nil, and the outer loop resets
    srcRows[mod.srcIdx].matched=false so the NOT MATCHED INSERT clauses can
    fire on the source row. srcIdx field added to mergePendingMod.

(C) isLiveForUniqueCheck: add TxnMgr.HasAbortedXID(xmin) arm before default
    so transactions that aborted after our snapshot was taken are correctly
    classified as non-live (fixes spurious 23505 when MERGE NOT MATCHED INSERT
    waits for a concurrent aborter).

(D) failed-transaction state (25P02): connTxState gains failed bool +
    Fail()/IsFailed() methods. After any errQueryErrorSent within an explicit
    transaction, Fail() is called. Subsequent statements return
    "current transaction is aborted, commands ignored" (25P02). COMMIT on a
    failed transaction silently ROLLBACKs and clears the failed flag.
    TestPort_IsolationMergeInsertUpdate: PASS (was SKIP).

commits.title: fix(executor): lockRowsOp follows committed-update CTID chain + RR/SER 40001
commits.description:
stampLockInner now handles real non-lock-only xmax from another xact
in three paths instead of the M0100-0005f skip-all:

(a) Non-key update + FOR KEY SHARE: preserve M0100-0005f semantics —
    skip stamping without blocking (FOR KEY SHARE doesn't conflict).
(b) Key-column update (HeapKeysUpdated set in infomask2) or FOR UPDATE:
    wait for in-progress xmax via WaitForXID (produces <waiting ...>),
    then under RC follow the CTID chain to the live successor and stamp
    it; under RR/SER raise 40001 serialization error.

updateViaIndex sets HeapKeysUpdated on the old tuple when !hotEligible
(i.e. at least one indexed column changed) — mirrors PG's HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED.
storage.HeapKeysUpdated = 0x2000 added; PageSetHeapTupleKeysUpdated added.

drainAndStamp records the successor ptr (entry.newPtrValid/newPtr);
Next() refetches the row via refetchRow when the chain was followed.
