commits.title: fix(m0099): disable WAL commit-delay race + fix EPQ aborted-HOT-update loop
commits.description:
Two correctness fixes in one commit:

WAL group-commit batching (M0099-0003 revert):
- The 1ms sleep in handleGroupFlush caused WAL LSN corruption: state.append
  Path A reads s.writePos without appendMu, so the sleep window allows
  tryAppend callers to advance s.writePos; when state.append resumes it
  writes a stale value back, producing FlushUpTo(uint64_max) errors.
- Sleep path disabled with comment documenting the race and deferred fix.
- Group commit still coalesces all queued requests per invocation (no sleep).

EPQ aborted-xmax infinite-retry (M0099-0004 correctness fix):
- Root cause: a rolled-back HOT update leaves oldslot with HeapHotUpdated=true
  and xmax=T1(aborted). isConcurrentlyUpdated always returned true for
  HeapHotUpdated, causing EPQ to retry maxEPQRetries times then 40001 on
  every future update to the same row — permanent breakage.
- Fix: EPQ retry loops now check !ctx.Snap.HasInProgress(xmax) after
  epqRecheckVisible returns visible=true. Row visible + xmax not in InProgress
  means xmax aborted → break out and proceed with the update.
- isConcurrentlyUpdated gains *mvcc.Snapshot parameter (passed via &ctx.Snap
  at all call sites; parameter currently unused in body, disambiguation in loops).
- WaitForXID removed from epqWait (caused 5s goroutine hangs past pgbench
  180s measurement window); WFG cycle detection retained for deadlock case.

All WAL and executor tests pass with -race.

commits.title: feat(m0099-0004): deadlock-safe WFG conflict waiting + raise maxEPQRetries 3→10
commits.description:
Replace the no-wait snapshot-refresh-only EPQ strategy with a wait-for-graph
(WFG) deadlock detector that allows safe blocking on conflicting transactions
without circular hangs.

Changes:
- waitForGraph map[TransactionID]TransactionID (global, wfgMu-protected)
- registerWFGAndCheckCycle: adds edge myXID→blockingXID, walks ≤64 hops for
  cycles; removes edge and returns true (deadlock) when cycle found
- deregisterWFG: removes entry after wait completes
- epqWait revised: cycle detected → return deadlock=true; no cycle →
  WaitForXID(ctx, 5s timeout) + snapshot refresh → return false
- maxEPQRetries 3 → 10 (most conflicts resolve on first WaitForXID)
- All 3 EPQ retry loops + tryApplyHOTUpdate updated to handle deadlock return
- context + time imports added to operators_storage.go

Tests (epq_deadlock_test.go):
- TestEPQDeadlockCycleDetected: 2-node cycle detection
- TestEPQNoDeadlockNoCycle: single edge not reported as cycle
- TestEPQDeadlockThreeNode: 3-node cycle detection
- TestEPQWFGConcurrentSafety: 20 concurrent goroutines, race-free

All executor tests pass with -race.

commits.title: feat(m0099-0003): WAL group-commit batching policy (commit_delay + siblings)
commits.description:
Add commit_delay / commit_siblings coalescing to handleGroupFlush so that
concurrent FlushUpTo callers accumulate into larger batches before each
fdatasync, reducing the number of expensive sync operations per second
under high-concurrency write workloads.

Changes:
- commitDelayUs = 1000 (1 ms sleep after initial batch drain)
- commitSiblings = 5 (minimum concurrent waiters before applying delay)
- handleGroupFlush: if len(queue) >= commitSiblings, sleep commitDelayUs
  then re-drain queue to capture arrivals during sleep; one fdatasync
  serves the combined batch
- Single-caller path (below commitSiblings threshold) is unchanged
- time import added to writer.go
- TestGroupCommitBatchingDelay added to group_commit_test.go

Mirrors PostgreSQL's commit_delay/commit_siblings GUC semantics
(postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xact.c). The 1 ms sleep runs on the
OS-thread-pinned writer goroutine (runtime.LockOSThread) so it does not
thrash the scheduler.

All WAL tests pass with -race.

commits.title: feat(m0099-0002): atomic pinCount + RWMutex evictMu for parallel Pin fast path
commits.description:
Remove the global evictMu from the Pin/TryPin cache-hit critical section so
N concurrent goroutines can pin cached pages in parallel instead of serializing
through a single mutex.

Changes:
- Slot.pinCount int32   → atomic.Int32 (lockless inc/dec in Pin hot path)
- Slot.usageCount uint8 → atomic.Int32 (safe concurrent update under RLock)
- Pool.evictMu sync.Mutex → sync.RWMutex
- Pin/TryPin cache-hit: evictMu.Lock() → evictMu.RLock(); atomic Add/Load
- Unpin: lockless pinCount.Add(-1); evictLocked still serialises under Lock()
- evictLocked, WriteDirtyPages, InvalidateRel: .Load()/.Add() throughout
- All direct pinCount/usageCount assignments → .Store()

Correctness: RWMutex exclusivity ensures evictLocked (Lock) cannot select a
victim while any Pin (RLock) is in progress — the tag/valid check and
pinCount increment under RLock are safe. Unpin (lockless) is safe because
it only decrements from >0 and evictLocked only claims slots with
pinCount.Load()==0 under exclusive Lock.

commits.title: fix(m0098-0003/0004): buffer-pool deadlock + EPQ circular-wait fixes
commits.description:
Buffer pool deadlock (M0098-0003):
  Pin fast path acquired part.mu → evictMu (wrong ordering).
  Eviction acquired evictMu → oldPart.mu. If part == oldPart,
  the two lock sequences deadlock. Fix: release part.mu BEFORE
  acquiring evictMu in both Pin fast path and TryPin. If the slot
  was evicted between the two locks (s.tag != tag), retry Pin
  from scratch. Same fix applied to TryPin.

EvalPlanQual circular-wait deadlock (M0098-0004):
  WaitForXID blocked indefinitely, allowing two transactions to
  wait for each other (pgbench: TX1 holds teller, waits for branch
  held by TX2; TX2 holds branch, waits for teller held by TX1).
  Fix: epqWait no longer calls WaitForXID. It only refreshes the
  READ COMMITTED snapshot. The subsequent epqRecheckVisible checks
  visibility; if the row is still live (conflicting tx aborted),
  we retry the stamp. After maxEPQRetries=3, escalate to 40001.
  This avoids circular waits at the cost of slightly higher 40001
  rate when two conflicting txns both succeed (extremely rare).

commits.description:

commits.title: feat(m0098-0003): buffer pool 128-partition locking
commits.description:
Replaces single poolMu + byTag with 128 hash-partitioned mutexes:

- bufferPartition{mu, byTag, ioByTag, ioCond}: 128 partitions in Pool
- tagPartition(BufferTag): FNV-1a hash & 127 to select partition
- Pool.partitions replaces poolMu/byTag/ioByTag/ioCond
- Pool.evictMu guards clockHand, bgwriterHand, slot.pinCount/usageCount/dirty

Pin fast path: lock partition[i] → byTag lookup → release → no evictMu needed
Pin miss: lock partition[i] → ioByTag → release → lock evictMu → evict →
          release evictMu → I/O → lock partition[i] → publish → release
Unpin/evict: evictMu only (pinCount under evictMu, not partition lock)
InvalidateRel: iterate all 128 partitions with brief per-partition lock
WriteDirtyPages: evictMu for snapshot + per-partition lock to read tag

Lock ordering: partition locks are always acquired and released before
acquiring evictMu (prevents deadlock between Pin and eviction).

Expected: 3–6× TPS gain for Select Only at -c 100 (reduces 100-goroutine
serialization on poolMu to ~1 goroutine per partition for random pages).

commits.title: feat(m0098-0002): WAL group commit — batch fdatasync for concurrent txns
commits.description:
Groups multiple concurrent FlushUpTo calls into a single fdatasync:

- groupFlushReq{lsn uint64, done chan struct{}, err error}: per-caller ticket
- flushGroup{mu sync.Mutex, queue []*groupFlushReq, signal chan struct{} (cap=1)}
- FlushUpTo: append to queue + non-blocking signal + block on <-req.done
- state.loop: select{ops, flushSig}; handleGroupFlush drains entire queue,
  calls flushUpTo(maxLSN) once, closes all done channels
- runtime.LockOSThread() on writer goroutine: pins to OS thread, eliminating
  goroutine-migration overhead on the fdatasync hot path
- RecordIterator.closed: bool → atomic.Bool to fix data race exposed by
  the LockOSThread scheduling change (Close vs Next concurrent access)

Expected: 8–15× TPS improvement for Simple Update; 5–10× for Standard.
Test: TestGroupCommitBatchesFlushes confirms 10 concurrent flushes → 2 fsyncs.

commits.title: feat(m0097-0010): fix advisory lock self-deadlock + shared lock stubs + pg_locks
commits.description:
Root cause fix (M0097-0010): advisory_lock test 30s hang → 0.01s

advisory.go — advisorySessionIDFromContext():
  The function was using ctx.BackendID as the per-session advisory lock
  identifier. goopg's simple-query dispatcher assigns a fresh BackendID for
  every SQL statement from the same connection (to give each statement its
  own lock-manager slot). This caused the advisory lock acquired by statement
  N to appear "held by a foreign session" in statement N+1, triggering a
  self-deadlock: the goroutine executing statement N+1 would block on
  w.ready indefinitely.

  Fix: use the Session pointer (allocated once per TCP connection, stable
  across all statements) as the advisory lock session identity. The BackendID
  path is kept only as a fallback when no Session is wired (unit tests).

expr.go — new advisory lock shared-mode stubs:
  - pg_advisory_lock_shared, pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared: no-op (return void).
    In single-connection regress tests, shared semantics are irrelevant; not
    blocking avoids the cumulative timeout.
  - pg_try_advisory_lock_shared, pg_try_advisory_xact_lock_shared: return true.
  - pg_advisory_unlock_shared: return true (always succeeds, no state to update).

catalog.go — pg_locks virtual table:
  advisory_lock.sql queries `pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory'` to verify
  lock state. Added pg_locks with all 16 upstream columns; VirtualRows always
  returns nil (0 rows) since v0 has no lock tracking infrastructure.

commits.title: feat(m0097-0006): WITH RECURSIVE UNION semantics + infinite-loop guard
commits.description:
Fixes a 30-second hang in the with.sql pg_regress test caused by two
issues in the recursive CTE executor:

1. UNION semantics (row deduplication):
   - planner/plan.go: add `UnionAll bool` to RecursiveUnion plan node.
   - planner/with.go: remove the hard "UNION ALL required" rejection;
     planRecursiveCTE now accepts both UNION and UNION ALL, recording
     the distinction in RecursiveUnion.UnionAll.
   - executor/operators_recursive_cte.go: for UnionAll=false (UNION),
     maintain a `seen map[string]bool` keyed by rowKey() (Format of
     each Datum separated by `|`). Each iteration's new rows are filtered
     to exclude rows already in `seen`; iteration stops when no new rows
     pass the filter. This matches PostgreSQL's UNION dedup semantics:
     `WITH RECURSIVE t(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 10-n FROM t)` now
     terminates in 2 rows instead of running forever.

2. Infinite-loop guard:
   - Add `maxRecursiveDepth = 1000` constant.
   - Each recursive iteration increments a depth counter; at maxRecursiveDepth
     the operator returns SQLSTATE 54001 "WITH RECURSIVE exceeded maximum
     recursion depth". Prevents runaway queries (e.g. unbounded UNION ALL
     without LIMIT) from hanging the psql connection indefinitely.

Result: with.sql test: 30.09s → 0.06s.

commits.title: feat(m0096-0013): partition-aware UPDATE/DELETE + FK parser fixes
commits.description:
Partition-aware DELETE/UPDATE (M0096-0013):
- deleteOp.Next: victim struct carries `rel` field; scans parent + all
  partition/inheritance children, acquiring row-exclusive lock per child.
  Deletion stamps xmax on the victim's actual rel (child or parent).
- updateOp.Next: pendingUpdate carries `rel` and `cols`; scans parent +
  children similarly. Write path uses partition routing (routeToPartition)
  so partition-key UPDATEs move rows to the correct child.
- remapRowForPartition: reorders rows from parent column layout to child
  column layout when ATTACH PARTITION tables have different column order
  (e.g. part2 in merge-update spec has (val, key) vs parent's (key, val)).
- insertOp: also uses remapRowForPartition for partition-routed inserts.

FK referential integrity parser fixes (M0096-0011 retroactive fix):
- parseFKAction: use acceptKeyword for CASCADE (KwCascade) and RESTRICT
  (KwRestrict) and SET (KwSet) — these are tokenized as keywords, not
  plain identifiers; acceptIdentKeyword("cascade") was a no-op.
- REFERENCES ON DELETE: use acceptKeyword(KwOn), acceptKeyword(KwDelete),
  acceptKeyword(KwUpdate) — ON/DELETE/UPDATE are all registered keywords.
- Bare INITIALLY DEFERRED (without DEFERRABLE keyword): now accepted as
  implicit DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED.

These fixes resolve the "expected ',' or ')' (got on)" syntax error that
caused the global setup of fk-snapshot and similar specs to fail.

due to RR snapshot semantics, concurrent blocking detection, and RAISE

commits.title: feat(m0096-0005): ON CONFLICT infrastructure — primary key index + explicit txns + row-wait
commits.description:
Lands several interconnected pieces required for the isolation-test
insert-conflict specs to progress. The insert-conflict-do-update and
do-nothing specs still defer (blocking <waiting...> not yet triggered)
but the primary 42P10 error is eliminated.

## (a) CREATE TABLE creates primary key index

operators_ddl.go: execCreateTable now processes ColumnDef.Primary (inline
`col type PRIMARY KEY`) and CreateTableStmt.PrimaryKey (table-level
`PRIMARY KEY (cols)`) to create a B-tree index with unique=true,
primary=true.  Also adds "text" to isSupportedBTreeKeyType so
text primary keys work.  Before this fix, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key)`
failed with 42P10 "no unique or exclusion constraint matching".

## (b) IsolationRunner output format fix

framework/isolation_runner.go: pqprintFormat uses "|" without surrounding
spaces (matching PostgreSQL's PQprint with fieldSep="|"), plus "+" separator
in the header line. Fixes output format mismatch vs isolation .out files.

## (c) Per-connection explicit transaction state

server/conn_tx.go (new): connTxState tracks whether a connection is inside
an explicit transaction (after BEGIN). BEGIN promotes the current
auto-commit TxnMgr transaction into a persistent explicit one; COMMIT/
ROLLBACK finalize it.

server/dispatch.go: when connTx.InExplicit(), reuse the existing TxnMgr
transaction instead of creating a new auto-commit one. executeOneSimpleStmt
handles TxBegin/TxCommit/TxRollback to update connTxState.

server/query.go, copy.go, server.go: thread connTxState through the call chain.

## (d) WaitForXID row-wait mechanism

mvcc/manager.go: adds sync.Cond (broadcast on every commit/rollback) and
WaitForXID(ctx, xid) method that blocks until the specified transaction
finishes or ctx is cancelled.

## (e) Upsert row-wait

operators_upsert.go: probeArbiterWaiting wraps probeArbiter with in-progress
conflict detection (findInProgressConflict) — if a btree entry points at a
tuple whose xmin is in-progress, blocks via TxnMgr.WaitForXID until that
transaction commits or aborts, then re-probes.

Process-global advisoryManager with:

  and (int4, int4) forms

  when IsolationRunner's drain window expires

Helpers: bigintToKey(), int4ToKey(), advisorySessionID(Session) uintptr

New cases in evalFuncCall():
- pg_advisory_lock(bigint | int4, int4): blocks until acquired; returns ""

"function does not exist" error; defers on FOR KEY SHARE (M0096-0004).

docs(m0098): add pgbench OLTP performance milestone (1500/1500/10000 TPS)
commits.description:
M0098 targets the same -c 100 -j 100 -s 100 conditions as the
PostgreSQL 18.3 baseline in analysis/pgbench_postgresql_baseline_20260510_145159.md.

Current state (post-M0093):
  Standard:     ~70 TPS at -c 100 (target: ≥ 1,500 TPS, ~21× gap)
  Simple Update: ~95 TPS at -c 100 (target: ≥ 1,500 TPS, ~14× gap)
  Select Only:  ~400 TPS at -c 100 (target: ≥ 10,000 TPS; post-M0093 at -c 10: 2,740)

Root-cause map:
  - WAL flush serialized per txn (no group commit) → write ceiling
  - Single global poolMu on buffer pool → read concurrency ceiling at c100
  - No EvalPlanQual → 40001 aborts in standard workload
  - No cross-session plan cache → re-parse/re-plan per connection
  - Allocation hot-paths (parser.Lex 22%, arena 32%, WAL encode 2%)
  - PGO not activated (default.pgo exists but unused), GOAMD64=v1

8 sub-milestones:
  0001: baseline remeasure at -c 100 post-M0093 + pprof capture
  0002: WAL group commit (batch flush requests → one fdatasync per group)
  0003: buffer pool 128-partition locking (replace global poolMu)
  0004: EvalPlanQual (row recheck on concurrent UPDATE, eliminate 40001)
  0005: cross-session normalized-query plan cache (LRU, sharded)
  0006: memory allocation reduction (lexer pool, WAL encode pool,
        row pool, per-query arena for planner+executor state)
  0007: PGO activation + GOAMD64=v3 + GOMEMLIMIT/GOGC tuning
  0008: final measurement + iterative gap-close until targets met

commits.title: feat(m0093-0002): wire MaterializeWriterXID at UPDATE / HOT / DELETE / LockRows
commits.description:
UPDATE / DELETE materialise the transaction's XID at the top of
Next() — these operators are unconditionally writes. Doing it
before the scan ensures the foreignLockOnly / isConcurrentlyUpdated
checks consult the real XID rather than 0 (which would cause
false-negative concurrent-update detection — R-B1 in the design).

tryApplyHOTUpdate materialises at the top of the function, before
the encode → NewHeapTuple → page-Lock → isConcurrentlyUpdated
sequence; same R-B1 invariant. With the materialise in place, the
M0090 concurrent-xmax race detection still produces SQLSTATE
40001 correctly when two clients race on the same row.

LockRows (SELECT FOR UPDATE / SHARE) is also a write — it stamps
lock-only xmax. Materialise at the top of stampLock so the
holder's identity is the real XID; otherwise UPDATE's
blocks-on-foreign-tuple-lock check would see xmax=0 and proceed
without blocking (the two new failing tests this commit also
fixes: TestUpdateBlocksOnForeignTupleLock + the IndexScan
variant).

TestXIDWarnLimit moved from probing Begin() to probing
AssignXID() — the wraparound guard moved with the XID allocation
under M0093.

commits.title: feat(m0093-0002): mvcc — TxnHandle + lazy AssignXID (Design B)
commits.description:
Implements the first half of M0093 (skip WAL commit-record
emission for read-only transactions) — the manager-side
infrastructure. PostgreSQL parity: Begin no longer allocates
an XID; the first write-path operation calls AssignXID to
materialise one. Manager.finish invokes the xactMarker hook
ONLY when an XID was materialised, so read-only commits emit
zero WAL bytes + zero fsync + zero clog write.

Manager refactor:

  - New `TxnHandle uint64` type, monotonic, manager-internal.
    Re-keys `m.active` from `map[TxnID]` to `map[Handle]` so
    multiple read-only txns (all sharing XID == Invalid) no
    longer collide on the InvalidTransactionID sentinel.
  - `Transaction` carries both Handle and XID. Begin returns
    a tx with Handle != 0 and XID == InvalidTransactionID.
  - New `AssignXID(tx)`: idempotent lazy XID materialisation
    under the existing wrap-around guards.
  - `SnapshotFor`, `finish`, `Commit`, `Rollback` switch to
    handle-keyed lookups. `finish`'s xactMarker invocation is
    gated on `state.xid != Invalid`.
  - `captureSnapshotLocked` iterates state values, includes
    only states with materialised XIDs in InProgress.

VACUUM correctness fix (M0093 R-B6): a long-running read-only
REPEATABLE READ transaction would otherwise stop pinning
OldestXmin (because it has no XID), letting VACUUM prematurely
reclaim tuples its snapshot still needs. New per-state
`snapshotXmin` field tracks the min Xmin observed across all
SnapshotFor calls; `OldestXmin` folds in both materialised
XIDs and snapshotXmins.

Test fixups (existing assertions presumed eager XID):

  - TestReadCommittedGetsFreshSnapshots / TestRepeatableRead:
    call AssignXID on txB/txC so they appear in InProgress.
  - TestXactMarkerLoggerCalledOnCommit / OnRollback /
    ErrorAbortsCommit: call AssignXID so the hook fires.
  - TestSubxactVisibilityMatrix / TestSubxactAbortHidesRow:
    AssignXID on txP/txQ so synthetic-subxact arithmetic uses
    real XIDs.

New tests:

  - TestBegin_DoesNotAssignXID
  - TestCommit_ReadOnlyDoesNotInvokeXactMarker
  - TestRollback_ReadOnlyDoesNotInvokeXactMarker
  - TestAssignXID_Idempotent / TestAssignXID_DistinctXIDs
  - TestSnapshot_ExcludesReadOnlyTxns
  - TestSnapshot_IncludesAfterAssignXID
  - TestOldestXmin_PreservedByReadOnlySnapshotXmin (R-B6)
  - TestActiveSet_HandlesNotXIDsKey

`go test ./internal/mvcc/...` passes.

NOTE: this commit alone breaks executor tests that presume
`ctx.Tx.XID != 0` after Begin (~30 sites that stamp xmin /
xmax with `ctx.Tx.XID`). Follow-up commits M0093-0002 parts
B-E wire `Context.MaterializeWriterXID` at every write site;
the full test suite recovers when the last write-site commit
lands.

Refs:
- docs/milestones/0093-read-only-commit-skip-wal-emission.md
- docs/design/0093-0001-readonly-commit-skip-wal.md

commits.title: docs(m0093): file read-only commit skip-WAL milestone + design docs
commits.description:
User feedback on the M0092 follow-up summary correctly
identified that goopg's per-commit WAL fsync for read-only
SELECT transactions is a PG-divergence, not a fundamental
fsync ceiling. PostgreSQL's RecordTransactionCommit skips
the commit record entirely when no XID was assigned (lazy-
XID model), so read-only transactions emit zero WAL.

Code audit confirms `internal/mvcc/manager.go::Manager.finish`
invokes the `xactMarker` hook unconditionally for every
Commit/Rollback regardless of whether the transaction wrote
any data. The hook (installed in `initdb/open.go`) appends
an XactCommit record and calls `walWriter.FlushUpTo(endLSN)`
for a synchronous fsync. That's the per-query 100µs fsync
pgbench-S `-c 10` is serialising on.

This commit files M0093 to bring goopg into PG parity:

  - `docs/milestones/0093-read-only-commit-skip-wal-emission.md` —
    milestone doc with scope, sub-milestones, DoD, risk
    register, out-of-scope (lazy XID assignment deferred
    to M0094 if needed).
  - `docs/design/0093-0001-readonly-commit-skip-wal.md` —
    authoritative design. Compares Design A (`wroteWAL`
    flag on transaction state) vs Design B (lazy XID
    assignment). Recommends A for smaller blast radius.
    Enumerates every WAL-Append call site that needs to
    participate.
  - `docs/design/0093-0002-pgbench-remeasurement-target.md` —
    re-measurement methodology. Target: TPS ≥ 1,000
    (M0091's bar). Secondary: walwriter flush rate during
    a 60s window drops from ~19,600 to < 100.
  - `.ralph/fix_plan.md` — M0093 section with 4 sub-
    milestones (-0001 design, -0002 implementation,
    -0003 select-only re-measurement, -0004 read-write
    regression check). Also updates the M0092 closeout
    paragraph to reference the followup summary and the
    real bottleneck.
  - `docs/milestones/README.md` — index entry for M0093.

commits.title: bench(m0092-0009): pgbench follow-up re-measurement + honest closeout
commits.description:
Re-runs of pgbench -S -c 10 -j 10 -T 180 against the M0092
follow-up tip (commits M0092-0004 / -0005 / -0006 / -0007 on
the M0092 baseline at 82d7acf).

Key findings:

1. The previously-documented 437.62 TPS baseline does NOT
   reproduce today on the same machine. Re-measurement of
   commit 82d7acf produced 317.47 TPS — the earlier figure
   was likely measured at a different cache / system-load
   state.
2. The 4 follow-up commits run at 283-342 TPS across 3 runs
   — overlapping range with the re-measured baseline. TPS
   doesn't move past the noise floor.
3. CPU pprof shows goopg at 0.17 % CPU during the run.
   The server is essentially idle; the bottleneck is per-
   commit WAL fsync (~19,600 walwriter flushes per 60 s
   matches the query rate). Allocation reductions can't
   help when CPU isn't the constraint.
4. The targeted alloc sites (SlotFromRow, PageGetHeapTuple,
   ParseHeapTuple, protocol cells/payload, 14
   LookupGoroutine I/O hooks) are gone from the steady-
   state top-23 alloc list. The reductions DID land — they
   just don't surface in pgbench-S TPS because pgbench-S is
   fsync-bound, not CPU-bound.

Filed for M0093 (highest leverage per this measurement):
skip WAL emission for read-only implicit transactions —
pgbench-S's implicit BEGIN/SELECT/COMMIT writes no data but
goopg currently emits a commit marker per query.

Also filed M0093 candidates: extended-protocol plan reuse
(the natural plan-cache scope per M0092-0008's analysis),
per-session GUC wiring for track_io_timing (process-wide
for now per M0092-0005's deferral).

Updated milestone doc with the honest outcome (M0092-0009
result section). Full analysis at
bench/pgbench-compare/results/20260511_goopg_select-only_m0092_followup_summary.md.

M0092-0009.

commits.title: fix(m0092-0005): gate client-driven I/O hooks behind track_io_timing
commits.description:
Fourteen wait-event hooks in initdb.Open (pool.OnPinWait/Done,
mgr.OnReadWait/Done, OnWriteWait/Done, OnExtendWait/Done,
OnSyncWait/Done, aioEngine.OnWaitStart/End) called
`activity.LookupGoroutine()` on every fire. Each call does
runtime.Stack to a 64 B buffer + a string allocation —
material overhead on the pgbench hot path, which Pins a heap
page and runs reads through the manager many times per query.

Mirror upstream PG: introduce a `track_io_timing` GUC (default
`off`). When false, the hooks are not installed at all — the
storage / pool / AIO layers' existing nil checks make them
zero-cost. When true, the existing LookupGoroutine path runs
and pg_stat_activity reports wait events.

Plumbing:

  - `config/defaults.go`: register `track_io_timing` (TypeBool,
    BootVal "off", ContextPostmaster, ScopeServer).
  - `cmd/goopg/main.go`: read it via boolGUC, pass to Open.
  - `initdb/OpenOptions`: new `TrackIOTiming bool` field.
  - `initdb/Open`: gate the 14 hook installations on the flag.

Default off matches PG; sessions that need wait-event telemetry
flip the GUC in postgresql.conf. Runtime SET is not yet wired
(M0093 candidate).

Tests: full suite passes (TestReplicationEndToEnd pre-existing
failure unrelated). The two test files that install
`pool.OnPinWait` directly (scan_ring_test, bm_io_in_progress_test)
bypass initdb.Open and are unaffected.

Refs design doc 0092-0005-lookup-goroutine-io-hooks-guc.md.
M0092-0005.

commits.title: fix(m0092-0006): ParseHeapTupleNoCopy + RLock-held-across-decode
commits.description:
indexScanOp.Next() previously released the page RLock and Unpinned
BEFORE DecodeRowInto, which forced PageGetHeapTuple to copy the
tuple bytes into a fresh slice (each tuple ~100 B; 2× copies via
PageGetHeapTuple → ParseHeapTuple). At 437 TPS that's ~90 KB/s of
allocation purely to bridge the post-Unpin decode window.

This commit:

  1. Adds `storage.PageGetHeapTupleNoCopy(p, slot)` and the
     `parseHeapTupleAlias` helper. The returned tuple's Data
     field ALIASES the page bytes — no copy. Caller MUST hold
     the page pin AND a content RLock for the tuple's lifetime.
     PageGetHeapTuple now uses parseHeapTupleAlias internally
     and copies once at the end (legacy callers untouched).
  2. Adds `executor.followHOTChainNoCopy` mirroring
     `followHOTChain` but on top of PageGetHeapTupleNoCopy.
  3. Re-orders indexScanOp.Next to hold the RLock across
     DecodeRowInto:

       slot.RLock()
       tuple, _, found := followHOTChainNoCopy(...)
       DecodeRowInto(scanRow, cols, tuple.Data)   // aliased
       slot.RUnlock()
       Pool.Unpin(slot)

     This blocks heap writers on the page for the duration of
     one tuple decode (~hundreds of ns for int rows, ~µs for
     wide rows). Same trade-off as M0091-0002's btree
     RangeScan; bounded write-starvation.

Tests: storage, executor, server, testport all pass.

Refs design doc 0092-0006-parseheaptuple-nocopy-aliasing.md.
M0092-0006.

commits.title: fix(m0092-0004): protocol DataRow allocation reduction
commits.description:
The simple-query result loop allocated ~87 B per emitted row
across 4 sites:

  - `cells := make([][]byte, ncols)`           24 B
  - `strconv.FormatInt(d.Int, 10)`             ~10 B (string)
  - `[]byte(d.Format())`                       ~24 B (slice)
  - `payload := make([]byte, 0, size)`         ~33 B

pgbench-style workloads (thousands of one-row SELECTs in
sequence on the same connection) paid this on every query.
This commit cuts those sites to O(1) per connection:

  1. New `Datum.AppendValueText(dst []byte) []byte` that
     emits the wire-text form directly into `dst`. KindInt
     uses `strconv.AppendInt`; KindString / KindBytes /
     arena variants append the underlying bytes; KindBool
     emits 't' / 'f'; KindTime uses `time.AppendFormat`.
     KindNumeric / KindInterval / unknown fall back to
     `Format()` (off the pgbench hot path).
  2. New `FrameWriter.WriteDataRowReuse(cells, scratch)`
     mirror of `WriteDataRow` that uses caller-provided
     scratch as the wire-frame payload; returns the
     (possibly grown) slice for reuse.
  3. New `FrameWriter.DataRowScratch / PutDataRowScratch`
     pair that stash three scratch buffers
     (`dataRowPayload`, `dataRowValues`, `dataRowCells`)
     on the FrameWriter itself so amortisation works
     across statements on the same connection — not just
     across rows within one statement.
  4. `executeOneSimpleStmt` switches to the scratch APIs.
  5. `executeExtendedQueryViaExecutor` switches to
     `AppendValueText(nil)` (one alloc per cell instead of
     two; the extended path still buffers per-row in
     `res.Rows` so the wire-frame pool doesn't fit).

Tests: protocol, server, executor, testport all pass.

Refs design doc 0092-0004-protocol-datarow-allocation-reduction.md.
M0092-0004.

commits.title: fix(m0092-0007): SlotFromRow stack-aliasing — &op.slot per Next
commits.description:
Per-Next() `&MaterializedSlot{}` allocations were ~32 B × 2-3 ops
per pgbench query = ~64-100 B / query before M0092-0007. At
437 TPS that's ~28-44 KB/s of slot-only allocation churn
keeping GC active during the simple-query hot path.

Each scan / project op now carries an embedded
`slot MaterializedSlot` field. Next() updates `slot.schema`
and `slot.row` then returns `&o.slot`. The pointer is stable
across calls; consumers that need to retain a slot past the
next Next() call invoke `slot.Materialize()` at the retention
boundary — the M0092-0002 slot-aliasing contract already
audited for projectOp now extends to leaf scan ops.

Ops migrated: indexScanOp, indexOnlyScanOp, seqScanOp,
projectOp. seqScanOp additionally drops the per-row
`cloneRow(row)` defensive copy — the embedded slot aliases
`scanRow` directly; retention boundaries (sortOp.Open,
windowOp.Open, lockRowsOp, executor.Run) Materialize.

All executor unit tests pass. TestReplicationEndToEnd
failure observed on this branch is pre-existing
(reproduces with these changes stashed) — unrelated WAL
LSN propagation issue in the replcluster test harness.

Refs design doc 0092-0007-slotfromrow-stack-aliasing.md.
M0092-0007.

commits.title: docs(m0092): design docs for the 5 follow-up sub-milestones
commits.description:
After the initial M0092 close-out showed that pgbench TPS
remained below M0091's 1,000 bar (510 → 437 TPS), the user
filed 5 follow-up sub-milestones targeting the broadly-
distributed allocation residuals:

- 0092-0004 protocol-datarow-allocation-reduction.md:
  hoist `cells` slice + pool WriteDataRow payload buffer +
  add `Datum.AppendValueText(dst)` for zero-string-alloc
  int formatting. ~87 B / row eliminated.
- 0092-0005 lookup-goroutine-io-hooks-guc.md: gate the 14
  client-driven I/O hooks in internal/initdb/open.go
  behind a `track_io_timing` GUC (default off, matching
  PG). When off, hooks are nil → zero runtime.Stack
  overhead.
- 0092-0006 parseheaptuple-nocopy-aliasing.md: add
  PageGetHeapTupleNoCopy mirroring the M0091-0002
  pattern. Re-order indexScanOp.Next to hold the heap-
  page RLock across DecodeRowInto so the alias is valid.
  ~tuple-size bytes / query eliminated.
- 0092-0007 slotfromrow-stack-aliasing.md: each leaf op
  embeds a `slot MaterializedSlot` field; Next() returns
  &o.slot instead of allocating fresh. 32 B / Next saved.
- 0092-0008 plan-cache-feasibility.md (DEFERRED, no code
  change): documents why a plan cache won't help
  pgbench-c10 (client-side literal substitution → 0 %
  cache hit on byte-for-byte key). Filed as a future-
  milestone candidate when extended-protocol prepared
  statements are wired.

Milestone doc updated with the new sub-milestones, the
acceptance target (TPS ≥ 700), and a section documenting
the GOGC=off / GOMEMLIMIT=12GiB experiment that did NOT
help (407 TPS < 437 baseline) so future investigators
don't redo it.

commits.title: bench(m0092-0003 + m0091-0005): pgbench close-out + baseline archived
commits.description:
Post-M0092 pgbench select-only re-measurement at scale 100,
-c 10 -j 10 -T 180:

  post-M0091 (commit 460809c): 510.52 TPS / 19.59 ms (best)
  post-M0092 (commit 8f32c07): 437.62 TPS / 22.85 ms (-14 %)

The M0092 structural changes (indexScanOp lazy iteration +
projectOp slot aliasing + Materialize-always-deep-copies +
NLI currentOuter deep-copy) are correct (all unit tests
pass, data integrity preserved) but did NOT deliver TPS
improvement for pgbench-c10. Post-fix alloc profile shows
rowPool.New STAYED at ~35 % of allocs: the cloneRow path
moved into slot.Materialize rather than being eliminated,
and the broadly-distributed residual (SlotFromRow,
ParseHeapTuple, PageGetHeapTuple, protocol cells slice) plus
80 % GC CPU share keeps each query slower.

M0091's TPS ≥ 1,000 bar remains unmet. Filed as M0093
candidate in the M0092 milestone doc:

  - Protocol-layer per-DataRow allocation (cells +
    []byte(d.Format())).
  - Plan cache for repeated SQL text.
  - Remaining 14 LookupGoroutine sites in initdb/open.go.
  - ParseHeapTuple aliasing via PageGetHeapTupleNoCopy.

The structural changes ARE real correctness / future-
workload improvements (wide TPC-H index scans get memory-
footprint reduction; slot contract tightened; NLI made
defensive against producer buffer reuse); they just don't
move pgbench-c10's needle.

M0091-0005 done: post-M0091 pprof profiles archived as the
baseline under pprof-data/baseline/select-only-c10/
(pprof-data is gitignored; README documents capture
conditions). Future regression checks can `go tool pprof
-base` against these.

commits.title: fix(m0092-0001): indexScanOp lazy iteration — TID-list-eager + heap-fetch-lazy
commits.description:
Replaces the eager `rows = append(rows, cloneRow(scanRow))` pattern
inside scanFn with a TID-only collection: scanFn appends each match's
(block, index-pointed offset) to o.tids; Next() pins the heap, follows
the HOT chain, decodes into the reusable scanRow, and returns a slot
ALIASING it.

The scanRow is acquired ONCE from the rowPool and reused across every
Next() call within an Open/Rescan lifecycle. No per-match cloneRow,
no per-match Row allocation. The slot contract is the same as
projectOp post-M0092-0002: "valid until the next Next() call;
consumers retain by calling Materialize()".

Removed fields:
  - `o.rows []Row` — no longer pre-materialised.
  - `o.arena *Arena` — single-row-in-flight has no batching benefit
    (the arena's per-page amortisation pattern is for multi-row
    decodes in seqScanOp, which keeps its arena). Decode falls back
    to `DecodeRowInto` (legacy `make([]byte)` per variable-length
    column).

Added fields:
  - `o.lastTID storage.ItemPointer` + `o.hasLast bool` — record the
    HOT-resolved actual slot for currentTID() (lockRowsOp consumer);
    populated by Next() during HOT-follow.

Locking + concurrency:
  - Per-Next pattern: Pool.Pin → slot.RLock → followHOTChain →
    slot.RUnlock → Pool.Unpin → DecodeRowInto. Same lock-acquisition
    order as the pre-fix scanFn; just moved from per-scanFn-invocation
    to per-Next.
  - tuple.Data returned by followHOTChain is a copy of the tuple
    bytes (per ParseHeapTuple), so DecodeRowInto post-RUnlock is
    safe.

Detoast:
  - DetoastRow runs per-Next when needsDetoast(scanRow) is true. Same
    as pre-fix (was per-scanFn) but invoked lazily. DetoastRow is
    idempotent and produces a fresh Row (not arena-backed), so it
    survives the next Next()'s scanRow overwrite if the caller
    Materializes.

Invisible-tuple skip:
  - followHOTChain returns found=false for HOT chains whose tail isn't
    visible to our snapshot. Pre-fix scanFn returned `(true, nil)`
    (continue iteration in btree). Post-fix Next() loops to the next
    TID — same semantics, just inside Next instead of inside scanFn.
  - Equivalent skip for DetoastRow errors (rare).

currentTID():
  - Returns o.lastTID with hasLast guard. Pre-fix used `o.tids[idx-1]`
    which stored the HOT-resolved offset captured during scanFn;
    post-fix the HOT-follow happens in Next() and records the result
    in lastTID. Same downstream behaviour for SELECT FOR UPDATE /
    FOR SHARE (lockRowsOp stamps the live version).

Tests:
  - All existing executor / btree / storage / server / initdb tests
    pass. The BenchmarkRangeScanPointLookup is unchanged (it exercises
    btree directly, not indexScanOp).

Expected impact: cloneRow eliminated from the indexScanOp hot path,
which was the second cloneRow site contributing to the 34 % rowPool.New
allocation share in the post-M0091 alloc profile. Combined with the
projectOp cloneRow removal in commit dc52f60, the rowPool should reach
steady-state warm — Open's acquireRow + Close's releaseRow pair
balances.

Design doc:
docs/design/0092-0001-indexscanop-lazy-iteration.md.

commits.title: fix(m0092-0002): drop projectOp cloneRow; Materialize always deep-copies
commits.description:
projectOp.Next now returns asSlot(o.schema, o.out) directly
without cloneRow. The slot aliases o.out, which is overwritten
on the next Next() call. Consumers that retain rows past next
Next() MUST call slot.Materialize() — the contract is unchanged,
but the no-op fast-path in Materialize had to go.

Updated Materialize to ALWAYS deep-copy the row slice (via
cloneRowOwned). Pre-fix, Materialize was a no-op when no
arena-backed Datums were present because every producer
(through cloneRow) already returned independent rows. Post-fix,
producers like projectOp may return slots aliasing internal
buffers, so the slice copy is mandatory.

Updated two tests that pinned the OLD contract:
  - TestM0069MaterializedSlot — was asserting Row()-after-
    Materialize aliases the original; now asserts content
    correctness (the slice address differs is the new
    contract).
  - TestM0073MaterializeNoArenaIsNoOp → renamed
    TestM0092MaterializeAlwaysDeepCopies — pins the new
    contract.

Consumer audit (per docs/design/0092-0002...md): all
production retainers (sortOp, windowOp, lockRowsOp, joinOp via
drainRowsCtx, aggregateOp via per-Datum extraction +
MaterializeArena, recursiveUnionOp via explicit copy) and the
Run() test helper already call Materialize. The one violator
(nestedLoopIndexJoinOp.currentOuter) got its independent-copy
fix in the prerequisite commit 5211387.

Expected impact: cloneRow eliminated from projectOp's hot path,
recovering the 34 % of allocs / 88 KB-per-query attributed to
rowPool.New in the post-M0091 alloc profile.

commits.title: fix(m0092 prereq): nestedLoopIndexJoinOp deep-copies outerRow into currentOuter
commits.description:
`operators_nljoin.go:211` stored `o.currentOuter = outerRow`
which aliases the upstream child's slot row. This works today
because every producer (projectOp via cloneRow, seqScanOp via
cloneRow on emit, etc.) returns rows that are independent of
internal buffers. But once M0092-0002 lands (drop projectOp's
cloneRow), the slot returned by projectOp.Next() aliases
o.out which the next Next() overwrites — corrupting
o.currentOuter mid-inner-loop.

Fix: deep-copy outerRow into o.currentOuter, reusing
capacity when sufficient (avoids per-outer allocation in the
steady state).

This is a strictly-safer change regardless of M0092-0002:
deep-copy is always correct, alias-only is correct only if
upstream guarantees no buffer reuse. Lands as its own commit
so M0092-0002 has a clean precondition.

Tests: executor test suite passes (no behaviour change in
the steady-state where upstream returns independent rows).

Design doc:
docs/design/0092-0002-projectop-slot-aliasing.md (audit
table identifies this as the only retention violator).

commits.title: docs(m0092): design docs for indexScanOp lazy + projectOp aliasing + rowPool decision
commits.description:
Three design docs authoritative for M0092 implementation:

- 0092-0001-indexscanop-lazy-iteration.md: replace eager
  cloneRow-into-o.rows with TID-list-eager + heap-fetch-lazy
  Next(). Drops the M0073 arena from indexScanOp (not useful
  with single-row-in-flight). Per-Next allocations drop from
  ~88 KB to under 1 KB for the pgbench select-only case.
- 0092-0002-projectop-slot-aliasing.md: drop the per-Next
  cloneRow in projectOp.Next, return slot aliasing o.out.
  Consumer audit table; identifies nestedLoopIndexJoinOp as
  the one violator that needs a prerequisite fix
  (deep-copy outerRow into o.currentOuter).
- 0092-0003-rowpool-warmup-or-removal.md: post-M0092
  decision — keep the pool unchanged. After cloneRow is no
  longer on the hot path, the remaining acquireRow callers
  follow correct release patterns.

commits.title: bench(m0091-0003): post-fix select-only re-measurement; file M0092 for residual
commits.description:
End-to-end pgbench re-measurement at scale 100, -c 10 -j 10
-T 180, -S after M0091-0001 (activity goroutineID closure-
capture) + M0091-0002 (btree.RangeScan zero-copy) landed:

  pre-fix:  350.89 TPS / 28.50 ms avg latency / 0 failed
  post-fix: 510.52 TPS / 19.59 ms avg latency / 0 failed
  → 1.45× improvement, ~30 % latency reduction

Below the M0091-0003 acceptance bar of TPS ≥ 1,000. M0091-0004
audit (post-fix pprof) identifies the new dominant bottleneck:

  executor.init.0.func1 (rowPool.New)  — 34.75 % of allocs
  executor.cloneRow → acquireRow path  — 2.6 GB / 60s

cloneRow fires at:
  - operators_index.go:285 (indexScanOp eagerly materialises
    o.rows via cloneRow per match)
  - operators.go:94 (projectOp.Next per emitted row)

The rowPool is effectively cold because cloned Rows are
NEVER returned to the pool (consumer retains TupleSlot
references past Close — a naïve release-on-Close was
attempted and broke vm_test.go:169).

Structural fix (lazy iteration in indexScanOp +
slot-aliasing in projectOp) is sizeable enough to warrant
its own milestone — filed as M0092
(docs/milestones/0092-lazy-row-emission-in-scan-and-project.md).

M0091 marked partial:
  M0091-0001 ✓  (commit 3bdc1ad)
  M0091-0002 ✓  (commit 460809c)
  M0091-0003 ✓  partial (this commit) — 1.45× TPS
  M0091-0004 ✓  audit complete; structural fix deferred to M0092
  M0091-0005    deferred (pin baseline after M0092)

Full close-out details in the milestone doc + summary file.

commits.title: fix(m0091-0002): btree.RangeScan zero-copy via parse-while-pinned
commits.description:
The pre-fix RangeScan copied EVERY leaf-page slot to a fresh
[]byte before releasing the pin so `fn` could re-enter the btree
without deadlocking. pprof of pgbench -S -c 10 showed this
allocating 173 MB / 30 s (rawSlots slice) + 126 MB / 30 s
(per-slot append([]byte(nil), r...)) + 104 MB / 30 s
(PageGetItemRaw's internal copy) — 13 % of total allocations
for a single hot site.

Caller audit (M0091 Explore agent): all 4 production
RangeScan callers (indexScanOp.Rescan, indexOnlyScanOp.Rescan,
upsertOp.probeArbiter, the non-HOT UPDATE index-probe) are
CAT-1 — they don't retain `key` past `fn`'s return and don't
re-enter THIS btree from `fn`. The copy-before-unpin pattern is
unnecessary.

Fix:
  - Rewrite RangeScan to parse + invoke `fn` while the pin is
    held. Pin released only after the leaf-page's last item
    has been fed to `fn` (or fn returned stop/error).
  - Add storage.PageGetItemRawNoCopy that aliases the page
    bytes (no allocation) — used by RangeScan only.
  - Add btree.parseItemNoCopy that aliases raw (no key copy)
    — used by RangeScan only.
  - Document the new CAT-1 caller contract in the RangeScan
    doc-comment.

Benchmark (BenchmarkRangeScanPointLookup, 10K-row pkey, point
lookups via RangeScan(k, k, fn)):
  pre-fix:  6,189 ns/op, 3,296 B/op, 275 allocs/op
  post-fix: 2,690 ns/op,   175 B/op,  15 allocs/op
→ 18× allocation reduction, 2.3× faster.

The remaining 15 allocs/op come from descendToLeaf + pinR
plumbing (smaller per-leaf wins, deferred).

The legacy `parseItem` (with key copy) and
`storage.PageGetItemRaw` (with allocation) remain for callers
that need to retain the key across page eviction — e.g., the
pageItems collector at btree.go:867 that returns an []item
for use after unpinR.

Design doc:
docs/design/0091-0002-btree-rangescan-allocation-reduction.md.

commits.title: fix(m0091-0001): closure-capture reg+pidStr in hot wait-event hooks
commits.description:
The 4 frame-reader/writer hooks in server.go::serveConn fire on
EVERY TCP read/write boundary (multiple per query). Each call
invoked activity.LookupGoroutine which internally does
runtime.Stack(buf, false) + a string allocation. pprof of
pgbench -S -c 10 showed activity.LookupGoroutine at ~11 % of
cumulative CPU.

Since `reg` and `pidStr` are already in scope in serveConn
(set at lines 556-578 — `reg = s.cfg.Activity` and `pidStr =
activity.PID(pid)`), the hooks can capture them via closure
directly. Zero-cost substitution; no plumbing.

Same pattern applied to the WAL writer's OnWALWrite +
OnWALSync/OnWALSyncDone hooks in initdb/open.go — those run
on the WAL writer goroutine which registered itself as
"wal-writer-0" at OnLoopStart, so we can use `act` + the
literal PID directly.

Client-driven Pool / Manager / AIO hooks (lines 478-895) are
left as-is for this commit. They fire on the CLIENT goroutine
and need its PID, which isn't lexically in scope at the hook-
definition site. Plumbing fix is deferred (out of M0091 scope;
filed in the M0091 milestone doc as a follow-up if post-fix
measurement shows residual activity-tracking overhead).
Spill-path hooks (executor/spill.go) are cold-path and left
as-is.

`activity.LookupGoroutine` continues to exist as the fallback

commits.title: fix(m0090-0002): detect concurrent UPDATE xmax-overwrite, fail with 40001
commits.description:
Two concurrent transactions both UPDATEing the same row via the HOT
path used to silently overwrite each other's xmax stamps. The
race:

  T1: Lock page. Pre-check OK. PageAddHeapTuple at S'.
      PageStampHotOldTuple writes xmax=T1.xid, CTID=(blk,S') on S.
      Unlock. Commit.
  T2: Lock page. Pre-check OK (slot S is STILL LP_NORMAL; the
      HOT-update changed the tuple header, not the line-pointer
      flags). PageAddHeapTuple at S''. PageStampHotOldTuple
      OVERWRITES xmax=T2.xid, CTID=(blk,S'') on S. Unlock. Commit.

End state: slot S has T2's xmax (T1's stamp lost). T1's new tuple
at S' has xmin=T1 (committed), xmax=Invalid → visible. T2's new
tuple at S'' has xmin=T2 (committed), xmax=Invalid → visible. One
logical row = two visible rows. The HOT chain from the index
pointer leads to S'' only, so S' is ORPHAN but still passes MVCC
visibility (xmin committed, xmax unset).

Over a 180s pgbench standard run at scale 100 (-c 100), the orphan
accumulation in `pgbench_branches` (and similarly `pgbench_tellers`)
drove the visible row count from 100 (expected) to 1,610 (observed)
— the M0090 Bug 2 symptom.

The earlier race-tolerance commits (18c60d9, 2c1e18e) only handled
the LP_NORMAL → LP_DEAD/LP_UNUSED transition. The HOT-update
xmax-overwrite happens entirely within LP_NORMAL, so neither commit
caught it.

Fix: under the page's exclusive Lock (after Pin + Lock + the
existing LP_NORMAL pre-check), call PageGetHeapTuple to re-read
the tuple header and detect whether ANOTHER transaction has
already stamped xmax / set HeapHotUpdated. If so, return SQLSTATE
40001 (serialization_failure). The check is added at all 4 sites
that stamp xmax:

  - tryApplyHOTUpdate (HOT path)
  - updateOp.updateViaIndex non-HOT branch
  - updateOp.Next seq-scan non-HOT branch
  - deleteOp.Next

A new helper `isConcurrentlyUpdated(h, myXID)` (`operators_storage.go`)
centralises the classification:
  - own xmax (xmax == myXID): not concurrent (re-update legal)
  - HeapHotUpdated bit set: concurrent
  - real xmax from another xact: concurrent
  - lock-only xmax (FOR UPDATE): not concurrent (no real delete)
  - HeapXmaxInvalid bit: not concurrent (hinted as no-deleter)

Trade-off (documented in
docs/design/0090-0002-update-concurrent-xmax-overwrite-fix.md):
under high contention, contended UPDATEs abort with 40001.
goopg has no EvalPlanQual to re-fetch + re-evaluate the predicate,
so failing is the correct alternative to silent MVCC corruption.

Tests (concurrent_update_xmax_test.go):
  - TestConcurrentHOTUpdateDetectsRace — T1 succeeds, T2 fails
    with 40001 (pre-fix both silently succeeded).
  - TestSelfUpdateInSameTxnNotBlocked — re-UPDATE within one
    transaction is allowed (xmax == myXID excluded).
  - TestIsConcurrentlyUpdatedHelper — unit table for the helper.

commits.title: fix(m0090-0001): TRUNCATE / DROP clear FSM + VM in-memory state
commits.description:
Previously, `execTruncate` invalidated buffer-pool slots and
truncated the on-disk relation file (nblocks → 0) but never
cleared the in-memory FSM / VM entries. The next INSERT
consulted `FSM.GetPageWithFreeSpace`, got a stale block number,
called `Pool.Pin → Manager.ReadBlock`, and errored with
`ErrShortRead` because the file was post-truncate empty.

Same gap in `execDropTable`.

`FSM.DropRelation` already existed with a doc-comment naming
TRUNCATE / DROP as expected callers, but no caller invoked it.
`VisibilityMap.DropRelation` similarly existed but went unused
from these paths. This commit wires both into `execTruncate`
and `execDropTable`.

The FSM/VM cleanup applies to the heap rel only; index
relfiles have their own block-tracking inside the btree and
don't use these maps.

Test: `internal/executor/operators_ddl_truncate_fsm_test.go`
asserts that after TRUNCATE the FSM no longer returns a block
for the relation, and that a subsequent INSERT succeeds (which
pre-fix would error with the short-read path).

Surfaced by the pgbench scale-100 reproduction in M0090 —
pgbench's pre-run TRUNCATE on `pgbench_history` left the FSM
holding stale entries from the init phase, which then routed
the first workload INSERT to a non-existent block.

commits.title: fix(m0089-0002): final checkpoint in Runtime.Close + file M0090
commits.description:
M0089-0002 (close-time durability boundary):
Inserts a synchronous `Checkpointer.CheckpointNow()` at the top
of `Runtime.Close` (internal/initdb/open.go). This closes the
window between the M0089-0003 OnStop checkpoint (which fires
while clients can still be inserting because `runCancel` is
async) and the eventual file-handle release.

Without this, the post-OnStop window allowed:
  - clients to PinNew → Extend new heap blocks (file grows
    synchronously on disk, but the in-memory dirty content is
    NOT yet flushed),
  - clients to commit (WAL durable, heap content not yet on
    disk),
  - `runCancel` to propagate and workers to exit,
  - server.Run to return → main.go's defer runs SaveCatalog /
    SaveVM / SaveFSM, capturing block references for content
    that hasn't been flushed,
  - rt.Close → Pool.FlushAll pwrites the dirty slots BUT does
    NOT fsync (M0089-0001's SyncAll is wired into the
    checkpointer, not into Pool.Close).

The Close-top CheckpointNow does flushDirty + SyncAll + WAL
flush by the time it returns, so file handles released in the
subsequent Close steps are durable on disk.

Unit test:
  internal/initdb/close_checkpoint_test.go ::
    TestRuntimeCloseTriggersFinalCheckpoint
A btree entry inserted into a fresh Runtime survives Close +
reopen with no explicit checkpoint from the caller.

The scale-100 pgbench symptom that originally drove M0089
PERSISTS after this fix. Post-investigation it is caused by
two SEPARATE bugs not within M0089's durability theme:
  1. pgbench_history INSERTs at scale 100 never reach the heap
     file (works at scale 5/10).
  2. UPDATE leaves duplicate visible rows in
     pgbench_branches / pgbench_tellers (xmax not properly
     stamped, likely the 18c60d9 race-skip policy being too
     permissive on the UPDATE side).
Both are now filed under M0090
(docs/milestones/0090-pgbench-scale-100-mvcc-and-insert-bugs.md)
with concrete investigation candidates.

M0089 is closed as accepted: all three durability boundaries
landed and unit-pinned. The remaining pgbench symptom is M0090.

commits.title: fix(m0088 + m0089): segmentSize fallback + data-file fsync + shutdown checkpoint
commits.description:
Three coordinated durability fixes surfaced by the pgbench measurement:

**M0088-0001 (reader.go)** — preserve the pre-existing positional
segmentSize fallback as an OR-condition with the new zero-tail
check. A pre-existing test (TestRestartAfterRetention) relied on
the loose "anything within the last segmentSize" graceful-EOS
behaviour for a post-retention cross-segment edge case. Both
heuristics now apply; either signal triggers graceful EOS:
  (a) post-record bytes are all zero (the torn-tail signal from
      a non-clean shutdown — primary M0088 target), OR
  (b) corrupt offset is within one segment-size of EOF (the
      existing tolerance for retention / cross-segment cases).
Update TestReadAllPropagatesRealMidStreamCorruption to use a
4-segment stream so the corrupt-mid-stream case is genuinely far
from EOF and exercises real-corruption detection.

**M0089-0001 (smgr.go, bufpool.go, checkpointer.go)** — add
`Manager.SyncAll` that fdatasyncs every open data file. Expose via
`Pool.SyncAllDataFiles` and the new `dataFileSyncer` interface;
wire `Checkpointer.runCheckpoint` to call it AFTER `FlushAllPaced`
completes. Without this, the previous behaviour was: checkpoint
pwrote dirty pages (in OS page cache only), then advanced the WAL
redo pointer — leaving a window where a host crash could rewind
data files even though WAL replay would believe those records
applied.

**M0089-0003 (server.go)** — `OnStop` now triggers an implicit
shutdown checkpoint via `Checkpointer.CheckpointNow()` before
calling `runCancel()`. Users no longer need to chain
`goopg checkpoint && goopg stop` to preserve writes; the single
`goopg stop` call now flushes + fsyncs everything. Failures
during the implicit checkpoint are logged but don't block
shutdown — the next start either replays cleanly or, if killed
mid-checkpoint, recovers via the M0088 torn-tail tolerance.

**M0089-0002** — dirty-tracking audit on `Pool.PinNew` / `Extend`
is deferred to a follow-up; the audit findings will be captured in
`docs/design/0089-0002-buffer-pool-dirty-tracking-on-extend.md`
when the milestone is picked up. The two fixes here close the
fsync + shutdown-checkpoint gaps surfaced empirically; the dirty-
tracking audit is the remaining piece if the pgbench re-run still
shows 0-byte heaps after a restart.

Tests pass: internal/wal/, internal/storage/, internal/server/,
internal/initdb/.

commits.title: fix(m0088-0001): WAL torn-tail recovery via post-record zero-tail check
commits.description:
Previously the WAL replay loop in `internal/wal/reader.go` treated
any `ErrCorruptRecord` as fatal once the corrupt offset was more
than one segment-size from EOF. This made any non-clean shutdown
that left a torn record outside the final 16 MiB unrecoverable —
the goopg pgbench workload reproduced this consistently because
its WAL ran ~1.3 GB and any SIGKILL anywhere but the very tail
yielded the fatal-startup pattern.

Replace the positional `len(stream)-off <= segmentSize` heuristic
with a torn-tail content check: when `decodeRecord` /
`decodeRecordXLog` returns a corrupt-record error, compute the
record's claimed end (header + payloadLen) and scan from there to
EOF. If every byte is zero, this is a torn write — the WAL
writer was killed mid-record and the preallocated zero-fill tail
extends to EOF. Treat as end-of-WAL and stop replay.

Mid-WAL real corruption (CRC mismatch followed by a valid next
record's non-zero bytes) still surfaces as an error, preserving
the on-disk-corruption signal.

The conservative edge case — a real bit-flip in the very last
record of an otherwise clean WAL — is silently treated as torn,
but this matches PostgreSQL's recovery semantics: the corrupt
tail is unrecoverable in either reading.

Both the legacy `decodeRecord` path and the page-aware
`decodeRecordXLog` path get the same treatment, with the
page-aware case using `off + consumed` (which includes intra-
record page-header bytes) for the tail-start computation.

Tests (`internal/wal/reader_torn_tail_test.go`):
  - TestReadAllStopsAtTornTailWithinLastSegment — regression
    guard for the pre-fix happy path.
  - TestReadAllStopsAtTornTailEarlySegment — the pgbench failure
    mode: corrupt record > 1 segmentSize from EOF, followed by
    multiple zero segments. Pre-fix this errored fatally; post-
    fix it succeeds with the records before the kill point.
  - TestReadAllPropagatesRealMidStreamCorruption — pins that
    real mid-stream corruption (non-zero bytes follow the
    corrupt record) still errors.
  - TestIsPreallocatedTail — direct unit-test of the helper's
    chunked zero-comparison.

All existing WAL tests continue to pass.

commits.title: fix(executor): tolerate post-prune race in tryApplyHOTUpdate stamp
commits.description:
When PageAddHeapTuple returned ErrNoSpaceInPage, tryApplyHOTUpdate
called PagePruneOpt to reclaim space and retried the insert. The
prune can mark the HOT old-image slot itself (or any other dead
tuple sharing the page) as LP_DEAD/LP_UNUSED in a tight window
between our pre-check (added in the prior commit) and the
subsequent PageStampHotOldTuple call. The stamp then failed with
ErrUnsupportedItem and the transaction aborted.

Tolerate that error by returning (false, nil) — the same
fall-through as the page-full case — so the caller's non-HOT path
(itself race-tolerant) either re-applies or skips the row.

Surfaced by repeated pgbench standard runs at -c 100; rate is
~1 abort per ~12k transactions (~0.008%) so this race is rare but
real.

commits.title: fix(executor): tolerate concurrent line-pointer state changes during UPDATE/DELETE
commits.description:
Concurrent UPDATE pressure (pgbench standard, -c 100) was aborting
clients with `ERROR:  storage: unsupported line pointer state:
slot=N flags=0`. The race:

  T1 SeqScan/IndexScan reads slot=N as LP_NORMAL under page RLock
  T1 releases RLock; T1 appends pendingUpdate{blk, slot=N, newRow}
  T2 concurrent UPDATE/DELETE on same row commits + opportunistic
     prune (or background HOT prune) flips slot=N to LP_DEAD/LP_UNUSED
  T1 re-pins page, calls PageSetHeapTupleXmax(page, N) → fails with
     ErrUnsupportedItem because flags != LP_NORMAL

Three modify-phase call sites had the same bug:
  - updateOp.updateViaIndex (index-driven UPDATE)
  - updateOp.Next          (seq-scan-driven UPDATE)
  - deleteOp.Next          (seq-scan-driven DELETE)
Each now catches ErrUnsupportedItem after PageSetHeapTupleXmax,
unpins the page, and `continue`s to the next pending row. goopg
lacks PostgreSQL's EvalPlanQual machinery, so the row is silently
dropped from the row-count rather than re-fetched + re-evaluated;
this is consistent with the "best-effort concurrent UPDATE" v0
semantics elsewhere (e.g. upsertOp.probeArbiter at l.234 already
tolerates the same error).

Also pre-check the old slot's LP flags inside tryApplyHOTUpdate
before calling PageAddHeapTuple, so a lost race does not leave an
orphan tuple body on the page: the function now returns
(false, nil) — same fall-through as the page-full case — and the
caller's non-HOT branch (now race-tolerant too) skips the row.

Surfaced by running the bench/pgbench-compare standard workload
(100 clients, 100 threads, 180s, scale 100) against a current
goopg binary. The 0.86 TPS pre-M0079 baseline is no longer the
limit; pre-fix the run held ~70 TPS but every aborted client lost
its tail of the workload.

commits.description:
Closes the two ❌ entries in the persistence audit
(`docs/design/0080-0002-remaining-pg-parity-records.md` §2):
goopg's in-memory `VisibilityMap` and `FSM` are now saved to
`<DataDir>/global/pg_vm_state.bin` and `pg_fsm_state.bin`
respectively on graceful shutdown, and loaded on startup.

PG's pg_visibility / pg_freespace fork files are per-relation;
goopg uses a single global blob per type for simplicity. Format
matches the M0079-0001 catalog-snapshot pattern:

  magic(4) | version(4) | numRels(4) |
  [ DBOid(4) | RelOid(4) | nBlocks(4) | body(... )*]

VM body: 1 byte per heap page (ALL_VISIBLE bit).
FSM body: 2 bytes per heap page (free-space estimate uint16).

Both writers go through `os.CreateTemp + Sync + Rename` so a
crash between `Save` and `Rename` leaves the previous snapshot
intact (same discipline as `internal/wal/slots.go` and
`Runtime.SaveCatalog`). Deterministic ordering (sort by
(DBOid, RelOid)) so two saves of the same state produce
byte-identical files.

Runtime wiring:

- `internal/initdb/open.go::Open` calls `rt.VM.Load(...)` and
  `rt.FSM.Load(...)` after constructing the VM / FSM. Missing
  file → fresh-cluster no-op. Corrupt file → hard startup
  failure (running with stale FSM bits would misdirect
  INSERTs).
- `Runtime.SaveVM()` / `Runtime.SaveFSM()` thin wrappers
  invoke the underlying Save with the canonical path.
- `cmd/goopg/main.go` defer alongside SaveCatalog: each
  failure logs a warning and proceeds — losing VM/FSM
  state only degrades performance (next VACUUM rebuilds VM
  bits; FSM is rebuilt opportunistically on insert-miss).

Tests:
- `internal/storage/vm_persistence_test.go`:
  `TestVisibilityMapSaveLoadRoundTrip` (3 blocks across 2
  rels), `TestVisibilityMapLoadMissingFileIsNoOp`,
  `TestVisibilityMapLoadRejectsBadMagic`,
  `TestVisibilityMapSaveDeterministicOrdering`.
- `internal/storage/fsm_persistence_test.go`:
  symmetric coverage.

After this commit goopg has parity with every PostgreSQL
persistent metadata surface the audit identified (clog,
catalog, WAL, replication slots, heap/index relfiles, VM,
FSM, subxact-via-WAL-replay). The remaining N/A entries
(`pg_multixact`, `pg_twophase`, `pg_commit_ts`) correspond to
features goopg has not yet implemented at the executor level.

commits.title: feat(m0080-0002): infra for HeapUpdate / MultiInsert / HeapVisible / BtreeReusePage / BtreeMetaCleanup WAL records
commits.description:
Adds the encode / decode / replay (or no-op routing) for the
remaining PostgreSQL btree + heap WAL record kinds that goopg
hadn't yet implemented:

| goopg kind                            | PG counterpart            |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| RecordKindHeapUpdate (27)             | XLOG_HEAP_UPDATE          |
| RecordKindHeapMultiInsert (28)        | XLOG_HEAP2_MULTI_INSERT   |
| RecordKindHeapVisible (29)            | XLOG_HEAP2_VISIBLE        |
| RecordKindBtreeReusePage (30)         | XLOG_BTREE_REUSE_PAGE     |
| RecordKindBtreeMetaCleanup (31)       | XLOG_BTREE_META_CLEANUP   |

`HeapUpdate` and `HeapMultiInsert` get full producer-driven
replay (read page → apply mutation → set pd_lsn → write back,
each half independently idempotent). The other three are
catalog / metadata-only and replay as no-ops in goopg's current
design — they are recognised by `ApplyRecord` so a future slice
can plug in producers (or hot-standby reads) without bumping
WAL format version.

Wire format documented inline at the constant declarations and
in `docs/design/0080-0002-remaining-pg-parity-records.md`. Tests
in `internal/wal/m0080_records_test.go` pin every new record's
round-trip + length guards + the kind-byte assignment table.

The design doc also closes the persistence-audit task: clog,
catalog, WAL, replication slots, heap/index relfiles, and
subxact (WAL-rebuilt) are all confirmed persistent. Two real
gaps remain: in-memory `VisibilityMap` and `FSM` are lost
across restart. Both have a functional fallback (VACUUM rebuilds
VM bits via `PageAllVisible`; FSM is rebuilt opportunistically
on insert-miss) so correctness survives — only the optimisation
metadata is lost. Persistent VM / FSM forks are tracked for
M0080-0003c / M0080-0004a in §4.3-4.4 of the design doc, along
with the deferred producer wiring for atomic UPDATE,
MULTI_INSERT, BTREE_REUSE_PAGE, and BTREE_META_CLEANUP.

commits.title: feat(m0079-0004 + m0080-0001): NewRoot producer wiring + RecordKindHeapFreeze
commits.description:
M0079-0004: btree NewRoot producer wiring
========================================

Wires `LogBtreeNewRoot` (M0079-0003 infra) into the two
producer sites that were still using FPI fallback:

* `createNewRoot` in btree.go (post-split bubbled root): when
  the hook is wired, emits ONE NewRoot record covering the new
  root page's two-item content + the metapage update. Both
  pages stamp the record's end LSN as pd_lsn via
  `MarkDirtyWithLSNLocked`.
* `resetToEmptyRoot` in btree_vacuum.go (post-full-vacuum
  empty reset): ditto, with `items=nil` indicating the
  reset-to-empty case.

A new `updateRootMetaWithLSN` helper threads the WAL record's
LSN to the metapage's pd_lsn so per-page replay idempotency
remains intact. The legacy FPI path (`updateRootMeta` +
`markDirtyWithPageRecord`) is preserved as the fallback for
test harnesses without a WAL writer.

This closes the last 0079-0002 §2 audit gap that had a real
producer site; `MarkPageHalfDead` infrastructure stays in place
for future use (no current producer outside the BtreeVacuum
flag-trailer path).

M0080-0001: RecordKindHeapFreeze
================================

Adds `RecordKindHeapFreeze` (26) to close the heap-side WAL
parity gap surfaced by an audit of remaining FPI fallback paths.
PostgreSQL has `XLOG_HEAP2_FREEZE_PAGE` (and the freeze portion
of `XLOG_HEAP2_PRUNE_VACUUM_SCAN` in PG17+); goopg's
`PageFreezeOldTuples` was emitting a "conservative FPI" comment
in `vacuum.go:157` — 8 KiB per frozen page vs. ~16-200 byte
logical record.

Wiring (mirrors M0079-0002 / M0080-0001 design doc):

- `wal/recovery.go`: `RecordKindHeapFreeze` (26) +
  `EncodeHeapFreeze` / `DecodeHeapFreeze` + `replayHeapFreeze`
  (calls `storage.PageFreezeBySlots` after pd_lsn check).
- `storage/freeze.go`: extends `PageFreezeStats` with
  `FrozenSlots []uint16` (1-based slot list of frozen tuples).
  Adds `PageFreezeBySlots` deterministic replay kernel —
  symmetric to `VacuumHeapPageBySlots`.
- `storage/bufpool.go`: `LogHeapFreezeFunc` +
  `Pool.LogHeapFreeze()` accessor + PoolConfig.LogHeapFreeze.
- `initdb/open.go`: wires `logHeapFreeze` to
  `walWriter.Append(wal.EncodeHeapFreeze(...))`.
- `vacuum/vacuum.go`: when the hook is wired, the freeze pass
  emits a logical record carrying `fs.FrozenSlots` instead of
  `MarkDirty(slot)`. Falls back to FPI when nil.

Tests:
- `internal/wal/heap_freeze_test.go`: encode/decode round-trip,
  truncated-payload + wrong-kind guards, kind-byte assignment.
- `internal/storage/freeze_replay_test.go`:
  `TestPageFreezeBySlotsReplaysFreezeMutations` (slots {2,4} of
  a 5-tuple page; assert exactly those xmins are frozen),
  `TestPageFreezeBySlotsRejectsOutOfRange` (defensive),
  `TestPageFreezeBySlotsEmptyListIsNoOp` (fast path),
  `TestPageFreezeOldTuplesReportsFrozenSlots` (producer-side
  contract).

Audit summary in `docs/design/0080-0001-heap-freeze-and-multi-insert-wal.md`
shows that with this slice, every PostgreSQL XLOG_HEAP / HEAP2
record has either a goopg counterpart or is N/A in goopg's
current scope. Remaining optimization-only gaps (atomic non-HOT
UPDATE, MULTI_INSERT, persistent VM-VISIBLE WAL) are tracked
for M0080-0002+.

commits.title: feat(m0079-0003): btree page-deletion + new-root logical WAL records
commits.description:
Adds three more PostgreSQL-aligned logical WAL records, closing
the remaining FPI fallback gaps on btree page deletion + root
replacement (per audit table in 0079-0002 §2):

* `RecordKindBtreeUnlinkPage` (23) — counterpart to
  PostgreSQL's `XLOG_BTREE_UNLINK_PAGE`. ONE atomic record
  covering the four page mutations of `unlinkEmptyLeaf`:
  left sibling Next, right sibling Prev, leaf opaque flags,
  and parent downlink removal. Each of the four pages has
  its own pd_lsn idempotency check during replay so a
  partial replay can resume cleanly. Replaces ~32 KiB of
  FPIs (4 × 8 KiB) per page deletion with a 41-byte logical
  record.

* `RecordKindBtreeNewRoot` (24) — counterpart to
  `XLOG_BTREE_NEWROOT`. Carries the new root's items + level
  + the metapage update implied. Replay reconstructs the root
  page from scratch and points the metapage at it. Used by
  `updateRootMeta` (split-bubbled new root) and
  `resetToEmptyRoot` (full-vacuum-empty reset). Format
  shipped + replay implemented; producer wiring (replacing
  the existing `markDirtyWithPageRecord` calls) deferred to
  M0079-0004 to keep the diff scoped.

* `RecordKindBtreeMarkPageHalfDead` (25) — counterpart to
  `XLOG_BTREE_MARK_PAGE_HALFDEAD`. Standalone leaf-only
  flags transition for the rare case where a leaf is already
  empty before a vacuum's dead-set scan. Most half-dead
  transitions are bundled into `BtreeVacuum`'s OpaqueFlags
  trailer (M0079-0002); this record covers the residual
  path. Format + replay shipped; producer wiring is
  M0079-0004 follow-up.

Wiring (mirrors M0079-0002):

- `wal/recovery.go`: 3 record kinds + payload structs +
  encode/decode + per-page replay (with pd_lsn idempotency
  check on each of the four pages for `UnlinkPage`).
- `access/btree/replay.go`: `ReplaySetSiblingNext`,
  `ReplaySetSiblingPrev`, `ReplaySetOpaqueFlags`,
  `ReplayRemoveParentDownlink`, `ReplayNewRootPage`,
  `ReplayMetaSetRoot` exported helpers.
- `storage/bufpool.go`: `LogBtreeUnlinkPage`,
  `LogBtreeNewRoot`, `LogBtreeMarkPageHalfDead` hooks +
  `BtreeUnlinkPageRequest` struct.
- `initdb/open.go`: wires all three hooks to
  `walWriter.Append(wal.Encode...)`.
- `access/btree/btree_vacuum.go`: refactored
  `unlinkEmptyLeaf` to gather the 4 mutation parameters
  upfront (parent downlink slot via
  `findDownlinkSlotInParent`, post-unlink leaf flags via
  `readLeafFlagsAfterUnlink`), emit one
  `RecordKindBtreeUnlinkPage`, then apply each mutation
  with `MarkDirtyWithLSNLocked(slot, recordLSN)`. The
  legacy per-page FPI path is preserved as
  `unlinkEmptyLeafFPI` for test harnesses without the
  hook wired.

Tests:
- `internal/wal/btree_pagedel_test.go`: encode/decode round-trip
  for all three record kinds (covering middle-of-chain,
  leftmost, single-page-tree, split-bubbled, reset-empty
  cases); truncated-payload and wrong-kind guards;
  kind-byte assignment.
- `internal/access/btree/btree_vacuum_wal_test.go`:
  `TestVacuumIndexPagesEmitsUnlinkRecord` (capture hook;
  assert post-unlink flag transitions and leaf identity).

Design: `docs/design/0079-0003-btree-page-deletion-and-root-wal.md`.
References PostgreSQL `xl_btree_unlink_page` /
`xl_btree_newroot` / `xl_btree_mark_page_halfdead` from
src/include/access/nbtxlog.h. The remaining unmigrated FPI
paths (`updateRootMeta`'s producer site, `resetToEmptyRoot`,
`clearHalfDead`, `BtreeReusePage` for FSM-backed page
recycling) are tracked for M0079-0004+.

commits.title: feat(m0079-0002): RecordKindBtreeVacuum — logical kept-items WAL for btree VACUUM
commits.description:
Replaces the FPI fallback in `btree.VacuumIndexPages` with a logical
WAL record that mirrors PostgreSQL's `XLOG_BTREE_VACUUM`. Pre-fix,
every pruned leaf page emitted an 8 KiB full-page image via
`markDirtyWithPageRecord` → `LogPageImage`. Post-fix, the record
carries the post-vacuum kept-items projection (each item as raw
`keyLen | ptr.block | ptr.offset | key` bytes — the same blob
`pageAddItemRaw` writes) plus the post-vacuum opaque flags. WAL
volume drops to ~item-bytes per leaf instead of ~8 KiB —
typically 50-90 % smaller.

Why kept-items vs PostgreSQL's removed-slot list: goopg's
VacuumIndexPages explodes posting-list line pointers into
individual (key, TID) items. A slot-list-only payload would force
replay to re-run that posting-list expansion, coupling WAL replay
to a goopg-specific page-layout transformation. Kept-items as raw
bytes makes the replay layout-stable regardless of how the
pre-vacuum page packed its line pointers.

Wiring (mirrors existing LogHeapVacuum):

- `wal/recovery.go`: `RecordKindBtreeVacuum` (22), `BtreeVacuumPayload`,
  `EncodeBtreeVacuum / DecodeBtreeVacuum`, `replayBtreeVacuum` (calls
  into `btree.ReplayVacuumPage` after pd_lsn idempotency check).
- `access/btree/replay.go` (NEW): `ReplayVacuumPage` exported helper —
  resets line pointers + data area, re-adds each kept item via
  `storage.PageAddItemRaw`, overwrites opaque flags.
- `storage/bufpool.go`: `LogBtreeVacuum` hook in PoolConfig + Pool
  accessor; mirrors LogHeapVacuum.
- `initdb/open.go`: wires `logBtreeVacuum := func(...) (LSN, error)`
  to `walWriter.Append(wal.EncodeBtreeVacuum(...))`.
- `access/btree/btree_vacuum.go`: VacuumIndexPages emits the new
  record when the hook is wired; falls back to the prior FPI path
  via `markDirtyWithPageRecord` when nil (test harnesses without a
  WAL writer).

Tests:
- `internal/wal/btree_vacuum_test.go`: encode/decode round-trip
  (empty-kept / multi-kept / max-flags), truncated-payload rejection,
  wrong-kind guard, kind-byte routing.
- `internal/access/btree/btree_vacuum_wal_test.go`:
  `TestVacuumIndexPagesEmitsLogicalRecord` (capture hook, assert
  emissions per pruned leaf with consistent kept items + flags),
  `TestVacuumIndexPagesFallsBackToFPIWhenHookNil` (backwards-compat).

Design: `docs/design/0079-0002-btree-record-wal-parity.md`. Audit
table in §2 catalogues every btree page-mutation site against
PostgreSQL's XLOG_BTREE_*; this slice converts the highest-volume
one (vacuum kept-items rewrite). The remaining FPI fallback paths
(BtreeUnlinkPage, BtreeNewRoot, BtreeMarkPageHalfDead,
BtreeReusePage) are tracked for M0079-0003+ as discrete slices.

commits.title: feat(m0079-0001): catalog-only DDL WAL records for CREATE/DROP INDEX recovery
commits.description:
Surfacing case: pgbench standard workload (100c/100t/180s, scale=100)
collapsed from ~60 TPS pre-M0077 to **0.86 TPS** after a non-graceful
restart. Goroutine profiles showed all 100 connections blocked in
buffer-pool mutex acquisition while EXPLAIN reported `Seq Scan on
pgbench_accounts` (10M rows) for `WHERE aid = :aid` — the planner
had lost `pgbench_accounts_pkey` from the catalog.

Root cause:

1. `Runtime.SaveCatalog()` is called only from a single defer in
   `cmd/goopg/main.go:331`. SIGKILL / OOM / panic bypasses it, so any
   DDL since the last graceful shutdown is lost from the JSON catalog
   snapshot.
2. `loadUserTablesFromHeap` recovers TABLES from `pg_class` but skips
   `relkind='i'` entries.
3. goopg has no `pg_index` heap relation — `syncIndexToCatalogHeap`
   writes only OID + name + relkind to `pg_class`. The column list,
   unique flag, primary flag, and owning-table OID would be lost
   even if a reader scanned `pg_class` for indexes.

Fix (mirrors `RecordKindCreateDatabase` / `RecordKindDropDatabase`
pattern from M0054-0001):

- New WAL records `RecordKindCreateIndex` (20) and
  `RecordKindDropIndex` (21) carry full Index metadata. Physical
  replay treats them as no-ops (the relfile + btree pages are
  restored by existing record kinds); a new `replayIndexDDLRecords`
  driver in `internal/initdb` walks the WAL after physical recovery
  and re-registers each index in the in-memory catalog.

- `catalog.InMemory.RegisterIndexDuringRecovery /
  UnregisterIndexDuringRecovery` mirror the existing
  `RegisterDatabaseDuringRecovery` shape: idempotent, OID-preserving,
  nextOID-advancing.

- Generic `Pool.LogChangeRecord(payload []byte)` hook lets the
  executor's CREATE/DROP INDEX paths emit pre-encoded WAL records
  without an executor → wal direct dependency. Wired in
  `internal/initdb/open.go::Open` to call `walWriter.Append`.

- `execCreateIndex` / `execDropIndex` emit
  `wal.EncodeCreateIndex(...)` / `wal.EncodeDropIndex(...)` after the
  catalog mutation. CREATE failure rolls back the catalog mutation
  AND the on-disk relfile so memory and durable state agree.

Tests:
- `internal/wal/index_ddl_test.go`: encode/decode round-trip,
  truncated-payload rejection, wrong-kind guard, ApplyRecord no-op.
- `internal/initdb/index_ddl_recovery_test.go`:
  `TestCreateIndexSurvivesRestartViaWAL` (delete JSON snapshot, reopen,
  index is back); `TestDropIndexSurvivesRestartViaWAL` (DROP
  suppresses resurrection); `TestCreateIndexRecoveredOIDDoesNotCollide`
  (post-recovery allocations don't reuse a recovered OID).

Index RECORD-level WAL coverage (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the heap
that maintain btree entries) is already correct via the pre-existing
`RecordKindBtreeInsert` / `RecordKindBtreeSplit` / FPI-via-VACUUM
records — design doc §2 audits that surface and confirms no gaps.

Design doc: `docs/design/0079-0001-index-ddl-wal-recovery.md`.
