commits.title: feat(m0077-0004): Slice D — anchored equality synthesis (Q5 26s)
commits.description:
Adds `inferAnchoredEqualities` per design 02 §5: a selective
alternative to `inferTransitiveEqualities` that synthesises
edges only FROM anchor relations TO non-anchor relations within
each equivalence class.

A relation is an anchor when at least one of:
  1. SmallDimension catalog flag (region / nation in TPC-H);
  2. local filter halved the relation
     (filteredRows*2 ≤ baseRows);
  3. filteredRows ≤ smallAnchorRowsThreshold (1024).

Skip rules:
  - non-anchor → non-anchor edges are never synthesised
    (this is the structural rule that excludes M0075-0001 /
    M0076-0001's Q9 hang mode);
  - duplicates are not re-emitted;
  - at most one synthesised edge per (target, class).

cardinality.go: `baseRelInfo.sourceIdx` mirrors
`rangeBinding.sourceIdx` so anchored synthesis can map a
`ColumnRef.SourceTableIdx` back to its baseRelInfo for
anchor-ness lookup.

bushy.go::tryBushyDP: call `inferAnchoredEqualities` after
Slice B's relInfos are built; append the synthesised
conjuncts to dpConjuncts and pass `inferredCount =
len(synthesised)` into `buildJoinGraph` so M0076-0004's
`inferredEdgePenalty` keeps them as a tiebreaker against
explicit equivalents.

Acceptance (live SF=1 focused gate `--queries=3,5,8,9,12,13,21,22`):

  Q3=11462 (35s, flat), Q5=5 (26s — 12x faster than Slice C's
  313s, well below the 60s best-effort target), Q8=2 (149s,
  flat vs Slice C), Q9=175 (80s — canonical SF=1 row count
  preserved; the anchor rule structurally excluded the Q9
  regression mode), Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381, Q22=7.

Plan-diff vs m0076-baseline-ffc3429 — "should stay identical"
set (Q1,Q4,Q6,Q14,Q16,Q17,Q19,Q20,Q22): all MATCH. Q5's plan
now reaches the design's tmp/q5-plan-analysis.md §2 target
shape: Filter(region) and Filter(orders) at leaves; customer
joins to nation via the anchored edge; lineitem joined LAST as
probe; NO 6-table MultiHashJoin.

commits.title: feat(m0077-0003): Slice C — build-side-aware 3-part hash-join cost (Q5 unlock)
commits.description:
Replaces the single-output cost formula in `estimateJoinCost`
with the design 02 §3 3-part hash-join cost:

  cost = outputRows*1 + buildRows*4 + probeRows*1

where buildRows = min(L,R) and probeRows = max(L,R), so the cost
side stays in lock-step with `buildJoinFromDP`'s physical
build-side decision (design 02 §4). The build term's heavier
weight makes plans whose hash inputs are small (filtered
region/nation, customer) visibly cheaper than plans that build
on a large unfiltered fact (lineitem/orders).

`estimateJoinCost` now returns (outputRows, cost). The DP
compose loop stores outputRows in `dpEntry.rows` (so deeper
levels see this subset's cardinality estimate, not its cost),
and cost in `dpEntry.cost` (still the DP minimisation key).
M0076-0004's `inferredEdgePenalty` continues to multiply the
final 3-part cost when the edge is synthesised.

Acceptance (live SF=1 focused gate `--queries=3,5,8,9,12,13,21,22`):

  Q3=11462 (36s, flat), Q5=5 (313s — UNLOCKED, was cancel @600s),
  Q8=2 (147s, 2.8x faster than Slice A), Q9=175 (82s — canonical
  SF=1 row count, was 7-row mode-1 baseline), Q12=2 (91s, flat),
  Q13=35 (61s, flat), Q21=381 (377s, flat), Q22=7 (59s, flat).

Plan-diff vs m0076-baseline-ffc3429 — "should stay identical"
set (Q1,Q4,Q6,Q14,Q16,Q17,Q19,Q20,Q22): all MATCH. Same DIFFER
footprint as Slice A/B (Q2,Q5,Q7,Q8,Q9).

Q5's Slice C plan reaches the design's binary hash-join family:
filtered region + filtered orders both attached at leaves;
customer joins to filtered nation via the existing edge set
(no synthesised edge needed); NO 6-table MHJ. Slice D's anchored
synthesis is now an optimisation opportunity rather than a
prerequisite for Q5 unlock.

commits.title: feat(m0077-0002): Slice B — post-filter base-row estimates + DP row plumbing
commits.description:
Implements Slice B of the M0077 Q5 planner fix per
docs/design/fix-for-q5/02 §2-§4:

1. selectivity.go: `selectivityEstimate{value, reliable}` plus
   `clauseSelectivityWithSource` / `eqOpSelectivityWithSource` /
   `rangeOpSelectivityWithSource`. The reliability flag is true
   only when stat-driven (MCV/histogram); fallback selectivities
   (defaultEq/defaultIneq/defaultGeneric) report unreliable so
   `baseRelInfo.filteredRows` keeps the pre-filter row count
   instead of over-trusting an arbitrary 0.005 / 0.333.

2. cardinality.go: `baseRelInfo` carries baseRows, filteredRows,
   localFilter, hasLocalFilter, isSmallDimension per binding.
   `estimateBaseRelInfo(binding, scan, local)` localizes the
   predicate via Slice A's `localizeExprToLeaf`, asks
   `clauseSelectivityWithSource`, and only adopts the scaled value
   when reliable=true. 1-row floor preserves the bushy DP's
   "no zero-row singletons" invariant.

3. bushy.go::dpEntry adds an explicit `rows int64`. Singleton
   subsets seed from `relInfos[i].filteredRows`; composed subsets
   carry the chosen join's output cardinality. `enumerateBushyPlans`
   accepts `[]baseRelInfo`; `tryBushyDP` builds the slice from
   Slice A's partition output before DP.

4. bushy.go::buildJoinFromDP takes `leftRows/rightRows` from the
   stored DP entries instead of re-reading `EstimateRows(plan)`,
   aligning the build-side decision with the same post-filter
   inputs used for cost.

Acceptance (live SF=1 focused gate `--queries=3,5,8,9,12,13,21,22`):

  Q3=11462, Q5 cancel @600s (Slice C/D job), Q8=2 (25s, 16x faster
  than Slice A's 421s), Q9=7 (mode-1 baseline), Q12=2, Q13=35,
  Q21=381, Q22=7.

Plan-diff vs m0076-baseline-ffc3429 — "should stay identical"
set (Q1,Q4,Q6,Q14,Q16,Q17,Q19,Q20,Q22): all MATCH. Diffs limited
to may-change set (Q2,Q5,Q7,Q8,Q9). Same diff footprint as Slice A.

Known carry-forward: Q9 wall time regressed 45s → 325s. Row-count
gate (rows=7) holds. The single-output `(L*R)/maxNDV` cost formula
misranks Q9's chained-NLI shape now that DP sees post-filter
rowcounts; Slice C's 3-part build-side-aware cost is designed to
restore Q9 wall time without rolling back B's row plumbing.

commits.title: feat(m0077-0001): Slice A — pre-MHJ leaf-local filter attachment + chained-NLI rebind robustness
commits.description:
Implements Slice A of the M0077 Q5 planner fix per
docs/design/fix-for-q5/01. Three coupled changes:

1. Planner: partition single-binding WHERE conjuncts before the
   bushy DP (`partitionConjunctsForJoinPlanning`) and re-attach
   them as `Filter(SeqScan)` wrappers on the bushy plan's leaves
   (`attachRelationLocalFilters`). New `Filter.LeafLocal` flag
   marks these wrappers so cumulative-space posMap passes
   (applyJoinTreePosMap, remapPosMapAfterRewrite) skip them. Gate
   `shouldAttachBeforeMHJ`: fromCount ≥ 5 AND any binding is
   `SmallDimension` — fires for Q5 / Q8 / Q21 shape, leaves
   smaller queries untouched.

2. Catalog: persist `SmallDimension` through Snapshot/Restore
   (TableEntry field + legacy fallback for region/nation). Without
   this, the live restarted bench server lost the hint and Slice A
   silently declined to fire.

3. NLI rebind: extend `tryBuildNLI`'s outer-rebind path to handle
   `outerIsJoin` (refresh outerJoin.schema via reresolveJoinByName,
   then SourceTableIdx/Name lookup). Add a type-mismatch override
   (`origTypeMatches`) that bypasses the M0075-0002 selectivity
   guard when the stale cr.Index points at a wrong-typed slot —
   without this Q8's chained NLI hit `not numeric at runtime
   (42804)` because its stale slot for c_nationkey was n_name
   (char). Q9's mode-1 baseline preserved (its stale slot has the
   right runtime type).

  Q3=11462, Q5 cancel @600s (Slice A is structural-only), Q8=2,

(Q1,Q4,Q6,Q14,Q15,Q16,Q17,Q19,Q20): all MATCH. Diffs limited to
expected may-change set (Q2,Q5,Q7,Q8,Q9). Q3/Q10/Q11/Q12/Q13/Q18/

commits.description:

inferTransitiveEqualities hook in tryBushyDP with the
M0076-0004 cost-model preparation
(inferredEdgePenalty=2.0, deterministic synthesis,
isInferred tagging) showed:

  `c.c_nationkey = n.n_nationkey` edge DID appear in
  Q5's plan (structural change from
  MultiHashJoin(6 tables) to nested Hash Join →
  Hash Join → MultiHashJoin(4 tables)).
- BUT the new plan was WORSE — intermediate
  `Hash Join (INNER) (rows=303042055)` estimates 303M
  rows for the lineitem⋈orders join, eclipsing the
  baseline's already-uncompletable cardinality.

The cost model picked the new plan because the
synthesised edge made it look cheap on paper —
estimateJoinCost's `(L * R) / max(NDistinct)` formula
favours high-NDistinct keys regardless of build-side
memory cost. The penalty=2.0 multiplier biases the DP
away from inferred edges proportionally to the explicit
edges' cost, but the baseline's edge selection wasn't
itself optimal — penalty alone can't differentiate
"cheap-looking-but-bad" plans from "actually cheap"
ones.

commits.title: feat(m0076-0004): cost-model edge discount + deterministic synthesis
commits.description:
Land the cost-model preparation that allows the
M0075-0001 inferTransitiveEqualities hook to be re-
enabled in the next commit (Commit D / M0076-0001)
without re-triggering the Q9 cancellation that caused
the original revert.

Two complementary fixes:

1. Deterministic synthesis ordering — the original
   `equiv_class.go::classes()` iterates Go maps which
   randomise iteration order, so the synthesised conjunct
   sequence appended to bushy DP's conjunct list shifted
   between runs and the DP picked different plans.
   M0076-0004 sorts each class's members by
   `compareColumnIdent` and sorts the iteration over
   class roots in `inferTransitiveEqualities`. Plan-
   snapshot diffs become reproducible.

2. Edge cost penalty — `joinEdge` gains an `isInferred bool`
   field. `buildJoinGraph` accepts a new `inferredCount int`
   parameter indicating how many trailing conjuncts are
   synthesised; edges produced from those conjuncts get
   `isInferred=true`. `estimateJoinCost` applies
   `inferredEdgePenalty = 2.0` when the edge is inferred,
   biasing the bushy DP away from plans that exploit
   transitively-redundant edges as if they were
   independent join opportunities.

Hook NOT YET enabled: this commit's `tryBushyDP`
caller passes `inferredCount=0` (historical pre-M0076
behaviour preserved), so all edges remain explicit
and `estimateJoinCost` returns the same values it
always has. Verified via plan-snapshot diff: all 21
TPC-H queries MATCH the M0076 baseline (Q15 special-
case skipped — see harness fix below).

commits.title: feat(m0076-0006): plan-snapshot regression harness + M0076 baseline
commits.description:
Land cmd/plan-snapshot — a planner-only regression
verification tool that captures EXPLAIN output for the
22 TPC-H queries and diffs against a saved baseline.
Provides ~30s feedback for planner-side commits vs the
~25min cost of the full 21-q sweep, addressing the
Phase 7 §8 lesson that subsequent planner work
(M0076-0004 cost-model, 0001 hook re-enable, 0005 Q9
fix) cannot afford per-commit sweeps.

Three equality modes (default: structural):
- structural — strips `(rows=N)` cost annotations;
  ignores cost variance from cost-model tweaks.
- strict-text — byte-for-byte comparison.
- semantic-cost — structural + cost ±10% tolerance.

CLI:
  plan-snapshot capture --label <name> [--queries 1,3,5-9]
  plan-snapshot diff    --label <name> [--queries 1] [--mode ...]

Makefile:
  make plan-snapshot-capture LABEL=<name>
  make plan-diff             LABEL=<name> [MODE=structural]

Decision tree (documented inline + in design doc):
  - planner-only changes (selectivity, transitivity,
    rebind, cost-model): plan-diff sufficient + targeted
    sweep on diverging queries.
  - executor / Datum / arena / catalog / wire-protocol:
    21-q sweep MANDATORY (M0075-0003 lesson reinforced).

Implementation:
- cmd/plan-snapshot/main.go (NEW): capture + diff
  subcommands; lib/pq connection (matches tpch-runner
  pattern); EXPLAIN text stored as
  plan_snapshots/<label>.txt with `=== Q<N>` delimiters.
- cmd/plan-snapshot/main_test.go (NEW): 9 unit tests
  pinning structural/strict-text/semantic-cost
  semantics + range-spec parsing + cost extraction.
- Makefile: plan-snapshot-build, plan-snapshot-capture,
  plan-diff targets.
- plan_snapshots/m0076-baseline-ffc3429.txt: M0076
  baseline (22 queries, 230 lines) captured at HEAD
  ffc3429 (M0075 close + M0076 docs).

Empirical caveat (documented in design doc status):
batch-mode diff (all 22 queries in one invocation)
shows ~9 queries diverging due to connection-pool
ordering effects (per-connection state accumulates
across consecutive EXPLAIN calls). Per-query mode
(`--queries=N`) is fully deterministic and matches
the baseline. Recommended workflow: per-commit
verification iterates per-query rather than batch.
Root-cause investigation (planner nondeterminism vs
pool-state) deferred to M0077.

Pre-commit gate (M0076 standard):
- go test ./cmd/plan-snapshot/... ./internal/{parser,
  planner,executor,testutil/tpch}/... PASS
- Per-query plan-diff against just-captured baseline:
  zero divergence (sanity).
- 21-q row counts: zero change (this commit doesn't
  touch executor at all; planner unaffected).

  FIRST so subsequent planner work uses fast plan-diff

- docs/design/0076-0004-cost-model-edge-discount.md —
  surgical cost-model preparation that allows the
  M0075-0001 inferTransitiveEqualities hook to be
  re-enabled without re-triggering the Q9 cancellation
  that caused the original revert. Two complementary
  fixes:
  (a) Deterministic synthesis ordering — equiv_class.go::

      deterministic conjunct order across runs); sorted

discount — bushy DP minimises cost, so larger cost on

feat(m0075-0002): chained-NLI rebind with per-outer selectivity guard (PARTIAL)
commits.description:
Land the per-outer selectivity guard for chained-NLI
rebind. The structural M0072-0002 hang is prevented:
when the rebind would land on a high-cardinality column,
the guard rejects it and the original ColumnRef.Index
is preserved (Q9 stays at mode-1 baseline).

Empirical result on Q9 (M0075 standard gate):
- Q9: OK 239s rows=7 (mode-1 baseline preserved)
- Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381, Q22=7 (silent-regression gate
  + M0071-0009 single-NLI invariant preserved)
- 21-q sweep: all row counts match Phase-6 baseline

The 100-row DETERMINISTIC target for Q9 is NOT met —
the guard correctly rejects all Q9 rebind candidates
because the per-outer match-set estimate exceeds 100
for every column NDistinct goopg has stats for. The
M0072-0002 hang mode (rebind onto high-cardinality
column → 600 s cancel with 0 rows) is structurally
prevented.

Implementation:
- internal/planner/nl_index_join.go:400 — rebind block
  extended to also fire for `*NestedLoopIndexJoin`
  outers. SourceTableIdx-aware lookup
  (findColumnIndexByNameAndSource from M0071-0009);
  rebinds without SourceTableIdx (cr.SourceTableIdx==0
  sentinel) are skipped (too risky to guess).
- internal/planner/nl_index_join_selectivity.go (NEW):
  - rebindPassesSelectivityGuard(outerNode, schema,
    newIdx) — returns false (reject rebind) when:
    - outerNode is nil / newIdx out of range
    - column NDistinct unavailable (no ANALYZE — safe
      conservative reject)
    - per-outer match-set estimate > 100
      (tableRows / NDistinct > threshold)
  - outerScanRowCount — walks past Project/Filter
    wrappers to find the chained-NLI outer's driving
    SeqScan / IndexScan; recurses on NLI.Outer for
    deeper chains; falls back to EstimateRows.
  - nliRebindSelectivityThreshold = 100 (constant)

Threshold rationale: the M0072-0002 postmortem
documented match-sets in the thousands at the failure
mode. 100 is conservative — well below the failure
threshold but permissive enough to allow legitimate
rebinds where per-outer selectivity is reasonable. If
future evidence shows 100 is too restrictive (Q9 stuck
at baseline despite the closure synthesis adding good
rebind candidates), M0076-0005 can raise it.

What lands:
- Code path is functional and integration-tested
  (full 21-q sweep parity).
- M0072-0002 failure mode (hang at 380-600 s with 0
  rows) structurally prevented for Q9 + any future
  chained-NLI candidate.
- Q21 single-NLI win from M0071-0009 unaffected (Q21
  not chained-NLI; takes the existing MHJ rebind path).

What does NOT meet target:
- Q9 row count: 7 (mode-1 baseline), not the 100+
  stretch target. The guard rejects all Q9 rebinds
  because every candidate column has high cardinality
  for the per-outer match-set heuristic. Unlocking
  Q9 needs M0076-0005 to combine the guard with
  M0075-0001 equivalence-class synthesis + refined
  cardinality estimates.

- 21-query SF=1 sweep PASS:
  - Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381, Q22=7 (silent-regression gate)
  - Q9=7 (mode-1 baseline preserved; M0072-0002 hang
    prevented)

  PASS

commits.title: feat(m0075-0005): numericDiv int64 fast-path
commits.description:
Wrap numericDiv with an int64 fast-path that skips
big.Int allocation when both operands are in the int64
lane (Big == nil) and the shifted numerator fits in
int64. Completes the M0074-0006 arithmetic-suite
coverage (cmp / add / sub / mul) for division.

TPC-H avg / sum-/-sum hot path coverage: Q1 (avg of
multiple lineitem columns), Q3 (avg via aggregate), Q5
(avg of lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)),
Q14 (sum / sum). The fast path eliminates the per-call
big.Int allocation overhead (~1 µs → ~50 ns).

Implementation:
- decimalDigitCount(v int64) — bits.Len64-based
  approximation of floor(log10(v)) + 1, refined via
  pow-table comparison. No floating-point math.
- floorDiv4(x int) — Go's int division rounds toward
  zero; this implements floor for negative inputs to
  match upstream's NBASE weight semantics.
- firstNBaseDigitInt64(absV, nd, dscale, w) — int64
  mirror of nbaseWeightAndFirstDigit; extracts the
  first 4-decimal-digit NBASE chunk from |v|·10^-dscale
  aligned to NBASE position w.
- numericDivScaleInt64(am, bm, da, db) — int64 mirror
  of numericDivScale; computes rscale via upstream's
  NBASE=10000 formula without decimal-string conversion.
- numericDivInt64Fast(a, b) — fast-path body. Zero-
  numerator short-circuit; rscale via numericDivScaleInt64;
  shift via mulInt64Pow10 (M0074-0006); integer divide;
  round half-away-from-zero with explicit q==0
  sign-handling matching the big.Int slow path
  byte-for-byte. Returns ok=false on shift>18 or
  intermediate overflow → caller falls through.

Wrap pattern (numericDiv body): try fast-path when
both operands are int64-lane; division-by-zero check
fires before either path; on fast-path overflow, fall
through to the existing big.Int code unchanged.

Result-correctness: TestNumericDivInt64FastVsBigPath
fuzzes 1000 random pairs at TPC-H scales (0/2/4/6);
fast-path output matches big.Int slow-path exactly via
numericCmp comparison. TestNumericDivInt64FastQEqualsZeroSignHandling
pins the tricky q==0 rounding case where the sign comes
from num*bm.

Pre-commit gate (M0075 standard):
- 21-query SF=1 sweep PASS:
  - Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381, Q22=7 (silent-regression gate)
  - Q9=7 (mode-1 baseline; M0075-0002 will fix)
  - All other rows match Phase-6 baseline
- go test ./internal/{parser,planner,executor,testutil/tpch}/...
  PASS
- New tests: numeric_div_int64_test.go (12 tests):
  - TestDecimalDigitCountBoundary — pin all 10^k
    boundaries
  - TestFloorDiv4 — pin negative-input floor semantics
  - TestNumericDivInt64FastBasic — TPC-H scales,
    sign combinations
  - TestNumericDivInt64FastVsBigPath — 1000-pair fuzz
  - TestNumericDivInt64FastZeroNumerator — short-circuit
  - TestNumericDivInt64FastDivisionByZero — 22012
  - TestNumericDivInt64FastShiftOverflowFallthrough —
    forced fallback
  - TestNumericDivInt64FastQEqualsZeroSignHandling —
    sign-handling edge case

    high scale with safe mantissa

commits.title: feat(m0074-0006): numeric int64 fast-path in cmp + add/sub/mul
commits.description:
Skip big.Int allocation in numericCmp / numericAdd /
numericSub / numericMul when both operands are in the
int64 lane (Big == nil) and aligned mantissas don't
overflow int64. TPC-H NUMERIC(15,2) columns
(lineitem.l_quantity, l_extendedprice, l_discount, l_tax,
orders.o_totalprice, etc.) all fit easily — the fast
path covers the dominant TPC-H comparison/arithmetic
workload.

Q5 CPU pprof at M0073-final showed compareDatum at
5.86 % flat / 12.17 % cum, with `numericMant` allocating
fresh big.Int per call (numeric.go:34-39) regardless of
operand kind. The int64 fast-path eliminates that
allocation outright on the dominant Q5 path.

Implementation:
- mulInt64Pow10(v, exp) — overflow-safe scale alignment.
  Uses division (math.MaxInt64/p) to detect overflow
  before the multiply itself wraps.
- alignNumericInt64(am, ascale, bm, bscale) — brings
  two int64 mantissas to a common scale via mulInt64Pow10.
  ok=false on overflow → caller falls through to big.Int.
- numericCmpInt64Fast — compares aligned int64 mantissas.
- addInt64Overflow / subInt64Overflow / mulInt64Overflow
  — sign-based overflow detection on the result of the
  arithmetic op.
- int64Pow10 lookup table for 10^0 .. 10^18.

Wrapping in numericCmp / numericAdd / numericSub /
numericMul: try fast path first, fall through to
existing big.Int path on overflow or when either operand
has Big != nil.

numericDiv NOT wrapped this commit — division must
preserve numericMinSigDigits via upstream's NBASE
formula (`select_div_scale`); int64 fast path requires
careful scale-bound analysis. Carries to M0075 if Q5/Q9
pprof shows numericDiv as a remaining hot path. (Q5
predicate is dominated by cmp+add+sub; mul appears in
revenue calculations.)

Pre-commit gate (M0074 standard):
- 21-query SF=1 sweep PASS:
  - Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381, Q22=7 (silent-regression gate)
  - Q9=7 (mode-1 baseline; M0074-0002 will fix)
  - All other rows match Phase-5 baseline
- go test ./internal/parser/... ./internal/planner/...
  ./internal/executor/... ./internal/testutil/tpch/...
  PASS
- New tests: numeric_int64_fast_test.go (boundary +
  fuzz vs big.Int slow path; 1000 random pairs at TPC-H
  scales 0/2/4/6 confirm result equivalence on Add/Sub/
  Mul; 1000 pairs confirm Cmp equivalence; overflow
  fallback exercised via MaxInt64/scale=18 case)

commits.title: docs(m0074): milestone + 5 design docs scaffolding (CPU + Q9 + Datum packed)
commits.description:
Land authoritative references for M0074 ahead of
implementation commits. M0074 follows M0073's docs-first
discipline (each implementation commit cites a landed
design doc).

Five sub-milestones across four independent tracks:

- M0074-0006 (numeric int64 fast-path) — `numericCmp` /
  `numericAdd/Sub/Mul/Div` skip `big.Int` allocation when
  both operands have `Big == nil` and aligned mantissas
  fit in int64. TPC-H NUMERIC(15,2) mantissas all fit
  easily; ~5.86 % flat CPU on Q5 reclaimed.

- M0074-0004 (DecodeRowProjectionIntoArena) — arena
  variant of the existing `DecodeRowProjection`; wire
  index-build paths in operators_ddl.go.

- M0074-0002 (chained-NLI virtual-coord propagation) —
  Q9 structural fix. Replaces M0072-0002's reverted
  rebind shortcut with executor-side virtual-coord
  resolution: when evalExprSlot evaluates a ColumnRef
  against a *VirtualSlot outer, route through the
  virtualCol indirection at runtime. Planner-side uses
  M0071-0009's SchemaColumn.SourceTableIdx +
  findColumnIndexByNameAndSource to bind the inner
  ColumnRef.Index correctly. Q9 must produce 175 rows
  DETERMINISTICALLY post-D.

- M0074-0001 (vectorised evalBinary + ColumnRef inline)
  — Q5 CPU drop. ColumnRef hoisted to first arm of
  evalExprSlot's type switch (saves 12 type-test
  comparisons per call). New `evalBinaryBatch` entry
  for OpEq/Lt/Gt/Le/Ge/Ne/Add/Sub/And/Or arms with
  conservative eligibility detector. seqScanOp predicate
  batch path. Q5 evalBinary cum CPU target ≤ 15 % (was
  33.72 %); evalExprSlot cum ≤ 50 % (was 68.68 %).

- M0074-0003 (Datum struct packed layout, HIGH RISK) —
  Buf [24B] + arena [8B] → ArenaRef + Offset + Length
  [12B]. Struct shrinks from 64 B → 52 B exact. Frees
  12 B headroom for future Datum field additions
  (nullable flag, lifetime tag, type-system flags).
  Per-process permArena (slot 0 of arenaRegistry) hosts
  literal Datums + detoasted bytes; never resets.
  arenaRegistry holds 256 slots with atomic CAS for
  per-arena registration. 38 NewStringDatum/
  NewBytesDatum sites + DetoastValue + spill + COPY
  paths migrate transparently via the constructor flip.
  TIGHT GATE: full 21-query SF=1 sweep + go test ./...
  must pass; revert immediately on row-count regression.

Land order (cheapest+independent → riskiest):
B (0006) → C (0004) → D (0002) → E (0001) → F (0003).

commits.title: feat(m0073-0002+0004): arena wiring + Materialize promotion (Q5/Q9 GC fix)
commits.description:
Wire the per-batch arena through DecodeRowInto + seqScanOp +
indexScanOp, and Materialize-promote arena Datums at the slot
pipeline's retention boundaries. M0072-0004 deferred the
producer integration; this commit lands it.

Q9's correct row set is ~25× larger than pre-M0072 (175 rows
vs 7 silent-FN); per-tuple `string()` allocations dominated
the resulting heap (M0072-final pprof: acquireRow 25.31% cum).
Per-batch arena allocation amortises across pages (one
~64 KiB allocation per page covers thousands of varchar
columns). Q5 / Q9 wall time and total heap should both
compress; Q12=2 / Q13=35 / Q21=381 silent-regression
gates preserved.

Scope:

DecodeRowInto arena dispatch (M0073-0002):
- internal/executor/codec.go:
  - DecodeRowInto / DecodeRowIntoArena: thin public
    wrappers around the new internal decodeRowIntoArena
    (arena param). When arena != nil, the producer's varchar
    / char / text / bytea columns emerge as
    KindStringArena / KindBytesArena Datums via decodeValueArena.
  - decodeValueArena (NEW): mirrors decodeValue for fixed-
    width types (int / time / numeric — those don't carry
    Buf payload), routes the variable-length default arm
    through arena.Allocate(n) + KindStringArena Datum.
  - Arena.Allocate signature change: returns (buf, offset)
    so decodeValueArena can encode the position into Datum.Int
    (high 32 bits offset, low 32 bits length).

Producer arena binding (M0073-0004):
- internal/executor/operators_storage.go::seqScanOp:
  - Add arena field; NewArena(0) at Open; Reset on per-block
    boundary (curBlock++); Drop at Close.
  - DecodeRowInto call → DecodeRowIntoArena with o.arena.
- internal/executor/operators_index.go::indexScanOp:
  - Add arena field; NewArena(0) at openPrep; Reset on
    Rescan (per-outer probe); Drop at Close.
  - DecodeRowInto call → DecodeRowIntoArena with o.arena.

Materialize promotion at retention boundaries (M0073-0004):
- internal/executor/operators_join_agg.go::evalGroupKey
  + applyAgg::min/max:
  - vals[i] = v.MaterializeArena() before storage in
    groupRuntime.groupValues (the M0071 silent-regression
    surface — group keys retained across many input rows
    must outlive the producer's arena.Reset).
  - st.value = arg.MaterializeArena() in min/max storage.
- internal/executor/operators_join_agg.go::drainRowsCtx:
  - cloneRowOwned when row has arena Datums (build-side hash
    table retention; mirrors the spill-path retention site).
- internal/executor/spill.go::drainRowsBounded:
  - cloneRowOwned at in-memory accumulation when row has
    arena Datums (transition to spill mode would otherwise
    serialise stale arena pages).
- internal/executor/storage_test.go::drainScan:
  - Test helper now calls slot.Materialize().Row(), mirroring
    executor.Run's public-boundary contract — tests that read
    rows[].Kind must see the promoted KindString / KindBytes
    (the production Run path already does this).

Cross-Kind comparison support (arena Datums compare equal
to non-arena Datums of the same logical type):
- internal/executor/expr.go::compareDatum + compareEq +
  promoteCrossKind:
  - Treat KindString / KindStringArena (and KindBytes /
    KindBytesArena) as the same logical Kind for equality
    and ordering. The existing Format-fallback works via
    StringValue() but the dedicated path keeps the byte
    compare on the hot path.
- evalSubstr / evalDatePart / evalToTimestamp arg-Kind
  checks now accept KindStringArena (the receiver routes
  through StringValue() which dispatches to arena.Bytes).
- operators_ddl.go btree-index-key encoding accepts arena
  Kind for varchar / char columns.

Datum-format / serialization sites updated:
- Format / datumKey / datumAsString / encode paths now
  switch on (KindString | KindStringArena) and
  (KindBytes | KindBytesArena) where applicable
  (numeric.go / spill.go / toast.go / copy_text.go /
  copy_binary.go / plpgsql_runtime.go / codec.go).

Verification (TPC-H SF=1, fresh restart):
- Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381 (382 s), Q22=7 spot-check PASS.
- Earlier sweep also showed Q1=4, Q3=11462, Q4=5, Q9=7,
  Q10=20574, Q11=1142, Q14=1, Q16=18170, Q17=1, Q18=11,
  Q19=1, Q20=99 preserved (the Q22 evalSubstr Kind-check
  fix was added in this same commit; the sweep that
  exposed the issue produced 21/22 OK + Q22 ERROR before
  the operators_ddl + evalSubstr fixes).
- go test ./... PASS (parser / planner / executor /
  testutil/tpch).

Q5 heap pprof verification carried to M0073-0005 (final
sweep + handover). Expected drop: acquireRow ≤ 5 % cum
heap (was 25.31 %), total Q5 heap ≤ 1.0 TB (was 1.46 TB).
Q9 wall time target ≤ 600 s (compression), hard floor ≤

commits.title: feat(m0073-0001): Datum.arena field + KindStringArena/BytesArena variants
commits.description:
Type surface for the per-batch arena integration. After M0072-0004
landed the Arena infrastructure (commit b081767) but left it
uncalled, this commit extends Datum to carry arena-backed
variants without producer wiring. Existing callers see no
behaviour change; subsequent commits (M0073-0002 + M0073-0004)
land DecodeRowInto + seqScan/indexScan + Materialize promotion.

Scope:
- internal/executor/datum.go:
  - DatumKind: add KindStringArena, KindBytesArena.
  - Datum struct: add `arena *Arena` field. Layout becomes
    64 B exact (was 56 B with 8 B padding); the compile-time
    assertion `64 - sizeof(Datum) == 0` still holds.
  - StringValue() / BytesValue() dispatch on Kind:
    arena variants resolve via arena.Bytes(offset, length);
    legacy KindString/KindBytes path unchanged. (offset, length)
    is packed into the existing Int int64 field — high 32 bits
    offset, low 32 bits length — saving two int32 fields.
  - newStringArenaDatum / newBytesArenaDatum constructors.
  - rowHasArena / cloneRowOwned helpers used by Materialize.

- internal/executor/arena.go:
  - Allocate signature change: returns (buf, offset) so
    M0073-0002's DecodeRowInto can encode the position into
    Datum.Int. Oversized-payload path inserts dedicated page
    after cur and reports the corresponding offset.
  - Bytes(offset, length) accessor (NEW; specified in design
    0068-0003 but omitted from M0072-0004's land). Resolves
    page-relative offset back to byte slice.

- internal/executor/arena_test.go:
  - Update existing tests for the new Allocate signature.

- internal/executor/slot.go:
  - MaterializedSlot.Materialize: rowHasArena fast-path skip
    preserves the no-arena no-op contract; when arena Datums
    are present, calls cloneRowOwned to deep-copy bytes into
    owned []byte. Pre-M0073-0004 (this commit) the slow path
    is exercised only by tests; production rows have no arena
    Datums until decode wiring lands.

- internal/executor/datum_arena_test.go (NEW):
  - TestM0073DatumStructSize pins the 64 B layout.
  - TestM0073DatumStringArenaRoundTrip / BytesArenaRoundTrip
    pin accessor dispatch.
  - TestM0073DatumNonArenaPathUnchanged pins backward compat:
    NewStringDatum / NewBytesDatum produce Datums with
    arena=nil and the legacy Buf-based accessors.
  - TestM0073RowHasArena / CloneRowOwnedPromotesArenaDatums
    pin the deep-copy semantics: post-arena.Reset() the
    promoted Datum still reads correctly even when the same
    arena page is reused for new payload.
  - TestM0073MaterializePromotesArenaDatum / NoArenaIsNoOp
    pin the slot.Materialize integration.

Verification:
- unsafe.Sizeof(Datum{}) == 64 (compile-time assertion).
- go test ./internal/executor/... PASS, incl. 8 new
  TestM0073* tests covering round-trip, deep-copy, and
  Materialize promotion.
- TPC-H gate (TPC-H SF=1, fresh-restart):
  Q12=2, Q13=35, Q21=381 (386 s, with 600 s budget) — all
  preserved. Type surface only; producer flow unchanged.
- 21-query sweep parity carried forward from M0073-0003 (no
  runtime change in this commit; arena-backed Datums never
  appear in production paths until M0073-0004 lands).

Carry-forward to M0073-0002 (DecodeRowInto arena param) +
M0073-0004 (seqScan/indexScan binding + Materialize promotion
exercised in production flow).

commits.title: feat(m0073-0003): UnaryOp / BinaryOp Op string → OpCode int8 enum

+ byte-comparison; expected ~2-4 × per-switch speedup on

  tryFoldUnaryOp / matchSingleTableConstantPredicate /

  rangeOpMatches / promoteToNumeric / arithmetic now take

commits.title: feat(m0072-0004): land Arena type + tests; integration carries to M0073
commits.description:
Per design 0068-0003 (Per-Batch String Arena), introduce
the Arena type as a standalone foundation:

- internal/executor/arena.go (NEW):
  - Arena struct with [][]byte page list + cur cursor.
  - Allocate(n) returns a writable slice within the active
    page; auto-grows to a fresh 64 KiB page when needed.
  - Oversized payloads (n > pageSize) get a dedicated page
    inserted after cur so subsequent small allocations

    multi-page growth, oversized fallback, zero-length

modifying Datum.Buf semantics + retention-site invariants

commits.description:

explicit outerWidth. The 3 outer-column read sites
(lookupKeys, lookupKey, lookupRangeBounds × 2) call

(was acquireRow(outerW + innerW)) and the per-outer two
copy() calls. The IndexScan reads outer columns directly
from o.outerMS, the persistent slot whose .row is updated
per outer match in the existing M0071-0013 path. The
inner's BindOuter / Rescan receive the slot directly.

a persistent o.scanRow buffer (mirrors seqScanOp's
M0054-0005a pattern). cloneRow on append keeps o.rows[]
ownership independent of the buffer. Net effect:
DecodeRow's per-tuple Row alloc moves out of the hot path.

- evalExpr is now a thin wrapper over evalExprSlot. ColumnRef

commits.title: feat(m0071-0010): Stage B — Operator.Next returns TupleSlot
commits.description:
Migrates Operator.Next() from (Row, error) to (TupleSlot, error)
per design doc 0068-0002. Stage A scaffold (MaterializedSlot +
VirtualSlot interfaces) was in place; this commit wires every
producer to wrap its row return in a slot via SlotFromRow, every
consumer to extract Row via slotRow(), and adds Materialize() at
retention sites that hold rows across many Next() calls.

The two prior Stage B attempts (08b1a5c, 3398d47, both reverted)
silently broke Q12=0/Q13=2 on the 22-query sweep. Their failure
mode was that they removed producer-side cloneRow on the
assumption that retention sites were defensively cloning — which
they were for Row-level slot reuse, but the slot itself doesn't
take ownership without Materialize.

This commit takes the safer approach:
- Producer cloneRow paths stay in place (existing OwnedRow
  semantics preserved).
- Slot wrapping at the Next() boundary is purely additive.
- Retention sites (sortOp.Open, windowOp.Open,
  lockRowsOp.drainAndStamp) explicitly call slot.Materialize()
  to take ownership independent of the producer's slot lifetime.
- Run() at the public boundary materializes for caller safety.

Stage C (filter/limit/instrument/projectOp pure VirtualSlot
pass-through), Stage D (NLI joinBuf and MHJ lazyOut →
VirtualSlot composition for Q5 GC fix), and Stage E (remove
Borrowable / OwnedRow / BorrowedRow / setChildBorrow) are
follow-on work; this commit lands the foundation.

commits.description:

  Phase 3 target)

remain in place). Carry-forward to Phase 3 slot pipeline.

commits.title: feat(m0071-0002-followup): Q20 scalar Project + NLI flip fix (re-land)
commits.description:
Re-applies commit f855627 on top of the Stage B+C revert.
The Q20 fix is independent of Stage B+C and gives Q20: 0 → 99
rows on its own.

Two coupled fixes for Q20's 0-rows regression:

1. **Scalar Project preservation in unnestSubquery**
   (`internal/planner/unnest.go`). The scalar subquery's outer
   Project (e.g. Q20's `SELECT 0.5 * sum(l_quantity)`) was
   being unwrapped and dropped — the substitution replaced the
   scalar with the raw aggregate column ref `sum`, losing the
   `0.5 *` multiplier. Now substitutes with a clone of the
   Project's target expression, replacing any ColumnRef whose
   Index points at the original Aggregate's single output
   column with the new merged-coord aggColRef.

2. **NLI flip decline in pickInnerSide**
   (`internal/planner/nl_index_join.go`). When the would-be
   NLI conversion has Left=SeqScan, Right=Aggregate (the
   scalar-decorrelation shape), pickInnerSide chose Left as
   inner and Right as outer — flipping the merged schema from
   `Left ++ Right` to `Right ++ Left`. Downstream Filter
   ColumnRefs (e.g. Q20's `ps_availqty/2 > 0.5 * sum/5`) bound
   to the pre-flip layout land on wrong slots: in the
   post-flip schema, ps_availqty is at index 5 and sum is at
   index 2, so the predicate becomes `sum > 0.5 *
   ps_availqty` — silently false for typical SF=1 data,
   filtering all rows. Decline NLI conversion in this shape;
   the HashJoin path keeps the canonical schema order and
   works.

Verification:

  - Q13 SF=1: 35 rows preserved
  - Q18 SF=1: 11 rows preserved
  - Q20 SF=1: 0 rows → **99 rows** (canonical ~186)

    ./internal/testutil/tpch/...                       PASS
  - Unit test `internal/planner/q20_unnest_test.go`
    pins the scalar Project's `0.5 *` multiplier survives
    the decorrelation rewrite.

commits.title: feat(m0071-0003-followup): lazy hash Semi/Anti residual eval + predRebind ambiguity preserve
commits.description:
Two correctness improvements for the EXISTS / NOT EXISTS
unnested join paths. Both are silent-bug fixes that the
M0071-0003 Q21 zero-rows investigation surfaced:

1. **lazy hash Semi/Anti now evaluates the residual Predicate
   per-match** (`operators_join_agg.go:semiAntiAnyResidualPasses`).
   The prior code at lines 564-582 short-circuited Semi on
   "any key match" and Anti on "any key match" — silently
   discarding the residual `l3.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey`
   (Q21's NOT EXISTS body) at runtime. Now Semi keeps the
   probe iff at least one matching build row passes the
   residual; Anti drops the probe iff at least one match
   passes (= a "real" match exists). Without this, Q21's
   Anti dropped every outer row on hash-key match alone
   regardless of the residual test.

2. **`bushy.go::predRebind` preserves the original ColumnRef
   Index when the suggested side has the name AMBIGUOUSLY**
   (was: silently rebound to the OTHER side's same-named
   column). The Q21 widened-schema case (l1.l_suppkey at
   left/4 + l2.l_suppkey at left/12 after EXISTS Semi's
   merged-schema widen) caused the AntiJoin's predicate
   `Col[l_suppkey/4]` to be rebound to `Col[l_suppkey/16]`
   (l3's l_suppkey on the right side), turning the predicate
   into `l3.l_suppkey <> l3.l_suppkey` (always false) →
   no real anti-match. Adding `schemaHasName` guard so the
   ambiguous case keeps the original (binder-set) index
   prevents this silent rebind.

Verification:
  - go test ./internal/planner/...
    ./internal/executor/...
    ./internal/testutil/tpch/...                       PASS
  - Q4 SF=1: 5 rows preserved (regression guard for EXISTS
    unnest).
  - Q22 SF=1: 7 rows preserved (regression guard for
    EXISTS unnest).

Q21 itself still returns 0 rows on SF=1. Both fixes here
are correctness improvements that close silent-bug
classes; the residual Q21 0-rows is now suspected to be
a separate issue in the NLI Semi (the EXISTS Semi was
NLI-converted via partsupp_pk-style index and may not be
emitting outer rows correctly), to be investigated in
M0071-0005 Stage D follow-up.

commits.title: feat(m0071-0004): push single-source MHJ filters into Tables[i] build inputs
commits.description:
Adds `pushSingleSourceFiltersIntoMHJTables` that walks
`mh.Filters`, classifies each conjunct against the cumulative
column-offsets of `Tables[i]`, and pushes any conjunct whose
every ColumnRef references a single Tables[i]'s
column-range down onto a `*Filter` wrapping that
`mh.Tables[i]`. Indices are localised to Tables[i].Output()
via a structural clone + shift so the wrapped filter
evaluates against the table's own row.

Unlike the existing
`rewriteMHJInputsWithSingleTablePredicates` (which only
promotes when a B-tree index exists on the column), this
pushdown applies to **any** single-source conjunct,
including `r_name = 'ASIA'` on Q5's region (no r_name
index loaded). The build-side cardinality drops before MHJ
hash-builds, cutting probe-time per-row work.

Walker integration:
  - Wired into `rewriteScanInputsWithSingleTablePredicates`
    as the post-step on each MultiHashJoin node, after the
    index-promotion pass and after recursive descent into
    Tables[i].

Q3 regression guard:
  - Single-source classifier requires every ColumnRef in
    the conjunct to land in EXACTLY one Tables[i]'s
    cumulative range. Cross-table conjuncts (Q3's join
    keys, Q5's `r_regionkey = n_regionkey`, etc.) stay in
    `mh.Filters` untouched.

Verification:
  - go test ./...                                PASS
  - tpch-runner --queries=3,5,7,10:
      Q3   45.63 s rows=11462  (preserved — M0066/M0067
                                  break-glass)
      Q5   ERROR cancel-400s   (still structural; M0070
                                  was cancel-1200s; Q5
                                  needs slot pipeline for
                                  the duffcopy/memmove
                                  residual ~60 % of CPU)
      Q7   37.89 s rows=4      (preserved)
      Q10  37.84 s rows=20574  (preserved)
  - 600 s Q5 re-test in progress.

Note: Q5's cancel persists because the Q5 cancel root cause
is GC/row-copy bound (M0067 baseline pprof: ~60 % is
duffcopy/memmove/memclr), not cardinality. The pushdown
helps build-time at the margin but doesn't move the
fundamental probe-loop cost. Q5 structural fix continues
to require M0071-0005 TupleSlot pipeline.

commits.title: feat(m0071-0003): defensive OuterColumnRef Name re-resolve in EXISTS unnest residual
commits.description:
`unnestExistsExpr`'s residual rewrite (lines 1815-1870) re-
indexes the lifted residual conjuncts via OuterColumnRef →
ColumnRef. The binder's Index was set against FROM-cumulative
offsets at parse time; after bushy / MHJ / NLI rewrites the
runtime row layout may have reordered, so x.Index can be
stale (cf. M0064 the same pattern at
nl_index_join.go:399).

Adds `resolveOuterIdx(name, fallback)` that:
- Returns fallback when outerSchema[fallback].Name matches
  (no shift needed).
- Otherwise walks outerSchema; if there's exactly ONE column
  matching by Name, returns that index.
- Otherwise (ambiguous self-join column like Q21's l1/l2/l3
  all containing `l_suppkey`) returns the fallback so the
  prior behaviour is preserved.

Q21 status:
  - Before: OK 384 s, rows = 0 (silent over-match).
  - After:  OK 396 s, rows = 0.
  Q21's Schema has TWO `l_suppkey` columns (l1 in the MHJ
  outer, l2 from the EXISTS sub-join). The fallback path
  fires; the underlying disambiguation requires alias-aware
  schema columns OR the TupleSlot pipeline's stable
  per-source coordinates (M0071-0005). Q21's residual
  zero-rows is therefore documented as
  slot-pipeline-blocked. The defensive re-resolve still
  protects unambiguous-column cases (Q4 / Q22 unchanged at
  5 / 7 rows).

commits.title: feat(m0071-0002): non-correlated IN inner Project marked IsolatedScope
commits.description:
Prevents the NLI rewriter (`tryBuildNLI` /
`internal/planner/nl_index_join.go::pickInnerSide`) from
flipping outer/inner roles on the SemiJoin that
`unnestNonCorrelatedInExpr` (M0069-0005) constructs. Without
the gate, pickInnerSide saw the SemiJoin's Right was a wrapped
Project+Filter+Scan, refused to use it as inner, then picked
the original SemiJoin's Left (e.g. `Scan(partsupp)`) as the
NLI inner — flipping the row layout from
`partsupp ++ part_inner` to `part_inner ++ partsupp` and
shifting inner-side Filter ColumnRefs (e.g. Q20's
`p_name LIKE 'forest%'`) past `partsupp_width`.

The shift produced silent zero-rows (or `column ref out of
range` runtime errors) on any TPC-H query that combines a
non-correlated IN with an indexable inner join key.

Empirical verification:
  Pre-fix:
    `partsupp WHERE ps_partkey IN (parts LIKE 'forest%')`
      → ERROR `column ref p_name/13 out of range`
    Q20 outer no-scalar
      → count = 0
  Post-fix:
    `partsupp WHERE ps_partkey IN (parts LIKE 'forest%')`
      → count = 8748 ✓
    Q20 outer no-scalar
      → count = 228 ✓ (was 0)
    Q20 outer no-scalar Q18 regression guard
      → Q18 rows = 11 unchanged ✓

Q20 (full, with the correlated scalar subquery on
`ps_availqty > 0.5*sum(l_quantity)`) still returns 0 rows.
The remaining 0-rows is a SEPARATE bug from this fix:
the scalar-subquery decorrelation (M0040-0002 / M0058-0001)
runs BEFORE the M0069-0005 IN unnest in the recursive
`unnestSubqueriesInPlan` call, mutating the partsupp Filter
child from `Scan(partsupp)` to `HashJoin(GroupAggregate,
partsupp)`. The subsequent IN unnest's outerKey index
(`ps_partkey` at `outerCol.Index = 0`) was bound at parse
time against the pre-decorrelation layout and now points at
the wrong slot in the decorrelated row. Tracked as a
follow-up (M0071-0002 second-pass — IN-unnest column-index
re-resolution against post-decorrelation outerChild.Output).

Refs:
  - docs/design/0071-0002-q20-zero-rows-diagnostic.md
    (H1/H2 confirmed; H3 partially confirmed for the
    scalar-decorrelation interaction)
  - internal/planner/nl_index_join.go:375 (M0063-0001
    IsolatedScope NLI gate; this commit hooks the same
    mechanism for IN-unnested inner subqueries)

commits.title: feat(m0069-0001): Stage B — Operator.Next returns TupleSlot
commits.description:
Migrates the executor pipeline to TupleSlot. Each producer
operator gains a per-instance `outSlot MaterializedSlot`
field; Next() sets `outSlot.row = row` and returns
`&o.outSlot`, avoiding per-call allocation. The slot's row
is invalidated by the next Next() call on the same operator
(slot-level borrow semantics, replacing the row-level
BorrowSemantics contract structurally).

What changed:
  - Operator.Next() (Row, error) → (TupleSlot, error)
  - 33 producer operator types: outSlot field + Next return
    via o.outSlot.set(row)
  - 33 consumer call sites: NextRow(op) helper that materialises
    back to Row at the boundary; existing Row-typed consumers
    remain Row-typed during the migration window
  - Per-op cloneRow / copyOut producer-side calls collapsed
    into the shared outSlot — clone responsibility shifts to
    retention consumers (sortOp drain, lockRowsOp pending,
    Run/drainScan retention loops)
  - Multi-hash-join's M0066-0002 copyOut() path removed —
    structurally preserved via outSlot pointing at lazyOut

Performance:
  - tpch-runner Q1/Q3/Q11/Q21 smoke (post-migration vs M0070):
      Q1   50.63 s   (was 41.83 s — +21 %)
      Q3   38.80 s   (was 36.73 s — flat)
      Q11   4.89 s   (was  2.96 s — +65 %)
      Q21 386.92 s   (was 384.56 s — flat, OK preserved)
  - The remaining wrap/unwrap cost on small-row queries is
    the consumer-side `slot.Row()` materialisation at the
    NextRow helper. Stages C/D will eliminate this for
    pass-through operators (filter/project/limit) by
    consuming TupleSlot natively.

commits.title: feat(m0070-0002): bgwriter scan releases poolMu between slots
commits.description:
The M0070 mutex profile on Q9 (218 s wall) showed 92.62 % of
all mutex contention coming from `Bgwriter.run` →
`Pool.WriteDirtyPages` holding poolMu across the full slot
scan loop while foreground Pin / Unpin callers blocked. With
64 K slots that's a ~640 µs critical section per bgwriter
tick, and at typical tick frequency it serialises with every
hot Pin path.

Fix: snapshot bgwriterHand once under poolMu, then walk the
slot range acquiring + releasing poolMu briefly per scanned
slot. Each slot's metadata read is consistent (the brief
acquire/release pair sees its tag/valid/dirty/pinCount
atomically) and the per-victim re-validation at the
flush-decision step still catches any staleness introduced
between scan iterations. Net effect: bgwriter critical
sections shrink from O(n) per tick to O(1) per slot, freeing
poolMu for foreground callers.

Verification:
  - go test ./internal/storage/... ./internal/...     PASS
  - tpch-runner --queries=9 (Q9 218 s wall):
      Pre  mutex contention: 1426.77 ms
                             93.61 % sync.Mutex.Unlock
                             92.62 % Bgwriter.run
                                     → WriteDirtyPages
      Post mutex contention:  160.89 ms (−89 %)
                             Bgwriter.run not in top 8

Profiles committed:
  - bench/tpch/pprof/mutex_q9_pre.prof
  - bench/tpch/pprof/mutex_q9_post.prof

This delivers M0070-0002 without a full poolMu sharding
rewrite. The remaining contention (160 ms over 215 s on a
single backend) doesn't justify the ~500-line shard-with-CAS
restructure that was the original M0070-0002 plan; the
documented null result for poolMu *partition* is acceptable
under the fix_plan acceptance criteria. The bgwriter fix is
the actionable subset that the profile pointed at.

commits.title: fix(m0069-0005): drop IN conjunct + use JoinTypeSemi for non-correlated unnest
commits.description:
Q18 regressed in the M0069-0005 sweep with
`column ref l_orderkey/33 out of range` because the
non-correlated IN unnest was:

  1. Adding the SemiJoin predicate `outer = inner` to the
     surviving Filter's conjunct list. The Filter's output is
     the Join's output, which is outer-only under JoinTypeSemi
     — so the inner-key reference at index outerWidth landed
     past the row's actual width.

  2. Initially using JoinTypeInner with mergedSchema
     (outer ++ inner). That widened every upstream
     column-index reference by innerWidth and broke any
     plan that aggregates over the outer (Q18 has
     SUM(l_quantity) above a 3-table FROM).

Fix mirrors the EXISTS unnest (M0061-0001):
  - Drop the IN conjunct from the Filter; the equality is
    encoded structurally via the join's (LeftKey, RightKey)
    and JoinTypeSemi.
  - Use JoinTypeSemi (executor emits probe row directly) and
    set the Join's schema = outer-only — preserves all
    upstream column indices.

commits.title: feat(m0069): M0069-0005 — non-correlated IN-subquery unnest to SemiJoin
commits.description:
Extends internal/planner/unnest.go's IN-unnest path
(M0040-0002) to handle the non-correlated case. Q20's outer
`s_suppkey IN (SELECT ps_suppkey FROM partsupp WHERE ...)`
has zero OuterColumnRefs in the inner plan, so the existing
collectUnnestParams returned empty and the IN survived as a
runtime SubPlan with the M0058-0001 cache. The cache served
correctness but the inner partsupp scan + nested IN/scalar
subqueries pushed Q20 past cancel-after=1200s.

New path:
  - canUnnestInExpr admits InExpr where IsNonCorrelated=true
    and the inner Output is a single column.
  - unnestNonCorrelatedInExpr builds a SemiJoin (encoded as
    JoinTypeInner with a single equality predicate, the
    same shape the existing correlated unnest produces) using
    InExpr.Operand as the outer key and the inner Plan's sole
    output column as the inner key.
  - Recursive unnestSubqueriesInPlan on the inner plan still
    runs so nested correlated subqueries inside the inner
    (Q20's lineitem aggregate inside partsupp's filter) get
    pulled up into the inner-side join.

Guards:
  - in.Negated=true (NOT IN) is rejected — anti-semi-join
    semantics out of scope for M0069-0005.
  - in.Operand must be a ColumnRef — non-trivial expressions
    on the LHS keep the runtime cache path.
  - Single-output subquery only.

commits.title: feat(m0068): Phase C — sortOp external sort with chunked spill (M0068-0006)
commits.description:
Bounds peak memory residency for sortOp to a configurable chunk
size (default 256 MiB) regardless of input row count. The previous
sortOp drained the entire child into one in-memory []Row before
sort.SliceStable, which OOM'd on large TPC-H sorts and made the
heap profile a tall spike at sort time.

Algorithm:
1. Open() drains child rows into an in-memory chunk, tracking
   estimatedRowBytes.
2. When chunkBytes exceeds chunkLimitBytes, the chunk is sorted
   in place, written to a new spill file via the existing
   spillWriter, and the in-memory slice is reset.
3. After child EOF, the final tail is sorted.
4. If any spill files exist, Next() lazily opens spillReaders for
   each plus uses the in-memory tail as one source, then runs an
   N-way merge using container/heap. Otherwise the existing
   in-memory emission path is preserved.

Key types:
  - sortOp.chunkLimitBytes — per-instance threshold (default 256 MiB)
  - sortSource — single merge input (spill file or in-memory tail)

commits.title: feat(m0068): Phase B — Row pool integration on operator scratch buffers (M0068-0004)
commits.description:
Wire `acquireRow`/`releaseRow` into scratch buffers that operators
own and reuse internally:
  - seqScanOp.scanRow      (per-block decode buffer)
  - projectOp.out          (per-row projection buffer)
  - nestedLoopIndexJoinOp.joinBuf (outer+inner combine buffer)
  - multiHashJoinOp.lazyOut (lazy MHJ output buffer)
  - drainRowsCtx.dup       (defensive clone in build drains)

Each is acquired in Open()/init and released in Close(), so the
sync.Pool warms up across operator lifecycles within a query
(and across queries via cross-query Pool persistence).

Per-row releaseRow on emitted rows is intentionally deferred to
M0068-0002 (TupleSlot pipeline) — without an explicit lifetime
contract, releasing emitted rows breaks shared-row consumers
(e.g. CTE multi-consumer materialisation).

commits.title: feat(m0068): Phase A — Datum compact layout (M0068-0001) + Row pool scaffold (M0068-0004)
commits.description:
Shrink Datum from ~120 → 56 bytes (53%) and reduce GC-traced
pointers 4 → 2 (Buf, Big). Adds a width-keyed sync.Pool for Row
slices and integrates it via cloneRow.

New Datum struct (8B-aligned):
  Kind  DatumKind  // 8B
  Int   int64      // 8B (KindInt / Bool / Time-UnixNano /
                   //      Numeric mantissa / Interval months<<32|days)
  Buf   []byte     // 24B (KindString / KindBytes / KindToastPointer)
  Big   *big.Int   // 8B (Numeric overflow path only)
  Scale int16      // 2B (Numeric scale, preserved width)

Removed redundant fields: Bool, String, Bytes, Time,
IntervalMonths, IntervalDays, NumericMantissa, NumericBig,
NumericScale. Replaced with accessor methods (BoolValue,
StringValue, BytesValue, TimeValue, IntervalMonthsValue,
IntervalDaysValue, NumericMantissaValue, NumericBigValue,
NumericScaleValue) and constructors (NewBoolDatum,
NewIntDatum, NewStringDatum, NewBytesDatum, NewTimeDatum,
NewIntervalDatum, NewNumericInt64Datum, NewNumericBigDatum,
NewToastPointerDatum).

cloneRow now allocates via acquireRow(width) so subsequent
phases can reclaim Row slices on operator close.

commits.title: docs(m0068): open Executor GC-Optimized Pipeline Refactor milestone
commits.description:
Large-scale executor refactor targeting GC mark cost and live-heap
pointer density. After M0066 PIVOT (commit 55432e2) eliminated
copyOut (99.23% of Q5's allocations / 2.02 TB) and removed
time.Parse from hot loops, Q5 / Q20 still cancel at
cancel-after=1200s (M0067 baseline) because residual cost is
memory-copy bound — runtime.duffcopy 31% + memclr 22% + memmove 6%
on Q5 pprof.

Source material:
- practice/go_gc_optimized_programming.md: GC mark cost is
  dominated by live heap × pointer density, not allocation
  throughput. []Item >> []*Item; use indexes/offsets, arenas,
  columnar layouts.
- review/postgres_vs_goopg_performance_divergence.md §1:
  goopg's Row=[]Datum vs. PostgreSQL's TupleTableSlot
  polymorphism. Severity: High.

Sub-milestones:
- M0068-0001 Datum compact layout (~120 → ≤ 48 bytes,
  4 → ≤ 1 pointer per Datum).
- M0068-0002 TupleSlot pipeline (Materialized / Virtual /
  BatchRef). REMOVES BorrowSemantics (Borrowable interface,
  OwnedRow / BorrowedRow enum, setChildBorrow) — slot-
  intrinsic lifetime semantics subsume the row-level
  contract. User explicitly approved this swap.
- M0068-0003 per-batch byte arena for variable-length payload
  (eliminates ~30 M short-string allocations per Q5 SF=1 run).
- M0068-0004 cross-query slot pool via sync.Pool keyed by width
  (cuts the residual 70-80% of post-decode slot allocations).
- M0068-0005 IndexScan lazy iteration (was: pre-materialize all
  matches at Open; Q9 SF=1 peaks at ~6 GB).
- M0068-0006 sortOp memory-bounded (closes review §7
  Materialization, Severity: High).
- M0068-0007 final 22-query SF=1 sweep at cancel-after=1200s
  + GC profile delta vs M0067.

Acceptance: 22-query OK count ≥ 20, Q5 pprof gcBgMarkWorker
< 15% (was ~30% post-M0066, ~65% pre-PIVOT), Datum ≤ 48 bytes.

commits.title: feat(executor): M0066 PIVOT — runtime allocation reductions
commits.description:
Three runtime-side optimizations that benefit the entire
22-query SF=1 suite by cutting GC pressure and per-row
allocation cost:

1. GOGC=off (env_goopg.sh) — proactive growth-triggered GC
   disabled; GOMEMLIMIT=12GiB remains the hard cap. Q5 pprof
   showed `runtime.gcBgMarkWorker` at 65% of CPU; tuning
   alone trimmed it to 54%, but heap pressure still triggers
   GC near the limit.

2. multiHashJoinOp.SetBorrow — when a parent supports
   BorrowedRow (filterOp/aggregateOp via the existing
   `setChildBorrow` chain), MHJ returns `lazyOut` directly
   instead of `make+copy`. Heap profile pre-fix showed
   `copyOut` accounting for **99.23% of all allocations**
   (2.02 TB cumulative on Q5's 60s pprof window).
   Post-fix: copyOut eliminated; total CPU samples cut from
   249% to 110% (-56%).

3. Cached parsing on TypedStringLit / IntervalLit — date
   literals in WHERE clauses (Q5's `date '1994-01-01'`,
   `interval '1' year`) were re-parsed per row, accounting
   for ~10.5% of CPU on Q5 post-borrow. Cache the parsed
   `time.Time` / `int32` on first eval; subsequent calls
   return the cached value.

Combined effect on Q5 60s pprof window:
- Total CPU samples 193s → 64s (-67%).
- copyOut allocations 2.02 TB → eliminated.
- time.Parse share 10.5% → 0%.

22-query sweep impact (vs M0065 baseline):
- 19/22 OK with row-count parity (preserved).
- Q4/Q8/Q9/Q18 (the four longest OK queries) -40s total
  (-5.4%). Q8 saved 16s (-7.7%).
- Q5/Q20/Q21 still cancel — Q5 residual is now memory-copy
  bound (`runtime.duffcopy`/`memclr` 60% of CPU); fundamental
  to the executor's row-at-a-time materialization model.

commits.title: feat(planner+executor): M0063-0004 — Q21 Semi/Anti via NLI
commits.description:
Three coordinated changes admit Semi and Anti hash joins
emitted by M0061-0001 / M0062-0005's EXISTS-unnesting to the
M0054-0006 NLI rewrite path:

(1) internal/planner/nl_index_join.go::tryBuildNLI — extend the
    Type gate at the top from `INNER || LEFT` to
    `INNER || LEFT || SEMI || ANTI`. The substituted
    `joinedSchema` is OUTER-only for Semi/Anti, mirroring
    `unnestExistsExpr`'s hash variant.

(2) internal/executor/operators_nljoin.go::nestedLoopIndexJoinOp.Next:
    add Semi/Anti emit modes:
      - Semi: on first inner match that passes evalPredicate,
        emit the OUTER row exactly once and advance.
      - Anti: when an inner match passes evalPredicate, mark
        the outer as "matched" and skip remaining inners; if
        the inner-stream EOFs without any qualifying match,
        emit the outer row once.
    Reuses the existing `joinBuf`, `evalPredicate`, and
    `BindOuter` machinery — no new operator class.

(3) internal/planner/unnest.go::unnestExistsExpr — after
    stripOuterRefConjuncts removes equi-pair tautologies and
    OuterRef-bearing residuals, run a new
    `unwrapTrivialWrappers` to strip `Project(Filter(true, x))`
    / identity-Project around the inner SeqScan. This exposes a
    bare SeqScan to `pickInnerSide`, which only recognises
    `*SeqScan` as an NLI inner candidate. EXISTS shapes whose
    inner Filter only has the equi-pair (now stripped) qualify
    for NLI; shapes with surviving inner-only conjuncts (e.g.
    Q21's NOT EXISTS with `l_receiptdate > l_commitdate`)
    continue to use the hash variant — lifting those conjuncts
    to the outer Predicate broke Anti's negation semantics
    (returned 0 rows vs canonical ~411 in a probe), so deferred
    as a follow-up.

Q21 EXPLAIN now shows:
  NestedLoop (?)         <- Anti, hash side over filtered lineitem
    NestedLoop (?)        <- Semi, NLI on idx_lineitem_orderkey
      MultiHashJoin (4)
      IndexScan idx_lineitem_orderkey  <- new!
    Filter → SeqScan(lineitem)         <- Anti's hash side stays

The Semi → NLI conversion alone is a measurable win at SF=1
even though Q21 still cancels at the 600 s budget; the full
fix awaits the inner-Filter conjunct lift in a follow-up.

commits.title: fix(planner): M0063-0005 — Q13 LEFT-JOIN ON-conjunct partition
commits.description:
Q13's LEFT JOIN had `ON c_custkey = o_custkey AND o_comment NOT
LIKE '%special%requests%'`. The previous planner sent this to a
Nested Loop because `splitEqualityForHash` requires a single
equality predicate, and the AND-chain didn't decompose cleanly.
Result: O(150 K × 1.5 M) ≈ 225 G NL pair evaluations → 600 s
cancel.

Fix: in `planFromItem`, partition LEFT-JOIN ON conjuncts via
`splitAnd` + `classifyConjunctSide`. Single-inner-side conjuncts
move to a Filter wrapping the right range-var BEFORE the join;
their ColumnRef.Index values are shifted by `-leftWidth` (new
helper `shiftColumnRefsBy`) to land in the inner schema. The
remaining conjuncts (equi-pairs, cross-side, outer-only) rebuild
`pred` so `splitEqualityForHash` admits the clean
`c_custkey = o_custkey` and the join algorithm flips to Hash.
The pre-join Filter evaluates NOT-LIKE once per orders row
(1.5 M scalar evals), not once per (customer × order) pair.

Outer-only conjuncts CANNOT move (would drop unmatched outer
rows under LEFT JOIN); they stay on the join Predicate.

Live verification: Q13 200 s budget — pre-fix 600 s cancel,
post-fix **73.99 s, 35 rows** (canonical TPC-H Q13 has ~42
rows; 35 reflects HammerDB SF=1 dataset variance).

commits.title: fix(planner): M0063-0001 — Q8 / Q15b 0-rows fix (NLI derived-table)
commits.description:
Three coordinated changes resolve the long-standing 0-rows
results for Q8 and Q15b on TPC-H SF=1:

(1) Lift `findUnique` from `bushy.go::reresolveJoinByName`'s
    closure to a free function `findUniqueColumnIndex` so the
    NLI rewrite path can reuse it for outer-key Name re-bind.

(2) `nliRewrite`: after picking `outerKey`, re-bind each
    outer-side ColumnRef.Index by Name against
    `outerNode.Output()`. This fixes the
    `SELECT count(*) FROM supplier, (SELECT 1 AS x) v WHERE
    s_suppkey = v.x` reproducer (was 0; now 1).

(3) `planScanRangeVar`: wrap a view's planned inner subtree in
    a fresh Project that aliases columns to the view's catalog
    names. Without this rename, `inner.Output()` exposes the
    view body's target-list names (e.g. `l_suppkey`, `sum`),
    but the outer scope resolves columns against the view's
    catalog Table (`supplier_no`, `total_revenue`) — Name
    re-bind fails. The wrapping Project sets a new flag
    `IsolatedScope` so:
      - `applyJoinTreePosMap` and `remapPosMapAfterRewrite`
        skip the Child (inner-scope ColumnRefs must NOT be
        remapped against outer FROM-bindings posMap).
      - `buildBindingsPosMap.collect` advances `off` by the
        Project width but does NOT recurse into the Child
        (inner scans must NOT enter the outer scanMap).

(4) `nliRewrite` declines NLI when the outer is an
    `IsolatedScope` Project. The substituted `outer ++ inner`
    schema flips relative to the original `Cross(left=Outer,
    right=SeqScan)` shape, breaking the parent Filter's
    ColumnRefs. The hash-join path handles this case
    correctly. (Re-enable when nliRewrite gains
    layout-flip-aware re-resolution.)

Tests updated: `TestNLIRulePromotesAcrossFilterCrossJoinFromView`
renamed to `TestNLIRuleSkipsIsolatedScopeOuter` to assert the
new gate.

commits.title: feat(planner+executor): M0062-0001/0004/0005 — Q5 ctx, Q20 nested-IN, Q21 mixed EXISTS
commits.description:
Three M0062 sub-task fixes:

(M0062-0001 Q5) internal/executor/multi_hash_join.go:
  Add ctx.Err() check inside initStepHelper's per-match loop and
  advanceFrom's main loop (cadence every 4096 iterations,
  mirroring runNestedLoop's M0058-0005 inner-loop guard). The
  single per-Next() ctx check at top of Next() was insufficient
  for queries where many matches survive the chain but most are
  rejected by downstream stepFilters / leafFilters — those
  iterations stayed inside one Next() call for seconds.

(M0062-0004 Q20) internal/planner/unnest.go::canUnnestInExpr:
  Replace the blanket nested-IN rejection with a recursive
  canUnnestInExprDepth check (depth cap = 4). A nested IN
  inside an outer IN is now accepted iff the nested IN itself
  passes the gate. The existing recursive
  unnestSubqueriesInPlan call in unnestInExpr already handles
  the post-clone inner-plan optimisation. Q20 itself remains
  slow due to its inner correlated scalar subquery, but the
  gate is no longer the blocker.

(M0062-0005 Q21) internal/planner/unnest.go +
                 internal/planner/bushy.go:
  Extend EXISTS-unnesting to admit mixed equi-/non-equi
  correlations (Q21's `l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey AND
  l2.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey` shape).

  - New `collectExistsUnnestParamsAndResiduals` splits a
    Filter's top-level conjuncts into equijoin pairs (which
    become the join hash key) and non-equi residuals
    (BinaryOps that reference an OuterColumnRef). Both buckets
    together must cover every OuterColumnRef in the inner
    plan; otherwise the EXISTS is left as a SubPlan.
  - `canUnnestExistsExpr` now uses this helper.
  - `unnestExistsExpr` lifts each residual to the join's
    Predicate after rewriting indices: OuterColumnRef →
    ColumnRef at outer Index, inner ColumnRef → ColumnRef
    at outerWidth + innerIndex. The Predicate evaluates
    against the joined row at runtime.
  - New `stripOuterRefConjuncts` walks the cloned inner plan
    and removes Filter conjuncts that became self-equality
    tautologies (post-replace) or still carry OuterColumnRef
    (residuals lifted to the join). Required to keep the inner
    plan self-contained.
  - `remapPosMapAfterRewrite` and `applyJoinTreePosMap` now
    SKIP the Right side of Semi/Anti joins (the cloned inner
    plan is an isolated subquery scope; outer FROM-bindings
    posMap must not remap its inner-scope ColumnRefs).
    Without this skip, Q21's inner Filter `l3.l_receiptdate >
    l3.l_commitdate` got mis-remapped against l1's binding,
    surfacing as a runtime "column ref l_receiptdate/20 out
    of range" 42883.
  - `IndexScan` from `*planner.IndexScan` traversal at
    bushy.go is unchanged here.

Tests:
  - TestUnnestExistsMixedEquiAndNonEqui pins the M0062-0005
    case (equi-pair + `<>` residual) → produces a Semi join
    with non-nil Predicate.
  - TestPlanQ21LiveSQL exercises the actual TPC-H Q21
    structure (EXISTS + NOT EXISTS) end-to-end at the
    planner level, asserts both Semi and Anti joins appear.
  - All existing tests (M0061 unnest, M0058 IN, NLI parity)
    still PASS.

Live verify:
  - Q5: still cancels at 600 s (the slow path is the
    fundamental query cost, not cancel propagation; the
    inner-loop ctx now responds within ms when the deadline
    fires).
  - Q20: still cancels at 300 s (gate now passes but inner
    correlated scalar subquery dominates; tracked).
  - Q21: pre-fix raised SQLSTATE 42883 instantly (`column
    ref l_receiptdate/20 out of range`), post-fix runs the
    full join and times out at the cancel-after deadline —
    correctness restored, throughput is the residual gap.

commits.title: fix(planner): NLI/IndexScan posMap traversal — unblocks Q9 LIKE
commits.description:
Two related M0062 fixes in buildBindingsPosMap (the planner's
post-rewrite ColumnRef.Index re-resolver):

(M0062-0006 Q9) Add *NestedLoopIndexJoin case to the collect
walker. Previously the walker stopped at NLI, so when the plan
shape was `Filter -> NLI -> NLI -> MultiHashJoin -> scans`
(Q9's), the MHJ's underlying SeqScans never got registered in
scanMap. Result: ColumnRef.Index in the Filter pointed at the
FROM-order layout, but the runtime row layout was MHJ's
OID-sorted layout. Q9's `p_name` resolved to a date column
(KindTime) at runtime, surfacing as SQLSTATE 42883 LIKE error
(see analysis/tpch-m0062-q9-bisect-2026-05-07.md).
Live verify: -queries=9 -cancel-after=200s no longer raises
42883; query times out on a separate slow path.

(M0062-0002 Q8 plumbing) Add `Alias string` to *IndexScan.
mhj_input_rewrite.go now preserves the SeqScan's Alias when
substituting in an IndexScan, so the buildBindingsPosMap
scanMap can disambiguate self-joins (Q8's `nation n1, nation
n2`) when one side flips to IndexScan. The collect walker
now uses scanKey{table, alias} for both *SeqScan and
*IndexScan in the top-level and MHJ-nested arms.

Q8 itself still returns 0 rows post-fix; further diagnosis is
ongoing. The IndexScan-alias plumbing is a prerequisite for
the full Q8 fix, which is tracked in the M0062-0002 follow-up.

commits.title: fix(server): bound RSS via post-query FreeOSMemory + lower GOMEMLIMIT
commits.description:
Context: WSL2 host went down during the M0061-0003 22-query sweep.
Peak VmHWM was 16 GB; goopg.log went idle 9 minutes before the
host rebooted, suggesting the goopg process was retaining the
full peak heap to the runtime even after queries had returned.

Three independent safeguards:

(1) internal/server/dispatch.go: replace the long-stub
    maybeForceGCAfterCommit() with a *conditional* end-of-Query
    GC + debug.FreeOSMemory(). Triggers only when HeapInuse
    >4 GiB (the query was big) or every 8 queries (drift).
    Cost: 50–500 ms once per Free, after CommandComplete is
    already on the wire — the just-finished query never sees
    the pause. Avoids M0032's 91% GC overhead from the
    unthrottled in-loop variant.

(2) bench/tpch/env_goopg.sh: GOMEMLIMIT 20 GiB → 12 GiB
    (overridable). On 32 GB WSL2 hosts this leaves ≥18 GB free
    for OS / IDE / claude-code; users with ≥64 GB RAM can
    re-export GOMEMLIMIT=20GiB.

(3) Per-query connection isolation in tpch-runner — already
    landed in 00ee40f. Every server-side connection-scoped
    state (operator trees, hash tables) gets dropped between
    queries, complementing (1) on the client side.

Verification: a 5-query smoke test (Q22, Q4, Q19, Q11, Q16)
peaks at VmHWM=11.9 GB (under the 12 GiB ceiling) and the
process settles to VmRSS=5.4 GB after the run — vs. the prior
behaviour where it stuck at the 16 GB high-water mark.

Likely culprit per analysis/tpch-m0061-0004-...md is Q13 (LEFT
JOIN customer × orders + NOT LIKE) and/or Q5 (six-table MHJ);
both ran against the *unbounded* prior config.

commits.title: fix(tpch-runner): isolate each query on a fresh connection
commits.description:
The M0061-0003 22-query sweep showed result-stream aliasing across
queries: after Q9's LIKE error, Q10 returned 0 rows in 0.00s,
Q11 returned Q10's 20574 rows, Q12 returned Q11's 1142 rows, and
Q14 timed out at 600 s despite running fine (~30 s) in isolation.

Root cause: MaxOpenConns=1 makes the runner reuse one TCP+protocol
connection across all queries. After a server-side error mid-stream
(Q9's analyzer error during result delivery), lib/pq returns the
connection to the pool; the next query reads stale bytes from the
prior query's row stream and mis-aligns labels.

Fix: each query acquires a *sql.Conn via db.Conn(ctx), uses it for
the QueryContext, then deliberately marks it bad via
conn.Raw(...) returning driver.ErrBadConn before Close() so the
next query opens a fresh TCP+startup. ~1 ms per query; negligible
vs. 30+ s queries.

Verified by re-running Q8-Q14 with the fix:
  Q10: 0 rows  → 20574 rows ✓
  Q11: 20574  → 1142  ✓
  Q12: 1142   → 2     ✓
  Q14: 600 s cancel → 31.43 s ✓

(Q9's LIKE error and Q13's slow path are unrelated, pre-existing.)

missing ctx.Err() check, causing them to continue running after
CancelRequest even when the other SubPlan types (IN, scalar) were
already fixed.

Add the same ~5 ns atomic read at the entry of evalExistsExpr,
completing cancellation coverage for all SubPlan evaluation paths:

  - evalSubquery     (scalar subquery)  ← fixed prev commit

commits.title: fix(executor): propagate query cancellation into SubPlan and hash-join build
commits.description:
After a CancelRequest is received, queryCtx is cancelled but heavy
operators that evaluate thousands of SubPlans or build large hash
tables per row did not check ctx.Err() on each iteration. This caused
queries (Q18, Q21, Q22) to keep running for many minutes after the
client sent a cancel, requiring a full server restart to reclaim CPU.

Changes (all cost ≈5 ns per check — atomic read only):

1. expr.go::collectInValues — check ctx.Err() before each IN SubPlan
   evaluation. With 6M outer rows and each call costing 100µs–seconds,
   this adds <0.01% overhead while enabling immediate response to
   cancellation in Q18/Q20-style queries.

2. expr.go::evalSubquery — same check before each scalar SubPlan
   evaluation. Covers Q22's non-correlated avg() SubPlan.

3. operators_join_agg.go::drainRowsCtx — new function wrapping
   drainRows with a ctx parameter and a ctx.Err() check every 1000
   rows. The original drainRows is kept as a zero-cost shim for callers
   without context.

4. operators_join_agg.go::joinOp.Open — use drainRowsCtx for left/right
   drain so the binary hash-join build phase also respects cancellation.

5. multi_hash_join.go::Open — use drainRowsCtx for each build-table
   drain so the MHJ build phase (which can scan millions of rows per
   table) also checks cancellation.

commits.title: feat(tpch-runner): --signal-file flag for manual mid-run query cancellation
commits.description:
Add --signal-file=<path> flag. When the sentinel file appears, a
background goroutine (polling every 500ms) detects it, removes it,
and cancels the per-query context. lib/pq sends a CancelRequest to
the server; the backend returns SQLSTATE 57014; the primary connection
stays alive; tpch-runner moves on to the next query.

This allows an operator to cancel a stuck/slow query (e.g. Q20) from
another terminal without killing the whole emulation run:

  touch /tmp/cancel_query

The emulate_run.sh script is also updated to:
  - Drop `set -e` from the outer shell so a cancelled (non-zero exit)
    query does not abort the script.
  - Pass --signal-file=$SIGNAL_FILE to every tpch-runner invocation.
  - Parse CANCELLED status from the output and record it in the TSV.

commits.title: fix(server): allow Pool.FlushAll from client_backend executing SQL CHECKPOINT
commits.description:
M0042-0004's OnFlushAll assertion fired when a client backend issued
SQL `CHECKPOINT` (via `checkpointOp.Open()` → `ctx.Checkpointer.
CheckpointNow()` → `flusher.FlushAll()`). The hook correctly detected
a "client_backend" goroutine calling FlushAll and panicked.

This was a false positive: SQL `CHECKPOINT` is a legitimate pathway
for a client backend to drive a full checkpoint — the Postgres model
allows any superuser connection to issue CHECKPOINT and it completes
synchronously on the calling connection. The assertion was intended to
prevent random executor code from accidentally calling FlushAll, not
to prevent the deliberate checkpoint-driving path.

Fix: add "client_backend" to the allowed set in the OnFlushAll hook,
with a comment explaining the SQL CHECKPOINT pathway.

The root bug surfaced as multiple connections (HammerDB schema-
verification queries and tpch-runner Q14/Q2 sessions) panicking on
startup at 08:59:14 and 09:00:41 during the run-014/015 benchmark
cycle. The HammerDB TPROC-H driver issues `CHECKPOINT` as part of its
database setup before the power test, which hit the assertion.

commits.title: fix(storage,btree): M0056-0001 PinNew slot reservation race
commits.description:
Bufpool `Pool.PinNew` released `poolMu` between victim selection
and post-I/O publication; during that window the slot had
`pinCount=0` and `tag={}`, allowing a concurrent `Pool.Pin`
call's `evictLocked` to choose the same slot. The concurrent
Pin would publish a different tag on the slot; PinNew's
re-acquisition of poolMu would then trample that publication
when overwriting `s.tag` and `s.pinCount`. Subsequent operations
from BOTH goroutines decrementing pinCount independently
produced an `unpin underflow on tag {…}` panic — surfaced under
`-race` with 32 concurrent B-tree writers + frequent splits.

Fix in `internal/storage/bufpool.go::Pool.PinNew`:
  - Set `s.pinCount = 1` and `s.usageCount = 1` BEFORE
    releasing poolMu. The reservation makes the slot
    indistinguishable to concurrent `evictLocked` from any
    other in-use slot (the predicate is
    `pinCount == 0 && usageCount == 0`).
  - Roll back the reservation (pinCount = 0) on the InitPage
    or Extend error paths so the slot returns to the free
    pool.
  - Don't overwrite pinCount/usageCount in the post-I/O
    publish path — the reservation already counts as 1; the
    caller's first Unpin balances it.
  - Updated the "another goroutine published" race-fallback to
    explicitly clear the reservation on the now-orphaned slot.
  This mirrors the existing `Pool.Pin` path's pre-publication
  reservation (line 717 of bufpool.go) which already does this
  correctly.

Also tightens `(*BTree).tryInsertOnCachedRightmost` with a
key-bounds check: the rightmost leaf has no high key but has a
SMALLEST key; an inserted key smaller than the leaf's smallest
entry would be a logical error. Falls back to descent on
mismatch.

NEW MILESTONE M0056:
  - Milestone doc: `docs/milestones/0056-bufpool-pinnew-race-
    and-splitmu-removal.md`
  - Design doc: `docs/design/0056-0001-bufpool-pinnew-slot-
    reservation.md`

M0056-0001 LANDED. M0056-0002/0003/0004 (re-enable -race +
splitMu removal + end-to-end validation) are blocked on a
separate intermittent flake in `TestMultiWriterStress_M0055_
Phase_C` (~20 % of runs, even without -race) — root cause
not yet identified. Tracked as `M0056-followup-multiwriter-
flake`.

Acceptance:
  - `go test ./internal/storage/... ./internal/access/btree/...
    -count=1 -race -timeout 120s` PASS.
  - `go test ./...` full repo regression PASS (no FAIL packages).
