commits.title: m0021: tuple-level locking step 4 — multi-holder FOR SHARE via lockmgr modes
commits.description:
Fixes the hidden bug where two concurrent SELECT FOR SHARE
sessions on the same row serialised because lockRowsOp.stampLock
acquired ExclusiveLock regardless of strength. Achieves
PostgreSQL's "multiple FOR SHARE holders coexist" semantics
WITHOUT introducing MultiXact infrastructure: the lockmgr's
existing conflict matrix already supplies what we need —
RowShareLock is compatible with itself and conflicts with
ExclusiveLock.

New lockRowsOp.tupleLockMode():

  - FOR UPDATE  (HeapXmaxExclLock)   → ExclusiveLock
  - FOR SHARE   (HeapXmaxShrLock)    → RowShareLock
  - FOR KEY SHARE (HeapXmaxKeyShrLock) → RowShareLock

UPDATE / DELETE foreign-lock detection in scanMatching keeps
ExclusiveLock so it conflicts with both shared and exclusive
holders, blocking until ALL of them release.

Transaction-scoped ReleaseAll(backendID) via the existing
dispatch.go hook cleans every holder up at commit/abort. No
MultiXact registry required for v0.

On-page xmax limitation noted: with multiple holders, the
second session's stamp overwrites the first's xmax bytes.
Harmless because (a) mvcc.TupleVisible short-circuits on
HeapXmaxLockOnly without consulting xmax value, (b) lockmgr
tracks each holder by backend ID independently, (c) WAL
records each emission's (xid, lockStrength) separately. The
remaining gap — accurate post-crash holder-set reconstruction
— is what MultiXact would solve; v0 defers because the
lockmgr's transaction-scoped state is in-memory only so all
locks are lost on crash anyway.

New TestForShareCompatibleMultipleHolders:

- Two sessions concurrently take FOR SHARE on the same row;
  second succeeds without blocking. Verifies both backends
  appear as holders via lm.Holders(tag).
- A third session UPDATE on the same row blocks waiting for
  BOTH holders, and unblocks only after both ReleaseAll fires
  — pins the conflict-with-shared semantics.

Full go test ./... green; race-mode targeted runs across
executor + lockmgr all green.

Lock-strength promotion (FOR SHARE → FOR UPDATE upgrade) +
persistent MultiXact identifier in xmax + tuple-level
NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED + streaming per-row stamping + pg_locks
introspection all stay deferred.

Design doc: docs/design/0021-0011-tuple-locking-for-share-multi-holder.md.

commits.title: m0021: tuple-level locking step 2d — UPDATE/DELETE via IndexScan path
commits.description:
Closes the seqScan-only restriction on the write side. UPDATE
and DELETE WHERE indexed_col = key now route through an
IndexScan-shaped plan node; the executor's
extractScanAndPredicate consumes both the new shape and the
historic Filter(SeqScan) one without losing the per-tuple
foreign-lock detection from step 2b.

planUpdate / planDelete: mirror planSelect's
planIndexScanFromWhere arm. When `WHERE indexed_col = key`
matches the single-column-equality shape with a constant /
param rhs, the planner picks IndexScan; otherwise falls
through to Filter(SeqScan). ctx.cat = cat set on the
singleBindingContext so subquery resolution inside the index
key works.

extractScanAndPredicate: extended to accept *planner.IndexScan
and *planner.Filter wrapping IndexScan. New indexScanPredicate
synthesises a `<indexed_col> = key` equality predicate — lhs
is a fresh ColumnRef pointing at the table's output ordinal for
the indexed column; rhs is the IndexScan's already-resolved
Key. Filter(IndexScan) ANDs the outer predicate with the
synthesised key predicate.

The runtime's scanMatching is inherently sequential — treating
IndexScan as "SeqScan with a synthesised key predicate" is
correct (the predicate filters the same tuples the index would
have probed) but doesn't exploit the index for fast access.
That optimisation is a separate follow-up; the point of this
slice is to lift the executor restriction so the planner is
free to emit IndexScan plans for UPDATE/DELETE.

Crucially, scanMatching's per-tuple foreign-lock detection
from step 2b is unchanged: every tuple the seq-scan visits
(including those passing the synthesised `=` predicate) goes
through lockedByForeign + acquireTupleLock. UPDATE WHERE
indexed_col against a row a SELECT FOR UPDATE holds still
blocks at the lockmgr.

Tests:
- TestUpdateViaIndexScanPath — UPDATE rewrite produces the
  same observable outcome as the pre-IndexScan SeqScan-only
  path.
- TestUpdateViaIndexScanBlocksOnForeignTupleLock — multi-
  session blocking still fires when UPDATE picks IndexScan;
  pins that the IndexScan promotion didn't bypass step 2b's
  tuple-tag waiting.

Full go test ./... green; race-mode targeted runs across
executor + planner all green.

Index-driven UPDATE/DELETE optimisation (probe instead of
seq-scan) + tuple-level NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED through UPDATE/DELETE
+ MultiXact multi-holder support + streaming per-row stamping
all remain deferred.

Design doc: docs/design/0021-0010-tuple-locking-index-update-path.md.

commits.title: m0021: tuple-level locking step 2c — IndexScan leaf support
commits.description:
Closes the seqScan-only restriction from step 2a. SELECT FOR
UPDATE WHERE indexed_col routed through the planner's IndexScan
path now stamps per-row lock-only xmax instead of falling
through to relation-level-only locking.

indexScanOp grew a parallel tids []storage.ItemPointer slice
populated in the btree.RangeScan callback alongside rows. New
currentTID() returns the just-emitted row's TID via
o.tids[o.idx-1] — mirrors seqScanOp's curSlot-1 post-fetch
convention.

New currentTIDProvider interface unifies seqScanOp /
indexScanOp; findSeqScan is replaced with findScanLeaf that
walks past Project / Filter wrappers and returns either leaf
type. lockRowsOp.scan field type changed from *seqScanOp to
currentTIDProvider; the rest of the two-pass drain-then-stamp
flow is untouched.

New TestLockRowsStampsLockOnlyXmaxIndexScan creates a unique
index on items.id, runs SELECT id FROM items WHERE id=2 FOR
UPDATE so the planner picks IndexScan, reads the heap page
back and verifies exactly one tuple (id=2) has xmax +
HeapXmaxLockOnly stamped — pins the per-row stamping property
regardless of whether the executor reached the row via SeqScan
or IndexScan.

Full go test ./... green; race-mode targeted executor runs
green.

UPDATE/DELETE-via-IndexScan stays out of scope —
extractScanAndPredicate requires Filter(SeqScan) and an
index-driven UPDATE plan would error before the lock-detection
logic runs. Tuple-level NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED + MultiXact +
streaming stamping all remain deferred.

Design doc: docs/design/0021-0009-tuple-locking-indexscan-leaf.md.

commits.title: m0021: tuple-level locking step 2b — blocking enforcement
commits.description:
Closes the gap between steps 1/2a/3 (data on the page) and
actual blocking. Concurrent UPDATE / DELETE now waits in the
lockmgr until a SELECT FOR UPDATE holder releases its tuple
lock at commit / abort.

lockmgr.LockTag grew Block + Offset uint32 fields. Both zero is
the historic relation-level tag (every existing caller
continues to work via Go's struct-literal zero-initialisation);
both non-zero is the new tuple-level tag. The two are
independent map keys so RowExclusiveLock at relation doesn't
accidentally block tuple-level acquirers. Mirrors upstream's
LOCKTAG_RELATION / LOCKTAG_TUPLE separation.

tupleLockTag(rel, ItemPointer) shifts Block/Offset by +1 when
packing so a tuple at (block=0, slot=0) doesn't alias the
relation tag (block=0, offset=0). Slot 0 is invalid in heap
line-pointer convention so this is defence-in-depth.

Context.acquireTupleLock / tryAcquireTupleLock mirror the
relation-lock SQLSTATE mappings (40P01 deadlock, 57014 cancel,
55P03 NOWAIT lock-unavailable, XX000 fallback).

lockRowsOp.stampLock now acquires ExclusiveLock on the tuple
tag BEFORE the xmax stamp — registers the holder so concurrent
UPDATE/DELETE can queue.

scanMatching captures `lockedBy` per match at scan time. When
the tuple's xmax has HEAP_XMAX_LOCK_ONLY set AND xmax !=
currentXID, lockedBy holds the locker's xid; otherwise zero.
After the page RLock/Unpin release, the dispatch loop fires
acquireTupleLock per locked-by match, blocking until the
locker's ReleaseAll at commit/abort.

PageSetHeapTupleXmax extended to clear HeapXmaxLockOnly +
HeapXmaxLockMask infomask bits on stamp. Without this fix the
locker's tuple-lock metadata leaks into our deleter's xmax
bytes and mvcc.TupleVisible's lock-only short-circuit would
mistake the just-stamped xmax for a still-locked tuple,
keeping the tuple visible after a real DELETE.

New TestUpdateBlocksOnForeignTupleLock multi-session test:
seeds rows under a committed xact (so subsequent xacts see
them live), runs SELECT id FOR UPDATE in session 1 + UPDATE
on the same row in session 2's goroutine, asserts session 2
registers as a waiter on the +1-shifted tuple tag, releases
session 1's holdings via ReleaseAll, confirms session 2
wakes and completes.

Full go test ./... green; race-mode targeted runs across
executor / lockmgr / storage / wal / initdb / mvcc all green.

IndexScan blocking + tuple-level NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED + MultiXact
multi-holder FOR SHARE + streaming-stamping refactor + pg_locks
introspection + multi-clause lock-strength merge all stay
deferred.

commits.title: m0021: tuple-level locking step 2a — producer wiring
commits.description:
The producer side of tuple-level pessimistic locking. SELECT FOR
UPDATE now stamps each yielded row's underlying heap tuple with
xmax = ctx.Tx.XID + HEAP_XMAX_LOCK_ONLY + a lock-strength bit,
and emits the xl_heap_lock WAL record so crash recovery can
re-apply it.

storage/bufpool.go: New LogHeapLockFunc type + logHeapLock field
+ Pool.LogHeapLock() accessor + PoolConfig.LogHeapLock field.
Mirrors the existing LogHeapInsert / LogHeapDelete /
LogHeapVacuum pattern; nil disables the optimisation and
MarkDirtyChangeRecord falls back to FPI emission for crash
safety.

initdb/open.go: Wires a logHeapLock closure that calls
wal.EncodeHeapLock + walWriter.Append, parallel to its
logHeapDelete / logHeapVacuum siblings.

executor/operators_storage.go: New seqScanOp.currentTID() exposes
(rel, ItemPointer) of the most recently returned row by reading
curBlock + (curSlot - 1) — curSlot is incremented post-fetch so
the slot of the row Next() just returned is curSlot - 1.

executor/operators_lockrows.go: switched to two-pass
drain-then-stamp protocol. seqScanOp holds the page's RLock
continuously across multiple Next() calls (RUnlock fires only at
page exhaustion / Close), so the slot's write Lock() for
stamping would deadlock against the scan's reader. First Next()
drains the child chain capturing (rel, ItemPointer, row) per row
inline (TID captured between child.Next() returns and the next
child.Next() call so seqScan's curBlock/curSlot is
authoritative), then after EOF — when seqScan has released all
page RLocks via releasePinned — runs the stamp pass: pin page,
Lock, PageSetHeapTupleLockOnly, MarkDirtyChangeRecord
(LogHeapLock), Unlock, Unpin. Subsequent Next() yields from the
buffer until EOF. Memory cost = result set size; SELECT FOR
UPDATE typically targets a small range so this is acceptable
for Stage A. Per-row streaming stamping needs a seqScanOp
Pin/RLock-per-row refactor and is deferred.

findSeqScan(op) walks past projectOp / filterOp wrappers to
surface the leaf seqScanOp; nil return (IndexScan, Values,
CTEScan) falls through to pass-through Next with only
relation-level lock applied.

Lock-strength selection: o.plan.Locks[0].Strength →
HeapXmaxExclLock for FOR UPDATE, HeapXmaxShrLock for FOR SHARE.
Multi-clause merge under strongest-wins deferred.

New test TestLockRowsStampsTupleLockOnlyXmax runs SELECT id FROM
items FOR UPDATE end-to-end through parser→analyzer→planner
→executor and verifies the heap page bytes after: every yielded
row carries Xmax == ctx.Tx.XID + HeapXmaxLockOnly +
HeapXmaxExclLock bits in infomask.

Full go test ./... green.

INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE detection of foreign lock-only xmax (the
actual blocking enforcement) + IndexScan currentTID twin +
MultiXact-aware multi-holder support + streaming-stamping
refactor + pg_locks introspection all stay deferred.

commits.title: tooling: add safe ralph state auto-repair mode
m0021: tuple-level locking step 3 — xl_heap_lock WAL record + replay
commits.description:
Pure-additive WAL record-kind for row-lock crash recovery, sequel
to step 1's storage primitives. No producer yet — the executor
wiring (lockRowsOp emitting HeapLock through ctx.Pool.LogHeapLock
parallel to LogHeapInsert / LogHeapDelete) is the next slice.

New RecordKindHeapLock=10 + 22-byte payload format:

  kind(1) | DBOid(4) | RelOid(4) | Fork(1) | Block(4) |
  LineSlot(2) | Xmax(4) | LockStrength(2) = 22 bytes

LockStrength carries the HeapXmax* mode bits to OR into the
tuple's infomask alongside HEAP_XMAX_LOCK_ONLY.

New EncodeHeapLock / DecodeHeapLock — decoder validates the
kind byte and payload length so a stray payload from another
record kind errors instead of silently constructing nonsense
ItemPointer / xmax values.

replayHeapLock(mgr, r) mirrors replayHeapDelete: validate the
block exists / page is initialised, idempotency via pd_lsn
(re-replay no-ops when MustHeader(page).LSN() >= r.EndLSN), call
the step-1 PageSetHeapTupleLockOnly, stamp pd_lsn, write back.

ApplyRecord switch grew a case for the new kind so missing
dispatch surfaces in tests.

Logical decoder's Classify intentionally skips lock records —
locking a row doesn't change replicated data, so apply workers
shouldn't see lock events. The classifier's trailing
default-skip comment covers the new kind without code change.

Tests in recovery_test.go: 5 scenarios — round-trip, wrong-kind
reject, idempotent replay pinning xmax + LockOnly + ExclLock
infomask bits + pd_lsn second-replay-no-op, missing-block
reject, ApplyRecord-routes-the-new-kind.

Full go test ./... green.

commits.title: m0021: tuple-level locking step 1 — storage primitives + MVCC hook
commits.description:
Foundation slice for per-row pessimistic locking that unlocks
blocking on UPDATE/DELETE against a row another xact holds via
SELECT FOR UPDATE, plus SKIP LOCKED's "silently drop contended
rows" semantics. Pure additive — no production callers yet;
executor wiring lands in subsequent slices.

New infomask flag-bit constants in internal/storage/heap.go
mirror upstream's htup_details.h byte-for-byte (HeapXmaxInvalid,
HeapXmaxCommitted, HeapXmaxLockOnly, HeapXmaxKeyShrLock,
HeapXmaxExclLock + composite HeapXmaxShrLock / HeapXmaxLockMask).
New predicate IsHeapTupleLockOnly(infomask) mirrors upstream's
HEAP_XMAX_IS_LOCKED_ONLY macro.

New PageSetHeapTupleLockOnly(p, slot, xmax, lockStrength)
companion to the existing xmax-delete stamper. Stamps xmax +
sets HeapXmaxLockOnly + sets the chosen lock-strength bit;
clears stale lock-strength bits and HeapXmaxInvalid before
OR-ing new bits in (so a re-stamp KeyShr→Excl doesn't
accumulate stale bits). Zero lockStrength rejected (would yield
"lock-only with unknown mode" corruption upstream's cleanup
paths can't interpret). Layout note: Infomask is at on-disk
bytes 20..21 (Infomask2 18..19, Hoff 22) — order swapped
relative to HeapTupleHeader struct field order; the helper
writes 20..21 to match MarshalBinary / ParseHeapTuple.

mvcc.TupleVisible learns the lock-only branch. When xmax has
HeapXmaxLockOnly set the tuple stays visible regardless of
holder progress (committed / aborted / in-progress), including
the self-lock case (Xmin == Xmax == currentXID + LOCK_ONLY)
which the pre-existing rule treated as "deleted by current
xact". Mirrors upstream's HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC handling. The
crucial property: a SELECT FOR UPDATE that stamps a row's xmax
must NOT make the row invisible to concurrent readers or to
itself on a re-scan within the same statement.

Tests: 4 storage tests + 2 mvcc tests covering normal usage,
stale-strength clearing on re-stamp, API misuse guards, and
the regression that plain committed deletes (no LOCK_ONLY bit)
remain invisible.

Full go test ./... green.

commits.title: m0021: NOWAIT runtime + SKIP LOCKED gate (M0021-0004)
commits.description:
Promotes SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT from the M0021-0003 0A000
reject to a working runtime at the relation-coarse layer.

New lockmgr.TryAcquire(b, t, m) non-blocking acquire path +
typed sentinel ErrLockNotAvailable — byte-identical to Acquire's
synchronous fast path (idempotent re-grant; FIFO-fair grant when
no waiters and no conflict) but returns the sentinel instead of
queueing on contention. Locks granted via TryAcquire are tracked
in the same state as Acquire's and released identically by
Release / ReleaseAll.

New Context.tryAcquireRelLock mirrors acquireRelLock for the
non-blocking variant; maps ErrLockNotAvailable → SQLSTATE 55P03
(upstream's canonical "could not obtain lock" code; message says
"relation" not "row" because goopg's locking is relation-coarse
today).

lockRowsOp.Open dispatches by WaitPolicy:

  - Block → acquireRelLock (unchanged from M0021-0003).
  - NoWait → tryAcquireRelLock.
  - SkipLocked → 0A000 with a specific "tuple-level pessimistic
    locking is the deferred follow-up" message. At relation-
    coarse granularity SKIP LOCKED's "silently drop contended
    rows" semantics can't be implemented (would either produce
    surprising empty results or be a no-op).

Observability counters (lock_wait_count / lock_wait_time /
pg_locks introspection) also deferred — every lock wait on
SELECT FOR UPDATE today is a single relation-level wait, not
the per-row contention pattern users care about. Counters land
alongside tuple-level locking infrastructure.

Tests in operators_lockrows_test.go: 3 new scenarios —
TestLockRowsNoWaitSucceedsUncontended (replaces the previous
NOWAIT-rejected test from M0021-0003),
TestLockRowsNoWaitFailsOnContention (multi-backend
ExclusiveLock blocker → 55P03 without waiting),
TestLockRowsRejectsSkipLocked (0A000 stable diagnostic).

Pre-existing TestLockRowsBlocksOnExclusiveLock was updated to
seed BEFORE wiring the lockmgr so the seed-insert's
RowExclusiveLock doesn't itself block the test's
ExclusiveLock blocker — a latent test-ordering bug that
surfaced when adding the new NOWAIT contention test.

Full go test ./... green.

commits.title: m0021: Stage A row-lock executor — relation-level RowShareLock (M0021-0003)
commits.description:
Runtime for the planner-emitted *planner.LockRows. New lockRowsOp
in internal/executor/operators_lockrows.go: Open() acquires
RowShareLock on each LockedRel.Table via Context.acquireRelLock,
then opens the child. Next()/Close() pass through.

Mirrors upstream — both FOR UPDATE and FOR SHARE take
RowShareLock at the relation level. RowShareLock conflicts with
ExclusiveLock and AccessExclusiveLock (DROP TABLE / ALTER TABLE /
VACUUM FULL) so schema changes can't yank the table out from
under a running SELECT FOR UPDATE. Compatible with
RowExclusiveLock so concurrent UPDATEs/DELETEs proceed unblocked
at the relation level — tuple-level row-blocking is the deferred
follow-up "Tuple-level pessimistic locking on top of M0012 lock
manager" item.

Open pre-pass acquires every lock first then opens the child —
alternative (lazy on first Next) would let SELECT see rows it
might still get blocked from later, matches upstream's
ExecLockRows placement.

Locks are transaction-scoped — released by
LockMgr.ReleaseAll(backendID) in dispatch.go at commit/rollback,
mirrors the existing relation-lock lifecycle.

Stage A scope guard: lockRowsOp.Open rejects non-Block
WaitPolicies with 0A000 so unmigrated runtime never silently
downgrades NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED to default-blocking.

Deadlock detection from M0012 just works — ErrDeadlockDetected
flows through acquireRelLock to surface as 40P01.

Tests in operators_lockrows_test.go: 4 scenarios — basic FOR
UPDATE acquires RowShareLock end-to-end, FOR SHARE same, NOWAIT
rejected with 0A000, multi-session blocking on ExclusiveLock
verified by spawning a goroutine, asserting it waits, releasing
the blocker, and confirming completion.

NOWAIT / SKIP LOCKED runtime + observability counters + tuple-
level pessimistic locking all stay deferred.

Full go test ./... green.

commits.title: m0021: row-lock planner metadata + LockRows plan node (M0021-0002)
commits.description:
Produces an executable plan node carrying the resolved per-
relation locking intent. The planner wraps the SELECT plan tree
in a LockRows node when the SELECT carries any FOR UPDATE / FOR
SHARE clause; pre-M0021 SELECTs never produce LockRows so
existing tests stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

New plan-side types in internal/planner/plan.go:

  - LockStrength enum (ForUpdate=iota+1, ForShare; zero
    reserved per the M0017 OnConflictNone precedent).
  - LockWaitPolicy enum (Block, NoWait, SkipLocked).
  - LockedRel (Table + Alias + Strength + WaitPolicy).
  - LockRows wrapper node with Child + Locks. Output()
    returns the child schema unchanged.

planSelect ends with a Project node as before. When
s.Locking != nil we wrap the Project in a LockRows carrying the
resolved Locks slice — last step so all per-clause work lives
below it (matches upstream's "LockRows at the top" placement).

resolveLockedRels(s, ctx) walks each parsed clause:

  - Empty Targets (bare FOR UPDATE) → one LockedRel per binding.
  - Non-empty Targets → one LockedRel per name via
    findBindingByName (alias-shadows-table, mirrors the
    analyzer's matcher).

Multiple clauses targeting the same rel produce duplicate
LockedRels; Stage A executor will fold them under strongest-
wins when it lands.

Executor: case *planner.LockRows in Build returns
"row-level locking execution is not supported in v0 (Stage A
executor lands in M0021-0003)" — two-step gate from
M0017-0002→0003: planner produces full plan so EXPLAIN works,
Build refuses to silently drop locking intent at runtime.

EXPLAIN: describePlan returns "LockRows"; planChildren returns
the wrapped Child so tree-recursion produces the inner plan
under the label.

all bind paths and the rollout guardrail.

commits.title: m0021: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE analyzer wiring (M0021-0001 step 2)
commits.description:
analyzeLockingClauses runs at the tail of analyzeSelectWithParent
when len(s.Locking) > 0. Mirrors upstream's transformLockingClause
/ preprocess_rowmarks rejection set:

  - Must have FROM — SELECT 1 FOR UPDATE → 0A000
    "FOR UPDATE/SHARE is not allowed in this context".
  - No GROUP BY / HAVING — aggregation produces grouped rows that
    don't map back to individual storage tuples; both → 0A000.
  - OF target resolution — each name must match a FROM-clause
    range variable by alias (when set) or by bare table name;
    mismatch → 42P01 "relation not in FROM".

lockingTargetMatches uses the alias-shadows-table rule (when
rel.alias != "" we ONLY check alias — matches upstream column-
reference rules; FROM pgbench_accounts a hides the bare table
name from `OF pgbench_accounts`).

Wait-policy modifiers (NOWAIT, SKIP LOCKED) accepted at analyze
time for AST stability across stages — planner/executor narrow
the supported runtime subset later.

the multi-clause shape.

subqueries deferred — neither has a clean predicate in the

commits.title: m0021: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE parser surface and AST (M0021-0001 step 1)
commits.description:
Parser-only additive slice mirroring the M0016-0001 / M0017-0001 /
M0018-0001 step-1 pattern. SelectStmt.Locking is empty for every
pre-M0021 SELECT so existing tests stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

New AST:

  - LockStrength enum: ForUpdate (iota+1) / ForShare. Zero value
    reserved (mirrors M0017's OnConflictNone).
  - LockWaitPolicy enum: Block / NoWait / SkipLocked.
  - LockingClause: Strength + Targets ([]string) + WaitPolicy.

New keywords: KwShare / KwOf / KwNowait / KwSkip / KwLocked
(KwFor / KwUpdate already exist).

parseLockingClause is called in a for-loop after the
LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH branch in parseSelect so multiple clauses
collect in source order — upstream allows
`FOR UPDATE OF a NOWAIT FOR SHARE OF b`. OF list captured as raw
identifiers; alias/table-name resolution against the FROM list
is the analyzer's job. SKIP requires LOCKED on the next token.

Stage A scope only accepts UPDATE and SHARE — NO KEY UPDATE /
KEY SHARE need NO+KEY composite tokens plus an extended
LockStrength enum, deferred.

planSelect second-line gate rejects len(s.Locking) > 0 with
0A000 "row-level locking clauses are not supported in v0
planner" — two-step gate pattern from M0017-0001/0002: parse
the surface so diagnostics surface specific feature names,
refuse to silently drop locking intent at runtime.

Tests in locking_test.go: 10 scenarios — all six accepted
shapes (bare FOR UPDATE / FOR SHARE / OF list / NOWAIT / SKIP
LOCKED / multi-clause / AFTER LIMIT) plus 2 diagnostic guards
(FOR READ, bare SKIP without LOCKED) plus 1 rollout guardrail.

commits.title: m0017: UPSERT Stage B — ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT name
commits.description:
Promotes the constraint-name target form from Stage A's hard

  - idx.Table != tbl → 42704 "constraint X does not belong to Y".

Mirrors upstream's three diagnostics from transformOnConflictClause.

column-set inference loop, returns the named index + tbl
ordinals matching idx.Columns so the executor's existing
ArbiterColumns handling works without change.

commits.title: m0017: UPSERT executor runtime — Stage A (M0017-0003)
commits.description:
New upsertOp consumes the planner-resolved OnConflict state
(arbiter index + bound UpdateSet/UpdateWhere) and runs the
INSERT … ON CONFLICT statement end-to-end.

Per row:

  - Reorder source row → target column order via plan.ColumnIndex.
  - Encode the conflict key from OnConflict.ArbiterColumns;
    NULL keys fall through to plain insert (upstream's
    NULL-never-matches rule for unique-constraint inference).
  - Probe arbiter btree via tree.RangeScan(key, key, callback);
    skip invisible tuples via mvcc.TupleVisible (essential —
    UPSERT writes duplicate index entries, historical dead
    versions are still reachable via the same key). First
    visible match becomes the conflict tuple.
  - No conflict: writeHeapRowReturning + arbiter Insert so
    subsequent rows in the same statement see the new entry.
  - Conflict + DO NOTHING: skip silently, RowsAffected stays
    put (matches upstream).
  - Conflict + DO UPDATE: build merged 2N-wide row (existing
    || inserted; planner's ColumnRef Index values already
    address this layout — `excluded.col` lands at N..2N-1).
    Evaluate UpdateWhere; non-true skips. Evaluate each
    non-nil UpdateSet[i]; nil inherits existing[i]. Stamp
    xmax on the conflicting tuple, writeHeapRowReturning the
    updated tuple, maintainArbiter inserts (key, newPtr) —
    the old (key, oldPtr) entry stays since btree.Insert
    allows duplicates and the visibility filter rejects the
    dead one on next probe.

Refactor: writeHeapRow split into the void wrapper +
writeHeapRowReturning that surfaces (block, slot) for index
maintenance. Existing INSERT/UPDATE callers unchanged.

Stage A scope guard at upsertOp.Open: UpdateSet targeting a
conflict-key column ordinal rejects with 0A000. Without it, the
arbiter entry for the original key would point at a tuple whose
actual key bytes differ; future probes would land on the wrong
row. Multi-column arbiters surface 0A000 at runtime — v0 btree
encoding is single-column.

Tests in operators_upsert_test.go: 6 end-to-end scenarios
through parser→analyzer→planner→executor covering insert /
update / nothing / merged-refs / where-skip / key-modify-reject.

Concurrency hardening (speculative insert + cleanup on conflict,
MVCC-correct under contention) deferred. Under concurrent
UPSERTs both writers may believe they're winning the race until
the next CREATE INDEX rebuild surfaces the duplicate.

Full go test ./... green.

commits.title: m0017: UPSERT planner + arbiter selection (M0017-0002)
commits.description:
Produces an executable plan node from the parser/analyzer-validated
ON CONFLICT AST.

New OnConflictPlan (Action / ArbiterIndex / ArbiterColumns /
UpdateSet / UpdateWhere) hangs off Insert.OnConflict — nil-default
keeps every pre-M0017 INSERT byte-unchanged. New OnConflictAction
enum (Nothing / Update).

resolveArbiterIndex(target, tbl, cat) walks cat.IndexesOnTable(tbl)
looking for a unique index whose column set (case-insensitive,
order-insensitive) equals the user-supplied target — first match
wins, catalog iteration order is stable so the choice is
deterministic. Returns 42P10 "no unique or exclusion constraint
matching the ON CONFLICT specification" on no match.
ArbiterColumns is the per-target-column ordinal list in
tbl.Columns order matching ArbiterIndex.Columns so the executor
extracts the conflict key without re-doing name lookup.

rangeBinding grew qualifiedOnly bool — same dual-restriction as
the analyzer's scopeRel.qualifiedOnly: hidden from the unqualified
loop AND restricted to alias-only on the qualified arm. Without
that, registering `excluded` as a synthetic binding pointing at
the same *catalog.Table would make every bare `col` ambiguous and
let `<target>.col` accidentally match excluded.

DO UPDATE planner builds a 2-binding scope (target at offset 0,
excluded at offset N qualifiedOnly), 2N-wide schema; UpdateSet
is parallel to tbl.Columns (nil = leave alone). Resolved
ColumnRefs carry Index values 0..N-1 (existing tuple) / N..2N-1
(inserted tuple) — the executor will arrange the merged layout
at runtime.

Executor *planner.Insert build-path rejects when p.OnConflict
!= nil with "ON CONFLICT execution is not supported in v0
(Stage A executor lands in M0017-0003)" — two-step gate: planner
produces full plan so misuses surface specific catalog/arbiter
errors not a generic curtain; executor refuses to silently drop
the clause.

Tests in internal/planner/with_test.go:
- TestPlanInsertOnConflictNoMatchingArbiter (42P10 without index).
- TestPlanInsertOnConflictWithUniqueIndex (full plan-shape
  assertion against an installed unique index).
- TestPlanInsertOnConflictDoNothingNoTarget (no-target form
  leaves ArbiterIndex nil for runtime).

commits.title: m0017: ON CONFLICT analyzer wiring (M0017-0001 step 2)
commits.description:
Validates the parsed OnConflictClause against catalog metadata and
the `excluded` pseudo-table scope so subsequent stages (planner
conflict-arbiter selection, executor concurrency path) can rely on
a fully-validated AST.

scopeRel grew a qualifiedOnly bool field — hides the rel from the
unqualified column-resolution loop AND restricts qualified-arm
matches to alias-only (never via the underlying table's catalog
name). Without that dual-restriction, registering `excluded` as a
synthetic rel pointing at the same *catalog.Table would (a) make
every bare `col` ambiguous between target and excluded, and (b)
make `<target>.col` ambiguous because both rels share
rel.table.Name.

New analyzeOnConflict(oc, tbl, cat, targetAlias) called from
analyzeInsert validates:

  - Stage B reject for `ON CONSTRAINT name` — 0A000.
  - DO UPDATE requires a target — 42601 mirroring upstream's
    "requires inference specification or constraint name".
  - conflict-target columns exist on target table — 42703 (planner
    picks the unique-arbiter index in M0017-0002).
  - DO UPDATE scope builds two rels — target (bare + qualified-
    by-alias resolve here) and `excluded` qualifiedOnly
    (reachable only via excluded.col).
  - SET assignment column existence (42703) + RHS type (42804)
    mirroring analyzeUpdate.
  - optional WHERE under the same scope, must be boolean (42804).

planInsert second-line gate rejects any InsertStmt carrying a
non-nil OnConflict with 0A000 so an executable plan never silently
drops the clause when a caller bypasses the analyzer (some test
paths do).

commits.title: m0017: ON CONFLICT parser surface and AST (M0017-0001 step 1)
commits.description:
Parser-only additive slice for INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, mirroring
the M0016-0001 / M0018-0001 step-1 pattern. InsertStmt grew an
optional OnConflict field — nil for pre-M0017 callers so existing
INSERT call sites are byte-for-byte unchanged.

New AST:

  - OnConflictAction enum: None (zero-value reserved for "no
    clause") / Nothing / Update.
  - OnConflictTarget: Columns + Constraint, exactly one populated
    for the two upstream forms; both empty means the no-target
    shape `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
  - OnConflictClause: Target + Action + UpdateSet + UpdateWhere.

New keywords: KwConflict, KwDo, KwNothing. UPDATE / SET / WHERE /
ON / CONSTRAINT already exist. `excluded` stays an unreserved
identifier so `excluded.col` parses as a normal qualified
ColumnRef — promoting it would shadow legitimate columns named
excluded in pre-UPSERT clusters and matches upstream's de-facto
rule.

parseOnConflict() handles the next-token disambiguation (`(` →
column list, `ON` keyword → constraint name, otherwise no
target) and the action keyword set (only NOTHING / UPDATE after
DO). The parser accepts every upstream shape including the
constraint-name target the milestone defers to Stage B — keeps
the AST shape stable so Stage B promotion doesn't change
parser-error semantics for tooling that depends on syntax-level
diagnostics.

shapes plus three diagnostic guards plus the rollout-invariance
guardrail. Full go test ./... green.

commits.title: m0018: XLOG page emission in writer + page-aware reader (M0014-0001 step 2)
commits.description:
Wires the page-header helpers landed in step 1 into the writer's
append path and the reader-side counterparts (RecordIterator +
ReadAll), gated by a new Config.PageHeaders flag (default false) so
existing data dirs and tests remain byte-unchanged.

When PageHeaders=true: state.append calls emitWithPageHeaders which
interleaves a 40-byte XLogLongPageHeader at every segment boundary
and a 24-byte short header at every other 8 KiB boundary. Records
crossing a page boundary set XLP_FIRST_IS_CONTRECORD and stamp
xlp_rem_len with the bytes-still-to-go on the next page; multi-page
records re-decrement page-by-page. writePos / WrittenLSN advance
over the combined stream length, preserving the upstream invariant
LSN = byte offset in the on-disk WAL stream. Append returns
startLSN = writePos + leading_header_bytes + 1 so the LSN lands on
the first record byte.

Reader side: RecordIterator.Next skips any header sitting at the
cursor before checking the write tail; readRecordBytesAt mirrors
the writer's interleave on reads, returning record bytes plus the
physical advance count. ReadAll auto-detects format via
DetectWALFormat (silent fallback to legacy on classification
errors so tiny test segments still work) and dispatches to
readAllPageAware for WALFormatPGCompat. scanLastSegmentEnd consults
cfg.PageHeaders directly; EOS becomes two-flavoured — all-zero page
header at a page boundary OR all-zero record header mid-page
(preserves the M0007 / 0007-0001 preallocated-tail contract).

MemRing capture, walBuf path, and writeAt layering all consume the
combined stream so direct-I/O alignment, AIO submission, and
walsender RAM streaming see the same physical bytes.

The XLogRecord-header switchover (M0014-0002 step 2) and pg_waldump
validation (M0014-0003) remain deferred — PageHeaders=true today
produces upstream-shaped pages with goopg's legacy 8-byte
length+CRC32-IEEE record frames inside.

New tests in internal/wal/xlog_emit_test.go:
TestPageEmissionLongHeaderAtSegmentStart,
TestPageEmissionShortHeaderAtPageBoundary (exact xlp_rem_len
arithmetic), TestPageEmissionRecordCrossesPage (Append/ReadAll LSN
cross-check), TestPageEmissionRecordCrossesSegment (long header on
next segment with both XLPLongHeader + XLPFirstIsContRecord),
TestPageEmissionIteratorRoundTrip, TestPageEmissionRecoversCleanly,
TestPageEmissionLegacyDefaultUnchanged (rollout invariant).

commits.description:

substitution. Each FROM-clause reference to a CTE name returns a

  siblings visible to later ones via the in-progress map.

  both checked here too as second-line defence.

  lookup, gated on rv.Schema == "" (CTE names are unschemed).
- planSelect / planInsert / planUpdate / planDelete each gained
  the preplanWithClause + defer-restore stanza.

- ZERO new CTE infrastructure. Stage A inlining produces a
  vanilla plan tree the existing operators run unchanged. This
  is the headline correctness argument.

m0016: WITH analyzer name resolution (M0016-0001 step 2)
commits.description:
Step 2 of M0016-0001: analyzer-side CTE scope rules so the
parser-attached WithClause from step 1 actually means something
semantically. Lands name resolution, scope visibility, alias-arity
validation, and Stage A's WITH RECURSIVE rejection.

Scope plumbing:
- scope grew `ctes map[string]*catalog.Table` — populated by the
  new analyzeWith helper at every entry point that takes a WITH
  clause. nil for pre-M0016 callers; existing code paths
  byte-for-byte unchanged.
- New resolveTable(ctx, rv) walks the scope chain head-first
  looking for a CTE before falling through to the catalog.
  Schema-qualified names bypass CTE lookup so
  `pg_catalog.foo` always hits the catalog.
- New buildSelectScopeIn(s, ctx) is the scope-aware variant of
  buildSelectScope, used inside CTE bodies and at the top of
  analyzeSelectWithParent so a SELECT's FROM clause sees the
  ctes map.

analyzeWith:
- Walks CTEs in declaration order. A later CTE in the same WITH
  list can reference an earlier sibling (left-to-right
  visibility, matches PG). Forward references error 42P01.
- Recurses into the inner SELECT under ctx so type errors inside
  a CTE body bubble up.
- Builds a synthetic catalog.Table mirroring
  synthesizeSubqueryTable's column-naming chain (explicit alias
  → derived name → ?column?N).
- Applies the optional (col, ...) alias list when present —
  arity mismatch errors 42P10 (invalid_column_reference);
  matching arity overrides the inner-derived names so the
  outer-query references must use the alias.
- Duplicate CTE name in one WITH list errors 42710.
- WITH RECURSIVE errors 0A000 — Stage A only. Stage B
  (M0016-0003) flips to actual recursive analysis.

Wiring:
- analyzeSelectWithParent calls analyzeWith first then routes
  FROM resolution through buildSelectScopeIn.
- analyzeInsert / analyzeUpdate / analyzeDelete each gained an
  early analyzeWith call so CTE-body type errors surface even
  though the Stage A planner/executor doesn't yet consume
  WITH-prefixed DML CTEs. Insert keeps lookupTable for its
  target relation (CTE shadowing of `INSERT INTO t` target is
  intentionally NOT supported — matches PG).

m0014: legacy-format detection helper (M0014-0004 step 1)
commits.description:
Pure additive read-only utility that complements the M0014-0001
step 1 / M0014-0002 step 1 typed sentinels: a future writer
startup can fail fast on format mismatch without committing to a
switchover policy yet. The actual loadState wiring lands in
step 2 alongside the joint writer/reader switchover so a
half-migrated segment file is impossible.

New internal/wal/format_detect.go:
- WALFormatVersion enum (Unknown / Legacy / PGCompat) with
  String() for log lines.
- DetectWALFormat(walDir) (WALFormatVersion, error):
  enumerate walDir, find the lowest-numbered file whose name
  parses as a segment under either format (legacy 24-hex
  flat counter via parseSegmentName, or pg-compat
  TLI/Log/Seg via ParseXLogFileName — both parsers return
  ok=false for non-WAL files like .gitignore so they're
  skipped). Read first 40 bytes; try DecodeXLogLongPageHeader
  then DecodeXLogPageHeader.
    magic match -> PGCompat
    errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidPageHeader) -> Legacy
    truncation < 24 bytes -> typed error
  Legacy frames can't collide with XLOGPageMagic=0xD119 at
  offsets 0..1 because uint32 length values up to ~16 MB
  never set the high bytes that produce that magic value.

Empty / nonexistent dirs return (Unknown, nil) so fresh-data-dir
bootstrap doesn't have to special-case.

CRC validation intentionally skipped — too expensive at
startup, and the writer's per-record validation catches real
corruption when reading begins.

- TestDetectWALFormatNonexistentDir
- TestDetectWALFormatEmptyDir
- TestDetectWALFormatIgnoresGarbageFiles

commits.description:

- XLogRecord (24 bytes): xl_tot_len/xl_xid/xl_prev/xl_info/xl_rmid
  + 2 zero pad + xl_crc, all little-endian.
- Rmgr enum with values matching upstream's RM_*_ID
  (RmgrXLog=0, RmgrXact=1, RmgrStorage=2, RmgrHeap2=9,

- XLogCRC32C uses Go's crc32.MakeTable(crc32.Castagnoli),
  which is a singleton for canonical polynomials so the
  table allocation happens once.
- The canonical "123456789" vector → 0xE3069283 is pinned by

  ErrInvalidRecordHeader (wrapped via %w) on non-zero
  padding, unknown rmid, or undefined framework bits — gives
  the M0014-0004 legacy-format detector clean branches.

  internal scratch copy to zero the CRC field so callers
  don't have to mutate on-disk bytes.

- DecodeXLogLongPageHeader: enforces XLPLongHeader is set —
  surfaces a long-form decode against a short-form page as a
  caller bug rather than reading garbage from bytes 24..39.

Filename helpers:
- XLogFileName(tli, segno, segSize) produces upstream's
  <TLI:%08X><Log:%08X><Seg:%08X> form (24 hex chars total —
  same width as legacy goopg counter format but with a
  different semantic split).
- ParseXLogFileName uses strconv.ParseUint(base=16) per 8-char
  field so partial-parse garbage like "0000000100000000000000FG"
  returns ok=false (Go's fmt.Sscanf %X is permissive — strict
  parse is required for the writer's segment-listing loop to
  skip unrecognised names cleanly).

Coexists with legacy formatSegmentName/parseSegmentName so the
writer/reader switchover in M0014-0001 step 2 lands atomically
without churning unrelated code first.

commits.title: m0013: WAL buffers observability + rollout (M0013-0003)
commits.description:
Closes M0013. Adds the SQL-queryable surface and startup log line

commits.title: m0013: WAL-before-data invariant tests for buffered-WAL eviction (M0013-0002)
commits.description:
Pure additive testing — no production code changes. M0013-0001's
two-stage FlushUpTo is already invoked by the existing flush
sites (Pool.flushSlot line 886, Pool.flushDirtyBatch line 836)
before mgr.WriteBlock, so the WAL-before-data invariant is
preserved by construction. This slice pins the invariant against
future regressions.

New internal/storage/wal_buffer_eviction_test.go (external
package storage_test so it can import wal without cycle):

- TestEvictionDrainsBufferedWALBeforeWritingPage:
    Real *wal.Writer with WALBuffers=64 KiB into a one-slot Pool.
    Append a small record -> assert segment 0 bytes (record in
    walBuf). Mutate a heap page, MarkDirtyWithLSN(endLSN), Unpin.
    Force eviction via a second PinNew. Assert heap byte
    persisted AND segment bytes > 0 AND ReadAll returns the
    payload. The dual assertion is the regression hook: a future
    bug that disables Stage 1 (drops drainBufferUpTo from
    flushUpTo) would persist the heap byte while leaving the WAL
    segment empty — recovery loses the record while the data
    mutation survives.

- TestFlushAllPacedDrainsBufferedWAL:
    Same invariant for the checkpointer path
    (Pool.FlushAllPaced -> flushDirtyBatch ->
    FlushUpTo(maxLSN)). Three pages, three buffered LSNs; after
    flush every payload is durable in WAL, every heap byte is
    on disk.

Failure-mode catalogue in the design doc maps each potential
bug (Stage 1 skipped / Stage 2 skipped / wrong call order /
stale maxLSN) to the assertion that catches it.

commits.title: docs: add milestone for PostgreSQL-compatible WAL format
m0013: wal_buffers architecture + bounded in-memory WAL buffer (M0013-0001)
commits.description:
Adds the bounded in-memory WAL buffer that holds generated WAL
records before they hit segment files. Records ≤ wal_buffers stay
in RAM until either an Append would overflow the buffer (drain
just enough to make room) or FlushUpTo demands a byte ≤ targetLSN
be on disk (Stage 1 drain, then Stage 2 dataSync — the milestone's
two-stage semantics).

GUC:
- new wal_buffers (TypeInt, BootVal 16 MiB, range [0, 1 GiB],
  ContextPostmaster). 0 disables the buffer entirely so every
  pre-M0013 test fixture and the legacy zero-config path keep
  working byte-for-byte.

Buffer:
- new internal/wal/wal_buffer.go: LSN-addressed ring (base/head/
  tail are absolute byte LSNs, not slice offsets) with byte-wise
  wraparound and a two-slice readForDrain that wraps without
  allocation.
- state grew walBuf and drainedLSN watermark.
- Invariant: flushedLSN ≤ drainedLSN ≤ writeLSN; walBuf covers
  (drainedLSN, writeLSN].

Append path:
- walBuf nil OR record larger than cap → bypass writeAt directly
  (drainedLSN keeps tracking writeLSN). Fragmenting an oversized
  record across drains complicates the contiguous-stream
  invariant for no benefit.
- Buffered: drainBufferBytes(need) drains just enough head bytes
  to make room, then the record is copied into walBuf.

FlushUpTo two-stage:
- Stage 1: drainBufferUpTo(targetLSN) pushes every buffered byte
  ≤ targetLSN to its segment file. The existing state.writeAt
  dirty-flag bookkeeping covers drained segments — the "sync
  debt" the milestone calls out is just the natural state.dirty
  entry.
- Stage 2 (unchanged): dataSync every dirty segment ≤ targetSeg.

Walsender:
- M0010-0002 MemRing keeps mirroring every Append regardless of
  whether it took the buffered or bypass path, so streaming-from-
  RAM behaviour is unchanged.

Plumbing:
- cmd/goopg start reads wal_buffers GUC into OpenOptions.WALBuffers
  → wal.Config.WALBuffers → state.walBuf.

Tests:
- TestWALBufferDisabledByDefault (legacy regression guard)
- TestWALBufferRetainsRecordsInRAM
- TestWALBufferOverflowDrainsToSegments
- TestFlushUpToDrainsBufferThenSyncs
- TestWALBufferRecordLargerThanBufferBypasses
- TestWALBufferReadAllRoundTrip (table test across 0/64KiB/256B
  caps — every config round-trips byte-identical)

Full \`go test ./...\` green.

Eviction/checkpoint drain verification (M0013-0002) and counters
+ observability surface (M0013-0003) are separate follow-up
slices.

commits.title: m0012: executor lock-wait integration + test matrix (M0012-0003)
commits.description:
Closes M0012. Wires the lockmgr core (M0012-0001) and deadlock
detector (M0012-0002) into the executor and pins the SQLSTATE
40P01 reporting contract.

Context plumbing:
- executor.Context grew LockMgr *lockmgr.LockManager and
  BackendID lockmgr.BackendID. Both optional — nil-LockMgr makes
  the helper a no-op so every existing storage_test fixture and
  the legacy COPY-only server path keep working unchanged.
- New Context.acquireRelLock(rel, mode) is the single funnel:
    ErrDeadlockDetected   -> *ExecError{Code: "40P01"}
    context.Canceled      -> *ExecError{Code: "57014"} (upstream's
                             query-cancel SQLSTATE)

Operator integration (5 paths):
- seqScanOp / indexScanOp take AccessShareLock.
- insertOp / updateOp / deleteOp take RowExclusiveLock.

Server integration:
- server.Config gained LockMgr; Server gained
  nextBackendID atomic.Uint32 (the youngest-backend victim
  policy from M0012-0002 relies on monotonic IDs).
- dispatch.go plumbs both into executor.Context and calls
  LockMgr.ReleaseAll(backendID) from the deferred txn-end block
  (after Commit/Rollback) so a leftover holder can never outlive
  the connection.

Test matrix in lock_integration_test.go:
- TestExecutorAcquireHelperNilLockMgr (regression guard)
- TestExecutorAcquireHelperGrantsLock
- TestExecutorDeadlockTwoSession (A<->B; pins 40P01 mapping)
- TestExecutorDeadlockThreeSession (A->B->C->A; exactly 1
  cancellation; BackendID 3 = youngest)
- TestExecutorNonDeadlockContention (linear chain; no
  false-positive 40P01)

All race-clean. Full \`go test ./...\` green.

Out of scope (separate follow-ups):
- DDL paths (DROP/ALTER) need AccessExclusiveLock.
- Catalog-level locks (pg_class etc.).
- lock_timeout GUC honouring.
- pg_locks SQL view.

commits.title: m0012: deadlock detection (M0012-0002)
commits.description:
Wait-for graph + cycle detection + victim selection + cancellation
contract on top of M0012-0001's lock manager.

Wait-for graph: for every parked Waiter w on tag t, emit edge
w.Backend -> h for every holder h of any conflicting mode
(ConflictsWith(w.Mode, holders[h])). Self-edges excluded by the
existing self-conflict-immunity rule.

Cycle detection: iterative three-colour DFS; a grey-on-grey edge
is a back-edge whose cycle is reconstructed via parent pointers.
Returns the cycle members for victim selection.

Victim selection: youngest backend in the cycle (max BackendID).
Mirrors upstream's "cancel youngest xact" heuristic — keeps older
work intact. Simpler than upstream's soft-edge / hard-edge
machinery because v0 doesn't yet have upgradable locks.

Cancellation contract: Waiter grew a second `victim chan struct{}`.
The detector splices the victim out of its parked queue under
lm.mu, sends on `victim`, and runs the wake-pass so waiters queued
behind the victim get a chance to advance. The victim's Acquire
selects on signal / victim / ctx.Done and returns
ErrDeadlockDetected (sentinel exported so higher layers can
translate to SQLSTATE 40P01). The Acquire goroutine then calls
ReleaseAll(b) outside the mutex so survivor wake-passes fire.

Scheduling: every parked Acquire arms a time.AfterFunc(
deadlockTimeout, runDeadlockCheck) — default 1s matches upstream's
deadlock_timeout GUC, tunable via SetDeadlockTimeout for tests.
Concurrent timer fires serialise on lm.mu and the detector is
idempotent.

Tests pin the contract:
- TestDeadlockDetectsTwoSessionCycle (classic A<->B)
- TestDeadlockYoungestBackendIsVictim (5 vs 9 -> 9)
- TestDeadlockDetectsThreeSessionCycle (A->B->C->A)
- TestDeadlockNoCycleNoCancel (linear chain, no false positive)
- TestDeadlockTimerSchedulesCheck (real AfterFunc path)
- TestDeadlockSurvivorMakesProgress

All race-clean. Full \`go test ./...\` green.

ErrDeadlockDetected -> SQLSTATE 40P01 wiring lands with executor
integration in M0012-0003.

commits.title: m0012: lock manager v0 surface (M0012-0001)
commits.description:
New internal/lockmgr package — PostgreSQL-style SQL lock manager
core. Sets up the data structures, mode semantics, and
acquire/release API that M0012-0002 (deadlock detection) and
M0012-0003 (executor integration) build on.

Surface:
- Eight lock modes (AccessShareLock ... AccessExclusiveLock) with
  numeric values matching upstream's lockdefs.h, so log lines and
  future SQL views share the vocabulary.
- conflictTab is ported verbatim from
  postgres/src/backend/storage/lmgr/lock.c LockConflicts[].
- Relation-level LockTag{DB, Rel}; forks intentionally collapsed.
- Per-tag lockState carries holders map[BackendID]Mask, FIFO
  waiters []*Waiter, and a cached granted mask. Lazy-alloc, GC'd
  to nil when both holders and waiters drain.
- Acquire(ctx, b, t, m) grants immediately when no conflict
  against grantedExcept(b) AND no waiters queued. The second
  check enforces strict head-of-line FIFO so a strong waiter
  doesn't starve behind a stream of compatible newcomers.
  Otherwise parks on a buffered signal chan; cancellation
  splices the waiter out under lm.mu and handles the
  Release-promoted-during-cancel race by releasing the
  just-granted bit.
- Release runs FIFO wake-pass head-first.
- ReleaseAll(b) drops every mode held across every tag — the
  txn-end hook.
- ConflictsWith(m, held) exported for the upcoming deadlock
  detector to ask the same question against the lock table.

Single coarse sync.Mutex; per-tag striping deferred. Self-
conflict is impossible by construction (grantedExcept(b)
excludes the requester's own holdings) so a backend can stack
modes — e.g. RowExclusive + AccessShare for INSERT ... SELECT.

Ten tests pin the contract end-to-end including matrix
verification, FIFO fairness, cancellation cleanup, and
ReleaseAll wakeup semantics. Race-clean.

commits.title: m0011: HammerDB TPC-H NUMERIC index validation (M0011-0003)
commits.description:
Closes M0011. Two pieces:

1. Planner: planIndexScanFromWhere accepts *NumericConst on the

   idx_lineitem_orderkey_fkidx). All 13 land cleanly. Direct
   btree.Search(EncodeNumericKey(k,0)) round-trips on orders_pk;

commits.title: add a completed milestones file.
m0011: B-tree NUMERIC build + UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY (M0011-0002)
commits.description:
Wires EncodeNumericKey (M0011-0001) into the live DDL, backfill,
and index-scan paths so HammerDB TPC-H's CREATE INDEX over a
NUMERIC column no longer aborts with "btree v0 only supports
int4 keys". Four changes:

1. Variable-length HighKey on disk. BTPageOpaque.HighKey is now
   []byte in memory; on disk a 2-byte length prefix at offset 14
   plus a 32-byte (MaxHighKeyLen) variable slot replaces the
   fixed [4]byte. Opaque grows 24 -> 48 bytes; btreeVersion
   bumps 2 -> 3 (pre-GA, older btrees error with ErrNotABTree).

2. Split path stops gating on len(sepKey) == len(op.HighKey) and
   just bounds-checks against MaxHighKeyLen.

3. createSingleColumnBTreeIndex accepts numeric/decimal via a
   new isSupportedBTreeKeyType predicate. Backfill's dedup map
   switches from map[int32]struct{} to map[string]struct{}
   keyed on the encoded bytes so (10,1) and (100,2) collapse
   into one UNIQUE entry. New shared helper
   encodeBTreeKeyForColumn branches on column type — int4 path
   is unchanged (range-check + EncodeInt4); numeric path runs
   EncodeNumericKey, with KindInt promoted to (n, 0).

4. indexScanOp.lookupKey calls the same helper so probe keys
   land on the bytes backfill produced.

Tests:
- TestDDLCreateNumericBTreeIndexAcceptsType (smoke)
- TestDDLNumericUniqueIndexCollapsesScales (1.0/1.00 -> 23505)
- TestDDLNumericIndexSplitWithVariableLengthHighKey (600 rows
  with mantissa+scale variation force non-uniform-length splits)
- TestDDLInt4IndexUnchangedRegressionGuard

Full \`go test ./...\` green.

commits.title: m0011: B-tree NUMERIC key ordering (M0011-0001)
commits.description:
Define a sortable byte encoding for NUMERIC B-tree keys so that
bytewise CompareKeys matches numeric order. Lays the encoding
contract for M0011 (TPC-H index-build unblock); DDL acceptance,
backfill, and HighKey widening land in M0011-0002.

EncodeNumericKey(mantissa, scale) layout:
  zero        -> [0x01]
  non-zero    -> sign(1) || biased exp(4 BE) || digits || term(1)
  positive    -> sign 0x02; exp = E + 0x80000000; digits '0'+d; term 0x00
  negative    -> sign 0x00; exp = 0x7FFFFFFF - E; digits '0'+(9-d); term 0xFF

After stripping trailing zeros, value = d_1.d_2..d_n × 10^E with
E = ndig - 1 - scale. Numerically-equal pairs ((10,1) and (100,2),
both 1.0) produce identical bytes — required for UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY
equality on NUMERIC columns. Encoding length ≤ 25 bytes (1 sign +
4 exp + ≤19 digits + 1 term).

Also switch CompareKeys from length-first comparison to straight
bytes.Compare. Length-first was always wrong for variable-length
keys and only worked for int4 because all int4 keys are exactly 4
bytes — so the existing path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Decoding is intentionally not provided: the B-tree never inverts
the encoding; index probes always re-encode from the live datum.

Tests pin the contract:
- TestEncodeNumericKeyZeroIsSingleByte
- TestEncodeNumericKeyScaleInvariance
- TestEncodeNumericKeySignOrder
- TestEncodeNumericKeyMonotone (23-element cross-sign / cross-magnitude)
- TestEncodeNumericKeySamePrefixDifferentLengths (terminator behaviour)
- TestEncodeNumericKeyMinInt64 (int64-min via uint64 abs path)

Built and full \`go test ./...\` green.

commits.description:

commits.title: m0010: walsender in-memory WAL handoff (M0010-0002)
commits.description:
Adds a bounded in-memory WAL byte ring backing walsender's
RecordIterator so streaming replication doesn't depend on OS
page-cache residency. Pairs with M0010-0001's wal_direct_io: with
direct I/O on, the page cache no longer warms WAL writes — the
ring is the cache replacement for sender-path reads.

Surface:

- New `wal.MemRing` (`internal/wal/mem_ring.go`): fixed-size
  []byte ring keyed by 0-based LSN-byte position.
  Append(pos, data) mirrors writer bytes; ReadAt(pos, out)
  returns (n, true) on full hit, (0, false) on miss (no
  partial-overlap stitching). Hits / Misses atomic counters.
- New `wal_sender_memory_buffer` GUC (TypeInt, default
  16777216 = 16 MiB, range [0, 1 GiB], ContextPostmaster).
  0 disables — every iterator read goes to disk.
- `state.append` calls `s.memRing.Append(writePos, record)`
  AFTER `state.writeAt` succeeds. Order matters: a failed
  pwrite must not appear in the ring.
- `RecordIterator.readBytesAt` consults the ring first;
  full-range hit returns from RAM (no syscall), miss falls
  through to the per-segment pread loop.
- `cmd/goopg start` logs `event=wal_sender_memory_buffer_attached
  capacity_bytes=N` at startup when configured.

Concurrency: single sync.RWMutex. Writers Lock during memcpy +
head/tail advance; readers RLock during their own memcpy so a
concurrent eviction can't free bytes mid-read. Multiple readers
run in parallel.

Eviction: FIFO by LSN. When tail - head > cap, head advances to
tail - cap. Lagging senders that fall outside the window miss
cleanly and resume from disk without dropping the connection.

Tests:
- Unit: TestMemRingNilSafe, TestMemRingRoundTripWithinCap,
  TestMemRingEvictsOldBytesOnOverflow,
  TestMemRingPartialOverlapMisses, TestMemRingWraps,
  TestMemRingWriteLargerThanCap, TestMemRingConcurrentReads
  (4 readers vs 100 writes — race-detector clean).
- Integration: TestIteratorReadsFromMemRing (ring on + segment
  file deleted post-Append → iterator still streams from RAM;
  Hits()>0), TestIteratorFallsBackToDiskWithoutRing (ring off
  + segment intact → legacy pread path unchanged).

Design doc docs/design/0010-0002-walsender-in-memory-wal-handoff.md
indexed; full `go test ./...` green. The
pg_stat_replication.send_buffer_* observability surface lands
in M0010-0003.

commits.title: m0010: WAL direct-I/O Phase 2 — flip O_DIRECT, per-write RMW
commits.description:
Second half of M0010-0001. With wal_direct_io=on AND probe ok,
WAL writes now bypass the OS page cache via per-write read-
modify-write through a page-aligned mmap'd scratch buffer.

Wire-up:

- `state.directIOActive` snapshots `directIORequested && fallback==""`.
- `enableDirectIO(f)` uses `fcntl(F_SETFL, flags|unix.O_DIRECT)`
  to flip the flag on the live fd AFTER preallocation finishes.
  Preallocation's 64-KiB heap-buffer zero-fill can't satisfy
  O_DIRECT alignment, so the flip is post-preallocation.
- `state.writeAt` dispatches to `state.writeAtDirectIO` when
  active. Per-write RMW: pread the aligned region (alignDown..
  alignUp around user bytes) into per-state scratch, overlay
  user bytes, pwrite the full aligned region back. Past-EOF
  reads zero-pad the tail (legacy lazy-grow correctness).
- `directIOScratchCap = 1 MiB`; outsized writes loop through
  the scratch.
- Aligned scratch lazy-allocated on first DirectIO write via
  `unix.Mmap(MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS)` (mirrors
  `internal/storage/arena.go`); freed in `state.close`.
- Block size hard-coded at 4 KiB. Every modern Linux DIO-
  capable FS satisfies this; STATX_DIOALIGN-driven detection
  is a future tightening.
- AIO+DirectIO interaction: bypasses the engine and uses the
  synchronous RMW path. Engine Submit holds the user buffer
  pointer (not page-aligned), so AIO+DirectIO needs an
  engine-side aligned-copy substrate — that's a perf-only
  follow-up (Phase 2.b in the design doc).
- Walreceiver's WAL-persist path delegates to wal.Writer.Append
  and inherits the alignment contract automatically.

Tests:
- TestDirectIORoundTripWithPreallocation: three appends + flush
  + ReadAll round-trip via RMW (SegmentSize=4 KiB).
- TestDirectIORecordSpanningBlocks: 12 KiB payload across ~3
  block boundaries; every byte round-trips through the kernel.
- Both `t.Skip` on probe fallback (matches the M0009 io_uring
  test idiom).

Crash-restart correctness rides on the existing
TestPreallocatedSegmentRecoversCleanly: the byte stream is
identical under O_DIRECT vs buffered (the RMW writes the same
bytes), so the M0007-0001 EOS-sentinel decoder sees no
difference.

Design doc updated; full `go test ./...` green.

commits.title: m0010: WAL direct-I/O Phase 1 — GUC, probe, fallback observability
commits.description:
First half of M0010-0001. Adds the surface area an operator needs to
opt into O_DIRECT WAL writes (`wal_direct_io=on`) and verify whether
the underlying filesystem honours the flag — without yet flipping
O_DIRECT on segment opens. Phase 2 (sibling slice in fix_plan.md as
M0010-0001b) lights up the actual write path; splitting keeps each
slice agent-sized.

Surface:

- `wal_direct_io` GUC (TypeBool, default off, ContextPostmaster).
- `wal.Config.DirectIO`; `loadState` runs `probeDirectIO(walDir)`
  once at construction when DirectIO=true. Probe opens
  `<walDir>/.wal_direct_io_probe` with O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_DIRECT,
  observes EINVAL / EOPNOTSUPP and returns a human-readable
  fallback reason (or empty on success). Other errnos surface as
  fail-fast errors.
- `Writer.DirectIORequested()` / `Writer.DirectIOFallbackReason()`
  accessors; stable for the writer's lifetime.
- `OpenOptions.WALDirectIO` plumbing in initdb.
- `cmd/goopg start` reads the GUC; logs `event=wal_direct_io_active`
  on probe success or `event=wal_direct_io_fallback reason=...` on
  failure. Mirrors M0009's `event=aio_*` log-line vocabulary.

Linux-only `direct_io_linux.go`; non-Linux stub
`direct_io_other.go` always falls back (mirrors the M0009 io_uring
stub). On the dev host (ext4) the probe succeeds with empty reason;
on tmpfs / overlayfs / non-Linux it falls back without affecting
correctness.

Phase 1 does NOT change WAL syscalls — `wal_direct_io=on` today is
plumbing-only at the kernel boundary. This is intentional: landing
the probe + log line first lets operators verify their FS supports
O_DIRECT before Phase 2 changes the syscall shape, so a
misconfiguration is caught at startup rather than at first commit.

Tests:
- TestDirectIODisabledByDefault — probe skipped when GUC off.
- TestDirectIOEnabledProbesFilesystem — probe runs, outcome plumbed
  correctly per GOOS (Linux ext4 succeeds, non-Linux falls back).
- TestDirectIOFallbackReasonStable — idempotent reads pin the
  lifetime contract.

Design doc `docs/design/0010-0001-wal-direct-io-write-path.md`
spans both phases with Phase 2 explicitly drafted; indexed in
docs/design/README.md.

commits.title: m0010: decompose WAL direct-I/O & walsender handoff into agent-sized slices
commits.description:
Replace the placeholder M0010 bullet in fix_plan.md with three concrete
slices matching the three required design-doc seams from the milestone
DoD:

- 0010-0001: WAL direct-I/O write path (primary + walreceiver) — O_DIRECT
  alignment, tail RMW, sync barrier preservation, EINVAL→buffered
  fallback.
- 0010-0002: walsender in-memory WAL handoff — bounded ring sized by a
  new GUC, retention / eviction by LSN window AND active sender
  demand, disk fallback for historical ranges.
- 0010-0003: WAL direct-I/O observability + operations — new
  pg_stat_wal_io counters, send-buffer hit/miss surfaces, startup log
  line, operator guidance.

This unblocks the next loop to pick up the topmost slice (M0010-0001)
without needing to re-read the milestone doc.

commits.title: m0009: AIO io_uring method (Linux)
commits.description:
Linux-only `io_uring` AIO method matching upstream `pgaio_uring.c`.
Talks to the kernel directly via syscall 425 (`io_uring_setup`) +
426 (`io_uring_enter`) — no third-party wrapper. SQ/CQ rings + SQE
array are mmap'd from the kernel-supplied byte offsets; SQE/CQE Go
structs mirror the kernel UAPI byte-for-byte.

`newMethodIOUring` runs the probe inline: any errno (ENOSYS / EPERM
under sysctl-disabled / EINVAL on too-old kernels / ENOMEM) returns
the sentinel `errProbeFailed`, which `NewEngine` matches via
`errors.Is` and uses to silently fall back to `MethodWorker`. The
non-Linux stub returns the same sentinel on every other GOOS.
`Engine.FallbackFrom() (requested, reason)` reports the fallback
so `cmd/goopg start` can log
`event=aio_method_fallback requested=io_uring actual=worker reason=...`.

Submission: SQE writes are serialised under `submitMu` (io_uring's
SQ is single-producer), tail bumped with a release-store, kicked
via `io_uring_enter(submit=1)`. A dedicated reaper goroutine blocks
in `io_uring_enter(0, min_complete=1, GETEVENTS)` and drains CQEs
into the per-handle map — idle ring costs one parked goroutine, no
busy spin. `Close` wakes the reaper out of GETEVENTS by submitting
an `IORING_OP_NOP` SQE with sentinel user_data; closing the ring
fd alone doesn't reliably unblock the syscall on every kernel.

Fd exposure for adapters: optional unexported interface
`fdHaver { Fd() uintptr }`. `*os.File` satisfies it natively;
`storage.relFile`, `initdb.aioFileAdapter`, and
`initdb.walAIOFileAdapter` add forwarding methods so the storage
and WAL caller chains preserve fd visibility through their
adapters. In-memory test files don't satisfy `fdHaver` and Submit
runs the I/O inline via `runOp`.

Tests: TestNewEngineIOUringConstructs (cross-platform — io_uring
always constructs, FallbackFrom reports correctly),
TestEngineIOUringReadWriteRoundTrip (Linux-only — pwrite-then-pread
through the kernel ring, per-direction counters bump),
TestEngineIOUringParallel (Linux-only — 64 concurrent writes + 64
reads verify no slot collisions in the userData→Handle map). Both
Linux-only tests `t.Skip` when the engine fell back so the suite
passes regardless of `io_uring_disabled` / seccomp.

Design doc: docs/design/0009-0006-aio-io-uring.md.

commits.title: m0009: AIO per-relation counters via pg_stat_aio_targets
commits.description:
aio.Engine gains a sync.Map[Target → *targetStats] with
atomic-counter values (submitted/completed/errored/
latencySum/latencyMax/bytes) so updates don't take a lock.
Submit and finishHandle update per-target alongside
per-direction counters; empty Target is ignored.
Engine.PerTarget() returns a lex-sorted snapshot.
pg_stat_aio_targets renders one row per target with the
counter set + avg/max latency. Operators can now ask both
'which side is hot?' (pg_stat_aio) and 'which file is hot?'
(pg_stat_aio_targets) without per-handle tracing.

commits.title: m0009: AIO per-direction latency (avg + max) in pg_stat_aio
commits.description:
aio.Engine gains four atomic latency counters (read/write ×
sum-micros / max-micros). finishHandle computes the elapsed
microseconds once per completion and Add()s the SumMicros +
CAS-monotonic-clamps the MaxMicros via a new advanceMax helper.
pg_stat_aio gains avg_latency_us and max_latency_us columns
rendered per-direction-row. Operators can now spot tail-latency
regressions per direction in the same view they already
read.

commits.title: m0009: AIO per-direction counter breakdown
commits.description:
aio.Engine gained six per-direction atomic counters
(read/write × submitted/completed/errored). Submit and
finishHandle bump them on the right side of each I/O. The
aggregate counters still equal the sum — invariant pinned by
TestEngineStatsPerDirection. pg_stat_aio reshaped to a
two-row-per-engine view (read row + write row) with an
`operation` column, mirroring upstream pg_stat_io's row shape.

commits.title: m0009: pg_aios.target_desc — file path on every outstanding I/O
commits.description:
aio.Op gained an optional Target string; engine inflight
tracking + InFlightInfo surface it. storage and wal both grew
matching Target fields on their AIOSubmitOp, the initdb
adapters propagate them, and the storage Manager / wal writer
stamp the relfile / segment path on every Submit. pg_aios now
renders a target_desc column so each row is attributable to a
specific file rather than just a numeric offset.

commits.title: m0009: WAL writer per-segment writeback through AIO engine
commits.description:
wal.Config.AIO seam threads an AIO engine (via narrow
wal.AIOEngine / AIOSubmitOp / AIOFile / AIOHandle /
AIODirection interfaces — parallel to the storage-side shapes,
keeping internal/wal free of internal/aio). state.writeAt
Submit→Waits per segment chunk when an engine is attached,
falls back to direct f.WriteAt when not. Commit-path fdatasync
barrier unchanged (single-threaded loop + inline Wait → all
bytes ≤ requested LSN are durably pwrite'd before
flushUpTo's fdatasync). initdb.Open builds a
walAIOEngineAdapter that delegates to the same *aio.Engine the
storage adapter uses, so reads, heap writes, and WAL writes all
flow through one pool — visible in pg_stat_aio / pg_aios.
Real perf-pipelining waits on a loop redesign that defers
Wait across Appends.

commits.title: m0009: Pool.FlushAllPaced batched AIO writeback
commits.description:
FlushAllPaced reshaped from a per-slot serial loop into a
batched WAL-flush + parallel AIO-submit + Wait loop. Each
batch holds contentMu RLocks across the data-write phase so
writers can't tear bytes; runs ONE wal.FlushUpTo at the
batch's max pd_lsn (WAL-before-data preserved); submits every
data write through Manager.WriteBlockAIO and waits on every
handle. SetAsyncFlushBatchSize controls the knob; the legacy
serial loop is bit-equivalent at batch=1. initdb.Open enables
batch=8 after attaching an AIO engine. WAL writer integration
remains a follow-up.

commits.title: m0009: AIO write-side substrate (Manager.WriteBlockAIO)
commits.description:
storage.AIOSubmitOp gained a Direction field (DirRead default
preserves prefetch semantics; DirWrite flips to pwrite).
AIOFile now requires both ReadAt + WriteAt; relFile satisfies
both. Manager.WriteBlockAIO submits writes through the engine
with Direction=AIODirWrite or falls back to synchronous
writeBlock when no engine is attached. The aio adapter in
initdb honours Direction and the file adapter's WriteAt
actually forwards to the storage file (it previously panicked
when only reads flowed through). Pool.FlushAllPaced and WAL
writer hot-path wiring is the next slice.

Wait-event hookup parked: the M0002 pg_stat_activity-shaped
wait-event surface fix_plan previously assumed exists has not
actually been built; AIO wait-event registration queues behind
that substrate's own milestone-scoped slice.

commits.title: m0009: AIO per-handle tracking + pg_aios view
commits.description:
aio.Engine gained per-Submit ID + an inflight map guarded by
inflightMu (touched only on Submit/completion, not the hot
path). Engine.registerInFlight stamps the handle and inserts;
Engine.finishHandle (replacing completionBookkeeping) combines
counters + map-removal + Handle.finish. Engine.InFlight()
returns a sorted snapshot. pg_catalog.pg_aios renders one row
per outstanding I/O — operation/off/length/submitted_at/
elapsed_us. AIO wait events composing on this surface remain a
follow-up.

commits.title: m0009: AIO observability — pg_stat_aio + startup log
commits.description:
Adds pg_catalog.pg_stat_aio backed by aio.Engine.Stats()
(method + submitted/completed/errored/in_flight counters);
single-row when an engine is attached, zero-row when not so
SELECT works on synchronous deployments. cmd/goopg start emits
event=aio_engine_attached method=... workers=... max=... when
rt.AIO != nil. Per-I/O pg_aios view + wait events remain a
follow-up — they need per-handle tracking on the engine.

commits.title: docs: add milestone 0012 lock manager and deadlock detection
m0009: heap-scan AIO prefetch (Pool.Prefetch + seqScanOp window)
commits.description:
Pool.SetPrefetchEnabled + Pool.Prefetch warm the kernel page
cache via Manager.PrefetchBlock when an AIO engine is attached.
seqScanOp keeps a 4-block lookahead window primed via
Pool.Prefetch on Open and after every block advance, so the
next-but-N block is being read by the engine while the consumer
decodes the current page. Default-off so synchronous
deployments don't pay for a redundant pread; initdb.Open flips
it on after attaching the engine.

commits.title: m0009: AIO engine lifecycle + storage Manager prefetch seam
commits.description:
storage.Manager gained SetAIO(eng) and PrefetchBlock(rel, blk,
buf) — the latter submits through the engine when one's
attached and falls back to a pre-completed handle when not, so
the caller's Submit/Wait code path is identical regardless.
initdb.Open constructs an aio.Engine when OpenOptions.AIOMethod
is set, surfaces it on Runtime.AIO, attaches it to the storage
manager, and closes it on shutdown. cmd/goopg start reads the
io_method / io_workers / io_max_concurrency GUCs and threads
them through; io_uring downgrades silently to worker until the
runtime probe lands. Heap-scan and checkpointer/WAL caller
integrations are the remaining M0009 slices.

commits.title: m0009: AIO read-stream API (predictive prefetch)
commits.description:
internal/aio/read_stream.go layers a NextBlock-callback-driven
prefetch surface on top of Engine.Submit. NewReadStream primes
a bounded lookahead window; Next() blocks on the head prefetch
and refills the window; Close drains rather than abandons
in-flight reads so the engine's InFlight counter stays honest.
Two backpressure layers stack — per-stream Lookahead AND the
engine's global io_max_concurrency. Heap-scan / ANALYZE caller
wiring is the next slice.

commits.title: docs: add milestone 0011 for btree numeric keys
m0009: AIO core (submit/wait/complete + sync + worker methods)
commits.description:
internal/aio/ ships the foundational submit/wait/complete API
plus the `sync` (inline syscalls) and `worker` (bounded
goroutine pool) methods; io_uring reserved for the Linux
follow-up. io_method/io_workers/io_max_concurrency GUCs
registered with upstream-aligned defaults but not yet consumed
by any caller — read-stream + heap-scan / checkpointer / WAL
writer wiring lands in subsequent slices.

commits.title: docs: add milestone 0010 for WAL direct I/O handoff
m0008: structured replication-event logging
commits.description:
Extends internal/wal/repllog.go's slog event vocabulary with
five new logical-replication constants. ApplyWorker emits
apply_commit/apply_error/tablesync_state_change events through
the existing slog seam; RunTableSync emits started, both i→d
and d→s state transitions, and completed with the row count.
Rejected an earlier draft that added a parallel
wal.ReplicationLogger interface — the slog pattern already in
use for M0005 retention/walreceiver covers it.

commits.title: m0008: pg_stat_subscription apply / tablesync hookup
commits.description:
ApplyWorker now MarkMessages each frame and AdvanceReceivedLSN
on commit when SetStatHandle is set; TableSyncConfig grew an
optional Stat handle that MarkMessages every CopyData frame;
RunTableSyncManager gained an OpenStat callback that owns the
per-rel Register/Unregister lifecycle. pg_stat_subscription
now reflects live apply / tablesync progress.

commits.title: m0008: pg_stat_subscription substrate
commits.description:
Adds wal.Subscribers registry (leader + tablesync workers, atomic
LSN counters, lock-free Snapshot in (subname, worker_type, relid,
pid) order) and the pg_stat_subscription virtual view backed by
it. Apply-worker / tablesync-manager hookup that actually
Registers into the registry remains the next slice.

commits.title: m0008: per-subscription tablesync manager
commits.description:
server.RunTableSyncManager walks pg_subscription_rel for one
subscription, skips rows already at state 'r', and drives a
RunTableSync exchange for every other rel via injected
ResolveRel / OpenConn / OpenWriter callbacks. Per-rel errors
don't abort the sweep; the apply-worker still owns the s → r
advance on commit-LSN crossover.

commits.title: feat(tpc-h): modified bench/tpch/run_all.sh internally use scripts for goopg
m0008: apply-worker tablesync integration
commits.description:
ApplyWorker now consults pg_subscription_rel: changes for rels
not yet at state 'r' are dropped (the tablesync worker owns that
data), and a commit at-or-after a rel's recorded sync-end LSN
promotes 's' → 'r' so streaming takes over. Mirrors upstream
worker.c's process_syncing_tables_for_apply.

commits.title: m0008: tablesync initial-COPY transport
commits.description:
internal/server/tablesync.RunTableSync drives a publisher →
subscriber `COPY <rel> TO STDOUT` exchange and walks
pg_subscription_rel.srsubstate through i → d → s. The
apply-worker integration that drives s → r on a streaming
commit boundary remains the next M0008 slice.

commits.title: m0008: tablesync state machine substrate (pg_subscription_rel)
commits.description:
catalog.PubSub gains SubscriptionRel rows with monotonic
i/d/s/r state transitions and max-only LSN merges; the
pg_subscription_rel virtual view renders from the registry.
The actual COPY transport and apply-worker integration
remain as the next two M0008 slices.

commits.title: m0008: publication-membership filter on the publisher walsender
commits.description:
Continues 0008-0003 / 0008-0004. Closes the remaining gap on
the publisher side: a slot's pgoutput stream now only emits
changes for relations named by the subscribed publications.

internal/wal/pgoutput.go:
  - New RelationFilter interface (Allows(rel, kind)).
  - PgOutput.SetFilter installs one; filter-rejected changes
    emit nothing — neither the R descriptor nor the I/D row
    payload. Subscribers never see a relation descriptor for
    changes they'll never receive.

internal/server/logicalwalsender.go:
  - publicationFilter implements wal.RelationFilter by ORing
    publish-flag bitsets across every subscribed publication
    that covers a relation. FOR ALL TABLES is a fast-path.
  - buildPublicationFilter walks ps.LookupPublication for
    each name in the slot's publication_names option.
    Unknown names are silently skipped (lenient v0 behavior;
    upstream rejects at CREATE SUBSCRIPTION).
  - relQualifiedName renders rels as "schema.name" so the
    lookup is byte-equal with what catalog.PubSub.Tables
    stores.
  - splitPublicationNames parses libpq's 'p1,p2,p3' option
    value with whitespace trimming + empty-entry drops.
  - runLogicalWalsender installs the filter via SetFilter
    when both the option list is non-empty and the runtime
    has a PubSub registry; missing either path leaves the
    filter nil so the old "ship everything" behaviour is
    preserved (still useful for tests and the
    catalog-only initial scaffolding).

Tests:
  wal:
    - TestPgOutputFilterSuppressesEmission (rejected change
      produces zero bytes)
    - TestPgOutputFilterPerKind (per-kind filter passes
      inserts, drops deletes, no stray R for the rejected
      delete)
  server:
    - TestPublicationFilterAllowsByTable
    - TestPublicationFilterAllTables (FOR ALL TABLES path)
    - TestPublicationFilterRespectsPublishFlags
    - TestPublicationFilterUnionAcrossPublications
      (any-publication-grants rule)
    - TestPublicationFilterUnknownPublicationSkipped
    - TestSplitPublicationNamesTrimsAndDropsEmpty

With this slice a real subscriber's
CREATE SUBSCRIPTION s CONNECTION '...' PUBLICATION p
actually only receives changes from p's tables — the wire
matches what publication DDL configured.

commits.title: m0008: publisher-side LOGICAL walsender
commits.description:
Continues 0008-0004. Lands the publisher-side completion of
the logical-replication wire path: a real subscriber can now
issue START_REPLICATION SLOT name LOGICAL and receive a stream
of pgoutput messages.

internal/server/replication.go::parseStartReplicationArgs grew
Mode + Options fields and now handles:

  START_REPLICATION SLOT name LOGICAL X/X
      ("key" 'value' [, ...])

Mode = PHYSICAL or LOGICAL (LOGICAL requires SLOT). The option
block parser splits libpq's quoted-pair syntax respecting
single-quote-quoted commas. Existing PHYSICAL callers are
unaffected.

replyStartReplication dispatches LOGICAL into the new
internal/server/logicalwalsender.go::runLogicalWalsender,
