which:

  - Snapshots the catalog at session start via
    wal.BuildCatalogSnapshot so pgoutput resolves relations
    against a stable shape.
  - Wraps the FrameWriter in walsenderPgoutputAdapter — an
    io.Writer that turns each pgoutput Begin/Commit/Change
    Write call into one 'w' CopyData frame with monotonic
    startLSN/endLSN, exactly the shape the subscriber's
    LogicalReceiver consumes.
  - Builds a wal.PgOutput against the snapshot + adapter and
    drives it through wal.NewSlotDecoderWithSnapshot so the
    slot's ConfirmedFlushLSN advances on every commit.
  - Spawns a receive-side goroutine that consumes
    standby-status CopyData (mirrors the PHYSICAL path) so
    the subscriber's ack also drives retention.
  - Returns cleanly on ctx cancel / CopyDone / Terminate /
    wal.ErrClosed; other errors flow through
    writeStreamingError.

New tests:
  - TestParseStartReplicationArgsLogical (full command +
    option-block round-trip)
  - TestParseStartReplicationArgsLogicalRequiresSlot
  - TestParseStartReplicationArgsPhysicalStillWorks
  - TestWalsenderPgoutputAdapterWrapsAsCopyData
    (every Write is one 'w' CopyData frame with monotonic
    LSNs that round-trip through DecodeReplicationMessage)

What's still deferred: publication-membership filter on the
publisher (today the walsender ships every change for every
relation in the snapshot — FOR TABLE t1, t2 doesn't restrict
the wire). Tablesync state machine and DELETE/UPDATE row
resolution remain the larger next steps.

With this slice the publisher and subscriber both speak the
LOGICAL wire shape end-to-end.

commits.title: m0008: subscriber-side logical-replication TCP transport
commits.description:
Continues 0008-0004. Lands the LogicalReceiver: subscriber-side
client that connects to a publisher, runs START_REPLICATION SLOT
... LOGICAL, and feeds each `'w'` CopyData payload through
wal.DecodeMessage → executor.ApplyWorker.

internal/server/logicalreceiver.go::LogicalReceiver mirrors the
WalReceiver structure but with three logical-mode differences:

  - Startup uses replication=database (not =true).
  - START_REPLICATION carries the LOGICAL keyword + the option
    block ("proto_version" '1', "publication_names" 'p1,p2').
    buildStartLogicalReplicationCommand renders the wire-level
    SQL string. Empty Publications drops publication_names
    entirely (matches libpq's "all visible publications"
    fallback).
  - Each 'w' CopyData payload is one pgoutput message; the
    receiver decodes it via wal.DecodeMessage and dispatches
    through *executor.ApplyWorker.ApplyMessage. ApplyMessage
    returns the commit LSN on `C` events, which the receiver
    caches as applyLSN so the next standby-status frame
    advances the publisher's confirmed_flush_lsn.

Run(ctx) spins a frame-reader goroutine, dispatches via
handleFrame → handleCopyData, and emits 'r' standby-status
CopyData on every StatusInterval tick (default 10s) and on
reply-requested keepalives. Apply errors trigger
Apply.SafeRollback() so the in-progress xact never leaks.

Tests:
  - TestBuildStartLogicalReplicationCommandShape pins the
    exact wire-level SQL command string.
  - TestBuildStartLogicalReplicationCommandNoPublications pins
    the no-publications shape.
  - TestLogicalReceiverHandleCopyDataAppliesPgoutputAndAdvancesLSN
    drives handleCopyData with B→R→I→C pgoutput bytes wrapped
    in 'w' CopyData payloads against a live ApplyWorker; the
    receiver's ApplyLSN() advances to the commit LSN, proving
    the wire-format → decode → apply path works end-to-end.

What's still deferred:
  - Publisher-side walsender support for logical slots
    (currently emits raw WAL, not pgoutput). The next M0008
    loop runs wal.SlotDecoder over a wal.PgOutput writer that
    wraps each message in a 'w' CopyData frame.
  - Tablesync state machine (i/d/s/r in pg_subscription_rel).
  - DELETE / UPDATE row resolution (wire format extension).

With this slice the subscriber side has full transport down to
the wire. Once the publisher walsender wraps pgoutput bytes,
the two halves connect.

commits.title: m0008: apply-worker per-event apply path
commits.description:
Continues 0008-0004. Lands the subscriber-side ApplyWorker that
turns decoded pgoutput messages into local table mutations.

internal/executor/applyworker.go:
  ApplyWorker{cat, pool, txnMgr, relations, currentTx, inXact}
  ApplyMessage(m *wal.DecodedMessage) (uint64, error)
    B: txnMgr.Begin(ReadCommitted). Defensive rollback on a
       stray B inside an open xact.
    R: cache remote DecodedRelation keyed by remote OID and
       resolve local *catalog.Table via LookupTable.
    I: parse each text-format column to a Datum
       (parsePgoutputText handles int4/int8/bool; varlen text
       falls back to KindString) and writeHeapRow into the
       local heap. Same path INSERT uses — apply triggers the
       same WAL change records.
    D: no-op in v0 (pgoutput emits an empty K body so the row
       to stamp xmax on isn't identifiable; tracked as a
       wire-format extension follow-up).
    C: commit local txn, return remote commit_lsn so the
       caller can advance confirmed_flush_lsn. A C with no B
       is tolerated as a no-op (catalog-only
       filter-everything xact).
  SafeRollback() is the deferrable cleanup that prevents
  open-xid leaks when the streaming driver bails.

End-to-end test pins the encoder→decoder→apply symmetry:
  TestApplyWorkerInsertsRowFromPgoutputStream
    Publisher emits B → R → I → C for a 2-column int4+text
    row through wal.PgOutput. The byte stream feeds
    wal.DecodeMessage → ApplyWorker.ApplyMessage. After C the
    subscriber's local `items` table contains exactly one row
    with id=7, label="alpha" (verified via SeqScan).

  TestApplyWorkerCommitOutsideXactIsNoop and
  TestApplyWorkerInsertWithoutRelationFails pin the protocol
  guards.

What's still deferred:
  - TCP transport (START_REPLICATION SLOT name LOGICAL +
    CopyData unwrap).
  - Tablesync state machine (i/d/s/r in
    pg_subscription_rel).
  - DELETE / UPDATE row resolution.

With this slice the apply path works end-to-end against
in-process byte streams. The next M0008 loop wires the libpq
transport so a real subscription can connect.

commits.title: m0008: pgoutput decoder + apply-worker design doc
commits.description:
First slice of M0008 / 0008-0004. Lands the design doc covering
the apply worker plus the immediate encoder/decoder symmetry the
worker needs.

internal/wal/pgoutput_decoder.go delivers DecodeMessage(payload),
the byte-for-byte inverse of 0008-0002's PgOutput encoder:

  Output types
    DecodedMessage{Kind, XID, CommitLSN, EndLSN, CommitTime,
                   Relation, RelOID, NewTuple, OldTuple}
    DecodedRelation{OID, Schema, Name, Replident, Columns}
    DecodedAttr{Flags, Name, TypeOID, TypeMod}
    DecodedColumn{Status, Bytes}

  Per-kind parsers cover
    B: kind | final_lsn | commit_time | xid          (21 bytes)
    C: kind | flags=0 | commit_lsn | end_lsn |
       commit_time                                   (26 bytes)
    R: rel_oid | nspname\0 | relname\0 | replident |
       natts | per-attr (flags | name\0 | typoid |
       typmod)
    I: rel_oid | 'N' | tuple-body
    D: rel_oid | 'K'/'O' | tuple-body

  Tuple bodies handle 'n' (NULL), 't' (text with length
  prefix), and 'u' (unchanged TOAST) status bytes.

Reader cursor enforces big-endian framing and surfaces
ErrTruncatedMessage on short payloads.

New tests pin the encoder/decoder symmetry:
  - TestPgoutputDecoderRoundTripBegin (xid + commit_lsn)
  - TestPgoutputDecoderRoundTripCommit (commit_lsn + end_lsn)
  - TestPgoutputDecoderRoundTripRelationAndInsert (2-column
    int4+text table; tuple body decodes to [t:"42",
    t:"alpha"] — exact byte sequence the encoder produced)
  - TestPgoutputDecoderRoundTripDelete (empty K body)
  - TestPgoutputDecoderRejectsTruncated

ApplyWorker scaffolding (per-event apply + xact lifecycle), TCP
transport, the i/d/s/r tablesync state machine, slot-start
handshake, and DELETE/UPDATE row resolution remain deferred to
subsequent M0008 loops. With this slice the bytes a publisher
emits can be turned back into typed events on the subscriber
side.

commits.title: m0008: parser + executor for CREATE/DROP PUBLICATION/SUBSCRIPTION
commits.description:
Continues 0008-0003. Lands the SQL surface that lets operators
mutate the publication / subscription catalog substrate from the
prior loop. The five virtual catalog views (pg_publication,
pg_publication_rel, pg_publication_tables, pg_subscription,
pg_subscription_rel) automatically reflect the new state.

Parser:
  - New keywords: publication, subscription, connection, for,
    tables. Option names (publish, enabled, slot_name) stay
    plain identifiers so they don't collide with column refs
    like pg_stat_replication.slot_name.
  - New AST nodes:
      CreatePublicationStmt {Name, AllTables, Tables, With}
      DropPublicationStmt   {Name, IfExists}
      CreateSubscriptionStmt {Name, Conninfo, Publications, With}
      DropSubscriptionStmt  {Name, IfExists}
  - parseCreate / parseDrop dispatch into new tail functions.
  - parsePubSubWithList handles `WITH (key = value [, ...])`;
    values may be string literals, identifiers, int literals,
    or keywords. `=` matches as TokenOperator (it's an
    operator, not a punctuation symbol).

Planner:
  - Pub/sub statements compile to *planner.DDL — same path as
    CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE — so the executor's existing DDL
    operator dispatches them.

Executor:
  - executor.Context grows PubSub *catalog.PubSub.
  - ddlOp adds execCreatePublication / execDropPublication /
    execCreateSubscription / execDropSubscription that call
    into Context.PubSub. Maps publish=... into the
    PublishInsert/Update/Delete flags via splitCommaList.
    Drop variants honour IF EXISTS.

Wire:
  - server.Config.PubSub field added; threaded from
    Runtime.PubSub in cmd/goopg start.
  - dispatch.go and dispatch_extended.go set
    ctx.PubSub = s.cfg.PubSub.

New tests:
  Parser:
    - TestParseCreatePublicationForTable
    - TestParseCreatePublicationForAllTables
    - TestParseCreatePublicationWithPublishOption
    - TestParseDropPublicationIfExists
    - TestParseCreateSubscription
    - TestParseDropSubscription
  Executor end-to-end:
    - TestDDLCreatePublicationEndToEnd
    - TestDDLCreateSubscriptionEndToEnd
    - TestDDLDropPublicationIfExists

With this slice 0008-0003 has a working SQL surface. Apply
worker + tablesync (0008-0004) and observability (0008-0005)
remain the next M0008 work.

commits.title: m0008: publication / subscription catalog substrate
commits.description:
First slice of M0008 / 0008-0003. Lands the in-memory catalog
substrate plus the five virtual catalog views the apply worker
and operator-facing tooling will consume. Parser surface,
executor wiring, slot provisioning, and persistence follow in
subsequent loops.

internal/catalog/pubsub.go::PubSub:
  - Publication{Name, OID, AllTables, PublishInsert/Update/
    Delete, Tables}
  - Subscription{Name, OID, Conninfo, Publications, SlotName,
    Enabled}
  - CreatePublication / DropPublication / LookupPublication /
    Publications()
  - CreateSubscription / DropSubscription /
    LookupSubscription / Subscriptions()
  - Deep-copy returns prevent aliasing into registry state
  - SlotName defaults to subscription name when empty
    (upstream behavior)
  - DefaultPublicationOptions() returns publish=insert+
    update+delete (truncate stays off — milestone-out-of-scope)

initdb.Runtime grows a PubSub *catalog.PubSub field. Open
constructs it via NewPubSub and registers the five views
alongside pg_replication_slots.

Five virtual views in replication_views.go:
  - pg_publication
  - pg_publication_rel
  - pg_publication_tables
  - pg_subscription
  - pg_subscription_rel (emits zero rows; tablesync state
    lives in the apply worker — 0008-0004)

Column shapes mirror upstream PG 18.x. Columns goopg doesn't
track yet (pubowner, pubviaroot, subbinary, substream,
subtwophasestate, prqual, prattrs) emit empty / `f` / `{}`.

Tests pin:
  - Publication round-trip (by table, ALL TABLES),
    duplicate-name rejection, drop semantics
  - Subscription round-trip + duplicate-name rejection
  - pg_publication view shape (puballtables / publish flags /
    pubtruncate=f)
  - pg_subscription view shape (subname / subenabled /
    subconninfo / subslotname / subpublications array
    formatting)

With this slice an operator's `\dRp` against goopg returns a
clean (empty) row set, and future loops just call
Runtime.PubSub.Create* — the views update automatically.

commits.title: m0008: pgoutput output plugin (0008-0002)
commits.description:
First implementation of the OutputPlugin interface from
0008-0001. PgOutput emits messages whose byte shapes match
upstream PostgreSQL pgoutput v1 protocol so a future apply
worker (0008-0004) can consume goopg's publisher output by
reading the same format upstream's walsender produces.

Wire shapes (all multi-byte ints big-endian):
  B  kind | final_lsn | commit_time | xid                   (21 B)
  C  kind | flags=0 | commit_lsn | end_lsn | commit_time    (26 B)
  R  rel_oid | nspname\0 | relname\0 | replident | nattrs |
       per-attr (flags | name\0 | type_oid | typmod)
  I  rel_oid | 'N' | tuple
  D  rel_oid | 'K' | nliveatts=0  (v0 HeapDelete carries no
                                   pre-image; apply worker
                                   resolves by (rel, blk, slot))

Tuple-body decoder mirrors executor/codec.go::DecodeRow
byte-for-byte (duplicated rather than imported because
executor depends on wal — inverting would create a cycle).
Supports int4 / int8 / bool / text / varchar / numeric /
timestamp / date. Per-column pg_type OID mapping via
pgoTypeOIDFor.

Relation messages are lazy-emitted via an emittedRel set —
the first Change touching a relation in a session emits R
ahead of the per-row message; subsequent changes skip R.
Mirrors upstream's relsynced behaviour.

Replica identity reports DEFAULT uniformly; every column
flagged as part of REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT so apply
workers' row-resolution path works for tables with primary
keys. Catalog-driven replica-identity modes land with the
publication / subscription DDL slice (0008-0003).

What's deferred:
  - 'U' UPDATE: v0 executor emits paired HeapDelete +
    HeapInsert; the reorder-buffer fold to a single U is
    its own loop.
  - 'T' TRUNCATE: M0008-out-of-scope.
  - 'Y' TYPE / 'M' MESSAGE / 2PC / streaming v2: out of
    scope.
  - Binary-format subscriptions: out of scope.

New tests:
  - TestPgOutputBeginEmitsCanonicalShape (21-byte B layout)
  - TestPgOutputCommitEmitsCanonicalShape (26-byte C layout)
  - TestPgOutputInsertEmitsRelationOnceThenInsert (lazy R)
  - TestPgOutputInsertEncodesIntAndText (int4 + text body)
  - TestPgOutputDeleteEmitsKMarker (0-attr K body)
  - TestPgOutputSkipsUnknownRelation (snapshot-time-only)

The pipeline now has its first real OutputPlugin. Next M0008
loop: 0008-0003 (publication / subscription DDL + catalog).

commits.title: m0008: HISTORIC catalog snapshot for the logical decoder
commits.description:
Sixth slice of M0008 / 0008-0001. Closes the snapshot gap so a
real pgoutput plugin (0008-0002) can interpret tuple bytes
against schema as it stood at slot creation.

catalog.InMemory.AllTables() returns deep copies of every
non-virtual user table in OID order — the iteration accessor
the snapshot builder needs.

internal/wal/snapshot.go:
  - RelationDef{Schema, Name, OID, Columns} + ColumnDef are
    the immutable per-relation snapshots a plugin reads.
  - CatalogSnapshot is a per-RelOid map. Lookup keyed by
    RelOid (stable across renames). Built once via
    BuildCatalogSnapshot(c) — mutations to the catalog
    afterwards cannot leak through (the Drop+recreate test
    pin guarantees this).
  - Virtual pg_catalog views are skipped — they re-register
    on every startup and aren't user-data.
  - SlotSnapshot{Catalog, MVCC} bundles the two frozen views
    a logical decoder needs at slot start: schema plus xact
    visibility.

wal.SlotDecoder grows a Snapshot field and a
NewSlotDecoderWithSnapshot constructor that captures the
bundle at construction time. The original NewSlotDecoder
stays for tests that don't need schema awareness. Plugins
read decoder.Snapshot once pgoutput (0008-0002) wires the
consumption path.

v0 cut: snapshot is fixed for the slot's lifetime. Schema
changes during the slot's life surface as decoder errors when
they bite — out of scope for the M0008 first acceptance bar.
The full upstream SnapBuild state machine and the per-slot
catalog-xmin retention hook in vacuum / pruning remain
deferred.

New tests:
  - TestBuildCatalogSnapshotFreezesShape (drop+recreate
    confirms the frozen view holds)
  - TestBuildCatalogSnapshotSkipsVirtualTables
  - TestSnapshotLookupMissingRelation
  - TestNewSlotDecoderWithSnapshotAttachesIt

With this slice 0008-0001 has the foundation a real pgoutput
plugin can build against. Next M0008 work moves to 0008-0002
(pgoutput message encoding + replica-identity handling).

commits.title: m0008: per-slot logical-decoder loop
commits.description:
Fifth slice of M0008 / 0008-0001. Ties the foundation laid by
loops 1-4 into a working end-to-end pipeline: a long-lived
goroutine per logical slot consumes a RecordIterator anchored
at the slot's RestartLSN, dispatches each record via Classify
into the M0008 Decoder, and advances the slot's
ConfirmedFlushLSN at every commit so a restart resumes from
the right anchor.

internal/wal/slot_decoder.go:
  - SlotDecoder.Run(ctx) loops iter.Next → Classify → (on
    XactCommit) AdvanceConfirmedFlushLSN(rec.EndLSN).
  - NewSlotDecoder rejects non-logical slots fast — physical
    slots feed the streaming-replication path, not pgoutput.
  - Close releases the iterator subscription.
  - ctx.Cancelled / ErrClosed / io.EOF return cleanly so a
    graceful shutdown is distinguishable from a crash.
  - One goroutine per active slot, sequential by design.

Wires into the loops 1-4 surface untouched:
  - loop 1's logical slots / pg_replication_slots view.
  - loop 2's ReorderBuffer / Decoder / OutputPlugin.
  - loop 3's RecordKindXactCommit/XactAbort + Classify.
  - loop 4's mvcc.Manager hook that puts xact markers in the
    WAL so the iterator actually sees them.

End-to-end test (TestSlotDecoderRunDrivesPluginThroughCommit):
real wal.Writer, real Slots registry, async Run goroutine,
appends three records (insert / insert / commit for xid 42),
confirms the thread-safe capture plugin observed
Begin → Change → Change → Commit and the slot's
ConfirmedFlushLSN advanced to the commit record's EndLSN.

What's still deferred for M0008: snapshot builder (so
plugins can interpret tuple bytes against schema), pgoutput
(0008-0002), publication / subscription DDL (0008-0003),
apply worker + tablesync (0008-0004), observability
(0008-0005), and the per-slot catalog-xmin retention hook in
vacuum / pruning.

commits.title: m0008: emit xact markers at txn boundaries via mvcc hook
commits.description:
Fourth slice of M0008 / 0008-0001. The classifier from loop 3
now sees real commit/abort markers in the live WAL stream
because every Begin/Commit/Rollback cycle emits one.

mvcc.Manager grows XactMarker enum (XactCommit / XactAbort)
and SetXactMarkerLogger(fn func(xid, kind) error). Both Commit
and Rollback invoke the logger under the manager lock before
the active-set delete; a logger error propagates back through
Commit / Rollback so a WAL-append failure stops the txn from
finishing and the caller can retry or escalate.

initdb.Open installs a hook that walWriter.Append's
EncodeXactCommit(xid) / EncodeXactAbort(xid). Single seam
covers every server path (simple-query, extended-query, COPY)
without per-call-site changes — every txn that flows through
the runtime's TxnMgr lands a marker in the WAL.

The end-to-end pin (TestOpenWiresXactMarkerHook) drives a real
Begin/Commit + Begin/Rollback through Runtime.TxnMgr, then
opens the WAL stream via wal.ReadAll and confirms both markers
are present with matching xids.

What's still deferred for the next M0008 / 0008-0001 loop: the
long-lived classifier loop (a goroutine per logical slot that
consumes a RecordIterator and drives a real OutputPlugin) and
the snapshot builder skeleton.

New tests:
  - mvcc/manager_test.go::TestXactMarkerLoggerCalledOnCommit
  - …::TestXactMarkerLoggerCalledOnRollback
  - …::TestXactMarkerLoggerErrorAbortsCommit
  - initdb/open_test.go::TestOpenWiresXactMarkerHook

commits.title: m0008: WAL classifier + xact-marker records
commits.description:
Third slice of M0008 / 0008-0001. Adds the two new WAL record
kinds the logical decoder needs and the in-process classifier
that dispatches a record stream into the M0008 Decoder.

New WAL record kinds:
  - RecordKindXactCommit (8): "kind | xid" = 5 bytes.
  - RecordKindXactAbort  (9): same shape.

Both are physical-recovery no-ops in ApplyRecord — the per-
record idempotency in the existing logical change records
(HeapInsert, HeapDelete, HeapVacuum, BtreeInsert) already
brings storage to a consistent state. The markers exist purely
so the M0008 logical decoder can drive its reorder buffer.

EncodeXactCommit, EncodeXactAbort, DecodeXactMarker round-trip
the xid.

internal/wal/classifier.go::Classify(d, r) walks one decoded
record and dispatches into the *Decoder:
  - HeapInsert: xmin parsed from the encoded heap-tuple header
                (offset 0..3, mirrors storage.HeapTuple.MarshalBinary).
  - HeapDelete: xmax already in the record payload.
  - XactCommit / XactAbort: xid in the marker payload.
  - HeapVacuum / BtreeInsert / BtreeSplit / PageImage /
    Checkpoint: silently skipped (not user-data txn events).

Per-record xid plumbing on the existing logical change records
was deliberately avoided — the on-disk tuple body already
carries xmin, and HeapDelete already carries xmax. That keeps
the wire format backwards-compatible with persisted WAL
streams.

What's still deferred for the next M0008 loop: the executor /
wire layer must call EncodeXactCommit(xid) at COMMIT and
EncodeXactAbort(xid) at ROLLBACK boundaries. Until that lands,
the classifier works against synthetic record streams in tests
but sees no markers in live workloads.

New tests:
  - TestClassifyHeapInsertRoutesByXmin
  - TestClassifyHeapDeleteRoutesByXmax
  - TestClassifyAbortDropsXact
  - TestClassifyIsolatesConcurrentXacts
  - TestClassifySkipsNonTxRecords
  - TestEncodeDecodeXactMarker

commits.title: m0008: reorder buffer + decoder orchestration skeleton
commits.description:
Second slice of M0008 / 0008-0001. Lays the in-memory data flow
that the future WAL classifier will drive: per-xact queueing,
commit-time drain, abort-drop, and the OutputPlugin interface
that pgoutput (0008-0002) will implement.

internal/wal/reorder.go — ReorderBuffer keyed by
storage.TransactionID:
  - Append(xid, Change) queues; first append records begin LSN.
  - Commit(xid) returns queued changes in append order, drops
    the entry, returns the begin LSN for the pgoutput `B`
    message.
  - Abort(xid) drops the entry without emitting.
  - Active() / OldestBeginLSN() for observability and the
    publisher's catalog-xmin tracker.
  - xid==0 is rejected (the InvalidTransactionID sentinel
    would conflate distinct xacts).
  - Single-decoder / non-goroutine-safe by design — the loop is
    sequential.

internal/wal/decoder.go — Decoder + OutputPlugin contract:
  - OutputPlugin{Begin(xid, commitLSN), Change(c),
    Commit(xid, commitLSN)} — small enough to be stub-friendly
    and full enough for pgoutput.
  - Decoder.ApplyChange / ApplyCommit / ApplyAbort drive the
    reorder buffer and, on commit, drain the buffer through the
    plugin in Begin → Change* → Commit order.
  - Unknown xids on ApplyCommit are no-ops (the future classifier
    may filter every change for some xacts; the commit record
    still arrives).
  - ErrNoPlugin guards a decoder configured with nil plugin
    against silently dropping output.

Change{Kind, LSN, Rel, Block, LineSlot, OldTuple, NewTuple}
covers Insert/Update/Delete. Update will be paired
HeapDelete + HeapInsert in v0 — the apply worker reconciles
until the decoder learns to fold them.

WAL classifier remains deferred. The current WAL records carry
no commit/abort markers and no per-record xid; driving the
decoder from RecordIterator needs new RecordKindXactCommit /
RecordKindXactAbort records plus xid plumbing on the existing
logical change records. Tracked as the next M0008 / 0008-0001
loop.

Snapshot builder and pgoutput remain deferred to their own
loops (0008-0002 etc.).

commits.title: m0008: logical replication slots + pg_replication_slots view
commits.description:
First slice of M0008 (logical replication support). Lays the
foundation that the decoder pipeline, pgoutput plugin, publication
DDL, and apply worker (all subsequent loops) build on.

`wal.SlotKind` grows `SlotLogical`; `wal.Slot` grows `Plugin`,
`Database`, and `CatalogXmin` fields — all JSON-tagged with
`omitempty` so physical-slot state files stay byte-identical to
their pre-M0008 shape and pre-M0008 slot files round-trip cleanly
into the new shape with zero-valued logical fields.

`Slots.Create` no longer hard-rejects non-physical kinds; new
typed constructor `Slots.CreateLogical(name, plugin, database,
startLSN)` enforces the logical-slot invariants (non-empty plugin
and database). WAL retention via `Slots.MinRestartLSN()` picks up
logical slots automatically because the `Slot` shape is shared —
no retention code change needed.

New `pg_catalog.pg_replication_slots` virtual view in
`internal/initdb/replication_views.go`, registered alongside
`pg_stat_replication` / `pg_stat_wal_receiver` in `initdb.Open`.
Column shape mirrors upstream PG 18.x:

  slot_name, plugin, slot_type, datoid, database, temporary,
  active, active_pid, xmin, catalog_xmin, restart_lsn,
  confirmed_flush_lsn, wal_status, safe_wal_size, two_phase

Columns goopg doesn't track yet (`temporary`, `xmin`,
`active_pid`, `safe_wal_size`, `two_phase`, `datoid`) emit empty
strings / `f` / `0`. `wal_status` is `reserved` for live slots
and `lost` for invalidated ones — the `extended` / `unreserved`
intermediate states aren't surfaced because the retention path
either keeps the slot live or invalidates it outright.

New tests:
  - TestCreateLogicalSlot
  - TestCreateLogicalRequiresPluginAndDatabase
  - TestPhysicalSlotJSONUnchangedAcrossM0008 (forward-compat pin)
  - TestPgReplicationSlotsViewRendersBothKinds

Reorder buffer, snapshot builder, decoder loop, pgoutput plugin,
publication / subscription DDL, apply worker, and the per-slot
catalog-xmin retention hook in vacuum / pruning all remain
deferred to subsequent loops in this milestone.

commits.title: m0007: fdatasync on the WAL commit path
commits.description:
Second slice of M0007. With 0007-0001's segment preallocation
making the inode size stable across commits, the per-segment
flushUpTo sync no longer needs to persist inode metadata. Switch
the commit path from full fsync(2) to fdatasync(2) on Linux to
shave the metadata-flush cost off every commit.

Build-tagged helper `dataSync(f *os.File) error`:

  - sync_linux.go    : unix.Fdatasync(int(f.Fd())) — mirrors
                       upstream's pg_fdatasync from
                       postgres/src/backend/storage/file/fd.c.
  - sync_other.go    : f.Sync() fallback for macOS/BSD/Windows.
                       Preserves the durability contract at the
                       cost of paying for inode metadata updates
                       fdatasync would have skipped.

flushUpTo's loop now calls dataSync(f) per dirty segment instead
of f.Sync(). The misleading "wal: fdatasync %s" error prefix is
now accurate.

Full fsync is preserved at segment creation
(preallocateSegment) and the directory-fsync after creation —
both need durable metadata. wal_sync_method GUC selector,
segment-removal directory fsync, and pgbench latency
measurement remain deferred.

commits.title: m0007: WAL segment preallocation with EOS sentinel
commits.description:
First slice of M0007. Zero-fill new WAL segments to SegmentSize
and fsync them (plus the parent directory) at creation time so
subsequent commit-path syncs no longer pay for inode metadata
updates or filesystem allocations on the hot path.

`wal.Config.Preallocate` (driven by the new `wal_init_zero` GUC,
default `on`) flips on the preallocator. `state.openSegment`
detects first-time creation via `os.Stat`, then writes zeros in
64-KiB chunks across the whole segment via `preallocateSegment`,
fsyncs the file, and fsyncs the directory entry — mirrors
upstream's XLogFileInitInternal + fsync_fname behaviour.

The encoded zero header (`len=0 && crc=0`) is now the EOS
sentinel:
  - `Writer.Append` rejects empty payloads (ErrEmptyPayload).
  - `ReadAll` and `scanLastSegmentEnd` stop on `isZeroHeader`.

`detectWritePos`'s legacy "sum of segment sizes" formula breaks
under preallocation (every segment is full-size). Replaced for
the last segment by `scanLastSegmentEnd`, which walks the
segment record-by-record to find the first zero header —
correct for both legacy short-tail segments and full-size
preallocated tails.

GUC plumbing: `cmd/goopg start` reads `wal_init_zero` via the
new `boolGUC` helper and forwards it through
`initdb.OpenOptions.WALInitZero` → `wal.Config.Preallocate`.

New tests in internal/wal:
  - TestPreallocatedSegmentIsFullSize
  - TestPreallocatedSegmentRecoversCleanly
  - TestAppendRejectsEmptyPayload

`fdatasync` switch (0007-0002), `wal_recycle`, eager next-segment
lookahead, counters, and the pgbench latency measurement remain
deferred.

commits.title: m0006: cost-driven INNER-join algorithm selection
commits.description:
Final slice of M0006. INNER-join algorithm picking moves from the
M0003 rules layer to a cost-driven score under unit-row costs:

  costHash = build + probe = min(L,R) + max(L,R) = L + R
  costMerge = L·log2(L) + R·log2(R) + L + R
  costNL   = L * R

`internal/planner/joincost.go::chooseInnerJoinAlgo(L, R)` returns
the cheapest with ok=true when both inputs have row estimates.
When either side has no estimate (table never ANALYZEd, no row-
count flowed through the bottom-up cardinality pass), the
function returns ok=false and the call site keeps its rule-based
JoinAlgoHash — the documented fallback per the M0006 DoD.

Wired into both INNER call sites:
  - planner.go's planFromRangeVars (the JOIN ... ON path)
  - pushdown.go's pushOneConjunct (CROSS-promotion path)

RIGHT/FULL still pick merge (semantics-driven, not performance);
LEFT still picks hash (executor outer-row preservation depends on
the right being the build side); CROSS and non-equality still
nestloop.

Stats-aware EXPLAIN: `Seq Scan on <t>` appends `(stats)` when the
table has been ANALYZEd, so an operator can see which scans feed
the cost model. Filter and Join nodes already render their
algorithm + estimated rows.

Existing planner tests stay green because they seed catalogs
without ANALYZE so they exercise the fallback path. New tests in
joincost_test.go pin the four-way contract: fallback when stats
missing, hash for balanced 10k/10k, nested-loop for tiny 1/1,
hash beats merge at 100/100.

commits.title: m0006: clauselist-selectivity Filter estimator
commits.description:
Third slice of M0006. The planner finally consumes the MCV lists
and histograms ANALYZE has been collecting — `EstimateRows` for
*Filter no longer collapses every predicate to 1/3.

`internal/planner/selectivity.go` adds `clauseSelectivity`, a
recursive walker shaped after upstream's
postgres/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c clauselist_selectivity:

  - col = const          → MCV-frequency lookup; falls back to
                           (1 - MCV_mass - null_frac) /
                           (NDistinct - len(MCV)), then to 1/200.
  - col <> const         → 1 - eqSel.
  - col <op> const       → equi-depth histogram interpolation
                           (bucketFraction), scoped to non-MCV
                           mass, plus MCV-hit contributions.
  - expr1 AND expr2      → product (independence assumption).
  - expr1 OR  expr2      → inclusion-exclusion.
  - NOT expr             → 1 - sel.
  - col IN (v1, v2, …)   → sum of per-value eqSels, capped at 1.

Constants are rendered through `formatExprConstant` so MCV /
histogram comparisons are byte-equal against the canonical
`Datum.Format()` strings ANALYZE stamped at sample time. New
`columnStatsForChild` walks SeqScan / Filter / Sort / Project
chains to find the per-column stats slot.

Unanalysed tables, unrecognised predicate shapes, ParamRef
constants, two-column predicates, LIKE, and IS NULL all fall
through to `defaultGenericSelectivity` (1/3) — the documented
M0003 fallback. Existing planner tests are unaffected because
they don't exercise the Filter selectivity path with stats
attached.

Cost-driven INNER-join algorithm selection (0006-0004) remains
deferred.

commits.title: docs: add milestones 0007 (WAL preallocation), 0008 (logical replication), 0009 (AIO)
commits.description:
Adds three new planned milestones under docs/milestones/ and updates the
index in README.md to match.

commits.title: m0006: persist TableStats through the catalog snapshot
commits.description:
Second slice of M0006. Stats from ANALYZE — RowCount, Pages,
AvgWidth, NDistinct, NullFrac, MCV lists, equi-depth histograms —
now survive a clean stop / start.

`catalog.TableEntry` grows `Stats *TableStats` (JSON-tagged with
omitempty); `TableStats` / `ColumnStats` / `MCVEntry` get JSON
tags (`row_count`, `pages`, `avg_width`, `columns`, `ndistinct`,
`null_frac`, `mcv`, `histogram`, `value`, `frequency`) so the
on-disk shape is frozen against Go-side renames. `Snapshot()`
deep-copies via a new `cloneTableStats` helper so the snapshot
owns its MCV / histogram slices rather than aliasing the source;
`Restore()` re-installs `Table.Stats` through the same helper.
`<DataDir>/global/pg_catalog.json` now grows the new field on
the next clean stop / start — no production wiring change.

Forward-compat is verified by
`TestRestoreAcceptsLegacySnapshotWithoutStats`: a literal
pre-M0006 JSON snapshot without `stats` keys round-trips cleanly
into `Table.Stats==nil` and presents the table as unanalysed.
End-to-end MCV / histogram round-trip pinned by
`TestSnapshotPreservesTableStats`; the JSON-shape forward-compat
property pinned by `TestSnapshotOmitsStatsWhenNil`.

Planner consumption (0006-0003) and cost-driven join algorithm
selection (0006-0004) remain deferred.

commits.title: m0006: sampling-based ANALYZE with MCV lists and histograms
commits.description:
First slice of M0006 (planner-grade statistics). Replaces M0003's
full distinct-set walk in `internal/executor/operators_analyze.go`
with a reservoir sampler sized at `default_statistics_target * 300`
(upstream's `targrows` from `analyze.c`).

Per-column ColumnStats grows MCV ([]MCVEntry, sorted by frequency
desc) and Histogram ([]string, equi-depth boundaries over the
non-MCV portion) slots. MCV admission uses upstream's margin rule
(freq >= 1.25 * avg_freq(remaining)) capped at statsTarget.
Histograms cover orderable kinds only (int / bool / string / time
/ numeric); bytes and interval columns leave Histogram empty.

The default_statistics_target GUC was already registered but not
honoured; now threaded through executor.Context.StatsTarget from
the session registry on both simple-query and extended-query paths
via a new sessionStatsTarget helper. Context.AnalyzeRandSeed gives
tests a deterministic sampler.

New tests pin the contract: TestAnalyzeBuildsMCVForSkewedColumn
(800/150/50 split → MCV[0]='F' freq ~0.8),
TestAnalyzeBuildsHistogramForOrderedColumn (uniform 1..1000 →
strictly ascending boundaries spanning the range), and
TestAnalyzeRespectsStatsTarget (statsTarget=1 caps the reservoir
at 300 so NDistinct stays ≤300 on a 400-row table). The pre-
existing 7-row pin still passes — small tables collect every
tuple.

Persistence (0006-0002) and planner consumption (0006-0003 /
0006-0004) deferred to subsequent loops. Design doc lands in
this commit; predecessor docs 0003-0003 and 0003-0010 cross-link
to it via `Superseded by`.

commits.title: docs: add lifecycle Makefile and README quickstart
commits.description:
Adds a top-level Makefile that wraps build / init / start / psql / stop /
clean for the typical goopg cluster lifecycle. Every target prepends the
in-tree postgres/local_install bin and lib directories to PATH and
LD_LIBRARY_PATH so the bundled psql resolves its shared libraries
without polluting the operator's environment. README.md gains a
Quickstart section that documents both the make-based flow and the
equivalent raw commands, including the PATH / LD_LIBRARY_PATH
boilerplate operators need when invoking the in-tree client tools by
hand.

commits.title: docs: add M0006 planner-statistics milestone; defer HammerDB SF1 runs
commits.description:
Adds docs/milestones/0006-planner-statistics.md covering sampling-based
ANALYZE, MCV lists, histograms, stats persistence, clauselist
selectivity, and cost-driven INNER-join algorithm selection; indexes it
in docs/milestones/README.md. Marks the two trailing TPC-H items in
.ralph/fix_plan.md (Q1–Q22 parity vs upstream PG, HammerDB Power Test
at SF1) as DEFERRED — running the full HammerDB TPROC-H workload at
SF1 is too long-running for the current acceptance loop, and the
goopg-side compatibility work for those items has already landed.

commits.title: m0005: structured replication event logging + lag warning
commits.description:
Replication lifecycle events used to log as free-form INFO/WARN
lines scattered across the receiver, replayer, walsender, and
retainer. Dashboards had to grep arbitrary text. Slot
invalidation by lag-eviction logged AFTER the slot flipped, with
no early-warning signal.

Ship a canonical event vocabulary so dashboards can gate alerts
on stable event=<name> field values, plus a pre-eviction warning
sweep so operators get a heads-up before a slot is invalidated:

- New internal/wal/repllog.go defines nine event constants
  covering walreceiver lifecycle (dial_failed, connected,
  disconnect), replayer lifecycle (error, stopped),
  walsender_disconnect, slot lifecycle (lag_warning,
  invalidated), and segment recycling.
- SlotAwareRetainer.Retain runs warnLaggingSlots() before
  invalidation: any non-invalidated slot whose lag has crossed
  LagWarnFraction (50%) of max_slot_wal_keep_size emits a
  slot_lag_warning INFO. Per-slot WARN log on actual
  invalidation so alerting can wake somebody up.
- cmd/goopg/main.go startWalreceiver and startStandbyReplayer
  stamp every lifecycle log with the appropriate event= field;
  new walreceiver_connected event proves the handshake
  succeeded (the prior "starting" log fired before the dial).
- internal/server/replication.go walsender adds a deferred
  walsender_disconnect log that fires on every exit path.

Also closes the reconnect-loop-with-backoff fix_plan item:
already implemented in the startWalreceiver goroutine
(exponential 500ms→30s, resumes from rt.WAL.WrittenLSN()).
Audited and confirmed correct; only the new structured logging
is added.

New test TestSlotAwareRetainerEmitsLagWarning + a JSON-decoding
logCapture helper pins the threshold + event-field contract.

Design doc: docs/design/0005-0007-replication-event-logging.md.

commits.title: m0005: replcluster harness + e2e acceptance test
commits.description:
Until this loop the M0005 acceptance criterion (DoD #4) had no
executable cover: every wire-level mechanic was unit-tested
intra-process, but the proof that two `goopg start` binaries
negotiate streaming replication out-of-process didn't exist.

internal/testutil/replcluster composes two *cluster.Cluster
handles with a Setup() that runs the v0 bootstrap (no
pg_basebackup yet): init primary → pre-create slot via
wal.OpenSlots(...).Create(...) while primary is offline → start
primary → stop cleanly → init standby → cloneDataDir from
primary→standby (skips postmaster.pid + .goopg.ctl.sock to
avoid pidfile races) → write standby.signal + append
primary_conninfo + primary_slot_name to standby's
postgresql.conf → restart primary → start standby. Stop()
joins errors; Promote() shells out to `goopg promote`.

TestReplicationEndToEnd exercises the full sequence: Setup →
wait for pg_stat_wal_receiver.status='streaming' → cross-check
pg_stat_replication shows the walsender for our slot → drive a
CHECKPOINT on primary, verify standby's written_lsn advances →
Promote() → verify standby.signal is gone.

Drive-by fix: cmd/goopg/main.go runStart now auto-discovers
<datadir>/postgresql.conf when -config is empty, mirroring
upstream pg_ctl. Without this the standby's primary_conninfo
line was silently ignored.

The "row visibility" / "write to promoted node" pieces are
gated on catalog persistence (v0's catalog is in-memory only).
Wire-connectivity + WAL-flow + LSN-advance + promote are the
strongest e2e checks possible at this milestone.

Design doc: docs/design/0005-0006-replcluster-harness.md.

commits.title: m0005: pg_stat_replication + pg_stat_wal_receiver views
commits.description:
Operators on goopg had no SQL-visible way to see whether a standby
was attached or how much WAL the primary was holding back on its
behalf. This loop ships the two views upstream PostgreSQL uses for
that — column shape mirrors PG 18.x so existing dashboards and
\watch muscle memory transfer verbatim.

- New internal/wal/replmon.go: in-process Senders + Receivers
  registries. Sender handles use atomic CAS for monotonic-forward
  LSN advance (stale standby reply can't push flush_lsn back).
  Receivers is single-slot with reconnect-safe Unregister (a stale
  goroutine's late Unregister doesn't blank the freshly-registered
  reconnected entry). Snapshot returns (slot,pid)-sorted rows so
  \watch shows stable order.
- internal/initdb/replication_views.go: registers
  pg_catalog.pg_stat_replication (21 columns) and
  pg_catalog.pg_stat_wal_receiver (15 columns) backed by the
  registries' Snapshot methods. LSNs render via formatLSN in
  upstream's XXXXXXXX/XXXXXXXX hex form.
- Server.Config grows WalSenders; replyStartReplication
  registers a Sender on entry, defer-unregisters on exit, and
  publishes sent_lsn after each WAL frame + standby-reported LSNs
  after each status reply.
- WalReceiverConfig grows Receivers + Conninfo; DialWalReceiver
  registers, Close unregisters, handleCopyData publishes
  SetReceivedLSN + MarkMessageReceived on each frame.
- initdb.Runtime carries both registries; cmd/goopg/main.go
  threads them into server.Config + WalReceiverConfig.

Lag intervals (write_lag etc.), backend_xmin, client_addr
plumbing, and a pg_replication_slots view are deferred — design
doc enumerates the out-of-scope list.

Tests: 6 registry unit tests (lifecycle, monotonicity, sort,
single-slot reconnect, progress advance, concurrent register
race) + 3 catalog view tests (column shape end-to-end, formatLSN).

Design doc: docs/design/0005-0003-replication-observability.md.

commits.title: m0005: standby promotion (PROMOTE control + goopg promote CLI)
commits.description:
Until this loop a standby could stream WAL forever but never
become a primary. There was no in-place failover path: the operator
had to stop the process, delete standby.signal by hand, and start
a fresh primary, losing the standby.signal-driven recovery
sequencing.

Wire the missing path end-to-end:

- control.Listener gains OnPromote + PROMOTE command handler with
  the same deadline-dropping policy CHECKPOINT uses (drain takes
  seconds). Replies OK only after the handler returns; nil callback
  emits "ERR promote not configured" so a stray promote against a
  primary fails loudly.
- server.Config grows a Promote seam wired into startControlPlane.
- New cmd/goopg/standby.go owns the receiver+replayer goroutines
  via standbyController. Promote(ctx) cancels the receiver, waits,
  snapshots WrittenLSN as the drain target, polls ApplyLSN every
  10ms with a 5s ceiling, cancels the replayer, removes
  standby.signal, and clears Runtime.Standby. Guarded by sync.Once
  + atomic.Bool against concurrent promotes.
- startStandbyReplayer now returns its *wal.StreamReplayer so the
  controller can poll ApplyLSN.
- New `goopg promote -D <dir>` CLI subcommand.

Tests: 3 new control-package tests (dispatch, unconfigured,
handler-error) + 2 cmd/goopg standby tests (idle promote removes
signal idempotently; pending-record promote actually waits for
ApplyLSN to catch up).

Design doc: docs/design/0005-0005-promotion.md.

commits.title: m0005: slot-aware WAL retention
commits.description:
The WAL writer never deleted segments before this commit and
replication slots' RestartLSN was an unread number. Together that
meant pg_wal/ grew unbounded and slots provided no actual retention
guarantee for connected standbys.

Built the recycling kernel as Writer.RemoveOldSegments(keepLSN), a
new opRecycle op on the writer's serialised loop that drops cached
fds, unlinks obsolete segments, and preserves the segment containing
keepLSN. Added Slot.Invalidated + Slots.InvalidateLagging so a slot
that lags past max_slot_wal_keep_size is evicted (mirrors upstream
KeepLogSeg's strict-> semantics) and stops pinning WAL. New
SlotAwareRetainer in internal/wal/retention.go ties them together,
wired into Checkpointer.runCheckpoint via SetRetainer.

initdb.Open now opens Slots so it lives on Runtime; cmd/goopg start
reads max_slot_wal_keep_size from the registry, builds the retainer,
and threads rt.Slots/rt.WAL into server.Config so replication slots
actually work in the production binary.

commits.title: m0005: continuous standby WAL replay (ApplyRecord + StreamReplayer)
commits.description:
Lifts the per-record dispatch out of `wal.ReplayRecords` into a new
`wal.ApplyRecord(mgr, r) (applied, err)` kernel and adds a streaming
`wal.StreamReplayer` driver that consumes from a `RecordIterator` and
applies each record as soon as it lands. Wired into
`cmd/goopg start`'s standby boot path so the receiver + replayer
goroutines run together; the iterator anchors at the writer's
post-recovery `WrittenLSN` and `pd_lsn` idempotency covers
restart-resume without a separate apply cursor. Lands alongside
`docs/design/0005-0002-standby-recovery-and-replay.md`.

commits.title: m0005: standby.signal detection + walreceiver auto-spawn at start
commits.description:
Fifth M0005 implementation slice. Closes the standby-side boot path
so `goopg start` automatically becomes a standby when
`<DataDir>/standby.signal` is present.

internal/initdb/standby.go (new):
- StandbySignalFile = "standby.signal" (mirrors upstream's
  STANDBY_SIGNAL_FILE in xlogrecovery.c).
- IsStandby(dataDir) (bool, error): empty data dir or missing file
  returns (false, nil); other I/O errors surface.
- CreateStandbySignal / RemoveStandbySignal: trigger-file helpers
  for the (future) base-backup tool and the promotion path.
  RemoveStandbySignal is idempotent.

internal/initdb/open.go:
- Runtime gains a `Standby bool` flag set at Open time via
  IsStandby(abs).

internal/config/defaults.go — replication GUCs:
- Primary-side: wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10,
  max_replication_slots=10, wal_sender_timeout=60s,
  max_slot_wal_keep_size=-1.
- Standby-side: primary_conninfo, primary_slot_name,
  wal_receiver_status_interval=10s, recovery_target_timeline=
  latest, hot_standby=on.
Names, units, ranges, defaults mirror upstream's guc_tables.c.
v0 doesn't yet hard-enforce primary-side caps but SET/SHOW
round-trip correctly.

cmd/goopg/main.go:
- New startWalreceiver helper: when Runtime.Standby is true and
  primary_conninfo parses to a host:port, dials a WalReceiver in
  a goroutine and Run's it. Reconnects with exponential backoff
  (500ms → 30s cap) on dial failures or run errors.
- StartLSN seeds from the local WAL writer's WrittenLSN so
  reconnects resume from the durable tail.
- Empty conninfo logs a warning and skips the spawn — useful for
  integration tests that exercise the standby-mode boot path
  without an actual primary.
- New parsePrimaryConninfo: libpq key=value bag parser, honours
  host + port (defaults port to 5432); user / sslmode / etc.
  follow in later loops.

Tests:
- internal/initdb/standby_test.go — three unit tests pin the
  helper contract: absent-returns-false, empty-data-dir,
  Create→IsStandby→Remove round-trip with idempotent double-Remove.

This closes M0005 fix_plan items: "standby.signal detection",
"primary-side replication GUCs", and "standby-side GUCs". The
remaining slice for the M0005 acceptance test is wiring the
streamed WAL into a continuous-replay loop so the standby's data
files actually update mid-stream (today the records land in
pg_wal but apply only on next restart via the existing
crash-recovery path).

commits.title: m0005: add standby-side walreceiver client + end-to-end streaming test
commits.description:
Fourth M0005 implementation slice. Closes the standby-side wire
path so a goopg cluster can now serve as both primary and standby
in a streaming-replication pair.

internal/server/walreceiver.go (new):
- WalReceiver speaks v3 wire protocol directly via the existing
  internal/protocol FrameReader/Writer — no third-party libpq
  dependency.
- DialWalReceiver(ctx, cfg):
    * TCP dial to PrimaryAddr with DialTimeout.
    * v3 startup handshake with replication=true.
    * START_REPLICATION [SLOT name] PHYSICAL X/X.
    * Drains frames until MsgCopyBothResponse confirms streaming
      mode (NoticeResponse and friends ignored).
    * ErrorResponse mid-handshake surfaces with code+message via
      summariseErrorResponse for triage.
- Run(ctx) drives the receive loop in a producer goroutine
  feeding a frame channel; the main select handles ctx.Done,
  CopyData (decoded via protocol.DecodeReplicationMessage),
  CopyDone (treated as clean stream end), and a status-update
  ticker (default 10s, mirroring upstream's
  wal_receiver_status_interval default).
- handleCopyData unwraps 'w' WAL-data payloads and Append's
  them to the local WAL writer; framing identity is preserved
  because the primary's walsender forwards record *payloads*
  (not their on-wire frames) and the standby's writer re-encodes
  with the same len|crc|payload layout. 'k' keepalives with
  replyRequested=true trigger an immediate status update.
- ApplyLSN() exposes the last record's local end-LSN for tests
  and (future) observability views.

internal/protocol/messages.go:
- WriteStartupMessage(params) builds the v3 startup packet with
  no leading type byte: int32 len | int32 protoVersion |
  (key NUL value NUL)* | NUL.
- WriteQuery(sql) emits a 'Q' frame with the trailing NUL the
  protocol requires. Both helpers are now usable by client-side
  code (the walreceiver) without duplicating the framing logic
  test helpers had.

Tests:
- internal/server/walreceiver_test.go —
  TestWalReceiverStreamsRecordsToLocalWAL: start the
  primary-fixture server (with WAL writer + slot store);
  CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT via a separate replication-mode
  connection; dial a WalReceiver pointing at it; Run; push
  three records on the primary; verify the standby's local
  pg_wal contains byte-identical record payloads in order
  with ApplyLSN equal to the standby writer's WrittenLSN.

This closes the gating slice for the M0005 acceptance test:
goopg can now run a primary+standby pair end-to-end with
streaming WAL. The next slice adds <DataDir>/standby.signal
detection so `goopg start` enters standby mode automatically and
spawns the walreceiver from configuration, plus a
recovery-loop integration so the standby applies the streamed
records into its data files.

commits.title: m0005: streaming WAL iterator + walsender for START_REPLICATION
commits.description:
Third M0005 implementation slice. Builds on the previous loops'
wire-protocol seam (MsgCopyBoth + WAL-data/keepalive/status framings)
and slot store (CREATE/DROP_REPLICATION_SLOT, IDENTIFY_SYSTEM) with:

internal/wal/writer.go — flush-event subscription:
- Writer.Subscribe(ch) / Unsubscribe(ch). The writer goroutine
  invokes notifyAppend after every successful append; sends are
  non-blocking so a stuck subscriber can't back-pressure the WAL
  writer. Subscribers wake on each append and re-poll WrittenLSN
  ("WAL has advanced" is idempotent).

internal/wal/iterator.go (new) — streaming record iterator:
- NewRecordIterator(writer, walDir, segSize, startLSN) returns a
  cursor that yields one Record per Next(ctx) call, decoding
  records on the fly from the segment files, transparently
  spanning segment boundaries.
- When the cursor catches up to WrittenLSN, Next blocks on the
  writer's subscription channel, returning promptly on
  ctx.Done() or wal.ErrClosed.
- Each yielded payload is a fresh slice the caller may retain.

internal/server/replication.go — walsender:
- replyStartReplication parses the upstream grammar
  `START_REPLICATION [SLOT name] PHYSICAL X/X [TIMELINE n]`,
  acquires the slot via SetActive(true), replies with
  WriteCopyBothResponse, then runs a three-legged loop:
    * producer goroutine — pumps RecordIterator.Next results
      into a buffered channel, ends on ctx.Done.
    * receiver goroutine — decodes inbound CopyData frames
      (StandbyStatusUpdate from libpq's walreceiver shape) and
      advances the slot's ConfirmedFlushLSN via
      Slots.AdvanceConfirmedFlushLSN. Ends on ReadFrame error
      (connection closed) or CopyDone.
    * main select — encodes each Record into an EncodeWALData
      frame and emits via WriteCopyData; emits keepalives via
      EncodeKeepalive every 10s when no records arrive;
      cleans up on cancel / EOF / iterator error.
- Single-timeline only (TIMELINE != 1 → feature_not_supported);
  LOGICAL rejected with the same code.

internal/server/server.go — wiring:
- Config.WALDirPath / WALSegmentSize fields so the walsender
  knows where to open WAL segments. nil/empty disables
  START_REPLICATION with feature_not_supported, matching the
  Slots-nil pattern.
- handleReplicationCommand now takes ctx + FrameReader so the
  walsender can subscribe to upstream wake-ups and read inbound
  client frames.

Tests:
- internal/wal/iterator_test.go — four tests pin the iterator
  contract (read existing, block-then-wake on Append, context
  cancel, mid-stream startLSN skip).
- internal/server/replication_test.go — two new tests:
    * TestReplicationStartReplicationStreamsRecord exercises
      the full walsender path: client → CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT
      → START_REPLICATION → primary Appends → client decodes
      a WAL-data 'w' CopyData frame and verifies payload + LSN
      range against the writer's report.
    * TestReplicationStartReplicationRejectsLogical pins the
      LOGICAL rejection and connection survival afterwards.

This closes the gating slice for the M0005 acceptance test:
goopg can now serve a libpq-compatible walsender stream backed by
its own WAL writer. The next slice adds the standby-side walreceiver
process and the end-to-end replcluster harness.

commits.title: m0005: add replication-slot store + IDENTIFY_SYSTEM / CREATE/DROP_SLOT
commits.description:
Second M0005 implementation slice. Builds on the wire-protocol seam
from the previous loop with the three replication-mode commands a
v0 walreceiver needs before it can stream:

internal/wal/slots.go (new) — replication-slot registry:
- Slot{Name, Kind, RestartLSN, ConfirmedFlushLSN, Active}.
- Persisted to <DataDir>/pg_replslot/<slot>/state as JSON via
  tempfile+rename for crash-safe rewrites.
- OpenSlots rehydrates every slot at startup.
- Create / Drop / Get / List / AdvanceConfirmedFlushLSN /
  SetActive / MinRestartLSN.
- Slot-name validation matches upstream's [a-z0-9_]{1,63}
  (postgres/src/backend/replication/slot.c
  ReplicationSlotValidateName).
- Active slots can't be dropped (ErrSlotInUse).
- AdvanceConfirmedFlushLSN is monotonic; it never moves an LSN
  backward.
- MinRestartLSN exposes the WAL retention anchor for the future
  segment-recycling integration.

internal/server/replication.go (new) — wire-layer dispatcher:
- handleReplicationCommand peels off recognised replication verbs
  before the regular SQL path. Unknown commands fall through so
  utility commands like SHOW still work for diagnostics on a
  replication connection.
- IDENTIFY_SYSTEM emits the upstream-aligned 4-column reply
  (systemid text, timeline int4, xlogpos text as `X/X` hex,
  dbname NULL for physical).
- CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT name PHYSICAL creates a slot and emits
  the upstream-shaped (slot_name, consistent_point,
  snapshot_name=NULL, output_plugin=NULL) response.
- DROP_REPLICATION_SLOT name removes a slot.
- Slot errors map to upstream-aligned SQLSTATEs (42710, 42704,
  55006, 22023).

internal/server/server.go — wiring:
- New Config fields: Slots *wal.Slots, WAL *wal.Writer,
  SystemID string. All optional; nil disables the corresponding
  feature with feature_not_supported.
- runPostStartupLoop now takes an isReplication bool and routes
  MsgQuery through handleReplicationCommand first when set.
- isReplicationStartupParam already plumbed in the previous loop.

Tests:
- internal/wal/slots_test.go — six tests (CRUD, duplicate
  rejection, name validation, active-drop guard, monotonic LSN
  advance + MinRestartLSN, persistence round-trip).
- internal/server/replication_test.go — three integration tests
  driving the wire from a real client conn: IDENTIFY_SYSTEM
  reply shape, CREATE then DROP slot lifecycle (verifying both
  the wire response and the on-disk store), and slot-name
  validation error path with continued connection use afterwards.

START_REPLICATION + walsender goroutine ship in the next M0005
loop, building on the same handler dispatch.

commits.title: m0005: add MsgCopyBoth + WAL-data/keepalive/status replication framing
commits.description:
First implementation slice for streaming replication, per the
hook list in 0005-0001-streaming-replication-architecture.md.

Wire-protocol additions:
- internal/protocol/protocol.go: MsgCopyBothResponse ('W') backend
  frame type next to CopyInResponse / CopyOutResponse.
- internal/protocol/replication.go (new): four encoders matching
  upstream PostgreSQL 18.3's walprotocol layout —
    'w' WAL-data:        startLSN(8) | endLSN(8) | sendTime(8) | payload
    'k' keepalive:       walEnd(8)   | sendTime(8) | replyRequested(1)
    'r' standby status:  writeLSN(8) | flushLSN(8) | applyLSN(8) | sendTime(8) | replyRequested(1)
    plus WriteCopyBothResponse on FrameWriter.
- DecodeReplicationMessage classifies a CopyData payload by its
  first byte and returns one of (*WALDataMessage,
  *KeepaliveMessage, *StandbyStatusUpdate) — used by both the
  primary-side walsender (to consume client status updates) and
  the standby-side walreceiver (to consume server WAL/keepalive).
- PgTimestampMicros / PgTimestampToTime convert against the
  upstream TimestampTz epoch (2000-01-01 UTC, microseconds), the
  same shape walsender.c emits.

Server wiring:
- internal/server/server.go: parse `replication` from the
  StartupMessage parameter bag via new isReplicationStartupParam
  helper. true / 1 / `database` (logical, treated as physical in
  v0) / any non-false value enables replication mode; tag is added
  to the per-conn logger and reserved for the next loop's
  IDENTIFY_SYSTEM / START_REPLICATION command-dispatch routing.

Tests pin the wire-format contract (round-trip for each of the
three inner messages, epoch-zero + 1-second sanity, and
unknown-byte rejection).

This is purely the seam — no walsender goroutine, no slot
machinery, no standby mode yet. The next M0005 loop adds
IDENTIFY_SYSTEM + CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT + START_REPLICATION
command handlers on top of these encoders.

commits.title: m0005: design doc for streaming replication architecture
commits.description:
Open M0005 (streaming replication) with the gating architecture
design doc. Covers:

- Process model: per-standby walsender goroutine on the primary
  spawned from a START_REPLICATION SQL command; standby
  walreceiver process feeding a single libpq-style connection
  to the primary; both reusing the existing per-connection
  goroutine model.
- Wire-protocol surface: replication=true in StartupMessage,
  IDENTIFY_SYSTEM / CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT / START_REPLICATION
  simple-query handlers, MsgCopyBoth ('W') as the new outer
  frame type, and inner WAL-data ('w') / keepalive ('k') /
  standby-status ('r') framings wire-compatible with upstream
  PG 18.3 (postgres/src/backend/replication/walsender.c +
  walreceiver.c shapes).
- State-transition diagram (Authenticated -> Streaming with
  reconnect cycle); promotion path via a new control-socket
  PROMOTE command.
- Replication-slot retention semantics: WAL recycling consults
  min(slot.RestartLSN) bounded by max_slot_wal_keep_size; slot
  invalidation on overrun mirrors upstream.
- GUC surface: wal_level, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots,
  wal_sender_timeout, max_slot_wal_keep_size on the primary;
  primary_conninfo, primary_slot_name,
  wal_receiver_status_interval, recovery_target_timeline,
  hot_standby on the standby.
- Hook list with concrete file:line references in
  internal/protocol/, internal/server/, internal/wal/,
  internal/control/, cmd/goopg/ for each implementation
  follow-up loop's seam.
- Out-of-scope: BASE_BACKUP wire command (replaced with a CLI
  base-snapshot tool), logical replication, sync replication,
  multi-timeline operation, cascading replication.

fix_plan.md decomposed into ~25 follow-up items grouped under:
architecture, wire protocol, WAL streaming machinery, replication
slots, standby side, configuration surface, promotion,
observability, and acceptance test.

Indexed as 0005-0001 in docs/design/README.md with `accepted`
status. The two companion docs (0005-0002 standby recovery and
0005-0003 observability) remain to be written before their
implementation lands.

commits.title: bench: add HammerDB-driven TPC-H runner against local PostgreSQL
commits.description:
Adds bench/tpch with shell + Tcl scripts that drive HammerDB 5.0 to
build the smallest-scale-factor (SF=1) TPC-H schema and run the
22-query power test against a temporary PostgreSQL cluster booted
from postgres/local_install. No server-side stored procedures are
used; all DDL, bulk loads, and queries are issued from the client.

The HammerDB tarball and the extracted release stay out of version
control via .gitignore, alongside the ephemeral runtime/ and logs/
directories the scripts populate.

commits.title: m0003: close codec / copy-text NUMERIC fallback gaps + regression tests
commits.description:
Audit per the previous loop's recommendation found two remaining
fallback paths where KindNumeric fell through to an explicit error
instead of being formatted as text:

- internal/executor/codec.go encodeValue() variable-length
  text-like fallback: a NUMERIC datum encoded against an
  unrecognised type name errored with "kind 6 cannot encode as
  <type>". Now formats via formatNumeric() to match the dedicated
  numeric arm above.
- internal/executor/copy_text.go datumToCopyText() default
  type-name handler: same shape, same fix.

Both were defensive — explicit errors rather than silent
fallthrough — but the hash-key bug and IN-list bug from the last
two loops both surfaced as silent failures that were hard to
diagnose, so closing the remaining KindNumeric gaps proactively
removes the next one before it's hit.

Also pin the existing fixes with regression tests:
- TestCanonicalNumericKey: 1, 1.0, 1.00 all canonicalise to m:1:0.
- TestDatumKeyNumericInteger: cross-kind hash compatibility
  (KindInt(1) and KindNumeric(1, 0) hash equal).
- TestCompareEqNumericIntList: compareEq across NUMERIC↔INT, with
  symmetry and NULL propagation.

These guard against regression of the parity-matrix fixes (Q3, Q5,
Q7, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q13 NUMERIC-hash-key cluster + Q16 IN-list
NUMERIC fix).

commits.title: m0003: route NUMERIC through compareEq; closes Q16 parity gap
commits.description:
compareEq() in internal/executor/expr.go (used by `IN (val_list)`
and the simple form of `CASE`) had no KindNumeric arm. Q16's
`p_size in (49, 14, 23, 45, 19, 3, 36, 9)` against the
`p_size NUMERIC` column always evaluated to false because the
int literals (KindInt) never matched the NUMERIC datums via
the kind-by-kind switch. Goopg returned 0 rows where upstream
returned 3.

Fix: when either operand is KindNumeric, delegate to compareDatum
which already handles cross-kind NUMERIC↔INT promotion via
numericFromInt and scale-aware mantissa comparison via numericCmp.
Incompatible kinds fall through to false (instead of erroring) so
IN-list semantics stay tolerant.

Parity matrix: identical 18 -> 19, divergent 4 -> 3. The 3
remaining divergences (Q1, Q8, Q14) are all pure NUMERIC precision
deltas gated on arbitrary-precision NUMERIC, deferred per design
0003-0012. No structural gaps remain on the synthetic dataset.

This is technically the same root-cause family as last loop's
datumKey fix — both came from KindNumeric being a kind without
a corresponding handler in a kind-switch. Future audit candidate:
grep for `case Kind*` switches missing KindNumeric arms.

commits.title: m0003: hash NUMERIC datums correctly; closes 7/11 parity divergences
commits.description:
datumKey() in internal/executor/operators_join_agg.go (used by
hash-join, count-distinct, and group-by hashing) had no
KindNumeric arm in its switch, so every NUMERIC value fell
through to the fmt.Sprintf("k:%d", d.Kind) fallback and hashed to
a single bucket. Since every TPC-H join key column (c_custkey,
o_custkey, l_orderkey, ps_partkey, etc.) is declared NUMERIC,
every NUMERIC-keyed hash join degenerated to a cross product —
goopg silently returned all-pairs combinations.

Surfaced by TestTPCHResultParity which showed Q3 returning 5 rows
where upstream returned 1, all with the same revenue and only
varying o_orderdate. Trace via psql/EXPLAIN confirmed the inner
Hash Join was emitting cross-product output.

Fix: extend datumKey to handle KindNumeric and KindInterval, with
a new helper `canonicalNumericKey(mantissa, scale)` that strips
trailing-zero pairs (one digit + one scale step at a time) until
either the scale reaches 0 or the trailing digit is non-zero. So
`1` (m=1,s=0), `1.0` (m=10,s=1), and `1.00` (m=100,s=2) all
canonicalise to `m:1:0` — required since two numerics that compare
equal MUST hash equal. KindInt now also routes through
canonicalNumericKey at scale 0 so cross-kind hashes match
(`aid = $1` works whether $1 lands as KindInt or scale-0
KindNumeric).

Parity matrix improvement: identical 11 -> 18, divergent 11 -> 4.
Closed Q3, Q5, Q7, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q13 in one fix. Q8 newly shows
NUMERIC-precision divergence (1.000000 vs 1.00000000000000000000)
because the join now runs correctly and exposes the underlying
precision delta. Remaining 4 divergences:
- Q1, Q8, Q14: NUMERIC precision (arbitrary-precision NUMERIC
  deferred per design 0003-0012).
- Q16: NOT IN (subquery) returns 0 vs upstream 3 — likely
  3VL-on-NULL handling.

Design doc 0003-0017 updated with the new matrix and triage
workstream reflecting the closure.

commits.title: m0003: add TPC-H result-parity test vs upstream PostgreSQL 18.3
commits.description:
Build the in-tree parity tester that closes the M0003 DoD #3 loop
on a synthetic dataset. The test runs each Q1..Q22 against both
goopg and upstream PostgreSQL 18.3 on the SAME 75-row synthetic
dataset and diffs the rows.

Components added:
- internal/testutil/tpch/upstreampg_test.go — minimal lifecycle
  wrapper for upstream PG (initdb / pg_ctl start / libpq query /
  pg_ctl stop) that runs in a per-test tempdir on a free port
  with fsync=off + LC_ALL=C so byte-wise text comparison works.
- internal/testutil/tpch/parity_test.go — TestTPCHResultParity:
  applies tpch.DDL() + tpch.SampleInserts() to both engines,
  ANALYZEs all 8 tables, then runs each query and records
  status/rowcount/first-diff. Logs a parity matrix; fails closed
  only on goopg-errors-while-upstream-OK (a real regression).

Skip conditions: testing.Short() OR upstream PG missing under
postgres/local_install/bin. Runs ~36s on dev machines with the
upstream install.

Current matrix on synthetic data:
  identical=11  divergent=11  goopg-errored=0  upstream-errored=0

Divergences group into three independent triage clusters:
  - NUMERIC precision in division (Q1, Q14) — gated on
    arbitrary-precision NUMERIC (deferred per 0003-0012).
  - Row-count divergences from join / GROUP BY semantics
    (Q3, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q13) — goopg consistently returns
    more rows than upstream; the highest-impact bug surface to
    investigate next.
  - NOT IN / HAVING scalar subquery semantics (Q11, Q16) —
    likely 3VL-on-NULL or scalar materialisation drift.

Indexed as docs/design/0003-0017-result-parity-testing.md with
the full triage workstream.

SF1 parity remains gated on the Docker / WSL2 reachability
infrastructure issue (see fix_plan.md 2026-04-29 SF1 attempt
notes); synthetic-data parity catches most semantic gaps at
much lower cost.

commits.title: m0003: cost-based join-order reordering for comma-FROM
commits.description:
Add a parser-level pre-pass that permutes the comma-FROM list so
small-cardinality tables join first when ANALYZE has supplied row
counts. Greedy nearest-neighbour by cardinality with equality-edge
preference; bare-column refs resolved via a column->relation owner
map (TPC-H queries write `c_custkey = o_custkey` rather than
`c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey`).

Operating at parser-AST level means no resolved ColumnRef.Index
needs remapping: the entire planner sees the new order as if the
user had written it that way. The pass aborts (preserving source
order) when:
- any FROM table lacks ANALYZE stats,
- any FromExpr carries an explicit JOIN ... ON clause,
- a derived-table subquery is in the FROM list,
- len(FROM) < 3, or
- the greedy pick equals source order.

Wires into planSelect via a SelectStmt copy when the rewrite
applies, so the original parser AST is never mutated.

TPC-H Q5's `customer, orders, lineitem, supplier, nation, region`
now reorders to `region, nation, supplier, lineitem, orders,
customer`, joining the 5-row dimension table first instead of
materialising 1500 x 15000 x 60000 rows up front.

Pinned by:
- planner.TestReorderCommaFromByCardinality (the canonical 6-table
  Q5 shape with row counts 5/25/100/1500/15000/60000),
- planner.TestReorderCommaFromByCardinalityNoStats,
- planner.TestReorderCommaFromByCardinalitySkipsExplicitJoin.
End-to-end exercised through TestRunTPCHQueriesAgainstSyntheticData
which ANALYZEs every table; all 22 queries continue to execute
with the reorder applied.

Marks the M0003 "Cost-based planner" item complete; design doc
0003-0016-join-order-reordering.md indexed in docs/design/README.md.

commits.title: m0003: TPC-H Q1-Q22 execute end-to-end; fix exprType for arithmetic
commits.description:
Add a true executor-time TPC-H smoke harness in
internal/testutil/tpch.TestRunTPCHQueriesAgainstSyntheticData. It
spins up a real goopg cluster, applies the eight TPC-H CREATE TABLE
strings, loads a small synthetic dataset (5-15 rows per table,
referentially consistent), and runs each Q1..Q22 against the live
server. Fail-closed: any pq error fails the test.

The first run surfaced a wire-format bug. 8 of 22 queries
(Q1/Q3/Q5/Q6/Q7/Q9/Q10/Q11) errored with the Go libpq driver
raising `strconv.ParseInt: parsing "20667.0000": invalid syntax`
on the result of `sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount))` and
similar aggregate-of-arithmetic shapes. Root cause:
`planner.exprType` only inspected *ColumnRef and returned
unknown for everything else. `buildAggregateCall` for sum then
fell back to int8 for the output type, the wire layer advertised
TypeOID 20 (int8), and the client's int8 text scanner choked on
the formatted decimal.

Fix: expand exprType to walk BinaryOp / UnaryOp / CaseExpr /
ExtractExpr / FuncCall / typed constants. Arithmetic with any
numeric operand promotes to numeric; comparison / boolean / LIKE
return bool; `||` returns text; extract / count return int8;
to_date / to_timestamp return date / timestamp; substr / substring
return text. CASE takes its first When branch's type as
representative.

After the fix, all 22 queries execute end-to-end on the synthetic
dataset (returning 0..25 rows depending on whether the
parameter-substituted filters match). Result-set parity vs
upstream PG is still pending the HammerDB SF1 harness path.

Also exposes tpch.DDL() and tpch.SampleInserts() helpers in the
shared testutil/tpch fixture so any future end-to-end test can
reuse the same load.

commits.title: m0003: extract TPC-H fixture; add executor Build smoke for Q1-Q22
commits.description:
Move the 8-table catalog + Q1..Q22 SQL templates out of
internal/planner/tpch_test.go (where they were _test-locked) into a
new internal/testutil/tpch package that both planner-side and
executor-side tests can consume.

Add internal/executor.TestBuildTPCHQueries to chase the planner's
output through executor.Build so every TPC-H query constructs a
complete operator tree. This catches plan-node → operator-node
gaps that the plan-time test alone can't see (e.g., a planner that
emits an unsupported Node type silently won't fail Plan, but will
fail Build). All 22 queries plan AND build today; the tests fail
closed if any regression is introduced.

Slim down internal/planner/tpch_test.go to consume the shared
fixture; the must-pass list is now the full 1..22 range since the
prior soft-list was always satisfied. Design doc 0003-0004 updated
to describe the two-tier coverage.

commits.title: m0003: add Q1-Q22 plan-time coverage test plus substr/to_date
commits.description:
Pin TPC-H query plannability with a new
internal/planner.TestPlanTPCHQueriesPlannable that seeds the eight
HammerDB-shaped tables and asks planner.Plan to produce a node tree
for each Q1..Q22 SQL with parameters substituted from HammerDB's
sub_query() default range. All 22 queries plan against the v0
planner today; the test guards against regressions while
execution-time gaps are filled in.

Two missing built-in functions surfaced and were added to unblock
the executor path:

- substr(text, int [, int]) / substring for Q22's country-code
  prefix extraction. 1-based indexing, NULL propagation,
  negative-length 22011 error matches upstream's text_substring.
- to_date(text, fmt) for Q15's view-defining
  WHERE l_shipdate >= to_date('1996-01-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD').
  Reuses pgFormatToGoLayout from to_timestamp and truncates the
  parsed instant to midnight UTC so the value behaves like a DATE.

Unit tests pin both contracts. Design doc 0003-0004 updated with
the new entry under "Q1-Q22 plan-time coverage" and the moved
NUMERIC-arithmetic note.

commits.title: docs: add milestone for streaming replication support
commits.description: Agent-Logs-Url: https://github.com/ryogrid/goopg/sessions/e5f8ee0a-59e6-454a-b732-d976229df0f3

commits.title: m0003: SF1 attempt finds Docker --network host blocker on WSL2
commits.description:
Surfaced by actually running Docker HammerDB SF1 buildschema
against goopg this loop. With every recent loop's compatibility
work in place (pg_indexes/pg_database/pg_roles/pg_tables,
targetless SELECT FROM, NUMERIC arithmetic, LIKE / BETWEEN /
embedded interval, derived tables, ORDER BY / GROUP BY alias,
predicate pushdown, hash-join build-side selection,
shared_buffers GUC, ALTER USER no-op, 24+ stub GUCs), goopg's
listener bound cleanly at [::]:55440 with shared_buffers=256MB
and the host's psql connected and ran SELECT 1 successfully.

But Vuser 1 (HammerDB's Monitor Thread) inside the Docker
container errored at the first connect:
  could not connect to server: Connection refused

goopg's server log records ZERO connection attempts during the
run — TCP is being refused before reaching the listener. With
host networking declared (--network host), Docker on WSL2 falls
back to bridge semantics; the container's 127.0.0.1 is its own
loopback, not the host's, so the goopg listener is unreachable.

This is a test-infrastructure constraint, not a goopg bug. The
handover note in fix_plan.md (section 2026-04-29 SF1 attempt)
documents the finding and lists workarounds for bare-metal
Linux / WSL2 / Mac+Windows Docker Desktop setups. A successful
SF1 buildschema is now a question of which environment the run
happens in — the goopg-side compatibility is closed.

commits.title: m0003: register common JDBC / planner-toggle / log_* GUC stubs
commits.description:
Surfaced by smoke-running common JDBC-issued SETs against
goopg — all failed with `unrecognized configuration
parameter`:
  - transaction_isolation (JDBC's getTransactionIsolation())
  - enable_seqscan / indexscan / indexonlyscan / bitmapscan /
    hashjoin / mergejoin / nestloop / sort / hashagg /
    material / partition_pruning (planner toggles —
    upstream test scripts use these to force specific plan
    shapes)
  - lock_timeout, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
  - log_statement, log_min_duration_statement
  - default_statistics_target

config: register all of them in BuildDefaultRegistry as
ContextUserset (or ContextSuset for log_*). Names, units,
ranges, and defaults mirror upstream's
postgres/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c entries.
transaction_isolation gets FlagReport so SHOW works without
a separate Set path. v0 doesn't honour any of these
semantically — the planner still uses its rules-based
decisions and the loggers ignore the verbosity GUCs — but
SET / SHOW succeed which is what JDBC, pgAdmin, DBeaver,
and upstream test fixtures need to proceed.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3: all SETs succeed, SHOW returns
canonical values, unit-converted forms (`SET
idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '60s'` -> 60000) work
correctly. Design doc root-0004 updated to enumerate the new
entries.

commits.title: m0003: register HammerDB workload-runner compat GUCs
commits.description:
Surfaced by smoke-running the SET statements HammerDB / psql /
pgbench issue before TPC-H queries: all seven failed with
`unrecognized configuration parameter`. Even though the
bootstrap and checkschema flows now resolve, the workload
runner's pre-query SETs would still abort the run.

config: register seven new GUCs in BuildDefaultRegistry as
ContextUserset (settable from SQL):
  - max_parallel_workers_per_gather (int, default 2)
  - client_min_messages (enum, default 'notice')
  - statement_timeout (int ms, default 0)
  - work_mem (int KB, default 4MB)
  - random_page_cost (real, default 4.0)
  - effective_cache_size (int KB, default 4GB)
  - search_path (string, default `"$user", public`)

Names, units, ranges, and defaults mirror upstream's
postgres/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c entries. v0
doesn't actually honour any of these semantically — the
planner / executor / search_path-resolution all ignore the
values — but registering them lets `SET` succeed and `SHOW`
return sensible canonical values, which is what the workload
runners need.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3: all seven SETs succeed,
unit-converted forms (`SET work_mem='64MB'` → 65536) work
correctly, and `SHOW <name>` round-trips. Design doc
root-0004 updated to list the new entries.

commits.title: m0003: pg_database / pg_roles / pg_tables + targetless SELECT
commits.description:
HammerDB's bootstrap and checkschema probe four pg_catalog shapes: - SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = '' - SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '' - SELECT 1 FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' - SELECT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND tablename='') Without these the buildschema flow can't start: HammerDB errors with `relation "pg_database" does not exist` before issuing any CREATE TABLE.
