Last loop landed pg_indexes; this loop closes the bootstrap probes. Catalog: three new virtual views alongside pg_class / pg_indexes: - pg_database — single seeded `postgres` row. Queries for other names filter to zero, taking HammerDB's CREATE DATABASE branch (absorbed by dispatch.go's no-op compat tag). - pg_roles — same shape, single `postgres` row. CREATE USER + GRANT + ALTER USER all flow through compat tags. - pg_tables — walks user (non-virtual) tables in deterministic key order, emitting (schemaname, tablename, tableowner). checkschema's existence probe needs targetless SELECT (below). Dispatch: ALTER USER / ALTER ROLE join the existing CREATE USER / CREATE DATABASE / GRANT no-op compatibility tags. HammerDB issues `ALTER USER PASSWORD '

'` after pg_roles returns non-empty, and that needs to silently succeed. Parser: parseSelect now accepts an empty target list when the next token is FROM. Upstream PG allows `SELECT FROM tbl` (one zero-column row per source row); HammerDB writes `SELECT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_tables WHERE …)` with this shape and v0 was rejecting it at parse time. Smoke-verified via psql 18.3 against all four HammerDB probe shapes plus the EXISTS / non-existing-table edge cases. TestPgCatalogBootstrapViews pins the lookup and VirtualRows shape. Design doc 0003-0015 grows three new sections. Out of scope: configurable search_path GUC, real multi-database/multi-role tracking, indexdef/tablespace reconstruction, the rest of pg_catalog (pg_namespace, pg_attribute, pg_index).

commits.title: m0003: pg_catalog.pg_indexes view for HammerDB checkschema
commits.description:
HammerDB's checkschema step probes
`SELECT tablename, indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename
 = '<t>'` to verify each TPC-H table has at least one index
after CreateIndexes runs. Without pg_indexes the probe raised
`relation "pg_indexes" does not exist`; HammerDB then aborted
with `TPROC-H Schema check failed ... no indices` before the
workload could start.

Catalog: register a second virtual view alongside pg_class.
pg_catalog.pg_indexes carries (schemaname, tablename,
indexname, tablespace, indexdef); the row provider walks
non-virtual user tables and their indexes in deterministic
key order. tablespace and indexdef are empty strings — v0
doesn't track them and HammerDB only reads tablename +
indexname.

LookupTable: when an unqualified lookup misses, retry under
the pg_catalog schema. This mirrors upstream's implicit
`search_path` entry where pg_catalog is always first; users
can write `pg_indexes` / `pg_class` without a qualifier and
v0 resolves them. User tables are unaffected because the
strict path matches first.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3 against HammerDB's exact query
shape: returns one row per index, empty result for
non-indexed tables, both `pg_indexes` (new) and `pg_class`
(regression check) resolve unqualified.

`TestPgIndexesView` pins the lookup, the virtual flag, and the
VirtualRows shape. Design doc 0003-0015 added and indexed;
fix_plan.md grows the bullet under §"Schema and loader".

Out of scope: configurable search_path GUC, indexdef /
tablespace reconstruction, the rest of pg_catalog
(pg_namespace, pg_attribute, pg_index).

commits.title: m0003: derived tables — `(SELECT …) AS alias` in FROM
commits.description:
Surfaced by running TPC-H Q13 end-to-end against goopg:
`FROM (SELECT c_custkey, count(o_orderkey) AS c_count FROM
customer LEFT OUTER JOIN orders ... GROUP BY c_custkey) AS
c_orders` parse-errored at the `(SELECT...)` shape. Closing
the last big TPC-H query-coverage gap.

Parser: parser.RangeVar grows a `Subquery *SelectStmt` field.
parseRangeVar's two-token lookahead `( + SELECT` parses the
inner SELECT, requires `)`, and demands a mandatory alias
(matches upstream's "subquery in FROM must have an alias"
rule). The resulting RangeVar has Name="" and Subquery!=nil
so existing JOIN / multi-table-comma-FROM handling on the
outside continues to work.

Analyzer: lookupTable branches on rv.Subquery!=nil to
synthesizeSubqueryTable, which analyzes the inner with no
parent scope (v0 doesn't support LATERAL — derived tables
can't reference outer columns), walks the target list to
derive column names (alias / bare-ColumnRef name /
function name / `?column?N`) and types via analyzeExpr,
and returns a transient *catalog.Table with Name=alias.
Never registered in catalog.

Planner: planScanRangeVar dispatches to
planSubqueryRangeVar when rv.Subquery!=nil. That helper
plans the inner via Plan(rv.Subquery, cat) and exposes its
Output() through a synthetic rangeBinding so outer ColumnRefs
to `alias.col` resolve normally. The inner plan can contain
any planner construct (joins, aggregates, sub-derived-tables,
CASE, LIKE, NUMERIC) because we recurse through Plan.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3:
- Q13's full shape with LEFT OUTER JOIN + NOT LIKE inside
  the derived table returns the expected histogram (0→2
  customers, 1→1, 2→1).
- Simple `FROM (SELECT a AS k FROM t WHERE ...) AS s ORDER
  BY s.k` works.
- Derived table without explicit aliases falls back to the
  derived names so outer `s.c_custkey` resolves correctly.
- Missing-alias case rejected at parse time.

`TestPlanDerivedTable` pins the four behaviours. Design doc
0003-0014 added and indexed; fix_plan.md grows the bullet.

Out of scope: LATERAL, CTEs (WITH), parenthesised plain
relations, set-operations inside derived tables.

commits.title: m0003: GROUP BY <alias> / <positional> substitution
commits.description:
Surfaced by running TPC-H Q7 end-to-end against goopg:
`extract(year FROM o_orderdate) AS yr ... GROUP BY yr`
errored with `column "yr" does not exist`. Q4 / Q5 worked
without changes (predicate-pushdown + EXISTS + 6-way joins);
Q7 hit this single gap.

GROUP BY accepts target-list aliases and positional indices
the same way ORDER BY does (PG extension; SQL standard
requires fully-qualified expressions). Both analyzer and
planner now route each GROUP BY entry through the same
substitution helper that already services ORDER BY:

  - Bare unqualified `ColumnRef` whose Column matches a
    target's Alias → target's parser expression.
  - `IntegerConst N` → `targets[N-1].Expr`.
  - Qualified `t.col` falls through to FROM-clause resolution.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3:
- TPC-H Q7-style `GROUP BY yr` over `extract(year FROM
  o_orderdate) AS yr` returns correct row counts.
- `GROUP BY 1` works for positional refs.
- `GROUP BY xx` over `a + 10 AS xx` aggregates correctly.

`TestPlanGroupByAliasAndPositional` pins the two planner
behaviours. Design doc 0003-0001's ORDER BY substitution
section retitled to cover GROUP BY too.

Q4 (EXISTS subquery) and Q5 (6-way join with multiple
WHERE-equalities) verified working in the same smoke run with
no code changes — predicate-pushdown, build-side selection,
NUMERIC arithmetic, BETWEEN, embedded-unit interval, and
ORDER BY alias substitution from prior loops carry them.

commits.title: m0003: ORDER BY <alias> / <positional> substitution
commits.description:
Surfaced by running TPC-H Q3 end-to-end against goopg:
`ORDER BY revenue DESC, o_orderdate` errored with
`column "revenue" does not exist`. SQL allows ORDER BY to
reference target-list aliases (TPC-H Q3/Q5/Q9/Q10/Q21 all use
this) and positional indices (`ORDER BY 1, 2`). v0 didn't.

Both analyzer and planner now substitute the underlying target
expression before resolving columns, via parallel helpers
`analyzer.orderBySubstitution` and
`planner.resolveOrderBySubstitution`:

  - Bare `ColumnRef` (no schema/table qualifier) whose column
    name case-insensitively matches a target's Alias becomes
    that target's parser expression.
  - `IntegerConst N` becomes `targets[N-1].Expr`.
  - Anything else (qualified refs, complex expressions) passes
    through unchanged.

Doing the substitution in both passes is necessary — the
analyzer runs first and rejects undefined columns before the
planner even sees the statement. Putting it only in the
planner left the original Q3 error in place. The two helpers
mirror each other so they stay in lockstep.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3:
- TPC-H Q3 with `ORDER BY revenue DESC, o_orderdate` plans
  and returns the expected row.
- Positional `ORDER BY 2 DESC` over a GROUP BY result works.
- Non-aggregate `SELECT a + 10 AS xx, b FROM t ORDER BY xx
  DESC` returns rows ordered by the computed expression.
- Non-alias bare ident still resolves via FROM (no false
  alias collision).

`TestPlanOrderByAliasAndPositional` pins the three planner
behaviours. Design doc 0003-0001 grows an "ORDER BY Alias and
Positional Substitution" section.

commits.title: m0003: accept embedded-unit interval literal `interval 'N unit'`
commits.description:
Surfaced by running TPC-H Q6 end-to-end against goopg:
`interval '1 year'` parse-errored because v0 only accepted the
trailing-unit shape `interval '1' year`. HammerDB's TPC-H
templates emit the embedded-unit form after parameter
substitution — Q1's `interval ':1 day'` becomes
`interval '90 day'`; Q4 uses `interval '3 month'`; Q5/Q6/Q12 use
`interval '1 year'` — so v0 has to accept both shapes for the
upstream queries to parse without source rewrites.

Parser: tryTypedLiteral's `interval` arm now tries Form 1
(`interval '<N>' <unit>`, three tokens) first; on miss it falls
back to Form 2 (`interval '<N> <unit>'`, two tokens) by
splitting the string-literal body via splitEmbeddedInterval.
Both forms produce the same IntervalLit AST so analyzer /
planner / executor stay unchanged. Plurals normalise to
singular; negative magnitudes round-trip.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3: TPC-H Q6's
`l_shipdate < date '1995-01-01' + interval '1 year'` now plans
and executes correctly. TestParseIntervalEmbeddedUnit pins
day/month/year (singular + plural) and the negative-magnitude
case.

Design doc 0003-0006 updated to describe both forms and the
parser's fallback ordering. fix_plan.md interval bullet annotated
with the new shape.

commits.title: m0003: BETWEEN / NOT BETWEEN with date codec coverage
commits.description:
TPC-H Q6 leans on `l_discount BETWEEN :1 - 0.01 AND :1 + 0.01`;
Q14/Q19 also use BETWEEN over numeric and date ranges. Without
it, those queries parse-error before any executor work runs.

Parser-side desugar: `expr [NOT] BETWEEN low AND high` rewrites
at parse time to `(expr >= low) AND (expr <= high)` (or
NOT-wrapped). The result is a tree of existing BinaryOp /
UnaryOp nodes — no analyzer/planner/executor changes needed,
SQL three-valued logic flows through the existing Kleene
helpers. KwBetween registered; parseBetweenTail handles the
parse and parses low/high at precAnd+1 so the construct's `AND`
separator isn't gobbled as a boolean conjunction inside `low`.

Date codec coverage (surfaced during BETWEEN smoke testing):
encoding KindTime into a column declared `date` failed with
"kind 5 cannot encode as date". The codec's encodeValue and
decodeValue switches now include `date` alongside
`timestamp`/`timestamptz`, sharing the 8-byte nanos-since-epoch
on-disk frame. Midnight-UTC coercion already happens at literal-
parse time (`date '...'` → KindTime at midnight), so arithmetic
and comparison flow through the same code paths as timestamps.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3: numeric/int/date BETWEEN, NOT
BETWEEN, and BETWEEN combined with another conjunct
(`l_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 100 AND l_discount > 0.05`) all
return correct rows. TestParseBetweenDesugar /
TestParseNotBetweenDesugar / TestParseBetweenWithTrailingAnd
pin the AST shape and the precedence-handling edge case.

Design doc 0003-0013 added and indexed; fix_plan.md grows the
BETWEEN bullet under §"Query coverage". BETWEEN SYMMETRIC,
KindDate carrier, and date-only Format() deferred.

commits.title: m0003: NUMERIC arithmetic via int64 mantissa+scale carrier
commits.description:
TPC-H Q1 (and Q5/Q7/Q8/Q9/Q10) leans on
sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)). Until this loop, NUMERIC
flowed through goopg as KindString — every arithmetic site
rejected non-int operands with "operator * requires integer".
This loop adds a real NUMERIC carrier and wires it end-to-end.

KindNumeric: Datum gains NumericMantissa (int64) + NumericScale
(int8). Value = mantissa * 10^-scale. parseNumeric / formatNumeric
move literals between text and the int form; sign lives in the
mantissa, scale is non-negative.

Arithmetic: numericAdd/Sub align scales then add/sub mantissas;
numericMul multiplies mantissas and sums scales (overflow-checked
via canMulInt64); numericDiv targets max(left, right, 6) scale and
uses int64 division. Mixed NUMERIC + INT promotes the int side
to scale=0. compareDatum handles NUMERIC ↔ NUMERIC and NUMERIC
↔ INT by promoting + scale-aligning, so ORDER BY / WHERE on
NUMERIC works through the existing call sites.

Codec: encodeValue formats KindNumeric back to decimal text in
the existing varlen frame; decodeValue parses into KindNumeric so
arithmetic doesn't re-parse on every row. KindString / KindInt
encode paths still work so HammerDB's quoted-string loader and
literal-INT inserts both round-trip.

Aggregates: aggRuntime grows numericSum; sum/avg detect
KindNumeric on the first non-NULL row and route through
numericAdd / numericDiv. INT accumulator stays for INT-only sums.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3: TPC-H Q1 shape
sum(extendedprice * (1 - discount)) returns 320.4500 / 1040.2000
across two groups; avg returns 175.250000 / 525.125000;
WHERE l_extendedprice > 100 (NUMERIC ↔ INT) and
WHERE l_discount >= 0.10 (NUMERIC ↔ NUMERIC) both filter
correctly. TestEncodeDecodeNumericRoundTrip pins the codec
behaviour for KindInt/KindString/KindNumeric inputs.

Bounded by int64 — sufficient for SF1 (worst-case Q1 accumulator
~6.5e15 << int64 max). Arbitrary-precision NUMERIC, numeric(p,s)
typmod enforcement, %/^/binary-wire-format are deferred. Design
doc 0003-0012 added and indexed.

commits.title: m0003: SQL LIKE / NOT LIKE pattern matching
commits.description:
Six TPC-H queries (Q2/Q9/Q13/Q14/Q16/Q20) lean on LIKE; the parser
rejected them with "syntax error". This loop wires `expr [NOT] LIKE
pattern` end-to-end through parse → analyze → plan → execute.

Parser: KwLike registered. parseExprPrec recognises `[NOT] LIKE`
as a postfix at comparison precedence (mirrors the existing
[NOT] IN handling). The result is a parser.BinaryOp{Op: "LIKE"}
or "NOT LIKE" — a separate node would buy nothing since the
binary-op shape is what the analyzer + executor already dispatch
on.

Analyzer: text-on-text → bool. Mirrors upstream's typeresolution
for OPERATOR ~~ (its internal representation of LIKE).

Executor: matchSQLLike is the standard two-cursor recursive
matcher with star-anchor backtracking. `%` matches any run, `_`
matches one byte, `\` escapes the next pattern byte. Avoids regex
translation so LIKE-special-only metachars (`.`, `+`, `*` in the
input) keep their literal byte semantics.

Smoke-verified via psql 18.3:
- 'PROMO%' (Q14 prefix), '%green%' (Q9 contains), '%COPPER'
  (suffix), '____%' (>=4 bytes), 'PROMO\%' (escape).
- NOT LIKE inverts correctly.
TestMatchSQLLike pins the truth table for plain, %, _, mixed,
escape, empty pattern, and TPC-H Q9/Q14 shapes.

Design doc 0003-0011 added and indexed in design/README.md;
fix_plan.md grows the LIKE bullet under §"Query coverage". ILIKE,
ESCAPE clause, and prefix-anchor index extraction are deferred.

commits.title: m0003: predicate-pushdown for comma-FROM CROSS joins
commits.description:
Comma-FROM with WHERE-side equalities — the canonical TPC-H
query shape — has been planning as
`Filter(Cross(Cross(r, n), s))`. Cartesian product through a
post-hoc filter is correct but Cartesian; SF1 never finishes.
This loop adds `pushPredicatesIntoCrossJoins` (post-FROM tree
rewrite) that walks the WHERE conjunction and rehomes each
disjoint-side equality onto the deepest Join whose schema
spans both sides. The Join's type flips
`JoinTypeCross → JoinTypeInner`, the conjunct becomes the
Join.Predicate, and `splitEqualityForHash` runs to promote to
JoinAlgoHash + the build-side selection from the prior loop.
Conjuncts that don't span exactly two sides — single-table
filters, OuterColumnRef, subqueries — stay on the outer
Filter.

Why a post-hoc rewrite: the planner already builds the
left-deep CROSS chain in `planFromRangeVars`, and the WHERE
filter is resolved against the merged ctx schema. Walking the
existing tree post-Filter and matching ColumnRef indices
against `Join.schema` widths means we don't have to thread
WHERE awareness back into FROM-clause planning. The pass
runs once per planSelect, immediately after the Filter is
built.

Smoke-verified end-to-end via psql 18.3:
- 3-table `FROM r, n, s WHERE r.rk = n.rk AND s.nk = n.nk`
  plans as `Project -> Hash Join -> Hash Join -> Seq Scan`
  (no Filter wrapper) and returns the expected rows.
- Mixed `FROM r, n WHERE r.rk = n.rk AND n.nk > 15` keeps the
  single-table predicate on top: `Project -> Filter ->
  Hash Join -> Seq Scan`.

`TestPlanCommaFromPushesEqualityIntoJoin` pins both behaviours
in the planner unit tests. `TestPlanSelectCommaFromUsesCrossJoin`
still passes — comma-FROM without WHERE keeps the CROSS join
shape, since there's nothing to push.

Design doc 0003-0001 grows a "Predicate Pushdown for
Comma-FROM" section; fix_plan.md cost-based-planner bullet
updated to reflect the rewrite (reorderer + algorithm choice
still TODO).

commits.title: m0003: hash-join build-side selection from cardinality estimates
commits.description:
The planner has had `EstimateRows` since 2026-04-28 but only
surfaced the estimates through EXPLAIN — not through any plan
decision. This loop wires the first such decision: for INNER
hash joins, set `Join.BuildLeft = true` when EstimateRows says
the left side is smaller, so the executor builds the hash table
on the smaller relation rather than always picking the right
input by convention.

Why INNER-only: LEFT JOIN's outer-row preservation depends on
the left side driving the probe loop (so unmatched rows can be
emitted with NULL right-half), which makes the build/probe roles
non-swappable without redesigning the unmatched-row emission.
RIGHT/FULL never reach the hash algorithm — they take merge
join — so there's nothing to flip.

Output ordering is preserved: the executor's new
`runHashJoinBuildLeft` mirror still emits rows as
`concatRows(l, r)` in the canonical [leftCols, rightCols] order,
so downstream operators and column-index resolution see no
change. EXPLAIN annotates the swap as
`Hash Join (INNER, build=left)`.

Smoke-verified end-to-end via psql 18.3:
small (3 rows) JOIN big (5 rows) with ANALYZE on both sides
produces the build=left annotation; the same query with the
two relations swapped does not, and both return identical rows.
`TestPlanJoinHashBuildSidePicksSmaller` pins the four cases
(smaller-left, smaller-right, no-stats, LEFT-JOIN-never-swaps).

Design doc 0003-0002 updated; fix_plan.md cost-based-planner
bullet updated to reflect that build-side selection now consumes
EstimateRows (reorderer + algorithm choice still TODO).

commits.title: m0003: wire shared_buffers GUC into the buffer pool size
commits.description:
Prior to this commit cmd/goopg start built the pool with the
hard-coded 1024-slot floor (8 MB) regardless of postgresql.conf,
so HammerDB SF1 loads tripped ErrNoBuffer long before exhausting
machine RAM. The fix:

  - BuildDefaultRegistry registers shared_buffers (UnitKB,
    BootVal=128MB, ContextPostmaster) so the upstream-aligned
    default is in the GUC table even without a conf file.
  - cmd/goopg runStart parses --config first, applies entries to
    the registry, then derives PoolSlots = sharedBuffersKB / 8
    and feeds it into initdb.Open.
  - initdb.OpenOptions.PoolSlots default bumped from 1024 to
    16384 so a no-conf run matches upstream's boot default.
  - poolSlotsFromGUC unit-tested against 8/32/128/256 MB
    overrides; smoke-verified end-to-end via 'goopg start
    --config' with shared_buffers = 32MB → log emits
    shared_buffers_slots=4096.

Tests pin exact values so a future loop can't silently reset the
default. Design docs root-0005 and root-0017 updated to describe
the new wiring.

docs: add hammerdb docker handover notes

testport: port TAP rows and extend cluster harness
m0004: classify upstream TAP coverage with generator
