m0003: cardinality-estimation pass (planner.EstimateRows)
commits.description:
Establishes the bottom-up cardinality-estimation
infrastructure that the cost-based planner work needs.
ANALYZE landed in the previous loop wrote per-table
RowCount and per-column NDistinct into the catalog;
this loop reads them.

planner/cardinality.go:
  - new free function EstimateRows(n Node) int64. 0 means
    "no estimate available" — explicit rather than misleading.
  - SeqScan: tbl.Stats.RowCount or 0.
  - IndexScan: 1 (equality probe).
  - Values: exact len.
  - Filter: child * defaultGenericSelectivity (= 1/3).
  - Limit: min(child, IntegerConst.Limit) when constant.
  - Sort / Project: child unchanged.
  - Join: upstream's |L|*|R|/max(NDistinct(L.k),
    NDistinct(R.k)) for hash joins with disjoint-equality
    predicates. Generic equality fallback (1/200) when
    NDistinct unavailable. CROSS = cartesian.
  - Aggregate: NDistinct of group key when single
    ColumnRef; else child / 2. count(*) (no GROUP) → 1.
  - Insert: estimate from Source.
  - Selectivity defaults match upstream's
    DEFAULT_INEQ_SEL = 1/3 and the 1/200 no-stats fallback.

executor/operators_explain.go:
  - walkPlan appends `(rows=N)` to each label when
    EstimateRows > 0. Suppressed for 0 — matches upstream's
    "no costs without ANALYZE" behaviour.

What's NOT in this loop (documented as deferred):
  - The estimates are surfaced but not yet consumed by
    planner decisions. Hash-join build-side selection,
    join-order reordering, and algorithm-vs-algorithm
    choice still use the rules-based logic.
  - Predicate selectivity inside Filter (col=const,
    col<const, etc.). Filter blanket-uses 1/3.
  - Histograms / MCV / extended stats for skewed-data
    range selectivity.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3:
  - Pre-ANALYZE EXPLAIN omits row counts.
  - Post-ANALYZE 4×4 join with NDistinct(c_custkey)=4,
    NDistinct(o_custkey)=3 → Hash Join (rows=4).
  - count(*) on filtered table → Aggregate (rows=1)
    over Filter (rows=1) (default 1/3 selectivity on
    filter without recognized shape, then ceil to 1).
  - LIMIT 2 over a 4-row Sort → Limit (rows=2).

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0003-statistics-and-cardinality.md
covers the formulas, deferred items, and EXPLAIN format.

commits.title: m0003: ANALYZE produces table + per-column statistics
commits.description:
The cost-based planner item needs cardinality estimates;
the existing vacuum.Analyze function returned numbers but
didn't write them anywhere reachable. This loop closes that
gap.

Catalog:
  - new catalog.TableStats {RowCount, Pages, AvgWidth,
    Columns []ColumnStats}.
  - new catalog.ColumnStats {NDistinct, NullFrac}.
  - Table.Stats *TableStats: nil until first ANALYZE.
  - new SetTableStats interface method on Catalog;
    InMemory implementation pointer-replaces atomically.

Executor:
  - new operators_analyze.go: analyzeOp drives ANALYZE
    against each target relation via analyzeRelation, which
    walks every block under a fresh ReadCommitted snapshot,
    decodes visible tuples through the executor codec, and
    accumulates per-table + per-column distinct sets via the
    same datumKey canonicalisation aggregateOp uses.
  - Build's *planner.Utility branch type-checks the inner
    Stmt: AnalyzeStmt → analyzeOp; everything else → the
    existing utilityNoOp (VACUUM kept on no-op until its
    full-relation prune is wired through a stmt-driven
    entry point).

What's NOT in v0 (documented as deferred):
  - Sampling. Upstream samples up to 30k rows via
    default_statistics_target; v0 does a full scan.
  - MCV lists. Needed for skewed-data selectivity.
  - Histograms. Needed for range-predicate selectivity.
  - Catalog-snapshot persistence of Stats — survives
    server restart only after ANALYZE re-runs.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>`:
  - CREATE TABLE / INSERT 7 rows / ANALYZE t / SELECT round-
    trips fine.

Tests: TestAnalyzeRelationPopulatesStats pins that 7 rows
seeded with 3 distinct labels yield RowCount=7,
Columns[0].NDistinct=7 (id), Columns[1].NDistinct=3 (label),
positive AvgWidth.

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0010-analyze-statistics.md
covers the v0 stats shape, decision-by-decision rationale,
and the deferred items.

commits.title: m0003: correlated subqueries via lexical-scope chains
commits.description:
TPC-H Q4 / Q21 / Q22 use `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inner WHERE
inner.col = outer.col …)` — correlated subqueries that
reference outer-scope columns. Without this, those queries
fail at planning with `column does not exist`.

This loop adds the parent-scope walk on three axes:

Analyzer:
  - `scope` gains `parent *scope` and `cat catalog.Catalog`.
  - `resolveColumnRefType` walks the chain (local → parent
    → grandparent …) on column lookup. Found at any level
    returns the column's type; only when all levels miss
    does it report 42703 / 42P01.
  - `analyzeSelectWithParent` is the recursive entry that
    sets the inner scope's parent. Called from the
    SubqueryExpr / InExpr / ExistsExpr handlers in
    `analyzeExpr` so each subquery's WHERE / target list
    sees the outer FROM's relations.
  - `OuterScope` (exported wrapper around *scope) +
    `NewOuterScope` + `SetOuterScope` give the planner a
    way to thread the outer scope into the recursive
    Analyze() call that `Plan()` triggers.

Planner:
  - `resolveContext.parent` mirrors the analyzer chain.
  - new `planner.OuterColumnRef{Level, Index, Name, Type}`
    is the parent-scope reference; emitted by
    `resolveColumnRefAt` when a ColumnRef hits a parent
    level (Level=1 = immediate parent, matching upstream's
    Var.varlevelsup).
  - `planSelectWithParent` is the subquery-planning entry:
    sets `planParent` (so planSelect's ctx inherits via
    `ctx.parent`) AND builds the analyzer's OuterScope
    chain via `buildAnalyzerOuterScope`, calls
    `analyzer.SetOuterScope`. Both restorers deferred.
  - planSubqueryExpr / planExistsExpr / planInExpr
    refactored to take the outer resolveContext instead of
    a bare catalog so they can pass parent down through
    planSelectWithParent.

Executor:
  - `Context.OuterRows []Row` is the push-pop stack used by
    correlated subqueries.
  - `evalSubquery` / `evalExistsExpr` (now take row + ctx)
    push the current outer row before opening the inner
    plan, pop on return via deferred slice trim.
  - `collectInValues`'s subquery branch does the same.
  - `evalOuterColumnRef` reads
    `OuterRows[len(OuterRows)-Level]`.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>`:
  - SELECT o_orderkey FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS
      (SELECT 1 FROM lineitem
       WHERE l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey AND l_status = 'F')
    correctly returns o_orderkey={1, 3}.
  - NOT EXISTS variant flips to {2}.
  - SELECT o_orderkey, (SELECT count(*) FROM lineitem
      WHERE l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey) FROM orders o
    returns the right per-outer-row count.

Tests: TestParseCorrelatedExists pins parse-time shape.

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0008-subqueries.md gained a
"Correlated subqueries (parameter pull-up)" section
covering the three-axis chain plus the deferred items
(decorrelation, initplan caching, ANY/SOME/ALL, LATERAL).

commits.title: m0003: verify 3-7 way JOIN + hash-aggregate (no code change)
commits.description:
Two M0003 fix-plan items verified as already implemented and
ticked:

  - 3- to 7-way JOIN planning: the M1 left-deep chain
    planner already handles both comma-FROM (with WHERE-side
    equalities) and explicit JOIN ... ON syntax. With hash
    join landed, each pairwise INNER join in the chain
    promotes to JoinAlgoHash. Verified end-to-end via psql
    18.3 with a 6-way comma-join and a 7-way explicit-JOIN
    query — both returned correct rows; EXPLAIN shows the
    expected left-deep Hash Join chain.

  - Hash aggregate: the executor's aggregateOp groups by
    `map[string]*groupRuntime{}` — already a hash aggregate
    since M1. The fix-plan wording ("replace today's
    sort-then-group") was speculative; v0 never shipped a
    sort-then-group path.

Cost-based join-ordering remains open as part of the
cost-based-planner item.

commits.title: m0003: CREATE / DROP VIEW for HammerDB Q15
commits.description:
HammerDB TPC-H Q15 builds a temporary view, queries it twice,
then drops it:
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW revenue (supplier_no, total_revenue) AS …;
  SELECT … FROM supplier, revenue WHERE … = (SELECT max(...) FROM revenue);
  DROP VIEW revenue;

Without view support, Q15 can't run. This loop adds it.

Parser:
  - new keywords KwView, KwReplace.
  - parseCreate handles `OR REPLACE` (recognised before the
    target-kind dispatch; rejected for CREATE TABLE / INDEX).
  - parser.CreateViewStmt{OrReplace, Name, Columns, Query}
    captures the optional column-alias list and the inner
    SELECT.
  - parser.DropViewStmt mirrors DROP TABLE/INDEX.

Catalog:
  - Table gains View *parser.SelectStmt and ViewColumnAliases
    fields. View-bearing tables stay Virtual=true so Pool /
    smgr keep ignoring them.
  - new (*InMemory).CreateView (honours OR REPLACE; rejects
    CREATE-without-REPLACE over an existing object) and
    DropView (rejects non-views; respects IF EXISTS).

Executor (operators_ddl):
  - execCreateView derives the catalog Columns from the
    explicit alias list, the target-list AS aliases, or
    deriveTargetName (bare ColumnRef → its name, FuncCall
    → function name). Column types default to "unknown" —
    overridden at every reference by the planner.
  - execDropView delegates to catalog.DropView.

Planner:
  - planScanRangeVar checks tbl.View first: plans the inner
    SELECT recursively, returns the inner node, and rebuilds
    the resolve context's schema to combine the view's column
    names with the inner plan's column types.
  - planSelect's `isSimpleSingle` fast path now delegates to
    planScanRangeVar instead of inlining the SeqScan
    construction, so view substitution lives in one place.
  - Plan dispatch accepts CreateViewStmt and DropViewStmt as
    DDL nodes.

Wire layer: ddlTag returns "CREATE VIEW" / "DROP VIEW".

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>` with the Q15 shape:
  - CREATE VIEW revenue (supplier_no, total_revenue) AS
    SELECT l_suppkey, sum(l_extendedprice) FROM lineitem
    GROUP BY l_suppkey
  - SELECT supplier_no, total_revenue FROM revenue
    ORDER BY supplier_no  → (1, 300), (2, 700)
  - SELECT … FROM revenue WHERE total_revenue =
    (SELECT max(total_revenue) FROM revenue) → (2, 700)
  - CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW revenue (sno, total) AS …
    correctly renames columns
  - DROP VIEW + DROP VIEW IF EXISTS both work

Tests: TestParseCreateViewWithExplicitColumns and
TestParseDropViewIfExists pin the parser-level shapes.

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0009-views.md covers the
substitution-at-plan-time approach (vs upstream's rewrite),
column-name derivation, the unified planScanRangeVar, and
the deferred items (DML on views, catalog persistence,
recursive / materialised views).

commits.title: m0003: IN / NOT IN / EXISTS / NOT EXISTS (uncorrelated)
commits.description:
Closes the uncorrelated half of the subquery workstream.
Required by TPC-H Q16/Q18/Q20 (IN with subquery), and a
prerequisite for Q4/Q21/Q22's correlated EXISTS shapes.

Parser:
  - new keyword KwIn (KwExists already existed for IF EXISTS).
  - parser.InExpr{Operand, Negated, Subquery, List}: either
    Subquery or List populated. parseInTail peeks for SELECT
    after `(` to disambiguate subquery vs value-list.
  - parser.ExistsExpr{Negated, Subquery}: leading EXISTS in
    primary-expression position. NOT EXISTS parses as
    UnaryOp{NOT, ExistsExpr}; the executor's bool NOT inverts.
  - parseExprPrec checks for `IN` and `NOT IN` postfix at
    comparison precedence; two-keyword lookahead for NOT IN.

Analyzer: types both InExpr and ExistsExpr as bool; recurses
into operand and list elements (subquery analysis happens
during planning).

Planner:
  - planner.InExpr / planner.ExistsExpr mirror the AST after
    the inner SELECT has been planned.
  - planInExpr resolves operand + list (via resolveExpr) and
    plans the subquery (via Plan(s.Subquery, ctx.cat)) when
    present.
  - planExistsExpr always plans the inner SELECT.
  - Both register in resolveExpr and resolveExprAfterAggregate
    so HAVING / target-after-GROUP-BY uses work.

Executor:
  - evalInExpr materialises the inner set per evaluation
    (no caching across rows in v0). Three-valued NULL:
      operand NULL → NULL
      inner contains NULL and no non-NULL match → NULL
      empty inner → false (NOT IN: true)
      match found → true (NOT IN: false)
    Multi-column subquery → 42601.
  - evalExistsExpr opens, asks for first row, returns
    `hasRow != Negated`. Output columns ignored — `SELECT 1`
    body works alongside any other.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>`:
  - WHERE p_partkey IN (SELECT ps_partkey FROM partsupp)
  - WHERE p_partkey NOT IN (SELECT ps_partkey FROM partsupp)
  - WHERE p_partkey IN (1, 4)
  - WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM partsupp WHERE ps_suppkey=100)
  - WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM partsupp WHERE ps_suppkey=999)
All return the expected row sets.

Tests: TestParseInExprSubquery, TestParseNotInExprList,
TestParseExistsExpr pin AST shapes for the three new
constructs.

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0008-subqueries.md gained an
"IN / NOT IN / EXISTS / NOT EXISTS (uncorrelated)" section.
Correlated subqueries / initplan caching / ANY-SOME-ALL stay
documented as deferred.

commits.title: m0003: scalar uncorrelated subqueries — `(SELECT …)` in expr pos
commits.description:
TPC-H Q15 / Q17 / Q22 use `WHERE col <op> (SELECT agg(...) FROM
…)` — the scalar uncorrelated form. This loop adds it
end-to-end. IN / NOT IN / EXISTS / correlated subqueries stay
open as separate workstreams.

Parser:
  - parsePrimary's `(` branch peeks one token: if it's
    KwSelect, recurse via parseSelect and wrap in
    parser.SubqueryExpr{Inner *SelectStmt}. Falls back to the
    existing parenthesised-expression path otherwise.
  - No grammar ambiguity: row-constructor `(a, b)` and
    parenthesised-expression `(x + 1)` never start with
    SELECT.

Analyzer: types SubqueryExpr as `unknown` (the unknown-coercion
rule in isAssignable keeps comparison sites happy).

Planner:
  - planner.SubqueryExpr{Plan Node} mirrors the parser AST
    after the inner SELECT has been planned.
  - planSubqueryExpr(x, cat) calls Plan(x.Inner, cat)
    recursively. The catalog is threaded through
    resolveContext.cat (set once at the top of planSelect)
    so subqueries inside expressions can plan without piping
    cat through every helper.
  - Both resolveExpr (regular) and resolveExprAfterAggregate
    (in HAVING / target-after-GROUP BY) call planSubqueryExpr
    via ctx.cat / agg.input.cat.

Executor (evalSubquery):
  - Build → Open → Next → drain → Close per evaluation.
  - 0 rows  → NullDatum (matches upstream "scalar subquery
    returned no rows is NULL").
  - 1 row × 1 col → returns the cell.
  - 1 row × N cols (N>1) → 42601 syntax error.
  - 2+ rows → 21000 cardinality_violation, upstream-aligned
    message.
  - Per-evaluation rebuild is correct but suboptimal —
    initplan caching is a follow-up perf optimisation.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>`:
  - SELECT … WHERE val = (SELECT max(val) FROM t)  → max row.
  - SELECT … WHERE val > (SELECT min(val) FROM t)  → 3 rows.
  - SELECT … WHERE val = (SELECT val FROM t WHERE id=999)
    (empty inner)  → 0 outer rows (NULL ≠ anything).
  - SELECT … WHERE val = (SELECT val FROM t)  → ERROR 21000.

Tests: TestParseSubqueryExpr pins AST shape (BinaryOp.Right is
*SubqueryExpr with non-nil Inner SelectStmt).

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0008-subqueries.md covers the
scope, parser ambiguity reasoning, planner threading, and the
deferred IN / EXISTS / correlated / initplan-caching items.

commits.title: m0003: EXPLAIN <stmt> renders the plan tree as text
commits.description:
Closes the M0003 EXPLAIN bullet. Hash-join vs nested-loop
algorithm choice (introduced in 0003-0002-join-executors.md)
is now visible without forcing the inner query through and
reading row-count patterns.

Parser:
  - KwExplain keyword + parser.ExplainStmt{Inner Stmt}.
  - parseExplain consumes the EXPLAIN token then re-enters
    parseStatement for the inner stmt. Optional `( option [,
    …] )` list (ANALYZE / VERBOSE / FORMAT) is deferred.

Planner:
  - planner.Explain{Child Node} wraps the planned inner node.
    Planning the inner stmt eagerly inside Plan() means
    planning errors surface at EXPLAIN time, matching
    upstream.
  - Output() declares a single-column "QUERY PLAN" text
    schema so RowDescription is correct on the wire.

Executor:
  - operators_explain.go: explainOp does a pre-order walk
    via walkPlan + describePlan, emitting one row per node
    as `<indent>->  <label>` (root has no leading "->").
  - planChildren is the recursion oracle covering Project /
    Filter / Sort / Limit / Aggregate / Join / Insert.
  - Labels surface algorithm hints:
      Join → "Hash Join (INNER)" or "Nested Loop (LEFT)" etc.
      Aggregate → "Aggregate" or "GroupAggregate (k, n)".
      SeqScan / IndexScan → relation + index name.

Wire:
  - dispatch.go: commandTagFor returns "EXPLAIN" for
    *planner.Explain.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>`:
  - Hash-decomposable join shows `Hash Join (INNER)`.
  - Inequality-predicate join shows `Nested Loop (INNER)`.
  - count(*) with no grouping shows
    `Aggregate (1 aggregates) -> Seq Scan on customer`.
  - Composite Filter/Sort/Limit/SeqScan stack renders with
    proper indentation.

Tests: TestParseExplainWrapsInner pins the AST shape.

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0007-explain.md covers the
text-format shape, the per-node label table, and the
deferred items (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, COSTS, the
DML sub-plan rendering).

commits.title: m0003: hash-join executor for disjoint-equality predicates
commits.description:
The M1 planner emitted only nested-loop joins. For TPC-H at
SF1 (LINEITEM ~6M rows × ORDERS ~1.5M rows) that's quadratic-
infeasible. This loop adds hash join as the preferred
algorithm whenever the predicate decomposes into a single
disjoint-side equality.

Planner:
  - new Join.Algo {NestedLoop, Hash}, LeftKey/RightKey fields.
  - splitEqualityForHash inspects the predicate and reports
    whether it's a top-level `BinaryOp{=}` whose two sides
    reference disjoint join inputs (one only the left input,
    one only the right). exprSide is the side classifier —
    sideUnknown for constants, sideLeft / sideRight for
    ColumnRefs, recursing through BinaryOp / UnaryOp / FuncCall
    / CaseExpr / ExtractExpr; sideMixed short-circuits the
    promotion.
  - When promoted, `right.col = left.col` is silently flipped
    so LeftKey always references the left input only.
  - INNER + LEFT only — RIGHT/FULL/CROSS keep the universal
    nested-loop fallback.

Executor (operators_join_agg.go):
  - one joinOp keeps Open/Next/Close unified; Open dispatches
    on plan.Algo into runHashJoin or runNestedLoop.
  - runHashJoin: build phase hashes right input on RightKey
    into map[string][]Row; probe phase evaluates LeftKey for
    each left row, walks the matching bucket, emits joined
    rows. NULL keys never match (matches upstream's
    NULL-aware equi-join). LEFT-join unmatched-left rows get
    a null-extended right side.
  - evalHashKey delegates to datumKey for canonical-string
    hashing — same encoding the aggregate operator uses for
    GROUP BY.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>`:
  - INNER hash join: customer ⋈ orders on c_custkey =
    o_custkey returns 4 expected rows.
  - LEFT hash join: customer LEFT JOIN orders correctly
    null-extends the unmatched 'carol' row.
  - Reversed equality (`o_custkey = c_custkey`) flips at
    plan time and still picks hash.

Tests: TestPlanJoinPicksHashAlgo pins which predicates promote
(INNER/LEFT equality, reversed equality) and which stay on
nested-loop (inequality, CROSS).

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0002-join-executors.md covers the
algorithm choice, sided-expr classifier, and the
deliberately-deferred items (sort-merge, multi-column hash
keys, RIGHT/FULL hash, cost-based build-side selection).

commits.title: m0003: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY as LIMIT synonym
commits.description:
TPC-H queries Q2/Q3/Q10/Q18/Q21 use the SQL-standard `FETCH
FIRST n ROWS ONLY` shape rather than upstream's `LIMIT n`.
parseSelect now accepts both. Five forms covered:

  FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY
  FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY        -- ROW vs ROWS
  FETCH FIRST ROW ONLY          -- count omitted, defaults to 1
  FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY        -- NEXT alias for FIRST
  OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY

Combining LIMIT and FETCH FIRST in the same SELECT is a syntax
error (matches upstream). The optional `OFFSET n {ROW | ROWS}`
SQL-standard trailer is also accepted (no-op for v0).

Plumbing:
  - new `acceptIdentKeyword(names...)` helper in parser.go for
    unreserved-keyword idents (FETCH / FIRST / NEXT / ROW /
    ROWS / ONLY are all bare TokenIdents in v0's lexer, not
    formal keywords — keeping them out of the global keyword
    table avoids reserving them in column / function position).
  - parseSelect grew the FETCH FIRST clause after LIMIT/OFFSET.
  - isAliasStart rejects bare-ident "fetch" so
    `FROM t FETCH FIRST …` no longer eats `fetch` as a table
    alias. Was the surfacing failure mode for the bare-FROM
    case (queries with ORDER BY before FETCH already worked).

Tests:
  - TestParseFetchFirstAsLimit covers all five accepted shapes
    and the OFFSET … FETCH NEXT combo.
  - TestParseFetchFirstRejectsCombinedLimit pins the
    `LIMIT … FETCH FIRST …` syntax error.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D
<dir>` — all five forms return the expected row counts.

commits.title: m0003: EXTRACT(field FROM source) for TPC-H Q7/Q8/Q9
commits.description:
EXTRACT has its own grammar — `EXTRACT(field FROM expr)` —
because the field is positional rather than a value
expression. parseColumnOrCall detects the leading `extract(`
ident and dispatches to parseExtractExpr (consume '(', ident,
FROM keyword, source expression, ')'). Result is a
parser.ExtractExpr{Field, Source}.

Fields supported (executor evalExtract):
  year / month / day / hour / minute / second
  dow (0=Sun … 6=Sat, upstream-aligned)
  doy / quarter / epoch

All return int8 — fractional-second fields and timezone
extraction wait on the type system.

Plumbing:
  - parser: ExtractExpr AST node + parseExtractExpr.
  - analyzer: types as int8; recurses into Source.
  - planner: planner.ExtractExpr mirror; resolveExpr in both
    the regular and after-aggregate sites.
  - executor: evalExtract switches on Field; non-time source
    is a 42883 type error; unknown field is 0A000.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against
`goopg start -D <dir>`:
  - SELECT extract(year FROM o_orderdate), … (all fields)
    returns correct values for Mar/Jul/Feb test rows.
  - WHERE extract(year FROM o_orderdate) = 1995 (TPC-H Q7
    shape) filters correctly.
  - Mixed: extract(year FROM date '1998-12-01' - interval
    '90' day) → 1998 (composes with date/interval arithmetic).

Tests: TestParseExtractExpr pins the AST shape (case-
insensitive field, source becomes ColumnRef).

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0006-date-interval-arithmetic.md
gained an EXTRACT section with the supported-field table.

commits.title: m0003: date/interval typed literals + time-interval arithmetic
commits.description:
Eight TPC-H queries (Q1/Q4/Q5/Q6/Q12/Q14/Q15/Q20) gate WHERE
on `<col> <op> date 'YYYY-MM-DD' ± interval 'N' unit`. Without
typed-literal date/interval syntax and the time±interval
arithmetic, none of these parse.

Parser:
  - parser.TypedStringLit{Type, Value} for `date '...'`,
    `timestamp '...'`, `timestamptz '...'`. tryTypedLiteral
    peeks one token ahead and falls back to the normal
    column-or-call parse if the shape doesn't match —
    avoids reserving these as global keywords.
  - parser.IntervalLit{Value, Unit} for `interval 'N' unit`.
    Units day(s), month(s), year(s) recognised; plurals
    normalise to singular. Sub-day units rejected — none of
    the load-bearing TPC-H queries need them.

Analyzer:
  - TypedStringLit types as its declared SQL type;
    IntervalLit types as `interval`.
  - new isTimestampLike groups timestamp / timestamptz / date.
  - isComparable allows any pair of timestamp-likes (Q1's
    `l_shipdate <= date '...'` shape).
  - BinaryOp `+` / `-` returns `timestamp` for
    `(timestamp-like, interval)` (and `+` for the reverse).

Planner: planner.TypedStringLit / planner.IntervalLit
1:1 mirrors; resolveExpr translates pass-through.

Executor:
  - new Datum KindInterval with IntervalMonths + IntervalDays
    int32 fields. Year intervals normalise to 12*months at
    eval; sub-day microseconds absent.
  - evalTypedStringLit parses the string body per Type at
    eval time. Date uses `2006-01-02`; timestamp tries
    `2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999`, then `2006-01-02 15:04:05`,
    then date-only fallback.
  - evalIntervalLit parses the int body and routes to the
    right Months/Days field.
  - evalBinary `+` / `-` routes through addTimeInterval(t, iv,
    subtract) which delegates to Go's time.AddDate so
    month-end overflow matches upstream PG (`Jan 31 + 1
    month` → Mar 3).

Verified end-to-end via upstream psql 18.3 against
`goopg start -D <dir>`:
  - Q1 shape `l_shipdate <= date '1998-12-01' - interval '90'
    day` filters to the right rows.
  - Q4/Q5/Q6 range `>= date '...' AND < date '...' + interval
    '2' month` returns the in-range rows.
  - `date '1995-01-01' + interval '1' year` evaluates to
    `1996-01-01 …`.

Tests: TestParseDateLiteral, TestParseIntervalLiteral
(all six unit aliases), TestDateMinusIntervalParses pin the
parse-tree shape.

Out of scope (deferred): EXTRACT (its own grammar),
timestamp-timestamp interval, sub-day units, multi-field
intervals. Documented in
docs/design/0003-0006-date-interval-arithmetic.md.

commits.title: m0003: CASE expressions (searched + simple forms)
commits.description:
TPC-H queries Q1, Q12, Q14 use CASE heavily — Q1 packs five of
them into the SUM aggregates. Goopg's parser had no CASE
support at all (KwCase wasn't even a keyword). This loop adds
both forms end-to-end through parser → analyzer → planner →
executor.

Parser:
  - new keywords KwCase/KwWhen/KwThen/KwElse (KwEnd already
    existed for COMMIT alias; reused as the CASE-end terminator).
  - parser.CaseExpr{Operand, Whens[]CaseWhen, Else}; nil
    Operand discriminates the searched form from the simple form.
  - parsePrimary dispatches on KwCase to parseCaseExpr.
  - At least one WHEN required (mirrors upstream's grammar).

Analyzer:
  - analyzeCaseExpr walks each WHEN/THEN/ELSE branch.
    Searched-form WHEN must be boolean-like (42804 otherwise);
    simple-form WHEN is checked but not type-compared.
  - Branch result types unify via sameOrCompatible (same name,
    both numeric-like, both string-like) — falls back to unknown
    when branches diverge so isAssignable accepts CASE results
    against any column type.

Planner:
  - planner.CaseExpr / planner.CaseWhen mirror the AST.
  - resolveCaseExpr translates parser → planner; both
    resolveExpr and resolveExprAfterAggregate dispatch through
    it (the after-aggregate site uses agg.input as the resolve
    context — CASE inside SUM is the TPC-H Q1 shape).

Executor:
  - evalCaseExpr walks Whens; first match wins. NULL WHEN is
    "not matched" per upstream three-valued logic.
  - compareEq is the simple-form comparator: int/int, bool/bool,
    string/string, time/time strict equality, plus int↔string
    format-compare for HammerDB's numeric-as-text columns.
    NULL on either side → NULL.

Verified end-to-end via psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D <dir>`:
searched form returns the right per-row label, simple form
maps integer codes correctly, and ELSE-omitted CASE correctly
yields NULL when no WHEN matches.

Tests: TestParseCaseExpr{SearchedForm,SimpleForm,RequiresWhen}
pin the AST shape and the at-least-one-WHEN syntax invariant.

Design doc: docs/design/0003-0005-case-expressions.md.

commits.title: m0003: ALTER TABLE ADD FOREIGN KEY accepted (enforcement no-op)
commits.description:
HammerDB's TPC-H post-load step (`HammerDB/src/postgresql/pgolap.tcl`
lines 529–536) issues eight `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT name
FOREIGN KEY (cols) REFERENCES other (cols) [NOT DEFERRABLE |
DEFERRABLE]` statements. v0 parses and accepts the syntax but
does not enforce, mirroring upstream's pattern of accepting
syntax for unimplemented features so the surrounding workflow
can complete.

Parser: new `AlterTableAddForeignKey` action kind on
`AlterTableAction`, with `RefTable` / `RefColumns` /
`Deferrable` fields. New `KwReferences` and `KwDeferrable`
keywords. The `[NOT] DEFERRABLE` trailer is optional.

Executor: `ddlOp` for ALTER TABLE accepts the new kind;
the only check it performs is that the referenced table
exists (42P01 otherwise). Cascade / lookup enforcement is
deferred to the constraint subsystem; TPC-H queries don't
need referential integrity, only the schema-build phase
to complete without errors.

Verified: all eight HammerDB TPC-H FK ALTER TABLEs from
`pgolap.tcl` run end-to-end via psql 18.3 against
`goopg start -D <dir>`.

Tests: `TestParseAlterTableAddForeignKey` covers HammerDB's
multi-column FK, the optional `[NOT] DEFERRABLE` trailer
(both spellings + omitted), and the bare-syntax form.

Design doc: `0003-0004-hammerdb-tpch-integration.md` gained
a section explaining the syntax-accepted / enforcement-no-op
decision.

commits.title: m0003: HammerDB TPC-H loader shape works end-to-end
commits.description:
HammerDB's TPC-H loader (`HammerDB/src/postgresql/pgolap.tcl`)
turns out not to use COPY at all — it issues multi-row INSERTs
with every literal as a single-quoted string, even into NUMERIC
columns:

    INSERT INTO REGION (R_REGIONKEY, R_NAME, R_COMMENT)
      VALUES ('0','AFRICA','lar deposits'), ...;

For TIMESTAMP columns the loader wraps the value in
`to_timestamp(text, fmt_text)`. Two changes make this shape
work end-to-end against goopg:

1. `text → numeric` assignability (narrow). Upstream PG accepts
   the loader pattern because bare string literals are typed
   `unknown` until inferred at the assignment site. goopg types
   them as `text`, so `isAssignable` gained an exception:
   `text → numeric/decimal` is allowed because v0's NUMERIC
   codec already stores string datums verbatim. Scope is
   intentionally narrow — `text → int4/int8` stays 42804
   (existing pgbench_accounts regression test still passes).

2. `to_timestamp(text, fmt)` executor builtin. The format
   translator `pgFormatToGoLayout` rewrites the PG codes
   HammerDB uses (`YYYY`, `Mon`, `MM`, `DD`, plus
   `HH24`/`MI`/`SS`) into Go's reference-time layout, then
   delegates to `time.Parse`. Locale-aware month names and
   timezone-aware parsing wait on the type system.

Verified end-to-end via upstream psql 18.3 against
`goopg start -D <dir>`:
  - REGION & SUPPLIER multi-row INSERTs with string-quoted
    NUMERIC values round-trip.
  - ORDERS INSERT with
    `to_timestamp('1995-Jan-15','YYYY-Mon-DD')` SELECTs back
    `1995-01-15 00:00:00.000000` and `173665.47`.

Tests: `TestPgFormatToGoLayout` pins the format translator;
existing analyzer / executor tests continue to pass.

commits.title: m0003: TPC-H DDL runs — NUMERIC codec + decimal literal lexer
commits.description:
Closes the M0003 \"DDL runs end-to-end\" bullet. All eight
HammerDB TPC-H CREATE TABLEs from
`HammerDB/src/postgresql/pgolap.tcl` now complete via upstream
psql 18.3 against `goopg start -D <dir>`, and round-trip
INSERTs with literal `901.01` / `1.5e3` SELECT back
byte-identically.

Two gaps surfaced and fixed:

1. NUMERIC codec. Integer datums (e.g. `INSERT INTO t (n)
   VALUES (1)`) used to fail with `integer datum cannot
   encode as numeric`. New `\"numeric\"`/`\"decimal\"` case in
   `internal/executor/codec.go` writes the value as varlen
   text in the same frame `varchar`/`char` use:
   - KindInt   → strconv.FormatInt → bytes
   - KindString / KindBytes → bytes
   DecodeRow surfaces it as KindString so the wire layer
   formats verbatim. Real precision-tracking arithmetic
   waits on the type-system milestone.

2. Decimal / scientific literal lexer. `123.45` and `1.5e-3`
   used to fail at parse time with `expected ')' (got .)`.
   Lexer's digit case now consumes an optional fractional
   part (only when followed by digits — `t.123` qualified
   names still resolve as ident.int) and an optional
   `e[+-]?digits` exponent (with conservative back-off on
   empty exponent body). When either fires, the token is
   `TokenNumericLit` with the verbatim source slice.

   AST gains `parser.NumericConst{Value string}`; analyzer
   types it as `numeric`; planner mirrors as
   `planner.NumericConst`; executor evaluator emits a
   KindString datum so the new codec path stores the literal
   byte-for-byte.

Tests:
  - `TestEncodeDecodeNumericRoundTrip` pins the codec for
    KindInt + KindString inputs.

Out of scope (deferred): real NUMERIC arithmetic, `numeric(p,s)`
enforcement, HammerDB COPY-based bulk loader. See
`docs/design/0003-0004-hammerdb-tpch-integration.md` and the
M0003 milestone for the rest of the workstream.

commits.title: checkpointer: surface counters as pg_stat_checkpointer view
commits.description:
Closes the M0002 operator-visibility bullet. Operators (and
HammerDB / pgbench tooling) can now query checkpoint cadence
without attaching a debugger.

Counters added to `wal.Checkpointer`:
  - numTimed     — incremented on timer-driven cycles
  - numRequested — SQL CHECKPOINT, CLI ctl, max_wal_size
  - writeTimeMs  — cumulative ms inside flushDirty
  - statsResetAt — set at construction (no reset verb yet)

`Stats()` returns a coherent atomic-load snapshot. Column shape
of the view matches upstream PG 18.x's pg_stat_checkpointer; the
columns v0 doesn't track (restartpoints_*, sync_time,
buffers_written, slru_written) report literal 0.

Plumbing:
  - `(*catalog.InMemory).RegisterVirtualTable` is the new public
    seam for runtime-installed virtual tables. Mirrors the
    seeded-at-construction `pg_class` pattern but lets out-of-tree
    callers contribute their own row providers (e.g. the wal
    package's checkpointer here, planner-stat views in M0003).
  - `initdb.Open` constructs the table at startup with a row
    provider that closes over the live Checkpointer. Like
    pg_class, the view is NOT persisted to pg_catalog.json — the
    runtime re-registers on every startup.

`pg_stat_bgwriter` has no analogue in v0: goopg has no separate
bgwriter (the buffer pool flushes only at checkpoint and on
Pool.Close). Documented in 0002-0001-checkpointing.md §7 +
Out-of-scope.

commits.title: vacuum: logical RecordKindHeapVacuum for page prunes
commits.description:
VACUUM was the last hot mutation path still emitting an FPI on
every dirty (the only safe option until logical change records
landed). This loop migrates it to the once-per-epoch FPI path
shared by HeapInsert / BtreeInsert / HeapDelete.

New `RecordKindHeapVacuum` (kind=7); fixed-header + variable
slot list:

  kind(1) | rel(9) | blk(4) | count(2) | slots[count](2 each)
  = 16 + 2*count bytes.

Storage gets two helpers that factor the prune kernel:

  - `CollectDeadHeapSlots(p, isDead) → []uint16` walks the page
    once and returns the 1-based LP_NORMAL slot numbers whose
    tuple satisfies isDead. Page bytes untouched.
  - `VacuumHeapPageBySlots(p, deadSlots) → stats` is the
    deterministic apply: reclaim the named slots to LP_UNUSED
    and repack survivors against pd_special. Both the live
    VACUUM path and replay call this, so the post-prune image
    is bit-exact regardless of who ran it.

`vacuum.Vacuum` now collects the dead set first (so the WAL
record carries the same slot list the prune is about to apply),
takes `Slot.Lock()` around the scan + repack + LSN stamp
(prune-vs-insert concurrency safety), and emits the record via
`Pool.MarkDirtyChangeRecord`. When no `LogHeapVacuum` hook is
wired (test pools), it falls back to `MarkDirty` so the
FPI-on-every-dirty path keeps the change durable.

Replay (`replayHeapVacuum`) re-runs `VacuumHeapPageBySlots`
against the existing page bytes, idempotent via pd_lsn.

Wiring: `storage.PoolConfig.LogHeapVacuum` + `Pool.LogHeapVacuum()`
accessor mirror the existing redo-record hook pattern;
`initdb.Open` constructs the closure from `wal.EncodeHeapVacuum`
+ `walWriter.Append`.

Tests: `TestEncodeDecodeHeapVacuumRoundTrip` and
`TestReplayHeapVacuumIdempotent` pin the wire format and the
"second replay is a no-op via pd_lsn" guarantee.

This closes the next-to-last item in the redo-record migration —
remaining FPI-every-dirty paths are the btree metapage,
internal-node, and clearRootFlag updates. Once those land,
`MarkDirty` flips back to once-per-epoch FPI globally.

Updated docs/design/0002-0003-redo-records.md and
.ralph/fix_plan.md.

commits.title: ctl: add `goopg ctl checkpoint` subcommand routed via control socket
commits.description:
Same semantics as the SQL `CHECKPOINT` verb — fires a synchronous
IMMEDIATE-speed checkpoint and only returns once the marker is
durable. The CLI uses a generous default 300s client timeout
(`-t`); the server drops the read deadline once it sees the
CHECKPOINT line so a long flush won't trip the listener's 5s
default.

Closes the M0002 control-plane bullet.

commits.title: heap: logical RecordKindHeapDelete for UPDATE/DELETE xmax stamps
commits.description:
Adds RecordKindHeapDelete (kind=6) — a fixed 20-byte logical
change record (rel + blk + lineSlot + xmax) for the executor's
xmax-stamp paths. updateOp (old-image stamp) and deleteOp (per
visible match) now route through a new markHeapDeleteDirty
helper that picks Pool.MarkDirtyChangeRecord when LogHeapDelete
is wired and falls back to the conservative MarkDirty otherwise.

Replay re-runs storage.PageSetHeapTupleXmax and is idempotent
via pd_lsn. The page must already exist (HeapInsert produced it
earlier in the same WAL stream); a missing block on replay is a
hard error.

Plumbing matches the existing pattern:
PoolConfig.LogHeapDelete -> Pool.LogHeapDelete() -> the executor
helper pulls the hook from the pool. initdb.Open wires the
closure to wal.EncodeHeapDelete + walWriter.Append.

WAL volume sanity: pgbench -i unchanged (no UPDATEs in -i).
pgbench -t 30 default mixed workload (~120 UPDATEs + ~30
INSERTs into history + SELECTs) keeps WAL flat at ~21 MB —
each UPDATE/DELETE was previously emitting an 8 KB FPI per
mutation, now emits a 20-byte logical record on every dirty
after the first per epoch.

New tests: TestEncodeDecodeHeapDeleteRoundTrip pins the
on-the-wire shape; TestReplayHeapDeleteIdempotent walks one
record through replay against a seeded page and verifies the
second replay is a no-op via pd_lsn.

Design doc 0002-0003-redo-records.md notes 0002-0003c as the
heap-delete landing; index entry refreshed.

commits.title: btree: logical RecordKindBtreeInsert for non-split inserts
commits.description:
Adds RecordKindBtreeInsert (kind=5) — a logical change record
carrying (rel, blk, marshalled-item-bytes) — for the B-tree's
non-split insert path. btree.insertIntoBlock now calls
Pool.MarkDirtyChangeRecord with a closure that emits the record
when the page has already been FPI'd this epoch; first dirty
still emits the FPI baseline as the redo anchor.

btree.ApplyInsertRecord is the new public replay helper that
re-runs insertItemSorted given the marshalled item. wal's
recovery.go imports btree to invoke it (one-direction dep, no
cycle) and skips the apply when the page's pd_lsn is already
>= record.endLSN.

Plumbing follows the existing closure pattern:
PoolConfig.LogBtreeInsert -> Pool.LogBtreeInsert() -> btree
pulls the hook from the pool. initdb.Open wires the closure
to wal.EncodeBtreeInsert + walWriter.Append.

Impact on pgbench -i -s 1:
  WAL volume: ~801 MB -> ~21 MB  (closes most of the regression)
  Runtime:    ~13.3s  -> ~9.25s  (primary-key build dropped 4s)

Pre-loop baseline before logical change records was ~1.6 GB
WAL; remaining ~11 MB above the M1-era ~10 MB floor comes from
heap UPDATE/DELETE xmax stamps and vacuum page prune still on
the FPI-every-dirty path. Each gets its own redo record in
subsequent loops.

New test: TestEncodeDecodeBtreeInsertRoundTrip pins the
on-the-wire shape. Existing crash-recovery test
(internal/initdb/recovery_test.go) continues to pass.

Design doc 0002-0003-redo-records.md updated to record the
landing; index entry refreshed.

commits.title: wal: logical heap-insert redo record + per-epoch FPI selector
commits.description:
Adds RecordKindHeapInsert (kind=4) — a logical change record
carrying (rel, blk, lineSlot, tuple-bytes) — and a new
Pool.MarkDirtyChangeRecord that emits an FPI baseline on
first-dirty-per-epoch and the caller's logical record on
subsequent dirties. The executor's writeHeapRow now uses the
new path so pgbench -i no longer emits an 8 KB FPI for every
INSERT.

Replay is idempotent via pd_lsn: HeapInsert decodes the rel
and slot, Extends the relation if the page is missing,
PageAddHeapTuples at the recorded slot, and stamps the page
header LSN. Re-replaying the same record is a silent skip when
the page already carries a >= LSN.

Plumbing matches the existing pattern: PoolConfig.LogHeapInsert
+ Pool.LogHeapInsert() exposed from initdb.Open's closure that
wraps wal.EncodeHeapInsert + walWriter.Append.

Impact on pgbench -i -s 1 WAL volume: ~1.6 GB → ~800 MB. Runtime
13s vs 18s. The remaining FPI volume comes from non-migrated
paths (btree non-split insert, heap update/delete xmax, vacuum
prune); migrating each restores more of the M1-era WAL footprint.

New tests: TestReplayHeapInsertIdempotent and
TestEncodeDecodeHeapInsertRoundTrip. Existing crash-recovery
test (internal/initdb/recovery_test.go) continues to pass —
the heap-insert path now emits logical records but the btree
metapage / leaf / split paths still emit FPI, and replay covers
both kinds.

Design doc: 0002-0003-redo-records.md (status: draft);
README index updated.

commits.title: recovery: wire WAL replay into startup + crash-recovery test
commits.description:
initdb.Open now invokes wal.ReplayFromDirWithMgr against
<dataDir>/pg_wal BEFORE constructing the buffer pool, so replay
reconstructs any post-mutation state that wasn't flushed before
an unclean shutdown. The new ReplayFromDirWithMgr variant takes
the runtime's existing storage.Manager so replay and subsequent
normal I/O share file handles; missing pg_wal on a fresh data
dir is treated as nothing-to-replay.

Surfaced and fixed a v0 redo-log gap while writing the M0002
crash-recovery test: FPI was previously emitted only on
first-dirty-per-epoch, which silently dropped every subsequent
mutation to the same page on replay (the test caught it
immediately — only the first-inserted key per leaf survived
recovery). v0 has no logical change records (heap_insert /
btree_insert deltas) yet, so the once-per-epoch optimisation
was correctness-incompatible. maybeEmitFPI now emits on every
MarkDirty; the fpiSinceCheckpoint flag is still tracked for the
checkpointer's epoch bookkeeping but no longer gates emission.

WAL volume cost: pgbench -i -s 1 grows from ~10 MB to ~1.6 GB.
Correctness is the M0002 priority. Logical change records to
restore the optimisation are deferred to a post-M0002 milestone.

The new internal/initdb/recovery_test.go simulates SIGKILL by
flushing WAL durable, then closing the WAL writer + Manager
WITHOUT calling Pool.Close (which would FlushAll the dirty
pages). Reopening the data dir, post-replay, must surface every
inserted key through a fresh btree handle. 800 keys, all
present.

Updated docs/design/0002-0001-checkpointing.md §5 to record the
policy change and link forward to the recovery test.

commits.title: btree: Landing 3a of M0002 — atomic split WAL records + replay
commits.description:
Adds a single WAL record (RecordKindBtreeSplit, kind=3) that
captures both halves of a page split — left's post-image and
right's freshly-populated image — in one durable unit. Emitted
from insertIntoBlock's split path via a LogSplit closure plumbed
through storage.PoolConfig.LogBtreeSplit → Pool.LogBtreeSplit() →
btree.BTree.logSplit (initdb.Open wires the pool field to
wal.EncodeBtreeSplit + walWriter.Append). Both pages get
pd_lsn = endLSN of the split record via a new
MarkDirtyWithLSNLocked variant — the original MarkDirtyWithLSN
self-deadlocks when the caller already holds the content latch
exclusively, which is the entire btree split path.

Replay (internal/wal/recovery.go) applies left first then right,
using a shared writeBlockOrExtend kernel that Extends the
relation when the target block is one past the end. Result: a
crash anywhere across the split sequence leaves the data files
in either pre-split or post-split state, never the torn state
where left advertises a right-link to a page whose disk image is
the bare smgr.Extend init zero page.

Verified with TestReplayBtreeSplitAtomic, TestEncodeDecodeBtreeSplit-
RoundTrip, TestSplitInvokesLogSplit, the full -race suite, and
pgbench smokes (-S -c 8 -j 4 ~20k TPS, default mixed -c 4 -j 2
65 TPS, no failures). WAL volume after pgbench -i grew from
~8 MB to ~11 MB — splits are infrequent, the per-record cost is
bounded.

Design doc 0002-0002 updated to "accepted (L1+L2+L3a); Landing 3b
still planned"; index entry refreshed.

commits.title: btree: Landing 2 of M0002 — per-page latches + Lehman-Yao right-link
commits.description:
Bumps the on-disk B-tree page format to v2: BTPageOpaque grows
from 16 to 24 bytes to carry a fixed-width 4-byte HighKey and a
new BTHasHighKey flag bit. Splits stamp the high key onto the
left page before dropping its latch so readers descending under
shared latches recover from concurrent splits via op.Next
(right-link recovery).

Concurrency model:

* Search and RangeScan take NO tree-wide lock. They pin each
  page, take Slot.RLock, read items + opaque, drop the latch
  before unpinning. keyExceedsHighKey signals a follow-the-
  right-link recovery step that catches the case where a split
  moved our target keys to the right sibling between descent
  and lookup.
* Insert keeps bt.mu (multi-writer concurrency lands in
  Landing 3 alongside split WAL records). Every mutation site
  inside the writer path runs under Slot.Lock so readers
  observe only pre- or post-split page images, never an
  intermediate state.

Verified with a concurrent insert+search stress test under
-race (one writer + 6 readers across 300 keys), the existing
btree suite, and the full go test ./... matrix. pgbench smoke:
-S -c 8 -j 4 -t 50 returns 400/400 tx at ~21k TPS (vs ~18k
under Landing 1), default mixed -c 4 -j 2 -t 30 returns 120/120
tx with no failures.

Format v2 is incompatible with v1 indexes; pgbench -i and the
test suite both create indexes fresh.

Design doc 0002-0002-btree-concurrency.md updated to "accepted
(L1+L2); Landing 3 still planned" and the index entry refreshed.

commits.title: docs(ralph): unify design-doc naming to <id>-NNNN
btree: Landing 1 of M0002 concurrent-btree — RWMutex parallelism
commits.description:
Replaces BTree.mu sync.Mutex with sync.RWMutex so multiple
Search/RangeScan callers parallelise. Insert/Create still hold
the writer lock; per-page mutations continue to use Slot.Lock()
from the buffer pool's content lock.

Adds a goroutine-stress test (8 goroutines x 500 lookups against
a populated tree) that runs clean under -race. pgbench -S
-c 4 -j 2 -t 50 against a live goopg returns 200/200 transactions
at ~18k TPS.

Lands alongside docs/design/0002-0002-btree-concurrency.md
(draft), which describes the three-landing rollout: Landing 1
(this commit) gives read parallelism, Landing 2 introduces
per-page latches with Lehman-Yao right-link descent, Landing 3
adds atomic split WAL records and page deletion.

Also folds in the user-side rename m0002-0001 ->
0002-0001-checkpointing.md and matches the new convention
in the new btree-concurrency doc + the README index.

commits.title: docs: design doc for M0002 checkpointing
commits.description:
Captures the production-grade checkpointer design landed across the
last few loops: GUC surface (checkpoint_timeout,
checkpoint_completion_target, max_wal_size, min_wal_size,
full_page_writes), max_wal_size volume trigger driven by an atomic
WrittenLSN mirror, spread/paced writeback via Pool.FlushAllPaced,
full-page-image WAL records emitted from MarkDirty on the first
dirty-per-epoch, SQL CHECKPOINT plumbing, and the structural seams
(epochResetter, pacedFlusher, volumeReporter optional interfaces).

Cross-references root-0008 for replay; recovery itself was unchanged
this milestone.

commits.title: checkpoint: spread dirty-page writeback per checkpoint_completion_target
commits.description:
Adds storage.Pool.FlushAllPaced(pacer) which snapshots the dirty
set, flushes each buffer through smgr, and invokes the pacer
after each one with progress in (0, 1]. wal.Checkpointer's
timer-driven path builds a deadline-based pacer aiming to finish
writeback at start + Interval * CompletionTarget so I/O is
spread across most of the checkpoint cycle instead of going out
in one synchronous burst.

Volume-triggered checkpoints (max_wal_size) and the SQL
`CHECKPOINT` verb (CheckpointNow) both run at IMMEDIATE speed —
they are backpressure / operator requests, not cadence work, and
they fall through to the unpaced FlushAll path.

goopg start reads checkpoint_completion_target from the registry
and calls Checkpointer.SetCompletionTarget at boot.

commits.title: storage: emit full-page-image WAL records on first dirty per epoch
commits.description:
Implements the milestone-0002 full_page_writes contract: the first
mutation of each page after every checkpoint emits a
wal.EncodePageImage record so crash recovery can replay it on a
torn page. Subsequent mutations of the same page in the same
checkpoint epoch skip the FPI.

storage.Pool gains a LogPageImage callback (initdb.Open wires it
to wal.Writer.Append) and a FullPageWrites toggle that
SetFullPageWrites flips at runtime. MarkDirty stamps the FPI's
end LSN into the page header so the existing flush-before-write
ordering still covers it. The checkpointer calls
Pool.ResetCheckpointEpoch after each successful checkpoint to
arm a fresh FPI per page.

goopg start honours the full_page_writes GUC at boot.

commits.title: chore: commit current renamed and modified files
checkpoint: fire on max_wal_size threshold, not just on the timer
commits.description:
Adds a volume-driven checkpoint trigger to wal.Checkpointer:
Writer.WrittenLSN() exposes the current write position via an
atomic mirror that's updated after each successful append, and
Checkpointer.Run polls it on VolumeCheckInterval (1s by default
when MaxWALBytes is set). When (writtenLSN - lastCheckpointLSN)
crosses MaxWALBytes, a synchronous checkpoint runs immediately
instead of waiting for the timeout tick.

goopg start reads max_wal_size (in MB) from the registry and
calls Checkpointer.SetMaxWALBytes before launching Run, so the
trigger threshold matches the upstream-aligned default of 1 GB.

commits.title: config: add M0002 checkpoint GUCs and honour checkpoint_timeout
commits.description:
Adds the five WAL/checkpoint GUCs with upstream-aligned defaults:
checkpoint_timeout (300s, range [30, 86400]),
checkpoint_completion_target (0.9, range [0.0, 1.0]),
max_wal_size (1024 MB), min_wal_size (80 MB), and full_page_writes
(on). All five mirror postgres/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c
on names, units, ranges, and PGC_SIGHUP context. The behaviour
they describe (spread checkpoints, max_wal_size triggering, full-
page images) lands in subsequent loops; today they're observable
via SHOW.

Wires checkpoint_timeout into wal.Checkpointer via a new
SetInterval method called from goopg start, so the production
cadence is upstream's 5 minutes rather than the development-time
10 seconds.

commits.title: checkpoint: implement SQL CHECKPOINT verb end-to-end
commits.description:
Wires wal.Writer + wal.Checkpointer into initdb.Runtime so every
started server has a real WAL stream and a periodic checkpointer.
The new SQL CHECKPOINT verb threads through parser → planner →
executor → wal.Checkpointer.CheckpointNow, returning a "CHECKPOINT"
CommandComplete tag.

The periodic checkpointer goroutine runs alongside srv.Run on a
child context that cancels on the way out, so a control-socket
STOP shuts down cleanly instead of hanging.

This is the first chunk of milestone 0002. fix_plan.md is updated
with M0002/M0003/M0004 task decompositions; pgbench -i and the
default workload still pass.

commits.title: docs: mention postgres submodule oracle at REL_18_3
goopg ctl: implement stop / status / reload via control socket
commits.description:
internal/control: new package shipping a postmaster.pid file and a
Unix-domain command socket under <DataDir>/.goopg.ctl.sock. The
pidfile carries pid / data-dir / start time / listen address /
socket path so `goopg status` doesn't need to touch the socket;
the socket carries operator commands (PING / STOP / RELOAD) so
graceful shutdown and config reload no longer require sending a
signal.

Server lifecycle integration: when DataDir is set on Config, Run
writes the pidfile, binds the control socket, wires OnStop to the
runCtx cancellation, and removes both files on shutdown. Empty
DataDir (the in-process test path) skips the control plane.

cmd/goopg subcommands:
- status -D: reads pidfile, kill(0) the process, optionally
  PINGs the socket. Exit 0 = running, 3 = not running (matches
  pg_ctl), 4 = process alive but socket unresponsive.
- stop -D: sends STOP, waits up to -t seconds for the process to
  exit so a follow-up start doesn't race the previous incarnation.
- reload -D: sends RELOAD (v0 server-side handler is a no-op until
  per-GUC SIGHUP-style refresh wires up).
- restart: documented stub since v0 runs in the foreground and
  the operator's supervisor restarts the process per spec §7.

Tests: pidfile round-trip, missing-file diagnostic, listener
PING/STOP with OnStop callback, ProcessAlive sanity. Manual smoke
against a live server confirmed the status→reload→stop→status
flow with the expected exit codes and clean teardown of the
pidfile + socket.

This satisfies spec §3.3 (signal-replacement commands) and §10 #7
(graceful shutdown + config reload reachable via dedicated CLI).
With this every item in .ralph/fix_plan.md is now checked: COPY
binary mode is genuinely deferred; the parser/analyzer parent is
satisfied as a composite of its sub-items, all already done.

commits.title: chore: add postgres submodule pinned to REL_18_3
storage: per-page content lock fixes concurrent heap-write race
commits.description:
Slot grows Lock/Unlock/RLock/RUnlock methods exposing the existing
contentMu RWMutex to executor callers. Heap-touching operators
now hold the lock across their read-modify-write windows, matching
upstream PostgreSQL's BUFFER_LOCK_EXCLUSIVE / BUFFER_LOCK_SHARED
contract:

- writeHeapRow: Pin → Lock → IsNew/InitPage/PageAddHeapTuple →
  MarkDirty → Unlock → Unpin (and same shape for the extend
  path). Without this, two concurrent writers to the same block
  computed the same upper offset, both copied their tuple over
  the same bytes, and the line pointer pointed at a half-
  overwritten payload — the "invalid t_hoff=0 len=44" symptom
  we hit under pgbench -c 4 -j 2.
- updateOp / deleteOp: Lock around PageSetHeapTupleXmax for the
  same reason.
- seqScanOp: RLock for the lifetime of the per-page iteration so
  writers can't tear the bytes we're decoding. Lock is released
  in the existing releasePinned() drop point.
- scanForMatches (used by Update/Delete): RLock the read phase.
- indexScanOp: RLock around PageGetHeapTuple.

Verified end-to-end against upstream pgbench 18.3:
- pgbench -c 4 -j 2 -t 5 (default TPC-B): 20/20 at ~66 TPS,
  0 failed.
- pgbench -c 4 -j 2 -t 50: 200/200 at ~65 TPS, 0 failed.
- pgbench -S -c 4 -j 2 -t 20: 80/80 at ~19k TPS still works.

This is milestone 7's final acceptance criterion (DoD #5):
"pgbench default and --select-only scripts run to completion
under concurrent clients with MVCC-consistent results."

commits.title: pgbench: --select-only and single-client default workloads run end-to-end
commits.description:
Five fixes unblock pgbench's TPC-B and select-only scripts against
goopg:

1. analyzer.isNumericTypeName recognises "int" (in addition to
   int4/int8/integer). pgbench's CREATE TABLE uses bare `int`, so
   `WHERE aid = $1::int8` previously failed with "incompatible
   operand types int and int8".
2. storage.Pool.Close flushes every dirty slot through smgr before
   releasing the arena. Heap data was reaching the buffer pool but
   never the data files at shutdown — restart saw zero rows.
3. mvcc.Manager grows SetNextXID/NextXID. The catalog snapshot
   carries `next_xid` so a new session continues the transaction
   counter from the previous session's high-water mark; without
   this, restored heap tuples (xmin from previous sessions) looked
   in-progress to the new session's snapshots and were filtered
   out by TupleVisible.
4. parser: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP / CURRENT_DATE / CURRENT_USER /
   LOCALTIMESTAMP and friends now parse as niladic FuncCall when
   they appear without parentheses (the SQL standard form pgbench's
   `INSERT ... VALUES (..., CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)` relies on). The
   executor already had the function-table entry; previously
   parsePrimary was producing a ColumnRef.

Verified end-to-end against upstream pgbench 18.3:
- `pgbench -i -s 1`: full init in ~7 s.
- Restart server, `SELECT count(*) FROM pgbench_branches`: 1 row
  (durability + xid persistence work).
- `pgbench -S -t 5`: 5/5 at ~7100 TPS.
- `pgbench -t 5` (TPC-B-like, single client): 5/5 at ~37 TPS.
- `pgbench -S -c 4 -j 2 -t 20`: 80/80 at ~19k TPS.

Concurrent default workload (-c 4 -j 2) hits a heap-tuple
corruption race ("invalid t_hoff=0 len=44") on INSERT/UPDATE —
the next blocker, likely a buffer-pool or page-add ordering bug
when multiple writers touch the same block.

commits.title: docs: update README and add LICENSE
pgbench -i now succeeds end-to-end against goopg
commits.description:
Two small fixes unblock the full pgbench init flow:

1. internal/server/copy.go: skip libpq's `\.` end-of-data marker
   in the CopyIn line splitter. pgbench (and other libpq callers
   using PQputline / PQputCopyData) terminate the data stream
   with a `\.` line before issuing CopyDone — protocol v3 uses
   CopyDone for the actual signal, but the literal frame still
   arrives. Previously the decoder treated it as a single-field
   row and errored out with "row has 1 fields, expected N".

2. internal/executor/executor.go: planner.Utility
   (VACUUM / ANALYZE) maps to a no-op operator. v0 doesn't yet
   wire the existing internal/vacuum / internal/analyze package
   functions into the executor; they're optimisations, not
   load-bearing for correctness, so the no-op lets pgbench's
   `vacuum analyze pgbench_branches` (and friends) succeed
   cleanly with the right CommandComplete tag.

Verified end-to-end: `goopg init -D /tmp/d && goopg start -D /tmp/d`
followed by upstream pgbench 18.3 `-i -s 1` runs the full init —
drop, create, 100k row COPY with freeze, vacuum, alter table add
primary key — in ~7 s with no errors. This is milestone 7's first
acceptance criterion (DoD #4 in the spec).

commits.title: catalog: add Virtual flag and seed pg_catalog.pg_class as a v0 view
commits.description:
catalog.Table grows a Virtual flag and a VirtualRows() func()
[][]string provider. catalog.NewInMemory pre-registers
pg_catalog.pg_class with one row per user table — the oid column
stores the relname so pgbench's `oid=$1::pg_catalog.regclass` shape
compares text-to-text and matches. Snapshot skips virtual tables
(they're re-registered on every startup); Restore re-installs them
after wiping.

Planner: when the FROM target is virtual, emit a materialised
Values node populated by calling VirtualRows() at plan time. The
WHERE/projection chain on top works unchanged because Values is
already a planner.Node.

Analyzer: `::` cast result reports type `unknown` so comparison
compatibility checks pass without a real type lattice. The operand
is still recursed into so genuine errors inside it surface.

Extended-query Describe(P): when storage is wired, parse + plan
the prepared statement and convert the planner's output schema
into a wire-protocol RowDescription. Previously Describe always
returned NoData for non-special queries, so libpq clients (pgbench)
got DataRow without a prior RowDescription.

Verified end-to-end: goopg start -D ... && pgbench -i now reaches
the COPY data-load step (it was previously stuck at the pg_class
probe one byte earlier). Next blocker: COPY field counting on
pgbench-generated rows surfaces "row has 1 fields, expected 3"
needing investigation in the wire-layer line splitter or the
CopyFromExecutor decode path.

commits.title: parser: support `::` typecast (treated as a no-op for v0)
commits.description:
Adds the `::` typecast operator end-to-end:

- Lexer recognises `::` as a TokenOperator; bare `:` still errors
  out so SQLSTATE 42601 surfaces cleanly.
- Parser introduces CastExpr in the AST. parseExprPrec consumes
  trailing `::typename` after every operand, supporting chained
  casts (`expr::int8::text`) and optional `(N)` / `(N,M)` typmods.
  Type names accept dotted forms like `pg_catalog.regclass`,
  unquoted identifiers, and the keyword aliases the lexer already
  knows (int, text, varchar, etc.).
- Planner unwraps CastExpr by recursing on the operand; the
  declared target type is preserved on the parser AST for future
  loops that wire up real type coercion. parserExprKey learns the
  shape so GROUP BY deduplication still works.

Driving pgbench 18.3 against goopg now reaches the next blocker:
pgbench probes `SELECT relkind FROM pg_catalog.pg_class WHERE
oid=$1::pg_catalog.regclass` and gets 42P01 ("relation \"pg_class\"
does not exist"), confirming the cast parses and planner reaches
the catalog lookup. Adding a minimal pg_catalog (pg_class +
pg_attribute + pg_namespace, populated from the in-memory catalog)
is the next sub-step.

Tests pin the schema-qualified shape, the `(N)` typmod tail, and
the chained-cast case.

commits.title: server: route extended-query path through parser+planner+executor
commits.description:
internal/server/dispatch_extended.go is the new seam the
extended-query protocol (Parse/Bind/Describe/Execute) lands on
when the server has storage handles wired. Bind parameters are
now mapped to executor.Datum (text-format integer literals
become KindInt; everything else becomes KindString) and flow
through executor.Context.Params for ParamRef resolution — so a
parameterised INSERT/SELECT actually executes against the heap
instead of erroring with "bind parameters in Execute are not
supported yet."

The result envelope still materialises into extendedQueryResult
so multi-batch Execute(maxRows) can drain a portal incrementally;
RowDescription field metadata comes straight from the planner's
output schema with the type→OID map shared with the simple-query
dispatch.

Verified: a server-level Parse/Bind/Execute test inserts 2 bind
values into items(id, label) and reads them back via SELECT.
Driving upstream pgbench 18.3 against goopg now reaches the next
blocker — pgbench's `WHERE oid=$1::pg_catalog.regclass` probe
trips the parser on the `::` typecast (separate loop) and would
trip 42P01 on pg_catalog.pg_class even with `::` parsed.

commits.title: server: route the simple-query path through parser+planner+executor
commits.description:
Adds internal/server/dispatch.go: when the server has storage
handles wired (goopg start -D ...), every simple-query statement
that isn't SHOW/SET/RESET goes through parser.Parse →
planner.Plan → executor.Build → Open/Next/Close, with the wire
layer emitting RowDescription/DataRow for read-shaped plans and
upstream-shaped CommandComplete tags for everything else
("DROP TABLE", "CREATE TABLE", "INSERT 0 N", "UPDATE N",
"DELETE N", "ALTER TABLE", "VACUUM", "ANALYZE", "BEGIN"/"COMMIT"/
"ROLLBACK", "SELECT N").

A per-Query-message ReadCommitted transaction frames the batch
so DML+DDL composite queries see one another; transaction verbs
(BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) are no-ops at the wire layer for v0
because each Query already has its own implicit transaction —
full session-tx semantics need session plumbing in a follow-up.

Adds executor.RowCounter interface (RowsAffected() int64)
implemented by insertOp/updateOp/deleteOp; renames the unexported
counter fields so the field/method namespace doesn't collide.
Test files updated to call the method.

Verified end-to-end against upstream pgbench 18.3:
goopg init && goopg start -D ... && pgbench -i now gets past
"dropping old tables", "creating tables", and the BEGIN that
opens the data-load block. Next blockers (separate loops): the
extended-query path doesn't yet route bind-parametered queries
through the executor, and pg_catalog system tables aren't
implemented.

commits.title: catalog: persist schema across restarts via global/pg_catalog.json
commits.description:
Adds catalog.Snapshot / catalog.Restore: a deterministic, OID-keyed
view of the in-memory schema (tables + columns + indexes including
primary-key flag and access method), suitable for JSON encoding.
Snapshots are sorted by OID so two saves of the same state produce
byte-identical output.

initdb.Open now replays <DataDir>/global/pg_catalog.json into the
freshly-allocated catalog when the file exists; missing is fine
(fresh-from-init case). Restore failures abort startup rather than
silently leaving a half-loaded catalog. Runtime.SaveCatalog writes
the snapshot atomically via tempfile + rename(2) so a crash mid-save
preserves the previous good copy.

cmd/goopg start calls SaveCatalog on shutdown before closing the
pool, so DDL declared during a session survives a restart.
Together with the existing storage-manager persistence, a goopg
binary now persists both schema and data files across restarts —
the last load-bearing piece between today's stack and pgbench -i
running end-to-end.

Tests cover the catalog-level round-trip (tables, indexes,
nextOID), dangling-index detection, snapshot determinism, and the
initdb-level save/reload flow that mirrors the goopg start
shutdown→startup transition.

commits.title: docs: add 0017-data-directory design doc
commits.description:
Pins the v0 data-directory layout (PG_VERSION, base/, global/,
pg_wal/, pg_xact/, sample postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf) and the
initdb.Open server-bootstrap seam that goopg start -D consumes.
Documents which upstream PostgreSQL pieces v0 deliberately defers
— on-disk catalog, pg_control, tablespaces, multi-database, locale
— and the strict PG_VERSION-equality check that gates future
catalog-version migrations.

commits.title: goopg start: open storage handles from -D <data-directory>
commits.description:
internal/initdb gains an Open helper that bundles the four
long-lived handles a running server needs: storage.Manager + Pool
under <DataDir>, an mvcc.Manager, and an in-memory catalog.Catalog.
Open verifies the directory was laid out by goopg init (PG_VERSION
present and matches the binary's CatalogVersion) before
allocating any state, so a wrong/stale path fails fast with a
clear "run 'goopg init -D ...' first" diagnostic. Runtime.Close
releases pool + smgr in order; idempotent.

cmd/goopg start now accepts -D <dir>: when set, it calls
initdb.Open and forwards the handles into Server.Config, so the
binary actually drives the parser→planner→executor COPY (and
future DML) path. With -D omitted the server still runs in
protocol-only fallback mode. Tests cover the happy path, the
uninitialized- and missing-dir paths, the catalog version
mismatch guard, and the close-idempotence contract.

Catalog persistence is still deferred — schema declared via SQL
during a session vanishes when the process exits, but data files
themselves persist via the storage manager.

commits.title: goopg init: lay out the v0 data directory
commits.description:
internal/initdb is the new package that ships the upstream-shaped
data directory layout: base/, global/, pg_wal/, pg_xact/ at mode
0700, a base/<DefaultDBOid> subdir for the default database, plus
PG_VERSION (containing the major version goopg reports in the
startup ParameterStatus) and sample postgresql.conf / pg_hba.conf
files. The pg_hba sample mirrors auth.DefaultPolicy() —
loopback-trust, reject everything else — so 'goopg init' and
'goopg start' agree on defaults out of the box.

Init refuses a non-empty target (matching upstream initdb's guard
so an operator can't accidentally clobber a real PG installation)
and accepts an existing-but-empty target so pre-created mountpoints
work. Wired into the CLI as 'goopg init -D <dir>'; the previous
not-yet-implemented stub is gone. Tests cover the layout, the
non-empty-dir refusal, the empty-existing-dir acceptance, the
PG_VERSION contents, the sample HBA rules, plus a CLI-level
integration test for argument parsing.

Spec references: .ralph/specs/GOAL_AND_REQUIREMENTS.md §6.1
(directory layout) and §10 #2 (definition of done #2).

commits.title: server: route COPY through parser+planner+executor when storage is wired
commits.description:
Server.Config grows three optional fields — Catalog, Pool, TxnMgr —
that together let the wire layer drive table-form COPY through the
real parser→planner→executor stack instead of the v0 string-matching
shape. When all three are nil, the legacy fallback is kept so
protocol-only tests and storage-less deployments keep working.

The new path in internal/server/copy.go:

- parser.Parse + planner.Plan with SQLSTATE-aligned errors
  (PlanError surfaces 42P01/42703/42701/42601/0A000 verbatim).
- Begins a fresh ReadCommitted transaction per COPY statement and
  builds an executor.Context with Pool/Catalog/TxnMgr/Tx/Snap.
- CopyTo: WriteCopyOutResponse → executor.RunCopyTo with each
  emitted COPY-TEXT line written as a CopyData frame → WriteCopyDone
  → CommandComplete "COPY N" → ReadyForQuery, then Commit.
- CopyFrom: WriteCopyInResponse, then per-frame: append payload to a
  line buffer, split on '\n', push each completed line through
  CopyFromExecutor.PushLine. CopyDone flushes any partial trailing
  line, commits, emits "COPY N" + ReadyForQuery. CopyFail / decode
  errors / unexpected frames roll back the transaction and emit a
  clean ErrorResponse.

Tests cover the executor-backed path end-to-end (COPY items FROM
STDIN → COPY items TO STDOUT round-trip against a real catalog) and
the planner-stage 42P01 propagation for unknown tables. The three
existing legacy tests still pass via the no-storage fallback.

commits.title: executor: add bidirectional COPY drivers
commits.description:
internal/executor/copy.go wires the COPY TEXT codec into the
operator stack:

- RunCopyTo(ctx, plan, emit) opens a SeqScan (table-form) or the
  planner-attached Query subtree (query-form), reorders + projects
  rows via plan.ColumnIndex when the user-specified column list
  differs from declared order, and pushes one COPY TEXT line per
  visible row through the emit callback.
- NewCopyFromExecutor / PushLine takes a line at a time, decodes
  via DecodeCopyTextRow, scatters the listed columns into the
  table's full column slice (unlisted columns land as NULL), and
  appends via the existing heap-write path with xmin = current
  xid. Bad field counts surface as SQLSTATE 22P04
  (bad_copy_file_format).

file/PROGRAM endpoints reject as 0A000. Tests cover the default
column list, projection+reorder, the query-form COPY (SELECT 1)
shape (driven through the real parser+planner pipeline), the
file-endpoint rejection, the bad field-count error, and a full
CopyFrom -> CopyTo round-trip against an in-memory catalog.

commits.title: executor: add COPY TEXT codec for pgbench-shaped rows
commits.description:
Adds EncodeCopyTextRow / DecodeCopyTextRow in
internal/executor/copy_text.go: tab-separated columns, trailing
newline, `\N` for NULL, the standard backslash-escape table
(\b/\f/\n/\r/\t/\v/\\, \xHH hex, \NNN octal, fall-through). Wires
through the v0 typed columns (int4/int8/bool/timestamp/text);
unknown types stay as raw strings.

The codec is the Datum⇄line bridge the wire-mode COPY path needs;
the server-side replacement of the current string-matching dispatch
in internal/server/copy.go follows once Server.Config grows the
catalog/storage handles.

commits.title: planner: add Copy plan node for COPY statements
commits.description:
Plan() now dispatches parser.CopyStmt to a new planCopy that:
- Resolves table-form COPY against the catalog (42P01 missing relation,
  42703 missing column, 42701 duplicate column).
- Plans the inner SELECT for query-form COPY through the regular
  planSelect path so the wire layer can drive a Project node when
  formatting CopyData rows.
- Defaults the column list to declared order when none is given,
  matching INSERT's behaviour.
- Validates COPY options at plan time so the wire layer doesn't have
  to: duplicate names (42601), unknown FORMAT (0A000), unknown
  options (0A000), bare flags vs. value-bearing options (42601),
  HEADER true/false/on/off/match.

planner.Copy carries Direction, Endpoint, Table+ColumnIndex (or
Query for query-form), Filename for file/PROGRAM endpoints, and the
verbatim option list. Output() returns a Schema mirroring the
selected columns so the wire layer's CopyOutResponse can be built
without a second resolution pass.

executor.Build now returns a stable feature_not_supported error for
planner.Copy until the executor copy operator lands; the existing
wire-protocol COPY path in internal/server/copy.go is untouched.
That replacement (and binary mode) come next.

Tests cover the pgbench shape, explicit column lists, query-form,
file/PROGRAM endpoints, accepted-option set, and the SQLSTATE
codes for the must-reject shapes.

commits.title: parser: add COPY statement support
commits.description:
Adds CopyStmt AST node and parser covering the upstream COPY surface
pgbench needs: FROM/TO + STDIN/STDOUT/file/PROGRAM, optional column
list, query-form (COPY (SELECT ...) TO STDOUT), parenthesised
WITH (...) option list, and the legacy WITH BINARY/HEADER trailing
syntax. STDIN/STDOUT/PROGRAM are matched by lower-cased identifier
text, mirroring upstream's "ColLabel" classification, so we don't
bloat the keyword set. FORCE_QUOTE/FORCE_NOT_NULL/FORCE_NULL accept
both '*' and parenthesised column lists.

Tests pin the pgbench shape (COPY pgbench_accounts FROM STDIN), the
existing wire-mode shape (COPY (SELECT 1) TO STDOUT), file and
PROGRAM endpoints, the legacy trailing syntax, and the must-reject
shapes (query-form FROM, STDOUT FROM, STDIN TO, missing direction).

Planner/executor wiring and the server replacement of the string-
matching dispatch in internal/server/copy.go come next.
