executor: add DDL operator path for CREATE/DROP/TRUNCATE
commits.description:
ddlOp dispatches on the wrapped parser.Stmt and runs catalog +
storage mutations directly:

  CREATE TABLE              catalog.CreateTable; relation file is
                            created lazily on first Pin/PinNew
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS  no-op when the table already exists
  DROP TABLE                Pool.InvalidateRel + smgr.DropRelation
                            after the catalog entry is gone
  DROP TABLE IF EXISTS      silently skip missing names
  TRUNCATE TABLE            Pool.InvalidateRel + smgr.TruncateRelation
                            (file truncate to 0 blocks)

Storage gains two thin operations: Manager.DropRelation closes the
file handle and removes the on-disk path; Manager.TruncateRelation
shrinks the relation file to zero blocks. Pool grows InvalidateRel
which evicts every unpinned slot bound to a buffer of the relation
— the executor calls it before issuing the smgr-level change so a
subsequent Pin returns a fresh page. Pinned slots are skipped
(matching upstream's AccessExclusiveLock requirement for v0).

SQLSTATE alignment: 42P07 duplicate_table on CREATE TABLE conflict,
42P01 undefined_table on DROP without IF EXISTS.

End-to-end tests run CREATE / CREATE IF NOT EXISTS / DROP / DROP IF
EXISTS / TRUNCATE through the full parser→planner→executor stack and
verify catalog state + relation-file size.

CREATE INDEX / DROP INDEX / ALTER TABLE remain on the to-do list —
they need catalog index metadata first.

commits.title: executor: add Update and Delete heap-touching operators
commits.description:
Both operators share a scanMatching helper that walks the heap
block-by-block, evaluates the WHERE predicate (extracted from the
child Filter(SeqScan), or no predicate when the child is a bare
SeqScan), and collects (block, slot, row) hits. The two-pass
collect-then-write shape keeps the iteration semantics simple — if
we wrote inline, an UPDATE that re-extends the relation would
re-encounter its own newly-inserted tuples on later pages and loop.

Update follows upstream's "delete + insert" pattern: stamp xmax on
the old tuple with storage.PageSetHeapTupleXmax (a new in-place
header-mutator on internal/storage), then writeHeapRow the new image
with xmin = current xid. Old + new live concurrently until VACUUM.

Delete is just the stamp half. mvcc.TupleVisible's
"xmax == currentXID" branch makes deleted rows invisible to the same
transaction's subsequent scans, matching upstream READ COMMITTED.

End-to-end tests cover three shapes: targeted UPDATE re-reads with
the new row visible while the old one isn't, DELETE WHERE id = 2
leaves two rows behind, DELETE without a predicate (bare SeqScan
child) clears the relation.

commits.title: executor: add SeqScan and Insert heap-touching operators
commits.description:
Row codec (internal/executor/codec.go) marshals Datum rows to/from
heap-tuple bytes using a private fixed-format encoding: one null-flag
byte per column followed by the value bytes (4-byte BE for int4,
8-byte BE for int8/timestamp, 1 byte for bool, 4-byte length-prefixed
for text/varchar/char). v0 doesn't yet match upstream's typlen/
typalign rules — that lands with the type system in milestone 7.

Context grows Pool/Catalog/TxnMgr/Tx/Snap so heap-touching operators
have what they need without a separate plumbing pass at every Next().

SeqScan iterates the buffer pool block-by-block, decoding LP_NORMAL
tuples that mvcc.TupleVisible accepts under (Tx.XID, Snap). LP_UNUSED
slots from prior vacuums are skipped silently.

Insert reorders source rows into table-column order via the planner's
ColumnIndex map, encodes via writeHeapRow, and writes to the last
block (extending via PinNew when it's full). RowsAffected accumulates
for the eventual `INSERT N` CommandComplete tag.

End-to-end tests cover insert→scan round-trip, the v0 visibility
behaviour after rollback (currently treats aborted xacts as committed
— a known limitation pinned by the test for future tightening when
commit-status tracking lands), and relation extension under a 600-row
load.

commits.title: executor: add v0 Volcano iterator scaffold
commits.description:
Fresh internal/executor package wires the planner's plan-tree output
to a runnable iterator graph. Design doc 0012-executor.md covers the
layering and the alternatives (push-based / closure-compiled / no-
abstraction).

Datum is a union with Kind ∈ {Null,Bool,Int,String,Bytes,Time}; Row
is []Datum aligned with the operator's planner.Schema. The expression
evaluator handles arithmetic (+ - * / %), string concat (||),
comparisons, unary -, +, NOT, and three-valued AND/OR/NOT per
Kleene; ParamRef looks up in Context.Params; FuncCall dispatches
against an in-tree registry that currently exposes
current_timestamp/now/transaction_timestamp/statement_timestamp/
current_date — they all return ctx.Now to match upstream's
"captured at statement start" semantics.

Operators implemented this loop are the pure-compute ones (Values,
Project, Filter, Limit, Sort) plus the Build(plan) wiring and a Run
helper for tests. SELECT 1 / SELECT 1 + 2 * 3 AS x / SELECT $1 + 5 /
LIMIT/OFFSET / ORDER BY DESC / division-by-zero (SQLSTATE 22012) /
current_timestamp() all run end-to-end. Heap-touching operators
(SeqScan/Insert/Update/Delete) are split into a follow-up so storage
plumbing doesn't churn the pure-compute tests.

commits.title: planner: add v0 catalog and rule-based planner
commits.description:
Two new packages bridge the parser AST to (eventual) executor input:

internal/catalog provides the in-memory schema seam used to resolve
names. Catalog is an interface (LookupTable/LookupColumn/CreateTable/
DropTable/RelFileNode); InMemory is the v0 implementation, assigning
sequential OIDs starting at 16384 (FirstNormalObjectId) and routing
each table's RelFileNode through DBOid=1 until the multi-database
layer arrives.

internal/planner is a single-pass rule-based planner. Logical plan
nodes mirror upstream nodeTags (SeqScan/Filter/Project/Sort/Limit/
Values/Insert/Update/Delete plus DDL/Transaction/Utility pass-through
wrappers). Each statement shape maps to a fixed template; name
resolution rewrites parser.ColumnRef into indexed planner ColumnRef
nodes so the executor can address columns by ordinal instead of
re-walking the parser AST. Errors are *PlanError with
SQLSTATE-aligned codes (42P01 undefined_table, 42703
undefined_column, 42601 syntax_error, 0A000 feature_not_supported).

Pgbench's three load-bearing DML queries + SELECT * + BEGIN/DROP
TABLE/VACUUM ANALYZE all plan end-to-end. Index-scan promotion,
multi-table joins, and GROUP BY/HAVING are deferred — the seam is in
place and the next executor loop unblocks them downstream.

Design doc 0011-planner.md covers the layering rationale, alternatives
(vendoring pg_query, pure AST-walking executor, persistent catalog
from day one), and the deferred-work list.

commits.title: parser: add ALTER TABLE with ADD PRIMARY KEY / ADD COLUMN
commits.description:
ALTER TABLE [IF EXISTS] name action [, action …]

with two actions in v0:

  ADD [CONSTRAINT name] PRIMARY KEY (col [, …])
  ADD [COLUMN] column_def

Pgbench installs primary keys after the data load via
  alter table pgbench_branches add primary key (bid)
which now round-trips through the parser. With this in, pgbench -i's
entire DDL surface (CREATE TABLE, the COPY-driven load, ALTER TABLE
ADD PRIMARY KEY, plus the surrounding DROP/TRUNCATE/VACUUM verbs)
parses end-to-end.

commits.title: parser: add CREATE/DROP/TRUNCATE DDL statements
commits.description:
Five DDL statements covering pgbench -i's init path on top of the
existing expression and DML support:

  CREATE [UNLOGGED] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] name
    (column_def [, …]) [WITH (k=v, …)] [TABLESPACE x]
  CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX [IF NOT EXISTS] [name]
    ON table [USING method] (col [, …])
  DROP TABLE [IF EXISTS] name [, …] [CASCADE|RESTRICT]
  DROP INDEX [IF EXISTS] name [, …] [CASCADE|RESTRICT]
  TRUNCATE [TABLE] name [, …] [CASCADE|RESTRICT]

ColumnDef carries a typed ColumnType (`char(22)` -> {Name:char, Args:
[22]}) and the `NOT NULL` / inline `PRIMARY KEY` flags; table-level
`PRIMARY KEY (a, b)` populates CreateTableStmt.PrimaryKey. WITH
options stash as a string→string map for the analyzer to interpret.

Pgbench's exact init strings — the four CREATE TABLE shapes (history
+ tellers + accounts + branches), the comma-separated DROP TABLE IF
EXISTS, and the comma-separated TRUNCATE TABLE — all round-trip
through Parse(). ALTER TABLE … ADD PRIMARY KEY is the remaining gap;
queued in fix_plan.

commits.title: parser: add INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE statements
commits.description:
Three DML statements covering the rest of the pgbench default script
on top of the expression tree we already have:

  INSERT INTO target [(col, …)] VALUES (val, …) [, …] [RETURNING …]
  UPDATE target SET col = expr [, …] [WHERE expr] [RETURNING …]
  DELETE FROM target [WHERE expr] [RETURNING …]

INSERT supports multiple parenthesised value tuples and an optional
column list; RETURNING in all three reuses the SELECT target-list
parser (so RETURNING * works). INSERT … SELECT, ON CONFLICT, UPDATE
FROM, and DELETE USING are deferred — pgbench doesn't need them and
they'd grow the surface area before the planner is wired.

Pgbench's three load-bearing DML queries
  UPDATE pgbench_accounts SET abalance = abalance + $1 WHERE aid = $2
  SELECT abalance FROM pgbench_accounts WHERE aid = $1
  INSERT INTO pgbench_history (tid, bid, aid, delta, mtime)
    VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, current_timestamp())
all parse end-to-end.

commits.title: parser: add expression tree and SELECT statement
commits.description:
Pratt-style precedence-climbing expression parser covering arithmetic
(+ - * / %), string concat (||), comparisons (= < > <= >= <> !=),
boolean (AND/OR/NOT), and unary +/-. Operator precedences are aligned
with upstream's gram.y so `a = 1 + 2 * 3 OR b > 4 AND c < 5` parses
into the expected tree shape.

Expression-tree node types: IntegerConst (int64), StringConst,
NullConst, BooleanConst, ParamRef ($N), ColumnRef (1/2/3-part names),
StarExpr (bare * and qualified t.*), BinaryOp, UnaryOp, FuncCall
(supporting count(*), DISTINCT, qualified function names).

SELECT shape: target list (expr [AS alias], or *, or t.*),
comma-separated FROM with optional AS or bare-ident alias, WHERE,
ORDER BY with ASC/DESC, LIMIT, OFFSET. The pgbench --select-only
canonical query
  SELECT abalance FROM pgbench_accounts WHERE aid = $1
parses end-to-end. JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, and set operations stay
deferred to the next loop alongside the planner work that needs them.

commits.title: parser: add v0 lexer, AST, and phase-1 statement parser
commits.description:
Hand-written recursive-descent parser scaffolded for the pgbench SQL
surface (design doc 0010). The lexer handles identifiers (quoted and
unquoted), integer and single-quoted string literals (with '' escape),
parameter placeholders ($N), line comments, nestable block comments,
and the multi-character operators we'll need (<>, !=, <=, >=, ||).
Keyword vs identifier classification happens after carving out the
identifier text, mirroring upstream's scan.l shape.

Phase-1 statements covered: BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK with the
END/ABORT/WORK/TRANSACTION aliases, VACUUM with VERBOSE/ANALYZE/target
list, ANALYZE, plus the SHOW/SET/RESET GUC verbs. SELECT/INSERT/etc.
arrive in subsequent loops alongside their expression-tree types —
fix_plan now decomposes the parser item into per-statement-family
sub-tasks so progress is trackable.

commits.title: vacuum: add v0 VACUUM and ANALYZE
commits.description:
internal/vacuum drives a heap page-prune across every block of a
relation. Dead tuples — those whose xmax is below the MVCC oldest-xmin
horizon — transition to LP_UNUSED while survivors are repacked against
pd_special, so pd_upper rises and the in-page free window is contiguous
again. Slot numbers are preserved so external pointers (B-tree leaf
items, future ctids) keep resolving and reclaimed slots simply surface
as LP_UNUSED on the next probe.

ANALYZE walks the heap with a fresh snapshot and returns row count plus
average tuple width over visible rows. Sampling and per-column stats
are deferred — the package functions are the seam the parser will wire
to in milestone 6.

Supporting plumbing: mvcc.Manager.OldestXmin returns the horizon that
matches a fresh snapshot's Xmin; storage.VacuumHeapPage is the
access-method-neutral page primitive; storage.Pool.NBlocks exposes the
relation block count for the full-relation walk.

commits.title: btree: add v0 B-tree index access method
commits.description:
Single-column int4 B-tree on top of the buffer pool. Pages mirror upstream
nbtree: 24-byte header + ItemId array + tuple region + 16-byte BTPageOpaque
(prev/next siblings, level, flags). Block 0 is the metapage; leaf splits
propagate a separator up the descent path and lift a new root when the
current root splits. Forward range scan walks right-sibling pointers.
Concurrency is one mutex per *BTree; Lehman/Yao crab-walk is deferred.

internal/storage/heap.go gains PageAddItemRaw / PageGetItemRaw — the
access-method-neutral counterparts of PageAddHeapTuple — so index AMs
can drop pre-encoded items into pages without going through the heap
tuple parser.

Tests: insert+search round-trip with a miss, 800-row insert that forces
several leaf splits, ordered range scan, reopen-then-search to verify
on-disk format consistency.

commits.title: mvcc: add snapshot manager and tuple visibility
storage: add heap tuple format with xmin/xmax metadata
wal: add periodic checkpointer goroutine
wal: add checkpoint-bounded crash recovery replay
wal: add minimal crash recovery replay seam
docs(ralph): update fix_plan after wal loop

feat(storage): O_DIRECT-aligned page allocator, smgr, clock-sweep buffer pool
commits.description:
First slice of Milestone 5 from .ralph/fix_plan.md. Lands the storage
foundation that every later piece (heap, btree, MVCC, WAL) will sit
on. SQL execution still routes through the existing in-memory
SELECT 1 / SHOW / SET shim — the next loops bolt heap+MVCC+WAL onto
this seam.

Highlights:

- internal/storage/page.go: BlockSize=8192 (matches upstream BLCKSZ),
  typed PageHeader view over the first 24 bytes mirroring upstream's
  PageHeaderData byte-for-byte (pd_lsn / pd_checksum / pd_flags /
  pd_lower / pd_upper / pd_special / pd_pagesize_version /
  pd_prune_xid). InitPage writes the canonical fresh-page layout
  (pd_lower=24, pd_upper=8192, pd_pagesize_version=0x2004 i.e.
  BlockSize | PG_PAGE_LAYOUT_VERSION=4). Plus RelFileNode +
  ForkNumber + BlockNumber + BufferTag types.
- internal/storage/arena.go + unsafe.go: mmap-backed page-aligned
  arena carved into BlockSize-sized slots. Anonymous private mmap
  returns 4 KiB-aligned memory which satisfies Linux O_DIRECT
  alignment on ext4/xfs. Falls back to a Go-heap allocation aligned
  by over-reserve+trim if mmap is unavailable.
- internal/storage/smgr.go: Manager opens per-relation files at
  <DataDir>/base/<dbOid>/<relOid>[<fork-suffix>] with
  os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE plus optional O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC. ReadBlock /
  WriteBlock / Extend / NBlocks / Sync operate at block-aligned
  offsets. ErrShortRead distinguishes past-EOF reads from I/O errors.
- internal/storage/direct_io_linux.go: fcntl-based F_SETFL toggle for
  O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC. Tolerates EINVAL on filesystems that don't
  honour O_DIRECT (notably tmpfs, used by t.TempDir on most Linux
  distros) so unit tests can run anywhere.
- internal/storage/bufpool.go: Pool is the buffer manager. Slot
  carries page (alias into the arena), tag (BufferTag), valid,
  dirty, pinCount, usageCount, contentMu. Pin walks byTag for hits
  and otherwise runs evictLocked to find a victim; dirty victims
  are flushed through smgr before reassignment. PinNew extends the
  relation by one block. MarkDirty + FlushAll round out the
  checkpointer-shaped seam. Clock sweep is bounded at 2*N+
  maxUsageCount passes with maxUsageCount=5, matching upstream's
  freelist.c:196.

Tests:
- TestInitPagePinsHeaderLayout pins the byte-level page header.
- TestSMGRReadWriteRoundTrip exercises Extend / WriteBlock /
  ReadBlock / Sync / ErrShortRead and verifies the on-disk path is
  base/<dbOid>/<relOid>.
- TestPoolPinReadsThroughSMGR confirms a Pin loads from disk and
  the byTag cache is hit on a second Pin (no re-read).
- TestPoolDirtyEvictionWritesBack mutates 3 blocks through a
  2-slot pool, confirms block 0 (which had to be evicted) reads
  back its mutated bytes.
- TestPoolPinAllExhaustsBuffers verifies ErrNoBuffer when every
  slot is pinned.
- TestPoolFlushAllClearsDirty pins the FlushAll contract.

go.mod adds golang.org/x/sys (only direct dependency goopg now
carries; it's the standard Linux syscall surface for fcntl/mmap).
The Go toolchain bumped from 1.22.2 to 1.25.0 as a side effect of
go get pulling in x/sys v0.43.

Deferred to subsequent loops in this milestone:
- Heap access method (insert/scan/delete/update) and tuple format
  (xmin/xmax/t_ctid/t_infomask) — needs MVCC for visibility.
- WAL writer + LSN comparison in eviction (the "thou shalt write
  xlog before data" rule).
- Background writer / checkpointer goroutines.
- BufferAccessStrategy ring for sequential scans / vacuum / copy.

commits.title: fix(server): SHOW ALL routing; verified end-to-end with real psql 18.3
commits.description:
Smoke-tested goopg against ./postgres/local_install/bin/psql 18.3 to
verify that milestones 1-4 actually interoperate with libpq. Most
checks passed cleanly:

- SELECT 1, SHOW server_version, SET application_name + SHOW
- Unsupported statement returns ErrorResponse with the connection
  staying alive (\conninfo subsequently works)
- SCRAM-SHA-256 against a real psql client succeeds with the right
  password and produces FATAL "password authentication failed for
  user X" with the wrong one — same wire-level interop the unit
  tests already pin via hand-rolled libpq computation

One regression surfaced: SHOW ALL was being routed through the
per-name SHOW arm because HasPrefix(upper, "SHOW ") matched first,
producing 'unrecognized configuration parameter "ALL"'. Reordered the
switch in handleQuery so SHOW ALL hits its own arm before the per-name
arm. RESET ALL had the same shape (HasPrefix could match "RESET
ALLPHA"); tightened it to exact-equality.

Added TestShowAllReturnsAllVariables to pin the fix.

commits.title: feat(config): postgresql.conf parser, GUC registry, SHOW/SET/RESET
commits.description:
Milestone 4 from .ralph/fix_plan.md. The hardcoded ParameterStatus
block in the server is now driven by a typed GUC registry, and clients
can SHOW / SET / SET LOCAL / RESET variables on the wire.

Highlights:

- internal/config/parser.go: postgresql.conf parser. Handles `name =
  value` (the `=` is optional), single- and double-quoted values, the
  `''` literal-quote escape, comments to end of line, and bareword
  multi-token sequences like `DateStyle = ISO, MDY` joined with a
  single space. include / include_if_exists / include_dir directives
  resolve recursively with cycle detection.
- internal/config/guc.go: typed Variable + Registry. Variable carries
  Type (Bool / Int / Real / String / Enum), Unit (bytes and time
  families), Context (Internal..Userset, mirroring guc.h), Source
  (where the current value came from), Scope (Server / Database /
  Role / Session / Transaction), and VarFlag (Report / DisallowInFile
  / NotInSample / Custom). canonicalize() normalises bool spellings,
  honours unit suffixes ("8MB" -> 8192 KB), and validates against
  Min/Max/EnumOptions. Registry.ApplyConfigEntries bypasses Context
  gating because file-driven sets at startup are allowed to touch
  Postmaster-context variables.
- internal/config/defaults.go: BuildDefaultRegistry seeds every GUC
  the server already advertises (server_version, server_encoding,
  client_encoding, DateStyle, IntervalStyle, TimeZone,
  integer_datetimes, standard_conforming_strings, is_superuser,
  session_authorization, in_hot_standby,
  default_transaction_read_only, application_name,
  default_transaction_isolation, listen_addresses, port,
  max_connections, scram_iterations).
- internal/config/session.go: SessionRegistry layers transaction
  (SET LOCAL) over session (SET) over the global registry. Variables
  flagged Report fire a hook on every effective-value change, which
  the server wires into ParameterStatus emission.
- internal/server: Config.Registry is the new seam; nil falls back to
  BuildDefaultRegistry. parameterStatusBlock is replaced by a
  ReportableVariables() walk; per-connection SessionRegistry echoes
  StartupMessage application_name / user into the appropriate layer.
  handleQuery learns SHOW / SHOW ALL / SET / SET LOCAL / RESET /
  RESET ALL — all return real RowDescription/DataRow output for
  SHOW and emit ParameterStatus for FlagReport variables on change.
- cmd/goopg start --config <path>: parses postgresql.conf and wires
  the resolved registry into Server.Config.

Tests:
- TestParseConfigLines pins the postgresql.conf shapes documented in
  0004.
- TestVariableUnitConversion verifies "8MB" → 8192 KB.
- TestSessionLayering verifies SET LOCAL drops on EndTransaction and
  RESET clears the layered overrides.
- TestReportableHookFires ensures Report-flagged variables call back
  exactly when their effective value changes.
- End-to-end TestShowReturnsRegistryValue,
  TestSetEmitsParameterStatusForReportable, TestSetThenShowSeesNewValue,
  TestSetRejectsPostmasterContextVar pin the wire-level contract.

`go test -race ./...` passes.

Deferred to milestone 5 (catalog) or beyond:
- pg_settings as a real catalog view (SHOW ALL covers the use case for now).
- current_setting() / set_config() SQL functions.
- ALTER SYSTEM / ALTER DATABASE...SET / ALTER ROLE...SET.
- Hot reload (pg_ctl reload). The Source provenance is recorded so a
  future reload can replace ConfigFile-sourced values without
  touching Session/Override/EnvVar values.

commits.title: feat(auth): SCRAM-SHA-256 (SASL) authentication
commits.description:
Completes Milestone 3 from .ralph/fix_plan.md. SCRAM-SHA-256 lands as
the preferred password-bearing auth method, alongside the existing
trust / reject / password / md5 paths.

Highlights:

- internal/auth/scram.go: full server-side SCRAM-SHA-256 per RFC 5802
  + RFC 7677. SCRAMSecret / NewSCRAMSecret / ParseSCRAMSecret round-trip
  the upstream `SCRAM-SHA-256$<iter>:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>`
  rolpassword shape. Hand-rolled PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 pinned to RFC 7914
  known-answer. SCRAMServer is the per-connection state machine: Step()
  consumes client-first / client-final, emits server-first /
  server-final, runs constant-time proof verification, and rejects with
  ErrInvalidPassword on bad proof or doomed mode (unknown user / wrong
  credential format).
- internal/auth/exchange.go: MethodSCRAMSHA256 case arm. SASL framing
  (advertise SCRAM-SHA-256, decode SASLInitialResponse mechanism +
  initial-data, drive the two-round exchange, emit SASLContinue +
  SASLFinal + AuthenticationOk). Doomed exchange falls back to
  ErrInvalidPassword so callers emit FATAL/28000 — same as upstream.
- internal/auth/userstore.go: PasswordSCRAMSHA256 credential format.
  VerifyCleartext recomputes StoredKey from a candidate password and
  constant-time compares against the stored value, mirroring
  scram_verify_plain_password. PasswordMD5 cannot satisfy SCRAM
  (no plaintext available); SCRAM credential satisfies cleartext
  `password` but not `md5`.
- internal/protocol: AuthenticationSASL / AuthenticationSASLContinue /
  AuthenticationSASLFinal encoders plus the full AuthenticationRequest
  sub-code table.
- docs/design/0003-authentication.md: SCRAM addendum covering the wire
  shape table, credential format, doomed-exchange / timing-parity
  rationale, and the deferred items (SASLprep, channel binding,
  scram_iterations GUC).

Tests:
- TestPBKDF2HMACSHA256KnownAnswer pins the PBKDF2 primitive to
  RFC 7914.
- TestSCRAMExchangeSuccess hand-rolls a libpq-style client (gs2
  header, salted password, client proof, server signature verify)
  against the in-process state machine.
- TestSCRAMExchangeRejectsBadProof / TestSCRAMServerDoomedFailsCleanly
  pin the failure paths.
- End-to-end TestSCRAMAuthSuccess / TestSCRAMAuthWrongPasswordRejected
  drive the wire protocol against a real listener, confirming the
  AuthenticationSASL / SASLContinue / SASLFinal / AuthenticationOk
  sequence and FATAL/28000 on wrong proof.

`go test -race ./...` passes.

commits.title: feat(auth): password (cleartext) and md5 authentication
commits.description:
Continues Milestone 3 from .ralph/fix_plan.md. Both methods drop in as
case arms in the new auth.Exchange and reuse the policy seam landed in
the previous loop.

Highlights:

- internal/auth/userstore: UserStore interface + MapUserStore (an
  in-memory, concurrency-safe map[name]Credential). Credentials carry
  one of two formats — plaintext or upstream's pg_authid-style
  "md5"+md5_hex(password+username). VerifyCleartext and VerifyMD5Challenge
  are constant-time and accept either format. NewMD5Credential matches
  pg_md5_encrypt(password, username) bit-for-bit; ParseMD5Stored ingests
  an already-shadowed value.
- internal/auth/exchange: Exchange() drives the wire-level auth
  exchange. Trust → AuthenticationOk. Password → R/3 + PasswordMessage.
  MD5 → R/5/4-byte-salt + PasswordMessage carrying
  "md5"+md5_hex(rolpassword_md5_tail+salt). Salt is fresh from
  crypto/rand per connection. Unknown-user and wrong-password failures
  share an identical FATAL emission so network observers can't
  distinguish them.
- internal/protocol: AuthenticationCleartextPassword / Authentication-
  MD5Password encoders, MsgPasswordMessage ('p') frontend tag, and the
  full AuthenticationRequest sub-code table from upstream.
- internal/server: Config.UserStore (auth.UserStore); checkAuth replaces
  the previous Authenticate() classifier with Exchange(), so the same
  call site handles trust + password + md5 + reject + unsupported. nil
  UserStore is fine for trust-only setups; password/md5 with nil store
  emit FATAL/0A000 (feature_not_supported) rather than panicking.
- docs/design/0003-authentication.md: addendum documents the password
  and md5 wire shapes, the credential formats, and the no-leak posture
  on auth failure.

Tests: TestMD5ChallengeReproducesClientResponse pins md5 interop by
performing the libpq-side computation and asserting our verifier
accepts it. End-to-end server tests cover password success / wrong
password / unknown user / nil-store fallback, and md5 success / wrong
response. `go test -race ./...` passes.

The dead Authenticate() classifier from the previous loop is removed —
Exchange is the single entry point now, and the typed error sentinels
(ErrRejected / ErrInvalidPassword / ErrMethodUnsupported / ErrAuthExchange)
remain the public surface for callers.

commits.title: feat(auth): pg_hba.conf-driven authentication policy with trust/reject
commits.description:
Milestone 3 (partial — trust + reject only) from .ralph/fix_plan.md.
The unconditional AuthenticationOk in handleStartup is replaced with a
policy-driven decision so password / md5 / scram can drop in as
case-arm additions in subsequent loops.

Highlights:

- internal/auth: Method (every upstream UserAuth keyword) + ConnType +
  Rule + RuleSet; tokenizer that honours quoted strings and inline `#`
  comments; parser for `local`, `host*` lines including the legacy
  IP+netmask two-token form; include / include_if_exists / include_dir
  with cycle detection; first-match Match() that mirrors upstream's
  check_hba semantics (no-match returns implicit-reject).
- internal/auth.Authenticate: dispatch shim. v0 implements MethodTrust
  (proceed) and the two reject methods (ErrRejected). Other methods
  return ErrMethodUnsupported so handleStartup can FATAL with a clear
  diagnostic instead of hanging.
- internal/server: Config gains Policy auth.Policy; default is
  auth.DefaultPolicy() (loopback IPv4/IPv6 trust, everything else
  implicit-reject). serveConn calls checkAuth between parsing the
  StartupMessage and sending the parameter-status block; rejected
  connections receive a FATAL ErrorResponse with SQLSTATE 28000
  (invalid_authorization_specification).
- cmd/goopg: `goopg start --hba <path>` loads a real pg_hba.conf.
- docs/design/0003-authentication.md: scope, format, matcher, server
  integration, and the explicit non-goals (TLS, ident map, regex/
  hostname address forms, password/md5/scram method bodies).

Tests: parser covers minimal rules, malformed methods, the four
documented address shapes, and include / include_if_exists / cycle
detection. Matcher covers first-match ordering and implicit reject.
End-to-end server tests cover (a) reject policy → FATAL with SQLSTATE
28000 and connection close, (b) parsed-but-unimplemented method
(scram-sha-256) → FATAL with SQLSTATE 0A000, (c) the default policy
still admits loopback so existing tests stay green. `go test -race
./...` passes.

commits.title: WIP
feat(server): simple Query path with SELECT 1, generated SQLSTATE table
commits.description:
Milestone 2 from .ralph/fix_plan.md. The goopg server now handles the
simple Query message: a `SELECT 1` returns a real RowDescription /
DataRow / CommandComplete / ReadyForQuery sequence, anything else
becomes a structurally-correct ErrorResponse, and the connection stays
usable across both outcomes.

Highlights:

- internal/sqlstate: a fully-generated package backing every SQLSTATE
  goopg ever emits. cmd/gen-sqlstate parses upstream's
  src/backend/utils/errcodes.txt and emits typed Code constants
  (FeatureNotSupported, ProtocolViolation, AdminShutdown, …) plus a
  Severity lookup. Six SQLSTATEs that upstream maps to multiple macros
  (e.g. 2202E for ARRAY_ELEMENT_ERROR / ARRAY_SUBSCRIPT_ERROR) keep both
  Go names with a single severities-map entry. Existing magic-string
  call sites in internal/server replaced with typed constants.
- internal/protocol: WriteRowDescription / WriteDataRow /
  WriteCommandComplete / WriteEmptyQueryResponse encoders, plus
  FieldDescription mirroring SendRowDescriptionMessage in
  postgres/src/backend/access/common/printtup.c.
- internal/server: handleQuery routes the simple Query path. v0
  recognises `SELECT 1` (case-insensitive, optional `;`), emits int4 OID
  23 with the `?column?` name and command tag `SELECT 1` matching
  upstream. Whitespace-only queries return EmptyQueryResponse. Anything
  else returns feature_not_supported ErrorResponse + ReadyForQuery, so
  the connection stays alive.
- docs/design/0015-simple-query-and-sqlstate.md: numbered out of band so
  the milestone-aligned 0010-0014 slots stay free for parser/planner/
  executor docs that will eventually replace this shim.

Tests: TestSelectOne pins the full RowDescription/DataRow/CommandComplete/
ReadyForQuery byte layout; TestSelectOneCaseAndSemicolon covers the
documented matcher tolerance; TestUnsupportedQueryProducesErrorResponse
checks the SQLSTATE; TestEmptyQueryReturnsEmptyQueryResponse covers the
heartbeat shape; TestConnectionStaysAliveAfterError pins the
"error then SELECT 1 still works" contract from the milestone spec.
`go test -race ./...` passes.

commits.title: feat(server): protocol-v3 startup handshake, framing, graceful shutdown
commits.description:
Milestone 1 from .ralph/fix_plan.md. The goopg binary now serves real
PostgreSQL clients through the startup handshake and waits at
ReadyForQuery. SQL execution still errors out with SQLSTATE 0A000 — that
arrives in milestone 2.

Highlights:

- internal/protocol: hand-rolled frame reader/writer, startup-packet
  decoder, and encoders for AuthenticationOk / ParameterStatus /
  BackendKeyData / ReadyForQuery / Error+NoticeResponse. Bounded read
  buffers (10 KB startup, 1 MiB per frame) protect against
  memory-exhaustion DoS.
- internal/server: TCP listener with context-driven graceful shutdown,
  per-connection goroutines, the v0 ParameterStatus block (server_version
  18.3, encodings, DateStyle, TimeZone, integer_datetimes,
  standard_conforming_strings, etc.), and SSL/GSS request rejection
  (single 'N' byte, then re-read the real startup packet).
- cmd/goopg: `goopg start [-listen host:port]` runs the server in the
  foreground; SIGINT and SIGTERM translate into context cancellation,
  matching the architecture in 0001-architecture-overview.md §3.3.
- docs/design/0002-wire-protocol.md: scope, framing model, parameter
  block, BackendKeyData semantics, and explicit non-goals (TLS, auth
  beyond AuthenticationOk, CancelRequest handling).

Tests: focused unit tests for frame round-trip, oversize-payload
rejection, startup parameter parsing, the full handshake against a real
TCP listener, the SSLRequest fallback, the unsupported-version path, and
graceful shutdown with a connected idle client. `go test -race ./...`
passes. Smoke-tested with a Python protocol probe: handshake completes
cleanly with R / S×13 / K / Z.
